subStrands.cbeCompetency: Financial capability, time management, analytical calculation, critical decision making, and practical life skills

subStrands.title: Geometry: Lines, Angles, and Polygons
subStrands.description: Identifying and drawing parallel, perpendicular, and intersecting lines; classifying angles (acute, right, obtuse, straight, and reflex) using a protractor; calculating interior angles of triangles (summing to 180°) and quadrilaterals (summing to 360°); identifying properties of equilateral, isosceles, and scalene triangles, and various quadrilaterals.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spatial visualization, geometric reasoning, precision measurement, and structural analysis

subStrands.title: 3D Solids and Nets
subStrands.description: Identifying and classifying three-dimensional geometric solids (cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, triangular prisms, square-based pyramids, spheres); determining the number of faces, edges, and vertices of polyhedra; verifying Euler's formula (F + V - E = 2); identifying and folding 2D nets into 3D shapes; exploring everyday Kenyan packaging solutions (cereal boxes, milk cartons, unga bales, and grain silos).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spatial awareness, geometric visualization, engineering design, structural reasoning, and modeling

subStrands.title: Data Handling, Patterns and Simple Algebra
subStrands.description: Collecting and recording data using tally marks and frequency tables; constructing and interpreting pictographs with scales; constructing and analyzing vertical and horizontal bar graphs; identifying rules in number sequences and arithmetic patterns; formulating simple algebraic expressions and solving one-step linear equations involving addition, subtraction, and multiplication in practical everyday situations.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Analytical thinking, data interpretation, pattern recognition, algebraic problem solving, and logical deduction

subStrands.title: School and Community Service
subStrands.description: Participating in community service projects, tree planting campaigns, and school clubs; distinguishing between concrete and abstract nouns; applying quantifiers (much, many, few, little, several, plenty of) accurately with countable and uncountable nouns; expanding civic vocabulary in everyday school and community dialogue.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Communication and collaboration, citizenship, self-efficacy, critical thinking, and social responsibility

subStrands.title: Family Celebrations and Cultural Heritage
subStrands.description: Describing family traditions, national cultural days (such as Utamaduni Day), and traditional festivities; using personal and possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs); mastering reflexive pronouns (myself, himself, herself, ourselves, themselves); appreciating Kenyan cultural diversity and heritage through expressive oral and written English.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Intercultural awareness, self-efficacy, respect for diversity, communication fluency, and social cohesion

subStrands.title: Good Manners and Digital Etiquette
subStrands.description: Practicing courteous dialogue, telephone etiquette, and responsible internet citizenship (netiquette); mastering modal verbs for polite requests and permission (could, would, may, might, should); expressing polite agreement and respectful disagreement in classroom discussions; promoting cyber-safety and anti-bullying in everyday communication.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Digital literacy, respectful communication, self-efficacy, empathy, and active listening

subStrands.title: Food, Balanced Diet and Culinary Arts
subStrands.description: Discussing indigenous Kenyan foods, balanced nutrition, and food hygiene; contrasting the simple past tense with the past continuous tense (was/were + -ing) in narrative storytelling; using time conjunctions (while, when) to connect simultaneous and interrupted past actions; expanding culinary and recipe vocabulary in English.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Health literacy, communication, critical thinking, linguistic precision, and self-expression

subStrands.title: Kenyan Wildlife and Marine Conservation
subStrands.description: Reading informational texts and narratives on Kenya's world-famous wildlife sanctuaries (Maasai Mara, Amboseli, Tsavo) and Indian Ocean marine reserves (Watamu, Kisite-Mpunguti); forming and comparing regular and irregular degrees of adjectives (positive, comparative, superlative); analyzing environmental conservation efforts to protect endangered species and coral reefs; expanding descriptive and conservation vocabulary.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Environmental awareness, descriptive expression, critical reading, inferential comprehension, and global citizenship

subStrands.title: Digital Learning and Modern Inventions
subStrands.description: Discussing the role of educational tablets, computer coding, digital encyclopedias, and modern technological tools in Kenyan classrooms; connecting ideas using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions of reason, contrast, and condition (because, since, so, although, even though, if, unless); mastering logical sentence structure and technical digital vocabulary.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Digital literacy, logical reasoning, syntactical fluency, problem solving, and technological curiosity

subStrands.title: Travel, Tourism and National Landmarks
subStrands.description: Reading about Kenyan travel adventures by train (SGR Madaraka Express), bus, and coastal ferry; discovering historical and geographical landmarks (Fort Jesus, Great Rift Valley, Mount Kenya, Vasco da Gama Pillar, Lake Victoria); mastering prepositions of place, direction, and movement (across, through, along, past, towards, into, onto, between, among); giving and following navigational travel directions in English.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Geographical inquiry, spatial communication, reading comprehension, cultural patriotism, and directional orientation

subStrands.title: Environmental Protection and Climate Action
subStrands.description: Discussing environmental conservation, forest restoration (honoring Nobel Laureate Prof. Wangari Maathai), plastic pollution prevention, and renewable energy (Olkaria geothermal, Lake Turkana wind power); mastering adverbs of manner (forming adverbs from adjectives by adding -ly), adverbs of time, and adverbs of frequency (always, often, rarely, seldom); expanding climate and eco-action vocabulary.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Environmental responsibility, linguistic precision, civic engagement, critical thinking, and global problem solving

subStrands.title: Talents, Occupations and Entrepreneurship
subStrands.description: Exploring career paths (agronomy, aviation, software development, medicine, craftsmanship, journalism); expressing planned and spontaneous future intentions using "will/shall" and "be going to"; mastering question tags for verification and polite conversation; understanding the value of thrift, entrepreneurship, and integrity in trade.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Career awareness, self-efficacy, critical thinking, linguistic precision, and financial capability

subStrands.title: Children's Rights, Leadership and Functional Writing
subStrands.description: Understanding child protection, fundamental rights (education, health, shelter, expression), and civic responsibilities; mastering punctuation mechanics (apostrophes in contractions and possession, quotation marks in direct speech); writing structured informal friendly letters, diary reflections, and thank-you notes with appropriate register.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Citizenship, moral leadership, empathy, communicative competence, and written composition

subStrands.title: Fungi and Bacteria
subStrands.description: Investigating the characteristics of fungi (mushrooms, yeast, moulds) and microscopic bacteria; distinguishing between useful and harmful fungi/bacteria; exploring biological processes such as decomposition, milk fermentation (mursik/yoghurt), and dough rising; understanding safety precautions when handling unknown moulds and mushrooms in the environment.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Scientific inquiry, health awareness, critical observation, hygiene safety, and environmental stewardship

subStrands.title: Flowering and Non-Flowering Plants
subStrands.description: Classifying plants into flowering plants (maize, beans, sunflowers) and non-flowering plants (ferns, mosses, pine/conifers); examining the reproductive anatomy of a complete flower (sepals, petals, stamen, pistil); investigating wind and insect pollination adaptations; understanding fertilization and seed formation in flowering plants.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Botanical classification, environmental awareness, analytical reasoning, and scientific modeling

subStrands.title: Invertebrates and Insect Metamorphosis
subStrands.description: Classifying common invertebrates (insects, arachnids, myriapods, molluscs, worms); examining physical characteristics such as body parts and leg counts; comparing complete and incomplete insect metamorphosis; investigating ecological and agricultural roles of invertebrates in Kenyan habitats.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Biological classification, careful observation, life cycle modeling, and environmental conservation

subStrands.title: Human Breathing System
subStrands.description: Identifying organs of the respiratory system (nose, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli, lungs, diaphragm); analyzing the mechanics of inhalation and exhalation; demonstrating gas exchange concepts; cultivating respiratory hygiene and habits that maintain lung health.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Anatomical understanding, scientific modeling, respiratory hygiene, and personal health management

subStrands.title: Human Sense Organs and Sensory Care
subStrands.description: Investigating the five human sense organs (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin); exploring sensory receptors and their specific stimuli (light, sound, chemicals, touch, temperature); practicing daily sensory hygiene; adopting protective measures against noise pollution, sharp objects, and eye hazards.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Sensory awareness, anatomical literacy, health habits, safety consciousness, and empathy towards persons with sensory impairments

subStrands.title: Mixtures and Separation Techniques
subStrands.description: Categorizing homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures (solid-solid, solid-liquid, liquid-liquid); experimenting with practical separation methods (sieving, winnowing, hand-picking, filtration, decantation, evaporation, magnetic separation); relating separation processes to Kenyan farming, domestic, and industrial practices.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Inquiry skills, experimental design, scientific classification, resource management, and environmental stewardship

subStrands.title: Light Energy, Shadows and Reflection
subStrands.description: Investigating sources of light; demonstrating that light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation); classifying materials as transparent, translucent, or opaque; exploring shadow formation and factors affecting shadow size; investigating plane mirror reflection and making simple optical devices like periscopes.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Scientific observation, optical modeling, critical thinking, experimental deduction, and technological innovation

subStrands.title: Heat Energy, Transfer and Temperature
subStrands.description: Exploring modes of heat transfer (conduction in solids, convection in fluids, radiation across space); differentiating between thermal conductors and insulators; investigating thermal expansion and contraction; measuring temperature accurately in degrees Celsius; applying heat conservation in Kenyan energy-saving jikos and cooking practices.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Thermodynamic inquiry, practical measurement, resource conservation, home safety, and environmental responsibility

subStrands.title: Word Processing and Digital Tools
subStrands.description: Navigating word processing applications; creating, editing, and formatting documents (font styles, sizes, colours, alignment, bullet points); inserting images and tables; practicing safe file saving and storage; applying healthy typing ergonomics and practicing cybersecurity ethics.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Digital literacy, creative communication, typing ergonomics, technological problem solving, and online safety

subStrands.title: Levers, Pulleys and Friction
subStrands.description: Investigating simple machines; identifying parts of a lever (fulcrum, load, effort); classifying first, second, and third class levers; exploring fixed and movable pulleys; analyzing friction as an opposing force, its everyday advantages, disadvantages, and methods of reducing or increasing friction in machines.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Mechanical reasoning, physical science inquiry, tool efficiency, problem solving, and occupational safety

subStrands.title: Soil Recovery and Erosion Control
subStrands.description: Identifying types of soil erosion (splash, sheet, rill, gully); investigating causes such as steep slopes, overgrazing, and deforestation; collecting and recovering topsoil from deposition sites; demonstrating soil conservation measures including contour farming, mulching, vetiver grass strips, and check dams across Kenyan agricultural landscapes.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Environmental conservation, soil stewardship, practical land care, critical observation, and community civic responsibility

subStrands.title: Organic Compost and Soil Fertility
subStrands.description: Exploring composting methods (pit method and heap method); selecting suitable organic materials (crop residues, animal manure, green grass, wood ash); constructing layered compost piles; managing decomposition through aeration and watering; testing compost maturity and applying finished organic humus to vegetable plots.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Sustainable farming, organic waste recycling, practical experimentation, teamwork, and soil fertility improvement

subStrands.title: Container Gardening and Innovative Cropping
subStrands.description: Designing innovative small-space cropping systems (container gardens, multi-storey sack gardens, vertical wall gardens, tyre gardens); preparing suitable potting soil mixtures (topsoil, organic manure, sand); planting and managing vegetables (sukuma wiki, spinach, coriander, capsicum); utilizing micro-irrigation and practicing progressive leaf harvesting in urban and peri-urban Kenyan homesteads.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Innovation, urban agricultural design, resourcefulness, waste repurposing, and household food self-sufficiency

subStrands.title: Vegetative Crop Propagation and Nursery Care
subStrands.description: Investigating vegetative asexual plant propagation using stem cuttings (cassava, sweet potatoes, sugarcane), suckers (banana, pineapple), splits (pyrethrum), and tubers (Irish potatoes); managing seedling nursery beds (watering, shading, thinning, pricking out, weeding, hardening off); transplanting healthy seedlings at late afternoon to minimize transplant shock.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Agronomic precision, nursery management, scientific inquiry, practical tool handling, and crop multiplication skills

subStrands.title: Rearing Small Domestic Animals
subStrands.description: Identifying small domestic animals reared on Kenyan farms (rabbits, poultry, guinea pigs); designing proper housing (hutches, chicken coops, ventilation, predator protection); providing balanced feeds (greens, grains, pellets) and clean water; applying humane animal handling and welfare practices in accordance with Kenyan guidelines.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Animal husbandry, humane handling, animal welfare ethics, practical construction skills, and resource responsibility

subStrands.title: Small Animal Health and Hygiene
subStrands.description: Distinguishing between healthy and diseased small animals through vital signs and behaviour; identifying common external parasites (fleas, mites, lice) and internal parasites (worms); executing routine hygiene and pest control (dusting, cleaning feeding troughs, pen disinfection); practicing biosecurity measures including isolation and sanitary carcass disposal.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Veterinary observation, hygiene management, biosecurity consciousness, problem-solving, and disease prevention

subStrands.title: Balanced Diet and Healthy Eating
subStrands.description: Categorizing foods into three major functional food groups (energy-giving carbohydrates & fats, body-building proteins, and protective vitamins & minerals); understanding the vital roles of dietary fibre and drinking water; planning balanced everyday Kenyan meals; promoting indigenous nutrient-rich food crops (millet, sorghum, managu, terere, nduma); preventing nutritional deficiency disorders (kwashiorkor, marasmus, rickets, anemia, scurvy).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Nutritional literacy, healthy lifestyle decision making, cultural appreciation of traditional food crops, and personal wellness

subStrands.title: Nutritive Value and Cooking Methods
subStrands.description: Investigating cooking methods (boiling, steaming, roasting, shallow frying); analyzing the effect of heat and cooking duration on food nutrients; practicing nutrient conservation techniques (washing vegetables prior to chopping, covering cooking pots, avoiding overcooking); demonstrating strict food hygiene, safe clean water handling, and domestic kitchen sanitation.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Culinary science, nutrient preservation, kitchen safety, hygiene consciousness, and domestic resource management

subStrands.title: Food Preservation Techniques
subStrands.description: Investigating causes of food spoilage (bacteria, moulds, yeasts, enzymes, moisture); mastering traditional Kenyan preservation methods (sun drying of vegetables, grains, and fish; smoking; salting; milk fermentation); applying modern hermetic grain storage (PICS bags, airtight containers, ash treatment) to eliminate storage pests without toxic chemicals.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Scientific resource preservation, post-harvest management, indigenous knowledge application, and food loss reduction

subStrands.title: Kitchen Gardening and Household Food Security
subStrands.description: Designing sustainable household kitchen gardens; establishing continuous crop rotation, companion planting, and safe greywater reuse; reducing post-harvest losses and food wastage; exploring value addition of farm surplus; promoting household nutritional self-sufficiency and communal zero-hunger ethics across Kenyan communities.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ecological gardening, community stewardship, financial resourcefulness, zero-waste practices, and empathy for food security

subStrands.title: Maps, Map Reading, Position & Size of Kenya
subStrands.description: Navigating using an 8-point compass; interpreting key map elements (title, frame, scale, key/legend, north arrow); identifying conventional topographical map symbols; locating the geographical position of Kenya on the globe using latitude (Equator) and longitude; defining Kenya’s approximate surface area; identifying neighboring nations (Uganda, Tanzania, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia) and international boundaries.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Cartographic literacy, spatial orientation, geographical reasoning, environmental inquiry, and national awareness

subStrands.title: Physical Features and Drainage in Kenya
subStrands.description: Exploring relief features of Kenya (mountains, Great Rift Valley, plateaus, plains, valleys, coastal lowlands); identifying major mountains (Mount Kenya, Mount Elgon); investigating drainage systems including major rivers (Tana, Athi, Nzoia, Ewaso Ng’iro) and their destinations; classifying Rift Valley freshwater lakes (Naivasha, Baringo) and soda lakes (Nakuru, Bogoria, Magadi, Elementaita); evaluating the economic importance and conservation of drainage basins.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Physical geography inquiry, environmental stewardship, landscape appreciation, critical thinking, and resource management

subStrands.title: Weather and Climate of Kenya
subStrands.description: Investigating weather elements (temperature, rainfall, wind direction, wind speed, air pressure, cloud cover) and measuring instruments (thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane, anemometer, barometer, hygrometer); distinguishing between weather and climate; identifying climatic zones of Kenya (Equatorial, Modified Equatorial/Highland, Tropical, Semi-Arid, and Arid); analyzing factors influencing climate; and examining climate change impacts and adaptation measures across Kenya.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Meteorological observation, climatic data interpretation, critical environmental inquiry, climate change mitigation, and scientific problem-solving

subStrands.title: Migration and Settlement of Kenyan Communities
subStrands.description: Tracing historical origins, migration routes, and entry points of major Kenyan language groups (Bantu, Nilotes - River-Lake, Plains, Highland, and Cushites); examining reasons for migration (famine, drought, search for pasture/farmland, internal conflicts, population pressure); analyzing historical settlement patterns across geographic regions; and appreciating inter-community interactions (trade, intermarriage, cultural exchange) that fostered peaceful coexistence.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Historical inquiry, cultural empathy, spatial tracing, inter-ethnic understanding, and national cohesion

subStrands.title: Culture, Social Organization and Traditional Governance
subStrands.description: Examining indigenous education systems (oral traditions, proverbs, apprenticeships, rites of passage); exploring social structures including family, clan, age-groups, and age-sets; analyzing traditional systems of governance (councils of elders such as Njuri Ncheke, Kiama, Kambi); and celebrating prominent historical leaders (Koitalel Arap Samoei, Mekatilili wa Menza, Nabongo Mumia, Masaku, Waiyaki wa Hinga) who shaped Kenya’s heritage.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Cultural literacy, historical appreciation, civic consciousness, leadership inquiry, and value orientation

subStrands.title: Agriculture and Crop Farming in Kenya
subStrands.description: Distinguishing between subsistence and commercial farming; identifying major cash crops (tea, coffee, sugarcane, pyrethrum, cotton, flowers/horticulture) and their geographical growing zones; investigating major national irrigation schemes (Mwea Tebere, Perkerra, Ahero, Bura); evaluating the economic contribution of agriculture to Kenya’s GDP, employment, and food security; and identifying solutions to modern agricultural challenges.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Economic literacy, agro-ecological reasoning, sustainable development, resource evaluation, and national problem-solving

subStrands.title: Livestock Farming, Fishing and Wildlife in Kenya
subStrands.description: Investigating pastoralism, commercial dairy and beef ranching across Kenya; examining freshwater inland fishing (Lake Victoria, Lake Naivasha, aquaculture ponds) and marine fishing along the Indian Ocean coast; exploring wildlife conservation, National Parks (Tsavo, Nairobi, Amboseli), National Reserves (Maasai Mara), and marine sanctuaries; and analyzing strategies for sustainable resource use and human-wildlife conflict mitigation.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Resource stewardship, blue economy literacy, conservation inquiry, eco-tourism awareness, and problem-solving

subStrands.title: Mining, Forestry and Trade in Kenya
subStrands.description: Examining major mineral deposits (soda ash at Lake Magadi, titanium in Kwale, limestone at Bamburi/Athi River, diatomite at Kariandusi, gemstones in Taita Taveta, crude oil in Turkana) and extraction methods; investigating indigenous water towers (Mau, Mount Kenya, Aberdares, Kakamega Forest) versus plantation forestry; and analyzing domestic and regional trade (exports of tea/flowers, imports of petroleum/machinery, and the East African Community market).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Mineral literacy, forest stewardship, macroeconomic understanding, trade integration, and environmental rehabilitation

subStrands.title: Citizenship, Human Rights and National Unity
subStrands.description: Understanding Kenyan citizenship (citizenship by birth and registration); exploring the Bill of Rights (civil, political, economic, and social rights); understanding citizen responsibilities (tax compliance, lawfulness, environmental protection); upholding children’s rights and protection from abuse; examining national symbols (National Flag, National Anthem, Coat of Arms, Public Seal); and championing factors promoting national unity while rejecting tribalism and discrimination.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Civic competence, human rights advocacy, constitutional literacy, national cohesion, and ethical responsibility

subStrands.title: Governance, Democracy and Rule of Law in Kenya
subStrands.description: Demystifying the democratic system of government in Kenya; exploring the two levels of government (National Government and 47 County Governments); analyzing the three arms of national government (Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary); examining county governance (Governor, County Executive Committee, and County Assembly); understanding the electoral process administered by the IEBC; and appreciating principles of good governance (transparency, accountability, rule of law, and public participation).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Democratic literacy, governance inquiry, institutional understanding, civic decision-making, and constitutional patriotism

subStrands.title: Drawing, Perspective, Tonal Variation & Still Life Composition
subStrands.description: Exploring elements of art (line, shape, form, texture, value/tone, space) and principles of design (balance, proportion, rhythm, emphasis); mastering tonal gradation techniques (cross-hatching, stippling, smudging); sketching still life compositions featuring authentic Kenyan items (traditional gourds, earthenware pots, tropical fruits); applying one-point linear perspective (horizon line, vanishing point, converging lines); and caring for artistic drawing instruments.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Visual observation, spatial estimation, fine motor control, aesthetic judgment, and artistic expression

subStrands.title: Painting, Color Harmony, Collage & Montage
subStrands.description: Investigating color theory (primary, secondary, tertiary hues, warm and cool color palettes); mixing tints (adding white) and shades (adding black) to render three-dimensional depth; painting expressive Kenyan landscape scenes; creating textured mixed-media collages using local found materials (banana fibres, sand, eggshells, dried grass); and designing thematic photo montages advocating environmental conservation and national values.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Chromatic literacy, creative innovation, material repurposing, thematic storytelling, and environmental consciousness

subStrands.title: Clay Modeling, Coil / Slab Pottery, Carving & Sculpting
subStrands.description: Preparing natural clay (slaking, sieving, wedging to expel air bubbles); mastering hand-building pottery techniques (pinch, coil with slip and scoring, slab construction); applying surface decorations (incising, stamping, burnishing); exploring open-pit and kiln firing; carving subtractive sculptures from soft wood or authentic Kisii soapstone (steatite); using gouges, rasps, and sandpaper; and finishing surfaces with wax or polish.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Tactile manipulation, three-dimensional modeling, material preparation, sculptural precision, and safety awareness

subStrands.title: Indigenous Kenyan Crafts: Basketry, Leather Craft & Traditional Beadwork
subStrands.description: Exploring indigenous basket weaving using sisal fibers, palm leaves, and reed grasses; dyeing sisal with natural plant pigments; weaving traditional Kenyan kiondo baskets (twining, coiling, plaiting); working with leather (cutting, awl punching, thonging, tooling); and crafting authentic beaded cultural ornaments (Maasai and Samburu necklaces, wristbands) while understanding ethnic color symbolism and cultural preservation.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Cultural craft preservation, indigenous technology, fine motor braiding, ornamental geometry, and entrepreneurial thinking

subStrands.title: Musical Rhythms, Staff Notation, Sol-fa & Vocal Performance of Folk Songs
subStrands.description: Mastering rhythm and meter in simple time (2/4, 3/4, 4/4); identifying musical notes (semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver) and rests; using French time names (taa, taa-aa, ta-te); reading the five-line musical stave in treble clef; signing tonic sol-fa with Curwen hand signs; practicing vocal techniques (breath support, diction, posture); classifying indigenous Kenyan folk songs (lullabies, work songs, initiation songs, celebration songs); and performing two-part choral harmony with expressive dynamics.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Aural discrimination, musical literacy, vocal breath control, rhythmic coordination, and cultural expression

subStrands.title: Traditional Kenyan Musical Instruments
subStrands.description: Classifying indigenous musical instruments into four organological families: Aerophones (flutes like Chivoti, horns like Abu and Coro), Chordophones (lyres like Nyatiti and Obokano, fiddles like Wandindi, arched harps like Adeudeu), Idiophones (Kayamba reed shakers, Kigamba leg bells), and Membranophones (Isukuti drums, Ohangla drums, Chapuo); examining natural building materials and acoustics; and mastering instrument tuning and preservation.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Organological classification, acoustic inquiry, instrument craftsmanship, percussive timing, and cultural stewardship

subStrands.title: Indigenous Kenyan Dances, Body Adornments, Costumes & Choreography
subStrands.description: Exploring traditional Kenyan folk dances across diverse communities (Mwomboko, Isukuti, Kamabeka, Gonda, Sengenya, Dodo); analyzing dance elements (body movement, space, rhythm, dynamics, relationship); designing choreography with varied geometric floor formations (circles, diagonals, serpentine lines); examining traditional dance regalia (sisal skirts, colobus monkey skins, ostrich feather headdresses, beaded headbands); and appreciating props (flywhisks, shields, walking sticks) in cultural storytelling.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Locomotor coordination, choreographic creativity, cultural empathy, rhythmic precision, and heritage appreciation

subStrands.title: Track Athletics: Sprint Starts, Relay Batons, Hurdles & Middle-Distance Running
subStrands.description: Mastering track athletics: sprint crouch starts ("On your marks", "Set", "Go / Gunshot"); acceleration mechanics and finish-line lean; executing relay baton exchanges (non-visual handover in 4x100m, visual handover in 4x400m, upsweep vs downsweep techniques within the 20-meter changeover box); practicing standing starts and aerobic pacing in 800m and 1500m middle-distance running; studying Kenyan world athletic champions; and adhering to track safety and sportsmanship.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Athletic speed, baton coordination, cardiovascular endurance, pacing strategy, and fair play

subStrands.title: Field Athletics & Ball Games: Long Jump, Football, Netball & Volleyball
subStrands.description: Mastering field athletics: executing long jump phases (run-up approach, take-off board mechanics, flight technique, and soft sand pit landing); refining core skills in major team ball games: Football (instep passing, dribbling, shooting, legal throw-ins, and fair play); Netball (footwork rule, chest/bounce passes, goal shooting, and court positions); and Volleyball (underhand service, overhead set, forearm bump/dig pass, and team rotation).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spatial agility, ball handling coordination, tactical teamwork, sportsmanship, and motor control

subStrands.title: Gymnastics, Rope Skipping, Water Safety, First Aid & Healthy Lifestyle
subStrands.description: Practicing educational gymnastics (forward and backward rolls with tucked chin, static balances like V-sit, arabesque, and supported headstand); mastering skipping rope agility (single bounce, double under, cross-over); upholding water safety guidelines and non-contact drowning rescue (reach or throw, don’t jump); administering sports First Aid for sprains and strains using the R.I.C.E. protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation); and promoting lifelong physical fitness and clean health.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Gymnastic balance, aquatic safety, emergency First Aid response, cardiovascular endurance, and health advocacy

subStrands.title: Creation, Human Stewardship and Environmental Conservation
subStrands.description: Understanding God’s purpose in creating humanity in His image and likeness; human duty as stewards to cultivate, tend, and protect the earth (Genesis 1 & 2); conserving Kenyan flora, fauna, and water catchment towers (Mau Forest, Mount Kenya); combating environmental degradation, plastic pollution, and soil erosion; and demonstrating compassion for domestic livestock and wildlife.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Environmental stewardship, moral accountability, ecological mindfulness, empathy toward living creatures, and community conservation initiative

subStrands.title: The Holy Bible: Structure, Divisions, Translations & Sacred Guidance
subStrands.description: Exploring the 66 books of the Holy Bible; differentiating the Old Testament (39 books: Law, History, Poetry, Major Prophets, Minor Prophets) and the New Testament (27 books: Gospels, Acts, Epistles, Revelation); appreciating the role of the Bible Society of Kenya in translating scripture into indigenous Kenyan languages; handling the Bible with reverence; and memorizing key scriptures to guide daily moral decision-making.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Biblical literacy, analytical classification, scriptural reflection, respectful handling of sacred texts, and ethical decision-making

subStrands.title: Faith and Obedience: Old Testament Heroes and Leaders
subStrands.description: Examining inspiring faith and obedience through Old Testament heroes and leaders: Abraham’s faith journey and covenant obedience (Genesis 12 & 17); Moses’ courage and servant leadership in leading the Israelites across the Red Sea (Exodus 14); the boy Samuel hearing and responding to God’s call in Shiloh (1 Samuel 3); and Prophet Elijah standing boldly for truth against false prophets on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Moral courage, faithful leadership, obedience to divine principles, discerning God’s calling, and standing firm for truth

subStrands.title: The Early Life, Baptism, and Temptation of Jesus Christ
subStrands.description: Investigating the early life and milestones of Jesus Christ: the Annunciation to Mary by Angel Gabriel (Luke 1); the humble birth in Bethlehem and visitation of the shepherds and wise men (Luke 2, Matthew 2); boyhood of Jesus in Nazareth and discussions in the Jerusalem Temple at age twelve; the baptism of Jesus by John the Baptist in the River Jordan and the descent of the Holy Spirit; and overcoming the threefold temptations in the wilderness by quoting Scripture (Matthew 4:1-11).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spiritual discernment, moral resilience against temptation, scriptural defense, humility, and filial obedience

subStrands.title: Miracles and Parables of Jesus Christ
subStrands.description: Exploring the compassion and divine power of Jesus through His miracles and kingdom parables: Healing miracles (healing the centurion’s servant - Luke 7, raising Jairus’ daughter - Luke 8, healing the blind Bartimaeus - Mark 10); Nature miracles (calming the storm on Lake Galilee - Luke 8, feeding the five thousand - John 6); Parables of the Kingdom and love for neighbor (The Parable of the Good Samaritan - Luke 10, The Parable of the Lost Sheep - Luke 15, The Parable of the Talents - Matthew 25); applying compassion, inclusive love, and faithful stewardship of personal talents.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Compassion, empathy, neighborliness, faithful stewardship of God-given abilities, and active kindness

subStrands.title: The Passion, Death, Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus Christ
subStrands.description: Examining the ultimate sacrifice and victory of Jesus Christ: The Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday (Luke 19); the Last Supper and the New Covenant of communion (Luke 22); fervent prayer and submission in the Garden of Gethsemane; the trial, crucifixion, and forgiveness on the Cross at Golgotha ("Father, forgive them" - Luke 23); the glorious Resurrection on Easter Sunday (Luke 24); the Emmaus Road encounter; and the Great Commission and Ascension into heaven (Matthew 28, Acts 1).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Sacrificial love, forgiveness, reconciliation, perseverance under suffering, and witnessing for Christ

subStrands.title: The Holy Spirit, Spiritual Gifts & The Early Church Community
subStrands.description: Understanding the role of the Holy Spirit in the believer’s life and the fellowship of the early Christian community: The Day of Pentecost (Acts 2:1-13 - sound of rushing wind, tongues of fire, speaking in other tongues, Peter’s bold sermon and 3,000 believers baptized); The Fruits of the Holy Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23 - love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control); The Gifts of the Holy Spirit for building the Church (1 Corinthians 12); Fellowship, unity, and communal sharing in the Early Church (Acts 2:42-47, Acts 4:32-35); resolving disagreements peacefully in Christian fellowship.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spiritual discernment, moral self-control, peaceful fellowship, collaborative generosity, and communal harmony

subStrands.title: Christian Living, Family Relationships, and Moral Values
subStrands.description: Developing Christian character, strong family relationships, and moral values in daily life: Honoring parents and guardians (Ephesians 6:1-3, Exodus 20:12); respect for elders and teachers; healthy friendships and positive peer influence (Proverbs 13:20, 1 Corinthians 15:33); managing emotions like anger and jealousy constructively (Ephesians 4:26-27, Proverbs 15:1); honesty, truthfulness, and integrity in academic work and chores; resisting modern vices (cheating, lying, stealing, cyberbullying, drug abuse).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Moral integrity, filial respect, emotional intelligence, positive socialization, and assertive resistance to peer pressure

subStrands.title: Compassion, Inclusion & Serving the Vulnerable in the Community
subStrands.description: Practicing Christ-like compassion, inclusion, and service toward vulnerable populations in Kenya: Caring for orphans and vulnerable children (James 1:27, Psalm 82:3-4); supporting widows and elderly persons (1 Timothy 5:3-4); welcoming and including persons living with disabilities (Luke 14:12-14 - the great banquet feast); showing love and hospitality to refugees, displaced persons, and immigrants (Leviticus 19:33-34, Matthew 25:35); Christian response to poverty, hunger, and disease; community service initiatives (visiting hospitals, community cleanups, charity donations).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Compassion, empathy, inclusive community engagement, social responsibility, and selfless service

subStrands.title: Justice, Peace, Integrity & Nation Building in Kenya
subStrands.description: Living as faithful Christian citizens in Kenya: Upholding justice, fairness, and the rule of law (Micah 6:8, Amos 5:24); rejecting corruption, bribery, tribalism, and favoritism (Proverbs 17:23, Exodus 23:8); promoting national cohesion and ethnic harmony (Galatians 3:28 - all are one in Christ); obeying lawful authority and paying taxes conscientiously (Romans 13:1-7, Matthew 22:21); peacebuilding, conflict resolution, and patriotism in our schools, villages, and nation; the role of the Church in promoting integrity and social transformation in Kenya.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Civic responsibility, moral courage against corruption, intercultural harmony, peacebuilding, and national patriotism

subStrands.title: Surah Al-Humazah and Surah Al-Asr: Speech Etiquette and Time Stewardship
subStrands.description: Recitation and comprehension of Surah Al-Humazah (warning against slander, backbiting, and hoarding wealth) and Surah Al-Asr (swearing by time, the four conditions for salvation: faith, righteous deeds, advising truth, and advising patience); applying ethical speech and diligent time management in school and daily life.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ethical verbal communication, emotional self-regulation, time stewardship, and mutual encouragement toward truth

subStrands.title: Surah At-Takathur and Surah Al-Qari’ah: Material Rivalry and the Day of Judgment
subStrands.description: Recitation and reflection on Surah At-Takathur (warning against obsessive worldly competition and reminder of gratitude) and Surah Al-Qari’ah (the striking hour of resurrection, mountains like wool, and the heavy scales of good deeds); cultivating contentment, accountability, and active good deeds.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spiritual accountability, contentment over materialism, moral reflection on consequences, and performing acts of righteousness

subStrands.title: Selected Hadith: Acts of Charity, Emotional Self-Control & Social Kindness
subStrands.description: Examining authentic prophetic traditions (Hadith): Hadith on every good deed being charity (Sadaqah - e.g. smiling at a brother, speaking a good word, removing harmful objects from the road); Hadith on anger management ("The strong person is not the good wrestler, but the one who controls himself when angry"); Hadith on honoring neighbors and guests ("Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor/guest"); understanding the structure of a Hadith (Isnad - chain of narrators, and Matn - text); applying prophetic character in school, home, and community.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Prophetic literacy, emotional self-regulation, empathy, peaceful neighborliness, and proactive charitable service

subStrands.title: The Call to Prophethood (Bi’thah) and Early Secret Da’wah in Makkah
subStrands.description: Investigating the inception of Islam: The Prophet’s retreats for contemplation in Cave Hira on Mount Nur (Jabal an-Nur); the descent of Archangel Jibril with the first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq 96:1-5 - "Iqra / Read in the name of your Lord"); the comforting role of Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA) and consultation with Waraqah ibn Nawfal; the first converts to Islam (Khadijah - first woman, Abu Bakr - first free adult male, Ali ibn Abi Talib - first youth/child, Zayd ibn Harithah - first freed slave); the three years of secret Da’wah (Da’wah Sirriyyah) and the sanctuary of Dar al-Arqam.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Historical reflection, spiritual seeking, marital comfort, loyal friendship, and wisdom in early community formation

subStrands.title: The Open Proclamation of Islam (Da’wah Jahriyyah) and Early Persecutions
subStrands.description: Tracing the prophetic mission from the secret phase to the public proclamation: The divine command to openly invite people to Islam (Surah Al-Hijr 15:94 and Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:214); the public address from Mount Safa and the reaction of the Quraysh clans; opposition from Abu Lahab and revelation of Surah Al-Masad; persecution of early vulnerable Muslims (Bilal ibn Rabah, Sumayyah bint Khayyat, Yasir ibn Amir, Ammar ibn Yasir, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt); steadfastness (Sabr) in faith; the first and second migrations to Abyssinia (Habashah); the justice of King Negus (Ashamah an-Najashi); and Ja’far ibn Abi Talib’s recitation of Surah Maryam.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Moral resilience, courage in upholding truth, empathy for the oppressed, peaceful dialogue, and refuge protection

subStrands.title: Belief in Revealed Divine Scriptures (Kutub) and the Archangels (Mala’ikah)
subStrands.description: Exploring two essential Pillars of Iman: Belief in the revealed Divine Books (Tawrat to Musa AS, Zabur to Dawud AS, Injil to Isa AS, and the Holy Qur’an to Muhammad SAW; the Scrolls/Suhuf of Ibrahim and Musa AS; the Holy Qur’an as the final, unchanged, preserved guidance for all humanity); and Belief in the Angels (Mala’ikah) created from light, their obedience without sin or fatigue, and specific roles of major Archangels (Jibril, Mika’il, Israfil, Malak al-Mawt, Kiraman Katibin - Raqib and Atid, Malik, Ridwan, Munkar and Nakir).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Theological literacy, accountability for daily actions, reverence for divine revelation, and moral self-monitoring

subStrands.title: Purification (Taharah: Najasaat & Tayammum) and Selected Sunnah Prayers
subStrands.description: Understanding physical and ritual cleanliness in Islam: Classification of impurities (Najasaat: Mukhaffafah - light; Mutawassitah - medium; Mughalladhah - heavy); methods of cleansing each type; conditions, pillars, and performance of dry ablution (Tayammum) using clean soil/dust; exploring the spiritual virtues and practical performance of Sunnah prayers: Tahiyyat al-Masjid, Salat ad-Dhuha, Sunan ar-Rawatib (12 daily rak'ahs), and Salat al-Witr.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Personal and environmental hygiene, ritual purity, spiritual devotion, self-discipline in voluntary worship

subStrands.title: The Pillar of Sawm (Fasting in Ramadan) and Zakat (Charity & Economic Justice)
subStrands.description: Deepening understanding of two foundational pillars of Islam: Sawm (fasting in Ramadan from dawn to sunset): definition, conditions, pillars, nullifiers, permissible exemptions (illness, journey, nursing, pregnancy), Qadha vs. Fidyah, and spiritual virtues of Taqwa; and Zakat: Zakat al-Fitr (due before Eid al-Fitr prayer) and Zakat al-Maal (annual 2.5% calculated on qualifying wealth reaching Nisab), and the eight rightful categories of recipients specified in Surah At-Tawbah 9:60.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Empathy for the vulnerable, socio-economic justice, self-restraint, charitable responsibility, community welfare

subStrands.title: Islamic Etiquette (Akhlaq), Modesty, and Honoring Family Ties
subStrands.description: Cultivating noble Islamic character: The comprehensive etiquette of Islamic greeting (As-Salamu 'Alaykum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh) and its spiritual virtues; prophetic table manners (saying Bismillah, eating with the right hand, eating from what is directly before you, sitting down to drink, not wasting food, saying Alhamdulillah); the virtue of modesty and moral dignity (Haya'); the duty of honoring parents (Birr al-Walidayn) emphasized in Surah Al-Isra 17:23-24 (not even saying "Uff" to them, speaking gently, making supplication for them); and preserving ties of kinship (Silat ar-Rahim) as a source of expanded sustenance and longevity.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Moral dignity, respectful communication, filial devotion, family unity, emotional empathy

subStrands.title: Peaceful Coexistence, Environmental Stewardship, and Nation Building in Kenya
subStrands.description: Applying Islamic values in the multi-ethnic and multi-religious context of Kenya: Peaceful coexistence (Ta'ayush) and tolerance with non-Muslim neighbors and citizens of diverse faiths, following the example of the Charter of Madinah (Sahifat al-Madinah) and the Quranic command to deal kindly and equitably with peaceful people (Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:8); environmental stewardship as stewards (Khulafa) of the Earth: water conservation during ablution even at a flowing river, planting trees as ongoing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), preventing animal cruelty; and contributing actively to Kenyan national development through anti-corruption integrity, academic diligence, and peaceful civic engagement.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Interfaith harmony, environmental responsibility, conservation ethics, national patriotism, anti-corruption integrity

subStrands.title: Attributes of Paramatma and the Cosmic Order (Rta)
subStrands.description: Exploring the infinite nature of Paramatma: Sarvavyapi (Omnipresent - existing everywhere and within every soul as Atman), Sarvashaktiman (Omnipotent - all-powerful creator and sustainer), and Sarvajna (Omniscient - all-knowing); the concept of Rta (the cosmic order, balance, and natural harmony governing nature and moral life); seeing divinity in nature and treating all living beings with reverence.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spiritual awareness, ecological consciousness, moral reflection, and respect for cosmic harmony

subStrands.title: Avatars of Preservation: Early Incarnations of Lord Vishnu
subStrands.description: Investigating the purpose of divine descent (Avatar): upholding Dharma (righteousness) and protecting the virtuous when cosmic order is threatened (Bhagavad Gita 4:7-8); exploring early manifestations of Lord Vishnu from the Dashavatara: Matsya (the Fish Avatar rescuing King Manu and sacred herbs), Kurma (the Tortoise Avatar supporting Mount Mandara during cosmic ocean churning), Varaha (the Boar Avatar rescuing Mother Earth / Bhumi Devi), and Narasimha (the half-lion, half-human Avatar protecting child devotee Prahlada).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spiritual literacy, moral courage, resilience against intimidation, and reverence for divine protection

subStrands.title: Lord Rama: The Embodiment of Dharma and Righteous Leadership
subStrands.description: Exploring the seventh Avatar of Lord Vishnu: Lord Rama as Maryada Purushottama (the ideal human maintaining moral boundaries); filial obedience to King Dasharatha; 14 years of forest exile; loyalty of brother Lakshmana and selfless detachment of Bharata; pure devotion (Bhakti) and selfless service of Shri Hanuman; vanquishing the tyrant Ravana; the reign of justice (Ramrajya); and moral lessons of truth, promise-keeping, and family harmony.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Moral leadership, filial devotion, loyalty, promise-keeping, and selfless friendship

subStrands.title: Lord Krishna: Joyful Leelas, Govardhan Hill, and Nature Stewardship
subStrands.description: Exploring the eighth Avatar of Lord Vishnu: The birth of Lord Krishna in Mathura and upbringing in Gokul and Vrindavan; loving childhood Leelas (Makkhan Chor - teaching non-attachment to hoarding); lifting Mount Govardhan upon His little finger to protect villagers, cows, and nature from torrential storms, emphasizing the worship and care of local ecology over fear; compassion for cows (Gopala) and wildlife; and defeating the tyrant King Kamsa.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Environmental stewardship, compassion for animals, joyful simplicity, and standing against bullying

subStrands.title: The Sacred Scriptures: The Four Vedas and Philosophical Wisdom of the Upanishads
subStrands.description: Exploring the eternal scriptural foundation of Sanatana Dharma: The classification of scriptures into Shruti (revealed divine wisdom heard by ancient Rishis) and Smriti (remembered traditions and epics); the Four Vedas: Rigveda (hymns of praise to cosmic forces and creation), Samaveda (sacred melodies and musical chants), Yajurveda (rituals, prayers, and prose mantras), and Atharvaveda (practical sciences, medicine/Ayurveda, and everyday living); and the profound philosophical insights of the Upanishads (dialogues exploring Brahman the Ultimate Reality, Atman the individual soul, and their oneness).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Textual literacy, philosophical inquiry, spiritual reflection, and respect for ancient literary heritage

subStrands.title: Sacred Mantras: Divine Vibrations of Aum, Gayatri, and Shanti Mantras
subStrands.description: Investigating the spiritual science of sacred sound (Nada Brahma): The cosmic primordial sound "Aum" (Om) representing creation, preservation, and transformation across three states of consciousness (waking, dreaming, deep sleep); the universally revered Gayatri Mantra from the Rigveda (3:62:10) invoking Savitur (the divine sun) to illuminate human intellect with wisdom; the Shanti Mantras invoking universal peace for the heavens, earth, waters, and vegetation; and the practical benefits of daily mantra chanting for focus and calm.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Mental mindfulness, auditory concentration, reverence for sacred languages, and peaceful meditation

subStrands.title: Sadachar: The Five Yamas (Moral Restraints for Character Building)
subStrands.description: Cultivating noble moral character (Sadachar) through the Five Yamas from Patanjali's Yoga Sutras: 1) Satya (truthfulness in speech, action, and digital life; avoiding gossip and lies); 2) Ahimsa (non-violence in thought, word, and deed; gentle speech, opposing bullying, and compassion for all living beings); 3) Asteya (non-stealing; respecting others' property, ideas, and academic honesty); 4) Brahmacharya (purity of thought, focus, self-control, and channeling energy into studies); and 5) Aparigraha (non-possessiveness, freedom from greed, sharing resources, and simple living).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Moral self-regulation, empathy, non-violence, ethical integrity, and academic honesty

subStrands.title: Pancha Mahayajna: The Five Daily Sacred Duties of Gratitude and Interconnection
subStrands.description: Exploring the five foundational daily duties (Pancha Mahayajna) through which a Hindu expresses gratitude to the cosmos and lives selflessly: 1) Deva Yajna (gratitude to the Divine and cosmic forces through prayer, offering, and reverence for nature); 2) Rishi / Brahma Yajna (gratitude to ancient sages, teachers, and knowledge through daily study and learning); 3) Pitru Yajna (gratitude and respectful service to parents, elders, and ancestors); 4) Manushya / Nri Yajna (gratitude and service to fellow human beings through hospitality, feeding guests, and helping the poor); and 5) Bhuta Yajna (gratitude and compassion toward animals, birds, insects, and plant life by feeding them and protecting habitats).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Gratitude, civic responsibility, filial devotion, animal welfare, and ecological stewardship

subStrands.title: Family Devotion, Guru Vandana, and Sewa (Selfless Community Service)
subStrands.description: Exploring family values, spiritual mentorship, and selfless community action: The sacred bond of family unity and reverence for parents and grandparents (Kula Dharma); Guru Vandana (expressing deep reverence to spiritual and academic mentors); the principle of Sewa (selfless service without expectation of reward / Nishkama Karma); various forms of Sewa: Tan (physical service), Man (mental/emotional comfort and prayer), and Dhan (charitable sharing of financial resources); and the inspiring history of Hindu community Sewa in Kenya (founding hospitals, schools, famine relief, eye clinics, and tree nurseries).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Filial piety, mentor appreciation, civic engagement, altruistic volunteerism, and social responsibility

subStrands.title: Sacred Festivals, Cultural Heritage, and National Coexistence in Kenya
subStrands.description: Celebrating major Hindu festivals and active participation in Kenyan nation-building: 1) Navratri (celebrating nine nights of divine feminine energy / Shakti, triumph of righteousness over Mahishasura, and joyful Garba/Dandiya folk dances); 2) Maha Shivratri (the night of Lord Shiva: meditation, fasting, self-discipline, and conquering negative impulses); 3) Guru Purnima (honoring Sage Vyasa and all educators who dispel ignorance); and 4) Peaceful coexistence, interfaith collaboration with Christian, Muslim, and indigenous Kenyan citizens, environmental stewardship, and anti-corruption integrity in nation-building.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Cultural appreciation, interfaith harmony, festival literacy, national patriotism, and civic integrity

subStrands.title: Maamkizi, Adabu za Kijamii na Ngeli ya U-I
subStrands.description: Kutambua maamkizi mbalimbali kulingana na wakati na umri (Sabalkheri, Masalkheri, Chei chei, Shikamoo); kuonyesha adabu za heshima mezani na hadharani; kuelewa ngeli ya U-I, nomino zake (mti/miti, mkate/mikate), na upatanisho sahihi wa kisarufi.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ustadi wa mawasiliano ya heshima, utambuzi wa upatanisho wa kisarufi katika ngeli ya U-I, na uthamini wa mshikamano wa jamii

subStrands.title: Lishe Bora, Usafi wa Mazingira na Ngeli ya YA-YA / Vihusishi
subStrands.description: Kusoma na kuelewa umuhimu wa lishe bora na usafi wa mazingira; kutambua msamiati wa vyakula na afya; kubainisha nomino za ngeli ya YA-YA (maji, maziwa, mafuta, marashi) na matumizi ya vihusishi vya mahali na nafasi (ndani ya, nje ya, kando ya, juu ya).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa stadi za afya na lishe, utumizi sahihi wa ngeli ya YA-YA na vihusishi katika sentensi, na uwajibikaji wa mazingira

subStrands.title: Shule Yetu, Masomo na Teknolojia ya Kidijitali (Ngeli ya I-ZI)
subStrands.description: Kutambua msamiati wa vifaa vya kidijitali shuleni (tarakilishi, kishikwambi, mtandao, projekta); kuzingatia usalama na maadili mtandaoni; kubainisha nomino za ngeli ya I-ZI (kalamu/kalamu, simu/simu, nyumba/nyumba) na upatanisho wa kisarufi wa I- (umoja) na ZI- (wingi).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ujuzi wa kidijitali na maadili mtandaoni, utambuzi wa upatanisho wa ngeli ya I-ZI, na mawasiliano fasaha ya shuleni

subStrands.title: Kilimo cha Kisasa, Uhifadhi wa Udongo na Hali ya Mazoea (-hu-)
subStrands.description: Kusoma kuhusu mbinu za kilimo bora nchini Kenya (umwagiliaji, samadi, upandaji miti ya matunda); kuelewa zana za kilimo; kubainisha matumizi ya hali ya mazoea kwa kiambishi "hu-" (mkulima hulima, mimea hustawi) na kuitumia katika sentensi zenye mtiririko sahihi.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa kilimo endelevu na uhifadhi wa mazingira, ustadi wa sarufi ya hali ya mazoea (-hu-), na uandishi wa sentensi sahihi

subStrands.title: Usalama Barabarani na Vivumishi Visivyobadilika
subStrands.description: Kusoma kuhusu kanuni za usalama barabarani na alama za trafiki nchini Kenya; kutambua msamiati wa usafiri (kivukio cha watembea kwa miguu, taa za trafiki, matatu, feri, gari-moshi); kubainisha vivumishi vya sifa (-zuri, -baya, -refu) na vivumishi visivyobadilika (safi, bora, ghali, tele, duni, kamili) katika sentensi fasaha.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa stadi za usalama barabarani, utambuzi na matumizi sahihi ya vivumishi visivyobadilika na vya sifa, na utungaji wa sentensi kamilifu

subStrands.title: Wanyamapori Wetu, Misitu na Ngeli ya U-YA / U-ZI
subStrands.description: Kusoma taarifa kuhusu urithi wa wanyamapori wa Kenya (simba, ndovu, kifaru, chui, twiga), makinda yao, na huduma ya KWS; kuelewa umuhimu wa mbuga za kitaifa (Maasai Mara, Amboseli, Tsavo); kubainisha nomino za ngeli ya U-YA na U-ZI (ukuta/kuta, ufa/nyufa, wimbo/nyimbo, ua/maua) na upatanisho wake wa kisarufi.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Uzalendo na uthamini wa mazingira ya wanyamapori, ufahamu wa kina wa ngeli za U-YA na U-ZI, na ufasaha wa kusoma hadithi na makala

subStrands.title: Sanaa za Kiasili, Utamaduni Wetu na Kauli za Vitenzi
subStrands.description: Kuthamini utamaduni na sanaa za jamii za Kenya (vyungu, vikapu, mikuki, shanga, leso, kikoi); kutambua sherehe za kitamaduni na maonyesho ya Bomas of Kenya; kubainisha kauli za vitenzi: Kutenda, Kutendea (-ia/-ea), na Kutendewa (-iwa/-ewa) na kuzitumia katika sentensi zenye upatanisho sahihi.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Uzalendo na uthamini wa turathi za kitamaduni, ustadi wa kunyumbua vitenzi katika kauli za kutendea na kutendewa, na ufasaha wa mawasiliano

subStrands.title: Ushairi, Fasihi Simulizi na Vinyume vya Maneno
subStrands.description: Kusoma na kuelewa mashairi ya watoto (ubeti, mshororo, vina, mizani); kutegua vitendawili na kueleza maana ya methali za kimaadili; kubainisha vinyume vya nomino, vivumishi, na vitendo (inuka/keti, fungua/funga, mrefu/mfupi, rafiki/adui, cheka/lia) katika matini mbalimbali.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa sanaa ya ushairi na fasihi simulizi, uchanganuzi wa lugha ya picha na methali, na umahiri wa vinyume vya maneno

subStrands.title: Biashara, Akiba, Ujasiriamali na Hali ya Masharti ("ki-")
subStrands.description: Kuelewa dhana za biashara, ununuzi, uuzaji, akiba ya kifedha (kibubu, benki, M-Pesa), na ujasiriamali nchini Kenya; kutambua msamiati wa kibiashara (faida, hasara, bei, risiti); kubainisha matumizi ya hali ya masharti kwa kiambishi "ki-" (ukisoma kwa bidii utafaulu; mvua ikinyesha tutalima) na ukanusho wake katika sentensi fasaha.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Stadi za kifedha na ujasiriamali, ufahamu wa kina wa hali ya masharti ("ki-"), na utatuzi wa matatizo ya kiuchumi

subStrands.title: Haki za Mtoto, Uongozi na Uandishi wa Barua ya Kirafiki
subStrands.description: Kutambua haki za msingi za mtoto (elimu, afya, ulinzi dhidi ya dhuluma, kutobaguliwa) na wajibu wake kulingana na Sheria ya Watoto ya Kenya; kuelewa sifa za kiongozi mwadilifu; kutumia alama za uakifishaji (kikomo, koma, alama ya kuuliza, alama ya hisi); na kujifunza muundo kamili wa barua ya kirafiki (anwani, tarehe, maamkizi, mwili wa barua, na hitimisho).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Uelewa wa sheria na haki za watoto, uongozi na uraia mwema, ustadi wa uakifishaji, na uandishi bora wa barua ya kirafiki

subStrands.title: Whole Numbers up to 1,000,000, Rounding & Roman Numerals
subStrands.description: Mastering place value and total value of digits in numbers up to 1,000,000; reading and writing numerals in words and symbols; rounding off to the nearest 100, 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000; and reading, converting, and calculating using Roman numerals up to M (1,000).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Numerical literacy, logical reasoning, estimation skills, and historical numeral systems understanding

subStrands.title: Multi-digit Operations & Order of Operations (BODMAS)
subStrands.description: Adding and subtracting multi-digit numbers up to 1,000,000 in real-life census and agricultural contexts; multiplying 4-digit numbers by 2-digit and 3-digit multipliers; dividing up to 6-digit dividends by 2-digit divisors; and applying the BODMAS order of operations to solve multi-step numerical expressions.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Computational fluency, problem solving, algorithmic thinking, and precision in multi-step arithmetic

subStrands.title: Divisibility Tests, Prime Factorisation, Squares & Square Roots
subStrands.description: Applying divisibility tests for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11; expressing composite numbers as products of prime factors using index notation; solving real-life GCD and LCM word problems; calculating squares of whole numbers up to 100; and determining square roots of perfect squares up to 10,000 using prime factorisation.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Number theory application, factorisation fluency, algebraic thinking, and systematic problem solving

subStrands.title: Fractions, Decimals, Percentages & Rate of Change
subStrands.description: Performing multi-step operations on proper, improper, and mixed fractions; evaluating reciprocals in division; converting between fractions, terminating/recurring decimals, and percentages; and calculating percentage increase and percentage decrease in real-world Kenyan commercial scenarios.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Proportional reasoning, quantitative estimation, computational accuracy, and commercial arithmetic fluency

subStrands.title: Length, Perimeter, Parts of Circles & Circumference
subStrands.description: Measuring lengths, finding perimeters of regular and composite rectilinear shapes, identifying parts of a circle (radius, diameter, circumference, chord, arc, sector, semicircle, quadrant), and calculating circumference using pi = 22/7 and pi = 3.14.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spatial measurement, geometric reasoning, practical circular estimation, and problem solving in agricultural and architectural layouts

subStrands.title: Area of Plane Figures (Triangles, Parallelograms, Trapezia & Circles)
subStrands.description: Calculating areas of triangles (A = 1/2 b h), parallelograms (A = b h), trapezia (A = 1/2 (a + b) h), and circles (A = pi r^2), along with composite land plots and shaded regions.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Area calculation, spatial computation, land parcel valuation, and architectural tiling estimation

subStrands.title: Volume, Capacity, Mass & Density Conversions
subStrands.description: Calculating volume of cubes, cuboids, cylinders (V = pi r^2 h) and prisms; interconverting metric units of volume and capacity (1 L = 1,000 cm^3, 1 m^3 = 1,000 L); converting mass units (tonnes, kg, g); and solving practical packaging and haulage problems.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Three-dimensional spatial visualization, fluid metric conversion, commercial mass estimation, and haulage logistics planning

subStrands.title: Time, 24-Hour Clock, Speed, Distance & Travel Graphs
subStrands.description: Reading and converting between 12-hour and 24-hour clock systems; calculating journey durations across midnight and interpreting bus and train timetables; calculating speed, distance, and time (S = D/T); converting between km/h and m/s; and interpreting travel graphs.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Temporal literacy, timetable navigation, kinematics problem solving, rate interpretation, and graphical data analysis

subStrands.title: Financial Literacy, Bills, Profit & Loss, Simple Interest & Postal Rates
subStrands.description: Preparing and auditing bills and invoices; calculating profit, loss, discount, percentage profit/loss; calculating simple interest (I = PRT/100), hire purchase terms, commission, and postal/parcel rates.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Financial literacy, consumer arithmetic, commercial budget calculation, and entrepreneurial problem solving

subStrands.title: Angles, Parallel Lines, Transversals & Polygons
subStrands.description: Classifying complementary, supplementary, vertically opposite, alternate, corresponding, and co-interior angles formed by transversals on parallel lines; calculating interior and exterior angles of polygons (triangles up to decagons); and applying geometric theorems.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Geometric reasoning, deductive spatial logic, angle measurement fluency, and polygon structural analysis

subStrands.title: 3D Solids, Polyhedra Nets & Cartesian Coordinates
subStrands.description: Analyzing faces, edges, and vertices of polyhedra using Euler's formula (F + V - E = 2); identifying and drawing nets of prisms, pyramids, and cylinders; plotting and reading coordinates in the first quadrant of the Cartesian plane; and calculating geometric distance and area on grids.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Spatial visualization, geometric abstraction, coordinate fluency, and mathematical modeling

subStrands.title: Data Handling, Probability & Linear Algebraic Equations
subStrands.description: Collecting and presenting data via tables, bar graphs, and pie charts; computing measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and range; determining experimental and theoretical probability; and forming and solving linear algebraic equations (ax + b = c).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Statistical reasoning, data interpretation, probability assessment, algebraic formulation, and KPSEA capstone problem solving

subStrands.title: Digital Learning, Cyber Ethics & Language Structures
subStrands.description: Using appropriate vocabulary on digital technology and Internet safety; mastering the Present Perfect Continuous tense (have/has been + verb-ing); identifying polite phone/online etiquette; and analyzing cyber safety scenarios in Kenyan schools.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Digital literacy, communicative competence, ethical critical thinking, and linguistic accuracy in modern communication

subStrands.title: Environmental Conservation, Tree Growing & Conditional Sentences
subStrands.description: Reading and comprehending persuasive texts on environmental protection, Mau Forest conservation, and Wangari Maathai's legacy; forming Conditional Sentences Type 1 (probable condition) and Type 2 (hypothetical condition); expanding ecological vocabulary; and mastering word formation with prefixes and suffixes.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Environmental stewardship, analytical reading, inferential comprehension, and mastery of hypothetical sentence structures

subStrands.title: Health, Balanced Diet, Wellness & Modal Verbs of Obligation
subStrands.description: Discussing balanced nutrition and traditional Kenyan indigenous foods; identifying causes and prevention of lifestyle and communicable diseases; mastering modal auxiliaries of obligation, advice, permission, and necessity (must, should, ought to, have to, need to); and exploring health idioms and vocabulary.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Health literacy, nutritional awareness, empathetic dialogue, and modal auxiliary grammatical fluency

subStrands.title: Tourism, Wildlife Conservation, National Parks & Order of Adjectives
subStrands.description: Reading descriptive travelogues and brochures exploring Kenya's iconic national parks (Amboseli, Tsavo, Maasai Mara, Lake Nakuru); understanding degrees of comparison (comparative and superlative); mastering the grammatical royal order of cumulative adjectives (Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Colour, Origin, Material, Purpose); and expanding wildlife and ecotourism vocabulary.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ecotourism appreciation, descriptive reading comprehension, wildlife stewardship, and syntactical adjective mastery

subStrands.title: Financial Literacy, Trade, Mobile Money & Advanced Conjunctions
subStrands.description: Developing financial vocabulary (budgeting, mobile money, investment, savings); practicing polite business negotiation and commercial etiquette; and mastering complex conjunctions of concession, contrast, reason, and condition (although, despite, in spite of, whereas, provided that).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Financial literacy, consumer discernment, commercial negotiation, and complex syntactic subordination

subStrands.title: Transport, Road Safety, Highway Code & Prepositions of Movement
subStrands.description: Engaging in structured debates on transport infrastructure (SGR vs road haulage); reading and applying the Highway Code and road safety rules; mastering prepositions of movement, place, and direction (through, across, along, into); and using travel phrasal verbs.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Civic safety consciousness, persuasive oral argumentation, spatial prepositional fluency, and travel register mastery

subStrands.title: Agriculture, Agro-Processing, Horticultural Exports & Active/Passive Voice
subStrands.description: Exploring modern agricultural enterprise (Hass avocado exports, Kericho tea processing, drip irrigation, value addition); writing procedural manuals and agribusiness logs; mastering structural transformations between Active and Passive Voice across various tenses; and applying agent phrases appropriately.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Agribusiness technical vocabulary, procedural sequence writing, and active-to-passive voice grammatical transformations

subStrands.title: Governance, Child Rights (Kenyan Constitution 2010) & Reported Speech
subStrands.description: Understanding democratic governance, devolution, Chapter Six integrity, and children's rights under Article 53 of the Constitution of Kenya 2010; mastering quotation mark punctuation in direct speech; and executing accurate transformations into indirect (reported) speech with grammatical backshifting and pronoun adjustments.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Civic literacy, child advocacy communication, direct quotation mechanics, and reported speech syntactic mastery

subStrands.title: Sports, Talent Development, National Heroes & Adverbs
subStrands.description: Celebrating Kenyan athletic legends (Eliud Kipchoge, Faith Kipyegon), motor sports, and grassroots academies; analyzing live sports commentary and athletic idioms; and mastering the syntactic classification and comparative forms of adverbs of manner, degree, frequency, time, and place.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Sports commentary listening comprehension, athletic values reflection, and versatile adverbial syntactic usage

subStrands.title: Cultural Heritage, Poetry, Figurative Language & KPSEA Composition
subStrands.description: Appreciating Kenyan oral traditions, indigenous folktales, proverbs, and poetry stanzas; analyzing figurative devices including similes, metaphors, personification, and alliteration; and applying master narrative composition architecture, "show don't tell" sensory descriptions, and proofreading for KPSEA national examination excellence.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Figurative and poetic analysis, narrative plot staging, vivid sensory composition writing, and KPSEA capstone mastery

subStrands.title: Usalama Mtandaoni, Mawasiliano ya Kidijitali & Ngeli za A-WA, KI-VI na LI-YA
subStrands.description: Kujenga msamiati wa teknohama na usalama mtandaoni (tovuti, nywila, mtandao, barua pepe); stadi za majadiliano na ushauri kuhusu matumizi salama ya vifaa vya kidijitali; na upatanisho sahihi wa kisarufi katika ngeli za A-WA, KI-VI na LI-YA.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ujuzi wa kidijitali, maadili ya mtandao, na umilisi wa upatanisho wa kisarufi katika ngeli za msingi

subStrands.title: Uhifadhi wa Mazingira, Misitu ya Mau & Ngeli za U-I, U-YA, YA-YA na I-ZI
subStrands.description: Kusoma makala kuhusu uhifadhi wa vyanzo vya maji (Mnara wa Mau, Mlima Kenya), kupanda miti na kuzuia mmomonyoko wa udongo; msamiati wa ikolojia na mazingira; na kutawala upatanisho wa ngeli za U-I, U-YA, YA-YA na I-ZI.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa makala ya ikolojia, uzalendo wa kimazingira, na umilisi wa ngeli za mimea, viowevu na nomino za I-ZI

subStrands.title: Lishe Bora, Afya ya Jamii & Ngeli za Nomino (I-I, U-U, KU na PA-MU-KU)
subStrands.description: Kusikiliza maelekezo ya wataalamu wa afya kuhusu mlo kamili wa kienyeji (managu, sukumawiki, ugali wa mtama), chanjo na kinga maradhi; msamiati wa afya na matibabu; na kutawala upatanisho wa ngeli za I-I, U-U, KU na ngeli za mahali (PA-MU-KU).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Uelewa wa mazungumzo ya afya na lishe, msamiati wa udaktari wa kimsingi, na umilisi wa ngeli za mahali na vitenzi-jina

subStrands.title: Utalii wa Ndani, Wanyamapori & Nyakati na Hali (LI, NA, TA, ME)
subStrands.description: Kusoma makala ya kitalii katika Hifadhi za Wanyamapori za Maasai Mara, Amboseli na Tsavo; msamiati wa utalii na wanyamapori; na kutawala nyakati kuu za kisarufi (Uliopita "LI", Uliopo "NA", Ujao "TA") na Hali Timilifu ("ME") pamoja na ukanushaji wake.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Msamiati wa kitalii, uzalendo wa maliasili, na matumizi fasaha ya viambishi vya nyakati na hali timilifu

subStrands.title: Elimu ya Kifedha, Biashara, M-Pesa & Hali za Masharti (KI, NGE, NGALI)
subStrands.description: Kujenga msamiati wa kibiashara, benki na huduma za pesa kwa njia ya simu (M-Pesa, akiba, bajeti, hisa); mazungumzo ya ununuzi na upatano wa bei sokoni; na kutawala hali za masharti ya uwezekano (KI na NGE) na masharti yasiyowezekana tena (NGALI) pamoja na ukanushaji wake.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa shughuli za kiuchumi, nidhamu ya kifedha, na umilisi wa miundo ya masharti katika sentensi changamano

subStrands.title: Usalama Barabarani, Usafiri wa SGR & Mnyambuliko wa Vitenzi
subStrands.description: Kujifunza sheria za usalama barabarani (ishara za trafiki, kivukio cha watembea kwa miguu, mikanda ya usalama) na usafiri wa kisasa wa reli ya SGR (Madaraka Express); na kutawala kauli za mnyambuliko wa vitenzi (Kutenda, Kutendwa, Kutendea, Kutendesha, Kutendana, Kutendeka).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa usalama wa usafiri, uzingatiaji wa sheria za trafiki, na umilisi wa mnyambuliko na kauli za vitenzi

subStrands.title: Kilimo Biashara, Ufugaji Bora & Vitate, Vitateka, Visawe na Vinyume
subStrands.description: Kujifunza msamiati wa kilimo biashara (ukulima wa parachichi za Hass, majani chai, umwagiliaji, kilimo cha mseto, ufugaji wa ng'ombe wa maziwa); na kubobea katika upambanuzi wa vitate (maneno yenye matamshi yanayotatanisha), vitateka/vitatanishi, visawe (maneno yenye maana sawa), na vinyume vya maneno.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa kilimo biashara na uzalishaji, na umilisi wa kiisimu wa vitate, visawe na vinyume

subStrands.title: Utawala Bora, Haki za Watoto & Kauli Halisi na Kauli Taarifa
subStrands.description: Kujifunza misingi ya ugatuzi, uongozi na uadilifu (Sura ya Sita ya Katiba), na haki za kimsingi za mtoto (Kifungu cha 53 cha Katiba ya Kenya 2010); na kutawala ubadilishaji wa sentensi kutoka Kauli Halisi (Direct Speech) hadi Kauli Taarifa (Indirect Speech) na kubadilisha viwakilishi vya nafsi na vielezi vya wakati na mahali.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Ufahamu wa katiba na uraia mwema, na umilisi wa kubadilisha kauli halisi kuwa kauli taarifa

subStrands.title: Michezo, Talanta za Kitaifa, Ushujaa & Vielezi na Vihusishi
subStrands.description: Kusifu mashujaa wa riadha wa Kenya (Eliud Kipchoge, Faith Kipyegon), mashindano ya Safari Rally na michezo ya shule; lugha ya matangazo ya michezo na misemo ya michezo; na kutawala vielezi vya namna, mahali, wakati, idadi/kiasi pamoja na vihusishi.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Uthamini wa talanta na ushujaa wa kitaifa, ufasaha wa utangazaji michezo, na umilisi wa vielezi na vihusishi

subStrands.title: Fasihi Simulizi, Ushairi & Utunzi wa Insha za KPSEA
subStrands.description: Kujifunza tanzu za fasihi simulizi (hadithi za wanyama, soga, methali, vitendawili, ushairi wa watoto); tamathali za usemi (tashbihi, sitiari, tashhisi, tanakali za sauti); na mbinu za kiufundi za uandishi wa insha za KPSEA (mwanzo unaovutia, mtiririko wa aya, kuonyesha badala ya kueleza, na uhariri).
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Uchambuzi wa fasihi simulizi na ushairi, utumiaji wa tamathali za usemi, na umilisi wa kiwango cha juu wa insha za KPSEA

subStrands.title: Classification of Living Things: Vertebrates and Invertebrates
subStrands.description: Observing, classifying, and comparing animals based on the presence of a vertebral column; examining the characteristics of the 5 vertebrate classes (mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish); exploring major invertebrate groups (insects, arachnids, crustaceans, molluscs, worms); and understanding ecological roles in Kenyan habitats.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Biological classification skills, scientific dichotomous discernment, comparative anatomy observation, and environmental conservation awareness

subStrands.title: Reproduction in Plants: Flower Anatomy, Pollination & Seed Dispersal
subStrands.description: Investigating the anatomy and physiology of a complete flower (sepals, petals, stamen, pistil/carpel); comparing self-pollination with cross-pollination and insect vs wind adaptations; tracing fertilization and zygote formation; and analyzing agents and adaptive features of fruit and seed dispersal in Kenyan flora.
subStrands.cbeCompetency: Botanical anatomical investigation, pollination mechanics analysis, and seed dispersal adaptation evaluation

subStrands.name: The Human Circulatory System
subStrands.description: Explore the structure and functions of the heart, blood vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries), and components of blood (plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets) alongside heart health and exercise.
competencies: Identify parts of the human heart and their functions in pumping blood
Differentiate between arteries, veins, and capillaries
Describe the four main components of blood and their roles in the body
Explain the impact of physical exercise and healthy nutrition on circulatory health

subStrands.name: The Human Excretory System
