questions.socraticHint: Which item is shaped like a rectangle with sharp corners?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School exercise books and textbooks.

questions.prompt: Match each type of straight line with its real-life example:

matchingPairs.rightText: The bottom edge of the blackboard
The sloping ramp of a school wheelchair path

questions.explanation: Vertical stands up; horizontal lies flat; slanting slopes at an angle.
questions.socraticHint: Think about which one goes up, which lies flat, and which slopes.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Accessibility ramps and structures in modern Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: True or False: A straight line can bend in the middle like a snake.
questions.storyScenario: Defining what is NOT a straight line.
questions.explanation: False! A line that bends or wiggles is a curved line, not a straight line.
questions.socraticHint: If a line bends, can you draw it along a straight ruler?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Distinguishing straight and curved lines is a fundamental CBC milestone.

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for drawing a straight line with a ruler in correct order:

options.text: Place the ruler flat and press down firmly with your fingers
Place your sharp pencil tip against the straight edge at the start point
Slide the pencil smoothly along the edge without moving the ruler
Lift the ruler to inspect your clean, straight line

questions.explanation: Hold ruler firm, position pencil, slide along edge, inspect result.
questions.socraticHint: What happens if you move the pencil before holding down the ruler?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fine motor skills and geometric drawing practice.

questions.prompt: Baraka is drawing a picture of a traditional hut. The walls are made of upright straight lines, and the flat ground is a straight line. What kinds of straight lines did he use?

options.text: Vertical lines for the walls and a horizontal line for the ground

questions.explanation: Upright walls are vertical lines; flat ground is a horizontal line.
questions.socraticHint: Upright = vertical. Flat = horizontal.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Architectural drawing in CBC art and mathematics.

questions.prompt: A straight line going from side to side is called a [BLANK] line.
questions.explanation: A line extending side to side is horizontal.
questions.socraticHint: Starts with "h". Like the horizon where the sun rises.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Observing the flat horizon across the Rift Valley.

questions.prompt: How many straight sides does a triangle have?
questions.storyScenario: Counting straight lines in basic polygons.
questions.explanation: A triangle is made of exactly 3 straight lines connected at 3 corners.
questions.socraticHint: "Tri" means three (like a tricycle has 3 wheels).
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Samosas and triangular road hazard signs.

questions.prompt: On a football pitch, the white goalposts stand straight up, while the crossbar lies flat across the top. What two types of straight lines form the goal?

options.text: Vertical goalposts and a horizontal crossbar

questions.explanation: The upright posts are vertical, and the crossbar connecting them across the top is horizontal.
questions.socraticHint: Which part stands up, and which part lies flat across the top?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Football pitch goalposts in school sports grounds.

questions.prompt: Which of the following lines bends smoothly without any sharp corners?
questions.explanation: A curved line bends smoothly without angles or corners.
questions.socraticHint: Which line bends like a rainbow or a smiling mouth?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Bending lines in African pottery and basket motifs.

questions.prompt: Which everyday object has a curved boundary line?
questions.storyScenario: Finding curved lines in natural and manufactured objects.

options.text: The circular rim of a teacup
The edge of an exercise book

questions.explanation: The rim of a teacup is a continuous smooth circle, which is a curved line.
questions.socraticHint: Which object is round like a wheel or coin?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Teacups and calabashes used in Kenyan homes.

questions.prompt: True or False: A rainbow in the sky after rain forms a beautiful curved line arching over the hills.
questions.explanation: True! Rainbows form an arch, which is a classic curved line in nature.
questions.socraticHint: Does a rainbow look like a straight wooden ruler or a graceful bending arch?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Rainbows over the Rift Valley and Mount Kenya after afternoon showers.

questions.prompt: A bicycle wheel has a round boundary line that forms a [BLANK] shape.
questions.explanation: A bicycle wheel forms a circle (duara), which is a closed curved line.
questions.socraticHint: What shape is completely round like a coin or chapati?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Bicycles (boda bodas) are common transport in Kenyan towns.

questions.prompt: What happens when you bend a flexible green tree twig gently with your hands?

options.text: It turns into a metal ruler
It bends from a straight line into a curved line

questions.explanation: Bending a straight twig turns it into a curved line or arch.
questions.socraticHint: Think about how curved roof frames of huts are made from bent twigs.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Using flexible tree branches to build structures and traps.

questions.prompt: Match each object with the primary type of line that defines it:

matchingPairs.leftText: A crescent moon in the night sky
A river winding through a valley

questions.explanation: Crescent moon is curved; needle is straight; winding river is wavy curved.
questions.socraticHint: Does a needle bend? Does a winding river stay straight?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Geography of Kenyan rivers winding toward lakes and the ocean.

questions.prompt: True or False: You can draw a curved line using only a standard straight ruler without moving the ruler.
questions.explanation: False! A straight ruler only creates straight lines. To draw curves, you use round templates or freehand drawing.
questions.socraticHint: Can a rigid straight ruler bend to draw a round circle?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Using compasses and coin templates to draw circles.

questions.prompt: Arrange these lines in order from completely straight to most curved/looped:

options.text: A gentle curve like a smiling mouth
A deep arch like a rainbow

questions.explanation: Straight line has zero curve, followed by gentle curve, deep arch, and a full circular loop.
questions.socraticHint: Start with the line that has no bend at all.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Curvature progression in design and typography.

questions.prompt: Amina is designing a greeting card. She draws a heart for her mother. What kinds of lines did she use to draw the heart?

options.text: Curved lines at the top that meet in straight lines at the point

questions.explanation: A heart shape features two rounded lobes (curved lines) at the top that taper to a bottom point.
questions.socraticHint: Look at the rounded top of a heart: are they straight or curved?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Creative arts drawing exercises in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Ocean waves on the beach create [BLANK] lines that roll up and down.
questions.explanation: Ocean waves create curved or wavy lines.
questions.socraticHint: Do rolling waves look straight or curved?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Coastal geography of Mombasa, Malindi, and Lamu.

questions.prompt: Which letter of the English alphabet is formed ONLY by curved lines?
questions.explanation: The letter O is a continuous closed curved line. L, T, and H are formed by straight lines.
questions.socraticHint: Which letter is round like a ring and has no straight parts?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Cross-curricular linkage between English alphabet writing and geometry.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: A pottery artisan in Voi is decorating a clay water pot. Around the rim, he presses a straight horizontal line. Below that, he draws 6 repeating wave curves. If each wave curve is 5 cm wide, what is the total distance covered by the 6 wave curves?
questions.explanation: 6 wave curves × 5 cm width each = 30 cm in total!
questions.socraticHint: Multiply 6 by 5 cm: 6 × 5 = ?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional pottery in Taita Taveta and western Kenya.

questions.prompt: How many corners does a circle have?
questions.explanation: A circle has zero sharp corners because it is formed by one smooth continuous curved line.
questions.socraticHint: Look at a coin or chapati: do you see any pointy sharp corners?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Coins and chapati round shapes in daily life.

questions.prompt: A 2D flat shape has 4 straight sides and 4 corners, and its opposite sides are equal in length. What shape is it?
questions.explanation: A rectangle has 4 straight sides and 4 corners with equal opposite sides.
questions.socraticHint: What shape is a standard classroom door or textbook?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom doors, blackboards, and desks are rectangles.

questions.prompt: True or False: A triangle has 3 straight sides and 3 corners.
questions.explanation: True! Every triangle has exactly 3 sides and 3 corners.
questions.socraticHint: Count the sides of a triangle: 1, 2, 3!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Triangle road signs warning motorists of school crossings.

questions.prompt: A chicken egg viewed from the front has an elongated curved shape called an [BLANK].
questions.blankTemplate: It has an elongated curved shape called an [BLANK].
questions.explanation: An egg shape is called an oval.
questions.socraticHint: Starts with the letter "o". Stretched circle.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Poultry egg shapes in science and farming.

questions.prompt: Which shape has all 4 sides of EXACTLY equal length?
questions.explanation: A square is a special rectangle where all 4 sides are exactly equal in length.
questions.socraticHint: A chessboard or square floor tile has 4 sides that are all identical.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Square ceramic floor tiles in modern homes.

questions.prompt: Match each 2D shape to the number of corners it possesses:
questions.explanation: Triangle has 3 corners; rectangle has 4 corners; circle has 0 corners.
questions.socraticHint: Count the sharp vertices on each shape.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Geometry manipulatives cut from recycled cardboard.

questions.prompt: True or False: Both a circle and an oval have zero straight sides.
questions.explanation: True! Circles and ovals are both bounded entirely by curved lines, so they have zero straight sides.
questions.socraticHint: Can you find any straight edges on a coin or an egg?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Natural curved shapes in Kenyan flora and fauna.

questions.prompt: Arrange these shapes in order of the number of sides they have, from least to most sides:
questions.explanation: Circle has 0 sides, triangle has 3 sides, rectangle has 4 sides.
questions.socraticHint: Order by the numbers: 0, 3, 4.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Logical sorting and classification skills.

questions.prompt: Otieno eats a samosa at break time. The samosa has 3 straight edges and 3 pointy corners. What 2D shape does the samosa represent?
questions.explanation: A 3-sided, 3-cornered shape is a triangle.
questions.socraticHint: How many sides does the samosa have? Three!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Samosas (sambusa) are a popular snack in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has [BLANK] corners.
questions.explanation: A rectangle has 4 corners.
questions.socraticHint: Count the 4 corners of a sheet of paper or door.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Identifying features of classroom objects.

questions.prompt: Which shape is shown on the Kenyan 20-shilling coin?
questions.explanation: All standard circulating Kenyan coins are circular.
questions.socraticHint: What shape is a round coin that can roll across a desk?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan currency coins.

questions.prompt: Pupils trace the bottom of a glue stick onto paper. The trace has no corners and bends evenly all around. What shape did they produce?
questions.storyScenario: Tracing everyday 3D objects to create 2D shapes.
questions.explanation: The cylindrical bottom of a glue bottle traces out a circular 2D shape.
questions.socraticHint: The bottom of a glue stick or bottle is round.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom art activities using everyday objects as stencils.

questions.prompt: Look at this repeating shape pattern: Triangle, Circle, Triangle, Circle, Triangle, ___? What shape comes next?
questions.explanation: The rule is alternating Triangle, Circle. After Triangle, the next shape must be Circle.
questions.socraticHint: Say the pattern out loud: Triangle, Circle, Triangle, Circle, Triangle, ...?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Alternating borders on traditional lesos (kangas).

questions.prompt: What comes next in this pattern: Rectangle, Rectangle, Circle, Rectangle, Rectangle, Circle, Rectangle, Rectangle, ___?
questions.explanation: The repeating block is "Rectangle, Rectangle, Circle". After two rectangles, Circle comes next.
questions.socraticHint: Every time there are 2 rectangles, what single shape follows them?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Beadwork patterns on Maasai wristbands.

questions.prompt: True or False: In a mathematical pattern, shapes repeat according to a predictable rule.
questions.explanation: True! A pattern must have an orderly, predictable repeating rule.
questions.socraticHint: If shapes were randomly scrambled with no order, would it be a pattern?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Order and harmony in traditional Kenyan craft designs.

questions.prompt: Complete the number and shape pattern: 1 Circle, 2 Circles, 3 Circles, [BLANK] Circles.
questions.explanation: The number of circles increases by 1 each time: 1, 2, 3, 4.
questions.socraticHint: Count: 1, 2, 3, ... what is the next counting number?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Growing bead necklaces in cultural ornamentation.

questions.prompt: Look at the color pattern on a beaded belt: Red, Green, Black, Red, Green, Black, Red, Green, ___? What color is missing?
questions.explanation: The core repeating block is Red, Green, Black. After Red and Green, Black comes next.
questions.socraticHint: Say the repeating group: Red, Green, Black! What finishes the group?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: National flag colors in beadwork and patriotic symbols.

questions.prompt: Match each pattern to its repeating rule block:
questions.explanation: Identifies the repeating core element (unit) of each pattern.
questions.socraticHint: Find the smallest group of shapes that repeats again and again.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Weaving patterns in ciondo sisal baskets.

questions.prompt: True or False: If a tile pattern is Triangle, Square, Triangle, Square, then the 7th shape in the pattern will be a Triangle.
questions.explanation: True! Odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th) are Triangles, and even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th) are Squares. So the 7th shape is a Triangle.
questions.socraticHint: Count: 1(Tri), 2(Sq), 3(Tri), 4(Sq), 5(Tri), 6(Sq), 7(?)
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mathematical reasoning in architectural paving patterns.

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for designing and printing a repeating pattern on fabric:

options.text: Carve a potato or wooden block with a single shape (e.g., triangle)
Press the block repeatedly in equal spaces along the fabric border
Let the repeating fabric print dry completely

questions.explanation: Carve block, dip paint, press repeatedly in sequence, dry fabric.
questions.socraticHint: What must you make first before you can dip it into paint?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Block printing using potatoes and leaves in CBC art and craft.

questions.prompt: Halima is weaving a border for a table mat in Mombasa. Her pattern rule is: Red circle, Blue circle, Yellow circle. She has made 4 complete repeating sets. How many circles has she woven in total?
questions.storyScenario: Calculating items in a repeating pattern.
questions.explanation: Each set has 3 circles. 4 sets × 3 circles = 12 circles in total.
questions.socraticHint: Multiply 4 sets by 3 circles: 4 × 3 = ?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional mat weaving (jamvi) on the Kenyan coast.

questions.prompt: Look at the shape pattern: Square, Oval, Square, Oval, Square, [BLANK].
questions.explanation: After Square comes Oval in this alternating pattern.
questions.socraticHint: Every Square is followed by which shape?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pattern recognition in woven floor mats.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a repeating pattern?

options.text: Red, Blue, Red, Blue, Red, Blue
Circle, Triangle, Rectangle, Circle, Circle, Triangle (random order)
Circle, Square, Circle, Square, Circle, Square
Triangle, Triangle, Circle, Triangle, Triangle, Circle

questions.explanation: Option 1 has random, irregular shapes without a consistent repeating rule.
questions.socraticHint: Which sequence breaks the rules and looks disordered?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Discerning pattern order from disorder.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: A school art team in Kitui paints a mural wall with 8 repeating panels. Each panel contains 2 rectangles and 3 triangles. How many total triangles are painted on the mural wall?
questions.storyScenario: Multi-step pattern calculation combining geometry and multiplication.
questions.explanation: 8 panels × 3 triangles per panel = 24 triangles in total!
questions.socraticHint: Multiply 8 panels by 3 triangles: 8 × 3 = ?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School perimeter wall murals depicting national heritage and education themes.

questions.prompt: Which word begins with the consonant blend "bl"?
questions.storyScenario: Listening for initial blends in English.
questions.explanation: The word "black" begins with the /bl/ blend. "Clock" begins with /cl/, "flag" with /fl/, and "plum" with /pl/.
questions.socraticHint: Listen to the first two letters: b + l make /bl/. Which word has b and l together at the start?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The black stripe on the Kenyan national flag represents the people of Kenya.

questions.prompt: Listen to this sentence: "The children ____ their hands happily." Which word best completes the sentence with the "cl" blend?
questions.explanation: "Clap" begins with the /cl/ blend (c + l). Children clap their hands to show joy.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with the letters "cl"? (c + l = cl-).
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Clapping rhythmically during music and poetry festivals.

questions.prompt: True or False: In a consonant blend like "fl" in "flower", you can clearly hear both the /f/ and the /l/ sounds.
questions.explanation: True! In a consonant blend, both consonant sounds are pronounced smoothly together.
questions.socraticHint: Say "flower" slowly: do your lips make the /f/ sound and your tongue touch the roof of your mouth for /l/?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Bright bougainvillea flowers growing along school fences in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A person who plants crops and trees on a shamba will [BLANK] seeds in tidy rows. (plant / clock / sleep)
questions.blankTemplate: They will [BLANK] seeds in tidy rows.
questions.explanation: "Plant" begins with the /pl/ blend (p + l). Farmers plant seeds in fertile soil.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "pl" and means putting seeds into the soil?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tree planting and kitchen garden agriculture in Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: Which word has the "gl" consonant blend?
questions.explanation: "Glass" begins with the /gl/ blend (g + l).
questions.socraticHint: Look for the word starting with the letters "g" and "l".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Drinking a clean glass of boiled water for good health.

questions.prompt: Match each initial blend to the correct word:
questions.explanation: bl- matches blanket; fl- matches flag; sl- matches slow.
questions.socraticHint: Look at the first two letters of each word to find its blend pair.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Maasai shuka blankets and the Kenyan national flag.

questions.prompt: True or False: The word "slide" begins with the same blend sound as "spoon".
questions.explanation: False! "Slide" begins with /sl/ (s + l), while "spoon" begins with /sp/ (s + p).
questions.socraticHint: Say both words aloud: sl-ide vs sp-oon. Do you hear an "l" sound in spoon?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Playground equipment (slides and swings) in school compounds.

questions.prompt: Arrange these words in alphabetical order by their initial blend (bl, cl, fl, pl):
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: b (Blue), c (Clean), f (Fly), p (Play).
questions.socraticHint: Look at the very first letter of each word: b, c, f, p. Which comes first in the ABC alphabet?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dictionary lookup skills introduced in Grade 3 English.

questions.prompt: Teacher Mary writes: "The ____ sailed smoothly across the calm blue lake." Which word best fits the sentence with the "fl" blend?
questions.explanation: "Flamingo" begins with /fl/ and is a famous water bird found on Lake Nakuru.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "fl" and names a pink bird that wades in Rift Valley lakes?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Lesser flamingos on Lake Nakuru and Lake Bogoria.

questions.prompt: When pupils enter the school room quietly in the morning, we say they are entering their [BLANK]. (class / black / fly)
questions.explanation: "Class" starts with /cl/ (c + l).
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "cl" and names the room where you learn?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Entering the Grade 3 classroom ready to learn.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the "sl" blend?
questions.explanation: "Sleep" begins with the /sl/ blend (s + l).
questions.socraticHint: Look for the word that starts with "s" and "l" together.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Healthy sleep habits taught in hygiene lessons.

questions.prompt: Wanjiku read this tongue twister: "Blind Brenda blew big black bubbles." What is the main consonant blend repeated in this sentence?
questions.storyScenario: Analyzing tongue twisters in oral language.
questions.explanation: "Blind", "blew", and "black" all repeat the /bl/ blend sound.
questions.socraticHint: What letters start the words Blind, blew, and black?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Oral language tongue twisters develop articulation in English.

questions.prompt: What polite phrase should you say when you accidentally step on someone's foot in a crowded matatu?
questions.explanation: Saying "I am sorry" shows that you apologize for an accidental mistake.
questions.socraticHint: What word do we use to apologize when we make a mistake?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Politeness and peaceful co-existence in public vehicles.

questions.prompt: What polite word should you always include when asking a teacher or friend for help?
questions.explanation: "Please" is the magic courtesy word used when making any request.
questions.socraticHint: What magic polite word turns a demand into a courteous request?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Respectful classroom etiquette in Kenyan primary schools.

questions.prompt: True or False: Saying "Thank you" when someone gives you a gift or lends you a pencil is a sign of good manners.
questions.explanation: True! Saying "Thank you" shows appreciation and good manners.
questions.socraticHint: Does showing gratitude make the giver feel respected and happy?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Cultivating values of gratitude and appreciation under CBC.

questions.prompt: When you want to pass between two teachers talking in the corridor, you should say, "[BLANK] me, please."
questions.explanation: We say "Excuse me" to politely get attention or pass through a crowded space.
questions.socraticHint: Which polite word completes "______ me, please"? In Swahili it is "Samahani".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Showing respect to teachers and elders in school.

questions.prompt: When your grandmother hands you a sweet ripe banana, what is the best response?
questions.explanation: Saying "Thank you, grandmother" expresses warmth and sincere gratitude.
questions.socraticHint: Which response shows appreciation for the fruit she gave you?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Respect for grandparents (nyanya / guka) in Kenyan culture.

questions.prompt: Match each situation to the most appropriate polite expression:
questions.storyScenario: Matching social contexts to courtesy phrases.

matchingPairs.leftText: You want to borrow a rubber eraser from a desk mate
You need to ask the teacher a question while she is writing
You accidentally knock over someone's water bottle
matchingPairs.rightText: "I am very sorry, let me help you pick it up."

questions.explanation: Borrowing uses "Please"; getting attention uses "Excuse me"; accidental spill uses "I am sorry".
questions.socraticHint: Think about whether you are asking, getting attention, or apologizing.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Promoting a peaceful, respectful school learning environment.

questions.prompt: True or False: Shouting loudly across the classroom to get someone's attention is considered polite behavior.
questions.explanation: False! Shouting is disruptive. You should raise your hand or walk quietly and speak in a polite voice.
questions.socraticHint: Does shouting make the classroom noisy and disturb other learners?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom discipline and self-regulation under CBC.

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for greeting a guest visiting your home in proper polite order:

options.text: Open the door with a warm smile
Say: "Good afternoon, welcome to our home."
Offer the guest a clean chair to sit down
Call your parents to inform them the guest has arrived

questions.explanation: Smile and open door, greet warmly, offer a seat, notify parents.
questions.socraticHint: What do you say first before offering a seat?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan hospitality (ukarimu) welcomed in all homes.

questions.prompt: Baraka is at the community water tap. An elderly grandmother arrives carrying a heavy water bucket. What is the most respectful thing for Baraka to say and do?
questions.storyScenario: Community service and respect for senior citizens.

options.text: Say: "Good morning, Shosho. Please let me help you fill your bucket first."
Pretend he does not see her and push in front
Tell her to wait until all children have finished

questions.explanation: Offering assistance and polite greeting to elderly neighbours demonstrates CBC core values of respect and love.
questions.socraticHint: Which action shows kindness and respect to an elder?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Honouring elders (wazee) in community chores.

questions.prompt: When someone says "Thank you" to you, the polite reply is "You are [BLANK]." (welcome / sorry / please)
questions.explanation: The standard courteous response to "Thank you" is "You are welcome."
questions.socraticHint: In Swahili we say "Karibu". What is the English phrase: "You are ______"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Everyday courteous exchanges in English and Swahili.

questions.prompt: How should you greet your school headteacher in the morning?
questions.explanation: "Good morning, Sir" or "Good morning, Madam" is the standard respectful school greeting.
questions.socraticHint: Which greeting shows formal respect to the head of the school?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Respectful address for school leaders in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Amina wants to borrow a coloured pencil, ask the teacher permission to sharpen it, and thank her friend when returning it. Which sequence of polite phrases should she use in order?

options.text: "Please may I borrow your pencil?" -> "Excuse me, Teacher, may I sharpen it?" -> "Thank you for sharing with me."
"Give me your pencil" -> "I am sharpening it" -> "Here take it back"

questions.explanation: First ask politely ("Please"), then request permission ("Excuse me"), and finally express gratitude ("Thank you").
questions.socraticHint: Follow the natural story: asking first (Please), asking teacher (Excuse me), giving it back (Thank you).
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Cultivating well-mannered communication habits among primary pupils.

questions.prompt: Who are the animals or people in a story called?
questions.explanation: The individuals or animals in a story are called characters (wahusika).
questions.socraticHint: In the story of Hare and Elephant, who are Hare and Elephant?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Character analysis in traditional Kenyan folk tales.

questions.prompt: What does the "setting" of a story describe?

options.text: Where and when the story takes place

questions.explanation: The setting (mandhari) describes the place and time of the events.
questions.socraticHint: If a story takes place "in a forest at sunset", what is that called?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Settings in African savannahs, villages, and rivers.

questions.prompt: True or False: In Kenyan folk tales, the Hare (Sungura) often uses clever thinking to overcome much bigger animals.
questions.explanation: True! Sungura is the classic trickster figure who relies on wits rather than brute physical force.
questions.socraticHint: Is Hare big and strong like an elephant, or small and clever?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The trickster figure of Sungura in East African oral literature.

questions.prompt: The good message or value that we learn from a story is called the [BLANK] lesson.
questions.storyScenario: Identifying the purpose of a fable.
questions.explanation: The life lesson taught by a story is called the moral lesson.
questions.socraticHint: Starts with "m". In Swahili it is "funzo".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Passing on societal morals and values through storytelling.

questions.prompt: In the story of Hare's tug-of-war, how was Hare able to challenge Elephant and Hippo at the same time?

options.text: Hare had giant muscles and pulled them both alone
Hare called a tractor to pull the rope
Hare tied opposite ends of the same long rope to Elephant and Hippo without them seeing each other

questions.explanation: Hare tricked Elephant and Hippo into pulling against each other across the river bushes.
questions.socraticHint: Did Hare pull the rope with his paws, or did he trick the two big animals into pulling each other?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Folk tales celebrating intelligence over mere size.

questions.prompt: Match each story element to its correct definition:

matchingPairs.rightText: The people or animals in the tale
The good virtue taught by the tale

questions.explanation: Title is the name; Characters are people/animals; Moral lesson is the virtue taught.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each term to what it tells you about a story.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Literary appreciation competencies in primary English.

questions.prompt: True or False: A good listener interrupts the storyteller frequently while they are speaking.
questions.explanation: False! A good listener listens quietly without interrupting until the speaker finishes.
questions.socraticHint: Can you hear the full story if you keep talking over the teller?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional etiquette during evening storytelling gatherings.

questions.prompt: Arrange the three basic parts of a story in correct sequential order:

options.text: The Beginning (Introduction of characters and setting)
The Middle (The problem or adventure unfolds)
The Ending (The solution and moral lesson)

questions.explanation: All traditional narratives follow Beginning, Middle, and Ending.
questions.socraticHint: How does every story start and finish?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Narrative structure taught in early primary language activities.

questions.prompt: After listening to a folk tale about a greedy hyena who tried to walk down two roads at once to reach two feasts and split in half, what is the moral lesson?
questions.storyScenario: Inferring moral lessons from animal fables.

options.text: Greed leads to loss; be content with what you have
Hyenas are the fastest animals in Kenya
Always go to two parties at the same time
Roads in the village are very wide

questions.explanation: The fable of the greedy hyena (fisi) teaches that greed and trying to take everything leads to foolish disaster.
questions.socraticHint: Why did the hyena suffer? Because of his excessive greed!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The proverb "Fisi alitaka njia mbili" (The hyena wanted two paths).

questions.prompt: To show that you are listening attentively to a speaker, you should maintain polite eye [BLANK]. (contact / sleep / games)
questions.explanation: Looking at the speaker attentively is called maintaining eye contact.
questions.socraticHint: Looking directly at someone's eyes while they speak is called eye _______.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Active listening and respectful engagement in classroom interactions.

questions.prompt: Which question word asks about the LOCATION or place of an event in a story?

questions.explanation: "Where" asks about location or place. ("Who" asks about people; "When" asks about time).
questions.socraticHint: Which word asks: "In which village did the story happen?"
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Basic inquiry questioning (Key Inquiry Questions in CBC).

questions.prompt: During an oral story session, Mwalimu Peter pauses and asks: "What do you think will happen next?" What skill is the teacher asking pupils to practice?

options.text: Making a prediction based on clues

questions.explanation: Guessing what comes next based on story clues is called making a prediction.
questions.socraticHint: When you guess what will happen in the future of the story, what are you doing?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Critical thinking and prediction during shared storytelling.

questions.prompt: Which transition word is best to use when describing the VERY FIRST event in a story?
questions.explanation: "First" introduces the opening event of a narrative.
questions.socraticHint: What word comes before second and third?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Chronological retelling in language lessons.

questions.prompt: Which word signals the END or conclusion of a story?
questions.explanation: "Finally" (or "In the end") indicates the final conclusion of the story.
questions.socraticHint: Which word means "at the very end"? (Similar to "hatimaye" in Swahili).
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Closing phrases of traditional stories.

questions.prompt: True or False: When retelling a story, it is best to jump straight to the ending before telling what happened at the start.
questions.explanation: False! A story should be told in orderly chronological sequence from beginning to end.
questions.socraticHint: Would listeners understand the story if you spoiled the ending first without explaining the beginning?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Logical presentation and clarity in speech.

questions.prompt: Words like "First", "Next", "Then", and "Finally" are called [BLANK] words because they show the order of events.
questions.explanation: They are sequence (or transitional) words that show chronological order.
questions.socraticHint: What word means the order in which things happen? Starts with "s".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Narrative sequencing skills in CBC primary English.

questions.prompt: Look at these three sentences about planting beans: 1. Watered the soil. 2. Dug the holes. 3. Placed the bean seeds in. What is the correct order of these events?

options.text: Watered the soil, placed seeds, then dug holes
Placed seeds, watered soil, then dug holes
Dug the holes, placed the seeds in, then watered the soil

questions.explanation: You must dig the planting hole first, insert the seed, and water the soil afterwards.
questions.socraticHint: Can you put a seed underground before digging a hole in the dirt?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Agricultural project procedures in primary school shambas.

questions.prompt: Match each sequence word to its position in a narrative:
questions.storyScenario: Mapping sequence words to narrative stages.
questions.explanation: First is the start; Next/Then are middle events; Finally is the conclusion.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each transition word to its place in the story flow.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Organized oral storytelling in classroom competitions.

questions.prompt: True or False: Using your own words when retelling a story shows that you understood the story deeply.
questions.explanation: True! Paraphrasing in your own words demonstrates comprehension and language mastery.
questions.socraticHint: Do you need to memorize every single word like a robot, or can you share the story naturally in your own words?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Self-expression and fluency goals under CBC.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of making a cup of tea in correct chronological order:

options.text: Boil water and fresh milk in a sufuria
Add tea leaves and tea spices
Stir in a spoonful of sugar
Pour the hot tea through a sieve into a teacup

questions.explanation: Boil liquid, add tea leaves, add sugar, sieve into cups.
questions.socraticHint: What must you heat up first on the stove?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Making morning chai in Kenyan homes.

questions.prompt: Amina is retelling the fable of Lion and Mouse. She says: "First, Lion caught little Mouse. Next, Mouse begged for mercy and Lion let him go. Then, Lion got trapped in a hunter's rope net. Finally, Mouse gnawed through the ropes and set Lion free!" What was the moral of her story?
questions.storyScenario: Identifying moral message in a retold fable.

options.text: Even small friends can be of great help; kindness is never wasted
Lions should never go into the forest

questions.explanation: The moral of Aesop's Lion and Mouse fable is that even the smallest friend can render great service, so we should treat everyone with kindness.
questions.socraticHint: How did little Mouse repay Lion's kindness?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Virtues of kindness, empathy, and mutual assistance in community life.

questions.prompt: When retelling a story, changing your voice to match different animal characters makes the story more [BLANK] for listeners. (exciting / boring / silent)
questions.blankTemplate: It makes the story more [BLANK] for listeners.
questions.explanation: Vocal expression and pitch modulation make oral storytelling lively and exciting.
questions.socraticHint: Does using deep voices for Elephant and squeaky voices for Hare make the story fun and exciting?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dramatic presentation during annual school drama festivals.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you forget one small detail while retelling a story to your class?

options.text: Stay calm, continue smoothly with the next event, and do not panic
Burst into tears and run out of class

questions.explanation: Staying calm and carrying on confidently is part of developing self-efficacy and resilience.
questions.socraticHint: Which response shows confidence and calm problem solving?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Building learner self-efficacy and public speaking confidence.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: During an inter-class storytelling competition, Otieno tells a story about caring for a wounded baby gazelle in Samburu. Which of the following features proves that Otieno is a Master Storyteller?

options.text: He recited words without pausing for breath
He told only the ending and forgot the beginning
He used clear sequence words (First, Next, Then, Finally), spoke with expressive voice and eye contact, and shared a clear moral lesson about protecting wildlife
He spoke in a quiet whisper while staring only at his shoes

questions.explanation: Master storytelling combines logical sequence, expressive delivery, active listener engagement, and a meaningful moral lesson.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the option that describes all the best presentation qualities combined.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Wildlife conservation and empathy for animals in Kenyan national parks.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the consonant digraph "ch"?
questions.explanation: "Chalk" begins with the /ch/ digraph. Teachers write on the blackboard using chalk.
questions.socraticHint: Which word has the letters "c" and "h" together at the beginning?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: White and coloured chalk used on classroom blackboards.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the /sh/ digraph sound?
questions.explanation: "Shirt" begins with the /sh/ digraph (s + h = /sh/).
questions.socraticHint: Listen for the sound you make when asking for quiet: "shhh". Which word starts with that sound?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School uniform shirts worn by primary pupils.

questions.prompt: True or False: The words "thumb", "three", and "thick" all begin with the "th" digraph.
questions.explanation: True! All three words begin with the letters "th" making the /th/ sound.
questions.socraticHint: Look at the first two letters of thumb, three, and thick. Are they all t and h?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Counting to three on thumbs and fingers.

questions.prompt: A bicycle has two round [BLANK] that turn when you pedal. (wheels / chairs / sheep)
questions.storyScenario: Completing sentences with a "wh" digraph word.
questions.explanation: "Wheels" begins with the /wh/ digraph. Bicycles travel on two wheels.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "wh" and means round turning parts of a bicycle?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Bicycles and boda bodas on Kenyan roads.

questions.prompt: Which word ENDS with the "ch" digraph?
questions.storyScenario: Locating digraphs at the end of words.
questions.explanation: "Bench" ends with the letters "ch" making the /ch/ sound. "Fish" ends with /sh/, and "path" with /th/.
questions.socraticHint: Look at the last two letters of each word: which word ends in -ch?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Wooden benches in school dining halls and churches.

questions.prompt: Match each digraph with the word that contains it:
questions.explanation: ch is in chicken; sh is in shell; wh is in white.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the matching first two letters in each word.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Free-range chickens and coastal seashells in Kenya.

questions.prompt: True or False: In a digraph like "sh", you pronounce the /s/ and /h/ separately as two different sounds.
questions.explanation: False! In a digraph, the two letters team up to make ONE single new sound (/sh/), not two separate sounds.
questions.socraticHint: Do you say "s-h-eep" or do you make one smooth "sh" sound like "sheep"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Understanding phonics foundations in early literacy.

questions.prompt: Arrange these digraph words in alphabetical order by their first letter:
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: c (Chair), s (Shop), t (Think), w (Whistle).
questions.socraticHint: Look at the first letter of each word: c, s, t, w. Put them in A-B-C order.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Organizing class word banks alphabetically.

questions.prompt: Otieno is helping prepare lunch. He uses a metal knife to ____ onions and carrots into small pieces. Which word with the "ch" digraph best fits?
questions.explanation: "Chop" means to cut into pieces with a knife, starting with /ch/.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "ch" and means cutting vegetables?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Chopping vegetables for dinner sukuma wiki.

questions.prompt: A person who catches fish from Lake Victoria is called a [BLANK]man. (fisher / teacher / farmer)
questions.explanation: "Fisherman" contains the /sh/ digraph in "fish".
questions.socraticHint: Look at the word that has "fish" in it: fi____man.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fishermen casting nets on Lake Victoria in Kisumu and Homa Bay.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the "th" digraph sound as in "feather"?
questions.explanation: "Mother" contains the voiced /th/ digraph in the middle (m-o-th-e-r).
questions.socraticHint: Which family word has the letters "th" in the middle?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Family words frequently used in primary reading.

questions.prompt: The sports teacher blows a shiny silver ____ to signal the start of the race. Which word starting with the "wh" digraph completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: A sports teacher blows a "whistle" to start a running race.
questions.socraticHint: What instrument makes a loud shrill sound when you blow into it?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Athletics races during school sports day.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the diphthong sound spelled with "oi"?

questions.socraticHint: Look for the word that has "o" and "i" sitting together in the middle.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan coins used for pocket money.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the /oy/ sound spelled at the END of the word with "oy"?

questions.socraticHint: Which word ends in the letters "o" and "y"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Everyday vocabulary in primary English texts.

questions.prompt: True or False: The words "soil" and "spoil" both have the same "oi" diphthong sound.

questions.socraticHint: Do "soil" and "spoil" rhyme when you say them aloud?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Rich volcanic red soil in the Kenyan highlands.

questions.prompt: The pupils jumped with [BLANK] when their school team won the football trophy. (joy / toy / soy)
questions.explanation: "Joy" means great happiness and ends with the "oy" diphthong.
questions.socraticHint: Which 3-letter word means great happiness and starts with "j"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Celebrations after inter-school football matches.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct spelling of the high-frequency sight word that means "for the reason that"?

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Standard Grade 3 English orthography.

questions.prompt: Match each diphthong word with its meaning:

The top layer of earth where plants grow
An object for children to play with

questions.socraticHint: Think about what you do to water in a kettle vs what you plant crops in.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Boiling drinking water to kill germs and planting crops in good shamba soil.

questions.prompt: True or False: Sight words should be memorized so that you can recognize them instantly without sounding out letter by letter.

questions.explanation: True! Recognizing sight words automatically frees your brain to focus on understanding the story.
questions.socraticHint: Does reading become faster when you know words instantly by sight?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Speed and fluency goals in early grade reading assessments (EGRA).

questions.socraticHint: Start with the capitalized subject "They". What action did they do?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Walking through Kakamega or Mau forest.

questions.socraticHint: We need the word that shows ownership: t-h-e-i-r.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Handwashing before meals is emphasized in school health clubs.

questions.socraticHint: Which word means all the time? Starts with "al-".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Helping parents with domestic duties after school.

questions.prompt: Which word has the /oi/ sound in the middle?

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pointing to places on a map of Kenya.

questions.socraticHint: Check each word carefully: boy (1), coin (2), moist (3), soil (4).
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Storybook sentence analyzing phonetic patterns.

questions.prompt: In the passage "Tsavo Elephant Rescue", where was the baby elephant trapped?
questions.storyScenario: Factual recall from the reading passage.

options.text: In the thick red mud near a dried waterhole
On top of a high baobab tree

questions.explanation: The text states that the calf was stuck deep in the thick red mud near a dried waterhole.
questions.socraticHint: Look back at where the elephant was stuck: was it in mud, a tree, or a room?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tsavo's famous red volcanic soils and dry season waterholes.

questions.prompt: Who came to rescue the baby elephant in the story?
questions.explanation: KWS park rangers heard the calf's distress calls and came to rescue it.
questions.socraticHint: Which organization protects wild animals in Kenyan national parks?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenya Wildlife Service rangers patrolling protected conservation areas.

questions.prompt: True or False: When you reach an exclamation mark (!) in a story, you should read with excitement or surprise.
questions.explanation: True! An exclamation mark shows excitement, danger, or strong emotion.
questions.socraticHint: Does an exclamation mark tell you to sound bored or to show feeling?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Expressive oral reading during English shared reading sessions.

questions.prompt: A baby elephant is called a [BLANK]. (calf / puppy / kitten)
questions.blankTemplate: A baby elephant is called a [BLANK].
questions.explanation: The young of an elephant (as well as cows and giraffes) is called a calf.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "c" and means a young elephant or cow?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan wildlife vocabulary in Lower Primary.

questions.prompt: What did the baby elephant do immediately after being pulled out of the mud?

options.text: It ran joyfully to join its herd

questions.explanation: The story tells that the freed baby ran joyfully back to its mother and herd.
questions.socraticHint: Where do wild animals feel safest after being rescued?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Elephant herds traveling together under a matriarch.

questions.prompt: Match each punctuation mark to the correct reading action:

matchingPairs.rightText: Take a complete breath and stop briefly
Raise your voice pitch at the end

questions.explanation: Full stops mean a full pause; commas are brief pauses; question marks raise voice pitch.
questions.socraticHint: Think about how your voice changes when asking a question versus ending a sentence.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Guided reading practice in Grade 3 literacy corners.

questions.prompt: True or False: KWS rangers rescued the elephant because protecting Kenya's wildlife is important for our country and tourism.
questions.storyScenario: Inferring purpose and values in conservation.
questions.explanation: True! Protecting wildlife preserves biodiversity and supports national heritage and tourism.
questions.socraticHint: Is wildlife conservation an important duty in Kenya?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: National pride in Kenya's wildlife conservation leadership.

questions.prompt: Arrange the events of the elephant rescue in correct chronological order:

options.text: Rangers heard a baby elephant trumpeting in distress
Rangers found the calf stuck deep in the waterhole mud
Rangers tied soft straps around the calf and pulled together
The baby elephant was freed and ran back to its herd

questions.explanation: Heard trumpeting -> found stuck calf -> pulled with straps -> calf ran to herd.
questions.socraticHint: What happened first: hearing the call or pulling the elephant?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Wildlife rescue documentaries and storybooks.

questions.prompt: The story says the baby elephant was "trumpeting in distress". What does the word "distress" mean here?

options.text: Great danger, pain, or need for help

questions.explanation: "Distress" means experiencing danger, extreme worry, or hardship.
questions.socraticHint: The baby was stuck in deep mud and crying out for help. Was it happy or in danger?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Inferring word meanings from emotional context.

questions.prompt: A large group of elephants living and travelling together is called a [BLANK]. (herd / pack / flock)
questions.explanation: A family group of elephants is called a herd.
questions.socraticHint: Which collective noun is used for cattle and elephants? Starts with "h".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Elephant herds grazing in Amboseli and Tsavo.

questions.prompt: Why was the baby elephant in danger at the dried waterhole?

options.text: It could not get out of the mud and might have starved or been attacked by predators
It wanted to take a swim
It was hiding from its mother

questions.explanation: Stuck in mud, wild animal calves cannot feed and are vulnerable to dehydration or predators like lions.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to a wild baby animal left alone in the mud under the hot sun?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Survival challenges during dry seasons in African savannahs.

questions.prompt: What core CBC value did the KWS rangers show by working tirelessly to rescue the elephant calf?

options.text: Responsibility, love, and care for nature

questions.explanation: The rangers showed responsibility, dedication, and compassion for animals.
questions.socraticHint: Which positive values describe helping a helpless creature in trouble?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: CBC core values: Responsibility, Love, Respect.

questions.prompt: In Chebet's report, what is the MAIN IDEA of the passage about harvest day?
questions.storyScenario: Identifying the main idea of a text.

options.text: How Kenyan farming families work together to harvest and store maize
How to buy black school shoes in Nairobi

questions.explanation: The entire passage describes the process of harvesting, drying, and storing maize on the farm.
questions.socraticHint: What is the topic discussed in every paragraph of the story?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Maize farming communities in the Rift Valley.

questions.prompt: How do farmers know that maize is ready to be harvested?

options.text: The green stalks and husks turn golden brown and dry

questions.socraticHint: What colour does dry maize become in the fields before harvesting?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional indicators of crop maturity in Kenyan farming.

questions.prompt: True or False: Maize is an important food in Kenya because it is used to make unga for ugali and uji.

questions.socraticHint: What flour is used to cook hot ugali for dinner?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Ugali as Kenya's national staple food.

questions.prompt: After picking the maize cobs, farmers remove the outer dry leaves called [BLANK]. (husks / roots / bark)
questions.explanation: The outer leafy covering of a maize ear is called a husk.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "h" and refers to the dry outer wrapping of a maize cob?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Peeling maize husks during harvest time in rural homes.

questions.prompt: Why do farmers dry the shelled maize kernels in the hot sun before storing them in bags?

options.text: To change the maize colour to purple
To remove moisture so the maize does not rot or grow mold in storage

questions.explanation: Drying grain thoroughly prevents mold, aflotoxins, and rotting during long-term storage in granaries.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to damp grain kept in closed sacks? It rots!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Spreading grains on large tarpaulins under the sun in Kenyan villages.

questions.prompt: Match each harvest step to its description:

matchingPairs.rightText: Plucking mature ears from the dry stalk
Peeling off the dry outer leaves
Separating the hard seeds from the central cob

questions.explanation: Picking is plucking; de-husking is removing leaves; shelling is removing grain.
questions.socraticHint: Think about the sequence of preparing maize from the stalk to the grain sack.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Communal harvest activities (harambee spirit) in rural Kenya.

questions.prompt: True or False: Storing maize in a dry, well-ventilated granary protects food security for the family throughout the year.
questions.explanation: True! Proper post-harvest storage ensures the family has sufficient nutritious food until the next harvest.
questions.socraticHint: Does having bags of dry grain in the store keep families fed during dry seasons?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional granaries (chika / ikumbi) and modern grain silos in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Arrange the stages of maize crop farming in correct seasonal order:

options.text: Ploughing the shamba and planting seeds when the rains start
Storing dried grain in sacks in the granary

questions.socraticHint: What happens before the crops can grow? Planting!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Annual farming cycles across Kenyan agricultural counties.

questions.prompt: The story mentions that the whole family worked together with laughter and singing during the harvest. What can we infer about how the family felt?

questions.explanation: Singing and laughter are textual clues that show happiness, unity, and celebration.
questions.socraticHint: Do people laugh and sing when they are sad, or when they are happy and grateful?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Harvest songs and communal solidarity across Kenyan communities.

questions.prompt: A building or raised storehouse used to keep harvested grain safe from moisture and pests is called a [BLANK]. (granary / garage / stadium)
questions.explanation: A granary (ghala) is a specialized storage building for grains.
questions.socraticHint: Which word starts with "g" and means a storehouse for grain?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional elevated granaries protect crops from weevils and rodents.

questions.prompt: What happens to the corn kernels after they are taken to the local posho mill?

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Local posho mills (kinu cha kusaga unga) in trading centers.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Chebet wants to write a 1-sentence summary of her report. Which sentence best summarizes the entire text?

"The sun is very hot in Eldoret."

questions.socraticHint: Which sentence mentions the whole farming journey and its value to families?

questions.storyScenario: Reading stories in the school library.
