questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Preparing nutritious sukuma wiki for dinner.

questions.prompt: In autumn, dry brown ______ (leaf) fall from the jacaranda trees.
questions.explanation: Words ending in -f usually change to -ves: leaf -> leaves.
questions.socraticHint: Replace the letter "f" with "ves".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Jacaranda blooming season in Nairobi.

questions.prompt: Kiptoo noticed a mistake on the park signpost: "Welcome to the Mara! Look at the beautifull zebras, lions, and deers." What should be corrected?

options.text: "deers" should be "deer" because deer has no -s in plural

questions.explanation: "Deer" is already plural without adding "s". The sign should read "deer".
questions.socraticHint: Look at the word "deers"—is that a real plural word?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Signboards at Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) gates.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Which sentence has ALL plural nouns spelled 100% correctly?

options.text: The childs saw five mouses running past the two mans.
The childrens saw five mice running past the two men.
The children saw five mouses running past the two mens.
The children saw five mice running past the two men.

questions.explanation: Children, mice, and men are all correct irregular plurals!
questions.socraticHint: Check every single plural noun: child -> children, mouse -> mice, man -> men.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom debates in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Kamau is very good at football. ______ scored two goals yesterday.
questions.explanation: Kamau is a boy, so the singular male subject pronoun is "He".
questions.socraticHint: Which pronoun replaces a single boy or man?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Primary school inter-house football matches.

questions.prompt: Amina loves to draw. ______ uses colored pencils to paint the sunset.
questions.explanation: Amina is a girl, so the singular female subject pronoun is "She".
questions.socraticHint: Which pronoun do we use for a girl or woman?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Creative arts practical sessions in CBC.

questions.prompt: True or False: We use the pronoun "it" to refer to a cat, a desk, or a tree.
questions.explanation: True! "It" is used for objects, places, and animals.
questions.socraticHint: Do we call an object or non-human thing "it"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: English language lessons in Kenya.

questions.prompt: My brother and I are walking home. ______ are carrying our school bags.
questions.storyScenario: Walking home from school in Kericho.
questions.explanation: When talking about yourself and someone else ("my brother and I"), use "We".
questions.socraticHint: Which pronoun means "I and another person"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pupils walking together through tea estates.

questions.prompt: Match each person or group to the correct pronoun:
questions.explanation: The farmers -> They; the tractor -> It; Halima -> She; Omari -> He.
questions.socraticHint: Pair each noun with the pronoun that matches its gender and number.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Farming life and family relationships.

questions.prompt: This basket belongs to grandmother. It is ______ basket.
questions.explanation: "Her" shows possession for a female person.
questions.socraticHint: Which possessive word belongs to grandmother (a woman)?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Woven kiondo baskets handmade by Kenyan grandmothers.

questions.prompt: The pupils washed ______ hands with clean running water and soap before lunch.
questions.explanation: "Their" shows possession for a plural group of people (the pupils).
questions.socraticHint: Which word spelled T-H-E-I-R shows ownership for a group?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) stations.

questions.prompt: Juma forgot his pencil, so Nekesa shared ______ pencil with him.
questions.explanation: Nekesa is a girl, so the possessive pronoun is "her".
questions.socraticHint: Which possessive pronoun belongs to Nekesa?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sharing and caring values under CBC.

questions.prompt: Order these pronouns from 1st person (self), 2nd person (listener), to 3rd person (others):
questions.explanation: 1st person is the speaker (I, We), 2nd person is the listener (You), and 3rd person is about others (He/She/They).
questions.socraticHint: Start with I/We, then You, then He/She, then They.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Understanding dialogue in reading passages.

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence where the pronoun DOES NOT match the noun:

options.text: Mary called her mother on the phone.
The boys carried her heavy water jerricans.
Ali lost his book, but they found it quickly.
The lion roared loudly because he was hungry.

questions.explanation: If the boys are carrying their own jerricans, it should be "their heavy water jerricans", not "her".
questions.socraticHint: Notice "The boys" is plural male, but "her" is singular female.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Helping at home by carrying clean water.

questions.prompt: Amani wrote: "Baraka and I helped father weed the carrots. Then them gave us sweet mangoes." What word should replace "them"?
questions.explanation: Father is one man, so as the subject doing the giving, the correct pronoun is "He" ("Then he gave us sweet mangoes").
questions.socraticHint: Who gave the mangoes? Father. What singular subject pronoun stands for father?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Family farming in Murang'a.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Which sentence replaces all nouns with pronouns correctly in: "Wanjiru and Kamau gave the teacher the book"?
questions.explanation: "They gave it to her" correctly replaces "Wanjiru and Kamau" (They), "the book" (it), and "the teacher" (her) in natural English.
questions.socraticHint: Replace Wanjiru and Kamau with "They", the book with "it", and the female teacher with "her".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom manners and handing homework to teachers.

questions.prompt: Which word in this sentence is the ACTION VERB? "Chebet jumped over the tall puddle."
questions.explanation: "Jumped" is the action that Chebet performed, so it is the verb.
questions.socraticHint: Which word tells what Chebet did with her body?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Children playing after fresh rains in Eldoret.

questions.prompt: Look! The girls ______ traditional songs for the music festival.
questions.explanation: "The girls" is plural, so we use the helping verb "are" with "singing".
questions.socraticHint: For more than one person doing something now, use "are + singing".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The annual Kenya National Music Festival.

questions.prompt: True or False: In "I am listening to teacher Mary", the helping verb is "am".
questions.explanation: True! "Am" helps the main verb "listening" to show the action is happening right now.
questions.socraticHint: Is "am" helping "listening" to show present action?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Morning school routines in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Teacher Otieno ______ (write) a spelling quiz on the blackboard right now.
questions.explanation: Teacher Otieno is singular, so right now he "is writing". Note: drop the "e" when adding -ing.
questions.socraticHint: Use is + write with -ing.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Chalkboard teaching in primary school classrooms.

questions.prompt: Match each subject with its correct present continuous form:
questions.explanation: I am swimming; The baby is sleeping; The boys are running; We are eating.
questions.socraticHint: Match I with am, singular with is, and plural with are.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Daily activities around school and home.

questions.prompt: When adding "-ing" to the verb "swim", how is it spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: In short consonant-vowel-consonant words like swim, we double the final letter: swimming.
questions.socraticHint: Does swim double the letter "m" before -ing?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Swimming in Lake Victoria sports clubs.

questions.prompt: Order the words to build a grammatically correct present continuous sentence:
questions.explanation: Subject (Father) + verb (is driving) + object (the blue matatu) + prepositional phrase (to town).
questions.socraticHint: Who is doing the action? What is he doing? What is he driving? Where?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Matatu transport on busy Kenyan roads.

questions.prompt: Every day before breakfast, Kiprono ______ 5 kilometers to train.
questions.explanation: For daily repeated habits with a singular subject (Kiprono), we add -s: Kiprono runs.
questions.socraticHint: For a regular daily habit with he/she, does the verb take an "s"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Iten, the Home of Champions for Kenyan distance runners.

questions.prompt: Right now, the cows ______ (graze) peacefully in the green pasture.
questions.explanation: Cows is plural, so present continuous is "are grazing". Drop the silent "e" in graze before adding -ing.
questions.socraticHint: Use are + graze ending in -ing.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dairy farming in the central highlands.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a subject-verb agreement ERROR?

options.text: The birds are singing in the mango tree.
The child are crying for her lost toy.
The teacher is explaining the math problem.

questions.explanation: "The child" is singular, so it must use "is crying", not "are crying".
questions.socraticHint: Look closely at option 2: should one child use "is" or "are"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Peer review in English composition classes.

questions.prompt: Asha is writing a caption for her photograph of the coastal beach: "Look at the fishermen! They ______ their fishing nets after catching tilapia." What is the best verb form?
questions.explanation: "They" is plural and the exclamation "Look!" signals an action happening right now: "are mending".
questions.socraticHint: The pronoun is "They"—should we use "is" or "are"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Artisanal fishing communities along the Kenyan coast and Lake Victoria.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Choose the sentence that correctly expresses an ongoing action happening right now:

options.text: At this moment, the pupils was doing their assessment.
At this moment, the pupils doing their assessment without a verb.
At this moment, the pupils is doing their assessment.
At this moment, the pupils are quietly doing their assessment.

questions.explanation: "The pupils are quietly doing" has the plural helping verb "are" and the -ing verb "doing".
questions.socraticHint: Find the sentence with pupils + are + doing.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Quiet assessment sessions in school.

questions.prompt: What is the past tense of the regular verb "play"? "Yesterday, we ______ football."
questions.explanation: Regular verbs add -ed: play + ed = played.
questions.socraticHint: Add "-ed" directly to play.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Playing soccer on the village green.

questions.prompt: What is the past tense of the irregular verb "go"? "Last Saturday, Baraka ______ to Gikomba market."
questions.explanation: The past tense of "go" is irregular: "went". We never say "goed".
questions.socraticHint: Which common word starts with "w" and means went somewhere in the past?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Shopping excursions to Gikomba Market.

questions.prompt: True or False: The past tense of "eat" is "eated".
questions.explanation: False! "Eat" is an irregular verb: its past tense is "ate" (e.g., "We ate hot chapatis").
questions.socraticHint: Did you say "I ate" or "I eated"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Enjoying hot chapati and beans for lunch.

questions.prompt: Last term, our school team ______ (win) the athletics cup in Nakuru.
questions.explanation: The past tense of "win" is "won".
questions.socraticHint: Change the "i" in win to "o".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Primary school zonal sports trophies.

questions.prompt: Match each present tense verb to its correct irregular past tense form:
questions.explanation: See -> saw, buy -> bought, drink -> drank, write -> wrote.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each present action to its past form.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Narrative storytelling around the fireside.

questions.prompt: Yesterday, grandmother ______ delicious chai with fresh ginger and milk.
questions.explanation: "Yesterday" refers to the past, so we use the regular past tense "cooked".
questions.socraticHint: Look at the time word "Yesterday"—which form has -ed?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan spiced ginger tea (chai ya tangawizi).

questions.prompt: Order the events of Mwangi's safari into logical chronological order:
questions.storyScenario: Recounting a trip to Lake Nakuru.

items.text: First, Mwangi boarded the school bus at dawn.
Next, they arrived at Lake Nakuru National Park.
Then, they saw thousands of pink flamingos.
Finally, they returned home singing happily.

questions.explanation: The logical story sequence: First boarded, next arrived, then saw flamingos, finally returned.
questions.socraticHint: Follow the transition words: First, Next, Then, Finally.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Educational field trips to Lake Nakuru.

questions.prompt: During the dry season, the heavy rains finally ______ (come) and filled the river.
questions.explanation: The past tense of "come" is "came".
questions.socraticHint: Change the "o" in come to "a".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Relief of the long rains (Masika) in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the past tense of "catch"?
questions.storyScenario: Story of the clever monkey and the mango.

options.text: The boy caught the falling mango.
The boy cotched the falling mango.
The boy was catch the falling mango.
The boy catched the falling mango.

questions.explanation: The past tense of "catch" is "caught" (spelled C-A-U-G-H-T).
questions.socraticHint: Catch changes to caught, like teach changes to taught.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Harvesting sweet mangoes in Ukambani.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: "Last night, father buyed new storybooks for us."
questions.explanation: "Buy" is irregular: its past tense is "bought", never "buyed".
questions.socraticHint: Look at the word "buyed"—is that a valid past tense in English?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Parents buying storybooks for children.

questions.prompt: Wacera wants to tell her class about yesterday's trip to Tsavo. Which sentence is written in the correct past tense?

options.text: Yesterday we sees elephants and we taking lots of pictures.
Yesterday we see elephants and we take lots of pictures.
Yesterday we saw elephants and we took lots of pictures.
Yesterday we seen elephants and we taked lots of pictures.

questions.explanation: Both verbs must be in past tense: see -> saw and take -> took.
questions.socraticHint: Change both "see" and "take" into their irregular past forms.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Wildlife safari memories in Tsavo.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Which sentence accurately mixes regular and irregular past tense verbs without any mistakes?

options.text: We planted maize seeds, watered the soil, and eated sweet sugarcane.
We planted maize seeds, water the soil, and ate sweet sugarcane.
We planted maize seeds, watered the soil, and eat sweet sugarcane.
We planted maize seeds, watered the soil, and ate sweet sugarcane.

questions.explanation: Planted (regular), watered (regular), and ate (irregular) are all accurately conjugated past tense verbs!
questions.socraticHint: Check all three actions: planted, watered, ate.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Shamba work and enjoying sugarcane treats.

questions.prompt: Which word in this sentence is an ADJECTIVE? "Mama bought three sweet pineapples."
questions.explanation: "Sweet" describes the taste of the pineapples, so it is an adjective.
questions.socraticHint: Which word tells what kind of pineapples Mama bought?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pineapple farming in Thika plantations.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective that describes the SIZE of the elephant: "The ______ elephant walked slowly."
questions.explanation: "Huge" describes size. Grey describes color, and friendly describes quality.
questions.socraticHint: Which word tells how big the elephant is?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Elephant herds with Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli.

questions.prompt: True or False: In "The baby has two soft blankets", both "two" (number) and "soft" (texture) are adjectives.
questions.storyScenario: Caring for baby brother at home.
questions.explanation: True! Words that tell how many (two) and what kind (soft) both describe the noun "blankets".
questions.socraticHint: Do number words and texture words describe nouns?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Warm Maasai fleece shukas used as baby blankets.

questions.prompt: The sky is ______ (color) and clear on a sunny morning in Nairobi.
questions.explanation: "Blue" is the color adjective describing the clear sunny sky.
questions.socraticHint: What color is the sky when there are no rain clouds?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Bright Kenyan highland weather.

questions.prompt: Match each noun with its most fitting descriptive adjective:
questions.explanation: Lemon is sour; tea is hot; cheetah is fast; feather is light.
questions.socraticHint: Pair each noun with the sensation or quality that fits it best.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sensory exploration in CBC Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Which sentence puts the adjectives in the correct order? (Size before Color)

options.text: Wanjiku bought big a red bag.
Wanjiku bought a red big bag.
Wanjiku bought a big red bag.

questions.explanation: In English, size comes before color: "a big red bag".
questions.socraticHint: Does size (big) come before color (red)?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School backpack shopping in Kenyan markets.

questions.prompt: Order the words to build a descriptive sentence:
questions.explanation: "The tall sunflower produced bright yellow petals" follows proper grammar and adjective placement.
questions.socraticHint: Start with the subject "The tall sunflower" and finish with the bright petals.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sunflower farming in Uasin Gishu.

questions.prompt: Find the OPPOSITE adjective of "heavy": "The sack of maize was heavy, but the paper bag was ______."
questions.storyScenario: Carrying goods from the posho mill.
questions.explanation: The opposite (antonym) of heavy is light.
questions.socraticHint: What is the opposite of heavy when carrying something?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Carrying farm produce home.

questions.prompt: Grandmother carved a ______ (shape) wooden spoon for stirring ugali.
questions.explanation: "Round" describes the circular shape of the wooden cooking spoon (mwiko).
questions.socraticHint: Which common shape word describes a circle or curved edge?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional wooden cooking sticks (mwiko) carved in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which word in this sentence is NOT an adjective? "The cheerful girl drank sweet milk."

options.text: Both cheerful and sweet are adjectives

questions.explanation: "Drank" is an action verb in the past tense, not an adjective.
questions.socraticHint: Which word shows an action that someone did?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fresh cow milk from local dairy farms.

questions.prompt: Kiprotich wants to describe his prized cow at the agricultural show: "She is healthy, gentle, and produces plenty of milk." Which two words are adjectives describing the cow's character and condition?
questions.explanation: "Healthy" describes her physical condition and "gentle" describes her calm temperament.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the two words that describe what kind of cow she is.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Annual ASK Agricultural Shows of Kenya.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Choose the sentence that contains THREE distinct adjectives (number, quality, and color):

options.text: Mother walked quickly to the market today.
Mother is cooking hot ugali for dinner.
The red apples fell from the tree.
Mother bought five sweet red apples at the supermarket.

questions.explanation: Option 1 has three adjectives: "five" (number), "sweet" (quality), and "red" (color).
questions.socraticHint: Look for a sentence with a number word, a taste word, and a color word.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fresh produce shopping in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Where is the book? "Achieng placed her English textbook ______ the wooden desk."
questions.explanation: We rest objects "on" a flat surface such as a desk.
questions.socraticHint: Which preposition means resting on top of a flat surface?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Desks in Kenyan primary schools.

questions.prompt: When the hot midday sun shone, the cattle rested ______ the shade of the acacia tree.
questions.explanation: Animals rest "under" the shade of a tree to escape the sun.
questions.socraticHint: When a tree is above you, you are sitting... where?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Seeking shade on the hot savannah grasslands.

questions.prompt: True or False: In "The coin fell inside the pocket", the preposition is "inside".
questions.explanation: True! "Inside" is the preposition telling where the coin went.
questions.socraticHint: Does "inside" show where the coin is located?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Carrying coin coins safely in school uniforms.

questions.prompt: The dog hid ______ the heavy wooden door when thunder rumbled.
questions.explanation: "Behind" shows the dog is located at the back of the door.
questions.socraticHint: Which word means at the back of something?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Rainstorms and thunderstorm safety.

questions.prompt: Match each location phrase to its meaning:

pairs.right: in the middle of two things
from one side to the other
at the head or face of a room

questions.explanation: Between = in the middle; under = below; across = from one side to the other; in front of = at the head.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each prepositional phrase with its everyday meaning.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Giving directions in local villages and trading centers.

matchingPairs.rightText: in the middle of two things
from one side to the other
at the head or face of a room

questions.prompt: The zebra jumped ______ the wooden fence into the green meadow.
questions.explanation: "Over" describes jumping from one side above an obstacle to the other side.
questions.socraticHint: When you jump across something without touching it, you leap... over it.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fenced ranches in the Great Rift Valley.

questions.prompt: Order the prepositions by spatial position from highest to lowest:
questions.explanation: From highest to lowest: above -> on -> under -> deep beneath.
questions.socraticHint: Start with the sky (above) and go all the way down into the ground (beneath).
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Spatial orientation and map reading skills.

questions.prompt: Ali walked safely ______ the zebra crossing to reach the school gate.
questions.explanation: To move from one side of a road to the other, we walk "across".
questions.socraticHint: Which preposition means moving from one side of the road to the opposite side?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Road safety rules and zebra crossings outside schools.

questions.prompt: Which preposition correctly completes the sentence? "The football rolled ______ the two red cones."
questions.storyScenario: Physical education drill on the pitch.
questions.explanation: We use "between" when referring to two distinct items (the two cones). We use "among" for three or more.
questions.socraticHint: For exactly two items, do we use "between" or "among"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Physical education games and ball drills.

questions.prompt: Spot the incorrect preposition: "Wambui dived on the swimming pool on a hot afternoon."

options.text: "on" should be "into" because she entered the water

questions.explanation: When movement enters inside an enclosed area or liquid, we use "into", not "on".
questions.socraticHint: When jumping inside water, do you dive "on" or "into"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Water sports and recreational swimming.

questions.prompt: Fatuma is explaining how to find the clinic in Malindi: "Walk straight past the post office, then turn right. The clinic is ______ the bank and the pharmacy." Which word shows its exact middle position?
questions.explanation: "Between" accurately shows the clinic is flanked on either side by the bank and the pharmacy.
questions.socraticHint: Which preposition sits right in the middle of two locations?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Town planning and wayfinding in coastal towns.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Choose the sentence that uses BOTH an adjective and a preposition 100% accurately:

options.text: The playfully kitten slept peacefully on under the table.
The playful kitten slept peacefully between the table.
The play kitten slept peacefully under wooden table.
The playful kitten slept peacefully under the wooden table.

questions.explanation: "Playful" and "wooden" are correct adjectives, and "under" is the correct preposition.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the sentence with proper adjectives ("playful", "wooden") and a clear preposition ("under").
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pets and domestic life in Kenyan homesteads.

questions.prompt: Join these two sentences: "Juma likes soccer. Juma likes swimming." Which conjunction adds the two sports together?
questions.explanation: "And" joins two similar ideas: "Juma likes soccer and swimming."
questions.socraticHint: Which joining word adds two hobbies together?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Co-curricular sports activities in schools.

questions.prompt: Kiprono ran as fast as he could, ______ he came in second place.
questions.explanation: "But" shows an unexpected contrast: he ran fast, but still came in second.
questions.socraticHint: Which word shows an unexpected difference or surprise?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Junior athletics championships in the Rift Valley.

questions.prompt: True or False: We use "because" when we want to explain the REASON why something happened.
questions.explanation: True! "Because" introduces a reason (e.g. "The plant withered because it lacked water").
questions.socraticHint: When someone asks "Why?", do you answer starting with "Because"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Environmental science inquiries in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Amina boiled the fresh milk ______ she wanted to drink warm chai.
questions.explanation: "Because" gives the reason why Amina boiled the milk.
questions.socraticHint: Which conjunction explains why she boiled the milk?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Preparing nutritious breakfast before school.

questions.prompt: Match each conjunction to its role in a sentence:
questions.explanation: And adds; but contrasts; because gives reason; or offers choice.
questions.socraticHint: Pair each word with how it links ideas together.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Building logical thinking skills in CBC.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly links two ideas using "and"?

options.text: Muthoni swept the compound and because fed the chickens.
Muthoni swept the compound, but and fed the chickens.
Muthoni swept the compound and she
Muthoni swept the compound and fed the chickens.

questions.explanation: "Muthoni swept the compound and fed the chickens" smoothly connects two chores.
questions.socraticHint: Which sentence is complete and uses only "and" to join two actions?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Helping with domestic chores in rural homesteads.

questions.prompt: Order these sentence chunks into a complete, logical sentence:
questions.explanation: Main clause + conjunction "because" + cause: "We took our umbrellas because dark storm clouds gathered in the sky."
questions.socraticHint: What did we take? Why did we take it? Conjunction connects them.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Preparing for afternoon tropical downpours.

questions.prompt: Choose the best conjunction: "The mango looked sweet and juicy, ______ inside it was not ripe yet."
questions.explanation: "But" is required because there is a contrast between looking good and not being ripe.
questions.socraticHint: Does the inside match the outside, or is there a surprising contrast?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Selecting sweet fruit in local markets.

questions.prompt: Would you like to eat sweet bananas ______ (or/and) juicy passion fruit?
questions.explanation: When offering a choice between two options, use "or".
questions.socraticHint: Which conjunction presents a choice between two snacks?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Nutritious Kenyan fruit snacks.

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence with an INCORRECT conjunction:

options.text: I drank cool water because I was very thirsty.
Akinyi wore a jacket but it was extremely cold.
The baby cried because she was feeling sleepy.
Baraka wanted to go outside, but it started raining.

questions.explanation: Wearing a jacket happens BECAUSE it was cold, not "but". "Akinyi wore a jacket because it was cold."
questions.socraticHint: Is cold weather the reason to wear a jacket? Then we use "because", not "but".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dressing warmly for cold highland mornings in Limuru.

questions.prompt: Wacera wants to combine: "The maize crop grew tall. There was plenty of rainfall in April." Which joined sentence is best?

options.text: The maize crop grew tall, or there was plenty of rainfall in April.
Because the maize grew tall, but there was rainfall.
The maize crop grew tall because there was plenty of rainfall in April.
The maize crop grew tall, but there was plenty of rainfall in April.

questions.explanation: Rainfall is the clear reason the maize grew tall, so "because" connects the cause and effect.
questions.socraticHint: Why did the maize grow tall? Look for the sentence using "because".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Agriculture and rainfall patterns in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Which complex sentence uses BOTH "and" and "because" correctly?

options.text: Baraka washed his hands because and sat down lunch was ready.
Baraka washed his hands but lunch was ready because he sat down.
Baraka washed his hands and because he sat down.
Baraka washed his hands and sat down because lunch was ready.

questions.explanation: "And" connects the two actions (washed hands and sat down), while "because" explains why he sat down.
questions.socraticHint: Look for two actions linked by "and" and a reason introduced by "because".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Family mealtime manners in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which question word asks about a PERSON? "______ is our new Grade 3 class teacher?"
questions.explanation: "Who" asks about a person.
questions.socraticHint: Which question word asks about people?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School opening day in January.

questions.prompt: Which question word asks about a PLACE or LOCATION? "______ did you leave your school bag?"
questions.explanation: "Where" asks about place or location.
questions.socraticHint: Which word asks where something is located?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom tidiness and personal responsibility.

questions.prompt: True or False: Every asking sentence (question) must end with a full stop (.).
questions.explanation: False! Questions must end with a question mark (?), while statements end with a full stop (.).
questions.socraticHint: What mark goes at the end of a question: a dot or a curly mark with a dot below?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Grammar and punctuation rules in CBC.

questions.prompt: "______ (time) does the morning assembly begin at school?"
questions.explanation: "When" asks about time or schedule.
questions.socraticHint: Which question word asks about time or clock hours?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Morning school parade and national anthem in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Match each question word to what it asks about:

pairs.right: asks about a thing or action

questions.explanation: Why -> reason; How -> manner; What -> thing; When -> time.
questions.socraticHint: Pair each inquiry word with the kind of information it seeks.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Scientific inquiry and critical thinking in CBC.

matchingPairs.rightText: asks about a thing or action

questions.prompt: "______ do you make delicious mandazi?" asks Amani. "First, mix flour, sugar, and yeast..."
questions.explanation: "How" asks about the steps, method, or procedure.
questions.socraticHint: Which question word asks for instructions or steps?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Baking mandazi for breakfast.

questions.prompt: Order the words to construct a proper question:
questions.explanation: Question word (Where) + verb (is) + subject (the nearest duka) + participle/adverb (located?).
questions.socraticHint: Start with "Where" and end with the question mark.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Asking for directions to the local shop.

questions.prompt: "______ did the chameleon change its color to brown?" "To camouflage against dry tree bark."
questions.explanation: "Why" asks for the reason or explanation.
questions.socraticHint: Which question word asks for the reason behind an animal's behavior?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan wildlife adaptations.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is written as a grammatically correct question?

options.text: What is your favorite CBC learning area?
What your favorite CBC learning area is.
Is what your favorite CBC learning area.
What is your favorite CBC learning area.

questions.explanation: Option 1 has correct word order and ends with a question mark (?).
questions.socraticHint: Notice the question mark at the end and the proper word order.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: CBC learning areas and pupil preferences.

questions.prompt: Pupil: "Excuse me, teacher. ______ many shillings does one pencil cost?"
questions.explanation: We use "How many" to ask about quantity, number, or price.
questions.socraticHint: Which word goes with "many" to ask about price or quantity?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Buying stationery at a local bookshop or duka.

questions.prompt: Reporter Ouma is interviewing an organic tea farmer in Kericho. He wants to know the season when tea leaves are picked. What question should he ask?

options.text: "What is the color of green tea?"
"When is the best season to harvest tea leaves?"

questions.explanation: "When" asks about the season and time of harvest.
questions.socraticHint: Since he wants to know about the season (time), which question starts with "When"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tea harvesting in the rolling hills of Kericho.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Which dialogue shows a correct question and a correct causal answer using "because"?

options.text: "Why do we wash our hands." — "Because clean hands prevent illnesses."
"Where do we wash our hands?" — "Because clean hands prevent illnesses."
"Why do we wash our hands?" — "And clean hands prevent illnesses."
"Why do we wash our hands?" — "Because clean hands prevent illnesses."

questions.explanation: The question correctly begins with "Why" and ends with "?", and the answer explains the reason starting with "Because".
questions.socraticHint: Match "Why...?" with "Because...". Look for proper punctuation.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Public health and hygiene promotion in schools.

questions.prompt: Which word in this sentence MUST be capitalized? "next tuesday, we will visit the museum."
questions.explanation: Days of the week (Tuesday) and the first word of a sentence (Next) must always be capitalized.
questions.socraticHint: Which day of the week is named here?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School visits to the Nairobi National Museum.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly capitalized country name:
questions.explanation: Proper nouns of countries always start with a capital letter: Kenya.
questions.socraticHint: Our homeland starts with a proud capital K.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: National pride and patriotism in Kenya.

questions.prompt: True or False: The word "i" when referring to yourself should always be written as a capital "I".
questions.explanation: True! The pronoun "I" is always capitalized, whether at the start or middle of a sentence.
questions.socraticHint: Can you ever write "i" by itself in lower case when talking about yourself?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Personal narrative writing in primary school.

questions.prompt: Jamhuri Day is celebrated in the month of ______ (december) every year.
questions.explanation: Names of months must always begin with a capital letter: December.
questions.socraticHint: Write the month of December starting with a capital D.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Jamhuri Day national celebrations on December 12th.

questions.prompt: Match each noun type with why it requires a capital letter:
questions.explanation: People, cities, days of the week, and rivers are all proper nouns requiring capitals.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each capitalized word to its proper noun category.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan names and geography.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has ALL capital letters written correctly?

options.text: In april, amani and I went to Kisumu.
In April, Amani and i went to kisumu.
in april, amani and i went to kisumu.
In April, Amani and I went to Kisumu.

questions.explanation: "In" (sentence start), "April" (month), "Amani" (name), "I" (pronoun), and "Kisumu" (town) are all capitalized.
questions.socraticHint: Check every single proper noun and the start of the sentence.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School holiday travel to lake-side city Kisumu.

questions.prompt: Order the words to form a properly capitalized sentence:
questions.explanation: "My friend Kiprono lives in Eldoret near the sports stadium." correctly places capitalized names.
questions.socraticHint: Start with the subject "My friend Kiprono" and follow with the location.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Athletics culture in Eldoret.

questions.prompt: Spot the word that SHOULD NOT have a capital letter: "We ate Sweet Mangoes from Machakos."
questions.explanation: "Sweet" is a common adjective in the middle of a sentence, not a proper noun, so it should be lower-case.
questions.socraticHint: Is "sweet" a special name or just a regular describing word?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mango harvesting in Machakos county.

questions.prompt: The highest mountain in our nation is Mount ______ (kenya).
questions.explanation: Mount Kenya is a proper noun, so Kenya must be capitalized.
questions.socraticHint: Write Kenya with a capital letter.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mount Kenya, the snow-capped pride of Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which pet name is capitalized correctly in a sentence?

options.text: Our faithful guard dog is named simba.
Our faithful guard dog is named Simba.
Our faithful guard dog is named sIMBA.
our faithful guard dog is named Simba.

questions.explanation: Both the first word "Our" and the pet's specific name "Simba" are properly capitalized.
questions.socraticHint: Look for both the start of the sentence and the dog's name being capitalized.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Guard dogs and pets in Kenyan homes.

questions.prompt: Baraka wrote: "every sunday, mother and i attend church in nairobi." How many capital letter corrections does Baraka need to make?
questions.explanation: He must capitalize 4 words: "Every" (sentence start), "Sunday" (day), "I" (pronoun), and "Nairobi" (city).
questions.socraticHint: Count: first word, the day of worship, the pronoun I, and the capital city.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Weekend routines and church attendance in Nairobi.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Choose the title of a story that follows standard CBC capitalization conventions:

options.text: the clever hare and the greedy hyena
THE CLEVER HARE AND THE GREEDY HYENA
The clever hare And The greedy Hyena
The Clever Hare and the Greedy Hyena

questions.explanation: Important words in titles are capitalized, while minor connecting words like "and" and "the" remain lowercase.
questions.socraticHint: Major nouns and adjectives take capitals, while "and" and "the" stay lowercase.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional Kenyan folklore titles.

questions.prompt: What punctuation mark belongs at the end of this sentence? "The matatu reached the bus stop on time__"
questions.explanation: This is a declarative statement telling a fact, so it ends with a full stop (.).
questions.socraticHint: Is this telling a fact or asking a question?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Boarding matatus at the stage.

questions.prompt: What punctuation mark belongs at the end of this sentence? "Where did you put the school register__"
questions.explanation: The sentence begins with "Where" and asks a direct question, requiring a question mark (?).
questions.socraticHint: Look at the question word "Where"—what mark belongs at the end?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Morning school register check in class.

questions.prompt: True or False: In a shopping list, commas are used to separate items: "Mother bought sukuma wiki, potatoes, and onions."
questions.explanation: True! Commas separate items in a series so the reader knows each distinct item.
questions.socraticHint: Do commas give pauses between different vegetables on a list?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Shopping lists for cooking hearty family dinners.

questions.prompt: A statement always ends with a ______ stop.
questions.explanation: A statement ends with a "full" stop (also called a period).
questions.socraticHint: The dot at the end of a sentence is called a... stop.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Writing rules taught in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Match each punctuation mark to its visual symbol:
questions.explanation: Full stop is .; Question mark is ?; Comma is ,; Exclamation mark is !.
questions.socraticHint: Match each punctuation name to its symbol.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Visual literacy and writing mechanics.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has COMMAS placed in the correct positions?

options.text: Ali packed, his pencils rubber ruler and sharpener.
Ali packed his pencils rubber, ruler and, sharpener.
Ali packed his, pencils, rubber, ruler and sharpener.
Ali packed his pencils, rubber, ruler, and sharpener.

questions.explanation: Commas correctly separate the listed stationery items: pencils, rubber, ruler, and sharpener.
questions.socraticHint: Look for commas placed neatly between each stationery item.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pencil case supplies in primary school.

questions.prompt: Order the sentence parts to show correct punctuation from beginning to ending mark:
questions.explanation: Capital letter starts the sentence and a question mark seals the asking sentence.
questions.socraticHint: Begin with the capital start and end with the question mark.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Inquiring about wildlife park routes.

questions.prompt: What mark should replace the star? "Watch out* A big branch is falling!"
questions.explanation: An exclamation mark (!) expresses sudden excitement, urgency, or warning.
questions.socraticHint: Which punctuation mark expresses an urgent warning or strong emotion?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Safety reminders during stormy weather.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a QUESTION that needs a question mark?

options.text: Can we go and watch the football match this afternoon
We went to watch the football match this afternoon
The football match was very exciting
I love playing football with my classmates

questions.explanation: "Can we go and watch..." is an asking sentence requesting permission, so it must end with ?.
questions.socraticHint: Which sentence asks for permission starting with "Can we"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Asking permission from parents and teachers.

questions.prompt: Look at the sentence: "Mumbi, could you please pass the salt." What punctuation mistake was made?

options.text: It should end with a question mark (?) because it is asking a polite question.
The comma after Mumbi should be removed.

questions.explanation: "Could you please pass the salt?" is a question and should end with a question mark.
questions.socraticHint: Is "Could you please...?" asking someone something?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dinner table etiquette and polite requests.

questions.prompt: Kiprono is checking his friend's writing: "In our school garden we grow sukuma wiki spinach tomatoes and sweet potatoes." Where should commas be added?

options.text: Between the crops: "sukuma wiki, spinach, tomatoes, and sweet potatoes."

questions.explanation: Commas are required between items in the list: sukuma wiki, spinach, tomatoes, and sweet potatoes.
questions.socraticHint: Where are the individual vegetables that need to be separated?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: CBC agriculture 4K Club school gardens.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Which sentence has PERFECT capitalization AND punctuation throughout?

options.text: on Friday, Wanjiku bought bananas apples and milk in nakuru.
On Friday, wanjiku bought bananas, apples and milk in Nakuru
On friday, Wanjiku bought bananas, apples, and milk in Nakuru?
On Friday, Wanjiku bought bananas, apples, and milk in Nakuru.

questions.explanation: Capital letters for "On", "Friday", "Wanjiku", and "Nakuru", commas separating the list, and a full stop at the end!
questions.socraticHint: Check every single capital letter, every comma in the list, and the final punctuation mark.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Weekend shopping in Nakuru town.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a TOPIC SENTENCE in a paragraph?

options.text: It introduces the main idea of the paragraph
It says goodbye at the end of a letter
It lists words in alphabetical order

questions.explanation: The topic sentence tells the reader what the entire paragraph will be about.
questions.socraticHint: Which sentence tells the main idea of what you are about to read?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: English composition writing in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would make the best TOPIC SENTENCE for a paragraph about caring for chickens?

options.text: The sun set at seven o'clock.
Chickens need good care, clean water, and fresh grain to stay healthy.
My shoes are brown and muddy.

questions.explanation: Option 1 clearly states the main topic: taking care of chickens to keep them healthy.
questions.socraticHint: Which sentence is directly about caring for chickens?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Rearing poultry (kuku wa kienyeji) in homesteads.

questions.prompt: True or False: Every sentence in a paragraph should support the same main topic.
questions.explanation: True! Paragraph unity means all sentences work together to describe the same topic without wandering off.
questions.socraticHint: Should all sentences stay focused on the same subject?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Writing coherence skills under CBC.

questions.prompt: The final sentence that wraps up a paragraph is called the ______ sentence.
questions.explanation: The concluding sentence summarizes and gives a satisfying finish to the paragraph.
questions.socraticHint: Which word means bringing to a conclusion or finish?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Creative composition classes in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Match each part of a paragraph to its job:

pairs.right: Small space at the beginning of the first line

questions.explanation: Topic sentence gives main idea; supporting gives details; concluding wraps up; indentation marks the start.

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Formatting handwritten exercise books in Kenyan schools.

matchingPairs.rightText: Small space at the beginning of the first line

questions.prompt: Read this paragraph: "Dogs make great farm guards. They bark when strangers approach. I like eating sweet ice cream. They also protect the sheep from wild animals." Which sentence DOES NOT belong?

options.text: They also protect the sheep from wild animals.
I like eating sweet ice cream.

questions.explanation: "I like eating sweet ice cream" has nothing to do with dogs protecting the farm.
questions.socraticHint: Which sentence talks about food instead of guard dogs?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Farm security and livestock protection.

questions.prompt: Order these sentences to create a cohesive paragraph about planting a tree:

items.text: Last Saturday, our environmental club planted a neem tree at school.
First, we dug a deep hole in the fertile soil.
Then, we placed the seedling inside and watered it gently.
We were excited knowing our tree will provide cool shade for years.

questions.explanation: Topic sentence (item 1) -> First dug hole (item 2) -> Then planted & watered (item 3) -> Conclusion (item 4).
questions.socraticHint: Start with the introduction of the tree planting, follow the steps, and end with the reflection.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenya National Tree Planting Day initiatives.

questions.prompt: Which transition word helps show what happened NEXT in a story?
questions.explanation: "Afterwards" shows sequence of time and what followed next.
questions.socraticHint: Which word means "after that"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Narrating sequential events in English.

questions.prompt: To make your writing lively and interesting, use descriptive ______ (parts of speech) like "sweet", "golden", and "sparkling".
questions.explanation: Adjectives bring writing alive by adding sensory details and vivid descriptions.
questions.socraticHint: What are describing words called?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Creative writing workshops in school.

questions.prompt: Which closing sentence provides the best conclusion for a paragraph about visiting Tsavo National Park?

options.text: A giraffe is taller than a goat.
It was an unforgettable adventure that made me love Kenya's wildlife even more.
I drank tea at four o'clock.

questions.explanation: Option 1 reflects on the whole experience and expresses a meaningful feeling about the visit.
questions.socraticHint: Which sentence gives a complete, happy reflection on the whole safari?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Field trips to national parks.

questions.prompt: Nekesa is writing a paragraph titled "My Grandmother's Shamba". She has written: 1) "Grandmother has a fertile shamba in Vihiga." 2) "She grows sweet bananas, sukuma wiki, and maize." What should her next supporting sentence describe?

options.text: Aeroplanes fly high in the sky.
Mombasa is near the Indian Ocean.
She also keeps three milking cows that provide fresh milk every morning.
My teacher gave us homework on multiplication.

questions.explanation: Adding details about the cows and milk fits perfectly with life on grandmother's shamba.
questions.socraticHint: Which option adds more details about grandmother's farm?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Farming homesteads in Western Kenya.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Which 4-sentence composition is the most unified and grammatically complete?

options.text: Our Grade 3 class celebrated Cultural Day. We wore clothes. I have a cat at home. It was raining yesterday.
Cultural Day was yesterday. Because we danced and then we ate and my shoes were black.
We celebrated Cultural Day with joy, but food was cooked, although shoes are good.

Our Grade 3 class celebrated Cultural Day with immense joy. We wore colorful traditional clothes from different communities in Kenya. Parents shared delicious dishes like mukimo, biryani, and mursik. It was a wonderful day that celebrated our national unity.

questions.explanation: Option 1 has a clear topic sentence, rich supporting details representing Kenya's diversity, and a powerful conclusion on national unity.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the well-structured paragraph that celebrates Cultural Day from start to finish.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School Cultural Days celebrating national unity in diversity.

questions.prompt: How should you begin a friendly note to your aunt? Which GREETING is correct?
questions.explanation: A friendly greeting starts with "Dear [Name]," capitalized and followed by a comma.
questions.socraticHint: Look for capital letters for Dear and the aunt's name, ending with a comma.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Letter writing to extended family members.

questions.prompt: Where does the DATE usually go when writing a friendly letter in your exercise book?

options.text: In the middle of the signature
At the very bottom upside down

questions.explanation: In traditional friendly letter format taught in Kenya, the date is placed at the top right.
questions.socraticHint: Which top corner displays the date of writing?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Writing exercises in CBC exercise books.

questions.prompt: True or False: In a thank-you note, you should clearly mention what gift or kind action you are thanking the person for.
questions.explanation: True! Stating the specific gift or action shows genuine appreciation and thoughtfulness.
questions.socraticHint: Does naming the specific gift make the person feel valued?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Expressing gratitude for hospitality and gifts.

questions.prompt: A polite friendly note ends with a sign-off like "Your ______ (loving/ugly) friend," followed by your name.
questions.explanation: "Your loving friend" or "Your caring friend" is a warm and respectful sign-off.
questions.socraticHint: Which positive, affectionate word describes a warm friend?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Warm friendship bonds in primary school.

questions.prompt: Match each letter section with an example sentence:

pairs.right: Thank you for the delicious honey.
I look forward to visiting you during the holidays.

questions.explanation: Greeting opens; gratitude expresses thanks; future hope connects; sign-off closes warmly.
questions.socraticHint: Match each friendly note section with its sample text.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Communicating with grandparents in the countryside.

matchingPairs.rightText: Thank you for the delicious honey.
I look forward to visiting you during the holidays.

questions.prompt: Which sign-off is MOST APPROPRIATE for a friendly letter to your classmate?
questions.explanation: "Your best friend," is warm and casual, ideal for a classmate. "Yours faithfully" is formal business style.
questions.socraticHint: Which sign-off sounds like a caring friendship between two children?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Writing pen-pal letters between schools.

questions.prompt: Order the parts of a friendly thank-you note from top to bottom:

items.text: Body message (Thank you for helping me learn division.)

questions.explanation: From top to bottom: Date -> Greeting -> Body message -> Sign-off & Name.
questions.socraticHint: Start with the date at top, greeting, message, and finish with your name.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Appreciation notes given to teachers on World Teachers' Day.

questions.prompt: After the greeting "Dear Grandmother", always put a ______ (,).
questions.explanation: A comma always follows the greeting in a friendly letter.
questions.socraticHint: Which punctuation mark looks like a little curl with a dot at the top?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Letter etiquette taught in primary schools.

questions.prompt: Achieng wants to thank her neighbor Mama Kiprono for lending her an umbrella during heavy rain. Which message is the MOST polite and heartfelt?

options.text: "Thank you so much for the umbrella. It kept me dry and safe from the heavy downpour yesterday."
"Umbrellas are made of plastic and metal."

questions.explanation: Option 1 expresses genuine gratitude and explains how the neighbor's kindness helped her.
questions.socraticHint: Which message specifically says thank you and explains how the kindness helped?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Good neighborliness (ujirani mwema) in Kenyan communities.

questions.prompt: What is missing from this note? "Dear Uncle John, Thank you for the birthday football. I play with it every afternoon. John"

options.text: A proper sign-off like "Your loving nephew," before his name.

questions.explanation: A friendly letter requires a closing sign-off (e.g. "Your loving nephew,") before the writer's signature.
questions.socraticHint: Notice how the writer jumped straight to his name without saying "Your nephew" or "Your friend".
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Polite family correspondence.

questions.prompt: Mutiso is making a get-well-soon card for his sick classmate who is in hospital in Machakos. What sentence should he include in the card to encourage him?

options.text: "We had a math exam and it was very difficult."
"We all miss your cheerful smile in Grade 3 and we pray you recover quickly!"

questions.explanation: Option 1 shows empathy, love, and community encouragement, uplifting the sick classmate.
questions.socraticHint: Which sentence offers warmth, care, and hopes for quick healing?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Empathy, compassion, and caring for the sick in Kenyan culture.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Choose the thank-you note that has ALL parts (Date, Greeting, Message, Sign-off, and Name) punctuated and formatted impeccably:

options.text:
dear Aunt Wambui
Thank you. Amani

We came to Nyeri and ate plums. Bye,
Amani

12th November 2026

Thank you
your niece amani

questions.prompt: Mtoto anapokutana na mtu mzima kama nyanya au babu, anapaswa kumsalimu vipi kwa heshima?

questions.prompt: Mtu mzima anapoambiwa "Shikamoo", huitikiaje?
questions.explanation: Jawabu sahihi la "Shikamoo" ni "Marahaba".
questions.socraticHint: Je, mtu mzima huitikiaje anaposalimiwa shikamoo?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Maadili na heshima ya Kiswahili Sanifu.

questions.prompt: Kweli au La: Unaposalimiwa na rafiki yako wa rika moja "Hujambo?", unaitikia "Sijambo".

questions.socraticHint: Kumbuka: Hu-jambo huitikiwa Si-jambo.

questions.socraticHint: Ikiwa mmoja anasema Sijambo, wengi wanasema Ha...jambo?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mwalimu anapowasalimu wanafunzi wote darasani.

questions.prompt: Oanisha salamu ifuatayo na jawabu lake sahihi:
questions.explanation: Shikamoo -> Marahaba, Hujambo -> Sijambo, Sabalkheri -> Aheri, U hali gani -> Mzuri.

items.text: Mwalimu: "Marahaba Baraka. Umeamkaje asubuhi ya leo?"
Mwalimu: "Vyema sana, ingia darasani ukaanze masomo."

questions.explanation: Mazungumzo huanza na salamu (Shikamoo), kuitikia (Marahaba), kuulizana hali, na kisha kuingia darasani.

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kufika shuleni asubuhi na kuwasalimu walimu.

questions.prompt: Wakati wa jioni jua linapotua, watu huagana kwa kusema:
questions.explanation: Wakati wa jioni tunatakiana "Jioni njema" au "Lala salama" tunapoenda kupumzika.

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Wanafunzi wakiagana wakirudi nyumbani jioni.

questions.prompt: Salamu ya jioni "Msalheri" huitikiwa kwa kusema: "______".
questions.explanation: Jawabu la "Msalheri" (jioni ya heri) ni "Aheri" (heri njema).
questions.socraticHint: Kumbuka: Sabalkheri huitikiwa Aheri, na Msalheri pia huitikiwa...?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kiswahili mufti na lugha fasaha.

questions.prompt: Musa alikutana na Chifu wa eneo lao barabarani. Chifu ni mtu mwenye heshima kubwa kijijini. Musa anapaswa kusema nini kwanza?
questions.explanation: Chifu ni kiongozi na mtu mzima, hivyo kusalimiwa kwa heshima ya "Shikamoo" kunathibitisha nidhamu ya mtoto.
