questions.explanation: Many wild plants produce toxic chemicals that cause severe poisoning if ingested.
questions.socraticHint: Why is it dangerous to eat colorful berries from bushes in the forest?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Child safety in rural environments.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of planting a tree seedling during National Tree Planting Day:

items.text: Dig a hole twice as wide and deep as the seedling container.
Carefully remove the seedling from the polythene tube without damaging roots.
Place the seedling upright in the hole and fill with topsoil mixed with compost.
Press soil gently around the stem, water generously, and protect with a thorn fence.

questions.explanation: Dig hole -> unwrap seedling -> position upright & fill soil -> water & protect.
questions.socraticHint: Start with digging the hole and finish with watering and protecting the seedling.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: National Tree Growing and Restoration Day in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Milky sap from plants like euphorbia can cause painful burning irritation if it touches your ______ (eyes/hair).
questions.explanation: Euphorbia and poisonous latex saps cause serious chemical burns to sensitive eyes and skin.
questions.socraticHint: Which sensitive facial organs must be protected from white plant sap?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Safety around euphorbia hedges in homesteads.

questions.prompt: Why should a thorn fence or wire mesh be placed around newly planted young tree seedlings?

options.text: To protect the tender green leaves from being eaten by goats, sheep, and cows
To keep the tree warm at night
To prevent rain from touching the seedling
To stop the tree from walking away

questions.explanation: Free-roaming livestock browse tender young leaves, killing seedlings unless protected by fencing.
questions.socraticHint: What grazing animals would love to chew on soft baby tree leaves?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Protecting school trees from village livestock.

questions.prompt: A pupil accidentally touches a stinging nettle (huruce) weed and feels burning itching on their arm. What is the BEST first step?

options.text: Ignore it and climb a thorny tree
Wash the arm gently with clean water and mild soap without scratching roughly
Rub dirt and mud into the scratch

questions.explanation: Washing gently with soap and cool water removes plant hairs and irritants without worsening skin inflammation.
questions.socraticHint: How does washing with clean water and soap soothe irritated skin?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Stinging nettles in Kenyan forests and farm edges.

questions.prompt: Kiprono and Achieng are weeding tomato plants in the school garden. They notice blackjack weeds with sticky needle-like seeds sticking to their clothes. Why is it important to weed blackjacks before they flower and produce seeds?

options.text: To prevent the weeds from dropping hundreds of new seeds that will multiply across the shamba

questions.explanation: Uprooting weeds before seed maturation breaks their reproductive cycle, keeping future gardens clean.
questions.socraticHint: What happens if weed seeds spread all over the soil before you pull them out?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Weed control in Kenyan agriculture.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: What combination of garden practices will produce the HEALTHIEST harvest of sukuma wiki in a school garden?

options.text: Planting in pure sand, never weeding, and watering at hot midday
Planting in cracked clay, letting livestock eat leaves, and adding salty water
Planting inside a dark cupboard without air or sunlight
Planting in fertile loam enriched with compost, watering early in the morning, weeding regularly, and mulching with dry leaves

questions.explanation: Combining fertile loam, compost manure, morning watering, timely weeding, and organic mulching guarantees bumper yields.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the option that combines all best farming practices together.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: 4K Club vegetable projects providing food for school lunches.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals is a DOMESTIC animal kept at home or on a shamba?
questions.explanation: A goat is a domestic animal raised by farmers for nutritious milk, meat, and skins.
questions.socraticHint: Think about which animal lives peacefully in a village homestead and is fed by farmers.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Goats grazing in rural homesteads across Machakos and Kitui.

questions.prompt: Chickens lay eggs that provide rich proteins for our breakfast and growth.
questions.explanation: Domestic chickens produce fresh eggs that are a delicious and protein-packed food for children.
questions.socraticHint: Think about what food chickens produce that we boil or fry for breakfast.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kienyeji chickens laying eggs in rural and peri-urban Kenya.

questions.prompt: The traditional fenced enclosure or wooden shed where cows and bulls sleep at night is called a ____.
questions.explanation: A cattle shed or fenced compound built to keep livestock safe at night is known as a boma.
questions.socraticHint: What Swahili word describes the secure wooden or thorny fence enclosure for livestock?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Livestock bomas across pastoralist and farming communities in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Match each domestic animal with its primary product or benefit to humans:
questions.explanation: Cows give milk, sheep yield wool, bees produce sweet honey, and donkeys assist with farm transport.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each animal with the food or work benefit it provides to farmers.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Products harvested on Kenyan smallholder farms.

questions.prompt: What special shelter is constructed to house domestic chickens and keep them safe from predators at night?
questions.explanation: A chicken coop (or poultry pen) provides safety, roosting perches, and nesting boxes for laying eggs.
questions.socraticHint: Which shelter is made with wire mesh or wood specifically for chickens?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Poultry coops built with timber and wire mesh in village compounds.

questions.prompt: It is good practice to leave farm animals without water on a hot sunny afternoon.
questions.explanation: Animals need clean water every day to survive and stay healthy, especially during hot weather.
questions.socraticHint: Would living animals suffer or fall sick if they do not drink water in the heat?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Providing water troughs for livestock in dry seasons in Garissa and Kajiado.

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for daily feeding and caring for a dairy cow in the correct sequence:
orderedItems: Clean out old dung and wet bedding from the cow shed
Provide fresh, chopped Napier grass and mineral lick in the trough
Fill the water container with cool, clean drinking water
Observe the cow to ensure it is healthy and content
questions.explanation: Cleaning the stall first prevents contamination of fresh feed, followed by giving fresh grass, water, and checking overall health.
questions.socraticHint: Start with cleaning the shed before putting fresh food into the trough.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Zero-grazing dairy farming routines in Kiambu and Nyeri.

questions.prompt: Which domestic animal is known for faithfully guarding the family home and barking when strangers approach?
questions.explanation: Dogs are loyal companions that alert families to visitors or intruders by barking.
questions.socraticHint: Which four-legged animal barks and lives in a kennel?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Homestead guard dogs in Kenyan rural and suburban homes.

questions.prompt: Rabbits are kept in wooden raised cages with wire mesh doors called a ____.
questions.explanation: A rabbit hutch is a raised wooden structure designed to keep rabbits warm, dry, and safe from ground pests.
questions.socraticHint: What specific English word beginning with letter H describes a cage for rabbits?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: 4K Club rabbit keeping projects in Kenyan primary schools.

questions.prompt: Wanjiku notices that the family goat is coughing, refuses to eat fresh potato vines, and is shivering in the shed. What should Wanjiku advise her father to do?
questions.storyScenario: Caring for a sick domestic animal on the farm.

options.text: Call an animal health officer (veterinary officer) to examine and treat the goat
Beat the goat with a stick to force it to eat
Chase the goat out of the compound into the road
Ignore the goat completely for two weeks

questions.explanation: Sick animals require professional medical attention from a veterinary officer to recover safely.
questions.socraticHint: Who is the expert doctor trained to treat sick livestock and farm animals?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sub-county veterinary services assisting Kenyan farmers.

questions.prompt: Which valuable fertilizer for growing maize and vegetables is produced from cow dung and animal bedding?
questions.explanation: Farmyard manure made from decomposed animal waste adds rich organic matter and nutrients to soil.
questions.socraticHint: What natural plant food is made by decomposing livestock waste?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Organic vegetable gardens in Kenyan homesteads using cow manure.

questions.prompt: Giving working donkeys very heavy loads beyond their strength is an act of cruelty that harms the animals.
questions.explanation: Animals must be treated with compassion. Overloading donkeys causes back injuries and exhaustion.
questions.socraticHint: Should we respect animals and protect them from pain and injury?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Animal welfare advocacy by KSPCA and communities caring for working donkeys.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals is a WILD animal that lives freely in Kenyan national parks and forests?
questions.explanation: A giraffe is a wild herbivore that browses on acacia tree leaves in open savanna grasslands.
questions.socraticHint: Which tall animal with a very long neck lives in game reserves, not in a home pen?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Giraffe Centre in Nairobi and Maasai Mara National Reserve.

questions.prompt: National parks like Amboseli and Tsavo are protected sanctuaries where wild animals can live safely without being hunted.
questions.explanation: Kenya Wildlife Service protects national parks so wild animals can breed, roam, and thrive in their natural habitat.
questions.socraticHint: Are national parks established to conserve wild nature and prevent poaching?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) conservation heritage.

questions.prompt: While playing near an old stone heap behind the classroom, Omondi spots a black snake sunning itself. What is the SAFEST action for Omondi to take?
questions.storyScenario: Encountering a snake in a school compound.

options.text: Try to catch the snake with bare hands
Poke the snake with a small stick to see if it moves
Stand still, slowly step backward without sudden movements, and alert the teacher immediately
Throw large stones at the snake to scare it

questions.explanation: Snakes strike when cornered or attacked. Stepping back calmly and calling an adult prevents dangerous bites.
questions.socraticHint: What peaceful, careful action avoids provoking the snake and brings an adult to handle it?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School compound safety drills across Kenyan rural primary schools.

questions.prompt: Match each wild animal with its natural home or habitat:
questions.explanation: Hippos cool down in water, monkeys swing through trees, lions hunt on open grasslands, and moles tunnel underground.
questions.socraticHint: Think about where each wild creature spends most of its day in nature.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Diverse Kenyan ecosystems from Lake Naivasha to the Mara plains.

questions.prompt: Why should pupils never throw stones at a swarm of bees or a wasps nest in a tree?

options.text: Bees will give away all their honey
Bees will fly into the classroom to write exams
The stones will turn into flowers
Bees will attack and sting anyone nearby, causing severe pain and swelling

questions.explanation: Disturbed bees defend their colony aggressively by stinging en masse, which is extremely dangerous.
questions.socraticHint: How do bees protect their queen and hive when someone attacks their home?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Safe beekeeping practices and tree safety in primary schools.

questions.prompt: The government agency responsible for protecting and managing wildlife throughout Kenya is called ____.
questions.explanation: The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) conserves and manages national parks and protects wildlife from poachers.
questions.socraticHint: Which organization wears olive green uniforms and guards our wild animals in parks?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenya Wildlife Service rangers on patrol in national parks.

questions.prompt: It is safe and advisable to stroke and pet an unknown stray dog walking on the road.
questions.explanation: Stray dogs can be aggressive or carry deadly diseases like rabies. Always keep your distance.
questions.socraticHint: Could a stray, unvaccinated dog bite and transmit rabies?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Rabies prevention and stray animal safety in Kenyan communities.

questions.prompt: Arrange the actions in order of safety if you discover a scorpion or centipede inside your shoe in the morning:
orderedItems: Always shake out boots or shoes upside down before putting your feet inside
Spot the crawling scorpion on the ground as it falls out
Move away calmly and keep your eyes on where it crawls
Call an adult immediately to safely remove it using a dustpan or broom
questions.explanation: Always inspect footwear first; if a pest falls out, step back safely and summon an adult to remove it.
questions.socraticHint: The very first habit is checking your footwear before putting your foot inside!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Common safety habits in semi-arid parts of Kenya like Turkana and Baringo.

questions.prompt: Why do international tourists visit Kenya from all over the world to see our wild animals?

options.text: Kenya has unique wildlife diversity and the famous Great Wildebeest Migration
Kenya has no trees or grass
To learn how to catch baboons for pets

questions.explanation: Kenya is world-renowned for its magnificent wildlife diversity, including the Big Five and the Maasai Mara migration.
questions.socraticHint: What world-famous natural spectacle happens annually in the Maasai Mara?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan eco-tourism driving national income and conservation.

questions.prompt: A tiny insect pest that bites cattle and domestic animals to suck their blood and spread East Coast Fever is a ____.
questions.explanation: Ticks attach to the skin of livestock to suck blood and transmit tick-borne diseases. Farmers use cattle dips to control them.
questions.socraticHint: What small eight-legged parasite is removed from cows during dipping?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Community cattle dips across farming counties in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Cutting down forests destroys the natural homes and food sources of wild animals like monkeys and elephants.
questions.explanation: Deforestation causes habitat loss, forcing wildlife out of their natural homes into human farmlands.
questions.socraticHint: Do wild animals rely on indigenous forests for shelter, water, and food?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Forest conservation around Mount Kenya, Mau Forest, and Kakamega Forest.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Baraka is walking home from school and sees baboons raiding maize cobs near the edge of a shamba. How should Baraka behave?
questions.storyScenario: Living in harmony with wildlife while maintaining safety.

options.text: Throw his shoes at the baboons
Keep a safe distance, do not tease or throw rocks at them, walk past quietly, and tell farm owners or village elders
Run directly at the baboons waving his school bag to fight them
Offer his lunch chapati to the big male baboon from his hand

questions.explanation: Baboons have sharp canines and can attack if threatened or approached. Staying clear and alerting adults ensures safety.
questions.socraticHint: Remember the golden rule: never approach, challenge, or feed wild primates directly.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Living adjacent to wildlife corridors in Laikipia and Rongai.

questions.prompt: What is the MAIN natural source of both light and heat for planet Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is our primary natural source of energy, bathing the Earth in bright light and vital warming heat.
questions.socraticHint: Which celestial body shines brightly in the daytime sky?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Abundant daily sunshine powering life across Kenya.

questions.prompt: Looking directly at the blazing sun with bare eyes is completely safe and harmless for children.
questions.explanation: Looking straight at the sun can severely burn the sensitive retina inside your eyes and cause permanent vision loss.
questions.socraticHint: Can intense ultraviolet light from the sun damage your eyesight?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sun safety and eye health lessons in Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: When an opaque object blocks the path of light, a dark shape called a ____ is formed on the ground.
questions.explanation: A shadow forms behind an object because light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through solid opaque objects.
questions.socraticHint: What dark silhouette follows you around when you walk outdoors on a sunny day?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Playing shadow games under acacia trees in the afternoon.

questions.prompt: Match each energy source with its primary everyday use in a Kenyan home:

matchingPairs.rightText: Generating electricity to charge phones and light lamps
Cooking ugali and boiling water in a sufuria
Drying wet washed clothes on a clothesline
Finding your way along dark paths at night

questions.explanation: Solar panels power lamps, jikos provide cooking heat, sunshine dries laundry, and torches guide nighttime steps.
questions.socraticHint: Match each item to the task it accomplishes in the household.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Household energy practices in Kenyan urban and rural homes.

questions.prompt: Why do farmers in Kitui and Machakos spread harvested maize cobs on a canvas tarpaulin in the direct sun?

options.text: To feed the birds and wild baboons
To melt the cobs into porridge liquid
To use heat from the sun to dry the grains so they do not rot in storage
To change the color of the maize to purple

questions.explanation: Solar heat evaporates moisture from grain, preventing mold and weevil attacks so food stores safely.
questions.socraticHint: What does heat do to moisture in damp cereal grains?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Post-harvest grain drying practices in Kenyan agricultural communities.

questions.prompt: A lit charcoal jiko should never be kept inside an unventilated bedroom with closed windows while sleeping.
questions.explanation: Burning charcoal in a closed room produces deadly, odorless carbon monoxide gas which can cause suffocation and death.
questions.socraticHint: Does burning charcoal in an airtight room produce poisonous fumes?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Public health awareness on jiko carbon monoxide poisoning prevention.

questions.prompt: Order the steps for safely handling a hot metal sufuria on a cooking fire:
orderedItems: Put on thick cloth potholders or use dry heat-resistant cooking mittens
Firmly grip both handles of the hot metal sufuria
Carefully lift the sufuria off the fire without splashing hot stew
Place the hot pot safely on a flat heat-proof trivet away from younger siblings
questions.explanation: Using thick cloth prevents hand burns, lifting steadily avoids scalds, and setting it down safely protects everyone.
questions.socraticHint: Protect your hands first before touching the blazing hot metal handles.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kitchen safety rules while preparing meals in Kenyan families.

questions.prompt: Which of the following objects produces light when switched on?
questions.explanation: A torch converts electrical energy from batteries into bright light to illuminate dark spaces.
questions.socraticHint: Which electrical tool has a bulb that lights up when you press its switch?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Handheld battery and solar torches used in homes.

questions.prompt: Modern clean lighting systems that collect energy from sunlight using rooftop panels are called ____ systems.
questions.explanation: Solar home systems capture renewable clean sunlight and provide eco-friendly light without smelly smoke.
questions.socraticHint: What word relates to the sun and solar panels on rooftops?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Widespread adoption of off-grid solar home systems in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Moraa is studying in the evening. Her mother wants to replace the old smoky tin kerosene lamp (koroboi) with a solar LED lantern. What is the BIGGEST benefit for Moraa?
questions.storyScenario: Choosing healthy, clean lighting for school study.

options.text: Clean bright light that does not emit soot, smoke, or sting her eyes while studying
The lantern will do her homework automatically
The lantern makes a loud whistling siren
The lamp requires charcoal to be loaded every hour

questions.explanation: Solar LED lanterns produce bright, steady light without toxic smoke or dangerous fire hazards, keeping lungs and eyes healthy.
questions.socraticHint: How does smokeless electric solar light protect a child’s eyes and lungs compared to soot from a koroboi?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Replacing kerosene lamps with solar lanterns across rural Kenyan counties.

questions.prompt: What happens to the length of your shadow when you stand outdoors at NOON when the Sun is directly overhead?

options.text: It is very short, right under your feet
It is ten meters long stretching far away
It flies high up into the clouds

questions.explanation: When the sun is high directly overhead at midday, shadows are at their shortest, cast directly beneath objects.
questions.socraticHint: Think about where light shines from when the sun is straight above your head at 12 o’clock noon.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Observing shadows during school midday playtime.

questions.prompt: Water boils when heated to 100 degrees Celsius, producing steam that can cause severe skin burns if touched.
questions.explanation: Boiling water and hot steam carry immense heat and can cause painful scalds; always keep a safe distance.
questions.socraticHint: Is steaming hot boiling water capable of burning skin?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kitchen safety around hot water kettles in Kenyan homes.

questions.prompt: How is sound produced when someone speaks, sings, or beats an instrument?
questions.explanation: All sounds originate from rapid back-and-forth vibrations of matter that travel as sound waves through the air.
questions.socraticHint: What physical movement happens to a drum skin or vocal cords when producing sound?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Music and sound exploration in CBC Grade 3 science.

questions.prompt: A gentle lullaby sung to a baby is an example of a pleasant, soothing sound.
questions.explanation: Pleasant sounds are melodious, gentle, and calming to human ears.
questions.socraticHint: Does a soft lullaby help a baby fall asleep peacefully?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan traditional cradle songs and lullabies.

questions.prompt: Unwanted, excessively loud sound that disturbs peace and can harm our hearing is called ____ pollution.
questions.explanation: Noise pollution refers to disturbing or harmful levels of noise that disrupt concentration, sleep, and well-being.
questions.socraticHint: What five-letter word describes loud, unpleasant sound that irritates the ears?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Regulations by NEMA to curb excessive noise in residential areas.

questions.prompt: Match each sound maker with the type of sound it produces:
questions.explanation: Flutes produce musical tones, sirens create sharp warnings, roosters crow, and leaves produce a soft rustle.
questions.socraticHint: Match each object to the character of sound it sends into the air.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sounds of village and urban environments in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which of the following actions is VERY DANGEROUS for your ears and should NEVER be done?

options.text: Listening to a teacher speak during assembly
Pushing sharp matchsticks, toothpicks, or pen caps into the ear canal
Washing the outside of the ears with soap and water

questions.explanation: Inserting sharp objects into the ear canal can puncture the delicate eardrum, leading to severe infection and deafness.
questions.socraticHint: Can poking sharp pointed things inside your ear tear your eardrum?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Ear hygiene lessons taught by community health nurses in schools.

questions.prompt: Sound can travel through air, liquids (like water), and solid objects (like a wooden door).
questions.explanation: Vibrations can travel through solids, liquids, and gases; for example, you can hear a knock through a wooden door.
questions.socraticHint: Can you hear someone tapping on the other side of a closed wooden desk?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Hands-on sound experiments using tin cans and string in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of how a child hears a school bell ringing:
orderedItems: The school prefect strikes the metal bell with an iron rod
The metal bell vibrates rapidly, setting air particles around it into motion
Sound vibrations travel through the air as sound waves across the school field
The sound waves enter the child’s ears and the brain recognizes it is time for break
questions.explanation: The bell vibrates upon impact, transfers wave vibrations through air particles, and enters the ear for hearing.
questions.socraticHint: What action happens first at the bell post, and how do waves travel to your ears?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The ringing of the school bell announcing morning assembly or break time.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a traditional Kenyan musical instrument played by blowing air into it?
questions.explanation: The Abu or animal horn is a wind instrument sounded by blowing air through the mouth hole.
questions.socraticHint: Which instrument produces sound from the breath of your mouth like a trumpet or horn?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional wind instruments in Kenyan musical heritage.

questions.prompt: Workers operating noisy jackhammers or chain saws wear cushioned ear ____ to protect their hearing from deafening noise.
questions.explanation: Earmuffs or ear defenders absorb acoustic energy and lower the decibel level reaching human ears.
questions.socraticHint: What protective headphone-like gear shields workers’ ears from loud machine noise?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Occupational safety equipment in Kenyan road construction sites.

questions.prompt: Listening to music on mobile phone headphones at maximum volume for hours every day keeps your hearing sharp and strong.
questions.explanation: Excessive volume directly into ear canals damages auditory nerve cells and leads to premature hearing loss.
questions.socraticHint: Does high sound intensity damage fragile sensory cells inside the ear?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Digital health and headphone safety for young learners.

questions.prompt: Why do hospitals and schools put up signs with a picture of a horn with a red slash through it (NO HONKING)?

options.text: To prevent loud noise that disturbs sick patients and studying students
Because horns consume too much petrol
To tell drivers that horns are free to buy
Because horn sounds scare the clouds away

questions.explanation: Hospital and school zones require peace and quiet so patients can heal and learners can concentrate without distraction.
questions.socraticHint: Why is quietness essential for healing patients and focused classroom learning?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Quiet zones outside Kenyan hospitals like Kenyatta National Hospital.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: A pupil sitting next to you during music practice has water trapped in their ear after swimming and complains it feels itchy. What is the BEST medical advice?
questions.storyScenario: Practicing proper ear hygiene and care.

options.text: Push small pebbles inside the ear canal
Tilt the head sideways toward the affected ear to let the water drain naturally, and see the school nurse if pain continues
Poke a sharp pencil lead deep into the ear to scratch the itch
Pour salty dirty water into the ear to push the other water out

questions.explanation: Tilting the head allows gravity to drain trapped water safely without risking mechanical injury to the eardrum.
questions.socraticHint: Which method uses gentle posture and gravity without inserting any objects into the ear?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: First aid and school dispensary advice for ear care.

questions.prompt: What is the HIGHEST mountain in Kenya, known for its snow-capped peaks and indigenous forests?
questions.explanation: Mount Kenya is the highest mountain in Kenya (and second highest in Africa) with peaks Batian, Nelion, and Lenana.
questions.socraticHint: Which mountain gives our nation its proud name Kenya?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mount Kenya (Kirinyaga), a major national water tower and UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.prompt: A valley is a low-lying stretch of land located between hills or mountains.
questions.explanation: A valley is the lower land nestled between highland hills or mountain ridges.
questions.socraticHint: Think about the land formation that dips down between two hills.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Great Rift Valley passing through Nakuru, Baringo, and Naivasha.

questions.prompt: A large flat area of grassland where wild animals graze and pastoralists keep herds is called a ____.
questions.explanation: Plains are broad, level grasslands, such as the Kapiti Plains or Serengeti-Mara Plains.
questions.socraticHint: What word describes flat, open land without steep hills?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Athi-Kapiti plains in Kajiado and Machakos.

questions.prompt: Match each Kenyan physical feature with its distinctive description:

matchingPairs.rightText: Largest freshwater lake providing fish like tilapia
Longest river in Kenya generating hydroelectric power
Highest mountain with permanent snow and ice
Deep, dramatic geological valley cutting across Kenya

questions.explanation: Lake Victoria gives fish, River Tana powers hydro dams, Mt Kenya has snow, and the Rift Valley is a vast trench.
questions.socraticHint: Match each geographical feature with its prominent landmark quality.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Geography of Kenya taught in CBC Grade 3 Environmental Activities.

questions.prompt: Why are forested mountains called "water towers" of Kenya?

options.text: Because rain only falls inside caves
Because fish swim up the trees
Their trees trap rainfall and release clean water into streams and rivers all year round
Because metal water tanks are built on the peaks

questions.explanation: Forested mountain catchment areas capture atmospheric moisture and feed the rivers that provide water to cities and farms.
questions.socraticHint: How do natural forest trees catch clouds and keep river streams flowing constantly?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Conservation of the Five Water Towers (Mau, Mt. Kenya, Aberdares, Mt. Elgon, Cherangany).

questions.prompt: Throwing garbage and plastic bottles into flowing rivers is a good way to clean the school compound.
questions.explanation: Dumping waste in rivers pollutes clean water, kills aquatic life, and spreads diseases like cholera to people downstream.
questions.socraticHint: Does dumping waste in rivers poison the drinking water of people and animals living downstream?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Nairobi River and local stream clean-up campaigns.

questions.prompt: Arrange the path of water from a mountain stream to a lake in order of flow:
orderedItems: Rain falls on high forested mountain slopes and forms tiny springs
Small bubbling streams join together to form a wide flowing river
The river flows steadily through valleys and plains
The river empties its fresh water into a large lake or ocean
questions.explanation: Water starts at high mountain springs, flows into streams, forms larger rivers in valleys, and empties into lakes or seas.
questions.socraticHint: Water always flows downhill from high mountain peaks toward lower lakes and oceans.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: River basins flowing into Lake Victoria and the Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which physical feature consists of a large body of salty water along Mombasa, Kilifi, and Lamu?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean borders Kenya along its southeastern coast, providing sandy beaches and maritime transport.
questions.socraticHint: Which huge body of salt water borders the coastal port city of Mombasa?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Kenyan coastline and Mombasa port along the Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: A steep face of rock or high cliff created by natural earth movements along the Rift Valley is an ____.
questions.explanation: An escarpment (like the Kikuyu Escarpment or Elgeyo Escarpment) is a steep cliff bordering the Rift Valley floor.
questions.socraticHint: What term describes the steep drop or cliff seen when driving down to Mai Mahiu from Limuru?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Viewpoints along the Great Rift Valley escarpment.

questions.prompt: Residents living on the steep slopes of Murang’a and Nandi hills cut down all trees to plant tea and vegetables. During heavy rains, the soil slides down the hill. What caused this landslide?

options.text: Cutting down trees destroyed the root network that held soil firmly on the steep hillside
The sun was shining too brightly
The tea bushes drank all the rocks

questions.explanation: Tree roots bind soil particles together. Removing trees on steep hills leaves soil exposed to landslides during downpours.
questions.socraticHint: What holds loose soil tightly on slopes to stop it from washing down during heavy rains?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Soil conservation and agroforestry on hillside farms in central and western Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which economic activity is commonly carried out in communities living near Lake Victoria and Lake Turkana?
questions.explanation: Lakes provide abundant fish stocks (like tilapia, Nile perch, and omena), supporting thriving fishing communities.
questions.socraticHint: What food do fishermen catch with nets and boats on large lakes?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fishing communities at Dunga Beach in Kisumu and Kalokol on Lake Turkana.

questions.prompt: Planting indigenous trees along riverbanks helps protect the river from drying up and prevents soil erosion.

questions.socraticHint: Which item is made of metal and can be remelted in a factory?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Scrap metal recycling in Jua Kali centers.

questions.prompt: A creative art project where old plastic bottle caps and waste paper are made into toys or mosaics is called up-____.
questions.explanation: Upcycling turns discarded waste items into beautiful artwork, crafts, or practical toys of higher value.
questions.socraticHint: Combining "up" with "cycling" gives the word for creative reuse of scrap.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Creative arts projects using recycled materials in CBC Grade 3.

questions.prompt: At lunchtime, Kiptoo sees pupils littering empty biscuit wrappers all over the school assembly grounds. What is the BEST leadership action for Kiptoo to take?
questions.storyScenario: Fostering school environmental sanitation and civic responsibility.

options.text: Pick up the wrappers, drop them in the litter bin, and politely remind peers to keep the school clean
Throw his own banana peels on the principal’s doorway
Shout and start throwing rocks at the pupils
Hide inside the classroom and ignore the rubbish

questions.explanation: Leading by example and reminding peers courteously creates an inspiring culture of cleanliness and environmental care.
questions.socraticHint: How can Kiptoo set a positive example and keep the school grounds spotless?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Environmental health clubs in Kenyan primary schools.

questions.prompt: What happens to domestic animals like goats and cows when they accidentally swallow plastic bags dumped on grazing grounds?

options.text: The plastic gives them extra energy
The plastic blocks their digestive stomach (rumen) causing sickness or death

questions.explanation: Plastic bags cannot be digested by livestock; they form deadly ball blockages in stomachs and kill animals.
questions.socraticHint: Does swallowed plastic choke and clog the digestive stomachs of ruminant animals?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Protecting grazing livestock from plastic pollution in rural areas.

questions.prompt: Cleaning our school latrines regularly with disinfectant water prevents bad smells and the spread of diarrheal diseases.
questions.explanation: Regular latrine sanitization with soap, ash, or disinfectant stops flies from carrying germs to our food.
questions.socraticHint: Does washing latrines stop flies and keep bacteria away from children?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) school programs in Kenya.

questions.prompt: At what critical moments MUST you always wash your hands thoroughly with clean water and soap?

options.text: After visiting the toilet, before eating meals, and after touching animals or soil
Only when your hands turn completely black with soot

questions.explanation: Washing hands after the toilet, before eating, and after soil exposure destroys disease-causing pathogens.
questions.socraticHint: Think about the times when germs are most likely to enter your mouth from your fingers.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Global Handwashing Day activities celebrated in Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: Washing hands with water alone without using soap is just as effective at killing stubborn germs and bacteria.
questions.explanation: Soap is essential because it dissolves oily germ membranes and lifts microscopic pathogens off the skin.
questions.socraticHint: Does soap break down greasy bacteria that plain water cannot rinse away alone?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Handwashing hygiene education in primary schools.

questions.prompt: A water-saving hygiene device made of a suspended container with a tiny hole tipped by a foot string is a ____.
questions.explanation: A tippy-tap provides hands-free running water for washing with minimal water wastage and zero tap contact.
questions.socraticHint: What innovative foot-operated washing tin is built outside latrines in rural schools?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tippy-taps installed beside pit latrines in Kenyan rural primary schools.

questions.prompt: Match each minor accident with its immediate first aid treatment:

matchingPairs.rightText: Cool immediately under clean running water for 10 minutes
Clean with safe water, pat dry, and cover with a sterile plaster
Rinse gently with clean cool water without rubbing the eye
Pinch soft nostrils gently and lean the head slightly forward

questions.explanation: Cool water soothes burns, gentle washing cleans cuts, rinsing clears dust, and pinching stops nosebleeds.
questions.socraticHint: Match each injury with the scientifically proven emergency first response.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: First aid training provided by the Kenya Red Cross Society in schools.

questions.prompt: What harmful thing should NEVER be smeared on a burn or scald wound?

options.text: Cooking fat, raw eggs, engine grease, or toothpaste

questions.explanation: Grease, eggs, and toothpaste trap heat inside the flesh and cause severe wound infections.
questions.socraticHint: Which common household items trap heat and contaminate open burns?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dispelling dangerous myths about burn treatments in first aid.

questions.prompt: If a stranger offers you sweets, money, or a lift in a car outside the school gate, you should accept happily.
questions.explanation: Never accept treats, money, or rides from strangers as it poses a serious child safety risk.
questions.socraticHint: Is it dangerous to accept gifts or rides from people you do not know?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Child protection guidelines and stranger danger awareness.

questions.prompt: Arrange the proper steps for thorough handwashing with soap and water:
orderedItems: Wet hands with clean running water and apply enough soap
Rub palms together, lather between fingers, back of hands, and under nails for 20 seconds
Rinse hands thoroughly under clean running water until all soap is gone
Dry hands with a clean single-use towel or let them air-dry
questions.explanation: Wet and lather for 20 seconds, scrub all finger crevices, rinse fully under running water, and dry cleanly.
questions.socraticHint: Wet and lather first, scrub all parts of the fingers, then rinse and dry.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Proper hand hygiene steps taught in primary school science.

questions.prompt: What special kit containing plasters, bandages, antiseptic, and scissors should every school classroom have?
questions.explanation: A First Aid Kit provides immediate medical supplies to treat minor classroom injuries and cuts.
questions.socraticHint: What emergency box marked with a red or green cross holds bandages and medicine?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom first aid boxes in primary schools.

questions.prompt: The emergency toll-free child helpline number in Kenya that children can dial for help and protection is ____.
questions.explanation: Childline Kenya operates the free national helpline 116 to protect children from abuse, danger, and exploitation.
questions.socraticHint: What three-digit number starting with 11 protects children across Kenya free of charge?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Child Helpline 116 operated by Childline Kenya.

questions.prompt: Your body belongs to you, and nobody has the right to touch you in private areas that make you feel uncomfortable or scared.
questions.explanation: Every child has bodily autonomy. If someone tries to touch private parts or makes you uncomfortable, shout NO and tell a trusted adult.
questions.socraticHint: Do you have the absolute right to protect your body and report inappropriate touches?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Child rights and bodily autonomy education in CBC.

questions.prompt: If you see an unfamiliar vehicle following you while walking home from school, what should you do immediately?

options.text: Walk briskly toward a crowded, safe place (like a busy shop or school gate) and scream for help
Climb inside the car boot to play hide and seek
Walk deeper into an isolated bush
Sit on the ground and close your eyes

questions.explanation: Moving quickly toward crowded public places and calling for help protects children from abduction and danger.
questions.socraticHint: Where is it safest: in a busy populated shop or alone in a dark corner?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Personal safety and community vigilance in Kenyan neighborhoods.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: During sports day, Nekesa trips on the running track and scrapes her knee, causing slight bleeding. How should the first aid team assist Nekesa?
questions.storyScenario: Demonstrating complete first aid care for playground wounds.

options.text: Ignore Nekesa and make her run five more laps
Clean the scrape gently with antiseptic water, pat dry with sterile gauze, apply a sterile adhesive plaster, and offer comforting words
Rub garden dirt and dry leaves into the open wound
Pour boiling hot tea on the knee

questions.explanation: Proper wound care cleans out dirt, stops infection with antiseptic dressing, and comforts the injured child.
questions.socraticHint: Which compassionate option properly washes and covers the scrape with clean sterile materials?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School Red Cross first aid teams on Sports Day.

questions.prompt: What type of line looks like sharp mountain peaks or flashes of thunderstorm lightning?
questions.explanation: A zigzag line changes direction sharply with sharp points, resembling lightning bolts or mountain peaks.
questions.socraticHint: Which line moves back and forth in sharp diagonal angles?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Patterns seen on traditional shields and beadwork.

questions.prompt: A line that runs flat from left to right like the calm surface of a lake is called a horizontal line.
questions.explanation: Horizontal lines run side to side across the page, just like the flat horizon where the sky meets the earth.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the word horizon when looking at flat open plains.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Flat horizons across the Kapiti Plains.

questions.prompt: A line that coils round and round outward from a central point like a snail shell is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: A spiral line curves continuously around a central point, winding steadily inward or outward.
questions.socraticHint: What word describes the coiled shape of a coiled spring or snail shell?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Spiral patterns on traditional ear ornaments and seashells at Diani.

questions.prompt: Match each type of line with an example found in nature or art:

matchingPairs.rightText: Gentle water ripples on a river
Tall straight trunk of a blue gum tree

questions.explanation: Waves ripple in curves, crocodile teeth are zigzags, tree trunks stand vertically, and chameleon tails coil in spirals.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each line type to the object that shares its distinct physical shape.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan wildlife and landscapes observed during nature walks.

questions.prompt: What artistic technique uses closely spaced parallel lines to create shade and darkness on an object?
questions.explanation: Hatching is drawing closely spaced parallel lines to create shadows and surface tone in sketches.
questions.socraticHint: What drawing term starting with H refers to parallel shading lines?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Shading techniques taught in Grade 3 art classes.

questions.prompt: Pressing a drawing pencil very hard onto the paper makes light, faint lines that are easy to erase.
questions.explanation: Pressing hard creates deep, dark grooves that tear paper and leave permanent marks when erased; artists sketch lightly first.
questions.socraticHint: Does heavy pressure make light lines or very dark deep marks?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pencil control skills in art and craft.

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for drawing a decorative geometric border on a picture frame:
orderedItems: Use a ruler to draw two straight parallel border lines around the page
Sketch repeating zigzag or triangle shapes inside the border lightly with pencil
Add wavy or dotted lines between the shapes to create an intricate pattern
Color the pattern neatly with contrasting bright crayon colors
questions.explanation: Frame lines first, sketch shapes, add detailed secondary lines, and complete by coloring brightly.
questions.socraticHint: Start with measuring the frame before adding the internal shapes and color.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Decorative borders in book covers and classroom wall charts.

questions.prompt: Which drawing tool is best for sketching faint outlines that can be easily corrected with a rubber eraser?
questions.explanation: An HB pencil produces clean, light lines that erase cleanly without smudging or ripping the paper.
questions.socraticHint: Which wooden stationery item contains erasable graphite lead?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: School stationery used daily by Kenyan primary school pupils.

questions.prompt: When two sets of parallel lines cross each other like a wire fence, the shading technique is called ____-hatching.
questions.explanation: Cross-hatching intersects two sets of lines at angles to produce deeper shade and shadow.
questions.socraticHint: What word means intersecting or making an X-like criss-cross pattern?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Texture rendering in Grade 3 drawing lessons.

questions.prompt: Amina wants to draw the ripples created when a pebble is tossed into a quiet river. Which combination of lines will best show the moving water ripples?
questions.storyScenario: Choosing line types to portray water movement.

options.text: Curved and concentric circular wavy lines spreading outward
Sharp vertical straight lines pointing to the sky
Tiny square boxes stacked like bricks

questions.explanation: Concentric expanding circles and curved ripples naturally depict the radiating waves of disturbed water.
questions.socraticHint: Think about what circular rings expand outward when a stone splashes in water.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Watching river ripples along the banks of River Yala or Sagana.

questions.prompt: What visual effect is created when you repeat the same pattern of lines over and over across a surface?
questions.explanation: Repetition of lines and motifs creates visual rhythm, harmony, and interesting textures.
questions.socraticHint: Just like repeating beats in music, repeating shapes in art creates visual rhythm.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Decorative basket and fabric patterns.

questions.prompt: Cleaning your eraser and keeping your drawing book free of pencil smudges is part of good art craftsmanship.
questions.explanation: Caring for drawing surfaces and keeping work clean is a fundamental CBC craft value.
questions.socraticHint: Does neatness and cleanliness improve the presentation of your artwork?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Assessment of neatness in CBC Art portfolios.

questions.prompt: What do artists call a drawing or painting of non-moving objects like a bowl of fruits or clay pots?
questions.explanation: Still life is the art of drawing stationary, inanimate objects placed together on a table.
questions.socraticHint: Which term has the word "still" because the objects do not move?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Still life compositions of tropical fruits and clay utensils.

questions.prompt: When coloring a drawn object, scribbling quickly outside the black outline makes the picture look neat and tidy.
questions.explanation: Neat coloring requires keeping strokes inside the object’s outline boundaries with controlled hand movements.
questions.socraticHint: Does coloring outside the lines make an artwork look neat or messy?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fine motor control skills developed in lower primary.

questions.prompt: A traditional African clay cooking pot usually has a round body and a circular opening called a ____.
questions.explanation: The top circular edge of a clay pot where food or liquid enters is called the rim or mouth.
questions.socraticHint: What do we call the circular lip or top edge of a cup or pot?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Earthenware cooking pots (nyungu) crafted in Kenyan villages.

questions.prompt: Match each Kenyan fruit with its basic geometric drawing shape:

matchingPairs.rightText: Oval with a gentle bottom curve
Crescent curve tapering at both ends
Triangle with a curved rind base

questions.explanation: Oranges are round circles, mangoes are ovals, bananas are crescents, and watermelon slices form triangles.
questions.socraticHint: Think about the simple shape you sketch first before adding details.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tropical fruits sold at Kongowea and Gikomba markets.

questions.prompt: Why do artists add dark shading to the underside of a fruit in a still-life drawing?

options.text: To hide the fruit so no one sees it
Because fruits always burn in the dark
To show shadow and make the fruit look solid and 3-dimensional
To make the paper heavy so it does not blow away

questions.explanation: Shading simulates shadows cast by light, giving flat shapes roundness and 3D depth.
questions.socraticHint: How does shading make a flat 2D circle look like a round 3D ball?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Observational drawing in Grade 3 Art.

questions.prompt: Looking closely at real fruits placed on a table while drawing them is called drawing from direct observation.
questions.explanation: Observational drawing trains learners to notice real proportions, curves, light, and textures directly from life.
questions.socraticHint: Does drawing from observation mean looking at real objects while sketching?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Still life setups in school art corners.

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for drawing and coloring a ripe sweet pineapple:
orderedItems: Draw an upright oval shape for the body of the pineapple
Add a crown of spiky, pointed leaves at the top using zigzag and curved lines
Draw diagonal criss-cross lines across the body to create the diamond skin pattern
Color the diamonds golden yellow and brown, and color the leaves rich green
questions.explanation: Start with the body oval, add top crown leaves, draw criss-cross diamond texture, and finish with colors.
questions.socraticHint: Sketch the main oval body first before adding leaves and diamond textures.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pineapples grown in Thika and Malindi.

questions.prompt: What technique helps blend crayon colors smoothly when coloring a ripe sunset mango from green to yellow and red?

options.text: Dipping the crayon into boiling cooking oil
Tearing the paper into tiny bits
Scraping the crayon with a rusty iron nail
Overlapping the edges of the colors gently with light strokes

questions.explanation: Overlapping and blending colors softly where they meet creates a natural color transition.
questions.socraticHint: How do you transition smoothly from one color to another on paper?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Color blending on tropical fruit drawings.

questions.prompt: The flat surface or horizontal line on which still-life objects sit in a drawing is called the ____ line.
questions.explanation: The table or ground line establishes a base so drawn objects do not appear to float in empty air.
questions.socraticHint: What horizontal baseline anchors objects so they look resting on a table?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Composition basics in primary school art.

questions.prompt: Using a wax crayon requires sharpening it in an electric machine every two minutes.
questions.explanation: Wax crayons can be used blunt for broad shading or gently peeled; they do not need constant machine sharpening.
questions.socraticHint: Are wax crayons durable and easy to shade with without sharp points?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Crayon handling in lower primary classes.

questions.prompt: Which traditional artifact has a narrow neck, rounded belly, and is made from a dried gourd, making it an excellent still-life subject?
questions.explanation: A calabash (kibuyu) is an iconic traditional vessel with beautiful natural curves ideal for still-life drawing.
questions.socraticHint: Which hollow dried gourd is used to store porridge and milk?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional gourds sketched in CBC cultural art.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Mwangi drew a clay pot and a ripe pawpaw on his paper, but they look like they are floating in the sky. What simple line should Mwangi add to make them look resting on a surface?

options.text: Color the whole page completely black with ink
Draw a horizontal tabletop line behind and underneath the objects, and add gentle cast shadows
Draw wings on the clay pot so it flies higher
Cut the paper into shreds and throw it away

questions.explanation: Adding a tabletop line and subtle cast shadows anchors objects firmly onto a resting surface.
questions.socraticHint: What horizontal line represents the tabletop where the pot and fruit sit?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Compositional techniques taught in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Which group contains the THREE PRIMARY COLORS that cannot be made by mixing other colors?
questions.explanation: Red, Yellow, and Blue are the foundational primary colors from which other colors are mixed.
questions.socraticHint: Which three colors sit at the root of the color wheel?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Basic color theory in CBC Grade 3 Art & Craft.

questions.prompt: When you mix Yellow paint with Blue paint, you create the secondary color GREEN.
questions.explanation: Yellow combined with blue produces green, the vibrant color of healthy leaves and grass.
questions.socraticHint: What color do you get when the golden sun (yellow) meets the blue sky on a fresh leaf?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mixing green to paint lush landscapes in Kericho.

questions.prompt: Mixing Red paint and Yellow paint together produces the secondary color ____.
questions.explanation: Red and Yellow blend to form orange, like ripe oranges or a glowing sunset.
questions.socraticHint: Which warm secondary color shares its name with a citrus fruit?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Painting sunsets across the Great Rift Valley.

questions.prompt: Match each color mixing recipe with the resulting secondary color:
questions.explanation: Red+Yellow makes orange, Yellow+Blue makes green, Blue+Red makes purple, and White+Black makes grey.
questions.socraticHint: Match the primary pairs to the exact secondary color they produce.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Color mixing experiments in primary art studios.

questions.prompt: Why must you rinse your paintbrush in clean water before dipping it into a different color paint?

options.text: To make the paint turn into ice
To avoid contaminating and muddying the clean paint in the palette

questions.explanation: Washing the brush keeps paints pure and vibrant without unintentional muddy mixing.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to clean bright yellow paint if you dip a brush covered in dark blue into it?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Brush care and studio hygiene in CBC classrooms.

questions.prompt: Secondary colors can be created by mixing any two secondary colors together.
questions.explanation: Secondary colors are specifically made by mixing two PRIMARY colors together.
questions.socraticHint: Are secondary colors produced from primary colors or from other secondaries?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Color wheel concepts in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for painting a picture with poster colors:
orderedItems: Sketch the picture lightly on paper using an HB pencil
Prepare your palette with small blobs of primary paint and a container of clean water
Dip brush in paint and apply smooth strokes inside the outlined areas
Rinse brush thoroughly and allow the painting to dry flat in a safe area
questions.explanation: Sketch first, prepare paint and water, paint within shapes, and rinse brush while letting work dry.
questions.socraticHint: Start with pencil sketch before wetting the brush with paint.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Art classroom painting routines.

questions.prompt: What flat board or tray do artists use to hold and mix small portions of paint?
questions.explanation: A palette is a flat surface (plastic, wood, or ceramic) on which artists lay out and mix colors.
questions.socraticHint: What special artist’s tray holds little dollops of paint?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Art equipment used in CBC creative practicals.

questions.prompt: Blue mixed with Red produces the regal secondary color ____.
questions.explanation: Blue and red blend into purple (violet), resembling ripe passion fruit or jacaranda blossoms.
questions.socraticHint: What deep floral color comes from combining blue and red?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Jacaranda blossoms in Nairobi during October.

questions.prompt: Njeri wants to paint a bright green grasshopper, but her paint box only has Red, Yellow, and Blue poster colors. How can Njeri make green paint?
questions.storyScenario: Solving a painting challenge through color mixing.

options.text: Mix Yellow paint and Blue paint together on her palette
Add mud from outside into the red paint
Give up and not paint the grasshopper

questions.explanation: Combining yellow and blue produces green, giving Njeri the exact hue she needs for the grasshopper.
questions.socraticHint: Which two primary colors combine to create leafy green?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Creative problem-solving in primary science and art.

questions.prompt: What natural objects can pupils use as creative stamps to print patterns with paint?

options.text: Cut potatoes, okra ladyfingers, leaves, and bottle tops

questions.explanation: Cut vegetables like potatoes, okra, and tree leaves make safe, eco-friendly stamping tools for printing patterns.
questions.socraticHint: Which safe kitchen vegetables and leaves have natural shapes for block printing?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Block printing using locally available materials in Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: Leaving paintbrushes resting head-down inside a water cup for days bends and damages their soft bristles.
questions.explanation: Leaving brushes squashed bristles-down permanently curls and ruins the brush tips; dry them flat or upright.
questions.socraticHint: Will heavy pressure bend the delicate hairs of a paintbrush permanently?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tool maintenance and care in school art rooms.

questions.prompt: What is a MOSAIC in art and craft?

options.text: A metal nail driven into wood
A picture made by pasting small pieces of colored paper, stone, or seeds side by side
A song sung by three people
A dance performed on one foot

questions.explanation: A mosaic is an artwork created by arranging and gluing small individual pieces (tesserae, paper, or seeds) onto a design.
questions.socraticHint: Which artwork arranges tiny individual pieces like a puzzle to form a picture?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Seed and paper mosaic projects in CBC Grade 3.

questions.prompt: In a collage, you can combine different materials like fabric scraps, eggshells, dried banana bark, and colored paper on the same picture.
questions.explanation: Collage comes from the French word meaning to paste; it creatively blends diverse textures and materials.
questions.socraticHint: Does collage celebrate assembling varied textures together on a single surface?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mixed-media collage using locally sourced materials.

questions.prompt: The adhesive liquid used to stick paper bits, seeds, and fabric firmly onto your drawing paper is ____.
questions.explanation: Glue (or homemade flour-and-water paste) bonds lightweight craft materials securely to the card surface.
questions.socraticHint: What sticky liquid keeps craft pieces firmly attached to paper?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Using craft glue or traditional cassava/flour paste.

questions.prompt: Match each locally available material with how it can be used in a craft project:

matchingPairs.rightText: Yellow seeds for a bird’s beak in a seed mosaic
Textured patterned clothing in a collage
White crackled texture for animal spots
Natural thatched roof on a drawn hut

questions.explanation: Maize provides yellow seeds, kitenge provides patterns, eggshells make white mosaic spots, and banana bark makes thatched roofs.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each raw item to its ideal decorative purpose in textured artwork.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Upcycling natural materials found in Kenyan homesteads.

questions.prompt: When creating a paper mosaic, what should you do with colored magazine pages or sugar paper?

options.text: Cut or tear them into small, even pieces and paste them inside the outline
Throw the entire magazine into a dustbin

questions.explanation: Tearing or cutting paper into small uniform tiles allows neat placement inside the drawing boundaries.
questions.socraticHint: How are small tiles or paper bits prepared before gluing them side by side?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Paper tearing and scissor cutting exercises in CBC.

questions.prompt: Pouring huge puddles of glue all over the paper will make the paper wrinkle, soggy, and messy.
questions.explanation: Too much glue makes paper soggy and wrinkled. Use small dots or spread glue thinly with a craft stick.
questions.socraticHint: Does applying excessive wet glue buckle and damage paper?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Neatness and adhesive control in school crafts.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence for making a seed mosaic of a butterfly:
orderedItems: Draw the clear outline of a butterfly on stiff cardboard with pencil
Apply a thin, even coat of glue to one wing section at a time
Carefully place colored beans and seeds side-by-side onto the glue
Allow the glue to dry completely before displaying the butterfly on the wall
questions.explanation: Sketch first, apply glue to small sections, arrange seeds meticulously, and let dry before mounting.
questions.socraticHint: Work one wing section at a time so the glue does not dry out before you place the seeds.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Seed mosaic displays during school parents’ day.

questions.prompt: Which Kenyan tree leaf, when dried, produces a durable golden-brown fiber perfect for collage thatched roofs?
questions.explanation: Dried banana bark (makuti ya ndizi) is soft, pliable, fibrous, and golden-brown, ideal for collage art.
questions.socraticHint: What plant produces sweet bananas and large fibrous leaves?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Banana bark crafts in Kisii, Meru, and Kakamega.

questions.prompt: Reusing old newspapers, eggshells, and scrap cloth for collage is an example of creative up-____.
questions.explanation: Upcycling repurposes waste items into creative works of art and utility.
questions.socraticHint: What word combines "up" and "cycling" to mean creative reuse?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Environmental care through CBC creative arts.

questions.prompt: In a mosaic, leaving tiny narrow gaps between the individual colored tiles or seeds helps define the pattern clearly.
questions.explanation: Small uniform spaces between mosaic pieces create the classic tessellated look and highlight individual tiles.
questions.socraticHint: Do tiny gaps between mosaic pieces make the pattern stand out like a stained glass window?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mosaic techniques in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: What should pupils always do after finishing a collage and glue project in the art room?

options.text: Wash hands, recap the glue bottle tightly, and tidy up scraps from the desk
Leave the open glue on the floor for someone to step on
Smear glue on other pupils’ hair
Wipe sticky hands on the classroom wall

questions.explanation: Proper cleanup, capping adhesives, and washing hands preserves materials and maintains a safe classroom.
questions.socraticHint: What responsible habits keep the classroom clean and preserve art supplies?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom responsibility and CBC values.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Juma wants to create a mosaic of the Kenyan National Flag using natural seeds. Which combination of seeds will best represent the three main bands: Black, Red, and Green?
questions.storyScenario: Selecting natural materials to match national flag colors.

options.text: Crushed grey stones for every stripe
Black beans (njahi) for black, red kidney beans for red, and dried green peas for green
White rice for black, red, and green

questions.explanation: Njahi black beans, red kidney beans, and green peas provide the authentic natural colors of the Kenyan Flag bands.
questions.socraticHint: Match black beans (njahi) to black, red beans to red, and green peas to green.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: National pride through agricultural seed crafts in Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: What are the two sets of threads or strips used in weaving called?
questions.explanation: The warp threads are held stationary vertically while the weft thread weaves horizontally over and under.
questions.socraticHint: Which pair of words starting with W describes the vertical and horizontal strands in weaving?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional weaving in Kenyan communities.

questions.prompt: In plain weaving, the horizontal weft strip passes over one warp strand and under the next in a regular pattern.
questions.explanation: The fundamental principle of plain weaving is the alternating over-and-under pattern across the warp.
questions.socraticHint: Does weaving alternate going over, then under, then over again?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Weaving mats with paper and banana fiber in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: A traditional coastal sleeping or sitting mat woven from dried palm fronds is known in Swahili as a ____.
questions.explanation: A mkeka is an authentic woven palm leaf mat widely used for seating and floor coverings along the Kenyan coast.
questions.socraticHint: What coastal Swahili word starting with M describes a woven palm sitting mat?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Mikunguni and Mombasa coastal palm weaving crafts.

questions.prompt: Match each plant with the craft material or product it yields:

matchingPairs.rightText: Strong fiber twine for weaving kiondo baskets
Fibrous bark for weaving table mats and ropes
Fronds for weaving coastal mikeka mats
Stiff river stems for weaving storage grain granaries

questions.explanation: Sisal makes kiondo twine, banana bark makes mats, palm fronds make mikeka, and reeds make granaries.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each Kenyan plant to its natural weaving fiber.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional materials used across different Kenyan regions.

questions.prompt: What happens if you weave the second row in the EXACT SAME WAY as the first row (over the same strands instead of alternating)?

options.text: The mat will immediately start singing
The strips will turn into water
