questions.explanation: The steady beat is the continuous, regular ticking pulse underlying all musical rhythm.
questions.socraticHint: Which musical word describes the regular heartbeat of a song?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tapping steady beats in music classes.

questions.prompt: Tempo refers to how fast or slow a musical piece is performed.
questions.explanation: Tempo is the Italian musical term designating speed, ranging from slow (lento) to rapid (presto).
questions.socraticHint: Does tempo describe the speed of music?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Music concepts in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: The musical term that describes how loud or soft music is played or sung is ____.
questions.explanation: Dynamics describes musical volume, from very quiet whispering to thunderous fortissimo.
questions.socraticHint: What term beginning with D refers to volume levels in music?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dynamics in choral singing.

questions.prompt: Match each musical term with its everyday definition:

matchingPairs.rightText: The steady recurring heartbeat of music
The speed of music (fast, moderate, or slow)
How high or low a musical sound is
How loud or soft the musical sounds are

questions.explanation: Beat is pulse, tempo is speed, pitch is high/low tone, and dynamics is loudness/softness.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each musical word with its precise musical quality.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Core musical concepts taught in CBC.

questions.prompt: Which of the following songs would naturally have a SLOW and gentle tempo?
questions.explanation: A lullaby requires a gentle, unhurried, slow tempo to calm and lull an infant to sleep.
questions.socraticHint: Which song needs to be calm and unhurried so a baby can fall asleep?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional lullabies in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A musical rest is a moment of silence where no sound is played or sung for a specific duration.
questions.explanation: Rests in music represent intentional pauses and silence, creating rhythm alongside sounds.
questions.socraticHint: Does music include moments of silence called rests?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Notation and rhythm in primary music.

questions.prompt: Arrange the tempos from SLOWEST to FASTEST speed:
orderedItems: Very slow crawl (like a tortoise on grass)
Steady moderate walking pace (like walking to assembly)
Brisk jogging pace (like skipping with a rope)
Lightning fast sprint (like a cheetah chasing on the savanna)
questions.explanation: Slow crawl, moderate walk, brisk jog, and fast sprint arrange speeds from slowest to fastest.
questions.socraticHint: Start with the slow tortoise pace and finish with the sprinting cheetah.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Tempo exploration through animal movements.

questions.prompt: What happens to the rhythm of a song when you clap the syllables of your name: "A-MI-NA"?

options.text: You do not clap at all
You clap 3 distinct beats corresponding to each spoken syllable

questions.explanation: Syllables produce rhythmic units: "A-mi-na" has 3 syllables and equals 3 rhythm claps.
questions.socraticHint: Count how many syllables are in the name A-mi-na: 1, 2, 3!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Rhythm games using Kenyan names in class.

questions.prompt: A musical pattern of sound where the volume gradually gets louder and louder is called a cres-____.
questions.explanation: Crescendo is the dynamic marking that signals musicians to gradually increase their volume.
questions.socraticHint: What Italian musical word means growing gradually louder?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dynamics training in Grade 3 choir.

questions.prompt: Mwalimu is conducting the school brass band. When she waves her arms wide and high, she wants the band to play LOUD. When she brings her palms down close to her chest, what should the band do?

options.text: Drop their instruments on the floor
Start screaming as loud as possible

questions.explanation: Lowering palms close to the body indicates softer dynamics, prompting performers to play quietly.
questions.socraticHint: What conductor gesture signals performers to reduce volume and play softly?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Conducting signals at the Kenya Music Festival.

questions.prompt: Which creature produces a very HIGH-PITCHED sound in nature?

options.text: A tiny whistling bird or mosquito

questions.explanation: Small animals with small vibrating organs produce fast vibrations that sound high in pitch.
questions.socraticHint: Which tiny creature makes a high squeaky whistling sound?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Aural sound discrimination in science and music.

questions.prompt: Practicing clapping along with a ticking metronome helps learners develop a rock-solid sense of steady beat.
questions.explanation: A metronome provides an unwavering acoustic pulse that trains musicians to maintain consistent tempo without speeding up.
questions.socraticHint: Does a ticking timekeeper help you keep a steady tempo?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Music timing practice.

questions.prompt: What traditional percussion instrument consists of a hollow wooden cylinder with stretched animal skin, beaten with hands or sticks?
questions.explanation: The ngoma is Kenya’s quintessential traditional drum, providing the rhythmic pulse for festivals, dances, and ceremonies.
questions.socraticHint: What Swahili word starting with N describes a beaten drum?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Ngoma drums played across all Kenyan communities.

questions.prompt: The KAYAMBA is a traditional woven reed tray filled with hard seeds, played by shaking it back and forth rhythmically.
questions.explanation: The kayamba is an authentic Kenyan rattle made of reed mats filled with wild seeds (like dried beans or sorghum).
questions.socraticHint: Is the kayamba a shaken reed tray with seeds inside?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Coastal and national festival performances with the kayamba.

questions.prompt: The traditional eight-stringed lyre instrument plucked with the fingers among the Luo community of Western Kenya is the ____.
questions.explanation: The nyatiti is an iconic 8-stringed bowl lyre plucked while the musician wears iron ankle bells (gara) and taps the toe ring (oduong’o).
questions.socraticHint: Which famous 8-stringed traditional instrument is plucked in Western Kenya?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Nyatiti lyre tradition of the Luo community.

questions.prompt: Match each traditional Kenyan musical instrument with how sound is produced on it:

matchingPairs.rightText: Struck with open palms or curved wooden drumsticks
Shaken from side to side using thumbs and wrists
Blown with the mouth across an embouchure hole
Plucked with the fingertips on stretched strings

questions.explanation: Drums are struck, kayambas are shaken, flutes are blown, and nyatitis are plucked.
questions.socraticHint: Match each instrument to the physical playing technique (striking, shaking, blowing, plucking).
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classification of indigenous Kenyan musical instruments.

questions.prompt: Which wind instrument, made from a long hollow horn or gourd, was blown by elders to summon villagers to meetings or war alerts?
questions.explanation: The Abu or animal horn (coro in Kikuyu) produces a booming, deep acoustic call audible across hills.
questions.socraticHint: Which hollow animal horn or gourd is blown to announce royal or community events?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Abu horn of Western Kenya and Coro of Central Kenya.

questions.prompt: Drying a traditional drum head near a gentle morning sun or warm fire tightens the animal skin and improves its resonant pitch.
questions.explanation: Gentle warmth dries ambient moisture, tightening the skin head (membrane) for a crisp, booming tone.
questions.socraticHint: Does warming a damp drum skin make it tighter and sound sharper?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional tuning of ngoma drums before performances.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence for playing the coastal kayamba in a folk dance ensemble:
orderedItems: Grip the wooden side rails of the kayamba firmly with both hands
Rest your thumbs gently on the upper reed surface to control seed bounces
Shake the kayamba sharply to the right and left in sync with the song’s rhythm
Tap your thumbs lightly on the reeds on the downbeats to add accent clicks
questions.explanation: Hold rails, position thumbs on reeds, shake laterally in rhythm, and add thumb accent taps.
questions.socraticHint: Grip the rails first before shaking the seeds laterally in time with the music.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kayamba playing technique at the Kenyan coast.

questions.prompt: What coastal bamboo or wooden transverse flute has a sweet melodious tone heard in Mijikenda cultural music?
questions.explanation: The chivoti is a traditional bamboo flute of the Mijikenda community, blown from the side with finger holes.
questions.socraticHint: Which coastal wind instrument made of bamboo is blown like a flute?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Chivoti flute music of Kilifi and Kwale counties.

questions.prompt: Metal rattle jingles tied around the dancer’s ankles to emphasize stomping rhythms in traditional dances are called ____.
questions.explanation: Pellet bells or leg rattles (gara) chime with every footstep, amplifying the dance rhythm.
questions.socraticHint: What metallic rattles are worn on the ankles during traditional dance performances?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Leg bells (gara/orutu) in Kenyan folk dances.

questions.prompt: Traditional Kenyan musical instruments should be stored carelessly in muddy rain puddles after performances.
questions.explanation: Water rots drum skins and warps wooden reeds; instruments must be kept clean, dry, and stored carefully.
questions.socraticHint: Will mud and rain destroy animal skins and delicate reed instruments?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Care and conservation of cultural artifacts.

questions.prompt: Which single-stringed traditional fiddle played with a curved bow is popular in western and central Kenya?
questions.explanation: The Orutu (Luo) or Wandindi (Kikuyu/Kamba) is a one-stringed bowed fiddle with a monitor lizard or python skin resonator.
questions.socraticHint: Which bowed fiddle with a single string plays high melodious notes in Kenyan folk ensembles?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Orutu and Wandindi fiddle traditions.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Your school music troupe is performing an authentic Kenyan celebration dance. How should the drum (ngoma), kayamba, and singers collaborate to deliver a breathtaking performance?
questions.storyScenario: Harmonizing varied traditional instruments and voices.

options.text: Everyone plays at different speeds with eyes closed
The ngoma anchors the steady heartbeat, the kayamba adds shimmering syncopated rattle pulses, and singers soar in call-and-response harmony
The drummer beats as loud and fast as possible to drown out the singers
The kayamba player throws the instrument into the audience

questions.explanation: True musical ensemble excellence combines steady bass percussion, crisp rhythmic accents, and unified choral singing.
questions.socraticHint: How do drums, rattles, and vocal harmonies complement each other in African musical ensembles?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan National Music Festival championship performance.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a LOCOMOTOR movement where your body travels from one place to another?
questions.explanation: Running is a locomotor movement because it transports your body across space from point A to point B.
questions.socraticHint: Which action carries your feet across the playing field?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Athletics and sprinting in Kenyan primary schools.

questions.prompt: Non-locomotor movements are movements performed in one stationary spot without traveling across the floor.
questions.explanation: Non-locomotor skills (like bending, swaying, twisting) occur around the body’s axis while feet stay anchored.
questions.socraticHint: Do you stay on the same spot when stretching or bending your torso?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Morning calisthenics on the parade ground.

questions.prompt: A rhythmic locomotor movement that alternates a step and a hop on the same foot is called ____.
questions.explanation: Skipping is a combined step-hop locomotor movement performed alternately on left and right feet.
questions.socraticHint: What step-and-hop rhythm do children do joyfully across the playground?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Playground movement skills in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Classify each movement as either LOCOMOTOR (traveling) or NON-LOCOMOTOR (stationary):

matchingPairs.leftText: Twisting the waist left and right

questions.explanation: Galloping and dodging travel across space (locomotor); twisting and stretching stay in one spot (non-locomotor).
questions.socraticHint: Ask: Does the body travel across the field, or does it stay anchored in one spot?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Movement classification in CBC Physical Education.

questions.prompt: What skill involves rapidly changing direction while running to avoid being tagged by an opponent?
questions.explanation: Dodging is a quick deceptive shift of body weight and direction used in tag and team games.
questions.socraticHint: What evasion move do you use in tag games to sidestep a chaser?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dodging in games like touch-tag and kati.

questions.prompt: Looking straight down at your feet while sprinting across a crowded playground helps you avoid collisions with other children.
questions.explanation: Looking down blinds you to approaching runners; keep your head up and scan the field to navigate safely.
questions.socraticHint: Can you see oncoming classmates if your eyes are glued to your shoes?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Spatial awareness in school playground safety.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence for performing a smooth skipping movement:
orderedItems: Step forward firmly on your right foot
Hop lightly on that same right foot while swinging left knee upward
Step forward onto your left foot as you land
Hop lightly on your left foot while swinging right knee upward
questions.explanation: Step right, hop right, step left, hop left: this creates the continuous alternating skipping pattern.
questions.socraticHint: Remember the skipping formula: Step, hop; step, hop!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Basic movement warm-ups in PE lessons.

questions.prompt: What part of the foot should you land on when running or jogging lightly for speed and comfort?
questions.explanation: Landing lightly on the balls/midfoot acts like natural springs, absorbing shock and propelling you forward.
questions.socraticHint: How do famous Kenyan marathoners land lightly without stomping heavily on hard heels?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kenyan running technique celebrated globally.

questions.prompt: A traveling movement where one foot leads forward and the trailing foot slides up to meet it in a horse-like gait is a ____.
questions.explanation: Galloping maintains one leading foot forward while the back foot continuously catches up.
questions.socraticHint: What equine traveling gait mimics a trotting horse or pony?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Locomotor patterns in Grade 3 Physical Education.

questions.prompt: During PE class, the teacher blows the whistle and calls out "Personal Space Bubble!" What should each pupil do immediately?

options.text: Stop traveling, stretch both arms wide in all directions, and ensure no one is touching them
Tackle the nearest classmate to the ground
Huddle together like sardines in a tight bunch
Run out of the school gates

questions.explanation: The personal space bubble reinforces non-contact safety, ensuring every child has clearance to move without injury.
questions.socraticHint: How do you test that you have enough clear space around your body without hitting anyone?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Safety drills in school physical education.

questions.prompt: How do your arms help you when sprinting at top speed across the field?

options.text: They pump forward and backward rhythmically to give momentum and balance
They should be kept inside your pockets
They should flap like butterfly wings in circles

questions.explanation: Pumping arms in sync with opposing legs balances rotational torso forces and drives forward speed.
questions.socraticHint: How do sprinters use their arms to drive faster across the track?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sprint mechanics taught by Kenyan sports teachers.

questions.prompt: Bending your knees when landing from a jump cushions your joints and protects your ankles from injury.
questions.explanation: Bending knees acts like shock absorbers, dissipating landing impact forces safely through large thigh muscles.
questions.socraticHint: Do bent knees absorb landing impact like bicycle shock absorbers?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Jump landing mechanics in gymnastics and long jump.

questions.prompt: In the FROG JUMP gymnastics movement, how does the learner execute the jump?

options.text: Slide on the stomach like a fish
Squat low with hands on the ground, then leap forward explosively with both legs
Stand completely stiff on one toe

questions.explanation: The frog jump begins in a deep squat with hands touching the ground before leaping forward like an amphibian.
questions.socraticHint: How does a green pond frog squat and leap forward?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Animal walks in primary school gymnastics.

questions.prompt: In the CRAB WALK, your stomach faces UP toward the sky while you walk on your hands and feet with hips raised.
questions.explanation: The crab walk is an inverted quadruped movement with chest and hips facing upward, moving backward or sideways.
questions.socraticHint: Does the crab walk keep your belly facing up toward the ceiling while your hands and feet support you?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Gymnastic floor conditioning.

questions.prompt: Standing steady on one foot with the other foot resting against your inner knee like a wading bird is the ____ balance.
questions.explanation: The stork (or flamingo) stand is a classic single-leg balance testing ankle stability and core equilibrium.
questions.socraticHint: Which tall wading bird stands motionless on one slender leg in Lake Nakuru?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Flamingos at Lake Nakuru and Bogoria.

questions.prompt: Match each gymnastics animal walk with its physical body position:

matchingPairs.rightText: Walking on hands and feet with belly facing down and knees off the ground
Inverted quadruped walk with belly facing up and hips lifted high
Deep squat with hands on ground leaping forward
Deep squat walking forward without placing hands on the floor

questions.explanation: Bear crawl faces down, crab walk faces up, frog jump leaps from squat, and duck waddle walks in a squat.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each animal title to the exact body orientation and movement.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Physical education gymnastics unit.

questions.prompt: What visual trick helps you maintain balance when standing on one leg without wobbling?

options.text: Closing your eyes and jumping randomly
Looking at birds flying across the sky
Focusing your eyes on a stationary (unmoving) spot straight ahead
Spinning your head in fast circles

questions.explanation: Fixing your gaze on a stationary focal point provides visual stabilization cues to the brain’s vestibular balance system.
questions.socraticHint: Does looking at an unmoving spot help stabilize your body equilibrium?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Balance training in athletics and gymnastics.

questions.prompt: In gymnastics, holding your core abdominal muscles firm and tight helps you balance longer with stability.
questions.explanation: Core engagement stabilizes the spine and pelvis, preventing wobbling during balance stunts.
questions.socraticHint: Does tightening your tummy muscles steady your whole body?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Core stability exercises in PE.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence for setting up and performing a crab walk relay race:
orderedItems: Sit on the start line with knees bent and feet flat on the grass
Place palms flat on the ground behind your hips with fingers pointing forward
Push down through hands and heels to lift your bottom high off the ground
Scuttle backward smoothly using alternate hand and foot steps toward the marker
questions.explanation: Sit down, position hands behind hips, lift hips into table position, and scuttle backward toward the line.
questions.socraticHint: Sit down and set your hands before lifting your hips into the crab position.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Inter-house school sports day fun relays.

questions.prompt: What physical body benefit do pupils gain from practicing animal walks regularly?

options.text: Turning into real animals with tails
Never needing to eat food again
Stronger arm, leg, and abdominal muscles, and improved flexibility

questions.explanation: Animal crawls are functional bodyweight exercises that build muscular strength, shoulder stability, and flexibility.
questions.socraticHint: How do quadruped crawls strengthen your arms, legs, and core?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Physical health and muscular endurance in CBC.

questions.prompt: When balancing on a narrow log or painted line, extending both arms straight out to the sides acts like a balancing ____.
questions.explanation: Extending arms increases rotational inertia and counterbalances small lateral tilts like a tightrope walker’s pole.
questions.socraticHint: How do outstretched arms work like wings to keep you from tipping over?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Balancing games along logs and curbs in school playgrounds.

questions.prompt: Animal walks should always be performed on hard, broken rocky surfaces with sharp pebbles.
questions.explanation: Palms and knees must be protected; always practice on soft grass, sawdust pits, or gymnastic foam mats.
questions.socraticHint: Could sharp rocks cut your hands and knees during crawls?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Facility safety for physical education.

questions.prompt: Which static balance resembles an aeroplane gliding through the air on one leg with the chest forward and arms spread wide?
questions.explanation: The aeroplane balance tilts the torso forward while extending one leg straight back and arms out like wings.
questions.socraticHint: Which pose spreads arms wide like aircraft wings while one leg lifts straight behind?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Gymnastic balance routines in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: During the PE obstacle course, Wanjiku must cross a 5-meter low balance log without stepping off. What three physical techniques will guarantee Wanjiku’s success?
questions.storyScenario: Mastering dynamic balance on a narrow surface.

options.text: Jump up and down in place until the log rolls over
Keep arms extended wide like wings, focus eyes on the end of the log, and walk heel-to-toe with steady breathing
Sprint as fast as possible with closed eyes
Put hands in pockets and look backward at friends

questions.explanation: Outstretched arms, focused gaze, and deliberate heel-to-toe foot placement ensure impeccable balance on narrow beams.
questions.socraticHint: Which combination uses arms for balance, eyes for focus, and steady deliberate footwork?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Obstacle course competitions in school sports.

questions.prompt: When catching a thrown ball, how should your hands and fingers be positioned?

options.text: Spread soft like a basket reaching forward, cushioning the ball into the chest

questions.explanation: Soft spread fingers create a welcoming cup that absorbs kinetic energy and traps the ball securely.
questions.socraticHint: Do open soft fingers cushion the ball better than closed fists?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Ball catching fundamentals in PE.

questions.prompt: Kicking a football with the inside part of your foot (instep) gives you much better control and accuracy than poking with your bare toes.
questions.explanation: The instep provides a broad, flat striking surface for accurate directional passes, avoiding painful toe jams.
questions.socraticHint: Does the flat inside arch of the foot give a wider, safer kicking surface than toes?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Football skills in Kenyan school tournaments.

questions.prompt: A durable homemade football crafted by stuffing old plastic bags and cloth tied with banana fiber or sisal twine is a ____ ball.
questions.explanation: Improvised balls made of recycled plastic and string (often called jua kali or bladder balls) have launched generations of Kenyan football stars.
questions.socraticHint: What homemade ball made of polythene and string is played in village football matches?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Playing with improvised polythene footballs across Kenya.

questions.prompt: Match each basketball/netball pass with how it is executed:

matchingPairs.rightText: Pushed directly from chest to chest with both hands
Bounced on the ground two-thirds of the way to a teammate
Thrown with both hands from behind and above the head
Rolled smoothly along the floor surface

questions.explanation: Chest pass travels straight, bounce pass strikes floor first, overhead pass clears defenders, and roll travels along ground.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each pass name to its distinct flight path through the air.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Netball and ball game skills in primary schools.

questions.prompt: What skill involves keeping the ball close to your feet with gentle taps while moving around defenders on the field?
questions.explanation: Dribbling uses controlled close taps to maneuver the ball past opponents while in motion.
questions.socraticHint: What football skill keeps the ball glued near your feet while you run?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Football dribbling drills.

questions.prompt: Pulling the ball toward your chest as you catch it reduces the impact force and stops the ball from bouncing out of your hands.
questions.explanation: Giving with the ball extends contact time and decelerates the ball gently, preventing painful rebounds.
questions.socraticHint: Does cushioning an incoming ball inward make it easier to hold on to?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Hand-eye coordination in sports.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence for making a strong improvised football:
orderedItems: Collect clean scrap plastic shopping bags, fabric scraps, and old socks
Roll the materials into a tight, dense spherical ball inside a sock
Wrap layers of twine, banana fiber, or sisal string around the ball in criss-cross loops
Tie a firm double knot and test the ball by bouncing and kicking lightly
questions.explanation: Collect scraps, pack into spherical shape inside sock, bind with string, and knot securely.
questions.socraticHint: Pack the ball shape tightly first before wrapping it securely with string loops.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Making play equipment with recycled items in CBC.

questions.prompt: Where should your non-kicking foot be planted when passing a soccer ball with your instep?

options.text: Right next to the ball, pointing in the direction of the target

questions.explanation: Planting your support foot beside the ball pointing at the target stabilizes your body and directs the kick accurately.
questions.socraticHint: Where does your standing foot point to guide the direction of the ball?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kicking biomechanics taught in school football.

questions.prompt: In a bounce pass, the ball should hit the floor about ____ of the distance toward your partner.
questions.explanation: Bouncing the ball roughly two-thirds of the way ensures it rises naturally to your partner’s waist height.
questions.socraticHint: Does the bounce happen closer to you or closer to your partner for a waist-high catch?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Ball passing geometry in netball.

questions.prompt: Ochieng is practicing soccer kicks. Every time he kicks with his bare big toe, his toe hurts and the ball flies wild into the school vegetable garden. What coaching advice will help Ochieng?

options.text: Turn your foot sideways and strike the center of the ball using the flat inside arch (instep) of your foot
Kick the ball with your knee cap
Head the ball while sitting on the ground
Kick the goalpost instead of the ball

questions.explanation: Using the instep distributes contact force safely across the foot and directs the pass straight and true.
questions.socraticHint: Which part of the foot offers a wide, flat, safe kicking surface instead of the fragile toe?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Grassroots football coaching in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why is teamwork essential when playing soccer or netball on the school field?

options.text: So that everyone can take a nap on the field
Passing to open teammates creates scoring opportunities and wins matches together
Because one player should never touch the ball
Because teams are meant to fight each other

questions.explanation: Cooperative teamwork and unselfish passing unlock winning plays and foster friendship.
questions.socraticHint: How does sharing the ball with teammates help the whole squad succeed?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Harambee spirit in sports.

questions.prompt: Cheating by using your hands to score a goal when playing outfield soccer is an acceptable tactic if the referee is not looking.
questions.explanation: Integrity and honesty mean respecting rules at all times, even when officials are looking away.
questions.socraticHint: Does genuine sportsmanship require honesty and following rules even when unobserved?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: CBC core value of integrity and moral ethics in games.

questions.prompt: In the classic Kenyan playground game of KATI (dodgeball), what do the middle players try to do?

options.text: Dig a hole in the tarmac
Dodge, jump, and duck to avoid being hit by the thrown soft ball
Sit on the ball and fall asleep

questions.explanation: In Kati, middle players display incredible agility, ducking and leaping to evade the soft thrown ball.
questions.socraticHint: What do players in the middle court of Kati do when the ball is thrown at them?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kati (Kenyan traditional dodgeball) played across primary schools.

questions.prompt: In Kati, if a middle player catches the thrown ball cleanly in the air, they earn an extra "life" that can save a friend.
questions.explanation: Catching the ball in Kati grants a bonus life, allowing the catcher to rescue an eliminated teammate back into the game.
questions.socraticHint: Does catching the ball reward your team with an extra life in traditional Kati?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Kati game rules.

questions.prompt: The traditional Kenyan game of hide-and-seek where runners race back to touch the home base is called ____.
questions.explanation: Kibe is Kenya’s beloved tag-and-hide game where players sprint back to tag the home base tree shouting "Kibe!".
questions.socraticHint: What traditional game shout is called out when touching the home tree?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional games in Kenyan childhood.

questions.prompt: Match each traditional Kenyan children’s game with its defining feature:

matchingPairs.rightText: Dodgeball between two outer throwers and middle runners
Hide-and-seek sprinting to touch a home base tree or wall
Flicking glass marbles into target ground holes
Soccer match played with a tightly bound polythene ball

questions.explanation: Kati is dodgeball, Kibe is hide-and-seek, Bano is marbles, and Bladder football uses improvised balls.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each traditional game name to its core gameplay activity.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Traditional sports and games of Kenya.

questions.prompt: What should a player do after losing a fair game of Kati or football to a classmate?

options.text: Blame the referee and start an argument
Shake hands with a smile, congratulate the winners, and look forward to the next match
Cry, throw stones, and steal the ball

questions.explanation: Grace in defeat and celebrating opponents’ skill are hallmarks of true sporting champions.
questions.socraticHint: How does a polite and mature pupil handle losing a friendly match?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sportsmanship education in primary schools.

questions.prompt: In traditional games, following agreed rules prevents arguments and ensures every player has fun safely.
questions.explanation: Rules establish boundaries of fairness and safety so everyone enjoys active play together.
questions.socraticHint: Do shared rules maintain peace and fun in playground games?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fair play and rule of law in childhood games.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence for setting up a game of Kati at school:
orderedItems: Draw two parallel end lines about 10 meters apart with chalk or a stick
Select two throwers to stand on the outer lines and dodge players in the middle
The throwers toss a soft ball back and forth trying to tag middle players below the waist
Middle players jump and dodge, earning lives on clean catches until the final count
questions.explanation: Mark boundary lines, place throwers on ends and dodgers in center, throw soft ball, and dodge or catch for lives.
questions.socraticHint: Mark the court boundaries first before placing throwers and dodgers.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Organizing games during physical education.

questions.prompt: Why should players only aim below the waist when throwing the ball at dodgers in Kati?

options.text: Because balls only fly near the ground
To hit the shoes for decoration
To protect the face, eyes, and head from painful injury

questions.explanation: Safety rules forbid head shots to prevent concussions, facial cuts, or eye trauma.
questions.socraticHint: Why is it dangerous to throw hard objects at someone’s head or face?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Playground safety rules enforced by teachers.

questions.prompt: The player who seeks and tries to discover all hidden friends in the game of Kibe is called the ____.
questions.explanation: The seeker closes their eyes at base while counting, then searches for hidden players.
questions.socraticHint: What do we call the person who closes their eyes and counts before searching?

options.text: Tackle the referee to the ground

questions.prompt: Why should you always perform warm-up exercises before playing vigorous sports?

options.text: To increase heart rate and prepare muscles, preventing painful strains and injuries
To make yourself fall asleep on the field
To make your shoes change color

Brings heart rate back to normal and prevents stiffness
Replenishes water lost through heavy sweating
Allows muscles and tissues to repair and grow strong

questions.socraticHint: Connect each daily healthy habit to how it cares for your growing body.

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Healthy sleep schedules for school children.

questions.explanation: Wholesome natural foods deliver carbohydrates for energy, proteins for muscle repair, and vitamins for immunity.

questions.prompt: After running a fast 400-meter race on Sports Day, Maina wants to immediately sit down flat on the cold ground without cooling down. What should Maina’s teacher advise him to do?

Drink three liters of freezing ice water in one gulp

NEVER enter any swimming pool, river, or ocean without an adult or lifeguard watching you

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Flood safety awareness along River Nyando and Tana.

questions.prompt: At a public swimming pool, you must always walk—never run—around the pool deck because the wet tiles are very ____.
questions.explanation: Wet tiles have reduced traction; running often results in catastrophic slips and head trauma on concrete edges.

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pool deck hygiene and safety rules.

questions.prompt: Match each water safety rule with the danger it prevents:

Throw heavy rocks at the struggling swimmer

Jump in immediately even if you cannot swim

questions.socraticHint: Remember the golden water rescue motto: Reach or Throw, Don’t Go!

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Preventing dangerous horseplay around water.

Lie flat on your stomach on the edge so you are not pulled into the water
Extend a long stick, tree branch, or towel for the person to grab

questions.explanation: Shout for adult help, lie flat on stomach for anchor stability, extend stick to reach, or throw floating object.
questions.socraticHint: Lie flat on your belly first before extending a stick so the victim does not pull you into the water.

questions.prompt: What common household container can be repurposed as a lifesaving float in rural areas if thrown with its cap screwed tightly?

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Using sealed plastic jerrycans as improvised floats along rivers.

questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Herding livestock in rural Kenya.

questions.prompt: David wore heavy bronze armor, an iron helmet, and carried a giant spear when he went to fight Goliath.
questions.explanation: King Saul offered David his heavy armor, but David took it off because he trusted in God’s power, not heavy armor.
questions.socraticHint: Did David take off Saul’s heavy armor because it was too bulky and he trusted in God?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: David and Goliath story.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of how David faced and conquered Goliath in the Valley of Elah:
orderedItems: David chose five smooth stones from the stream and placed them in his shepherd’s pouch
David approached Goliath armed with his staff, sling, and unshakable faith in God
David slung a stone that struck Goliath on his forehead, bringing the giant down
The army of Israel rejoiced and praised God for the great victory
questions.explanation: Picked 5 stones, approached with sling and faith, struck Goliath with a stone, and celebrated God’s victory.
questions.socraticHint: David chose the smooth river stones first before confronting Goliath with his sling.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Courage and faith in facing challenges.

questions.prompt: How many smooth stones did David pick from the brook for his sling?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:40 states that David chose five smooth stones from the stream and put them in his pouch.
questions.socraticHint: How many smooth stones: count on the fingers of one hand!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sunday school memory questions.

questions.prompt: David declared to Goliath: "You come against me with sword and spear, but I come against you in the name of the ____ Almighty!"
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:45 shows that David’s ultimate confidence was in the name and power of the Lord Almighty.
questions.socraticHint: In whose mighty name did young David face the giant?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Trusting God during trials.

questions.prompt: Like young Samuel and David, children today can be used by God to do great things and help others.
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 4:12 reminds youth not to let anyone look down on them because they are young, but to set an example in faith and love.
questions.socraticHint: Does God use young children who have obedient and faithful hearts?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christian youth empowerment in Kenya.

questions.prompt: What wild animals had David killed with God’s help while protecting his father’s flock of sheep in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:36-37: David testified that when a lion or bear attacked the sheep, the Lord rescued him and struck them down.
questions.socraticHint: Which two ferocious predators did shepherd David slay to protect his sheep?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Pastoralist bravery in defending livestock from savanna predators.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Brian is frightened about sitting for his end-of-term exams because the questions seem like giant challenges. How can the story of David and Goliath inspire Brian?
questions.storyScenario: Overcoming fear through faith and diligent preparation.

options.text: Hide under the school desk and weep
Remember that with diligent revision and prayer, God will give him calm courage to conquer giant challenges just like David
Tear up his exam papers and run home
Bring a sling and stones into the exam room

questions.explanation: David’s story teaches that trusting God replaces paralyzing fear with peace, confidence, and courage.
questions.socraticHint: How does faith in God transform scary "giants" into manageable challenges through prayer and study?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Spiritual encouragement during school examinations in Kenya.

questions.prompt: In which town in Judea was Jesus Christ born according to the scriptures?
questions.explanation: Micah 5:2 and Luke 2:4 record that Jesus was born in Bethlehem, the city of David.
questions.socraticHint: Which small town of Judea is sung about in "O Little Town of Bethlehem"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christmas carols and Nativity plays in Kenyan churches.

questions.prompt: Baby Jesus was laid in a manger because there was no room for Mary and Joseph in the inn.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:7 records that Mary placed Baby Jesus in a manger (animal feeding trough) because the inn was full.
questions.socraticHint: Did the innkeeper turn them away because all the rooms were taken?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Nativity story taught in Sunday School.

questions.prompt: The mother of Jesus who gave birth to Him in Bethlehem was the Virgin ____.
questions.explanation: Mary was chosen by God to be the earthly mother of our Lord Jesus Christ.
questions.socraticHint: What four-letter name belongs to the blessed mother of Jesus?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Nativity story.

questions.prompt: Match the three royal gifts brought by the Wise Men with what they symbolize:

matchingPairs.rightText: Divine deity and priestly prayer worship
Sacrifice and human mortality of Jesus
Guiding light leading travelers to Bethlehem

questions.explanation: Gold is for a king, Frankincense represents divinity/priesthood, Myrrh foretells sacrifice, and the star guided them.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each gift of the Magi to its spiritual meaning.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Epiphany and Christmas celebrations.

questions.prompt: Who were the very first people to hear the good news of Jesus’ birth from the angels in the fields?

options.text: Humble shepherds keeping watch over their flocks at night

questions.explanation: Angels appeared first to humble nighttime shepherds, proving God’s love reaches everyday working people first.
questions.socraticHint: Who was watching over sheep out in the cold fields when the angels sang?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Shepherds in Kenyan pastoral traditions.

questions.prompt: The Wise Men were guided to Baby Jesus in Bethlehem by following a bright miraculous star in the east.
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:2 tells how the Magi followed the star from the East until it stopped over where Jesus lay.
questions.socraticHint: Did the Star of Bethlehem guide the Wise Men on their long journey?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Star of Bethlehem in Christmas songs.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of events of the very first Christmas night in order:
orderedItems: Mary and Joseph travel from Nazareth to Bethlehem for the Roman census
Jesus is born in a stable and laid gently in a feeding manger
Angels appear to shepherds in the fields singing "Glory to God in the highest!"
Shepherds hurry into Bethlehem to see Baby Jesus and spread the wonderful news
questions.explanation: Travel to Bethlehem, birth in manger, angelic announcement to shepherds, and shepherds visiting the stable.
questions.socraticHint: Start with the journey to Bethlehem before the birth and angel chorus.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Nativity plays presented during school closing ceremonies.

questions.prompt: What was the earthly profession of Joseph, the foster father of Jesus?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:55 identifies Joseph as a humble, hardworking carpenter in Nazareth.
questions.socraticHint: Which skilled trade did Joseph work with wood, chisels, and saws?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Dignity of manual labor and carpentry.

questions.prompt: The Christian celebration commemorating the birth of Jesus Christ on December 25th is ____.
questions.explanation: Christmas (Krismasi) is the worldwide celebration of the incarnation and birth of Jesus Christ.
questions.socraticHint: What festive holiday on December 25th celebrates the birth of Jesus?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christmas family gatherings across Kenyan villages and towns.

questions.prompt: During Christmas season, Amani’s family buys new clothes and prepares tasty chapatis. How can Amani best practice the true Christian spirit of Christmas toward poor children in their neighborhood?

options.text: Share food, chapatis, and gifts with needy children and invite them to celebrate with joy
Eat all the food alone behind closed doors and laugh at hungry children
Throw good food into the mud so no one can eat it
Boast about new clothes and insult friends

questions.explanation: Christmas is about God’s ultimate gift of love; sharing with the needy reflects Christ’s generosity.
questions.socraticHint: How does sharing festive food with hungry neighbors reflect Christ’s love?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sharing Christmas food with neighbors and orphans in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which wicked king in Jerusalem wanted to harm Baby Jesus after hearing about the new King from the Wise Men?
questions.explanation: King Herod was jealous and plotted to destroy the newborn King, but an angel warned Joseph to flee to Egypt.
questions.socraticHint: Which jealous ruler ordered the flight of Joseph and Mary to Egypt?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The flight to Egypt in Matthew 2.

questions.prompt: Jesus’ birth in a humble stable shows that God honors humility rather than pride and worldly riches.
questions.explanation: Jesus came as a humble servant King, demonstrating that true greatness in God’s kingdom is found in humility.
questions.socraticHint: Does Jesus’ birth in a simple manger teach us the beauty of humility?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christian values of simplicity and humility.

questions.prompt: In which river was Jesus Christ baptized by John the Baptist?
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:13 records that Jesus came from Galilee to River Jordan to be baptized by John.
questions.socraticHint: Which famous biblical river flows through the Holy Land where John baptized believers?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Baptism traditions in Kenyan churches.

questions.prompt: As Jesus came up out of the water after baptism, the Holy Spirit descended upon Him in the form of a gentle dove.
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:16 tells how the heavens opened and the Spirit of God descended like a dove upon Jesus.
questions.socraticHint: Which gentle white bird symbolized the Holy Spirit at Jesus’ baptism?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Symbols of the Holy Spirit in Christian art and scripture.

questions.prompt: What did the voice of God the Father from heaven say at Jesus’ baptism: "This is my beloved ____, in whom I am well pleased"?
questions.explanation: God the Father affirmed Jesus’ divine identity, saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
questions.socraticHint: What family word confirms that Jesus is God’s only begotten child?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Holy Trinity revealed at Jesus’ baptism.

questions.prompt: Match each person at Jesus’ baptism with what they did or said:

matchingPairs.rightText: Baptized Jesus in the waters of River Jordan
Descended visibly like a gentle dove from heaven
Spoke from heaven saying: "This is my beloved Son"
Obediently submitted to baptism to fulfill all righteousness

questions.explanation: John baptized, Spirit descended as a dove, Father spoke from heaven, and Jesus fulfilled righteousness.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each member of the Trinity and John the Baptist to their role at River Jordan.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christian theology of baptism in Grade 3.

questions.prompt: What were the two brothers Simon Peter and Andrew doing when Jesus first called them to follow Him?

options.text: Casting fishing nets into the Sea of Galilee

questions.explanation: Matthew 4:18 tells that Peter and Andrew were fishermen casting their nets into the lake when Jesus called them.
questions.socraticHint: What trade did Peter and Andrew work on the waters of the Sea of Galilee?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fishermen along Lake Victoria and Naivasha.

questions.prompt: Jesus told the fishermen Peter and Andrew: "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
questions.explanation: Jesus called them to leave their fish nets and bring people into the kingdom of God through the gospel.
questions.socraticHint: Did Jesus promise to make them fishers of men to spread God’s love?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Evangelism and discipleship lessons.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of how Jesus called His first four disciples at the Sea of Galilee:
orderedItems: Jesus walks along the shore of the Sea of Galilee and sees Simon Peter and Andrew casting a net
Jesus calls out: "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men!"
Peter and Andrew leave their nets immediately and follow Jesus
Jesus calls James and John who are mending nets in a boat with their father Zebedee
questions.explanation: Jesus walks by lake, calls Peter and Andrew, they follow, then calls James and John.
questions.socraticHint: Peter and Andrew were called first before James and John.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The call of the disciples in Mark 1 and Matthew 4.

questions.prompt: How many close disciples did Jesus choose to learn from Him and preach the Kingdom of God?
questions.explanation: Jesus chose twelve apostles to accompany Him during His earthly ministry and spread the gospel.
questions.socraticHint: How many disciples: count 10 plus 2 more!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Twelve Apostles in CRE.

questions.prompt: Christian baptism by water symbolizes the washing away of sins and rising to a new life in ____.
questions.explanation: Baptism represents dying to old sinful habits and rising to clean new spiritual life in Jesus Christ.
questions.socraticHint: In whose holy name are Christians baptized to begin a new life of faith?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christian sacrament of baptism.

questions.prompt: When Jesus called Peter and Andrew, they delayed and made excuses for five years before following Him.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:20 emphasizes that they left their nets AT ONCE and followed Jesus without hesitation.
questions.socraticHint: Did the disciples leave their nets immediately to obey Jesus’ call?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Obedience to God’s calling.

questions.prompt: What food did John the Baptist eat while preaching in the Judean wilderness?
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:4 describes John the Baptist wearing camel’s hair clothes and eating locusts and wild honey.
questions.socraticHint: What simple wilderness food of insects and honey from wild bees did John eat?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: John the Baptist in Sunday School.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: What does it mean for a primary school pupil in Kenya today to be a "fisher of men" like the disciples?
questions.storyScenario: Living as a disciple of Jesus in school.

options.text: Selling fish inside the church altar
Living a kind, honest life, sharing the love of Jesus, and inviting friends to know God through good examples
Catching classmates with fishing hooks in the classroom
Throwing water buckets at other children during lunch

questions.explanation: Being "fishers of men" today means drawing people to Christ through acts of kindness, honesty, and sharing the gospel.
questions.socraticHint: How does showing love, truthfulness, and kindness bring friends closer to God?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christian witness in school and neighborhood.

questions.prompt: What was Jesus doing in the boat when the ferocious windstorm struck the Sea of Galilee?

options.text: Rowing the boat as fast as He could

questions.explanation: Mark 4:38 records that Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on a cushion, showing His absolute trust and peace.
questions.socraticHint: Where was Jesus resting peacefully while the disciples were terrified of the waves?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Faith in the storms of life.

questions.prompt: When Jesus commanded the wind and waves "Quiet! Be still!", the storm immediately stopped and became completely calm.
questions.explanation: The wind died down and it was completely calm, demonstrating Christ’s divine power over all natural forces.
questions.socraticHint: Did the wind and raging waves obey Jesus’ voice instantly?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Jesus’ power over nature in Christian doctrine.

questions.prompt: The young boy in the crowd generously shared his lunch of five barley loaves and two small ____.
questions.explanation: John 6:9 records that a young boy offered five small barley loaves and two small fish.
questions.socraticHint: What sea creature was paired with the five loaves of bread in the boy’s basket?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sharing food with generosity.

questions.prompt: Match each miracle element with its biblical detail:

matchingPairs.rightText: Jesus commands: "Quiet! Be still!" and the sea obeys
Five barley loaves and two small fish
Over 5,000 men besides women and children
Twelve full baskets of broken pieces

questions.explanation: Storm obeyed Jesus, boy had 5 loaves and 2 fish, 5,000 fed, and 12 baskets leftover.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each detail to the exact numerical and biblical facts.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Miracles of Jesus in CBC Grade 3 CRE.

questions.prompt: How many baskets of leftover bread pieces did the disciples gather after everyone had eaten their fill?
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:20 states that the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
questions.socraticHint: How many baskets were gathered: one for each of the twelve disciples!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Preventing food waste and God’s abundance.

questions.prompt: The young boy hid his five loaves and two fish under his shirt so no one else could eat them.
questions.explanation: The boy gave his entire lunch cheerfully into Jesus’ hands, setting an example of selfless sharing.
questions.socraticHint: Did the boy share his lunch cheerfully with Jesus?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Generosity and sharing among Kenyan children.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of how Jesus fed the five thousand people:
orderedItems: Jesus tells the disciples to have the people sit down in groups on the green grass
Jesus takes the five loaves and two fish, looks up to heaven, and gives thanks
Jesus breaks the loaves and gives them to the disciples to distribute to the crowd
All the people eat until satisfied and twelve baskets of leftovers are collected
questions.explanation: People sat down, Jesus gave thanks, broke and distributed bread, and gathered 12 baskets leftover.
questions.socraticHint: Jesus looked up to heaven and gave thanks to God before breaking and distributing the food.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Praying before meals in Christian families.

questions.prompt: What did the amazed disciples say to each other after Jesus calmed the violent storm?

options.text: "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!"

questions.explanation: Mark 4:41 records their awe: "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!"
questions.socraticHint: What question did the disciples ask in holy wonder when the storm ceased?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Awe and reverence for Jesus Christ.

questions.prompt: Before sharing the five loaves and two fish, Jesus looked up to heaven and said a prayer of ____ to God.
questions.explanation: Jesus modeled gratitude by blessing the food and giving thanks to God the Father before eating.
questions.socraticHint: What prayer do we say before every meal to thank God for our food?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Table grace prayer before eating in Kenyan homes.

questions.prompt: At lunchtime in school, Nekesa has two mandazis while her classmate Faith forgot her lunch at home and is hungry. How can Nekesa follow Jesus’ teaching on sharing?
questions.storyScenario: Practicing Christian generosity in the classroom.

options.text: Cheerfully share one mandazi with Faith so they both enjoy a nourishing lunch with joy
Eat both mandazis quickly while laughing at Faith
Drop her mandazi on the dusty ground so no one can eat it
Hide inside the washroom to eat alone

questions.explanation: Sharing our meals with those who have none is the very heart of Christian fellowship and love.
questions.socraticHint: How does sharing half your snack reflect the spirit of the young boy who shared his lunch with Jesus?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sharing food at school break time in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why did Jesus perform miracles like healing the sick and feeding the hungry crowds?

options.text: Because He had deep compassion and love for suffering human beings
To show off and become rich
To charge money from sick people

questions.explanation: Matthew 14:14 states that Jesus saw a large crowd, had compassion on them, and healed their sick.
questions.socraticHint: What loving emotion motivated Jesus to heal, feed, and help people?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Compassion (huruma) in Christian service.

questions.prompt: Jesus is with us even during difficult times and illness, giving us peace when we pray to Him.
questions.explanation: Philippians 4:6-7 promises that prayer brings the peace of God which surpasses all human understanding.
questions.socraticHint: Does Jesus give us calm peace and comfort when we pray in hard times?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Comfort through prayer in Kenyan families.

questions.prompt: What happened to the Jewish traveler on his way down from Jerusalem to Jericho in the parable?

options.text: He became the king of Jericho
Robbers attacked him, beat him, stole his belongings, and left him half dead
He found a treasure chest full of gold

questions.explanation: Luke 10:30 describes how robbers attacked the traveler, stripped him of his clothes, and beat him severely.
questions.socraticHint: What violent attack happened to the traveler on the dangerous road to Jericho?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Parable of the Good Samaritan.

questions.prompt: The priest and the Levite stopped immediately to wash the wounded man’s sores and carry him to hospital.
questions.explanation: Both the priest and the Levite saw the injured man but crossed over and walked past on the other side of the road.
questions.socraticHint: Did the religious leaders stop to help, or did they pass by on the other side of the road?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: True religion shown by deeds, not just titles.

questions.prompt: The traveler from Samaria who stopped to dress the wounded man’s injuries with oil and wine is known as the Good ____.
questions.explanation: The Good Samaritan has become the world’s greatest symbol of self-sacrificing compassion for strangers.
questions.socraticHint: Which title starting with S belongs to the merciful hero of Jesus’ parable?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Good Samaritan parable.

questions.prompt: Match each character in the parable of the Good Samaritan with their action:

matchingPairs.rightText: Saw the wounded man and crossed to the other side
Looked at the suffering traveler and passed by
Bandaged wounds, put him on his donkey, and paid the inn
Cared for the injured traveler at the inn

questions.explanation: Priest and Levite walked by, Samaritan showed mercy and paid the bill, innkeeper nursed him.
questions.socraticHint: Match each traveler with how they treated the beaten man.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Compassion and helping victims of accidents in Kenya.

questions.prompt: What soothing remedies did the Good Samaritan pour on the wounded man’s cuts to treat them?
questions.explanation: Luke 10:34 says the Samaritan went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil (to soothe) and wine (as antiseptic).
questions.socraticHint: Which ancient Mediterranean first aid remedies did the Samaritan use on the cuts?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Biblical first aid practices.

questions.prompt: In Jesus’ time, Jews and Samaritans were best friends who loved eating and traveling together.
questions.explanation: Jews and Samaritans had deep historical prejudice and did not associate, making the Samaritan’s kindness extraordinarily heroic.
questions.socraticHint: Did the two groups have bitter prejudice, making the Samaritan’s mercy surprising and radical?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Overcoming tribal and cultural prejudice in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of the Good Samaritan caring for the wounded stranger:
orderedItems: The Samaritan feels deep pity and approaches the injured man by the roadside
He bandages the wounds, pouring on soothing oil and cleansing wine
He lifts the man onto his own donkey and walks beside him to a roadside inn
He gives money to the innkeeper and promises to repay any extra expenses
questions.explanation: Felt pity, bandaged wounds, transported to inn, and paid for ongoing care.
questions.socraticHint: He treated the wounds first before transporting him on his donkey to the inn.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Caring for emergency victims in Kenyan communities.

questions.prompt: According to Jesus, who is our "neighbor" whom we must love as ourselves?

options.text: Only people from our own family
Only people who give us money
Only people who live in the same house
Anyone in need who crosses our path, regardless of tribe, race, or religion

questions.explanation: Jesus redefined "neighbor" from just friends and clan members to anyone in need of our compassion and care.
questions.socraticHint: Does Jesus teach that everyone in need of help is our neighbor?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: National cohesion and Christian neighborliness.

questions.prompt: At the end of the parable, Jesus gave the command: "Go and do ____."
questions.explanation: Luke 10:37: Jesus told him, "Go and do likewise," instructing us to show active mercy to others.
questions.socraticHint: What word meaning "in the same way" completes Jesus’ instruction?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christian command to live out love.

questions.prompt: Ignoring an injured pupil who fell and scraped their knee on the school field is the behavior of a Good Samaritan.
questions.explanation: A true Good Samaritan stops, shows kindness, helps the injured friend up, and assists them to the school dispensary.
questions.socraticHint: Would a Good Samaritan ignore a friend or immediately offer help?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: First aid and peer assistance in Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: What did the Good Samaritan sacrifice to save the stranger’s life?

options.text: His time, his donkey, his own oil and bandages, and his hard-earned money
He took the wounded man’s shoes

questions.explanation: True love is sacrificial: the Samaritan gave his own resources, time, energy, and money without expecting repayment.
questions.socraticHint: Did the Samaritan give his personal time, supplies, and money freely?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Sacrificial love in Christian living.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: On the way to church, Juma sees an elderly woman from a different ethnic community drop her heavy basket of sweet potatoes. What would the Good Samaritan do?
questions.storyScenario: Putting Christian neighborly love into practice.

options.text: Cross to the other side of the road and pretend he saw nothing
Immediately stop, help the grandmother pick up the potatoes gently, and assist in carrying the basket safely to her door
Laugh at her and run away to church
Steal two sweet potatoes and hide them in his pockets

questions.explanation: True Christian love cuts across tribal boundaries to help anyone in distress with respect and kindness.
questions.socraticHint: How does helping the elderly grandmother demonstrate the character of the Good Samaritan?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Respect for elders and unity across all 47 counties of Kenya.

questions.prompt: What tree did Zacchaeus climb so he could see Jesus over the tall crowd in Jericho?
questions.explanation: Luke 19:4 records that Zacchaeus ran ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree because he was short.
questions.socraticHint: Which leafy biblical tree did Zacchaeus climb in Jericho?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The story of Zacchaeus in Sunday school.

questions.prompt: Zacchaeus was despised by his fellow citizens because he was an unfair tax collector who cheated people.
questions.explanation: Tax collectors collected taxes for Roman rulers and often extorted extra money for themselves, making them unpopular.
questions.socraticHint: Did the people resent Zacchaeus for cheating them on their taxes?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Honesty and anti-corruption values in CRE.

questions.prompt: When Jesus stopped under the tree, He looked up and said: "Zacchaeus, come down immediately; today I must stay at your ____."
questions.explanation: Jesus chose to visit and dine at Zacchaeus’ home, extending grace and fellowship.
questions.socraticHint: Where did Jesus say He wanted to stay that day with Zacchaeus?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Hospitality (ukarimu) in Kenyan culture.

questions.prompt: Match each action of Zacchaeus with its spiritual significance:

matchingPairs.rightText: Eagerness and effort to see Jesus despite obstacles
Restitution and repairing wrongs done to others
Acceptance of God’s love and salvation

questions.explanation: Tree showed effort, half to poor showed generosity, 4-fold showed restitution, and welcome showed acceptance.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each of Zacchaeus’ actions to how it demonstrated his genuine change of heart.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Repentance and making amends.

questions.prompt: How many times did Zacchaeus promise to pay back anyone he had cheated?
questions.explanation: Luke 19:8: Zacchaeus vowed: "If I have cheated anybody out of anything, I will pay back four times the amount."
questions.socraticHint: How many times: count one, two, three, four!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Restitution in biblical justice.

questions.prompt: Making restitution means apologizing to someone and returning or replacing what was wrongfully taken or broken.
questions.explanation: Restitution is repairing damage or returning stolen property, proving that an apology is sincere.
questions.socraticHint: Does real repentance include returning what you took wrongfully?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Conflict resolution and fairness in school.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence of Zacchaeus’ transformation in Jericho:
orderedItems: Zacchaeus climbs a sycamore-fig tree because he is too short to see Jesus
Jesus stops under the tree and calls him by name to come down
Zacchaeus welcomes Jesus into his home with great joy and hospitality
Zacchaeus repents, pledges half his wealth to the poor, and restores cheated money fourfold
questions.explanation: Climbs tree, Jesus calls him, welcomes Jesus, and repents with fourfold restitution.
questions.socraticHint: He climbed the tree first before Jesus noticed him and called him down.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The conversion of Zacchaeus.

questions.prompt: What did the crowd mutter and grumble when Jesus chose to visit Zacchaeus’ home?

options.text: "He is going to buy a new horse"
"Zacchaeus is the best man in town"
"He has gone to be the guest of a sinner!"

questions.explanation: Luke 19:7: People grumbled because they thought sinners should be shunned, but Jesus came to seek and save the lost.
questions.socraticHint: Why were the self-righteous people annoyed that Jesus ate with a tax collector?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Jesus reaches out to outcasts and sinners.

questions.prompt: Jesus concluded the story by declaring: "For the Son of Man came to seek and to ____ the lost."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:10: "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost," summarizing Jesus’ mission of salvation.
questions.socraticHint: What four-letter word describes rescuing and delivering people from sin?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Key gospel verse memorized in Sunday school.

questions.prompt: Kipchumba accidentally sat on his deskmate’s ruler and broke it, but hid it without saying anything. After learning about Zacchaeus, what should Kipchumba do?
questions.storyScenario: Practicing honesty and restitution at school.

options.text: Admit his mistake honestly, apologize to his deskmate, and replace the broken ruler with a new one
Blame another classmate and start a fight
Throw the broken pieces into the teacher’s tea cup
Pretend he never saw the ruler

questions.explanation: Confessing mistakes and replacing broken items models Zacchaeus’ restitution and biblical integrity.
questions.socraticHint: How can Kipchumba make things right through honesty and replacement?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Classroom accountability and Christian ethics.

questions.prompt: What Christian value is demonstrated when a tax collector stops taking bribes and cheating citizens?
questions.explanation: Refusing corruption and treating people with justice embodies Christian integrity and honesty.
questions.socraticHint: Which core moral virtue stands against cheating, bribes, and lies?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Anti-corruption and civic integrity education in CBC.

questions.prompt: Jesus rejects anyone who has made mistakes in the past and refuses to ever forgive them.
questions.explanation: Jesus welcomes everyone with open arms; when we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us (1 John 1:9).
questions.socraticHint: Does Jesus offer limitless mercy and forgiveness to anyone who repents with a sincere heart?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: God’s unconditional forgiveness.

questions.prompt: What does Ephesians 6:1 command children to do regarding their parents?

options.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right
Children, shout at your parents every morning
Children, run away from your homestead

questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:1 commands children to obey and honor their parents, which brings God’s blessing and long life.
questions.socraticHint: What virtue of respect and listening to parents does the Apostle Paul teach?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Honoring parents in Kenyan Christian families.

questions.prompt: The commandment to honor your father and mother is the first commandment that comes with a special promise of a long and blessed life.
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:12 and Ephesians 6:2-3 declare that honoring parents carries the divine promise: "that it may go well with you and you may enjoy long life."
questions.socraticHint: Does honoring parents carry the promise of a long, blessed life?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Ten Commandments taught in CRE.

questions.prompt: When someone offends us and says "I am sorry", we should choose to ____ them from our heart.
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:13 urges: "Forgive as the Lord forgave you." Forgiveness frees our hearts and restores peace.
questions.socraticHint: What act of mercy releases anger and restores friendship?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Reconciliation and peace building in schools.

questions.prompt: Match each Christian duty with its practical expression at home or school:

matchingPairs.rightText: Fetching water or washing dishes promptly when asked
Listening attentively in class and completing homework
Letting go of anger and smiling when an apology is made
Sharing school stationery with a deskmate who has none

questions.explanation: Obedience does chores, respect listens in class, forgiveness releases anger, and charity shares stationery.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each Christian value to how you live it out every day.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Christian values in daily Kenyan life.

questions.prompt: What does the Book of James (James 1:27) say is pure and undefiled religion before God our Father?

options.text: To shout louder than everyone else during prayers
To stay at home and ignore everyone
To look after orphans and widows in their distress and keep oneself unpolluted by the world
To wear golden jewelry to church

questions.explanation: James 1:27 identifies caring for the vulnerable (orphans and widows) as true and pure worship.
questions.socraticHint: Who are the vulnerable groups God asks us to care for in James 1:27?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Caring for orphans and vulnerable children in Kenya.

questions.prompt: When Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive a brother who wrongs him, Jesus said: "Not seven times, but seventy-seven times."
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:22: Jesus taught that forgiveness should have no limit, just as God never stops forgiving us.
questions.socraticHint: Does Jesus teach that we should forgive without keeping count of how many times?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Unlimited forgiveness taught in the Gospels.

questions.prompt: Arrange the sequence for resolving a playground disagreement peacefully like a Christian peacemaker:
orderedItems: Stop playing and take a deep breath to cool down heated tempers
Listen calmly to what your friend has to say without interrupting
Explain your feelings gently and apologize if you made a mistake
Exchange a handshake or hug, forgive each other, and resume playing happily
questions.explanation: Cool down, listen calmly, communicate and apologize, forgive and reconcile.
questions.socraticHint: Cool down first before listening and offering an apology.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Peace clubs and conflict resolution in Kenyan primary schools.

questions.prompt: Which famous beatitude from the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:9) praises those who bring peace?

options.text: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God"

questions.explanation: Matthew 5:9 promises that peacemakers are called children of God because they reflect God’s loving character.
questions.socraticHint: Who does Jesus call "children of God" in the Beatitudes?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: The Beatitudes in Christian living.

questions.prompt: In Galatians 5:22, the first fruit of the Holy Spirit listed is ____.
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:22: "The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control."
questions.socraticHint: Which supreme virtue heads the list of the Fruit of the Spirit?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fruit of the Spirit in CBC CRE.

questions.prompt: Disobeying parents and sneaking out of the house at night brings joy and peace to the family.
questions.explanation: Disobedience causes grief, danger, and broken trust; obedience preserves family harmony and safety.
questions.socraticHint: Does disobeying your parents cause sadness and put you in danger?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Family values and filial piety in Kenya.

questions.prompt: What did the early church Christians do with their food and possessions in Acts 2:44-45?

options.text: They had everything in common, shared with anyone who had need, and ate together with glad hearts
They locked their food in vaults
They charged interest on each other

questions.explanation: The early Christians shared their possessions generously so that there were no needy people among them.
questions.socraticHint: How did the early believers in Acts share with anyone in need?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Harambee and communal sharing in Kenyan churches.

questions.prompt: Grandmaster Challenge: Wendo accidentally spilled water on Maria’s exercise book, ruining her drawing. Maria is furious and wants to tear Wendo’s book. How can Maria act like a follower of Christ?
questions.storyScenario: Choosing forgiveness and peacemaking over revenge.

options.text: Never speak to Wendo for the rest of her life
Take a deep breath, accept Wendo’s heartfelt apology, forgive her, and work together to redraw the picture peacefully
Tear Wendo’s exercise book into tiny shreds and throw it out the window
Pour ink all over Wendo’s uniform

questions.explanation: Forgiving accidents and working together in peace reflects Christ’s love and produces true friendship.
questions.socraticHint: Which peaceful response chooses forgiveness and teamwork over destructive revenge?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Peacemaking and forgiveness in Kenyan schools.

questions.prompt: What is the very first opening chapter (Surah) of the Holy Qur'an called?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah means "The Opening" and is the opening Surah of the Holy Qur'an, recited in every prayer.
questions.socraticHint: Which Surah begins with "Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'alamin"?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Madrasa and school recitation across Kenyan Muslim communities.

questions.prompt: Surah Al-Ikhlas teaches that Allah is One, has no partners, and was neither born nor has any children.
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas proclaims pure Tawhid: "Qul Huwallahu Ahad, Allahus-Samad, Lam yalid wa lam yulad, Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad."
questions.socraticHint: Does Surah Al-Ikhlas emphasize that Allah is One and has no equals?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Core Islamic theology taught in Grade 3 IRE.

questions.prompt: Before beginning recitation of the Holy Qur'an, we seek refuge from Shaytan by saying "A’udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-____".
questions.explanation: Ta’awwudh is seeking protection from Allah against the cursed Satan: "A’udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim."
questions.socraticHint: What Arabic word meaning "the accursed/outcast" completes the phrase?
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Islamic recitation etiquette in Madrasa.

questions.prompt: Match each Ayah from Surah Al-Fatihah with its meaning in English:

matchingPairs.rightText: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds
The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful
Sovereign of the Day of Recompense / Judgment
Guide us to the straight path

questions.explanation: Praise to Lord of worlds, Merciful, Day of Judgment, and guide to straight path.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each familiar Ayah of Al-Fatihah with its English meaning.
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Understanding the meanings of daily prayers.

questions.prompt: How many verses (Ayat) are in Surah Al-Fatihah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah consists of seven oft-repeated verses (Sab’ul Mathani) essential for Salah.
questions.socraticHint: How many days are in a week? Surah Al-Fatihah has the exact same number of verses!
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Qur'an memorization in Madrasa.

questions.prompt: A Muslim can perform valid obligatory prayer (Salah) without reciting Surah Al-Fatihah.
