Huonyesha matokeo au athari ya tendo
Huonyesha hiari au kuchagua kitu kimoja

questions.prompt: Kamilisha hitimisho la barua ya kirafiki: 'Wako wa moyoni, ____' (anwani / rafiki yako mwaminifu)
questions.explanation: Mwisho wa barua ya kirafiki huhitimishwa kwa maneno ya upendo kama 'rafiki yako mwaminifu' au 'wako wa dhati'.
questions.socraticHint: Mwisho wa barua kwa rafiki unaandika nini kabla ya jina lako?

questions.prompt: Amina anataka kumwandikia binamu yake barua kumkaribisha Nairobi wakati wa likizo. Ni mpangilio upi wa sehemu za barua utakaomfaa?

options.text: Kuandika tu sentensi moja bila anwani wala tarehe.
Anwani na tarehe juu kulia, maamkizi, mwili wenye ujumbe wa mwaliko, hitimisho na jina lake.
Kuanza na jina lake katikati, kisha maneno ya biashara bila anwani.
Kuandika anwani mbili kama barua rasmi ya kuomba kazi.

questions.correctAnswer: Anwani na tarehe juu kulia, maamkizi, mwili wenye ujumbe wa mwaliko, hitimisho na jina lake.
questions.explanation: Muundo sahihi wa barua ya kirafiki una anwani moja, tarehe, maamkizi ya kirafiki, mwili na hitimisho.
questions.socraticHint: Kumbuka barua ya kirafiki ina anwani ngapi na ipo upande gani?

questions.prompt: Chagua sentensi iliyo sahihi kisarufi inayotumia viunganishi viwili kuleta mtiririko kamili:

options.text: Juma alitaka kusoma wala lakini hakuwa na kitabu.
Juma alitaka kusoma ingawa lakini hakuwa na kitabu kwa hivyo.
Juma alitaka kusoma, lakini hakuwa na kitabu, kwa hivyo alienda maktabani.
Juma alitaka kusoma kwa sababu lakini hakuwa na kitabu au alienda maktabani.

questions.correctAnswer: Juma alitaka kusoma, lakini hakuwa na kitabu, kwa hivyo alienda maktabani.
questions.explanation: Sentensi hii ina mtiririko sahihi wa kimantiki: ukinzani ('lakini hakuwa na kitabu') na matokeo ('kwa hivyo alienda maktabani').
questions.socraticHint: Tazama sentensi yenye maana inayoeleweka bila viunganishi kugongana.

questions.prompt: Kweli au Si kweli: Katika barua ya kirafiki, si lazima kuweka alama za vituo kama vile koma baada ya maamkizi na anwani.
questions.explanation: Uakifishaji sahihi (koma, nukta, herufi kubwa) ni muhimu sana katika kuandika barua nadhifu na sahihi.
questions.socraticHint: Je, alama za vituo kama koma na nukta zinahitajika katika uandishi wowote sahihi?

questions.prompt: Panga sehemu kuu tano za barua ya kirafiki kwa mpangilio unaotakiwa kuanzia mwanzo hadi mwisho:
questions.correctAnswer: Anwani ya mwandishi na Tarehe, Maamkizi ya kirafiki, Mwili wa barua (ujumbe mkuu), Hitimisho na sahihi/jina la mwandishi
questions.explanation: Mfuatano rasmi wa barua ya kirafiki: Anwani na tarehe, Maamkizi, Mwili/Ujumbe, kisha Hitimisho na jina.
questions.socraticHint: Unaanza juu kwa anwani na unamalizia chini kwa jina lako.

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a flowering plant commonly grown in Kenya?
questions.explanation: Maize is a flowering plant because it produces flowers that develop into seeds on a cob.
questions.socraticHint: Which of these crops produces flowers and seeds that we eat as ugali or roasted maize?

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between flowering and non-flowering plants?

options.text: Flowering plants cannot grow in soil
Non-flowering plants are always taller than flowering plants
Flowering plants produce flowers, while non-flowering plants do not
Non-flowering plants do not need water to survive

questions.correctAnswer: Flowering plants produce flowers, while non-flowering plants do not
questions.explanation: The presence or absence of flowers is the primary scientific basis for classifying these two plant groups.
questions.socraticHint: Look at the names: flowering vs non-flowering. What does one produce that the other does not?

questions.prompt: True or False: Ferns and mosses are examples of non-flowering plants that reproduce without flowers.
questions.explanation: Ferns and mosses do not produce flowers; they reproduce using tiny dust-like spores.
questions.socraticHint: Do you ever see colourful petals or flowers on a fern or moss growing on a damp rock?

questions.prompt: Pine trees and cedar trees do not produce true flowers; instead, they produce woody structures called ____ to hold their seeds.
questions.explanation: Conifers such as pine, cypress, and cedar produce cones, making them non-flowering plants.
questions.socraticHint: What cone-shaped wooden parts do pine trees drop on the forest floor?

questions.prompt: Which pair of plants consists entirely of non-flowering plants?
questions.explanation: Both ferns and mosses are non-flowering plants that reproduce by spores.
questions.socraticHint: Identify the option where neither plant bears any flowers.

questions.prompt: Match each plant to its correct classification:
questions.correctAnswer: Bean plant -> Flowering plant, Fern -> Non-flowering plant, Mango tree -> Flowering plant, Pine tree -> Non-flowering plant
questions.explanation: Beans and mangoes produce flowers and fruits, while ferns and pines do not produce flowers.
questions.socraticHint: Think about whether each plant produces blossoms before producing seeds.

questions.prompt: Why are bright petals important for many flowering plants?

options.text: They attract insects and birds for pollination
They absorb water directly from the air
They hold the plant firmly in the soil
They keep the roots warm during the night

questions.correctAnswer: They attract insects and birds for pollination
questions.explanation: Brightly coloured petals attract pollinators such as bees and sunbirds, which help transfer pollen.
questions.socraticHint: Why do bees and butterflies visit colourful flowers?

questions.prompt: True or False: Grass in the school field is a non-flowering plant because its flowers are not large and bright.
questions.explanation: Grass IS a flowering plant; it produces small, wind-pollinated flowers at the tips of its stalks.
questions.socraticHint: Does grass produce seeds that birds eat? Seeds come from flowers!

questions.prompt: In flowering plants, the part that develops into a fruit containing seeds is the ____ of the flower.
questions.explanation: After fertilisation, the flower's ovary swells and develops into a fruit containing seeds.
questions.socraticHint: Which female part at the base of the flower swells to become the fruit?

questions.prompt: During a nature walk in Karura Forest, Amina found a soft, green, carpet-like plant growing on a wet rock. It has no roots, stems, or flowers. What plant did Amina most likely observe?
questions.explanation: Moss is a small, non-flowering plant that grows in moist, shady places and forms dense green carpets.
questions.socraticHint: Which non-flowering plant forms velvety green carpets on damp rocks and tree trunks?

questions.prompt: Arrange the life cycle stages of a flowering plant from first to last:

options.text: Seed germinates into a young seedling
Plant grows mature green leaves and stems
Flowers produce fruits containing new seeds

questions.correctAnswer: Seed germinates into a young seedling, Plant grows mature green leaves and stems, Plant produces flowers, Flowers produce fruits containing new seeds
questions.explanation: The plant starts as a germinating seed, grows vegetative organs, flowers, and finally produces fruits and seeds.
questions.socraticHint: Start with what happens underground when you plant a bean seed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following plants reproduces by microscopic spores found on the underside of its fronds (leaves)?
questions.explanation: Ferns have brown clusters of spore cases (sori) on the underside of their leaves called fronds.
questions.socraticHint: Which non-flowering plant has feather-like leaves called fronds?

questions.prompt: Why are mushrooms classified as fungi and NOT as green plants?

options.text: They do not have chlorophyll and cannot make their own food
They do not need moisture to grow

questions.correctAnswer: They do not have chlorophyll and cannot make their own food
questions.explanation: Fungi lack chlorophyll, so they cannot perform photosynthesis; they absorb nutrients from dead organic matter.
questions.socraticHint: What green substance do plants use to make food that mushrooms lack?

questions.prompt: Which microscopic fungus is used by bakers in Kenya to make bread and mandazi dough rise?
questions.explanation: Yeast produces carbon dioxide gas during fermentation, which makes dough rise and become spongy.
questions.socraticHint: Which tiny fungus do bakers add to warm water, sugar, and flour?

questions.prompt: True or False: It is completely safe to pick and eat any wild mushroom you find in the school field or forest.
questions.explanation: Many wild mushrooms (toadstools) contain deadly toxins that can cause severe illness or death if consumed.
questions.socraticHint: Can you easily tell if a wild mushroom is poisonous just by looking at it?

questions.prompt: The umbrella-shaped wild fungi that are often brightly coloured and poisonous are called ____.
questions.explanation: Toadstools are wild, non-edible or poisonous mushrooms that should never be eaten.
questions.socraticHint: What word is commonly used for poisonous wild mushrooms?

questions.prompt: What is the green, white, or black fuzzy growth that appears on a piece of bread left in a warm, damp cupboard for several days?
questions.explanation: Bread mould is a type of fungus that grows rapidly on damp, stale bread by producing thread-like hyphae.
questions.socraticHint: What fuzzy fungus spoils old moist bread?

questions.prompt: What protective gear should learners wear when collecting plant and fungal specimens during a Science field study?
questions.explanation: Gloves protect hands from thorns and plant toxins, while closed shoes protect feet from sharp objects and biting insects.
questions.socraticHint: What should you put on your hands and feet to avoid cuts and harmful plant sap?

questions.prompt: Match each fungus to its role or characteristic:

options.text: Yeast -> Used in baking bread and fermentation
Bread mould -> Spoilage of damp stored bread
Edible mushroom -> Grown by farmers as nutritious food

questions.correctAnswer: Yeast -> Used in baking bread and fermentation, Bread mould -> Spoilage of damp stored bread, Edible mushroom -> Grown by farmers as nutritious food, Toadstool -> Wild poisonous mushroom
questions.explanation: Each of these fungi has distinct characteristics and impacts on human life.
questions.socraticHint: Link each fungal type with how it is used or its danger.

matchingPairs.rightText: Used in baking bread and fermentation
Grown by farmers as nutritious food

questions.prompt: Fungi play a crucial role in our environment as ____ because they break down dead plants and animal waste into rich soil nutrients.
questions.explanation: Fungi decompose dead organic matter, recycling essential nutrients back into the ecosystem.
questions.socraticHint: What is the scientific term for organisms that rot and break down dead matter?

questions.prompt: While playing in the school shamba, Brian found several large, white mushrooms growing near a compost heap. He asked his classmates if they could cook and eat them for lunch. What is the safest advice?

options.text: Boil them for two minutes to remove all poison.
Do NOT eat them because wild mushrooms can be poisonous; only eat mushrooms bought from approved grocery shops or verified farms.
Taste a tiny piece first to see if it tastes sweet.
Wash them with cold water and eat them immediately.

questions.correctAnswer: Do NOT eat them because wild mushrooms can be poisonous; only eat mushrooms bought from approved grocery shops or verified farms.
questions.explanation: Cooking or washing does NOT destroy all fungal toxins. Never consume wild mushrooms.
questions.socraticHint: Is boiling or tasting a wild mushroom safe, or should you completely avoid eating unidentified wild mushrooms?

questions.prompt: Which of the following plants produces a milky white sap that can cause severe skin irritation and blindness if it gets into the eyes?
questions.explanation: Euphorbia plants produce a caustic white latex sap that is toxic and dangerous to the skin and eyes.
questions.socraticHint: Which thorny succulent plant common in dry Kenyan ridges has irritating white milky sap?

questions.prompt: True or False: Washing your hands with soap and clean running water immediately after touching plant or fungal specimens is an essential laboratory safety rule.
questions.explanation: Handwashing removes harmful sap, fungal spores, dirt, and microscopic pathogens from your skin.
questions.socraticHint: Why must you always clean your hands after practical science activities?

questions.prompt: Arrange the safety steps for carrying out a plant collection activity:

options.text: Put on protective gloves and sturdy shoes
Carefully collect plant specimens using forceps or tongs
Place specimens into clean collection bags or jars
Remove gloves and wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean water

questions.correctAnswer: Put on protective gloves and sturdy shoes, Carefully collect plant specimens using forceps or tongs, Place specimens into clean collection bags or jars, Remove gloves and wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean water
questions.explanation: Standard safety protocol: wear protective gear, collect specimens safely, store them properly, and wash hands at the conclusion.
questions.socraticHint: What do you put on before you begin, and what do you do after you finish the activity?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What defining internal structure do all vertebrate animals possess?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates are defined by having an internal vertebral column or backbone.
questions.socraticHint: Touch the middle of your back. What bone runs down from your neck to your hips?

questions.prompt: Which vertebrate group has bodies covered with feathers and lays hard-shelled eggs?
questions.explanation: Birds are the only animal group characterized by having feathers.
questions.socraticHint: What animal covering helps eagles, hens, and crowned cranes stay warm and fly?

questions.prompt: True or False: Mammals are animals whose bodies are covered with fur or hair and who feed their young on mother's milk.
questions.explanation: All female mammals produce milk from mammary glands to nourish their newborn young.
questions.socraticHint: Do cows and human mothers feed their young milk?

questions.prompt: Fish breathe underwater using specialized respiratory organs called ____.
questions.explanation: Gills extract dissolved oxygen from water as it passes over the gill filaments.
questions.socraticHint: What feathery red slits on the sides of a tilapia's head allow it to breathe underwater?

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals is an amphibian that has smooth, moist skin and can live both in water and on land?
questions.explanation: Frogs and toads are amphibians; their skin is moist and they lay eggs in water that hatch into tadpoles.
questions.socraticHint: Which animal starts life as a swimming tadpole before growing legs to hop on land?

questions.prompt: Match each vertebrate class to its characteristic body covering:
questions.correctAnswer: Mammals -> Fur or hair, Birds -> Feathers, Reptiles -> Dry scales, Fish -> Slimy, wet scales
questions.explanation: Each vertebrate class has evolved an outer body covering suited to its lifestyle and environment.
questions.socraticHint: Match the animal group with what protects its skin from the outside.

questions.prompt: A crocodile in the Mara River lays eggs on sandy banks and has dry, scaly skin. In which vertebrate class does it belong?
questions.explanation: Crocodiles, snakes, lizards, and tortoises are reptiles because they have dry scaly skin and lay eggs on land.
questions.socraticHint: Does a crocodile have moist amphibian skin or tough, dry scaly skin?

questions.prompt: True or False: A whale and a dolphin are fish because they swim in the ocean.
questions.explanation: Whales and dolphins are warm-blooded mammals that breathe air through lungs and give birth to live calves.
questions.socraticHint: Do whales feed their young milk and breathe air at the surface of the water?

questions.prompt: Animals whose body temperature changes with the temperature of their surroundings are described as ____-blooded.
questions.explanation: Reptiles, amphibians, and fish are cold-blooded (ectothermic); they rely on external heat to warm up.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the opposite of warm-blooded.

questions.prompt: While visiting Lake Baringo, Dennis observed an animal with dry scaly skin basking in the morning sun on a flat rock. Why was the animal sunbathing?

options.text: It was breathing air through its gills.
It is a cold-blooded reptile absorbing heat from the sun to warm its body and become active.
It was drying its feathers after swimming.
It was producing milk for its young.

questions.correctAnswer: It is a cold-blooded reptile absorbing heat from the sun to warm its body and become active.
questions.explanation: Reptiles cannot generate their own body heat, so they bask in the sun to raise their body temperature.
questions.socraticHint: Why do lizards and crocodiles lie motionless on warm rocks in the morning?

questions.prompt: Arrange the life cycle stages of a frog from beginning to adulthood:

options.text: Jelly-like eggs laid in calm water
Tadpole with gills and a swimming tail
Tadpole grows hind legs and lungs
Adult frog hops on land with four legs and no tail

questions.correctAnswer: Jelly-like eggs laid in calm water, Tadpole with gills and a swimming tail, Tadpole grows hind legs and lungs, Adult frog hops on land with four legs and no tail
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis starts with eggs (spawn), hatches into an aquatic tadpole, develops limbs, and becomes an adult frog.
questions.socraticHint: Start with what is laid in the water ponds, followed by the swimming stage.

questions.prompt: Which Kenyan bird is the largest flightless bird in the world and can run at high speeds across the savanna?
questions.explanation: The ostrich is the largest living bird; although it cannot fly, it has powerful legs capable of running over 65 km/h.
questions.socraticHint: Which giant savanna bird has long strong legs and lays the largest eggs?

questions.prompt: How many walking legs does a typical adult insect have?
questions.explanation: All adult insects possess three pairs of jointed legs (total of 6 legs) attached to the thorax.
questions.socraticHint: Count the legs of an ant, bee, or grasshopper. How many are there in total?

questions.prompt: What are the three main body parts of an insect?
questions.explanation: An insect's body is divided into three distinct segments: the head (front), thorax (middle), and abdomen (rear).
questions.socraticHint: Which trio represents the standard anatomical segments of an insect body?

questions.prompt: True or False: A spider is an insect because it is small and crawls on walls.
questions.explanation: Spiders are arachnids, not insects; they have 8 legs, 2 body parts, and no antennae or wings.
questions.socraticHint: Count a spider's legs: does it have 6 legs like an insect, or 8 legs?

questions.prompt: An earthworm has a soft, segmented body and moves through garden soil without bones; therefore, it is classified as an ____.
questions.explanation: Earthworms do not have any bones or backbones, so they are invertebrates.
questions.socraticHint: What general term describes all animals that lack a backbone?

questions.prompt: To which body part of an insect are all six walking legs and wings attached?
questions.explanation: The thorax is the middle segment of an insect where the legs and wings are anchored.
questions.socraticHint: Which middle section of an insect bears the locomotive organs?

questions.prompt: Which pair of organs on an insect's head is used for sensing touch, smell, and vibrations in the air?
questions.explanation: Antennae are sensory organs located on the head that detect chemicals, touch, and air movement.
questions.socraticHint: What two long feelers stick out from the front of an insect's head?

questions.prompt: Match each small animal to its correct description:

options.text: Honeybee -> Insect with 6 legs and a painful defensive stinger
Garden snail -> Invertebrate with a soft body and coiled protective shell
Spider -> Arachnid with 8 legs and silk-spinning spinnerets
Earthworm -> Burrowing invertebrate that loosens and enriches soil

questions.correctAnswer: Honeybee -> Insect with 6 legs and a painful defensive stinger, Garden snail -> Invertebrate with a soft body and coiled protective shell, Spider -> Arachnid with 8 legs and silk-spinning spinnerets, Earthworm -> Burrowing invertebrate that loosens and enriches soil
questions.explanation: These invertebrates have specialized body structures that allow them to thrive in diverse micro-habitats.
questions.socraticHint: Match the animal to its unique feature (legs, shell, or stinger).

matchingPairs.rightText: Insect with 6 legs and a painful defensive stinger
Invertebrate with a soft body and coiled protective shell
Arachnid with 8 legs and silk-spinning spinnerets
Burrowing invertebrate that loosens and enriches soil

questions.prompt: A snail protects its soft body from predators and drying out by retreating into its hard, calcium-rich ____.
questions.explanation: The spiral shell provides a protective shelter for the snail against danger and dehydration.
questions.socraticHint: What hard spiral home does a snail carry on its back?

questions.prompt: During outdoor cleaning at school, Kevin accidentally disturbed a wasp nest under the classroom eaves. What is the safest immediate action for Kevin and his classmates?

options.text: Stand still and shout loudly at the wasps.
Move away quickly and quietly without flailing arms or hitting the insects, and alert the teacher.
Throw stones at the nest to break it into pieces.
Try to catch the wasps with bare hands.

questions.correctAnswer: Move away quickly and quietly without flailing arms or hitting the insects, and alert the teacher.
questions.explanation: Swatting or screaming agitates wasps and triggers a swarm attack. Backing away calmly prevents multiple stings.
questions.socraticHint: Does waving your arms and shouting calm stinging insects, or make them attack?

questions.prompt: Which tool should a young scientist use to observe the tiny legs and mouthparts of a live ant without injuring it?
questions.explanation: A magnifying lens enlarges tiny structures without causing harm to live specimens.
questions.socraticHint: Which glass tool makes small objects appear larger?

questions.prompt: True or False: Earthworms are harmful pests in a farm shamba and should be eliminated with chemical sprays.
questions.explanation: Earthworms are beneficial; their burrowing aerates the soil and their castings provide rich organic fertilizer.
questions.socraticHint: Do earthworms help plants grow by loosening the soil and creating compost?

questions.prompt: Arrange the safety steps to take if someone is stung by a bee in the school garden:

options.text: Move to a safe, shaded area away from the swarm
Gently scrape away the visible stinger without squeezing it
Wash the sting area with clean water and mild soap
Apply a cold compress or ice pack and report to the school first aid post

questions.correctAnswer: Move to a safe, shaded area away from the swarm, Gently scrape away the visible stinger without squeezing it, Wash the sting area with clean water and mild soap, Apply a cold compress or ice pack and report to the school first aid post
questions.explanation: Standard first aid: get to safety, remove stinger, clean site, and apply cold treatment to reduce swelling.
questions.socraticHint: First ensure you are away from more bees, then treat the sting.

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: Which chisel-shaped front teeth are primarily used for biting and cutting food?
questions.explanation: Incisors are the 8 sharp, flat-edged front teeth adapted for biting and cutting food into pieces.
questions.socraticHint: Which flat teeth at the front of your mouth bite into an apple or a piece of bread?

questions.prompt: Which sharp, pointed teeth are designed for gripping and tearing tough food such as meat?
questions.explanation: Canines are pointed, cone-shaped teeth situated next to the incisors that tear fibrous food.
questions.socraticHint: Which pointed teeth are named after dog teeth and sit at the corners of your smile?

questions.prompt: True or False: An adult human being with a complete permanent set of teeth has a total of 32 teeth.
questions.explanation: A full permanent set consists of 32 teeth: 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars, and 12 molars.
questions.socraticHint: How many permanent teeth does an adult have: 20 or 32?

questions.prompt: The temporary set of teeth that young children grow, which begins to fall out around age six, is called ____ teeth.
questions.explanation: Milk teeth (primary teeth) total 20 in number and are naturally replaced by permanent teeth.
questions.socraticHint: What common drink gives its name to a baby's first set of teeth?

questions.prompt: How many total milk teeth does a young child have before shedding begins?
questions.explanation: Children develop a complete set of 20 milk teeth (10 in the upper jaw and 10 in the lower jaw).
questions.socraticHint: Adults have 32 teeth; young children have 12 fewer teeth.

questions.prompt: Match each tooth type to its main function:

options.text: Molar -> Grinding food into a fine pulp

questions.correctAnswer: Incisor -> Cutting and biting food, Canine -> Tearing tough food, Premolar -> Chewing and crushing food, Molar -> Grinding food into a fine pulp
questions.explanation: Each tooth shape correlates directly with its mechanical role in chewing and food processing.
questions.socraticHint: Connect the chisel shape to cutting, the pointed shape to tearing, and broad shapes to grinding.

matchingPairs.rightText: Grinding food into a fine pulp

questions.prompt: Which teeth are the largest and have wide, flat surfaces with multiple cusps located at the very back of the mouth?
questions.explanation: Molars are situated at the back of the jaw and possess large surface areas for thorough grinding.
questions.socraticHint: Which broad grinding teeth are located furthest back in your mouth?

questions.prompt: True or False: If an adult loses a permanent tooth due to an accident, a new natural tooth will grow back in its place.
questions.explanation: Permanent teeth are not replaced once lost; only artificial replacement (dentures/implants) is possible.
questions.socraticHint: Does a permanent tooth grow back after being knocked out in an adult?

questions.prompt: The natural process where children's milk teeth loosen and fall out to make way for permanent teeth is called tooth ____.
questions.explanation: Tooth shedding is the normal biological process where primary tooth roots dissolve so adult teeth can erupt.
questions.socraticHint: What word describes trees dropping leaves or children dropping baby teeth?

questions.prompt: Ten-year-old Omondi noticed that his lower front tooth was slightly wobbly and loose, but it didn't hurt. What is the most scientific explanation for this?

options.text: His teeth are turning into fish scales.
His milk incisor is naturally shedding as the permanent adult tooth pushes up beneath it.
His tooth has decayed completely and will cause all teeth to fall out.
He ate too much ugali and weakened the jaw bone.

questions.correctAnswer: His milk incisor is naturally shedding as the permanent adult tooth pushes up beneath it.
questions.explanation: Between ages 6 and 12, milk teeth normally loosen and shed as permanent teeth grow underneath.
questions.socraticHint: Is a loose baby tooth in a 10-year-old a normal milestone or an illness?

questions.prompt: Arrange the teeth in order from the front center of the jaw to the back of the mouth:
questions.correctAnswer: Incisors (front), Canine (beside incisors), Premolars (behind canines), Molars (furthest back)
questions.explanation: The anatomical sequence from front to back is: incisors, canines, premolars, and molars.
questions.socraticHint: Start with your front biting teeth and move your tongue backward.

questions.prompt: How many canines does a human being have in each jaw (upper and lower)?
questions.explanation: There are two canines in the upper jaw and two in the lower jaw, making 4 canines in total.
questions.socraticHint: Count the pointed teeth on your top jaw: one on the left, one on the right.

questions.prompt: How many times a day should a person brush their teeth to keep them clean and healthy?
questions.explanation: Dentists recommend brushing at least twice daily—in the morning after breakfast and before bed at night.
questions.socraticHint: When should you brush your teeth: once in the morning and once at night?

questions.prompt: What is the sticky, colourless or yellowish film of bacteria that forms on uncleaned teeth called?
questions.explanation: Plaque is a sticky layer of bacteria and food particles that causes tooth decay if not brushed away.
questions.socraticHint: What sticky substance builds up on teeth when they are not brushed?

questions.prompt: True or False: Eating large amounts of sugary candies and drinking sweet sodas throughout the day protects teeth from decay.
questions.explanation: Sugar feeds oral bacteria, which produce harmful acids that dissolve tooth enamel and cause cavities.
questions.socraticHint: Does excess sugar help teeth stay strong, or does it cause tooth decay?

questions.prompt: A traditional chewing stick used to clean teeth in many Kenyan communities is commonly known as a ____.
questions.explanation: A mswaki is a traditional chewing stick with natural antibacterial properties that cleans teeth effectively.
questions.socraticHint: What Kiswahili word refers to both a toothbrush and a traditional chewing stick?

questions.prompt: What mineral is commonly added to toothpaste because it strengthens tooth enamel against acid attacks?
questions.explanation: Fluoride remineralizes and hardens tooth enamel, protecting it against decay.
questions.socraticHint: Look at a tube of toothpaste: which protective mineral is prominently advertised?

questions.prompt: A medical specialist who checks, treats, and cares for human teeth and gums is called a ____.
questions.explanation: A dentist is a qualified healthcare professional specialized in oral health and dentistry.
questions.socraticHint: Which doctor do you visit when you have a toothache or cavity?

questions.prompt: Match the dental problem to its cause or symptom:

options.text: Cavity (caries) -> Hole in the tooth caused by bacterial acid
Plaque -> Sticky film of bacteria on unbrushed teeth
Toothache -> Pain caused by decay reaching the tooth nerve
Bleeding gums -> Sign of gum disease caused by poor oral hygiene

questions.correctAnswer: Cavity (caries) -> Hole in the tooth caused by bacterial acid, Plaque -> Sticky film of bacteria on unbrushed teeth, Toothache -> Pain caused by decay reaching the tooth nerve, Bleeding gums -> Sign of gum disease caused by poor oral hygiene
questions.explanation: Understanding dental issues helps learners take preventive care before problems become severe.
questions.socraticHint: Connect each oral health term with its accurate medical description.

matchingPairs.rightText: Hole in the tooth caused by bacterial acid
Sticky film of bacteria on unbrushed teeth
Pain caused by decay reaching the tooth nerve
Sign of gum disease caused by poor oral hygiene

questions.prompt: Using teeth to open metal soda bottle tops or crack hard stones can cause the hard outer tooth layer, called ____, to crack or chip.
questions.explanation: Enamel is the hard, protective white outer covering of the crown of the tooth.
questions.socraticHint: What is the hard, shiny white outer shell of a tooth called?

questions.prompt: Sharon went camping with the scouts and forgot her plastic toothbrush. Nearby, she found a neem (mwarobaini) tree. How can Sharon safely clean her teeth?

options.text: Use a sharp metal knife to scrape her teeth.
Cut a fresh pencil-sized twig, chew one end gently until it forms soft bristles, and brush her teeth thoroughly.
Rub her teeth with coarse sand and gravel from the river.
Do nothing for a whole week.

questions.correctAnswer: Cut a fresh pencil-sized twig, chew one end gently until it forms soft bristles, and brush her teeth thoroughly.
questions.explanation: A traditional chewing stick from a safe tree such as neem or mswaki works effectively as an organic toothbrush.
questions.socraticHint: How do traditional communities make a soft brush from a chewing twig?

questions.prompt: Which food item is best for strengthening teeth and bones because it is rich in calcium?
questions.explanation: Milk and dairy products are packed with calcium and vitamin D, which build dense, strong teeth and bones.
questions.socraticHint: Which calcium-rich white drink builds strong bones and teeth?

questions.prompt: True or False: Dental floss is a thin thread used to remove trapped food and plaque from narrow spaces between teeth where a toothbrush cannot reach.
questions.explanation: Flossing cleans between teeth to prevent interdental cavities and gum inflammation.
questions.socraticHint: Does dental thread (floss) clean between tight teeth?

questions.prompt: Arrange the correct steps for brushing teeth properly:

options.text: Apply a pea-sized amount of toothpaste on a clean toothbrush
Brush the outer, inner, and chewing surfaces using gentle circular strokes for 2 minutes
Gently clean the surface of the tongue to remove bacteria
Spit out excess toothpaste and rinse mouth thoroughly with clean water

questions.correctAnswer: Apply a pea-sized amount of toothpaste on a clean toothbrush, Brush the outer, inner, and chewing surfaces using gentle circular strokes for 2 minutes, Gently clean the surface of the tongue to remove bacteria, Spit out excess toothpaste and rinse mouth thoroughly with clean water
questions.explanation: Correct brushing protocol: apply paste, brush all tooth surfaces, clean the tongue, and spit/rinse.
questions.socraticHint: Start with preparing your brush and finish by rinsing your mouth.

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?

questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: Where does the process of digestion begin in the human body?
questions.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth where teeth chew food and saliva starts breaking down starches.
questions.socraticHint: Where does food first enter your body and get mixed with saliva?

questions.prompt: What is the name of the muscular tube that carries food from the mouth down into the stomach?
questions.explanation: The gullet (oesophagus) is the food pipe that pushes chewed food into the stomach.
questions.socraticHint: What pipe carries food, as opposed to the windpipe which carries air?

questions.prompt: True or False: The stomach is an elastic muscular bag that churns food with digestive juices and acid.
questions.explanation: The stomach contracts its muscular walls to churn food with gastric acid and enzymes.
questions.socraticHint: Does your stomach churn food like a blender to break it into a soupy liquid?

questions.prompt: Liquid produced by glands in the mouth that softens chewed food and digests starches is called ____.
questions.explanation: Saliva contains the enzyme amylase, which moistens food and begins chemical digestion of carbohydrates.
questions.socraticHint: What watery fluid fills your mouth when you smell delicious food?

questions.prompt: In which organ is digestion of food completed and most digested nutrients absorbed into the bloodstream?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is the site of final chemical digestion and absorption of nutrients into blood vessels.
questions.socraticHint: Where are digested nutrients absorbed into the blood: small intestine or large intestine?

questions.prompt: Match each digestive organ to its primary function:

options.text: Mouth -> Chewing food and mixing with saliva
Stomach -> Churning food with acid and protein enzymes
Small intestine -> Completing digestion and absorbing nutrients
Large intestine -> Absorbing water and forming solid waste

questions.correctAnswer: Mouth -> Chewing food and mixing with saliva, Stomach -> Churning food with acid and protein enzymes, Small intestine -> Completing digestion and absorbing nutrients, Large intestine -> Absorbing water and forming solid waste
questions.explanation: Each organ along the alimentary canal carries out a specialized stage of digestion.
questions.socraticHint: Link each organ to its main task in processing food.

matchingPairs.rightText: Chewing food and mixing with saliva
Churning food with acid and protein enzymes
Absorbing water and forming solid waste

questions.prompt: What is the main role of the large intestine?

options.text: To absorb water and mineral salts from undigested food
To pump oxygen into the blood
To grind large pieces of meat

questions.correctAnswer: To absorb water and mineral salts from undigested food
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs excess water from remaining food waste, turning it into semi-solid faeces.
questions.socraticHint: Does the large intestine absorb nutrients, or does it reabsorb water to prevent dehydration?

questions.prompt: True or False: Undigested solid food waste is temporarily stored in the rectum before leaving the body through the anus.
questions.explanation: The rectum holds faecal matter until muscle contractions expel it through the anus.
questions.socraticHint: Is the rectum the temporary storage chamber for stool at the end of the digestive tract?

questions.prompt: The wave-like muscular contractions that push food along the gullet and intestines are called ____.
questions.explanation: Peristalsis is the rhythmic involuntary contraction of digestive tract muscles that propels food.
questions.socraticHint: What scientific term describes the squeezing wave motion of the digestive muscles?

questions.prompt: Chebet swallowed a bite of roasted maize without chewing it properly. She felt a sharp, uncomfortable lump slowly moving down her chest. Which organ was struggling to push the unchewed food?
questions.explanation: The gullet connects the throat to the stomach through the chest; unchewed boluses stretch its muscular walls.
questions.socraticHint: Which tube passes down the middle of the chest behind the breastbone to reach the stomach?

questions.prompt: Arrange the organs in the correct sequence through which food travels during digestion:
questions.correctAnswer: Mouth, Gullet (Oesophagus), Stomach, Small intestine, Large intestine and Anus
questions.explanation: Food enters the mouth, passes down the gullet, enters the stomach, moves to the small intestine, and ends in the large intestine/anus.
questions.socraticHint: Follow the path of food from where you take a bite down to where waste exits.

questions.prompt: What is the function of the strong acid found naturally inside the human stomach?

options.text: It prevents food from entering the gullet
It kills harmful bacteria in food and provides an acidic medium for protein digestion

questions.correctAnswer: It kills harmful bacteria in food and provides an acidic medium for protein digestion
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach destroys ingested microbes and activates digestive enzymes.
questions.socraticHint: Why does the stomach contain acid: to kill germs and digest meat/protein, or to cool food?

questions.prompt: Why is it important to chew food slowly and thoroughly before swallowing?

options.text: It changes food directly into water
It breaks food into smaller pieces, making it easier for enzymes and the stomach to digest
It prevents food from ever reaching the stomach
It stops the mouth from producing saliva

questions.correctAnswer: It breaks food into smaller pieces, making it easier for enzymes and the stomach to digest
questions.explanation: Thorough chewing increases the surface area of food for digestive juices to act upon efficiently.
questions.socraticHint: Does smaller crushed food digest faster and easier than large swallowed chunks?

questions.prompt: Which component of our diet adds bulk to stool and helps prevent painful constipation?
questions.explanation: Fibre (roughage) absorbs water and adds bulk to waste, promoting smooth bowel movements.
questions.socraticHint: What plant component found in whole grains and kales keeps our digestive waste moving?

questions.prompt: True or False: Drinking enough clean water throughout the day helps dissolve nutrients and prevents hard, dry stool.
questions.explanation: Water is vital for chemical digestion, dissolving nutrients, and keeping waste soft and easy to pass.
questions.socraticHint: Does water keep digestion smooth and waste soft?

questions.prompt: The difficulty in passing hard, dry stool due to lack of water or roughage in the diet is called ____.
questions.explanation: Constipation occurs when waste moves too slowly through the large intestine and loses too much water.
questions.socraticHint: What medical term describes difficulty passing hard bowel movements?

questions.prompt: Which of the following local Kenyan foods is the richest source of dietary fibre (roughage)?
questions.explanation: Green leafy vegetables and legumes are rich in plant cellulose and dietary fibre.
questions.socraticHint: Which option contains fresh vegetables and legumes with fibrous skins?

questions.prompt: What is the biological term for the removal of undigested food waste from the body via the anus?
questions.explanation: Egestion is the discharge of undigested matter from the digestive tract.
questions.socraticHint: Ingestion is taking food in; what is expelling solid waste out?

questions.prompt: Match each digestive stage to what occurs during that phase:

Egestion -> Expelling undigested waste as faeces

questions.correctAnswer: Ingestion -> Putting food into the mouth, Digestion -> Breaking down food chemically and mechanically, Absorption -> Nutrients entering the blood through intestinal walls, Egestion -> Expelling undigested waste as faeces
questions.explanation: These four stages represent the complete pathway and transformation of food in our bodies.
questions.socraticHint: Follow the stages: take in, break down, absorb, and remove waste.

matchingPairs.rightText: Breaking down food chemically and mechanically
Nutrients entering the blood through intestinal walls

questions.prompt: Tiny finger-like projections lining the inner walls of the small intestine that increase surface area for nutrient absorption are called ____.

questions.socraticHint: What microscopic finger-like projections line the small intestine?

questions.prompt: Kiprono has been experiencing painful constipation and stomach cramps for several days. He rarely drinks water and only eats refined white bread and sausages. What dietary change will help him most?

options.text: Eat more white sugar and candies.
Drink at least 6 to 8 glasses of clean water daily and eat fresh fruits, kales, and whole grains.
Stop eating all fruits and vegetables immediately.

questions.correctAnswer: Drink at least 6 to 8 glasses of clean water daily and eat fresh fruits, kales, and whole grains.
questions.explanation: Increasing water intake and dietary fibre softens stool and restores regular bowel movements.
questions.socraticHint: Which two things restore smooth digestion: water and fibre, or more sugar?

questions.prompt: Which digestive juice produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder helps break down fats into tiny droplets?
questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies fats in the small intestine, breaking large fat globules into tiny droplets for easy enzyme action.
questions.socraticHint: Which greenish-yellow fluid produced by the liver digests fats?

questions.prompt: True or False: Rushing through meals and swallowing large chunks of food without chewing can cause indigestion, bloating, and choking.
questions.explanation: Eating too fast swallows air and overburdens the stomach, leading to indigestion and heartburn.
questions.socraticHint: Is eating hurriedly and gulping down food healthy or harmful?

questions.prompt: Arrange the healthy mealtime habits in the recommended order:

options.text: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and running water before sitting to eat
Sit comfortably and take manageable bites of food
Chew each bite slowly and thoroughly before swallowing
Drink water moderately and rinse mouth with water after eating

questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and running water before sitting to eat, Sit comfortably and take manageable bites of food, Chew each bite slowly and thoroughly before swallowing, Drink water moderately and rinse mouth with water after eating
questions.explanation: Good hygiene starts before the meal, continues with mindful eating, and ends with proper hydration and mouth rinsing.
questions.socraticHint: Start with hand washing and finish after the meal is concluded.

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...

questions.prompt: What is environmental pollution?

options.text: The natural falling of rain from clouds
The introduction of harmful or poisonous substances into the environment
The process of planting many green trees in a forest
The building of modern classrooms in a school

questions.correctAnswer: The introduction of harmful or poisonous substances into the environment
questions.explanation: Pollution occurs when contaminants degrade air, water, or land quality and harm living organisms.
questions.socraticHint: Does pollution make the environment clean or dirty and harmful?

questions.prompt: Which of the following activities causes air pollution?

options.text: Sweeping dry leaves into a compost pit
Burning plastic waste and rubber tyres in the open air
Watering vegetable seedlings in the garden

questions.correctAnswer: Burning plastic waste and rubber tyres in the open air
questions.explanation: Burning plastic releases dangerous toxic smoke, soot, and chemical fumes into the atmosphere.
questions.socraticHint: Which action produces thick, bad-smelling smoke that hurts your chest when inhaled?

questions.prompt: True or False: Washing clothes, dishes, and spraying chemical pesticides directly in rivers causes water pollution.
questions.explanation: Soap detergents, chemicals, and dirty wash water contaminate river water, poisoning fish and downstream communities.
questions.socraticHint: Do soaps and pesticides make river water safe or polluted for people drinking downstream?

questions.prompt: Unwanted and excessively loud sounds that can damage human eardrums and cause headaches are known as ____ pollution.
questions.explanation: Noise pollution is unwanted or harmful environmental sound that disrupts health and hearing.
questions.socraticHint: What kind of pollution comes from blaring speakers, hooting, and roaring engines?

options.text: Spreading decomposed farmyard manure on garden crops
Harvesting rainwater from iron sheet roofs
Indiscriminate dumping of non-biodegradable plastics and broken glass

questions.correctAnswer: Indiscriminate dumping of non-biodegradable plastics and broken glass

questions.socraticHint: Which waste item takes hundreds of years to rot in the ground?

questions.prompt: Match each type of pollution to its primary source:

options.text: Air pollution -> Exhaust fumes from old vehicles and factory chimneys

Soil pollution -> Discarded plastic bags and uncollected market garbage
Noise pollution -> Blaring commercial loudspeakers and loud traffic horns

questions.correctAnswer: Air pollution -> Exhaust fumes from old vehicles and factory chimneys, Water pollution -> Untreated sewage and chemical fertilizer runoff into rivers, Soil pollution -> Discarded plastic bags and uncollected market garbage, Noise pollution -> Blaring commercial loudspeakers and loud traffic horns

questions.socraticHint: Link each pollution category with where its contaminants originate.

questions.socraticHint: Why must a room always be well-ventilated when a jiko is in use?

questions.prompt: Harmful chemicals sprayed on agricultural crops to kill pests that often wash into rivers during heavy rains are called ____.

questions.socraticHint: What chemical sprays kill agricultural insects and pests?

questions.prompt: A car repair garage next to a school empties old engine oil and battery acid directly into an open storm drain. What is the most dangerous consequence of this practice?

options.text: It cleans the school storm drain.
The toxic chemicals seep into underground water and wash into rivers, poisoning drinking water and aquatic life.

It makes passing cars drive faster.

questions.correctAnswer: The toxic chemicals seep into underground water and wash into rivers, poisoning drinking water and aquatic life.

questions.prompt: Arrange the chain of events showing how untreated sewage leads to illness in a community:

options.text: Untreated raw sewage is discharged into a local river
Water becomes contaminated with cholera and typhoid bacteria
Downstream residents fetch and drink untreated river water
Residents fall ill with severe waterborne diarrhoeal diseases

questions.correctAnswer: Untreated raw sewage is discharged into a local river, Water becomes contaminated with cholera and typhoid bacteria, Downstream residents fetch and drink untreated river water, Residents fall ill with severe waterborne diarrhoeal diseases

questions.prompt: Which of the following creates severe noise pollution that can cause temporary hearing loss and stress?

options.text: The sound of falling rain on grass
Blaring airplane jet engines and heavy industrial machinery
Gentle rustling of tree leaves in a breeze

questions.correctAnswer: Blaring airplane jet engines and heavy industrial machinery
questions.explanation: Decibel levels above 85 dB, such as from jet aircraft and heavy machinery, cause hearing damage.
questions.socraticHint: Which option produces extremely loud, jarring sound energy?

questions.prompt: What does the '3Rs' rule for waste management stand for?

questions.prompt: True or False: Breathing air full of smoke, soot, and industrial dust can cause respiratory problems such as coughing and asthma.
questions.explanation: Airborne particulates irritate the lining of the lungs and worsen conditions like asthma and bronchitis.
questions.socraticHint: Does dirty, smoky air irritate your lungs and respiratory tract?

questions.prompt: Organic waste such as vegetable peelings, bean pods, and maize cobs can be converted into rich natural fertilizer called ____.
questions.explanation: Composting decomposes organic waste into nutrient-rich humus that enriches garden soil.
questions.socraticHint: What organic manure is made by letting food scraps decompose in a pit?

questions.prompt: How does water pollution directly affect aquatic organisms like tilapia and catfish?

options.text: It makes fish grow warm fur
It helps fish breathe air on land
It turns river water into milk

questions.explanation: Recycling involves industrial reprocessing of waste materials into new useful products.

questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen, purifying the surrounding air.
questions.socraticHint: Which greenhouse gas do plants absorb during photosynthesis?

options.text: Dump all the rubbish into the nearby drinking water well.
Provide separate labelled bins for organic waste (to make compost) and plastic waste (to be collected for recycling).
Dig a hole in the middle of the playground and set all the rubbish on fire.
Throw all the waste over the perimeter fence into the neighbour's plot.

questions.correctAnswer: Provide separate labelled bins for organic waste (to make compost) and plastic waste (to be collected for recycling).
questions.explanation: Source separation allows organics to be safely composted while plastics can be collected for recycling.
questions.socraticHint: What waste sorting practice separates rot-able food scraps from recyclable plastics?

questions.prompt: Why did the Kenyan government implement a strict ban on single-use plastic carrier bags in 2017?

options.text: Because plastic bags absorbed all the rain in Kenya
Because plastic bags caused cars to break down
Because plastic bags choked drainage systems, killed livestock that swallowed them, and polluted soils without decomposing
Because plastic bags were too heavy to carry

questions.socraticHint: What environmental and animal health hazards did flying plastic bags cause in Kenya?

questions.prompt: True or False: Burning piles of dry plastic bottles in your backyard is an eco-friendly way of reducing landfill waste.

questions.socraticHint: Does burning plastic destroy the material safely, or does it release deadly toxic air pollutants?

questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for organizing a successful school compound clean-up drive:

options.text: Equip learners with protective gloves, litter bags, and masks
Collect and separate litter into organic scraps and recyclable plastics
Transfer organic waste to the school compost pit and recyclables to collection bins
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean water after the clean-up

questions.correctAnswer: Equip learners with protective gloves, litter bags, and masks, Collect and separate litter into organic scraps and recyclable plastics, Transfer organic waste to the school compost pit and recyclables to collection bins, Wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean water after the clean-up

questions.socraticHint: Start with protective gear and conclude with hand hygiene.

questions.explanation: Drip irrigation minimizes water loss from evaporation and runoff by targeting plant root zones directly.

questions.socraticHint: Does a running tap let clean water flow unused down the drain?

questions.explanation: Mulching shades the soil surface, reducing water loss through evaporation.

Direct the downpipe into a clean, covered water storage tank

To prevent fish from flying inside

To prevent water from turning into milk

To add sugar to the water
To remove suspended dirt particles, silt, and debris

questions.correctAnswer: To remove suspended dirt particles, silt, and debris
questions.explanation: Filtration mechanically strains out solid particles, leaving the water clear.
