It acts as a porous drainage and watering core, allowing water poured at the top to reach lower root levels evenly
It makes the sack too heavy to be stolen by monkeys

questions.correctAnswer: It acts as a porous drainage and watering core, allowing water poured at the top to reach lower root levels evenly
questions.explanation: The stone core creates a continuous vertical conduit for irrigation water to percolate down to the lowest tiers without waterlogging.
questions.socraticHint: How does a hollow pipe filled with small pebbles in the center help water trickle all the way to the bottom?

questions.prompt: How are planting holes created on the sides of a multi-storey sack garden without tearing the sack apart?

options.text: By setting fire to the sack with a matchstick
By kicking large jagged holes into the sack with boots
By making neat small staggered cuts (cross slits) with a sharp knife at 15–20 cm intervals

questions.correctAnswer: By making neat small staggered cuts (cross slits) with a sharp knife at 15–20 cm intervals
questions.explanation: Neat diagonal slits maintain the structural strength of the woven sack while creating secure pockets for seedling insertion.
questions.socraticHint: Small, neat cross cuts allow seedlings to poke through without making the sack burst open.

questions.prompt: Which combination of crops is best arranged on a multi-storey sack garden for optimal sunlight exposure and yield?

options.text: Kales or spinach along the side slits, and capsicums, coriander, or onions on the flat top
Eucalyptus on the sides and pine trees on top
Only water lilies on the sides and floating reeds on top
Coffee bushes on the sides and tea bushes on top

questions.correctAnswer: Kales or spinach along the side slits, and capsicums, coriander, or onions on the flat top
questions.explanation: Leafy greens trail outward along the sides, while fruiting or upright herbs on top receive maximal overhead sunlight.
questions.socraticHint: Leafy greens thrive along the vertical walls; which upright vegetables grow well on the top surface?

questions.prompt: Applying a thin layer of dry grass or sawdust over the exposed soil surface of container pots to reduce water evaporation is called micro-_______.
questions.explanation: Micro-mulching conserves moisture in small containers, suppresses weeds, and maintains even soil temperatures.
questions.socraticHint: What agricultural practice covers soil with dry organic matter to conserve moisture?

questions.prompt: Over-watering container plants until water continuously pools on the soil surface is beneficial and prevents all plant diseases.
questions.explanation: Overwatering suffocates roots, leaches soluble nutrients out through drainage holes, and encourages fungal damping-off.
questions.socraticHint: Can giving too much standing water drown roots and cause fungal rot?

questions.prompt: What is progressive leaf harvesting (pricking) when harvesting container-grown sukuma wiki (kales)?

options.text: Stripping off all leaves including the tiny central shoot
Snapping off only the mature lower outer leaves while leaving the top growing shoot intact to produce more leaves
Cutting the whole plant down at ground level with a panga
Pulling the whole plant out by the roots and throwing the pot away

questions.correctAnswer: Snapping off only the mature lower outer leaves while leaving the top growing shoot intact to produce more leaves
questions.explanation: Progressive harvesting ensures prolonged vegetative production, allowing households to pick fresh vegetables continuously for months.
questions.socraticHint: Why do farmers pick only the big lower leaves of kales for supper while letting the top tip keep growing?

questions.prompt: A learner notices that water applied to a multi-storey sack garden drains out of the bottom within seconds without wetting the soil. What is the cause?

options.text: Earthworms have built an underground city
The soil has turned into gasoline
The soil has dried out and shrunk away from the sack sides, creating open gaps that allow water to bypass the roots
The sack is made of solid glass

questions.correctAnswer: The soil has dried out and shrunk away from the sack sides, creating open gaps that allow water to bypass the roots
questions.explanation: Severely dry potting soil shrinks; watering slowly in stages or tamping edges rehydrates the core properly.
questions.socraticHint: When dry soil shrinks and pulls away from the container edge, where does water immediately run down?

questions.prompt: Which simple water-saving irrigation method uses an inverted plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap buried near the roots of container plants?
questions.explanation: Bottle drip irrigation delivers slow, targeted moisture directly to root zones with minimal evaporation losses.
questions.socraticHint: What method uses an upside-down water bottle to drip water drop-by-drop onto the roots?

questions.prompt: How does staking support climbing container crops like cherry tomatoes or passion fruit vines?

options.text: It provides vertical support stakes that keep vines and heavy fruits off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal infection
It attracts caterpillar pests to the garden
It cools the plant roots down to zero degrees
It stops the plant from absorbing sunlight

questions.correctAnswer: It provides vertical support stakes that keep vines and heavy fruits off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal infection
questions.explanation: Staking trains vines upward, improving air circulation, sunlight penetration, and preventing ground-contact rot.
questions.socraticHint: Why do farmers tie tomato stems to upright wooden sticks?

questions.prompt: The practice of growing plants without soil by providing nutrients through mineral-rich water solutions is known as _______.
questions.explanation: Hydroponics is soilless cultivation where roots absorb nutrients directly from an oxygenated water solution.
questions.socraticHint: The prefix "hydro-" means water: what is water-based soilless farming called?

questions.prompt: How does maintaining a family vertical container garden contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal of "Zero Hunger" in Kenya?

options.text: It forces everyone to eat only wild grass
It provides a continuous year-round supply of fresh, nutrient-rich indigenous vegetables right at the doorstep at negligible cost
It eliminates the need for any agriculture across Kenya

questions.correctAnswer: It provides a continuous year-round supply of fresh, nutrient-rich indigenous vegetables right at the doorstep at negligible cost
questions.explanation: Micro-gardening strengthens household nutritional security, dietary diversity, and resilience against fluctuating food prices.
questions.socraticHint: How does growing your own fresh greens at home improve family food security and nutrition?

questions.prompt: What is vegetative plant propagation in crop science?

options.text: Importing genetically modified seed bags from overseas
Multiplying plants using non-seed vegetative parts such as stems, roots, suckers, or tubers
Growing crops exclusively from dried flower seeds
Spraying chemical hormones onto bare soil

questions.correctAnswer: Multiplying plants using non-seed vegetative parts such as stems, roots, suckers, or tubers
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction using vegetative organs to generate complete, independent plants.
questions.socraticHint: When you plant sweet potato vines or cassava stems instead of seeds, what type of propagation is that?

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a major advantage of vegetative propagation over growing crops from seeds?

options.text: New plants take ten times longer to produce harvest
Plants grown vegetatively never need water
New plants are genetically identical to the parent and mature much faster than seed-grown crops
New plants produce completely random unpredictable fruit

questions.correctAnswer: New plants are genetically identical to the parent and mature much faster than seed-grown crops
questions.explanation: Asexual propagation preserves true-to-type traits (taste, yield, disease resistance) and bypasses the lengthy juvenile seed phase.
questions.socraticHint: Do cuttings grow faster and look exactly like the high-yielding mother plant?

questions.prompt: Which planting material is used to propagate sweet potato crops across Kenyan counties like Migori, Bungoma, and Homa Bay?
questions.explanation: Sweet potatoes are routinely multiplied using healthy, vigorous vine cuttings (terminal vine portions of 25–30 cm).
questions.socraticHint: What green creeping parts of the sweet potato plant do farmers cut and plant in ridges?

questions.prompt: What vegetative planting material is used to establish a new cassava crop on a farm in Kilifi or Busia?

options.text: Mature woody stem cuttings with active buds

questions.correctAnswer: Mature woody stem cuttings with active buds
questions.explanation: Cassava is propagated using mature woody stem cuttings (about 20–30 cm long) inserted into the soil at an angle or vertically.
questions.socraticHint: Which thick stem sticks with visible eye nodes are chopped and planted for cassava?

questions.prompt: Banana plants do not produce viable seeds for farming. What vegetative structures growing at the base of the parent pseudostem are used to propagate new banana plants?
questions.explanation: Bananas produce lateral offshoots called suckers from their underground rhizome (corm); sword suckers make the best planting material.
questions.socraticHint: What are the young shoot offshoots sprouting from the base of a mother banana tree called?

questions.prompt: Irish potatoes are propagated using underground swollen stems called stem tubers, which have "eyes" that sprout into new shoots.
questions.explanation: Irish potato tubers have auxiliary buds ("eyes") that sprout into vigorous stems and roots when planted.
questions.socraticHint: Do potato tubers have tiny little sprouts called "eyes" that grow into green plants?

questions.prompt: What vegetative propagation part is used when multiplying sugarcane stalks in the sugar belt of Western Kenya (e.g. Mumias, Awendo)?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is planted using stem cuttings called "setts", each containing 2–3 active nodes where root bands and shoots sprout.
questions.socraticHint: What cut sections of mature sweet cane with buds are laid horizontally in furrows?

questions.prompt: Pyrethrum, an insecticidal crop grown in high altitude zones like Nyandarua and Molo, is commonly multiplied using which vegetative method?
questions.explanation: Mature pyrethrum crowns are divided or split into individual rooted plantlets called splits and transplanted into prepared fields.
questions.socraticHint: Which method divides or "splits" the root crown of a mature pyrethrum bush into several pieces?

questions.prompt: Pineapple plants can be vegetatively propagated using crowns, slips, or _______ from the base of the parent plant.
questions.explanation: Pineapples are propagated vegetatively through crowns (tops), slips (side shoots on peduncle), and ground suckers.
questions.socraticHint: Like bananas, pineapples produce ground shoots called...

questions.prompt: Why is it critical for a farmer to obtain vegetative planting materials only from healthy, vigorous, disease-free mother plants?

options.text: Because viral, fungal, and bacterial diseases in the mother plant are directly transmitted into the new clonal crop
Because sick plants produce sweet honey
Because diseased plants grow twice as fast
Because sick plants scare away pests

questions.correctAnswer: Because viral, fungal, and bacterial diseases in the mother plant are directly transmitted into the new clonal crop
questions.explanation: Since vegetative offspring share the exact parent vascular tissues, systemic viruses (like cassava mosaic) are passed directly to daughter plants.
questions.socraticHint: If you take a stem cutting from a sick, diseased cassava plant, will the new plant also be infected with the disease?

questions.prompt: Tea bushes on Kenyan plantations in Kericho and Nandi are primarily multiplied through single-leaf internode stem cuttings raised in polythene sleeves.
questions.explanation: Clonal tea propagation uses single internode cuttings rooted in polythene tubes under nursery polythene tunnels.
questions.socraticHint: Do tea farmers use vegetative stem cuttings inside small plastic sleeves to raise tea clones?

questions.prompt: Which of the following crops is propagated through seeds (sexual propagation) rather than vegetative parts in standard Kenyan farming?
questions.explanation: Maize is an annual cereal propagated exclusively through sexual seeds; sweet potato, cassava, and sugarcane use vegetative cuttings.
questions.socraticHint: Which staple food is planted as individual grain seeds from a dry cob?

questions.prompt: What is the primary function of a crop nursery bed on a school farm?

options.text: To burn dry weeds from the farm
To provide intensive care and protection for delicate tiny seeds and young seedlings until they are sturdy enough for the main field
To store harvested maize cobs during the dry season
To park farm tractors and machinery safely

questions.correctAnswer: To provide intensive care and protection for delicate tiny seeds and young seedlings until they are sturdy enough for the main field
questions.explanation: Nursery beds protect tender young seedlings from harsh sunlight, pests, weeds, and heavy storms during their vulnerable early life.
questions.socraticHint: Just like a human baby nursery, what special care does a plant nursery provide for baby seedlings?

questions.prompt: Why is a light overhead shade built over a seedling nursery bed using dry grass or netting on a wooden frame?

options.text: To prevent the wind from ever blowing
To protect delicate seedlings from scorching midday sunshine and violent raindrops that could dislodge them
To make the nursery bed completely pitch-black dark 24 hours a day

questions.correctAnswer: To protect delicate seedlings from scorching midday sunshine and violent raindrops that could dislodge them
questions.explanation: Light thatch softens scorching direct UV heat and breaks heavy raindrops into fine mist, protecting tiny emerging shoots.
questions.socraticHint: How does an overhead thatched frame shield tender seedlings from direct burning sun and pounding raindrops?

questions.prompt: What watering tool should be used when irrigating a delicate seedling nursery bed?

options.text: A large bucket dumped violently from 2 meters above
A kitchen tablespoon once per week
A watering can fitted with a fine rose (perforated sprinkler head)

questions.correctAnswer: A watering can fitted with a fine rose (perforated sprinkler head)
questions.explanation: A fine-rose nozzle breaks the water stream into gentle fine droplets that moisten soil without washing away seeds or flattening stems.
questions.socraticHint: Which gardening can has a shower-like head with tiny holes for gentle sprinkling?

questions.prompt: What routine nursery management practice involves carefully removing excess overcrowded seedlings to give remaining plants adequate space and nutrients?
questions.explanation: Thinning removes crowded, weak seedlings so remaining seedlings develop sturdy stems and strong root systems.
questions.socraticHint: What do we call removing extra crowded seedlings so the remaining ones are not too tightly packed?

questions.prompt: Carefully transferring overcrowded seedlings from a nursery germination bed into individual pots or seedling trays is called _______ out.
questions.explanation: Pricking out transfers tiny seedlings into individual containers to develop robust independent root balls before field transplanting.
questions.socraticHint: The term begins with "p" and ends with "ing out".

questions.prompt: What is the vital practice of "hardening off" conducted on seedlings two weeks before transplanting?

options.text: Gradually removing the nursery shade and reducing watering frequency so seedlings adapt to harsh open-field conditions
Freezing seedlings in an ice block
Painting seedling stems with clear nail polish

questions.correctAnswer: Gradually removing the nursery shade and reducing watering frequency so seedlings adapt to harsh open-field conditions
questions.explanation: Hardening off acclimates seedlings to full sunlight, fluctuating temperatures, and wind, preventing fatal transplant shock.
questions.socraticHint: How does slowly getting baby seedlings used to full sun and less water make them tough for the open field?

questions.prompt: Transplanting seedlings at noon under scorching direct sun is the best time because hot sunlight stimulates instant root growth.
questions.explanation: Midday transplanting causes severe transpirational water loss and heat shock, leading to wilting and death of young seedlings.
questions.socraticHint: Does hot midday sun cause newly dug seedlings to wilt and dry up rapidly?

questions.prompt: What is the best time of day to transplant vegetable seedlings into the main farm field in Kenya?

options.text: At 2:00 in the afternoon during the hottest hour
Only during a violent thunder and lightning storm
Late in the afternoon (evening) or on a cool cloudy day
At 12:00 midday under bright scorching sunshine

questions.correctAnswer: Late in the afternoon (evening) or on a cool cloudy day
questions.explanation: Late afternoon transplanting allows seedlings the cool overnight hours to establish root contact with the soil before encountering morning sun.
questions.socraticHint: Why is the cool evening or a cloudy afternoon best for moving seedlings to the field?

questions.prompt: What essential step should a pupil take immediately before lifting seedlings from a nursery bed for transplanting?

options.text: Bake the nursery soil with fire until it turns to dust
Cut off all the roots with razor blades
Pull seedlings vigorously by their tender stems
Water the nursery bed thoroughly a few hours in advance so moist soil clings to the roots

questions.correctAnswer: Water the nursery bed thoroughly a few hours in advance so moist soil clings to the roots
questions.explanation: Pre-watering loosens the soil, prevents fine root hairs from tearing, and keeps a protective ball of soil around the root system.
questions.socraticHint: Why does moistening the nursery soil allow you to lift seedlings gently without ripping their roots?

questions.prompt: Which small garden hand tool is most appropriate for lifting seedlings gently from the nursery bed with their root ball intact?
questions.explanation: A curved garden trowel scoops underneath the root zone, lifting the seedling with its surrounding soil ball undisturbed.
questions.socraticHint: Which small handheld metal shovel is designed specifically for scooping soil around garden plants?

questions.prompt: The temporary wilting and slowing of growth experienced by young seedlings immediately following field transplanting is known as transplant _______.
questions.explanation: Transplant shock is physiological stress caused by root damage, change of soil environment, and temporary water uptake disruption.
questions.socraticHint: What word describes the sudden trauma or disturbance plants feel after being uprooted and moved?

questions.prompt: What protective management practices must be performed immediately after placing seedlings into their new field planting holes?

options.text: Do not apply any water for two weeks
Firm the soil gently around the stem, water generously, and apply dry grass mulch around the base
Leave the roots exposed to the air without any soil
Stomp heavily on the seedling with work boots until it is flattened

questions.correctAnswer: Firm the soil gently around the stem, water generously, and apply dry grass mulch around the base
questions.explanation: Firming eliminates air pockets, watering settles soil against roots, and mulch conserves moisture and cools the soil.
questions.socraticHint: What three caring steps ensure newly planted seedlings settle into their new homes without drying out?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What are small domestic animals in Kenyan agricultural farming?

options.text: Small tame animals reared for meat, eggs, fur, and manure such as rabbits, poultry, and guinea pigs
Wild lions and cheetahs living in national parks

questions.correctAnswer: Small tame animals reared for meat, eggs, fur, and manure such as rabbits, poultry, and guinea pigs
questions.explanation: Small domestic animals are domesticated species that can be reared in small spaces for food, income, and fertilizer.
questions.socraticHint: Which animals are gentle, small, and commonly raised on home compounds for food and fertilizer?

questions.prompt: What special name is given to the housing structure built specifically for rearing rabbits?
questions.explanation: A hutch is a specialized wooden and wire-mesh cage structure designed to house rabbits safely.
questions.socraticHint: A dog lives in a kennel, cows live in a kraal/shed: what is a rabbit house called?

questions.prompt: Why should a rabbit hutch be elevated at least 90 cm to 1 meter above ground level on sturdy wooden posts?

options.text: To allow rabbits to jump out and fly
To make the hutch invisible to people
To expose rabbits to strong direct rain
To protect rabbits from ground dampness, cold drafts, and crawling predators like rats, snakes, and dogs

questions.correctAnswer: To protect rabbits from ground dampness, cold drafts, and crawling predators like rats, snakes, and dogs
questions.explanation: Elevating the hutch keeps it dry, promotes air circulation beneath, allows droppings to fall away, and protects against predators.
questions.socraticHint: What dangers on the ground (damp mud, wandering dogs, snakes) are avoided by raising the hutch on stilts?

questions.prompt: Why is the floor of a rabbit hutch commonly constructed using welded wire mesh with 1-cm spacing or smooth wooden slats?

options.text: To allow urine and fecal pellets to drop through freely, keeping the bedding dry and clean
To trap rabbit feet so they cannot run
To allow cold wind to freeze the animals
To let food fall away so rabbits cannot eat

questions.correctAnswer: To allow urine and fecal pellets to drop through freely, keeping the bedding dry and clean
questions.explanation: Slotted or mesh floors are self-cleaning, preventing the accumulation of wet manure that harbors pathogens and parasites.
questions.socraticHint: Why is a slotted floor with gaps helpful for letting rabbit droppings fall through into a collection tray?

questions.prompt: An adult male rabbit is known as a buck, an adult female is called a doe, and a baby newborn rabbit is called a _______.
questions.explanation: Young newborn rabbits are called kits (or kittens).
questions.socraticHint: What three-letter word beginning with "k" is used for baby rabbits?

questions.prompt: A nesting box lined with clean dry grass should be placed inside the hutch when a doe is about to give birth (kindle).
questions.explanation: Does line nesting boxes with their own chest fur to keep naked, hairless newborn kits warm and protected.
questions.socraticHint: Do newborn kits need a sheltered warm box with dry bedding to survive their first days?

questions.prompt: Which essential housing feature must be incorporated into poultry houses to ensure healthy respiration and prevent ammonia build-up?

options.text: Removing the roof completely so rain pours inside
Adequate cross-ventilation openings covered with wire mesh on opposite walls
Sealing all windows and doors completely airtight with concrete
Painting all walls with pitch-black tar

questions.correctAnswer: Adequate cross-ventilation openings covered with wire mesh on opposite walls
questions.explanation: Cross-ventilation expels moist, toxic ammonia fumes from bird droppings and supplies fresh oxygen without creating chilly drafts.
questions.socraticHint: Why do chickens need fresh breeze flowing through opposite mesh windows?

questions.prompt: What predator-defense modification can be installed on the supporting wooden stilts of a chicken coop or rabbit hutch in rural Kenya?

options.text: Removing the poles so the hutch falls down
Attaching wooden ladders for wild animals to climb
Fitting inverted metal cones or grease bands around each wooden post to prevent rats and snakes from climbing up

questions.correctAnswer: Fitting inverted metal cones or grease bands around each wooden post to prevent rats and snakes from climbing up
questions.explanation: Slick metal cones and greased bands act as physical baffles, preventing rodents and snakes from scaling the support posts.
questions.socraticHint: How does a slippery metal funnel or grease ring around a post stop rats and snakes from climbing up?

questions.prompt: Raised horizontal wooden poles installed inside a chicken coop where hens sleep comfortably at night are called _______ roosts.
questions.explanation: Perches satisfy the natural avian instinct of chickens to roost above the ground away from predators at night.
questions.socraticHint: What horizontal wooden poles do chickens sit and sleep on at night?

questions.prompt: Rabbits and domestic poultry reared in clean, well-sheltered houses produce valuable organic manure that can be used directly to enrich school vegetable gardens.
questions.explanation: Poultry and rabbit droppings are exceptionally rich in nitrogen and phosphorus, making premium organic fertilizer.
questions.socraticHint: Is animal manure from chicken coops and rabbit hutches great for garden soil?

questions.prompt: Which domestic bird species is known for producing speckled brown eggs and alerting farmers with loud warning calls when predators approach?
questions.explanation: Guinea fowls are excellent farm alarm birds that roost high, consume garden insects, and lay rich speckled eggs.
questions.socraticHint: Which speckled domestic bird makes loud chatter when strange dogs or hawks approach the farm?

questions.prompt: Why should poultry nest boxes be placed in a quiet, dimly lit corner of the chicken house?

options.text: To provide hens with privacy and comfort, encouraging regular egg laying and discouraging egg eating
To make hens fall asleep permanently
To hide eggs from the farmer so they are never found
To prevent the hens from eating chicken feed

questions.correctAnswer: To provide hens with privacy and comfort, encouraging regular egg laying and discouraging egg eating
questions.explanation: Darkened, secluded nests reduce stress and prevent hens from pecking and breaking freshly laid eggs.
questions.socraticHint: Why do laying hens prefer quiet, shaded corners rather than bright, noisy spots to lay eggs?

questions.prompt: Why should fresh green leafy forages (like sweet potato vines or desmodium) be wilted in the shade for a few hours before feeding to rabbits?

options.text: To remove all vitamins from the forage
To reduce excessive moisture content that can cause severe, fatal digestive bloat and diarrhea in rabbits
To make the leaves turn completely into dry ash
To attract caterpillars to the leaves

questions.correctAnswer: To reduce excessive moisture content that can cause severe, fatal digestive bloat and diarrhea in rabbits
questions.explanation: Wet, succulent greens ferment rapidly in the rabbit’s delicate caecum, producing excess gas that causes life-threatening bloat.
questions.socraticHint: Why is it dangerous to feed soaking wet, freshly cut grass directly to young rabbits?

questions.prompt: What essential roughage feed must be provided to domestic rabbits daily to maintain healthy teeth wear and proper intestinal motility?

options.text: Soft wheat bread soaked in milk

questions.explanation: Rabbits are hindgut fermenters; fibrous dry hay wears down continuously growing teeth and keeps the digestive tract moving.
questions.socraticHint: Which dry fibrous grass feed provides the roughage rabbits need to chew every single day?

questions.prompt: What is the correct, humane technique for lifting and holding an adult domestic rabbit safely?

options.text: Lift the rabbit by its long ears with one hand
Dangle the rabbit upside down by its back legs
Pick the rabbit up by its tail
Gently grasp the loose skin over the shoulders (scruff) with one hand while firmly supporting the rabbit’s rump (hindquarters) with the other hand

questions.correctAnswer: Gently grasp the loose skin over the shoulders (scruff) with one hand while firmly supporting the rabbit’s rump (hindquarters) with the other hand
questions.explanation: Supporting the heavy hindquarters prevents the rabbit from kicking violently and breaking its fragile lumbar spine.
questions.socraticHint: Always support the rabbit's bottom with one hand: never lift a rabbit by its ears or legs alone.

questions.prompt: Lifting a rabbit by its ears is acceptable and harmless because rabbit ears are designed by nature to carry the rabbit’s body weight.
questions.explanation: Lifting by the ears causes severe cartilage tears, extreme pain, and tissue damage, and constitutes animal cruelty.
questions.socraticHint: Is picking up an animal by its delicate ears painful and cruel?

questions.prompt: Why should poultry and rabbits have continuous access to fresh, clean drinking water at all times?

options.text: Water aids digestion, regulates body temperature, transports nutrients, and prevents dehydration
Water stops animals from ever getting hungry
Water makes eggs hatch in two minutes

questions.correctAnswer: Water aids digestion, regulates body temperature, transports nutrients, and prevents dehydration
questions.explanation: Water constitutes over 70% of animal body mass; water deprivation rapidly stops egg laying, impairs digestion, and causes death.
questions.socraticHint: Why is clean drinking water vital every day for all living animals?

questions.prompt: Why should water containers in rabbit hutches and chicken coops be heavy earthen pots or securely clamped to the cage wall?

options.text: To warm the water to boiling point
To prevent the active animals from accidentally tipping or knocking over the water container and soaking the floor
To prevent water from evaporating into the air

questions.correctAnswer: To prevent the active animals from accidentally tipping or knocking over the water container and soaking the floor
questions.explanation: Unstable lightweight tins are easily spilled, leaving animals thirsty and wetting the floor, creating disease risks.
questions.socraticHint: Why do heavy clay dishes stop playful rabbits or scratchy chickens from spilling water everywhere?

questions.prompt: Small insoluble stones or coarse sand particles swallowed by chickens that help grind hard grains inside the muscular gizzard are called _______.
questions.explanation: Chickens lack teeth; insoluble grit in the gizzard functions as biological millstones to crush hard seeds and grains.
questions.socraticHint: What are the tiny stones chickens pick from the ground to grind food in their gizzard called?

questions.prompt: Which of the following greens is a safe, highly nutritious fodder crop commonly fed to domestic rabbits in Kenya?
questions.explanation: Desmodium and sweet potato vines are palatable, high-protein legumes; nightshade family leaves (tomato/potato) contain toxic solanine.
questions.socraticHint: Sweet potato vines and desmodium are rich in protein and completely non-toxic for rabbits.

questions.prompt: Domestic animals have the right to the Five Freedoms of animal welfare, which includes freedom from hunger, thirst, pain, injury, and fear.
questions.explanation: The internationally recognized Five Freedoms guide compassionate, ethical animal husbandry worldwide.
questions.socraticHint: Do animals deserve humane care, good nutrition, clean shelter, and kind treatment?

questions.prompt: Why should a wooden block of untreated softwood be placed inside a rabbit hutch?

options.text: For the rabbit to sleep on
To keep the hutch smelling like fresh paint
To serve as a plate for rabbit pellets
To provide safe gnawing material that helps wear down the rabbit’s continuously growing incisor teeth naturally

questions.correctAnswer: To provide safe gnawing material that helps wear down the rabbit’s continuously growing incisor teeth naturally
questions.explanation: Rabbit incisors grow continuously; gnawing on clean wood prevents malocclusion (overgrown teeth that prevent feeding).
questions.socraticHint: Rabbit teeth grow non-stop: what does chewing on a piece of clean wood do to their teeth?

questions.prompt: What is the consequence of overcrowding too many birds inside a small chicken coop?

options.text: It triggers stress, feather pecking, cannibalism, rapid disease spread, and decreased egg production
It makes birds lay twice as many eggs
It stops all birds from producing manure

questions.correctAnswer: It triggers stress, feather pecking, cannibalism, rapid disease spread, and decreased egg production
questions.explanation: Overcrowding creates social stress and competition, triggering aggression like feather pecking and facilitating air-borne infections.
questions.socraticHint: What happens when too many chickens are crammed into a tiny space without room to move?

questions.prompt: Which humane action demonstrates good CBC citizenship and compassion when caring for poultry on a school farm?

options.text: Tying chicken legs tightly with wire
Providing daily clean water, inspecting for injuries, speaking calmly, and handling birds gently without chasing them frantically
Throwing heavy stones at chickens to herd them into the coop
Leaving birds without water over long holiday weekends

questions.correctAnswer: Providing daily clean water, inspecting for injuries, speaking calmly, and handling birds gently without chasing them frantically
questions.explanation: Compassionate handling builds trust, reduces stress, and reflects core ethical values in agricultural citizenship.
questions.socraticHint: Which gentle, responsible care shows compassion and good animal handling?

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a clear sign of good physical health in domestic poultry?

options.text: Bright alert eyes, red moist comb and wattles, smooth glossy feathers, and active feeding
Dull sunken eyes and drooping wings
Standing motionless in dark corners with ruffled feathers

questions.correctAnswer: Bright alert eyes, red moist comb and wattles, smooth glossy feathers, and active feeding
questions.explanation: A healthy bird is energetic, active, responsive to food, with smooth preened plumage and vibrant red head appendages.
questions.socraticHint: Look at a vigorous, healthy hen: are its eyes bright and comb a vibrant red?

questions.prompt: A learner in Eldoret observes a rabbit sitting hunched in a corner, refusing green feed, with dull eyes and teeth grinding. What does this indicate?

options.text: The rabbit has turned into a wild hare
The rabbit is simply practicing sleeping standing up
The rabbit is sick and in severe pain or distress, requiring immediate veterinary attention
The rabbit is extremely happy and singing a song

questions.correctAnswer: The rabbit is sick and in severe pain or distress, requiring immediate veterinary attention
questions.explanation: Hunching, anorexia, and loud tooth grinding (bruxism) are classical signs of severe abdominal pain or illness in rabbits.
questions.socraticHint: When an animal refuses food and grinds its teeth in a corner, is it sick and suffering from pain?

questions.prompt: What visible symptom in a flock of chickens strongly suggests a respiratory illness such as infectious coryza or Newcastle disease?

options.text: Sneezing, nasal discharge, swollen face, and rattling wheezing breath sounds

questions.correctAnswer: Sneezing, nasal discharge, swollen face, and rattling wheezing breath sounds
questions.explanation: Respiratory pathogens inflame airways, producing mucus discharges from nostrils, facial swelling, and noisy tracheal rales.
questions.socraticHint: What sounds and nasal discharges occur when chickens catch a respiratory infection in their airways?

questions.prompt: What is the immediate first action a farmer must take upon identifying a sick chicken or rabbit in a herd?

options.text: Isolate the sick animal immediately into a separate isolation pen away from the healthy stock
Leave the sick animal to share feeding and drinking troughs with healthy birds
Throw the animal into the neighbor’s compound
Ignore it and hope it cures itself

questions.correctAnswer: Isolate the sick animal immediately into a separate isolation pen away from the healthy stock
questions.explanation: Isolation (quarantine) breaks the transmission cycle, preventing contagious germs from spreading to the rest of the flock.
questions.socraticHint: Why should you separate a sick animal into its own cage immediately to protect other healthy animals?

questions.prompt: An animal that lives on or inside another animal (the host) and causes it harm by sucking blood or stealing nutrients is called a _______.
questions.explanation: A parasite derives nutrition from a host organism at the host’s expense, causing irritation, anemia, or disease.
questions.socraticHint: Fleas, lice, and tapeworms are all examples of which type of harmful organism?

questions.prompt: External parasites live on the skin, fur, and feathers of animals, while internal parasites live inside organs like the intestines.
questions.explanation: Ectoparasites (fleas, mites, lice) inhabit the body surface; endoparasites (worms, coccidia) reside within internal viscera.
questions.socraticHint: External means outside (skin/fur) and internal means inside (guts/organs).

questions.prompt: Which external parasite burrows under the skin of chicken unfeathered legs, causing raised, rough, thick, chalky crusts (scaly leg disease)?
questions.explanation: Knemidocoptes mutans mites burrow under leg scales, generating proliferative crusty lesions and lameness.
questions.socraticHint: What microscopic mites burrow under the scales on chicken shanks causing rough crusts?

questions.prompt: What condition occurs in rabbits when microscopic ear mites multiply inside the ear canals, causing intense head shaking and thick brown crusty scabs?
questions.explanation: Psoroptes cuniculi mites infest the outer ear canal, causing ear canker characterized by brownish exudate and intense pruritus.
questions.socraticHint: What ear disease in rabbits causes crusty scabs inside the ears and constant head shaking?

questions.prompt: Which tiny dark external parasites cluster in large stationary colonies around the unfeathered eyes, comb, and wattles of poultry, sucking blood?
questions.explanation: Sticktight fleas (Echidnophaga gallinacea) anchor their mouthparts into bare head skin, causing blood loss and blindness in chicks.
questions.socraticHint: Which fleas stick tightly in clusters to the combs and wattles of chickens?

questions.prompt: Internal parasites like roundworms and tapeworms rob infected poultry of digested nutrients, leading to poor growth, emaciation, and reduced egg lay.
questions.explanation: Intestinal helminths compete for nutrients in the lumen and damage the gut lining, causing wasting and nutrient deficiencies.
questions.socraticHint: Do worms in the intestines steal food and nutrients from the host chicken?

questions.prompt: What physical appearance of animal feces indicates healthy digestive functioning in a domestic rabbit?

options.text: Firm, round, uniform, dry brown pellets
White chalky soup with foul odor

questions.correctAnswer: Firm, round, uniform, dry brown pellets
questions.explanation: Healthy rabbits produce dry, uniform fecal spheres; soft or liquid stool indicates digestive imbalance or coccidiosis.
questions.socraticHint: Healthy rabbit droppings look like small, dry, round brown beads or pellets.

questions.prompt: What deadly viral disease of poultry in Kenya causes sudden high mortality, twisted necks (torticollis), greenish diarrhea, and gasping for breath?
questions.explanation: Newcastle disease is a highly contagious paramyxovirus infection causing catastrophic neurological and respiratory signs in unvaccinated poultry.
questions.socraticHint: Which widespread viral chicken disease causes twisted necks and is prevented by routine eye-drop vaccines?

questions.prompt: What is biosecurity in livestock production on a Kenyan farm?

options.text: Fencing farms with barbed wire to keep rain away
A set of hygienic practices and physical measures designed to prevent diseases and parasites from entering or spreading on a farm
Buying security guards with walkie-talkies to patrol rabbit hutches

questions.correctAnswer: A set of hygienic practices and physical measures designed to prevent diseases and parasites from entering or spreading on a farm
questions.explanation: Biosecurity encompasses all proactive procedures that shield animals from infectious agents and prevent disease transmission.
questions.socraticHint: What measures protect farm animals from being exposed to germs and infectious disease?

questions.prompt: Why is a footbath containing disinfectant solution placed at the entrance of a poultry house on a school farm?

options.text: To give chickens a place to drink water
To catch stray mice entering the building
To disinfect the footwear of workers and visitors, preventing them from tracking disease germs into the house
To wash mud off the floor so it stays shiny

questions.correctAnswer: To disinfect the footwear of workers and visitors, preventing them from tracking disease germs into the house
questions.explanation: Footwear carries contaminated soil and feces; stepping into disinfectant decontaminates boots before entry.
questions.socraticHint: Why do you dip boots into a shallow basin with medicine before stepping inside a chicken coop?

questions.prompt: How can a farmer safely treat and control external lice and sticktight fleas on domestic chickens?

options.text: Dipping the chickens into boiling water
Spraying petrol directly into the chickens’ eyes
Plucking out all the feathers with tweezers
Dusting the birds gently with approved insecticidal powder (such as pyrethrum powder) around the vent, under wings, and neck

questions.correctAnswer: Dusting the birds gently with approved insecticidal powder (such as pyrethrum powder) around the vent, under wings, and neck
questions.explanation: Approved dusting powders kill external ectoparasites safely without poisoning the host bird when applied properly.
questions.socraticHint: Which gentle powder made from pyrethrum flowers is dusted under wings to kill fleas and lice?

questions.prompt: What simple traditional remedy is used to treat scaly leg mites on chickens by suffocating the burrowing mites beneath the leg scales?

options.text: Coating the affected shanks with liquid paraffin, petroleum jelly, or vegetable oil
Painting the legs with red school ink
Wrapping the legs with dry sandpaper
Washing the legs with salty ocean water

questions.correctAnswer: Coating the affected shanks with liquid paraffin, petroleum jelly, or vegetable oil
questions.explanation: Applying mineral oil or petroleum jelly suffocates the microscopic mites trapped beneath leg scales without harming the bird.
questions.socraticHint: Which thick oily substance smothers and suffocates tiny mites living under the scales of chicken legs?

questions.prompt: Administering veterinary oral medications periodically to destroy internal intestinal worms in livestock is known as _______.
questions.explanation: Deworming (anthelmintic administration) eliminates internal worms to restore growth rates and gut health.
questions.socraticHint: What term describes removing or killing worms inside an animal?

questions.prompt: Emptying, washing, and sanitizing feeding and drinking troughs regularly prevents the accumulation of mold and microbial contamination.
questions.explanation: Dirty feeders and drinkers foster bacterial biofilms and toxic molds that cause enteritis in small domestic stock.
questions.socraticHint: Does washing feed and water dishes keep animals healthy and free from stomach bugs?

questions.prompt: What is the correct, hygienic procedure for disposing of an animal that has died from an infectious disease on a Kenyan farm?

options.text: Selling the diseased carcass to a local meat butchery
Burying the carcass deeply (at least 1.5 to 2 meters) in the ground, sprinkling lime powder over it, and covering it firmly with soil
Throwing the dead carcass into a nearby community river
Leaving the carcass exposed in the open field for stray dogs and vultures to eat

questions.correctAnswer: Burying the carcass deeply (at least 1.5 to 2 meters) in the ground, sprinkling lime powder over it, and covering it firmly with soil
questions.explanation: Deep burial with lime prevents scavengers from exhuming the carcass and stops pathogens from contaminating air and groundwater.
questions.socraticHint: Why must dead carcasses be buried deep in the ground so dogs cannot dig them up and spread disease?

questions.prompt: Why should wild birds (like pigeons and sparrows) and rodents be prevented from entering chicken houses and rabbit hutches?

options.text: They turn chicken coops into concrete
They make rabbit fur grow green
They carry infectious poultry diseases (such as fowl cholera and salmonella) and consume costly animal feeds
They make chickens lay too many eggs

questions.correctAnswer: They carry infectious poultry diseases (such as fowl cholera and salmonella) and consume costly animal feeds
questions.explanation: Wild birds and rodents are biological disease vectors that contaminate feed and water with infectious feces.
questions.socraticHint: Wild birds carry wild germs and eat animal food: why is keeping them out a key biosecurity rule?

questions.prompt: How long should newly purchased rabbits or chickens be kept in a separate quarantine pen before introducing them to the main farm flock?

options.text: At least 2 to 3 weeks (14 to 21 days)

questions.correctAnswer: At least 2 to 3 weeks (14 to 21 days)
questions.explanation: A 2–3 week quarantine window allows latent disease incubation periods to manifest before healthy home stock is exposed.
questions.socraticHint: Why is keeping new animals apart for two to three weeks safe for spotting any hidden sickness?

questions.prompt: Whitewashing (painting with slaked lime) the inner wooden walls of rabbit hutches and poultry coops helps kill hidden mites and brightens the interior.
questions.explanation: Slaked lime creates an alkaline, hostile environment that seals cracks, kills mites and lice, and sanitizes surfaces.
questions.socraticHint: Does white lime wash act as a natural disinfectant that destroys parasites in wood cracks?

questions.prompt: Administering biological vaccines to young chicks (such as against Gumboro and Newcastle disease) confers active immune _______.
questions.explanation: Vaccines stimulate antibody production, preparing the immune system to defend against future viral attacks.
questions.socraticHint: What shield or defense does a vaccine give to chicks against dangerous diseases?

questions.prompt: What important personal hygiene practice must pupils always observe immediately after handling rabbits, cleaning coops, or gathering eggs?

options.text: Washing hands thoroughly with clean running water and soap
Wiping hands on their clothes and eating food immediately
Rubbing their eyes with unwashed hands
Putting dirty fingers in their mouth

questions.correctAnswer: Washing hands thoroughly with clean running water and soap
questions.explanation: Handwashing prevents zoonotic transmission of bacteria like Salmonella and parasites from livestock to humans.
questions.socraticHint: What basic health habit should you always do with soap and water after touching animals or cleaning cages?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
