questions.text: What is the vital golden rule of water rescue for a primary school student who spots someone struggling in deep water?

options.text: Walk away quietly and tell nobody about what happened
"Reach or Throw, Don’t Go!" (Use a pole, towel, or throw a float from the safety of the bank; do NOT jump in)
Jump in immediately with all your clothes and shoes on
Throw heavy concrete rocks at the struggling swimmer

questions.correctAnswer: "Reach or Throw, Don’t Go!" (Use a pole, towel, or throw a float from the safety of the bank; do NOT jump in)
questions.explanation: Untrained children must never enter deep water because a panicking victim will grasp and submerge the rescuer. Always reach, throw, and call adults.
questions.socraticHint: Why should you extend a pole or throw a float from dry land instead of jumping into deep water yourself?
questions.prompt: What is the vital golden rule of water rescue for a primary school student who spots someone struggling in deep water?

questions.text: Why is running strictly forbidden on tiled decks surrounding swimming pools?

options.text: The pool water will turn into solid ice
Running makes the depth of the pool change instantly
Wet pool tiles are extremely slippery, creating severe hazards for falls, fractures, and head concussions
Running makes the chlorine evaporate from the pool water

questions.correctAnswer: Wet pool tiles are extremely slippery, creating severe hazards for falls, fractures, and head concussions
questions.explanation: Wet tiles have near-zero friction; slipping can lead to dangerous skull and bone injuries.
questions.socraticHint: What happens when shoes or bare wet feet sprint across slippery wet tile surfaces?
questions.prompt: Why is running strictly forbidden on tiled decks surrounding swimming pools?

questions.text: What does the acronym "R.I.C.E." stand for in First Aid treatment of sprains and muscle strains?
questions.explanation: R.I.C.E. is the universal sports First Aid protocol: Rest the joint, Ice to reduce inflammation, Compress with bandage, and Elevate above heart level.
questions.socraticHint: What do the letters R - I - C - E stand for when treating an athlete’s sprained ankle?
questions.prompt: What does the acronym "R.I.C.E." stand for in First Aid treatment of sprains and muscle strains?

questions.text: When applying ice to a sprained ankle, why must the ice or frozen pack be wrapped in a thin towel rather than placed directly onto bare skin?

options.text: Direct ice contact on bare skin can cause ice burns (frostbite) and tissue damage
The ice will instantly melt and flood the entire room
The towel makes the ice turn into boiling water
Direct ice turns the skin into solid metal

questions.correctAnswer: Direct ice contact on bare skin can cause ice burns (frostbite) and tissue damage
questions.explanation: A protective cloth barrier protects skin cells from cryogenic cold burns while allowing cooling to reach deep tissues.
questions.socraticHint: Why does placing raw ice directly against bare skin cause cold burns?
questions.prompt: When applying ice to a sprained ankle, why must the ice or frozen pack be wrapped in a thin towel rather than placed directly onto bare skin?

questions.text: How should you administer First Aid to a learner who develops a nosebleed after an active game?

options.text: Stuff dirty dry grass deep into both nostrils
Have the learner sit upright, lean slightly forward, pinch the soft lower part of the nostrils firmly for 10 minutes, and breathe through the mouth
Tilt the head backwards and pour hot tea down the nose
Tell the learner to run around the field shouting

questions.correctAnswer: Have the learner sit upright, lean slightly forward, pinch the soft lower part of the nostrils firmly for 10 minutes, and breathe through the mouth
questions.explanation: Leaning forward prevents blood flowing down the throat, and pinching compresses bleeding vessels until a clot forms.
questions.socraticHint: Should a person with a nosebleed lean forward and pinch their nose, or tilt their head back?
questions.prompt: How should you administer First Aid to a learner who develops a nosebleed after an active game?

questions.text: What immediate action should be taken when an athlete suffers a painful sudden muscle cramp in the calf during a match?

options.text: Force the athlete to sprint another 5 kilometers immediately
Pour boiling water directly onto the leg
Gently stretch and massage the calf muscle, pull the toes upward toward the shin, and provide sips of water with electrolytes
Hit the cramped calf with a heavy wooden bat

questions.correctAnswer: Gently stretch and massage the calf muscle, pull the toes upward toward the shin, and provide sips of water with electrolytes
questions.explanation: Gentle passive stretching and hydration relax contracted muscle fibers and relieve spasms.
questions.socraticHint: How does gentle stretching and rehydration relieve a tight, contracted calf cramp?
questions.prompt: What immediate action should be taken when an athlete suffers a painful sudden muscle cramp in the calf during a match?

Leaving your shoes with a friend while swimming alone at midnight
Taking photographs of yourself with a floating camera
Pairing each swimmer with a partner so that both watch out for each other and immediately report if one is in distress

questions.correctAnswer: Pairing each swimmer with a partner so that both watch out for each other and immediately report if one is in distress
questions.explanation: The buddy system ensures continuous mutual monitoring so no swimmer disappears unnoticed.

questions.prompt: What is the "buddy system" in swimming and water recreation?

Sugary carbonated sodas and fried oily crisps
Artificial chemical candy and chewing gum
Refined white sugar cubes dissolved in cooking oil

questions.correctAnswer: Boiled sweet potatoes, arrowroots (nduma), beans, and ugali with greens (sukuma wiki)
questions.explanation: Whole indigenous foods provide sustained complex energy, vitamins, and minerals that nourish active developing bodies.
questions.socraticHint: Which nutritious local foods like nduma, sweet potatoes, and ugali fuel athletes with clean long-lasting energy?

Compression - Wrap the joint snugly with an elastic crepe bandage to limit fluid buildup
Elevation - Prop the injured limb up on pillows above heart level to assist drainage

questions.explanation: Rest stops damage; Ice reduces swelling; Compression limits fluid; Elevation drains fluid via gravity.

options.text: Pour hot boiling soup on the swollen ankle
Help the student sit down safely, apply the R.I.C.E. protocol with an ice pack and bandage, and inform the teacher immediately
Force the student to stand up and run three more laps on the twisted ankle
Twist the ankle vigorously in circles to hear if the bone snaps

questions.correctAnswer: Help the student sit down safely, apply the R.I.C.E. protocol with an ice pack and bandage, and inform the teacher immediately
questions.explanation: Immediate rest, cold therapy, compression, and adult notification prevent further ligament damage.
questions.socraticHint: How does providing immediate rest, ice, and alerting a teacher protect an injured classmate?

questions.prompt: According to Genesis 1:26-27, in whose image and likeness were human beings created by God?
questions.text: According to Genesis 1:26-27, in whose image and likeness were human beings created by God?

options.text: In the likeness of celestial stars and planets
In the image and likeness of God
In the likeness of powerful sea creatures
In the image of towering cedar trees

questions.correctAnswer: In the image and likeness of God
questions.explanation: The biblical creation account in Genesis 1:26-27 explicitly states that God made humanity in His own image and likeness, bestowing upon human beings unique spiritual dignity, reason, and moral responsibility.
questions.socraticHint: Which divine being said, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness"?

questions.prompt: What special responsibility did God give to human beings in the Garden of Eden according to Genesis 2:15?
questions.text: What special responsibility did God give to human beings in the Garden of Eden according to Genesis 2:15?

options.text: To abandon the garden and live in desert caves
To burn down the trees to build stone towers
To cultivate and keep (tend and protect) the garden
To exhaust all natural resources as quickly as possible

questions.correctAnswer: To cultivate and keep (tend and protect) the garden
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:15 records that the Lord God placed humanity in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it, establishing the foundational principle of environmental stewardship.
questions.socraticHint: Did God command humans to destroy the garden or to nurture and protect it carefully?

questions.prompt: What does the term "Christian stewardship" mean regarding our relationship with the natural environment?
questions.text: What does the term "Christian stewardship" mean regarding our relationship with the natural environment?

options.text: Claiming total ownership of the earth to exploit it for money
Ignoring pollution because nature cleans itself automatically
Prioritizing factory profits over clean air and clean drinking water
Being responsible, caring managers of God’s creation

questions.correctAnswer: Being responsible, caring managers of God’s creation
questions.explanation: A steward is a trusted manager who looks after another person’s property. Christian stewardship acknowledges that the earth belongs to God (Psalm 24:1) and humans are entrusted to manage it responsibly.
questions.socraticHint: When someone manages property on behalf of the real owner, what kind of care and accountability do they owe?

questions.prompt: How does being created in the "image of God" influence how Grade 5 learners should treat other people?
questions.text: How does being created in the "image of God" influence how Grade 5 learners should treat other people?

options.text: By treating every person with respect, love, and equal dignity
By looking down on children from poorer backgrounds
By only showing kindness to people from one’s own ethnic group
By mocking classmates who have physical or learning disabilities

questions.correctAnswer: By treating every person with respect, love, and equal dignity
questions.explanation: Because every human person is created in God’s image, all human life possesses sacred dignity. Christians are called to love, respect, and value every individual regardless of wealth, background, or physical ability.
questions.socraticHint: If every human being reflects God’s divine image, how should we value their worth and treat them in school?

questions.prompt: In Genesis 1, what repetitive phrase did God declare after observing each stage of His creation?
questions.text: In Genesis 1, what repetitive phrase did God declare after observing each stage of His creation?

options.text: God saw that nature was completely worthless
God saw that it was good
God saw that it was incomplete and faulty
God noticed that humans would soon ruin it

questions.correctAnswer: God saw that it was good
questions.explanation: Throughout the six days of creation in Genesis 1, God evaluated His work and saw that it was "good," and upon creating humanity on the sixth day, He saw that it was "very good" (Genesis 1:31).
questions.socraticHint: What positive word does Genesis 1 repeat when God examines the light, seas, plants, and animals?

questions.prompt: Which of the following actions at school best demonstrates the Christian principle of stewardship over physical resources?
questions.text: Which of the following actions at school best demonstrates the Christian principle of stewardship over physical resources?

options.text: Throwing plastic juice bottles across the playing field after break time
Leaving school lights on in empty classrooms throughout the weekend
Turning off running water taps and caring for textbooks so others can use them
Writing graffiti on newly painted classroom walls and school desks

questions.correctAnswer: Turning off running water taps and caring for textbooks so others can use them
questions.explanation: Stewardship involves preserving and managing resources responsibly. Conserving water and taking good care of shared school learning materials demonstrates respect for God-given resources and community welfare.
questions.socraticHint: Which option shows careful preservation and thoughtful conservation of school facilities and resources?

questions.prompt: What fundamental truth about God’s ownership of the earth is taught in Psalm 24:1?
questions.text: What fundamental truth about God’s ownership of the earth is taught in Psalm 24:1?

options.text: The earth belongs completely to whoever buys title deeds at the market
The earth belongs only to wild animals and has no spiritual purpose
The earth is an accidental creation without any supreme ruler
The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it, the world and all who live in it

questions.correctAnswer: The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it, the world and all who live in it
questions.explanation: Psalm 24:1 states: "The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it." This reminds believers that God is the true sovereign owner of all creation.
questions.socraticHint: According to King David in Psalm 24, whose possession is the entire planet and its inhabitants?

questions.prompt: A farmer in Murang’a decides to cut down all riverbank trees and cultivate up to the water’s edge. How does this conflict with Christian stewardship?
questions.text: A farmer in Murang’a decides to cut down all riverbank trees and cultivate up to the water’s edge. How does this conflict with Christian stewardship?

options.text: It causes riverbank soil erosion and pollutes drinking water downstream for other families
It shows extreme wisdom because trees consume too much river water
It obeys Genesis commands by eliminating useless indigenous wild plants
It guarantees that fish in the river will grow twice as fast without shade

questions.correctAnswer: It causes riverbank soil erosion and pollutes drinking water downstream for other families
questions.explanation: Christian stewardship requires protecting riparian land to prevent soil erosion and keep downstream water clean. Destroying riparian vegetation harms the ecosystem and deprives neighbors of clean water.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to the soil and downstream communities when protective vegetation along riverbanks is removed?

questions.prompt: How did God provide for the nourishment of human beings and land animals in Genesis 1:29-30?
questions.text: How did God provide for the nourishment of human beings and land animals in Genesis 1:29-30?

options.text: By withholding all plants until humans learned to irrigate fields
By providing every seed-bearing plant and fruit-bearing tree as food
By instructing them to manufacture chemical food pills in factories
By allowing humans to consume soil and rocks from river beds

questions.correctAnswer: By providing every seed-bearing plant and fruit-bearing tree as food
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:29-30 states that God gave every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree with fruit with seed in it for food, showing God’s loving provision for living creatures.
questions.socraticHint: What natural living provision did God establish on earth for food during the creation week?

questions.prompt: Why did God rest on the seventh day after finishing creation in Genesis 2:1-3?
questions.text: Why did God rest on the seventh day after finishing creation in Genesis 2:1-3?

options.text: Because God was discouraged by how the animals were behaving
To show that work is an evil activity that should be avoided forever
To bless and sanctify the seventh day as a day of rest and worship (Sabbath)
Because God ran out of energy and could not create anything more

questions.correctAnswer: To bless and sanctify the seventh day as a day of rest and worship (Sabbath)
questions.explanation: God did not rest because of exhaustion; God is almighty and never grows weary (Isaiah 40:28). He rested to set a divine pattern of rest, blessing the seventh day and making it holy for worship and renewal.
questions.socraticHint: Did God run out of power, or did He set a holy rhythm of rest and dedication for humanity to follow?

questions.prompt: When pupils notice that tap water at school is running continuously into the mud, what is their Christian moral duty?
questions.text: When pupils notice that tap water at school is running continuously into the mud, what is their Christian moral duty?

options.text: Walk past quickly pretending not to see it because it is not their home tap
Splash the wasting water on fellow classmates to make mud games
Open the tap fully so the water runs out faster and stops making noise
Immediately close the tap tightly and report any leak to the school caretaker

questions.correctAnswer: Immediately close the tap tightly and report any leak to the school caretaker
questions.explanation: Water is a precious, life-giving gift from God. Preventing wastage through prompt action shows practical Christian stewardship and love for the community.
questions.socraticHint: What immediate responsible action stops the loss of precious drinking water?

questions.prompt: Which statement best contrasts human beings with all other earthly creatures in God’s creation design?
questions.text: Which statement best contrasts human beings with all other earthly creatures in God’s creation design?

options.text: Humans possess a moral conscience, free will, and spiritual fellowship with God
Humans are physically stronger and faster than all wild animals on earth
Humans do not require water, air, or sunlight to survive on the planet
Humans were created without any responsibility to care for living organisms

questions.correctAnswer: Humans possess a moral conscience, free will, and spiritual fellowship with God
questions.explanation: Human beings are uniquely made in God’s image, giving them a spiritual soul, moral conscience, ability to reason, and the capacity to worship and enter into a personal relationship with God.
questions.socraticHint: What spiritual and moral qualities make humans accountable to God in a way animals are not?

questions.prompt: Which of the following is one of Kenya’s five major "water towers" that Christians are called to conserve?
questions.text: Which of the following is one of Kenya’s five major "water towers" that Christians are called to conserve?
questions.explanation: Kenya’s five major water towers are the Mau Forest Complex, Mount Kenya, the Aberdare Range, Mount Elgon, and the Cherangani Hills. They supply vital water catchments across the nation.
questions.socraticHint: Which vast highland indigenous forest in the Rift Valley serves as a primary catchment area for several Kenyan rivers?

questions.prompt: According to Proverbs 12:10, how does a righteous person treat their domestic animals?
questions.text: According to Proverbs 12:10, how does a righteous person treat their domestic animals?

options.text: A righteous person abandons sick cattle in the road to fend for themselves
A righteous person starves poultry to maximize egg production profits
A righteous person cares for the needs and well-being of their animals
A righteous person overburdens their donkey without water until it collapses

questions.correctAnswer: A righteous person cares for the needs and well-being of their animals
questions.explanation: Proverbs 12:10 says: "The righteous care for the needs of their animals, but the kindest acts of the wicked are cruel." God expects believers to be compassionate caretakers of domestic animals.
questions.socraticHint: Does God’s Word praise compassion or cruelty when caring for donkeys, cows, and pets?

questions.prompt: A Christian youth fellowship in Nakuru organizes a tree-planting day. Why is planting indigenous trees considered an act of faith and love?
questions.text: A Christian youth fellowship in Nakuru organizes a tree-planting day. Why is planting indigenous trees considered an act of faith and love?

options.text: It allows church members to show off their new gardening boots on social media
It makes sure that wild animals will have fewer places to hide and be captured
It generates immediate cash prizes from international commercial timber companies
It restores God’s creation, purifies air, and ensures rainfall and water for future generations

questions.correctAnswer: It restores God’s creation, purifies air, and ensures rainfall and water for future generations
questions.explanation: Planting trees restores damaged habitats, prevents desertification, attracts rainfall, and purifies the air. It is a selfless act of love for our neighbors and future generations, honoring God’s creation.
questions.socraticHint: How does reforesting degraded ground demonstrate selfless service to God’s environment and fellow citizens?

questions.prompt: How can Grade 5 learners in Kisumu actively practice environmental stewardship around Lake Victoria?
questions.text: How can Grade 5 learners in Kisumu actively practice environmental stewardship around Lake Victoria?

options.text: Participating in beach clean-ups to remove plastic waste and avoid dumping trash into the lake
Throwing broken glass and plastic polythene bags into the lake waters during boat rides
Catching juvenile fingerling fish in prohibited breeding bays for personal fun
Washing fuel trucks directly along the lake shoreline to save domestic tap water

questions.correctAnswer: Participating in beach clean-ups to remove plastic waste and avoid dumping trash into the lake
questions.explanation: Keeping lake shorelines clean from plastics protects aquatic life like tilapia and Nile perch from ingesting microplastics and preserves freshwater quality for the community.
questions.socraticHint: Which activity protects lake water purity and fish breeding habitats from pollution?

questions.prompt: What negative spiritual attitude is demonstrated when a person engages in illegal poaching or destructive logging in Kenyan forests?
questions.text: What negative spiritual attitude is demonstrated when a person engages in illegal poaching or destructive logging in Kenyan forests?

options.text: Courageous leadership in developing rural industrial infrastructure
Greed and selfish disregard for God’s created order and community welfare
Sacrificial humility and deep dedication to church principles
Obedience to biblical principles of sharing communal property

questions.correctAnswer: Greed and selfish disregard for God’s created order and community welfare
questions.explanation: Illegal logging and poaching stem from greed, putting personal enrichment above respect for God’s handiwork, Kenyan wildlife laws, and the well-being of future generations.
questions.socraticHint: Does destroying protected forests for quick illegal gain stem from godly humility or selfish greed?

questions.prompt: Which biblical passage reminds believers that all creatures wait upon God for their food and preservation?
questions.text: Which biblical passage reminds believers that all creatures wait upon God for their food and preservation?
questions.explanation: Psalm 104:27-28 declares of all living creatures: "All creatures look to you to give them their food at the proper time. When you give it to them, they gather it up; when you open your hand, they are satisfied with good things."
questions.socraticHint: Which beautiful psalm celebrating creation describes animals depending on God’s open hand for food?

questions.prompt: When Peter sees a neighbor beating an injured donkey overloaded with heavy sacks of maize, what is the most Christ-like response?
questions.text: When Peter sees a neighbor beating an injured donkey overloaded with heavy sacks of maize, what is the most Christ-like response?

options.text: Join the neighbor in beating the animal so it walks faster to the market
Laugh loudly at the donkey and take entertaining videos for classmates
Throw sharp stones at both the donkey and the neighbor to chase them away
Calmly speak to the neighbor, offer to help lighten the load, and provide water for the donkey

questions.correctAnswer: Calmly speak to the neighbor, offer to help lighten the load, and provide water for the donkey
questions.explanation: Christians are called to be peacemakers and advocates of mercy. Helping reduce an overburdened animal’s suffering reflects Proverbs 12:10 and God’s compassion toward all living creatures.
questions.socraticHint: How does offering practical help and showing mercy to an exhausted working animal reflect Christ’s heart?

questions.prompt: Why should Kenyan Christians avoid burning dry plastic waste in open fires at home or school?
questions.text: Why should Kenyan Christians avoid burning dry plastic waste in open fires at home or school?

options.text: Burning plastics releases toxic smoke that damages respiratory health and pollutes God’s atmosphere
Plastic smoke attracts harmful locust swarms from neighboring deserts
Open fires of plastic cause rainstorms that flood dry savannah regions
Burnt plastics cause wild birds to sing in completely different musical pitches

questions.correctAnswer: Burning plastics releases toxic smoke that damages respiratory health and pollutes God’s atmosphere
questions.explanation: Burning plastics emits hazardous chemicals like dioxins and furans that harm human lungs and pollute the environment. Proper disposal and recycling uphold Christian duty to protect community health.
questions.socraticHint: What poisonous impact does burning plastic produce on the air breathed by children, elders, and neighbors?

questions.prompt: How did Kenyan environmentalist Professor Wangari Maathai exemplify biblical stewardship in our nation?
questions.text: How did Kenyan environmentalist Professor Wangari Maathai exemplify biblical stewardship in our nation?

options.text: By advising farmers never to dig contours or trenches on hilly agricultural land
By mobilizing rural women to plant over 50 million trees and defending Karura Forest from destruction
By advocating for all Kenyan forests to be cleared to construct tall apartment buildings
By encouraging imported plastic bags to replace traditional woven sisal baskets

questions.correctAnswer: By mobilizing rural women to plant over 50 million trees and defending Karura Forest from destruction
questions.explanation: Professor Wangari Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement, courageously defending public green spaces like Karura Forest and Uhuru Park in Nairobi, inspiring millions to care for God’s creation.
questions.socraticHint: Which legendary Kenyan Nobel laureate led nationwide grassroots tree-planting to restore degraded soils?

questions.prompt: In Luke 12:6, how did Jesus illustrate God’s intimate care for even the smallest and humblest creatures?
questions.text: In Luke 12:6, how did Jesus illustrate God’s intimate care for even the smallest and humblest creatures?

options.text: By declaring that birds have no value in the Kingdom of Heaven
By instructing disciples to trap and cage wild birds for sport
By pointing out that not one common sparrow is forgotten in God’s sight
By explaining that lions are the only animals God pays attention to

questions.correctAnswer: By pointing out that not one common sparrow is forgotten in God’s sight
questions.explanation: In Luke 12:6, Jesus asked: "Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God." Jesus showed that God cares for every single humble creature in His world.
questions.socraticHint: Which small, inexpensive bird did Jesus mention to show that God forgets none of His creations?

questions.prompt: A school in Machakos experiences acute water shortages during dry months. How can the school community apply Christian stewardship to harvest water?
questions.text: A school in Machakos experiences acute water shortages during dry months. How can the school community apply Christian stewardship to harvest water?

options.text: Waiting until all boreholes dry up and closing the school indefinitely
Selling school desks to purchase expensive bottled water from distant towns
Diverting dirty runoff water directly into the school kitchen cooking pots
Installing roof gutters and water tanks to harvest rainwater during the rains for dry seasons

questions.correctAnswer: Installing roof gutters and water tanks to harvest rainwater during the rains for dry seasons
questions.explanation: Rainwater harvesting using gutters and storage tanks utilizes God’s gift of rain wisely, preventing water scarcity during dry seasons and protecting the health and dignity of learners.
questions.socraticHint: How can a school capture and store free rain poured from heaven for future use in dry seasons?

questions.prompt: Which of the following environmental crises represents a failure of human stewardship, and what is the Christian solution?
questions.text: Which of the following environmental crises represents a failure of human stewardship, and what is the Christian solution?

options.text: Deforestation causing drought; solved by collective tree planting, protection of water towers, and renewable energy
Natural solar eclipses; solved by cutting down ancient cedar trees across Kenya
Ocean tides rising and falling; solved by draining freshwater rivers into valleys
Seasonal bird migrations; solved by shooting migratory birds near lake wetlands

questions.correctAnswer: Deforestation causing drought; solved by collective tree planting, protection of water towers, and renewable energy
questions.explanation: Deforestation is a direct result of human greed and mismanagement that disrupts rainfall patterns and causes desertification. Christian stewardship responds by reforesting, conserving water towers, and using sustainable energy.
questions.socraticHint: Which widespread environmental problem results from excessive tree felling, and what restorative action reverses it?

questions.prompt: How many total books are contained in the standard Protestant Holy Bible used in Kenyan primary schools?
questions.text: How many total books are contained in the standard Protestant Holy Bible used in Kenyan primary schools?
questions.explanation: The standard Holy Bible contains 66 books in total, composed of 39 books in the Old Testament and 27 books in the New Testament.
questions.socraticHint: What is the sum of the 39 books of the Old Testament and the 27 books of the New Testament?

questions.prompt: How many books are in the Old Testament, and what is its first book?
questions.text: How many books are in the Old Testament, and what is its first book?
questions.explanation: The Old Testament consists of 39 books, and Genesis is the first book, recording the creation of the heavens and the earth and God’s covenant with humanity.
questions.socraticHint: Which foundational book comes right at the beginning of the 39 Old Testament books?

questions.prompt: What are the first five books of the Old Testament collectively known as?
questions.text: What are the first five books of the Old Testament collectively known as?

options.text: The Books of Law or Pentateuch (Torah)

questions.correctAnswer: The Books of Law or Pentateuch (Torah)
questions.explanation: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy are known as the Books of Law, the Pentateuch (Greek for "five scrolls"), or the Torah in Hebrew, associated with Moses.
questions.socraticHint: Which group name refers to the five books containing the moral and ceremonial laws given to Moses?

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of an Old Testament Historical Book?
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an Old Testament Historical Book?
questions.explanation: The Old Testament Historical Books (12 books from Joshua to Esther) chronicle the historical journey of the Israelites, including the conquest of Canaan led by Joshua.
questions.socraticHint: Which leader succeeded Moses and has an Old Testament historical book bearing his name?

questions.prompt: Which group of books includes Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and the Song of Songs?
questions.text: Which group of books includes Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and the Song of Songs?
questions.explanation: These 5 books use Hebrew poetic structure and practical wisdom literature to explore faith, praise, suffering, moral decisions, and deep reverence for God.
questions.socraticHint: Which category title describes books filled with sacred songs, wise sayings, and philosophical reflections on life?

questions.prompt: Why are prophets like Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel categorized as "Major Prophets"?
questions.text: Why are prophets like Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel categorized as "Major Prophets"?

options.text: Their prophecies were considered much more important by God than other messages
They were the only prophets who served as military generals in the army
Their prophetic books are longer in length and volume than those of the Minor Prophets
They were physically older and taller than all the other prophets in Israel

questions.correctAnswer: Their prophetic books are longer in length and volume than those of the Minor Prophets
questions.explanation: The distinction between "Major" and "Minor" prophets refers strictly to the length of their preserved writings, not their spiritual importance or status before God.
questions.socraticHint: Does the label "major" describe the physical length and volume of their scrolls or their spiritual rank?

questions.prompt: How many books are in the New Testament, and what is its concluding prophetic book?
questions.text: How many books are in the New Testament, and what is its concluding prophetic book?
questions.explanation: The New Testament contains 27 books, and Revelation (Apocalypse) is the final book of prophecy, written by the Apostle John on the island of Patmos.
questions.socraticHint: What is the very last book of the 27 books in the New Testament called?

questions.prompt: Which four New Testament books record the life, miracles, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ?
questions.text: Which four New Testament books record the life, miracles, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ?

options.text: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John (The Gospels)

questions.correctAnswer: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John (The Gospels)
questions.explanation: The four Gospels—Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John—form the heart of the New Testament, providing four complementary accounts of the life, teachings, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ.
questions.socraticHint: Which four biographical books at the beginning of the New Testament are known as the Gospels?

questions.prompt: Which New Testament book is unique because it serves as the single historical record of the Early Church after Jesus ascended?
questions.text: Which New Testament book is unique because it serves as the single historical record of the Early Church after Jesus ascended?
questions.explanation: The Acts of the Apostles, written by Luke, is the sole historical book of the New Testament. It records the coming of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost and the growth of the early Christian Church.
questions.socraticHint: Which book chronicles the actions and missionary journeys of the apostles like Peter and Paul?

questions.prompt: What was the primary purpose of the Epistles (letters) written by Paul, Peter, and other apostles in the New Testament?
questions.text: What was the primary purpose of the Epistles (letters) written by Paul, Peter, and other apostles in the New Testament?

options.text: To share secret recipes for unleavened bread and Mediterranean olive dishes
To record mathematical formulas for measuring stone pillars in synagogues
To encourage, instruct, and guide early churches in Christian living and sound doctrine
To demand taxes and financial tributes on behalf of the Roman emperor

questions.correctAnswer: To encourage, instruct, and guide early churches in Christian living and sound doctrine
questions.explanation: The Epistles were written to guide, correct, and encourage new Christian congregations in various cities, addressing practical moral challenges and explaining faith in Jesus Christ.
questions.socraticHint: Why did apostolic leaders send pastoral letters to early Christian communities in Rome, Corinth, and Ephesus?

questions.prompt: Grace wants to find a book in the Bible that offers practical short sayings on honesty, hard work, and wisdom. Which book should she turn to?
questions.text: Grace wants to find a book in the Bible that offers practical short sayings on honesty, hard work, and wisdom. Which book should she turn to?
questions.explanation: The Book of Proverbs is a collection of inspired wisdom sayings primarily written by King Solomon, giving practical moral guidance on honesty, diligence, speech, and the fear of the Lord.
questions.socraticHint: Which Old Testament wisdom book is famous for short, memorable guidelines on righteous daily living?

questions.prompt: How do the Old Testament and New Testament complement each other in God’s plan of salvation?
questions.text: How do the Old Testament and New Testament complement each other in God’s plan of salvation?

options.text: The Old Testament points forward with covenants and prophecies that are fulfilled by Jesus Christ in the New Testament
The New Testament completely cancels out and proves that the Old Testament was totally false
They were written for two completely different gods who had opposing beliefs about humanity
The Old Testament is for children while the New Testament is strictly reserved for ordained clergy

questions.correctAnswer: The Old Testament points forward with covenants and prophecies that are fulfilled by Jesus Christ in the New Testament
questions.explanation: Saint Augustine famously observed: "The New Testament lies hidden in the Old, and the Old is unveiled in the New." The Old Testament prepares the way and points toward Christ, who fulfills God’s promises in the New Testament.
questions.socraticHint: How does the arrival of Jesus in the New Testament connect with the promises and prophecies of the Old Testament?

questions.prompt: What does 2 Timothy 3:16 state about the origin and authority of the Holy Scriptures?
questions.text: What does 2 Timothy 3:16 state about the origin and authority of the Holy Scriptures?

options.text: Only the Ten Commandments were inspired while the rest is mere human folklore
All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness
Scripture was written by kings solely to collect taxes from poor citizens
The Bible contains human opinions that have no relevance to moral decisions

questions.correctAnswer: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 3:16 declares: "All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness." This affirms the divine inspiration and moral authority of the Bible.
questions.socraticHint: What special biblical term in 2 Timothy indicates that God inspired the human authors of the Bible?

questions.prompt: In Psalm 119:105, what powerful metaphor is used to describe God’s Word in our everyday journey?
questions.text: In Psalm 119:105, what powerful metaphor is used to describe God’s Word in our everyday journey?

options.text: Your word is a thick dark fog over the hills
Your word is a noisy trumpet in the desert
Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path
Your word is an iron chain that ties our feet

questions.correctAnswer: Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:105 says: "Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path." Scripture guides believers, illuminating the right, ethical path in life and dispelling moral darkness.
questions.socraticHint: Which familiar verse compares scripture to a light showing where to step on a dark road?

questions.prompt: Which organization in Kenya is officially dedicated to translating, publishing, and distributing the Holy Bible in indigenous languages?
questions.text: Which organization in Kenya is officially dedicated to translating, publishing, and distributing the Holy Bible in indigenous languages?
questions.explanation: The Bible Society of Kenya (BSK) is a Christian non-governmental organization serving churches by translating, publishing, and distributing the Holy Scriptures in languages Kenyans understand best.
questions.socraticHint: Which national faith organization bears the words "Bible Society" in its title?

questions.prompt: Why is it important to translate the Bible into indigenous Kenyan languages like Kikuyu, Dholuo, Kalenjin, Kamba, and Rendille?
questions.text: Why is it important to translate the Bible into indigenous Kenyan languages like Kikuyu, Dholuo, Kalenjin, Kamba, and Rendille?

options.text: So that people can hear, understand, and experience God’s Word deeply in their heart language
To prevent people from learning national and international languages like English and Kiswahili
Because the original English version of the Bible had too many spelling mistakes
So that books can only be read by village elders and hidden from school children

questions.correctAnswer: So that people can hear, understand, and experience God’s Word deeply in their heart language
questions.explanation: Reading the Bible in one’s mother tongue allows individuals to connect intimately with God’s truth, understanding theological concepts clearly in words and idioms that resonate with their culture.
questions.socraticHint: How does reading sacred scripture in your native mother tongue help you understand God’s message more deeply?

questions.prompt: Which early missionary in Rabai, Mombasa pioneered translating portions of the Christian scriptures into Kiswahili in the 1840s?
questions.text: Which early missionary in Rabai, Mombasa pioneered translating portions of the Christian scriptures into Kiswahili in the 1840s?
questions.explanation: Dr. Johann Ludwig Krapf, working with the Church Missionary Society (CMS) in Rabai near Mombasa, was the pioneer translator who produced the earliest Kiswahili translation of parts of the New Testament.
questions.socraticHint: Which German CMS missionary who lived at Rabai worked on the very first Swahili scripture translation?

questions.prompt: Which of the following practices demonstrates respectful physical handling of the Holy Bible?
questions.text: Which of the following practices demonstrates respectful physical handling of the Holy Bible?

options.text: Tearing out Bible pages to roll toy balls or wrap roasted maize
Leaving the Bible opened on the damp ground under direct rain
Storing the Bible in a clean, elevated place and handling its pages with clean, dry hands
Using the Bible as an outdoor footrest while eating lunch in the school compound

questions.correctAnswer: Storing the Bible in a clean, elevated place and handling its pages with clean, dry hands
questions.explanation: Christians revere the Bible as God’s inspired Word by handling the physical book with care, keeping it clean, storing it in an elevated place, and turning pages respectfully.
questions.socraticHint: Which action treats the holy printed text with cleanliness, carefulness, and honor?

questions.prompt: In James 1:22, what vital admonition is given to everyone who reads or listens to God’s Word?
questions.text: In James 1:22, what vital admonition is given to everyone who reads or listens to God’s Word?

options.text: Memorize all verses so you can win debates and make others feel inferior
Only listen to the word on Sundays and forget about it throughout the school week
Keep the word secret so other communities never hear the good news
Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says

questions.correctAnswer: Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says
questions.explanation: James 1:22 urges: "Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says." Real Christian reverence for scripture is shown through active obedience and ethical living.
questions.socraticHint: Does the Apostle James emphasize merely hearing the word or actively putting it into practice?

questions.prompt: During an end-of-term examination, David sees that a classmate has dropped their answer sheet where it is clearly visible. How can David apply Biblical teaching?
questions.text: During an end-of-term examination, David sees that a classmate has dropped their answer sheet where it is clearly visible. How can David apply Biblical teaching?

options.text: Refuse to cheat, focus on his own work with integrity, and notify the invigilator about the dropped paper
Quickly copy all the answers and thank God for providing a miraculous shortcut
Pass the dropped paper secretly to his best friend so they both get higher marks
Step on the paper to hide it until after the exam and then claim it as his own

questions.correctAnswer: Refuse to cheat, focus on his own work with integrity, and notify the invigilator about the dropped paper
questions.explanation: Proverbs 11:1 states that "The Lord detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him." Living out God’s Word means maintaining honest integrity even when tempted to cheat.
questions.socraticHint: Which response reflects Christian honesty and refusal to take dishonest shortcuts?

questions.prompt: What was the original language in which the majority of the Old Testament was composed?
questions.text: What was the original language in which the majority of the Old Testament was composed?
questions.explanation: The Old Testament was originally written primarily in biblical Hebrew, with a few small portions composed in Aramaic (such as sections in Daniel and Ezra).
questions.socraticHint: In which ancient Semitic language spoken by the Israelites was the Old Testament originally penned?

questions.prompt: What was the common language in which the New Testament was originally written across the Mediterranean world?
questions.text: What was the common language in which the New Testament was originally written across the Mediterranean world?
questions.explanation: The New Testament was written in Koine Greek (common Greek), which was the widely spoken international language across the Roman Empire during the first century AD.
questions.socraticHint: Which common Mediterranean language was spoken widely in the Roman world when the Apostles wrote the Gospels and Epistles?

questions.prompt: A family in Kakamega begins holding daily evening scripture devotion. What positive spiritual benefit does this bring to the home?
questions.text: A family in Kakamega begins holding daily evening scripture devotion. What positive spiritual benefit does this bring to the home?

options.text: It ensures that no family member ever has to do school homework or house chores
It causes neighbors to become jealous and file formal complaints at the chief’s camp
It guarantees that the family will instantly become millionaires without farming
It nurtures love, peaceful resolution of disagreements, moral accountability, and spiritual growth

questions.correctAnswer: It nurtures love, peaceful resolution of disagreements, moral accountability, and spiritual growth
questions.explanation: Gathering to read and apply scripture fosters mutual love, forgiveness, spiritual grounding, and moral character among family members, creating a peaceful, godly home environment.
questions.socraticHint: How does reading God’s Word together strengthen relationships, forgiveness, and moral discipline in a home?

questions.prompt: Why does Christian tradition describe the Holy Bible as "inspired by the Holy Spirit" rather than just ordinary human literature?
questions.text: Why does Christian tradition describe the Holy Bible as "inspired by the Holy Spirit" rather than just ordinary human literature?

options.text: Because God guided the thoughts of human authors so that they faithfully conveyed God’s divine truth without error in matters of faith
Because the physical pages were printed in heaven and dropped onto a mountain by angels
Because the authors were under a trance and had no idea what words their hands were writing
Because human beings played no role at all, and it appeared in modern English out of thin air

questions.correctAnswer: Because God guided the thoughts of human authors so that they faithfully conveyed God’s divine truth without error in matters of faith
questions.explanation: Biblical inspiration means God’s Holy Spirit worked within the human authors, using their personalities, historical backgrounds, and writing styles, while guiding them to record God’s infallible truth for humanity.
questions.socraticHint: How did God work through the minds and lives of human writers while guiding the truth of their message?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What did God command Abraham (Abram) to do in Genesis 12:1 to demonstrate his faith and obedience?
questions.text: What did God command Abraham (Abram) to do in Genesis 12:1 to demonstrate his faith and obedience?

options.text: Abandon his livestock in the desert and become a merchant in Egypt
Leave his country, his people, and his father’s household for a land God would show him
Construct a high stone wall around the city of Haran to prevent foreigners from entering
Conquer neighboring tribes by leading a huge cavalry of war horses

questions.correctAnswer: Leave his country, his people, and his father’s household for a land God would show him
questions.explanation: In Genesis 12:1, the Lord told Abram: "Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you." Abraham obeyed without knowing the exact destination, proving his deep faith.
questions.socraticHint: Which great departure did God require of Abraham to test his trust in divine guidance?

questions.prompt: What major covenant promise did God make to Abraham in Genesis 12:2-3?
questions.text: What major covenant promise did God make to Abraham in Genesis 12:2-3?

options.text: I will ensure that none of your descendants ever have to till agricultural land
I will make you the earthly king of all nations in Asia and Africa immediately
I will make you into a great nation, bless you, and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you
I will give you all the silver coins currently minted in the Roman Empire

questions.correctAnswer: I will make you into a great nation, bless you, and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you
questions.explanation: God promised Abraham that He would make him a great nation, bless him, make his name great, and through him all families and peoples of the earth would be blessed.
questions.socraticHint: What threefold covenant promise of land, descendants, and worldwide blessing did God give to Abraham?

questions.prompt: Why is Abraham widely revered across Christian history as the "Father of Faith"?
questions.text: Why is Abraham widely revered across Christian history as the "Father of Faith"?

options.text: He wrote down the entire Old Testament on papyrus scrolls by himself
He possessed more physical gold and camels than any king in the ancient world
He was the first high priest to build the stone temple in Jerusalem
He trusted God’s promises completely and obeyed even when situations seemed impossible

questions.correctAnswer: He trusted God’s promises completely and obeyed even when situations seemed impossible
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:8 notes that "By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, even though he did not know where he was going." His unwavering trust makes him the father of all believers.
questions.socraticHint: What outstanding character trait made Abraham obey God even when he could not see the final outcome?

questions.prompt: Where and how did God first reveal Himself to Moses to call him as the deliverer of Israel?
questions.text: Where and how did God first reveal Himself to Moses to call him as the deliverer of Israel?

options.text: At Mount Horeb in a bush that burned with fire but was not consumed
Inside the royal throne room of Pharaoh while Moses was wearing gold robes
On a fishing boat floating on the Mediterranean Sea during a violent storm
In a crowded marketplace in Babylon while purchasing linen cloth

questions.correctAnswer: At Mount Horeb in a bush that burned with fire but was not consumed
questions.explanation: In Exodus 3:1-4, God appeared to Moses on Mount Horeb in flames of fire from within a bush that burned without being consumed, instructing him to take off his sandals because he stood on holy ground.
questions.socraticHint: What miraculous sight caught Moses’ attention while tending Jethro’s sheep in the wilderness?

questions.prompt: When Moses felt inadequate and complained that he was slow of speech, whom did God appoint to assist him as his spokesman?
questions.text: When Moses felt inadequate and complained that he was slow of speech, whom did God appoint to assist him as his spokesman?
questions.explanation: In Exodus 4:14-16, God appointed Moses’ brother Aaron the Levite, who could speak well, to act as his spokesman before the elders of Israel and Pharaoh.
questions.socraticHint: Which eloquent biological brother was assigned to speak alongside Moses before Pharaoh?

questions.prompt: When the Israelites were trapped between the Red Sea and Pharaoh’s advancing army, what inspiring words did Moses speak in Exodus 14:13?
questions.text: When the Israelites were trapped between the Red Sea and Pharaoh’s advancing army, what inspiring words did Moses speak in Exodus 14:13?

options.text: Jump into the deep waters and try to swim to the opposite shore before nightfall
Scatter into the wilderness hills and let everyone fight for their own life
Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today
Surrender immediately to the Egyptian soldiers and beg for mercy as slaves

questions.correctAnswer: Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today
questions.explanation: Moses showed extraordinary faith and godly composure in crisis, telling the terrified Israelites: "Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today. The Lord will fight for you; you need only to be still."
questions.socraticHint: Which famous statement commanded the people to reject fear and trust God’s miraculous salvation?

questions.prompt: How did God miraculously deliver the Israelites across the Red Sea in Exodus 14:21-22?
questions.text: How did God miraculously deliver the Israelites across the Red Sea in Exodus 14:21-22?

options.text: God sent hundreds of wooden canoes from Phoenicia to ferry the people across
The sea froze into solid ice and the Israelites skated across without wet shoes
An earthquake formed an underground tunnel beneath the sea floor
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and God drove the sea back with a strong east wind, dividing the waters so they walked on dry ground

questions.correctAnswer: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and God drove the sea back with a strong east wind, dividing the waters so they walked on dry ground
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:21-22 explains that Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the Lord drove the sea back with a powerful east wind, turning the seabed into dry land with a wall of water on their right and left.
questions.socraticHint: How did God’s power divide the waters of the sea to create a safe dry pathway for His people?

questions.prompt: What leadership quality demonstrated by Moses is essential for a school class prefect in Kenya today?
questions.text: What leadership quality demonstrated by Moses is essential for a school class prefect in Kenya today?

options.text: Servant leadership: putting the welfare of others first and praying for their guidance in difficult moments
Dictatorial rule: punishing smaller pupils unfairly to prove how powerful and feared they are
Favoritism: excusing friends from class duties while overloading pupils they dislike
Dishonesty: taking snacks from classmates in exchange for hiding bad behavior from the teacher

questions.correctAnswer: Servant leadership: putting the welfare of others first and praying for their guidance in difficult moments
questions.explanation: Moses was a humble servant leader (Numbers 12:3). Christian leadership involves selflessly serving others, seeking God’s guidance in difficulties, and defending justice rather than abusing authority.
questions.socraticHint: Which leadership style focuses on humble service, fair defense of others, and seeking divine guidance?

questions.prompt: When God asked Abraham to sacrifice his only promised son Isaac on Mount Moriah (Genesis 22), what divine truth was revealed when God provided a ram caught in a thicket?
questions.text: When God asked Abraham to sacrifice his only promised son Isaac on Mount Moriah (Genesis 22), what divine truth was revealed when God provided a ram caught in a thicket?

options.text: Sacrificing sheep is forbidden under all circumstances in scripture
God provides for our needs (Yahweh Yireh / The Lord Will Provide) and honors faithful obedience
God delights in taking away human life without reason
Abraham made a serious mistake by climbing Mount Moriah without food

questions.correctAnswer: God provides for our needs (Yahweh Yireh / The Lord Will Provide) and honors faithful obedience
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:14 states that Abraham called the place "The Lord Will Provide" (Yahweh Yireh). God did not want Isaac harmed; He tested Abraham’s devotion and provided a substitute sacrifice, foreshadowing Christ.
questions.socraticHint: What special name meaning "The Lord Will Provide" did Abraham give to the place where God provided a ram?

questions.prompt: How did Moses demonstrate humility when his father-in-law Jethro visited him in Exodus 18?
questions.text: How did Moses demonstrate humility when his father-in-law Jethro visited him in Exodus 18?

options.text: He claimed that because he spoke to God directly, he had no need for human counsel
He resigned from leadership immediately and hid in a tent until Jethro left camp
He humbly accepted Jethro’s wise advice to delegate judicial responsibilities to capable, God-fearing leaders
He angrily banished Jethro for interfering in the political affairs of the nation of Israel

questions.correctAnswer: He humbly accepted Jethro’s wise advice to delegate judicial responsibilities to capable, God-fearing leaders
questions.explanation: Moses listened to Jethro’s wise counsel and appointed trustworthy, God-fearing men as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, avoiding burnout and serving the community more effectively.
questions.socraticHint: How did Moses respond when Jethro advised him to share the burden of judging disputes with other leaders?

questions.prompt: A learner named Wanjiku is transferred to a new boarding school in a distant county where she knows nobody. How does Abraham’s faith journey encourage her?
questions.text: A learner named Wanjiku is transferred to a new boarding school in a distant county where she knows nobody. How does Abraham’s faith journey encourage her?

options.text: She realizes that she must refuse to eat any school food until her parents take her back home
She decides that traveling to new places always brings bad luck and curses
She assumes she must change her religious beliefs whenever she enters a new town
She knows that just as God guided and protected Abraham in an unfamiliar land, God will be with her wherever she goes

questions.correctAnswer: She knows that just as God guided and protected Abraham in an unfamiliar land, God will be with her wherever she goes
questions.explanation: Abraham’s journey reminds believers that God’s presence, guidance, and protection are not limited by geography. Trusting God brings peace and confidence in new, unfamiliar environments.
questions.socraticHint: How does trusting in God’s omnipresent care help someone facing a new and unfamiliar environment?

questions.prompt: What common theological theme unites both Abraham’s call and Moses’ mission at the Red Sea?
questions.text: What common theological theme unites both Abraham’s call and Moses’ mission at the Red Sea?

options.text: Total trust in God’s sovereign promises and obedient action despite human impossibility
Relying entirely on human military weapons and chariot cavalry to solve problems
Accumulating commercial silver wealth before obeying any divine instruction
Refusing to move forward unless angels are visibly walking in front of the camp

questions.correctAnswer: Total trust in God’s sovereign promises and obedient action despite human impossibility
questions.explanation: Both Abraham and Moses faced situations that seemed impossible by human logic, yet their active faith and obedience allowed God’s miraculous power and covenant purposes to prevail.
questions.socraticHint: What core spiritual principle requires stepping forward in trust even when human eyes see obstacles?

questions.prompt: Under whose care and priestly mentorship was the boy Samuel serving in the sanctuary at Shiloh?
questions.text: Under whose care and priestly mentorship was the boy Samuel serving in the sanctuary at Shiloh?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:1 records that the boy Samuel ministered before the Lord under Eli the priest at Shiloh, where the Ark of God was kept.
questions.socraticHint: Which elderly priest at Shiloh mentored young Samuel in the sanctuary?

questions.prompt: What exact words did Eli instruct Samuel to say if he heard the divine voice calling him again in the night (1 Samuel 3:9)?
questions.text: What exact words did Eli instruct Samuel to say if he heard the divine voice calling him again in the night (1 Samuel 3:9)?

options.text: Wait until morning, Lord, when the sun rises
Speak to Eli, Lord, because he is older than me
Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening
Go away, Lord, for I am trying to sleep

questions.correctAnswer: Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 3:9, Eli told Samuel: "Go and lie down, and if he calls you, say, ‘Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.’" This reflects humble, attentive readiness to hear God’s will.
questions.socraticHint: Which respectful phrase expressing readiness to listen did Eli teach Samuel to say?

questions.prompt: What does young Samuel’s response teach Grade 5 learners about their own spiritual lives?
questions.text: What does young Samuel’s response teach Grade 5 learners about their own spiritual lives?

options.text: God only speaks to people who have gray hair and walk with wooden walking sticks
Children should ignore church teachings until they finish university education
Listening to parents and teachers is unnecessary if you have a Bible
Children can hear God’s calling, develop spiritual sensitivity, and serve God with humble hearts

questions.correctAnswer: Children can hear God’s calling, develop spiritual sensitivity, and serve God with humble hearts
questions.explanation: Samuel was called while still a boy. This teaches that age is not a barrier to hearing and obeying God; young people can cultivate attentive, obedient hearts to serve God in their families and schools.
questions.socraticHint: Can God speak to and use young boys and girls, or does He only speak to elderly individuals?

questions.prompt: Which wicked king and queen led the nation of Israel into widespread idolatry and Baal worship during the time of Elijah?
questions.text: Which wicked king and queen led the nation of Israel into widespread idolatry and Baal worship during the time of Elijah?

options.text: King Solomon and Queen of Sheba

questions.explanation: King Ahab and his Phoenician wife Jezebel promoted the worship of Baal and Asherah, leading Israel away from the God of Abraham and persecuting God’s true prophets (1 Kings 16:30-33).
questions.socraticHint: Which notorious royal couple reigned in Samaria and introduced state-sponsored Baal worship?

questions.prompt: On which famous mountain did Prophet Elijah challenge 450 prophets of Baal to a contest of fire?
questions.text: On which famous mountain did Prophet Elijah challenge 450 prophets of Baal to a contest of fire?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:19 records Elijah challenging Ahab to assemble all Israel and the 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel to determine who was the true God.
questions.socraticHint: Which coastal mountain ridge in northern Israel was the setting for the dramatic contest between Elijah and Baal’s prophets?

questions.prompt: What was the condition agreed upon between Elijah and the prophets of Baal to prove who was the true God?
questions.text: What was the condition agreed upon between Elijah and the prophets of Baal to prove who was the true God?

options.text: Whoever collects the largest pile of gold jewelry from the spectators wins
The side that can shout the loudest without drinking water for three days wins
The god who answers by sending fire to consume the sacrifice is the true God
The group that can run up the mountain fastest will be declared winners

questions.correctAnswer: The god who answers by sending fire to consume the sacrifice is the true God
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:24, Elijah declared: "The god who answers by fire—he is God." Baal, who was worshiped as the god of storms and fire, proved completely powerless, while the Lord God answered with divine fire.
questions.socraticHint: How did Elijah propose that the true God should reveal His supremacy over the wooden and stone idols?

questions.prompt: How did the 450 prophets of Baal behave during the morning and afternoon contest on Mount Carmel?
questions.text: How did the 450 prophets of Baal behave during the morning and afternoon contest on Mount Carmel?

options.text: They quietly prayed a psalm of repentance and received immediate answers
They admitted immediately that Baal was fake and walked away quietly
They poured freshwater on their altar to cool down the hot stones
They shouted, danced frantically, and cut themselves with knives, but there was no response or fire

questions.correctAnswer: They shouted, danced frantically, and cut themselves with knives, but there was no response or fire
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:26-29 describes Baal’s prophets shouting from morning till evening, leaping on the altar, and cutting themselves until blood flowed, yet "there was no response, no one answered, no one paid attention."
questions.socraticHint: Did the false prophets of Baal receive any answer despite shouting and slashing themselves all day?

questions.prompt: Before offering his prayer, what bold action did Elijah take that made lighting the altar humanly impossible?
questions.text: Before offering his prayer, what bold action did Elijah take that made lighting the altar humanly impossible?

options.text: He had large jars of water poured over the offering and wood three times until the trench was filled
He placed the wood inside an underground cave where air could not reach it
He covered the wood with heavy wet cow dung to smother any sparks
He waited until a heavy thunderstorm blew away all the dry branches

questions.correctAnswer: He had large jars of water poured over the offering and wood three times until the trench was filled
questions.explanation: Elijah commanded four large jars of water to be poured over the sacrifice three times (12 jars in total), drenching the wood and filling the trench, ensuring everyone knew only miraculous divine power could ignite the fire.
questions.socraticHint: What liquid did Elijah order to be poured repeatedly over the wood and sacrifice to eliminate any trickery?

questions.prompt: When the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt offering, wood, stones, and water, how did the people of Israel respond (1 Kings 18:39)?
questions.text: When the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt offering, wood, stones, and water, how did the people of Israel respond (1 Kings 18:39)?

options.text: They ran away in terror into the Mediterranean Sea to escape the heat
They fell prostrate and cried, "The Lord—He is God! The Lord—He is God!"
They laughed loudly and claimed Elijah had used magic gunpowder from Egypt
They demanded that Elijah apologize to King Ahab and Queen Jezebel

questions.correctAnswer: They fell prostrate and cried, "The Lord—He is God! The Lord—He is God!"
questions.explanation: Upon witnessing the supernatural fire consuming the entire soaked altar, all the people fell prostrate on the ground and proclaimed: "The Lord—He is God! The Lord—He is God!" (1 Kings 18:39).
questions.socraticHint: What unanimous declaration of praise and faith in Yahweh broke out among the crowd?

questions.prompt: During a class election, all classmates are voting for a student who bullies smaller children. Brian bravely votes for an honest, kind candidate. Who in scripture does Brian resemble?
questions.text: During a class election, all classmates are voting for a student who bullies smaller children. Brian bravely votes for an honest, kind candidate. Who in scripture does Brian resemble?

options.text: Priest Eli’s wicked sons, who abused their religious positions for personal gain
The merchants of Babylon, who cared only about monetary profits
Prophet Elijah, who stood alone boldly for God’s truth against 450 false prophets
King Ahab, who followed Queen Jezebel into wickedness to stay popular

questions.correctAnswer: Prophet Elijah, who stood alone boldly for God’s truth against 450 false prophets
questions.explanation: Elijah stood courageously for God even when he was outnumbered 450 to 1. Standing for righteousness against peer pressure reflects Elijah’s moral courage.
questions.socraticHint: Which Old Testament prophet had the courage to stand alone for truth when the majority followed falsehood?

questions.prompt: How did God speak to a discouraged Elijah when he hid in a cave at Mount Horeb in 1 Kings 19:11-13?
questions.text: How did God speak to a discouraged Elijah when he hid in a cave at Mount Horeb in 1 Kings 19:11-13?

options.text: Through a terrifying earthquake that destroyed the entire mountain range
Through blinding lightning bolts that struck down every tree around the cave
Through a violent hurricane wind that shattered giant rocks into dust
Not in the great wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a gentle whisper (still small voice)

questions.correctAnswer: Not in the great wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a gentle whisper (still small voice)
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:11-12 tells how the Lord was not in the wind, the earthquake, or the fire, but after the fire came a gentle whisper (a still small voice), teaching that God often speaks in quiet stillness.
questions.socraticHint: Did God reveal His message in the loud spectacular forces or in a gentle, quiet whisper?

questions.prompt: What vital moral lesson do both young Samuel and Prophet Elijah teach Christians in 21st-century Kenya?
questions.text: What vital moral lesson do both young Samuel and Prophet Elijah teach Christians in 21st-century Kenya?

options.text: Listen attentively to God’s calling and boldly stand for righteousness regardless of public opinion
Only speak up for justice when everyone else in the community agrees with you
Use supernatural fire to punish anyone who disagrees with your personal opinions
Never accept leadership roles because leaders always face criticism

questions.correctAnswer: Listen attentively to God’s calling and boldly stand for righteousness regardless of public opinion
questions.explanation: Samuel exemplifies attentive obedience to God’s call, and Elijah demonstrates fearless dedication to divine truth. Together, they model living with integrity, faith, and moral courage in modern society.
questions.socraticHint: What shared qualities of attentive listening and uncompromising courage define their lives?

questions.prompt: Which archangel was sent by God to Mary in the town of Nazareth to announce the birth of Jesus (Luke 1:26)?
questions.text: Which archangel was sent by God to Mary in the town of Nazareth to announce the birth of Jesus (Luke 1:26)?
questions.explanation: Luke 1:26-28 states that God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a town in Galilee, to a virgin pledged to be married to a man named Joseph, whose name was Mary.
questions.socraticHint: Which angel delivered the news of the Messiah’s conception to Mary in Nazareth?

questions.prompt: What humble and faithful response did Mary give to the angel in Luke 1:38?
questions.text: What humble and faithful response did Mary give to the angel in Luke 1:38?

options.text: I will only accept if you make me the earthly queen of the Roman Empire
I do not believe in angels and want you to leave my house immediately
I am the Lord’s servant. May your word to me be fulfilled
No, choose another woman in Jerusalem who has more silver and gold

questions.correctAnswer: I am the Lord’s servant. May your word to me be fulfilled
questions.explanation: In Luke 1:38, Mary answered with supreme faith and humility: "I am the Lord’s servant. May your word to me be fulfilled." She willingly submitted to God’s divine plan.
questions.socraticHint: Which submissive, trusting phrase expressed Mary’s willingness to be used by God?

questions.prompt: In which town was Jesus born, fulfilling the Old Testament prophecy of Micah 5:2?
questions.text: In which town was Jesus born, fulfilling the Old Testament prophecy of Micah 5:2?
questions.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, the city of David, where Joseph and Mary had traveled for the Roman census decreed by Caesar Augustus (Luke 2:4-7).
questions.socraticHint: In which small Judean town, also called the City of David, was Jesus born?

questions.prompt: Why was baby Jesus placed in a humble manger (animal feeding trough) after His birth?
questions.text: Why was baby Jesus placed in a humble manger (animal feeding trough) after His birth?

options.text: Because there was no guest room available for them in the inn
Because Joseph preferred sleeping in barns rather than comfortable rooms
Because King Herod had locked all hotel doors across Judea
Because Roman law forbade babies from sleeping inside houses

questions.correctAnswer: Because there was no guest room available for them in the inn
questions.explanation: Luke 2:7 records: "She gave birth to her firstborn, a son. She wrapped him in cloths and placed him in a manger, because there was no guest room available for them in the inn."
questions.socraticHint: Why was there no normal bed available for Joseph and Mary in Bethlehem?

questions.prompt: To whom did the angels first announce the joyous news of the Saviour’s birth in Luke 2:8-14?
questions.text: To whom did the angels first announce the joyous news of the Saviour’s birth in Luke 2:8-14?

options.text: The high priests and scribes presiding over the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem
Humble shepherds keeping watch over their flocks in the fields at night
The Roman governor Pontius Pilate in his grand palace in Caesarea
The wealthy merchants trading purple cloth in Athens

questions.correctAnswer: Humble shepherds keeping watch over their flocks in the fields at night
questions.explanation: God chose humble, ordinary shepherds working night shifts in the fields to be the very first recipients of the angelic announcement of the Messiah’s birth, demonstrating that the Good News is for everyone.
questions.socraticHint: Which ordinary working-class group tending sheep received the midnight angelic visitation?

questions.prompt: What three symbolic gifts did the Magi (wise men from the East) present to the young child Jesus (Matthew 2:11)?
questions.text: What three symbolic gifts did the Magi (wise men from the East) present to the young child Jesus (Matthew 2:11)?

options.text: Silk robes, Woolen blankets, and Leather sandals
Wheat flour, Olive oil, and Fresh goat milk
Silver coins, Copper plates, and Iron shields

questions.explanation: Matthew 2:11 records that the Magi opened their treasures and presented Jesus with gifts of gold (for a King), frankincense (incense for God/Priest), and myrrh (anointing spice for burial).
questions.socraticHint: Which precious metal and two fragrant spices were gifted by the Magi from the East?

questions.prompt: When Jesus was twelve years old, where did his parents find Him after searching for three days in Jerusalem (Luke 2:46)?
questions.text: When Jesus was twelve years old, where did his parents find Him after searching for three days in Jerusalem (Luke 2:46)?

options.text: At the Roman military barracks watching soldier drills
At the city gates buying sweets and figs from street vendors
Swimming with neighborhood children in the Pool of Siloam
In the Temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions

questions.correctAnswer: In the Temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions
questions.explanation: Luke 2:46 states that after three days they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the religious teachers, listening to them and asking thoughtful questions, and everyone was amazed at His understanding.
questions.socraticHint: Where in Jerusalem was the boy Jesus found conversing with Jewish teachers of the Law?

questions.prompt: What did young Jesus answer Mary when she asked why He had stayed behind in Jerusalem (Luke 2:49)?
questions.text: What did young Jesus answer Mary when she asked why He had stayed behind in Jerusalem (Luke 2:49)?

options.text: Why were you searching for me? Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house (about my Father’s business)?
I was tired of traveling on donkey trails and wanted to rest in a city hotel
I got lost in the crowded bazaar and forgot where you parked the carriage
I decided that I never wanted to return to Nazareth again

questions.correctAnswer: Why were you searching for me? Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house (about my Father’s business)?
questions.explanation: Jesus replied: "Why were you searching for me? Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?" Even at age 12, Jesus demonstrated deep consciousness of His unique divine mission and filial relationship with God the Father.
questions.socraticHint: Which response showed young Jesus’ awareness of His heavenly Father’s priority?

questions.prompt: According to Luke 2:52, in what four dimensions did Jesus grow during His boyhood in Nazareth?
questions.text: According to Luke 2:52, in what four dimensions did Jesus grow during His boyhood in Nazareth?

options.text: In isolation, silence, physical weakness, and fear of crowds
In wisdom, stature, and in favor with God and man
In military power, wealth, land ownership, and political dominance
In stubbornness, pride, anger, and avoidance of physical work
