questions.correctAnswer: In wisdom, stature, and in favor with God and man
questions.explanation: Luke 2:52 summarizes Jesus’ holistic development: "And Jesus grew in wisdom (intellectually) and stature (physically), and in favor with God (spiritually) and man (socially).
questions.socraticHint: Which verse outlines the intellectual, physical, spiritual, and social growth of young Jesus?

questions.prompt: How does Jesus’ obedience to Mary and Joseph in Nazareth (Luke 2:51) guide Kenyan school learners at home?
questions.text: How does Jesus’ obedience to Mary and Joseph in Nazareth (Luke 2:51) guide Kenyan school learners at home?

options.text: Learners should demand payment before doing any domestic chores like washing dishes
Learners should ignore parental advice once they enter Grade 5
Learners should honor, respect, and obey their parents and guardians in all daily family duties
Learners should argue with their parents because children know more about smartphones

questions.correctAnswer: Learners should honor, respect, and obey their parents and guardians in all daily family duties
questions.explanation: Although Jesus was the Son of God, Luke 2:51 states He went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. Christian children are called to show filial respect, honor, and obedience to parents.
questions.socraticHint: How does Jesus’ submission to his earthly parents model behavior for children in their families?

questions.prompt: Why did Joseph and Mary flee with baby Jesus to Egypt according to Matthew 2:13-14?
questions.text: Why did Joseph and Mary flee with baby Jesus to Egypt according to Matthew 2:13-14?

options.text: They wanted to take a luxury holiday along the River Nile
Joseph had found a high-paying carpentry job in the city of Alexandria
Bethlehem had run completely out of clean drinking water
An angel warned Joseph in a dream that King Herod was searching for the child to kill Him

questions.correctAnswer: An angel warned Joseph in a dream that King Herod was searching for the child to kill Him
questions.explanation: An angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying: "Get up, take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt... for Herod is going to search for the child to kill him." They fled by night to protect Jesus.
questions.socraticHint: Which jealous ruler sought to kill the newborn Messiah, causing the holy family to seek refuge in Egypt?

questions.prompt: What profound lesson does Jesus’ birth in a humble Bethlehem manger teach about God’s values compared to worldly values?
questions.text: What profound lesson does Jesus’ birth in a humble Bethlehem manger teach about God’s values compared to worldly values?

options.text: True greatness is rooted in humility, servant hood, and simplicity, rather than worldly status and luxury
God prefers to work only in magnificent palace bedrooms with gold chandeliers
Poor people are not allowed to be part of God’s covenant family
Worldly wealth and expensive designer clothing are the true signs of spiritual perfection

questions.correctAnswer: True greatness is rooted in humility, servant hood, and simplicity, rather than worldly status and luxury
questions.explanation: God chose a humble stable, poor parents, and ordinary shepherds for the incarnation of the King of Kings. This demonstrates that God values humility, meekness, and spiritual purity over earthly prestige.
questions.socraticHint: Does the Lord define true greatness through worldly prestige and luxury, or through humble love and simplicity?

questions.prompt: In which river was Jesus baptized by John the Baptist (Matthew 3:13)?
questions.text: In which river was Jesus baptized by John the Baptist (Matthew 3:13)?
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:13 states: "Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John." The River Jordan is the historic river where John conducted his baptism of repentance.
questions.socraticHint: Which famous biblical river in Israel did John the Baptist use to baptize people and Jesus?

questions.prompt: Why did Jesus insist on being baptized even though John felt unworthy and knew Jesus had committed no sin (Matthew 3:15)?
questions.text: Why did Jesus insist on being baptized even though John felt unworthy and knew Jesus had committed no sin (Matthew 3:15)?

options.text: To demonstrate that John’s preaching was completely mistaken
To compete with Pharisees who held outdoor ceremonial hand-washing rituals
To fulfill all righteousness and identify fully with humanity in obedience to God’s plan
Because the weather was too hot in Galilee and He wanted a refreshing swim

questions.correctAnswer: To fulfill all righteousness and identify fully with humanity in obedience to God’s plan
questions.explanation: Jesus told John: "Let it be so now; it is proper for us to do this to fulfill all righteousness." Jesus was baptized to inaugurate His messianic ministry, identify with sinful humanity, and fulfill God’s divine requirements.
questions.socraticHint: Why did Jesus say it was necessary for them to complete this act of obedience to God’s righteousness?

questions.prompt: What miraculous signs occurred immediately as Jesus came up out of the water after His baptism (Matthew 3:16-17)?
questions.text: What miraculous signs occurred immediately as Jesus came up out of the water after His baptism (Matthew 3:16-17)?

options.text: A violent earthquake split Mount Hermon into two equal halves
A total solar eclipse darkened Judea for twelve hours straight
John the Baptist was carried up to heaven in a fiery chariot like Elijah
Heaven opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and a voice from heaven said: "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased"

questions.correctAnswer: Heaven opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and a voice from heaven said: "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased"
questions.explanation: At Jesus’ baptism, the Trinity was revealed: the Son was baptized, the Holy Spirit descended in the bodily shape of a dove, and the Father spoke from heaven affirming His beloved Son.
questions.socraticHint: What heavenly voice spoke, and in what form did the Holy Spirit descend upon Jesus?

questions.prompt: How long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before being tempted by the devil (Matthew 4:2)?
questions.text: How long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before being tempted by the devil (Matthew 4:2)?

options.text: One hundred days and one hundred nights

questions.explanation: Matthew 4:2 states that after fasting forty days and forty nights, Jesus was hungry, at which point the tempter approached Him.
questions.socraticHint: Which significant biblical duration of fasting did Jesus observe in the Judean desert?

questions.prompt: What was the devil’s first temptation to Jesus in Matthew 4:3, targeting His physical hunger?
questions.text: What was the devil’s first temptation to Jesus in Matthew 4:3, targeting His physical hunger?

options.text: Curse John the Baptist for making you wet in River Jordan
If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread
Jump off the highest pinnacle of the temple into the valley
Bow down and worship me to receive all the kingdoms of the world

questions.correctAnswer: If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread
questions.explanation: The tempter said: "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread." Satan tempted Jesus to use His divine power selfishly to satisfy His bodily appetite apart from God’s will.
questions.socraticHint: What food did the devil tempt hungry Jesus to miraculously create from desert rocks?

questions.prompt: How did Jesus overcome the devil’s first temptation in Matthew 4:4?
questions.text: How did Jesus overcome the devil’s first temptation in Matthew 4:4?

options.text: He argued that barley bread tasted better than stone bread
He asked angels to deliver a basket of hot fish and unleavened bread
He quoted Scripture: "It is written: Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God"
He threw desert stones at Satan until the devil ran away

questions.correctAnswer: He quoted Scripture: "It is written: Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God"
questions.explanation: Jesus answered by quoting Deuteronomy 8:3: "It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’" Spiritual life and obedience to God take precedence over physical cravings.
questions.socraticHint: Which scripture from Deuteronomy taught that spiritual nourishment from God’s Word is greater than physical bread?

questions.prompt: In the second temptation, Satan placed Jesus on the highest point of the temple and urged Him to jump. How did Jesus respond (Matthew 4:7)?
questions.text: In the second temptation, Satan placed Jesus on the highest point of the temple and urged Him to jump. How did Jesus respond (Matthew 4:7)?

options.text: Let me put on wings first before jumping into the courtyard
I will jump if the Roman centurions catch me on their shields
I will only jump if you promise to worship God in heaven
It is also written: Do not put the Lord your God to the test

questions.correctAnswer: It is also written: Do not put the Lord your God to the test
questions.explanation: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 6:16: "It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’" Believers must not recklessly endanger themselves or manipulate God’s protection through presumption.
questions.socraticHint: What scriptural command forbids testing or daring God through foolish, presumptuous actions?

questions.prompt: In the third temptation, Satan showed Jesus all kingdoms of the world and offered them in exchange for worship. What was Jesus’ definitive response (Matthew 4:10)?
questions.text: In the third temptation, Satan showed Jesus all kingdoms of the world and offered them in exchange for worship. What was Jesus’ definitive response (Matthew 4:10)?

options.text: Away from me, Satan! For it is written: Worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only
Give me half the kingdoms first and I will think about your proposal tomorrow
I will worship you only if you make me the Emperor in Rome
Let us sign a treaty to divide power over the nations equally

questions.correctAnswer: Away from me, Satan! For it is written: Worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded: "Away from me, Satan! For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only’" (Deuteronomy 6:13). Worship belongs to God alone; worldly glory cannot buy a Christian’s allegiance.
questions.socraticHint: Which decisive rebuke commanded Satan to leave, reaffirming that God alone is worthy of worship?

questions.prompt: What spiritual weapon did Jesus consistently rely on to defeat every single temptation of the devil in the wilderness?
questions.text: What spiritual weapon did Jesus consistently rely on to defeat every single temptation of the devil in the wilderness?

options.text: Bribing the devil with bags of silver and gold
The written Word of God ("It is written...")
Physical wooden clubs and sharp bronze daggers
Calling Roman legionnaires to arrest the tempter

questions.correctAnswer: The written Word of God ("It is written...")
questions.explanation: In all three temptations, Jesus replied with "It is written," quoting God’s inspired Word. Ephesians 6:17 calls the Word of God "the sword of the Spirit," the ultimate weapon against evil.
questions.socraticHint: With what phrase did Jesus begin each of His three victorious answers to the tempter?

questions.prompt: A friend dares Kevin to climb onto a slippery water tank roof to prove he is not a coward. How can Kevin apply Jesus’ wilderness response to this dangerous dare?
questions.text: A friend dares Kevin to climb onto a slippery water tank roof to prove he is not a coward. How can Kevin apply Jesus’ wilderness response to this dangerous dare?

options.text: Tell his friend that he will only climb if they take photos to post on the internet
Push his friend up the tank first to see if the metal sheet breaks
Refuse firmly, remembering that scripture says "Do not put the Lord your God to the test" by taking foolish, dangerous risks
Climb the slippery roof quickly with eyes closed to show how much faith he has in guardian angels

questions.correctAnswer: Refuse firmly, remembering that scripture says "Do not put the Lord your God to the test" by taking foolish, dangerous risks
questions.explanation: Just as Jesus refused to jump from the temple roof to show off divine protection, Christian children should reject dangerous dares that put their lives and bodies at risk, knowing that testing God is wrong.
questions.socraticHint: Which scripture teaching about not putting God to the test helps someone reject reckless peer pressure?

questions.prompt: According to Hebrews 4:15, why is Jesus able to empathize completely with our human struggles when we face temptation?
questions.text: According to Hebrews 4:15, why is Jesus able to empathize completely with our human struggles when we face temptation?

options.text: Because He never lived as a real human and only watched humanity from afar
Because He gave in to temptation several times before becoming holy
Because temptation is an imaginary feeling that does not actually affect humans
Because He was tempted in every way, just as we are, yet He did not sin

questions.correctAnswer: Because He was tempted in every way, just as we are, yet He did not sin
questions.explanation: Hebrews 4:15 comforts believers: "For we do not have a high priest who is unable to empathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who has been tempted in every way, just as we are—yet he did not sin."
questions.socraticHint: Why can Jesus understand what it feels like to be tempted while remaining completely without sin?

questions.prompt: What happens immediately after the devil leaves Jesus at the conclusion of the wilderness temptation in Matthew 4:11?
questions.text: What happens immediately after the devil leaves Jesus at the conclusion of the wilderness temptation in Matthew 4:11?

options.text: Angels came and attended to (ministered to) Him
Jesus became angry and called down fire on the desert rocks
The Roman emperor Tiberius arrived on a golden chariot to congratulate Him
Jesus decided to cancel His public ministry and live in a cave

questions.correctAnswer: Angels came and attended to (ministered to) Him
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:11 states: "Then the devil left him, and angels came and attended to him." When we resist the devil with God’s Word, he flees (James 4:7), and God provides divine comfort and renewal.
questions.socraticHint: Who came to comfort, strengthen, and minister to Jesus once the devil departed from the wilderness?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: In Luke 7:1-10, what remarkable statement did the Roman centurion make that caused Jesus to marvel at his faith?
questions.text: In Luke 7:1-10, what remarkable statement did the Roman centurion make that caused Jesus to marvel at his faith?

options.text: My soldiers will arrest you if you do not walk to my palace immediately
Lord, I do not deserve to have you come under my roof. But say the word, and my servant will be healed
I will pay you fifty Roman silver coins if my servant recovers by evening
Build a Roman stone temple in Capernaum before performing this healing miracle

questions.correctAnswer: Lord, I do not deserve to have you come under my roof. But say the word, and my servant will be healed
questions.explanation: The centurion demonstrated profound humility and absolute trust in Jesus’ divine authority, recognizing that Jesus only needed to speak the word from afar to heal his paralyzed servant.
questions.socraticHint: Which humble words showed that the Roman officer believed Jesus could heal without physically entering his home?

questions.prompt: What was Jesus doing in the boat when a sudden furious windstorm struck Lake Galilee in Luke 8:23?
questions.text: What was Jesus doing in the boat when a sudden furious windstorm struck Lake Galilee in Luke 8:23?

options.text: He was throwing fish back into the water
He was preaching to crowds along the distant shore
He was rowing the oars with Peter

questions.explanation: Luke 8:23 notes that as they sailed, Jesus fell asleep. Even amidst torrential waves and howling wind, Jesus rested in complete peace and trust in the Father.
questions.socraticHint: What was Jesus doing in the stern of the boat that showed his perfect peace amidst the raging tempest?

questions.prompt: How did Jesus calm the wind and the turbulent waves on Lake Galilee in Luke 8:24?
questions.text: How did Jesus calm the wind and the turbulent waves on Lake Galilee in Luke 8:24?

options.text: He ordered the disciples to throw all heavy luggage into the lake
He jumped into the water and pushed the wooden boat ashore
He called for an emergency rescue boat from the Roman port
He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and the storm subsided into complete calm

questions.correctAnswer: He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and the storm subsided into complete calm
questions.explanation: Jesus got up, rebuked the wind and the raging waters; the storm ceased and all was calm. His divine authority over nature left the disciples asking, "Who is this? He commands even the winds and water, and they obey him!"
questions.socraticHint: By what spoken command did Jesus silence the stormy elements of nature?

questions.prompt: In John 6:9, what food did a generous young boy offer that Jesus used to feed the 5,000 men?
questions.text: In John 6:9, what food did a generous young boy offer that Jesus used to feed the 5,000 men?

options.text: Five small barley loaves and two small fish
Ten baskets of fresh wheat flour and roast lamb
Three bowls of wild honey and dried locusts
A sack of ripe pomegranates and dried figs

questions.correctAnswer: Five small barley loaves and two small fish
questions.explanation: Andrew brought forward a young boy who had five small barley loaves and two small fish. Jesus received this modest, selfless lunch, gave thanks to God, and multiplied it to satisfy thousands.
questions.socraticHint: Which small humble packed lunch consisting of bread and fish did the boy willingly share?

questions.prompt: How many baskets of leftover pieces did the disciples gather after all the people had eaten and were satisfied in John 6:13?
questions.text: How many baskets of leftover pieces did the disciples gather after all the people had eaten and were satisfied in John 6:13?

options.text: Zero baskets, everything was completely finished

questions.explanation: John 6:13 states that they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten, demonstrating God’s abundant provision and anti-waste stewardship.
questions.socraticHint: How many baskets—one for each of the twelve disciples—were filled with leftover food fragments?

questions.prompt: What moral lesson on sharing can Grade 5 pupils in Kenya learn from the young boy with five loaves and two fish?
questions.text: What moral lesson on sharing can Grade 5 pupils in Kenya learn from the young boy with five loaves and two fish?

options.text: Only rich business owners have enough wealth to do charity work in church
It is foolish to share food with others unless they pay you money in advance
Even our smallest resources or talents, when shared selflessly with Christ, can bring blessing to many people
Children should hide their packed snacks in school bags so nobody asks for a bite

questions.correctAnswer: Even our smallest resources or talents, when shared selflessly with Christ, can bring blessing to many people
questions.explanation: The boy’s willingness to surrender his lunch shows that no contribution is too small for God. When we generously share what we have, God multiplies it to bless our community.
questions.socraticHint: How does surrendering whatever small lunch or gift you have into God’s hands multiply its impact?

questions.prompt: In Mark 10:46-52, how did blind Bartimaeus show persistent faith when people told him to be quiet outside Jericho?
questions.text: In Mark 10:46-52, how did blind Bartimaeus show persistent faith when people told him to be quiet outside Jericho?

options.text: He kept quiet, sat down in the dust, and cried softly to himself
He threw stones at the crowd to make them run away
He walked away to ask the Roman soldiers for gold coins
He shouted all the more: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

questions.correctAnswer: He shouted all the more: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
questions.explanation: Mark 10:48 records that many rebuked Bartimaeus and told him to be quiet, but he shouted all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!" Jesus stopped, called him, and restored his sight because of his persistent faith.
questions.socraticHint: Did Bartimaeus give up when discouraged by the crowd, or did he cry out even louder to Jesus?

questions.prompt: What did Jesus do before distributing the five loaves and two fish to the crowd, demonstrating gratitude to God (John 6:11)?
questions.text: What did Jesus do before distributing the five loaves and two fish to the crowd, demonstrating gratitude to God (John 6:11)?

options.text: He gave thanks to God (offered a prayer of thanksgiving)
He counted the exact number of people to ensure there was enough
He asked the Roman soldiers to verify the freshness of the fish
He charged everyone one copper coin before handing out bread

questions.correctAnswer: He gave thanks to God (offered a prayer of thanksgiving)
questions.explanation: John 6:11 states: "Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted." Giving thanks before meals acknowledges God as the provider of daily bread.
questions.socraticHint: What holy prayer of gratitude did Jesus say before breaking the loaves?

questions.prompt: When Jairus was told his 12-year-old daughter had already died (Luke 8:49-50), what comforting words of faith did Jesus give him?
questions.text: When Jairus was told his 12-year-old daughter had already died (Luke 8:49-50), what comforting words of faith did Jesus give him?

options.text: I cannot help you because you are a synagogue ruler
Don’t be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed
It is too late, you should have come to me yesterday
Go and hire professional mourners to weep at your house

questions.correctAnswer: Don’t be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed
questions.explanation: Jesus said to Jairus: "Don’t be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed." Jesus went to the house, took the child by the hand, and called out, "My child, get up!" and her spirit returned.
questions.socraticHint: Which encouraging words urged the grieving father to replace fear with trusting belief?

questions.prompt: A learner named Faith is anxious and terrified before sitting her national CBE assessments. How does Jesus calming the storm comfort her?
questions.text: A learner named Faith is anxious and terrified before sitting her national CBE assessments. How does Jesus calming the storm comfort her?

options.text: She assumes the test papers will magically fill themselves with correct answers
She decides to skip school on exam day because life is too stormy
She realizes that Jesus is present in life’s stormy anxieties and can bring His calm peace to her troubled heart
She decides that praying is an alternative to studying her class revision notes

questions.correctAnswer: She realizes that Jesus is present in life’s stormy anxieties and can bring His calm peace to her troubled heart
questions.explanation: Jesus’ power over storms reminds believers that when fear, anxiety, and pressure overwhelm us, bringing our fears to Christ in prayer brings divine peace and inner calm (Philippians 4:6-7).
questions.socraticHint: How does trusting in Jesus’ presence help calm internal storms of fear and anxiety in difficult moments?

questions.prompt: Why did Jesus perform miracles during His earthly ministry, according to biblical revelation?
questions.text: Why did Jesus perform miracles during His earthly ministry, according to biblical revelation?

options.text: To become wealthy by charging expensive entrance fees to watch supernatural signs
To entertain curious spectators and show magicians that He was superior
To establish an earthly political kingdom that would overthrow the Roman senate
To reveal God’s compassionate love, alleviate human suffering, and prove His divine authority as Messiah

questions.correctAnswer: To reveal God’s compassionate love, alleviate human suffering, and prove His divine authority as Messiah
questions.explanation: Jesus’ miracles were signs (semeia) of the Kingdom of God, demonstrating God’s boundless compassion, healing broken humanity, and authenticating His mission as the promised Son of God.
questions.socraticHint: What deeper theological purposes of divine compassion and kingdom revelation motivated Jesus’ works?

questions.prompt: In John 6:12, after feeding the 5,000, why did Jesus instruct disciples to gather the leftovers saying "Let nothing be wasted"?
questions.text: In John 6:12, after feeding the 5,000, why did Jesus instruct disciples to gather the leftovers saying "Let nothing be wasted"?

options.text: To model responsible stewardship of resources and show respect for God’s provision
Because they wanted to sell the stale bread to travelers for a profit
Because the Roman police would fine them for leaving breadcrumbs on grass
Because the fish bones were needed to construct fishing hooks

questions.correctAnswer: To model responsible stewardship of resources and show respect for God’s provision
questions.explanation: Jesus’ command to gather leftovers so that "nothing is wasted" teaches prudent stewardship, avoiding food wastage, and honoring God’s provision even in times of miraculous abundance.
questions.socraticHint: What Christian value of avoiding waste and stewarding food carefully is taught by gathering leftovers?

questions.prompt: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37), which two religious figures walked past the wounded traveler on the other side of the road?
questions.text: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37), which two religious figures walked past the wounded traveler on the other side of the road?

options.text: A Roman soldier and a Greek philosopher

questions.explanation: Luke 10:31-32 describes a priest traveling down the road who saw the wounded man and passed by on the other side, followed by a Levite who did the same.
questions.socraticHint: Which two temple officials from the religious hierarchy failed to help the wounded traveler?

questions.prompt: How did the Samaritan show practical mercy and love to the wounded victim on the dangerous road from Jerusalem to Jericho?
questions.text: How did the Samaritan show practical mercy and love to the wounded victim on the dangerous road from Jerusalem to Jericho?

options.text: He took pictures of the crime scene to report to the Roman garrison next week
He blamed the victim for traveling without bodyguards and hurried past
He bandaged his wounds with oil and wine, put him on his own donkey, took him to an inn, and paid for his ongoing care
He searched the traveler’s pockets for money and left him in the sun

questions.correctAnswer: He bandaged his wounds with oil and wine, put him on his own donkey, took him to an inn, and paid for his ongoing care
questions.explanation: The Samaritan went to him, bandaged his wounds pouring on oil and wine, put the man on his own donkey, brought him to an inn, took care of him, and gave two silver denarii to the innkeeper.
questions.socraticHint: Which compassionate actions provided immediate medical first aid, transport, lodging, and full payment?

questions.prompt: Why was it particularly shocking to Jesus’ Jewish listeners that a Samaritan was the hero of the story?
questions.text: Why was it particularly shocking to Jesus’ Jewish listeners that a Samaritan was the hero of the story?

options.text: Samaritans were forbidden by law from riding donkeys across Israel
Samaritans were famous for being the wealthiest merchants in the Roman Empire
The Samaritan had forgotten to pay taxes to the Roman governor
Jews and Samaritans harbored deep historical hostility and ethnic prejudice toward each other

questions.correctAnswer: Jews and Samaritans harbored deep historical hostility and ethnic prejudice toward each other
questions.explanation: In first-century Palestine, Jews and Samaritans had intense ethnic and religious animosity (John 4:9). By making the despised Samaritan the hero of mercy, Jesus broke down ethnic barriers to show true neighborliness.
questions.socraticHint: What deep-seated ethnic and religious rivalry existed between Jews and Samaritans at that time?

questions.prompt: According to Jesus’ conclusion in the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who is our "neighbor"?
questions.text: According to Jesus’ conclusion in the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who is our "neighbor"?

options.text: Anyone in need to whom we can show compassion and mercy, regardless of their ethnic group or background
Only people who live in the house next door to our fence
Only relatives who speak the exact same mother tongue as our parents
Only wealthy people who are able to repay our favors with gifts

questions.correctAnswer: Anyone in need to whom we can show compassion and mercy, regardless of their ethnic group or background
questions.explanation: Jesus redefined "neighbor" from a narrow tribal or geographical boundary to a universal moral call: anyone who needs help, love, or mercy is our neighbor, and we must love them as ourselves.
questions.socraticHint: Does Christian neighborliness stop at ethnic boundaries or extend to anyone who needs help and compassion?

questions.prompt: In Luke 15:3-7, what does the shepherd do when one of his one hundred sheep wanders away and is lost?
questions.text: In Luke 15:3-7, what does the shepherd do when one of his one hundred sheep wanders away and is lost?

options.text: He punishes the flock by locking them in a dark cave without grass
He leaves the ninety-nine in the open country and goes after the lost sheep until he finds it
He forgets about the lost sheep because losing one percent is normal in business
He sells the remaining ninety-nine sheep to buy wild goats instead

questions.correctAnswer: He leaves the ninety-nine in the open country and goes after the lost sheep until he finds it
questions.explanation: Luke 15:4 records: "Doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost sheep until he finds it?" When he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders and calls friends to celebrate.
questions.socraticHint: What persistent search does the loving shepherd conduct to rescue the single stray sheep?

questions.prompt: What spiritual truth did Jesus explain regarding the rejoicing over the found sheep in Luke 15:7?
questions.text: What spiritual truth did Jesus explain regarding the rejoicing over the found sheep in Luke 15:7?

options.text: God prefers large herds of animals over individual human beings
Repentance is only necessary for people who commit major civil crimes
There is more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need to repent
Shepherds should always charge money before rescuing animals from cliffs

questions.correctAnswer: There is more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need to repent
questions.explanation: In Luke 15:7, Jesus reveals the heart of God: "I tell you that in the same way there will be more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need to repent."
questions.socraticHint: How does heaven react when a single lost person repents and turns back to God?

questions.prompt: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), what did the servant who received five talents do with his master’s money?
questions.text: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), what did the servant who received five talents do with his master’s money?

options.text: He buried the five talents in a hole in the ground to keep them safe from thieves
He spent all five talents on luxury robes and feast parties with friends
He gave the money away to traveling magicians in Babylon
He went at once and put his money to work and gained five more talents

questions.correctAnswer: He went at once and put his money to work and gained five more talents
questions.explanation: The servant who received five talents went immediately, put his money to work, and gained five more (Matthew 25:16), displaying industrious stewardship and faithfulness.
questions.socraticHint: Did the first servant invest his money diligently to double it, or hide it in the dirt?

questions.prompt: Why was the master angry with the servant who received one talent in Matthew 25:24-28?
questions.text: Why was the master angry with the servant who received one talent in Matthew 25:24-28?

options.text: Because out of fear and laziness, he dug a hole in the ground and hid his talent, producing zero return
Because he lost all the money in an unsuccessful grain trading venture
Because he donated all the master’s coins to poor widows in Jerusalem
Because he demanded to be paid higher wages before starting work

questions.correctAnswer: Because out of fear and laziness, he dug a hole in the ground and hid his talent, producing zero return
questions.explanation: The third servant was condemned as "wicked and lazy" because he allowed fear and sloth to paralyze him, burying his talent rather than putting it to fruitful use for the master.
questions.socraticHint: What did the third servant foolishly do with his talent instead of investing it productively?

questions.prompt: What commendation did the master give to both the faithful servants in Matthew 25:21?
questions.text: What commendation did the master give to both the faithful servants in Matthew 25:21?

options.text: You are now permitted to retire and never do any work for the rest of your life
Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master’s happiness!
You should have worked even harder to triple the profits instead of doubling them
Give all the profits back to me immediately and go back to being ordinary slaves

questions.correctAnswer: Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master’s happiness!
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:21 records the joyous praise: "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master’s happiness!"
questions.socraticHint: Which famous blessing begins with "Well done, good and faithful servant"?

questions.prompt: At a primary school in Eldoret, learners see an elderly woman trip and drop her basket of vegetables across the road. How can they apply the Parable of the Good Samaritan?
questions.text: At a primary school in Eldoret, learners see an elderly woman trip and drop her basket of vegetables across the road. How can they apply the Parable of the Good Samaritan?

options.text: Kick the spilled cabbages and carrots into the roadside drainage ditch
Walk past pretending not to see because she is not a relative from their clan
Stop immediately, help her up gently, collect her scattered vegetables, and escort her safely across the road
Laugh loudly with classmates and run to the canteen to buy mandazis

questions.correctAnswer: Stop immediately, help her up gently, collect her scattered vegetables, and escort her safely across the road
questions.explanation: The Good Samaritan models active, compassionate empathy that stops what it is doing to help anyone in distress, regardless of who they are.
questions.socraticHint: What immediate kind action provides respectful help to an elderly person in distress?

questions.prompt: How does the Parable of the Talents apply to a Kenyan student who has a natural gift for drawing, singing, or mathematics?
questions.text: How does the Parable of the Talents apply to a Kenyan student who has a natural gift for drawing, singing, or mathematics?

options.text: They should boast about their superiority and refuse to participate in school events
They should hide their ability so that classmates never ask them for assistance
They should demand money before singing in the school choir or drawing posters
They should practice diligently, develop their gift, and use it to glorify God and serve others, rather than hiding it

questions.correctAnswer: They should practice diligently, develop their gift, and use it to glorify God and serve others, rather than hiding it
questions.explanation: God endows each person with unique abilities and talents. Christian stewardship requires us to cultivate, polish, and deploy those gifts to serve our community and honor God.
questions.socraticHint: What should a learner do with God-given talents according to the master’s expectations in the parable?

questions.prompt: What common theological thread links the Good Samaritan, the Lost Sheep, and the Talents parables?
questions.text: What common theological thread links the Good Samaritan, the Lost Sheep, and the Talents parables?

options.text: God’s unconditional love demands active, compassionate response and accountable stewardship in our daily lives
Believers should avoid interacting with anyone who does not belong to their specific denomination
Material wealth is the ultimate sign of divine favor in the Kingdom of Heaven
God expects humans to solve all problems through strict military discipline

questions.correctAnswer: God’s unconditional love demands active, compassionate response and accountable stewardship in our daily lives
questions.explanation: All three parables emphasize that receiving God’s grace and love carries a responsibility: we must love our neighbors unconditionally, value every lost soul, and faithfully use what God has entrusted to us.
questions.socraticHint: How do all three parables call believers to active compassion, radical inclusion, and faithful responsibility?

questions.prompt: On which animal did Jesus ride into Jerusalem during His Triumphal Entry on Palm Sunday (Luke 19:35)?
questions.text: On which animal did Jesus ride into Jerusalem during His Triumphal Entry on Palm Sunday (Luke 19:35)?

options.text: A ceremonial white bull from Mount Zion
A desert camel with purple silk saddles

questions.explanation: Luke 19:35 and Matthew 21:5 record Jesus riding a donkey colt, fulfilling the messianic prophecy of Zechariah 9:9: "See, your king comes to you, righteous and victorious, lowly and riding on a donkey."
questions.socraticHint: Which humble beast of burden did Jesus ride to symbolize peace rather than military conquest?

questions.prompt: How did the crowd welcome Jesus as He entered Jerusalem on Palm Sunday (Luke 19:36-38)?
questions.text: How did the crowd welcome Jesus as He entered Jerusalem on Palm Sunday (Luke 19:36-38)?

options.text: They locked the city gates and demanded a toll tax before letting Him pass
They stood completely silent and covered their faces with black cloths
They spread their cloaks on the road, waved palm branches, and shouted: "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!"
They threw stones at the donkey and told Jesus to return to Galilee

questions.correctAnswer: They spread their cloaks on the road, waved palm branches, and shouted: "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!"
questions.explanation: The crowds celebrated Jesus enthusiastically, spreading cloaks and leafy branches along the road while singing: "Hosanna! Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"
questions.socraticHint: What joyful gestures with garments, branches, and shouts of praise greeted Jesus?

questions.prompt: In John 13:4-15, what humble act of service did Jesus perform for His disciples before the Last Supper?
questions.text: In John 13:4-15, what humble act of service did Jesus perform for His disciples before the Last Supper?

options.text: He made them bow down and kiss His royal ring
He hired servants to carry them on golden chairs into the upper room
He commanded Peter to prepare a silver crown for Him
He washed the disciples’ feet with water and dried them with a towel

questions.correctAnswer: He washed the disciples’ feet with water and dried them with a towel
questions.explanation: Jesus took a towel, poured water into a basin, and washed His disciples’ feet, saying: "Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet. I have set you an example."
questions.socraticHint: Which menial servant chore did the Master perform to model humility and servant leadership?

questions.prompt: What did the bread and the cup of wine represent when Jesus instituted Holy Communion at the Last Supper (Luke 22:19-20)?
questions.text: What did the bread and the cup of wine represent when Jesus instituted Holy Communion at the Last Supper (Luke 22:19-20)?

options.text: The bread represented His body given for us; the cup represented the new covenant in His blood poured out for forgiveness
The bread represented the physical soil of Judea; the wine represented water from the River Jordan
The bread represented the gold coins of the temple; the wine represented grape juice for celebration feasts
The bread represented Moses’ manna; the wine represented ancient Egyptian rivers

questions.correctAnswer: The bread represented His body given for us; the cup represented the new covenant in His blood poured out for forgiveness
questions.explanation: Jesus said of the bread: "This is my body given for you; do this in remembrance of me." And of the cup: "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you."
questions.socraticHint: What did Jesus say the broken bread and poured cup symbolized regarding His coming sacrifice?

questions.prompt: In which garden on the Mount of Olives did Jesus pray in deep agony before His arrest (Luke 22:39-44)?
questions.text: In which garden on the Mount of Olives did Jesus pray in deep agony before His arrest (Luke 22:39-44)?
questions.explanation: Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives to the Garden of Gethsemane, an olive grove where He poured out His soul in prayer to the Father.
questions.socraticHint: Which historic olive grove garden was the scene of Jesus’ midnight prayer and agony?

questions.prompt: What profound prayer of complete surrender and obedience did Jesus pray in Gethsemane (Luke 22:42)?
questions.text: What profound prayer of complete surrender and obedience did Jesus pray in Gethsemane (Luke 22:42)?

options.text: Father, make me the earthly king of Israel so I can punish the Sanhedrin elders
Father, cancel the salvation of humanity because the suffering is too difficult
Father, if you are willing, take this cup from me; yet not my will, but yours be done
Father, strike down all Roman soldiers with fire from heaven immediately

questions.correctAnswer: Father, if you are willing, take this cup from me; yet not my will, but yours be done
questions.explanation: Jesus’ prayer—"Yet not my will, but yours be done"—embodies supreme submission to the Father’s redemptive purpose, placing God’s will above personal comfort or human dread of pain.
questions.socraticHint: Which famous sentence surrendered Jesus’ human desire to the Father’s divine will?

questions.prompt: Which disciple betrayed Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane with a kiss (Luke 22:47-48)?
questions.text: Which disciple betrayed Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane with a kiss (Luke 22:47-48)?
questions.explanation: Judas Iscariot guided the armed crowd from the chief priests and betrayed Jesus with a hypocritical greeting and kiss in exchange for thirty pieces of silver.
questions.socraticHint: Which disciple turned against Jesus for thirty pieces of silver and identified Him with a kiss?

questions.prompt: When Peter drew a sword and cut off the right ear of the high priest’s servant Malchus, how did Jesus respond (Luke 22:50-51)?
questions.text: When Peter drew a sword and cut off the right ear of the high priest’s servant Malchus, how did Jesus respond (Luke 22:50-51)?

options.text: He commanded Peter to stop, touched the servant’s ear, and healed him
He praised Peter and encouraged the other disciples to draw weapons as well
He ordered the disciples to flee into the olive trees and leave the servant bleeding
He took the sword and challenged the temple guards to a duel

questions.correctAnswer: He commanded Peter to stop, touched the servant’s ear, and healed him
questions.explanation: Jesus said: "No more of this!" He touched Malchus’ ear and healed him. Jesus rejected physical violence, living out His teaching to love our enemies even during His unjust arrest.
questions.socraticHint: How did Jesus respond with peace and immediate healing rather than violence?

questions.prompt: How many times did Simon Peter deny knowing Jesus before the rooster crowed, just as Jesus had predicted (Luke 22:54-62)?
questions.text: How many times did Simon Peter deny knowing Jesus before the rooster crowed, just as Jesus had predicted (Luke 22:54-62)?
questions.explanation: Peter denied knowing Jesus three times in the courtyard of the high priest. When the rooster crowed, the Lord turned and looked at Peter, and Peter went outside and wept bitterly in deep repentance.
questions.socraticHint: How many times did Peter claim, "I do not know Him," before hearing the morning bird crow?

questions.prompt: How can Kenyan primary school leaders emulate Jesus washing the disciples’ feet in their school duties?
questions.text: How can Kenyan primary school leaders emulate Jesus washing the disciples’ feet in their school duties?

options.text: By refusing to participate in any manual work during communal school cleanup days
By taking the best sports equipment for themselves while denying others a turn
By serving fellow students with humility, assisting in class cleaning, and listening with patience and respect
By commanding younger students to carry their school bags and polish their shoes

questions.correctAnswer: By serving fellow students with humility, assisting in class cleaning, and listening with patience and respect
questions.explanation: Servant leadership means using authority to uplift, support, and serve others. Emulating Christ means demonstrating humility through helpful practical deeds rather than seeking special privileges.
questions.socraticHint: How does true Christian leadership show itself through humble service and shared labor?

questions.prompt: Why did Jesus wash His disciples’ feet, an act usually performed only by household slaves?
questions.text: Why did Jesus wash His disciples’ feet, an act usually performed only by household slaves?

options.text: Because the upper room in Jerusalem had no clean towels for eating supper
Because the disciples had walked through the muddy River Jordan that afternoon
To prove that religious leaders should never speak or teach in public synagogues
To provide an unforgettable living object lesson on humility, selflessness, and servant leadership

questions.correctAnswer: To provide an unforgettable living object lesson on humility, selflessness, and servant leadership
questions.explanation: Jesus deliberately took the role of the lowest household slave to overturn worldly concepts of status and power, teaching that in God’s kingdom, the greatest must become the servant of all.
questions.socraticHint: What revolutionary kingdom lesson about true greatness through humble service did Jesus illustrate?

questions.prompt: When facing peer pressure or difficult trials, how can praying "Yet not my will, but yours be done" strengthen a Christian learner?
questions.text: When facing peer pressure or difficult trials, how can praying "Yet not my will, but yours be done" strengthen a Christian learner?

options.text: It aligns our desires with God’s righteous purpose, giving us moral strength and courage to resist wrong choices
It allows us to blame God whenever we fail an exam or make a bad decision
It guarantees that we will never have to face any homework challenges at school
It removes all need to make personal ethical decisions because everything happens automatically

questions.correctAnswer: It aligns our desires with God’s righteous purpose, giving us moral strength and courage to resist wrong choices
questions.explanation: Surrendering to God’s will replaces selfish anxiety with divine peace and moral clarity, empowering believers to stand firm for what is right even when pressured to compromise.
questions.socraticHint: How does yielding our will to God give us spiritual courage and clarity during moral tests?

questions.prompt: What extraordinary prayer of divine forgiveness did Jesus speak from the Cross for His executioners (Luke 23:34)?
questions.text: What extraordinary prayer of divine forgiveness did Jesus speak from the Cross for His executioners (Luke 23:34)?

options.text: Father, remember my suffering and take away their land forever
Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing
Father, send ten legions of angels to destroy this city of Jerusalem
Father, punish their children for the agony they are causing me

questions.correctAnswer: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing
questions.explanation: From the Cross, Jesus prayed: "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." In the ultimate display of divine agape love, Jesus forgave those who mocked, tortured, and crucified Him.
questions.socraticHint: Which unforgettable prayer for His persecutors revealed Jesus’ unmatched mercy and forgiveness?

questions.prompt: What did Jesus promise the repentant criminal crucified beside Him who asked to be remembered in Jesus’ Kingdom (Luke 23:42-43)?
questions.text: What did Jesus promise the repentant criminal crucified beside Him who asked to be remembered in Jesus’ Kingdom (Luke 23:42-43)?

options.text: Wait in the tomb for one thousand years before entering heaven
If you pay thirty silver coins to the temple, you might be saved
Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise
You are too wicked to receive any forgiveness from God

questions.correctAnswer: Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise
questions.explanation: Jesus answered the repentant thief: "Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise." This shows that God’s mercy is available to anyone who repents in genuine faith, even at life’s final moment.
questions.socraticHint: What glorious promise of immediate fellowship in paradise did Jesus give to the repentant thief?

questions.prompt: What miraculous event occurred in the Jerusalem temple the moment Jesus breathed His last on the Cross (Matthew 27:51)?
questions.text: What miraculous event occurred in the Jerusalem temple the moment Jesus breathed His last on the Cross (Matthew 27:51)?

options.text: All the gold lampstands melted into liquid metal
The stone pillars collapsed and crushed the altar
A river of water gushed out from the temple foundation
The temple curtain tore in two from top to bottom

questions.correctAnswer: The temple curtain tore in two from top to bottom
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:51 records that the temple curtain tore in two from top to bottom, symbolizing that Christ’s death opened the way into God’s holy presence for all people, without the need for animal sacrifices.
questions.socraticHint: What sacred divider in the temple was supernaturally ripped in two from top to bottom?

questions.prompt: Who boldly requested the body of Jesus from Pontius Pilate and buried Him in his own new rock-cut tomb (Luke 23:50-53)?
questions.text: Who boldly requested the body of Jesus from Pontius Pilate and buried Him in his own new rock-cut tomb (Luke 23:50-53)?
questions.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council who had not consented to their decision, went to Pilate, asked for Jesus’ body, wrapped it in linen cloth, and laid it in a new rock-cut tomb.
questions.socraticHint: Which wealthy council member from Arimathea donated his own new tomb for Jesus’ burial?

questions.prompt: When godly women visited the tomb early on the third day (Easter Sunday), what joyful question did the angels ask them (Luke 24:5)?
questions.text: When godly women visited the tomb early on the third day (Easter Sunday), what joyful question did the angels ask them (Luke 24:5)?

options.text: Who gave you permission to roll away the Roman seal from the entrance?
Why do you look for the living among the dead? He is not here; He has risen!
Why have you brought olive oil and myrrh when the Roman guards are sleeping?
Did you not know that tombs are locked until Monday morning?

questions.correctAnswer: Why do you look for the living among the dead? He is not here; He has risen!
questions.explanation: In Luke 24:5-6, the angels asked: "Why do you look for the living among the dead? He is not here; he has risen! Remember how he told you, while he was still with you in Galilee."
questions.socraticHint: Which unforgettable angelic greeting announced that Jesus had conquered death and was alive?

questions.prompt: On the road to Emmaus, when were the eyes of the two disciples finally opened to recognize the risen Jesus (Luke 24:30-31)?
questions.text: On the road to Emmaus, when were the eyes of the two disciples finally opened to recognize the risen Jesus (Luke 24:30-31)?

options.text: When they reached the town gate of Emmaus and heard a rooster crowing
When He pointed out the distant hills of Galilee across the valley
When He sat at the table, took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and began giving it to them
When He showed them a Roman passport with His name inscribed on it

questions.correctAnswer: When He sat at the table, took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and began giving it to them
questions.explanation: Luke 24:30-31 records that when Jesus was at the table with them, He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and began to give it to them. Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Him, and He disappeared from their sight.
questions.socraticHint: In what familiar Eucharistic action of taking, blessing, and breaking bread was Jesus recognized?

questions.prompt: What did the risen Jesus say to disciple Thomas, who doubted Jesus’ resurrection until he saw the nail marks (John 20:29)?
questions.text: What did the risen Jesus say to disciple Thomas, who doubted Jesus’ resurrection until he saw the nail marks (John 20:29)?

options.text: You are no longer an apostle because you asked too many difficult questions
True believers must never require any evidence or witness before believing
Go and live in isolation until you learn how to believe without seeing
Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed

questions.correctAnswer: Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed
questions.explanation: Jesus invited Thomas to touch His wounds and declared: "Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed." This blesses all subsequent believers who trust in Christ through faith.
questions.socraticHint: Which blessing did Jesus speak upon all future generations who believe without physical sight?

questions.prompt: What core mission did Jesus give to His followers in the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20)?
questions.text: What core mission did Jesus give to His followers in the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20)?

options.text: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything He commanded
Conquer foreign kingdoms by force and establish military rule in Rome
Collect gold and silver from all temples to construct magnificent marble cathedrals
Keep the teachings of Jesus completely secret within the borders of Israel

questions.correctAnswer: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything He commanded
questions.explanation: The Great Commission directs Christians worldwide to make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Triune God and teaching them to observe Christ’s commands, with the promise: "I am with you always, to the very end of the age."
questions.socraticHint: What worldwide mandate to preach the gospel, make disciples, baptize, and teach did Jesus give?

questions.prompt: What comforting promise did Jesus give at the conclusion of the Great Commission in Matthew 28:20?
questions.text: What comforting promise did Jesus give at the conclusion of the Great Commission in Matthew 28:20?

options.text: The work of spreading the Gospel will be finished in three weeks
And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age
You will never encounter any opposition or persecution anywhere in the world
All believers will receive crowns of gold made by Roman goldsmiths

questions.correctAnswer: And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age
questions.explanation: Jesus promised His perpetual presence: "And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age." Believers never carry out God’s mission alone; Christ’s presence and power abide with them continually.
questions.socraticHint: What enduring promise of His unfailing presence did Jesus give to His disciples?

questions.prompt: When someone falsely accuses John at school, how can John reflect Jesus’ response on the Cross at Golgotha?
questions.text: When falsely accuses John at school, how can John reflect Jesus’ response on the Cross at Golgotha?

options.text: Spread false, damaging rumors about the accuser’s family to retaliate
Steal the accuser’s school textbooks and throw them in the river
Choose forgiveness over revenge, speak truth with calm gentleness, and pray for those who hurt him
Fight the accuser behind the school latrines after class dismissed

questions.correctAnswer: Choose forgiveness over revenge, speak truth with calm gentleness, and pray for those who hurt him
questions.explanation: Jesus demonstrated supreme forgiveness on the Cross, praying for His executioners. Following Christ means renouncing retaliation, extending forgiveness, and speaking the truth in love.
questions.socraticHint: How does forgiving and praying for someone who wronged you reflect Christ’s example at Golgotha?

questions.prompt: Why is the resurrection of Jesus Christ considered the foundation of Christian faith and hope (1 Corinthians 15:14-20)?
questions.text: Why is the resurrection of Jesus Christ considered the foundation of Christian faith and hope (1 Corinthians 15:14-20)?

options.text: It showed that human bodies are completely unimportant in God’s design
It proved that the Roman Empire was the most righteous government in history
It meant that disciples no longer had to pray or read the Holy Scriptures
It conquered sin and death, proved Jesus is the true Son of God, and guarantees eternal life for all who believe

questions.correctAnswer: It conquered sin and death, proved Jesus is the true Son of God, and guarantees eternal life for all who believe
questions.explanation: As Paul wrote in 1 Corinthians 15, if Christ has not been raised, our faith is futile. The resurrection validates Christ’s victory over death and sin, giving believers hope for their own resurrection and eternal life.
questions.socraticHint: How does Christ’s bodily triumph over death authenticate the entire Christian faith and promise of eternal life?

questions.prompt: From which mountain outside Jerusalem did Jesus ascend bodily into heaven forty days after His resurrection (Acts 1:9-12)?
questions.text: From which mountain outside Jerusalem did Jesus ascend bodily into heaven forty days after His resurrection (Acts 1:9-12)?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:9-12 records that after blessing His disciples, Jesus was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid Him from their sight. They returned to Jerusalem from the hill called the Mount of Olives.
questions.socraticHint: From which olive-covered hill east of Jerusalem was Jesus taken up into heaven in the presence of the disciples?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What miraculous signs accompanied the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Day of Pentecost in Acts 2:2-3?
questions.text: What miraculous signs accompanied the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Day of Pentecost in Acts 2:2-3?

options.text: An angelic choir singing from the top of the Roman fortress
A sound like the blowing of a violent wind and tongues that looked like fire resting on each of them
A violent earthquake that flattened the walls of the temple
A torrential rainstorm that flooded the lower streets of Jerusalem

questions.correctAnswer: A sound like the blowing of a violent wind and tongues that looked like fire resting on each of them
questions.explanation: Acts 2:2-3 describes a sound like the rush of a violent wind filling the house, and tongues as of fire appearing, separating, and resting on each believer.
questions.socraticHint: Which sensory signs of rushing wind and fiery tongues marked the arrival of the Holy Spirit?

questions.prompt: How did the Holy Spirit empower the disciples immediately after filling them in Acts 2:4?
questions.text: How did the Holy Spirit empower the disciples immediately after filling them in Acts 2:4?

options.text: They were able to turn ordinary stones into silver denarii
They became invisible to all Roman soldiers in Jerusalem
They began to speak in other tongues (languages) as the Spirit enabled them
They grew physical wings and flew over the Mount of Olives

questions.correctAnswer: They began to speak in other tongues (languages) as the Spirit enabled them
questions.explanation: Acts 2:4 states: "All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them," proclaiming God’s wonders in foreign languages they had never learned.
questions.socraticHint: What miraculous ability to proclaim God’s wonders in diverse languages did the disciples receive?

questions.prompt: Why were the visiting Jews from various nations amazed and bewildered in Acts 2:7-11?
questions.text: Why were the visiting Jews from various nations amazed and bewildered in Acts 2:7-11?

options.text: They saw the disciples wearing expensive royal purple robes from Greece
The disciples offered them free gold coins from the Roman treasury
The temple gates had been miraculously moved into the desert
They heard Galilean disciples declaring the wonders of God in their own native mother tongues

questions.correctAnswer: They heard Galilean disciples declaring the wonders of God in their own native mother tongues
questions.explanation: Pilgrims from Parthia, Media, Mesopotamia, Egypt, Rome, and elsewhere were bewildered because each one heard Galileans speaking in their own dialect and native tongue about the wonderful works of God.
questions.socraticHint: What amazed visitors from across the world when listening to Galilean speakers on Pentecost?

questions.prompt: Which Old Testament prophet’s promise did Peter quote to explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit in Acts 2:16-17?
questions.text: Which Old Testament prophet’s promise did Peter quote to explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit in Acts 2:16-17?

options.text: Prophet Joel ("In the last days, God says, I will pour out my Spirit on all people")
Prophet Jonah ("In three days Nineveh shall be overturned")
Prophet Elijah ("The god who answers by fire is God")
Prophet Daniel ("The kingdom of God shall stand forever")

questions.correctAnswer: Prophet Joel ("In the last days, God says, I will pour out my Spirit on all people")
questions.explanation: Peter explained that this fulfilled Joel 2:28-32: "In the last days, God says, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams."
questions.socraticHint: Which Old Testament prophet wrote that God would pour out His Spirit on all people in the last days?

questions.prompt: When the crowd was pierced to the heart by Peter’s sermon and asked what they should do, how did Peter instruct them in Acts 2:38?
questions.text: When the crowd was pierced to the heart by Peter’s sermon and asked what they should do, how did Peter instruct them in Acts 2:38?

options.text: Join the Roman imperial guard to enforce order in Judea
Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit
Pay fifty silver coins to the temple priests to purchase a certificate of salvation
Flee into the desert hills and never speak to anyone in Jerusalem again

questions.correctAnswer: Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Peter commanded: "Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit." Repentance and baptism are the doorway to new life in Christ.
questions.socraticHint: What twofold call to repentance and baptism did Peter give for the forgiveness of sins and the gift of the Spirit?

questions.prompt: How many people accepted Peter’s message and were baptized on that single Day of Pentecost (Acts 2:41)?
questions.text: How many people accepted Peter’s message and were baptized on that single Day of Pentecost (Acts 2:41)?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:41 records: "Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day."
questions.socraticHint: What large number of converts—about three thousand—marked the dramatic birth of the Early Church?

questions.prompt: How did the Holy Spirit transform Simon Peter from the fearful man who denied Jesus in the high priest’s courtyard?
questions.text: How did the Holy Spirit transform Simon Peter from the fearful man who denied Jesus in the high priest’s courtyard?

options.text: He became a quiet monk who refused to speak with anyone for the rest of his life
He joined the Roman army to acquire weapons and military protection
He moved to Rome to build a trade business buying and selling fishing boats
He became a bold, courageous preacher of the Gospel who fearlessly proclaimed Jesus before thousands in Jerusalem

questions.correctAnswer: He became a bold, courageous preacher of the Gospel who fearlessly proclaimed Jesus before thousands in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit replaced Peter’s fear and insecurity with boldness and power (Acts 1:8). The man who once cowered before a servant girl now stood before thousands proclaiming Christ without fear of arrest.
questions.socraticHint: What dramatic change from timid fear to fearless preaching did the Holy Spirit work in Peter’s life?

questions.prompt: In Acts 1:8, what core purpose did Jesus promise the Holy Spirit would accomplish in believers?
questions.text: In Acts 1:8, what core purpose did Jesus promise the Holy Spirit would accomplish in believers?

options.text: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth
You will receive the ability to turn dry sand into golden jewelry
You will never have to face physical illness or bodily tiredness
You will be appointed political governors over the Roman empire

questions.correctAnswer: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: Jesus declared: "You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth." The Holy Spirit empowers believers to witness for Christ.
questions.socraticHint: Which key verse promises divine power to be Christ’s witnesses across the entire earth?

questions.prompt: How can a Grade 5 pupil at school rely on the Holy Spirit when feeling shy or fearful about standing up for truth?
questions.text: How can a Grade 5 pupil at school rely on the Holy Spirit when feeling shy or fearful about standing up for truth?

options.text: Fight bullies physically with sticks on the playing field
Pray quietly for the Holy Spirit’s courage and wisdom to speak truth gently and do what is right
Pretend to agree with bullies so they do not mock you
Stay away from school whenever there is a moral challenge in class

questions.correctAnswer: Pray quietly for the Holy Spirit’s courage and wisdom to speak truth gently and do what is right
questions.explanation: Just as the Holy Spirit emboldened Peter, believers today can pray for the Spirit’s presence to grant moral courage, calmness, and wisdom to uphold truth and justice in school.
questions.socraticHint: How does praying for the Holy Spirit’s inner strength help a learner overcome fear and speak up for what is right?

questions.prompt: Why were the tongues of fire significant on the Day of Pentecost in Acts 2?
questions.text: Why were the tongues of fire significant on the Day of Pentecost in Acts 2?

options.text: Fire showed that God was going to burn down all the buildings in Jerusalem
It was a theatrical show designed to attract merchants from the marketplace
Fire symbolized God’s purifying holy presence and divine power resting upon each individual believer
The room was cold and needed heating from supernatural sparks

questions.correctAnswer: Fire symbolized God’s purifying holy presence and divine power resting upon each individual believer
questions.explanation: Throughout Scripture (like Moses’ burning bush and Mount Sinai), fire symbolizes God’s holiness, presence, and power. On Pentecost, tongues of fire resting on each person showed that God’s presence now indwells every believer.
questions.socraticHint: In biblical imagery, what divine qualities of holiness, purification, and divine power does fire represent?

questions.prompt: What was the immediate practical consequence of the baptism of the 3,000 believers in Jerusalem?
questions.text: What was the immediate practical consequence of the baptism of the 3,000 believers in Jerusalem?

options.text: The Roman emperor issued an immediate decree closing all Jewish synagogues
All 3,000 people immediately left their homes to live in mountain caves
The believers organized a political rebellion against the governor Pilate
A loving, united community of faith (the Church) was born that learned, worshiped, and shared resources together

questions.correctAnswer: A loving, united community of faith (the Church) was born that learned, worshiped, and shared resources together
questions.explanation: The baptism of 3,000 converts gave birth to the early Church, a vibrant community characterized by devotion to apostolic teaching, mutual fellowship, breaking of bread, and shared prayer (Acts 2:42).
questions.socraticHint: What new spiritual and communal family came into being when thousands were baptized into Christ?

questions.prompt: How does the universal language miracle at Pentecost reverse the ancient division caused at the Tower of Babel (Genesis 11)?
questions.text: How does the universal language miracle at Pentecost reverse the ancient division caused at the Tower of Babel (Genesis 11)?

options.text: At Babel human pride scattered nations through confused languages; at Pentecost the Holy Spirit united diverse nations through one Gospel understood by all
At Babel humans built stone altars while at Pentecost they tore down all brick buildings
At Babel people spoke Hebrew while at Pentecost everyone spoke only Latin
Pentecost proved that only one language should ever be spoken across the entire earth

questions.correctAnswer: At Babel human pride scattered nations through confused languages; at Pentecost the Holy Spirit united diverse nations through one Gospel understood by all
questions.explanation: At the Tower of Babel, human pride led to language confusion and dispersal. At Pentecost, the Holy Spirit brought unity, enabling people of every tongue to understand the wonderful works of God in Christ.
questions.socraticHint: How does the Holy Spirit’s uniting of diverse tongues heal the scattering and division that occurred at Babel?

questions.prompt: Which nine Christian virtues comprise the Fruit of the Holy Spirit in Galatians 5:22-23?
questions.text: Which nine Christian virtues comprise the Fruit of the Holy Spirit in Galatians 5:22-23?

options.text: Faith, Hope, Charity, Justice, Prudence, Temperance, Fortitude, Zeal, and Honor
Love, Joy, Peace, Patience, Kindness, Goodness, Faithfulness, Gentleness, and Self-control
Wealth, Honor, Fame, Strength, Speed, Pride, Anger, Ambition, and Courage
Gold, Frankincense, Myrrh, Bronze, Silver, Iron, Silk, Wool, and Linen

questions.correctAnswer: Love, Joy, Peace, Patience, Kindness, Goodness, Faithfulness, Gentleness, and Self-control
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:22-23 lists the ninefold fruit of the Spirit: "love, joy, peace, forbearance (patience), kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Against such things there is no law."
questions.socraticHint: Which list contains love, joy, peace, and ends with self-control as recorded in Galatians 5?

questions.prompt: What did the believers in the Early Church devote themselves to according to Acts 2:42?
questions.text: What did the believers in the Early Church devote themselves to according to Acts 2:42?

options.text: Building stone statues of the apostles across Judea
Arguing over who among them was the greatest disciple
The apostles’ teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayer
Military drills, political debates, and collecting taxes for Rome

questions.correctAnswer: The apostles’ teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayer
questions.explanation: Acts 2:42 outlines the four foundational pillars of early Christian communal life: "They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer."
questions.socraticHint: Which four essential spiritual practices formed the core of daily life in the early church?

questions.prompt: How did the early Christians demonstrate radical generosity toward those in need (Acts 2:44-45)?
questions.text: How did the early Christians demonstrate radical generosity toward those in need (Acts 2:44-45)?

options.text: They kept their wealth hidden in locked jars buried deep under their houses
They charged high interest rates when lending money to fellow Christians
They expelled poor members from the congregation so only wealthy believers remained
All the believers were together and had everything in common; they sold property and possessions to give to anyone in need

questions.correctAnswer: All the believers were together and had everything in common; they sold property and possessions to give to anyone in need
questions.explanation: Acts 2:44-45 records that early Christians had everything in common and sold possessions to meet the needs of all members, ensuring no one suffered from poverty in their community.
questions.socraticHint: How did early believers share property and possessions so that no one was left in lack?

questions.prompt: What was the generous act of Barnabas (Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus) recorded in Acts 4:36-37?
questions.text: What was the generous act of Barnabas (Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus) recorded in Acts 4:36-37?

options.text: He sold a field he owned, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet to help the needy
He built a large personal mansion in Antioch to host parties for governors
He bought a fleet of merchant ships to trade goods across the Mediterranean
He wrote a letter demanding that the apostles appoint him as their high priest

questions.correctAnswer: He sold a field he owned, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet to help the needy
questions.explanation: Barnabas (meaning "Son of Encouragement") sold a field he owned and brought the entire proceeds to the apostles to support vulnerable believers, modeling cheerful Christian philanthropy.
questions.socraticHint: What property did Barnabas sell to support the fellowship of believers in Jerusalem?

questions.prompt: In Acts 6:1-6, how did the early church resolve the complaint regarding unfair food distribution to Grecian widows?
questions.text: In Acts 6:1-6, how did the early church resolve the complaint regarding unfair food distribution to Grecian widows?

options.text: They asked the Roman police to supervise church lunch queues
They selected seven reputable men full of the Spirit and wisdom (deacons, including Stephen) to manage the food distribution fairly
The apostles stopped all food distribution and told the widows to fend for themselves
They expelled the Grecian believers from the church community

questions.correctAnswer: They selected seven reputable men full of the Spirit and wisdom (deacons, including Stephen) to manage the food distribution fairly
questions.explanation: The community chose seven Spirit-filled men of good reputation (deacons) to oversee the daily food distribution, ensuring equity and allowing the apostles to focus on prayer and preaching.
questions.socraticHint: How did appointing seven wise, Spirit-filled men solve the food distribution dispute peacefully and fairly?

questions.prompt: What does 1 Corinthians 12 teach about how different spiritual gifts should function within the Body of Christ?
questions.text: What does 1 Corinthians 12 teach about how different spiritual gifts should function within the Body of Christ?

options.text: Gifts should be used to boast and compete with fellow church members to see who is superior
Believers should hide their spiritual gifts so that others do not ask for help
Just as a human body has many parts with different functions that work together, all spiritual gifts are valuable and must cooperate in harmony
Only believers with the gift of public preaching are important, while all other gifts are useless

questions.correctAnswer: Just as a human body has many parts with different functions that work together, all spiritual gifts are valuable and must cooperate in harmony
