questions.explanation: Paul uses the human body metaphor to teach unity in diversity: the eye cannot say to the hand, "I don’t need you." Every member and gift is essential for the healthy functioning of the church community.
questions.socraticHint: How does Paul’s metaphor of the human body teach mutual respect and cooperation among believers with different gifts?

questions.prompt: Which Fruit of the Spirit is demonstrated when a learner remains calm, polite, and respectful even when teased by a classmate?
questions.text: Which Fruit of the Spirit is demonstrated when a learner remains calm, polite, and respectful even when teased by a classmate?
questions.explanation: Self-control enables believers to master their reactions and impulses, while gentleness responds with calm grace rather than retaliation, embodying the Fruit of the Spirit.
questions.socraticHint: Which virtues keep your temper in check and respond with peaceful softness instead of violence?

questions.prompt: In what practical way can Kenyan church youth groups follow the fellowship model of the Early Church today?
questions.text: In what practical way can Kenyan church youth groups follow the fellowship model of the Early Church today?

options.text: Studying the Bible together, praying for one another, and organizing food and clothes drives for local children’s homes
Excluding members who do not wear expensive brand shoes from youth activities
Spending all youth fellowship funds on luxury trips to beach resorts
Refusing to help elderly church members with their compound chores

questions.correctAnswer: Studying the Bible together, praying for one another, and organizing food and clothes drives for local children’s homes
questions.explanation: Devoting time to scripture, mutual intercession, and practical charity to help the vulnerable directly reflects Acts 2:42-45 in modern Kenyan community life.
questions.socraticHint: Which activities combine scriptural learning, shared prayer, and selfless charity for the needy?

questions.prompt: Why does Paul state in 1 Corinthians 13:1-3 that all spiritual gifts are worthless without "love" (agape)?
questions.text: Why does Paul state in 1 Corinthians 13:1-3 that all spiritual gifts are worthless without "love" (agape)?

options.text: Because only the apostles were permitted to possess both love and gifts
Love is the supreme motivating virtue; without genuine love, gifts become noisy, selfish, and spiritually useless
Because love is an emotion that requires no action or commitment
Because gifts of speaking and knowledge are forbidden for Christians

questions.correctAnswer: Love is the supreme motivating virtue; without genuine love, gifts become noisy, selfish, and spiritually useless
questions.explanation: Paul emphasizes that even if one has the gift of tongues, prophecy, or faith to move mountains, without love it profits nothing. Love is the essential foundation that gives meaning to all spiritual gifts.
questions.socraticHint: Why is selfless agape love the essential foundation that makes all spiritual gifts truly beneficial?

questions.prompt: What did the Roman world and Jewish neighbors notice about the Early Church that caused their numbers to grow daily (Acts 2:47)?
questions.text: What did the Roman world and Jewish neighbors notice about the Early Church that caused their numbers to grow daily (Acts 2:47)?

options.text: Their enormous stockpile of gold captured from pagan temples
Their strict refusal to speak to anyone who was not a baptized Christian
Their genuine love, joyful unity, generosity, and sincere praise to God won the favor of all the people
Their huge army of trained soldiers carrying sharp bronze swords

questions.correctAnswer: Their genuine love, joyful unity, generosity, and sincere praise to God won the favor of all the people
questions.explanation: Acts 2:47 notes that the believers enjoyed the favor of all the people, praising God with glad hearts, and "the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved." Love and unity were their greatest testimony.
questions.socraticHint: What attractive qualities of joyful worship, selfless charity, and authentic love attracted people to Christ?

questions.prompt: A disagreement breaks out between two learners in the school Christian Union about who should lead Sunday praise. How does biblical early church leadership guide them?
questions.text: A disagreement breaks out between two learners in the school Christian Union about who should lead Sunday praise. How does biblical early church leadership guide them?

options.text: Engage in a shouting match during chapel until the patron chooses the loudest person
Split the Christian Union into two rival factions that refuse to speak to each other
Refuse to sing or play musical instruments unless one is made the supreme leader
Pray together, resolve the matter with mutual humility and patience, and share the leading responsibilities in harmony

questions.correctAnswer: Pray together, resolve the matter with mutual humility and patience, and share the leading responsibilities in harmony
questions.explanation: The Early Church resolved conflicts through prayer, mutual deference, and peaceful cooperation (Philippians 2:3, Acts 6). Servant leadership shares responsibility and puts the fellowship’s unity above personal vanity.
questions.socraticHint: How does peaceful cooperation, prayer, and mutual humility resolve leadership disputes in Christian fellowship?

questions.prompt: How does the Fruit of the Spirit differ from physical or temporary human talents?
questions.text: How does the Fruit of the Spirit differ from physical or temporary human talents?

options.text: The Fruit of the Spirit reflects the eternal, holy character of Christ produced in a believer’s heart by the Holy Spirit
The Fruit of the Spirit can be purchased with money at a church bookshop
The Fruit of the Spirit is only given to professional athletes and singers
The Fruit of the Spirit disappears permanently whenever a person becomes sick

questions.correctAnswer: The Fruit of the Spirit reflects the eternal, holy character of Christ produced in a believer’s heart by the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: While natural talents are specific abilities for tasks, the Fruit of the Spirit is the moral and spiritual character of Jesus Christ produced by the Holy Spirit within every believer, lasting for eternity.
questions.socraticHint: How does the Fruit of the Spirit transform the inner moral character of a person to reflect Jesus Christ?

questions.prompt: What divine promise is attached to the Fifth Commandment ("Honor your father and your mother") in Exodus 20:12 and Ephesians 6:2-3?
questions.text: What divine promise is attached to the Fifth Commandment ("Honor your father and your mother") in Exodus 20:12 and Ephesians 6:2-3?

options.text: That you will receive fifty head of cattle from the community elders
That it may go well with you and that you may enjoy long life on the earth
That you will be appointed a government minister in your county
That you will never have to wash dishes or clean your bedroom

questions.correctAnswer: That it may go well with you and that you may enjoy long life on the earth
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:2-3 states: "Honor your father and mother—which is the first commandment with a promise—so that it may go well with you and that you may enjoy long life on the earth."
questions.socraticHint: Which special blessing of well-being and long life is promised to children who honor their parents?

questions.prompt: What does Ephesians 6:1 specifically command children regarding their parents?
questions.text: What does Ephesians 6:1 specifically command children regarding their parents?

options.text: Children, ignore your parents if you have a smartphone
Children, only obey your parents when they give you pocket money
Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right
Children, argue with your parents whenever they give you chores

questions.correctAnswer: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:1 commands: "Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right." Respectful obedience to parents is a fundamental moral duty pleasing to God.
questions.socraticHint: Which clear, direct instruction opens Ephesians chapter 6 concerning children and parents?

questions.prompt: How can a Grade 5 pupil demonstrate honor and respect toward their parents in practical daily life at home?
questions.text: How can a Grade 5 pupil demonstrate honor and respect toward their parents in practical daily life at home?

options.text: Rolling eyes and grumbling loudly whenever asked to sweep the floor
Demanding expensive gifts before greeting them after school
Leaving their school uniform and dirty socks scattered across the living room
Speaking to them politely, obeying instructions promptly, and helping cheerfully with domestic chores

questions.correctAnswer: Speaking to them politely, obeying instructions promptly, and helping cheerfully with domestic chores
questions.explanation: Honoring parents involves respectful communication, willing cooperation, prompt obedience, and actively easing their burdens through domestic assistance and loving gratitude.
questions.socraticHint: Which actions show polite speech, willing obedience, and cheerful helpfulness at home?

questions.prompt: What responsibility does Ephesians 6:4 give to Christian parents regarding the upbringing of their children?
questions.text: What responsibility does Ephesians 6:4 give to Christian parents regarding the upbringing of their children?

options.text: Do not exasperate your children; instead, bring them up in the training and instruction of the Lord
Demand that children work on farms 24 hours a day without attending school
Never discipline children even when they commit serious moral wrongs
Give children everything they demand so they never feel disappointed

questions.correctAnswer: Do not exasperate your children; instead, bring them up in the training and instruction of the Lord
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:4 guides parents to avoid harsh, unreasonable treatment that provokes children to anger, commanding them to raise children in godly instruction, discipline, and loving guidance.
questions.socraticHint: How are parents instructed to nurture children without exasperating them?

questions.prompt: According to Leviticus 19:32, how should young people treat elderly persons in their community?
questions.text: According to Leviticus 19:32, how should young people treat elderly persons in their community?

options.text: Avoid greeting elderly neighbors when walking along village paths
Stand up in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly and revere your God
Ignore elderly persons because their ideas are outdated and irrelevant
Mock elderly people when they walk slowly with walking sticks

questions.correctAnswer: Stand up in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly and revere your God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:32 commands: "Stand up in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly and revere your God. I am the Lord." Respect for elders is linked directly with reverence for God.
questions.socraticHint: What respectful physical gesture in the presence of elderly people is commanded in Leviticus?

questions.prompt: In Luke 2:51, what example did Jesus set as a twelve-year-old boy in Nazareth regarding family living?
questions.text: In Luke 2:51, what example did Jesus set as a twelve-year-old boy in Nazareth regarding family living?

options.text: He told Joseph that divine children do not need to follow earthly house rules
He spent His days playing games and avoided learning practical crafts
He went down to Nazareth with Mary and Joseph and was obedient to them
He left His parents to establish an independent carpentry business in Jerusalem

questions.correctAnswer: He went down to Nazareth with Mary and Joseph and was obedient to them
questions.explanation: Luke 2:51 states: "Then he went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them." Jesus’ perfect submission to His earthly parents models filial obedience for every child.
questions.socraticHint: What exemplary attitude of obedience did Jesus show to Mary and Joseph in Nazareth?

questions.prompt: When parents correct or discipline a child for wrongdoing, how does Proverbs 3:11-12 explain this correction?
questions.text: When parents correct or discipline a child for wrongdoing, how does Proverbs 3:11-12 explain this correction?

options.text: Correction proves that parents hate their children and want to punish them unfairly
Correction shows that parents have run out of patience and want to be mean
Correction is a legal formality that has no spiritual meaning
Correction is a proof of genuine love, just as a father disciplines the son he delights in

questions.correctAnswer: Correction is a proof of genuine love, just as a father disciplines the son he delights in
questions.explanation: Proverbs 3:11-12 explains: "Do not despise the Lord’s discipline... because the Lord disciplines those he loves, as a father the son he delights in." Godly parental discipline stems from loving protection.
questions.socraticHint: Does godly correction stem from hatred and cruelty or from loving concern and protection?

questions.prompt: A learner named Moses is asked by his mother to look after his younger brother while she finishes cooking supper. How can Moses honor God in this situation?
questions.text: A learner named Moses is asked by his mother to look after his younger brother while she finishes cooking supper. How can Moses honor God in this situation?

options.text: Care for his little brother attentively and kindly, helping his mother cheerfully
Shout at his brother and run away to play football in the street
Demand ten shillings from his mother before agreeing to watch the baby
Pinch his brother so the baby cries loudly and makes the mother stop cooking

questions.correctAnswer: Care for his little brother attentively and kindly, helping his mother cheerfully
questions.explanation: Helping with siblings cheerfully and without complaint demonstrates loving service, filial honor, and responsible Christian family behavior.
questions.socraticHint: Which option shows cheerful cooperation and loving care for a younger family member?

questions.prompt: What did Jesus do while dying on the Cross to ensure His widowed mother Mary was cared for (John 19:26-27)?
questions.text: What did Jesus do while dying on the Cross to ensure His widowed mother Mary was cared for (John 19:26-27)?

options.text: He asked the high priest to provide a room for Mary in the temple courtyard
He entrusted Mary to the care of the beloved disciple John, saying, "Dear woman, here is your son," and to John, "Here is your mother"
He asked the Roman centurions to pay Mary a monthly widow’s pension
He told Mary that His death ended all family obligations between them

questions.correctAnswer: He entrusted Mary to the care of the beloved disciple John, saying, "Dear woman, here is your son," and to John, "Here is your mother"
questions.explanation: Even in His deepest physical agony on the Cross, Jesus fulfilled the fifth commandment by providing loving lifelong shelter and care for His mother through John, who took her into his home from that hour.
questions.socraticHint: To which beloved disciple did Jesus tenderly entrust the care of His mother Mary?

questions.prompt: How does holding regular family prayer and scripture reading contribute to peace in a Kenyan household?
questions.text: How does holding regular family prayer and scripture reading contribute to peace in a Kenyan household?

options.text: It replaces the need for family members to apologize when they offend each other
It makes sure that parents never have to work to provide food and school fees
It builds spiritual unity, fosters forgiveness, resolves misunderstandings, and invites God’s peace into the home
It creates strict silence so family members never talk to each other about problems

questions.correctAnswer: It builds spiritual unity, fosters forgiveness, resolves misunderstandings, and invites God’s peace into the home
questions.explanation: Gathering for prayer and scripture allows families to surrender anxieties to God, seek mutual forgiveness, reinforce shared moral values, and invite the peace of Christ into everyday life.
questions.socraticHint: How does praying together as a family promote reconciliation, forgiveness, and moral harmony?

questions.prompt: Which of the following actions constitutes a serious failure to honor one’s parents under Christian moral teaching?
questions.text: Which of the following actions constitutes a serious failure to honor one’s parents under Christian moral teaching?

options.text: Asking parents for guidance on a difficult homework question in science
Washing dishes and sweeping the floor before being asked
Praying for parents when they leave early for farming or trading work
Speaking to parents disrespectfully, lying about school performance, and stealing household money

questions.correctAnswer: Speaking to parents disrespectfully, lying about school performance, and stealing household money
questions.explanation: Disrespect, deceit, and theft violate both the Fifth and Eighth Commandments, damaging parental trust, dishonoring family dignity, and sinning against God.
questions.socraticHint: Which harmful behaviors violate parental honor, honesty, and biblical commandment?

questions.prompt: Why does God place human beings in families as the primary environment for spiritual and moral development?
questions.text: Why does God place human beings in families as the primary environment for spiritual and moral development?

options.text: Families provide nurture, unconditional love, moral instruction, and a living sanctuary where children first learn to love God and neighbor
Families exist solely as economic units to generate commercial profits through manual labor
Families are temporary shelters until children learn how to hunt in the wild
God prefers humans to live in isolation without any social obligations

questions.correctAnswer: Families provide nurture, unconditional love, moral instruction, and a living sanctuary where children first learn to love God and neighbor
questions.explanation: The family is God’s appointed sanctuary where children experience love, safety, moral values, and faith modeled in daily life, preparing them to be responsible, godly citizens in society.
questions.socraticHint: What foundational role does the family play in nurturing faith, love, and moral character in a growing child?

questions.prompt: What profound warning regarding friendships is given in Proverbs 13:20?
questions.text: What profound warning regarding friendships is given in Proverbs 13:20?

options.text: The more friends you have, the less you need to study for exams
Walk with the wise and become wise, for a companion of fools suffers harm
Avoid all friends because nobody can be trusted in this world
Only befriend people who give you expensive toys and sweets

questions.correctAnswer: Walk with the wise and become wise, for a companion of fools suffers harm
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:20 warns: "Walk with the wise and become wise, for a companion of fools suffers harm." Our choice of companions strongly shapes our character, wisdom, and future.
questions.socraticHint: Which proverb connects walking with wise people to becoming wise, and warning of harm from foolish companions?

questions.prompt: What does 1 Corinthians 15:33 teach about the danger of negative peer pressure?
questions.text: What does 1 Corinthians 15:33 teach about the danger of negative peer pressure?

options.text: Good character automatically protects you from any peer influence
You should copy everything your peers do to fit into the group
Do not be misled: Bad company corrupts good character
Bad company makes you more popular and successful in school

questions.correctAnswer: Do not be misled: Bad company corrupts good character
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:33 states: "Do not be misled: ‘Bad company corrupts good character.’" Associating with peers who engage in wrongdoing gradually erodes our moral values and integrity.
questions.socraticHint: Which concise verse warns that "bad company corrupts good character"?

questions.prompt: According to Proverbs 15:1, what is the best way to diffuse an angry confrontation at school?
questions.text: According to Proverbs 15:1, what is the best way to diffuse an angry confrontation at school?

options.text: Shouting insults louder than the other person to intimidate them
Throwing school bags at the person to make them back away
Challenging the classmate to a physical wrestling contest
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger

questions.correctAnswer: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger
questions.explanation: Proverbs 15:1 teaches: "A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger." Responding calmly and gently disarms anger and prevents conflict from escalating.
questions.socraticHint: What kind of gentle verbal response turns away anger according to Proverbs 15?

questions.prompt: What wise instruction does Ephesians 4:26 give about handling anger constructively?
questions.text: What wise instruction does Ephesians 4:26 give about handling anger constructively?

options.text: In your anger do not sin: Do not let the sun go down while you are still angry
Keep your anger inside for years until you find an opportunity to take revenge
Destroy personal property whenever you feel frustrated or angry
Refuse to speak to anyone in your family for an entire month

questions.correctAnswer: In your anger do not sin: Do not let the sun go down while you are still angry
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:26-27 warns: "In your anger do not sin: Do not let the sun go down while you are still angry, and do not give the devil a foothold." Resolving anger quickly prevents bitterness and hatred.
questions.socraticHint: Before what natural time marker (sunset) should anger be reconciled to avoid sin and bitterness?

questions.prompt: A classmate tries to persuade Mercy to steal a packet of colored pencils from another pupil’s desk. How should Mercy respond?
questions.text: A classmate tries to persuade Mercy to steal a packet of colored pencils from another pupil’s desk. How should Mercy respond?

options.text: Take the pencils and bury them in the playground sand
Firmly refuse, saying: "No, stealing is wrong and against God’s commandments," and encourage the classmate to return to their seat
Steal the pencils quickly and split them half-and-half with the classmate
Agree to keep watch while the classmate steals the pencils

questions.correctAnswer: Firmly refuse, saying: "No, stealing is wrong and against God’s commandments," and encourage the classmate to return to their seat
questions.explanation: The Eighth Commandment commands: "You shall not steal" (Exodus 20:15). Christian integrity requires assertive moral resistance: saying a firm "No" to wrongdoing and standing for righteousness.
questions.socraticHint: Which response demonstrates assertive Christian integrity by refusing to participate in theft?

questions.prompt: What does Proverbs 12:22 declare about God’s attitude toward lying and truthfulness?
questions.text: What does Proverbs 12:22 declare about God’s attitude toward lying and truthfulness?

options.text: God prefers clever deceit over honest truthfulness in business
Telling lies is a normal skill that every person must master
The Lord detests lying lips, but He delights in people who are trustworthy
Lying is acceptable as long as you do not get caught by the teacher

questions.correctAnswer: The Lord detests lying lips, but He delights in people who are trustworthy
questions.explanation: Proverbs 12:22 teaches: "The Lord detests lying lips, but he delights in people who are trustworthy." God is a God of truth, and integrity in speech pleases Him.
questions.socraticHint: What does God detest and in what kind of trustworthy behavior does He delight?

questions.prompt: What is "cyberbullying," and why does it violate Christian moral principles?
questions.text: What is "cyberbullying," and why does it violate Christian moral principles?

options.text: Learning computer coding to develop educational math games for primary schools
Sending online homework assignments to class teachers via email
Searching for biblical maps of Jerusalem on school tablets
Using phones or the internet to send cruel, insulting messages or embarrass others, violating Christ’s command to love and protect our neighbor’s dignity

questions.correctAnswer: Using phones or the internet to send cruel, insulting messages or embarrass others, violating Christ’s command to love and protect our neighbor’s dignity
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying involves using digital platforms to harass, insult, or intimidate others. Ephesians 4:29 warns against unwholesome talk, commanding us to use words only to build up and encourage others.
questions.socraticHint: How does using digital technology to mock or insult classmates violate Christian love and respect?

questions.prompt: Why should Kenyan school learners completely reject alcohol, smoking, and illicit drugs according to 1 Corinthians 6:19-20?
questions.text: Why should Kenyan school learners completely reject alcohol, smoking, and illicit drugs according to 1 Corinthians 6:19-20?

options.text: Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit bought at a price, and we must honor God with our bodies
Because drugs are expensive and children should save money to buy candy
Because smoking only harms people when they become over eighty years old
Because physical health has no connection to spiritual life

questions.correctAnswer: Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit bought at a price, and we must honor God with our bodies
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 reminds us: "Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore honor God with your bodies."
questions.socraticHint: Why is viewing our physical body as a temple of the Holy Spirit a powerful reason to keep it pure and healthy?

questions.prompt: During sports day, Patrick loses the 100-meter sprint to his classmate. What is the Christian response to feelings of jealousy?
questions.text: During sports day, Patrick loses the 100-meter sprint to his classmate. What is the Christian response to feelings of jealousy?

options.text: Cry and refuse to eat food for three days to make everyone feel guilty
Sincerely congratulate the winner, rejoice in their success, and thank God for his own running ability
Trip the winner during the prize presentation to humiliate them
Spread malicious rumors that the winner cheated or took unauthorized medicine

questions.correctAnswer: Sincerely congratulate the winner, rejoice in their success, and thank God for his own running ability
questions.explanation: Romans 12:15 commands us to "Rejoice with those who rejoice." Overcoming jealousy with genuine celebration of others’ success reflects true Christian humility and sportsmanship.
questions.socraticHint: How does congratulating the winner and rejoicing in their success overcome bitter feelings of jealousy?

questions.prompt: What quality of true friendship is exemplified by Jonathan’s covenant friendship with David in 1 Samuel 18:1-4?
questions.text: What quality of true friendship is exemplified by Jonathan’s covenant friendship with David in 1 Samuel 18:1-4?

options.text: Using a friend’s skills to make oneself look more important in the palace
Abandoning a friend as soon as they encounter dangerous challenges
Selfless loyalty, sacrificial love, and protecting one’s friend even at personal cost
Compromising on moral principles to keep each other’s bad secrets

questions.correctAnswer: Selfless loyalty, sacrificial love, and protecting one’s friend even at personal cost
questions.explanation: Jonathan loved David as his own soul, giving him his robe, sword, and bow. He protected David from King Saul’s jealousy, demonstrating sacrificial, selfless, and godly friendship.
questions.socraticHint: What noble qualities of sacrificial loyalty and protective love defined Jonathan’s friendship with David?

questions.prompt: In Matthew 5:9, what high honor and blessing does Jesus give to peacemakers in the Beatitudes?
questions.text: In Matthew 5:9, what high honor and blessing does Jesus give to peacemakers in the Beatitudes?

options.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will receive gold crowns from Rome
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will never have to work for a living
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will become kings of all earthly armies
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God

questions.correctAnswer: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God
questions.explanation: In the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:9), Jesus declared: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God." Peacemaking reflects the very character of our Heavenly Father.
questions.socraticHint: Which Beatitude states that those who actively foster peace will be recognized as children of God?

questions.prompt: Why is personal integrity—doing the right thing even when no one is watching—the true mark of Christian character?
questions.text: Why is personal integrity—doing the right thing even when no one is watching—the true mark of Christian character?

options.text: Because God sees everything (Proverbs 15:3), and living with integrity reflects genuine reverence for God rather than mere eye-service for humans
Because being honest guarantees that school exams will always be simple and easy
Because people who practice integrity never face any disagreements with peers
Because human integrity is an invention of Greek philosophers with no connection to biblical faith

questions.correctAnswer: Because God sees everything (Proverbs 15:3), and living with integrity reflects genuine reverence for God rather than mere eye-service for humans
questions.explanation: Proverbs 15:3 says: "The eyes of the Lord are everywhere, keeping watch on the wicked and the good." Christian integrity springs from inner love and reverence for God, choosing righteousness for His glory.
questions.socraticHint: Why does knowing that God sees all our actions motivate true integrity beyond human praise?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: How does James 1:27 define pure and faultless religion before God the Father?
questions.text: How does James 1:27 define pure and faultless religion before God the Father?

options.text: To memorize religious texts without ever helping anyone in need
To look after orphans and widows in their distress and keep oneself from being polluted by the world
To build the tallest church tower in the county with golden bells
To fast for three days every week while ignoring poor neighbors

questions.correctAnswer: To look after orphans and widows in their distress and keep oneself from being polluted by the world
questions.explanation: James 1:27 defines pure religion: "Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is this: to look after orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world."
questions.socraticHint: Which two vulnerable groups are specifically highlighted as receiving care in pure religion?

questions.prompt: What command regarding vulnerable people is given in Psalm 82:3-4?
questions.text: What command regarding vulnerable people is given in Psalm 82:3-4?

options.text: Collect taxes only from widows and fatherless children
Expel foreigners and poor people from the city gates
Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed
Ignore the cries of the poor so they learn to work harder

questions.correctAnswer: Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed
questions.explanation: Psalm 82:3-4 commands believers: "Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed. Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
questions.socraticHint: What divine command requires believers to stand up for the weak and fatherless against injustice?

questions.prompt: In 1 Timothy 5:4, who does the Apostle Paul say has the primary responsibility to support elderly widows?
questions.text: In 1 Timothy 5:4, who does the Apostle Paul say has the primary responsibility to support elderly widows?

options.text: Foreign tourists visiting the country on holidays
The Roman emperor through military distributions
Their own children and grandchildren, putting their religion into practice by repaying their parents

questions.correctAnswer: Their own children and grandchildren, putting their religion into practice by repaying their parents
questions.explanation: Paul teaches that if a widow has children or grandchildren, they should learn first of all to put their religion into practice by caring for their own family and repaying their parents, for this pleases God.
questions.socraticHint: Which family members are biblically responsible for caring for their own elderly mothers and grandmothers?

questions.prompt: How did ancient Israelite harvesting laws (gleaning laws in Leviticus 19:9-10) protect widows and orphans?
questions.text: How did ancient Israelite harvesting laws (gleaning laws in Leviticus 19:9-10) protect widows and orphans?

options.text: Farmers were forbidden from harvesting the field edges or picking dropped grapes, leaving them for the poor and foreigners to gather
Widows were forced to buy all grain directly from royal government stores at double price
Poor travelers were prohibited from setting foot on agricultural fields
All leftover crops had to be burned with fire to keep the fields clean

questions.correctAnswer: Farmers were forbidden from harvesting the field edges or picking dropped grapes, leaving them for the poor and foreigners to gather
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:9-10 instructed landowners not to reap to the very edges of their field or gather fallen grapes, deliberately leaving grain for the poor, fatherless, and foreigners to gather with dignity.
questions.socraticHint: How did leaving the edges of fields unharvested provide food for the fatherless and widows?

questions.prompt: In our Kenyan community, unscrupulous relatives attempt to chase a widowed mother and her children off her deceased husband’s land. What is the Christian response?
questions.text: In our Kenyan community, unscrupulous relatives attempt to chase a widowed mother and her children off her deceased husband’s land. What is the Christian response?

options.text: Remain completely neutral because land disputes are none of our business
Stand with the widow, defend her lawful rights, and seek support from church elders and local authorities to protect her family
Help the relatives grab the land because the widow has no male guardian
Laugh at the children and tell them to find another piece of land in the forest

questions.correctAnswer: Stand with the widow, defend her lawful rights, and seek support from church elders and local authorities to protect her family
questions.explanation: God is the "defender of widows" (Psalm 68:5). Defending vulnerable widows and orphans from illegal land dispossession is an essential expression of Christian justice and biblical obedience.
questions.socraticHint: How does defending a vulnerable widow against land grabbing reflect God’s command to protect the fatherless?

questions.prompt: How can Grade 5 learners in Kenya participate in caring for orphaned children in their locality?
questions.text: How can Grade 5 learners in Kenya participate in caring for orphaned children in their locality?

options.text: Refusing to sit next to orphaned pupils in the classroom or share pencils with them
Demanding payment before allowing orphaned children to join playground games
Contributing clothes, books, and food to children’s homes, visiting them to play together, and showing genuine friendship
Teasing orphaned classmates at school because they do not have parents at visiting day

questions.correctAnswer: Contributing clothes, books, and food to children’s homes, visiting them to play together, and showing genuine friendship
questions.explanation: Children can show Christ-like compassion by contributing gently used clothes, stationery, and food, visiting children’s homes, and treating orphaned peers with warmth, dignity, and inclusive love.
questions.socraticHint: Which actions show practical kindness, sharing, and authentic friendship toward children without parents?

questions.prompt: In Luke 7:11-15, what deep emotion moved Jesus when He saw a widow in the town of Nain mourning her only son?
questions.text: In Luke 7:11-15, what deep emotion moved Jesus when He saw a widow in the town of Nain mourning her only son?

options.text: He was annoyed by the noise of the funeral procession and walked around the town
He asked the crowd how much money they had collected for the burial
He told the mother that losing an only son was a punishment for her past deeds
His heart went out to her with deep compassion, and He said, "Don’t cry," before raising the young man to life

questions.correctAnswer: His heart went out to her with deep compassion, and He said, "Don’t cry," before raising the young man to life
questions.explanation: Luke 7:13 records that when the Lord saw the grieving widow, "his heart went out to her and he said, ‘Don’t cry.’" He touched the coffin and raised the young man back to life, restoring him to his mother.
questions.socraticHint: What tender divine compassion moved Jesus when He saw the grieving widow of Nain?

questions.prompt: What does Proverbs 19:17 teach about showing generosity to the poor and needy?
questions.text: What does Proverbs 19:17 teach about showing generosity to the poor and needy?

options.text: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and He will reward them for what they have done
Giving to the poor causes a person to run out of money quickly
The poor should only be given help if they agree to work as domestic servants
God pays no attention to whether we help the needy or ignore them

questions.correctAnswer: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and He will reward them for what they have done
questions.explanation: Proverbs 19:17 says: "Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and he will reward them for what they have done." Kindness to the underprivileged is counted as service to God Himself.
questions.socraticHint: According to Proverbs 19, who are we lending to when we show kindness to the poor?

questions.prompt: How can a church fellowship in Kenya help elderly grandmothers (shoshos) in rural villages who struggle with arthritis?
questions.text: How can a church fellowship in Kenya help elderly grandmothers (shoshos) in rural villages who struggle with arthritis?

options.text: Telling them to walk five kilometers to the nearest borehole every morning
Organizing youth teams to fetch firewood and water, weed kitchen gardens, and provide warm blankets and food hampers
Leaving them to manage on their own because old age is a natural process
Demanding that they attend church meetings three times a day despite physical pain

questions.correctAnswer: Organizing youth teams to fetch firewood and water, weed kitchen gardens, and provide warm blankets and food hampers
questions.explanation: Practical Christian service eases physical burdens for the elderly through home visits, domestic assistance, provision of warm essentials, and medical support.
questions.socraticHint: Which practical assistance with household tasks and warm essentials helps elderly people in villages?

questions.prompt: In Acts 9:36-39, what generous deeds was the disciple Tabitha (Dorcas) celebrated for in Joppa before Peter raised her from the dead?
questions.text: In Acts 9:36-39, what generous deeds was the disciple Tabitha (Dorcas) celebrated for in Joppa before Peter raised her from the dead?

options.text: She built huge stone monuments to honour the apostles across Judea
She composed battle hymns for the Jewish freedom fighters
She was always doing good and helping the poor, making robes and other clothing for poor widows
She traded expensive purple dyed wool to Roman senators in Caesarea

questions.correctAnswer: She was always doing good and helping the poor, making robes and other clothing for poor widows
questions.explanation: Acts 9:36-39 describes Dorcas as a woman full of good works and acts of charity. Widows stood around weeping, showing the tunics and garments she had sewn for them while she was with them.
questions.socraticHint: What practical clothing did Dorcas lovingly sew with her own hands to clothe poor widows?

questions.prompt: Why does God repeatedly identify Himself in Scripture as the "Father to the fatherless, a defender of widows" (Psalm 68:5)?
questions.text: Why does God repeatedly identify Himself in Scripture as the "Father to the fatherless, a defender of widows" (Psalm 68:5)?

options.text: Because earthly fathers are completely unnecessary in God’s design
Because widows and orphans have no need for food, shelter, or community support
To show that God is only interested in people who live in rural villages
To reveal His special tender care for the most powerless and ensure His people prioritize justice for the defenseless

questions.correctAnswer: To reveal His special tender care for the most powerless and ensure His people prioritize justice for the defenseless
questions.explanation: God’s character is defined by righteousness and tender mercy toward those without earthly protectors. By revealing Himself as their defender, He commands His people to reflect that same protective love.
questions.socraticHint: Why does God declare Himself the protector of those who lack earthly defenders in society?

questions.prompt: Which of the following attitudes violates Christian teaching when interacting with street children in Kenyan towns?
questions.text: Which of the following attitudes violates Christian teaching when interacting with street children in Kenyan towns?

options.text: Viewing them with disgust, calling them criminals, and ignoring their human dignity and trauma
Supporting feeding programs and rehabilitation shelters that rescue and educate them
Recognizing that they are children created in the image of God who need love and care
Praying for their safety and supporting community initiatives to reunite them with families

questions.correctAnswer: Viewing them with disgust, calling them criminals, and ignoring their human dignity and trauma
questions.explanation: Christ calls us to love the vulnerable with empathy. Contempt and dehumanization violate Christ’s teaching that "whatever you did for one of the least of these, you did for me" (Matthew 25:40).
questions.socraticHint: Which contemptuous attitude denies the divine image and sacred dignity of vulnerable street children?

questions.prompt: In Luke 14:12-14, whom did Jesus instruct a banquet host to invite if they desire true heavenly blessing?
questions.text: In Luke 14:12-14, whom did Jesus instruct a banquet host to invite if they desire true heavenly blessing?

options.text: Only close family relatives who will invite you to their luxury banquets
The poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind who cannot repay you
Wealthy business executives who can give you big contracts
The Roman governor and palace dignitaries to gain political favor

questions.correctAnswer: The poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind who cannot repay you
questions.explanation: Jesus said: "When you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind, and you will be blessed. Although they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
questions.socraticHint: Which marginalized group that cannot repay you did Jesus command us to invite to feasts?

questions.prompt: How did King David demonstrate extraordinary covenant kindness (hesed) to Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s crippled son (2 Samuel 9)?
questions.text: How did King David demonstrate extraordinary covenant kindness (hesed) to Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s crippled son (2 Samuel 9)?

options.text: He ordered him to serve as a foot soldier in the army against the Philistines
He confiscated all his livestock and gave them to palace servants
He restored all his grandfather Saul’s land to him and welcomed him to eat permanently at the king’s royal table
He had him banished to a distant fortress in the desert so no one saw his disability

questions.correctAnswer: He restored all his grandfather Saul’s land to him and welcomed him to eat permanently at the king’s royal table
questions.explanation: David sought out Mephibosheth, who was crippled in both feet, restored all of Saul’s inheritance to him, and said: "You will always eat at my table," modeling unconditional covenant mercy and inclusion.
questions.socraticHint: How did King David honor and include Jonathan’s crippled son at the royal banquet table?

questions.prompt: How should a Kenyan primary school class include a new pupil who uses a wheelchair?
questions.text: How should a Kenyan primary school class include a new pupil who uses a wheelchair?

options.text: Leave the pupil outside the classroom door during assembly and lunch breaks
Stare at the wheelchair and laugh when they try to move up steps
Tell the pupil that sports day and clubs are strictly reserved for walking students
Ensure paths and classroom entrances have smooth ramps, assist with moving between desks, and include them in games and group discussions

questions.correctAnswer: Ensure paths and classroom entrances have smooth ramps, assist with moving between desks, and include them in games and group discussions
questions.explanation: Inclusion means removing physical and social barriers, ensuring accessibility, showing respectful assistance, and treating classmates with disabilities as equal, valued members of the school family.
questions.socraticHint: Which actions show thoughtful accessibility, helpfulness, and equal participation for a wheelchair user?

questions.prompt: What command regarding foreign immigrants and refugees does God give in Leviticus 19:33-34?
questions.text: What command regarding foreign immigrants and refugees does God give in Leviticus 19:33-34?

options.text: Treat the foreigner residing among you as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt
Expel all foreigners from the borders immediately without food or water
Charge foreigners five times higher prices for food in the marketplace
Forbid foreigners from worshiping the Lord God of Israel

questions.correctAnswer: Treat the foreigner residing among you as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:33-34 commands: "When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt. I am the Lord your God."
questions.socraticHint: How does God command His people to treat foreign residents as native-born and love them as themselves?

questions.prompt: In Matthew 25:35-40, with which group of people does Jesus deeply identify Himself when describing the final judgment?
questions.text: In Matthew 25:35-40, with which group of people does Jesus deeply identify Himself when describing the final judgment?

options.text: The high priests presiding over the temple treasury
The hungry, the thirsty, the stranger, the naked, the sick, and the imprisoned ("the least of these")
The victorious Roman generals marching into cities with trophies
The wealthy merchants who owned fleets of trade ships

questions.correctAnswer: The hungry, the thirsty, the stranger, the naked, the sick, and the imprisoned ("the least of these")
questions.explanation: Jesus declared: "I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in... Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me."
questions.socraticHint: With which hungry, thirsty, sick, and vulnerable individuals did the King identify as "the least of these"?

questions.prompt: Kenya hosts thousands of refugees fleeing war from neighboring countries in camps like Kakuma and Dadaab. What is the Christian duty toward these displaced families?
questions.text: Kenya hosts thousands of refugees fleeing war from neighboring countries in camps like Kakuma and Dadaab. What is the Christian duty toward these displaced families?

options.text: Refuse to share any international relief supplies with their children
Bar them from attending Christian worship services in Kenya
Show hospitality, provide food, clean water, and education, and treat them with dignity and Christ-like love
Blame them for all economic problems in Kenya and demand their immediate expulsion into conflict zones

questions.correctAnswer: Show hospitality, provide food, clean water, and education, and treat them with dignity and Christ-like love
questions.explanation: Christians follow Christ’s command of hospitality (Matthew 25:35, Hebrews 13:2) by welcoming refugees, defending their human rights, providing humanitarian aid, and showing compassion to displaced families.
questions.socraticHint: How does offering humanitarian aid, shelter, and love to displaced refugees fulfill Christ’s command of hospitality?

questions.prompt: In John 9:1-3, when the disciples asked whether a blind man was born blind because of his own sin or his parents’ sin, how did Jesus correct them?
questions.text: In John 9:1-3, when the disciples asked whether a blind man was born blind because of his own sin or his parents’ sin, how did Jesus correct them?

options.text: His parents committed a secret crime in Jerusalem
The man sinned while he was an infant in his mother’s arms
God curses children with physical blindness whenever communities break laws
Neither this man nor his parents sinned; this happened so that the works of God might be displayed in him

questions.correctAnswer: Neither this man nor his parents sinned; this happened so that the works of God might be displayed in him
questions.explanation: Jesus completely rejected the superstitious belief that disability is a punishment for personal or parental sin, stating that it occurred so that God’s glory and healing grace could be revealed in his life.
questions.socraticHint: How did Jesus refute the superstitious idea that disabilities are caused by parental or personal curses?

questions.prompt: A student who is deaf joins Grade 5. Some classmates giggle when the student uses Kenyan Sign Language (KSL). What should a Christian classmate do?
questions.text: A student who is deaf joins Grade 5. Some classmates giggle when the student uses Kenyan Sign Language (KSL). What should a Christian classmate do?

options.text: Stop the giggling classmates, learn basic sign language greetings to communicate, and welcome the student warmly into class activities
Join in giggling to avoid feeling left out by the popular group in class
Ignore the deaf student completely and pretend they are invisible
Tell the teacher that deaf children should not be allowed in ordinary primary schools

questions.correctAnswer: Stop the giggling classmates, learn basic sign language greetings to communicate, and welcome the student warmly into class activities
questions.explanation: Christian love defends the vulnerable and practices inclusion. Defending the student from mockery and making the effort to learn Kenyan Sign Language (KSL) honors God and builds a loving community.
questions.socraticHint: Which proactive response defends the student against mockery and builds communication through sign language?

questions.prompt: What did the Apostle Paul teach in Galatians 6:2 about sharing communal burdens in the Christian fellowship?
questions.text: What did the Apostle Paul teach in Galatians 6:2 about sharing communal burdens in the Christian fellowship?

options.text: Only carry the burdens of people who belong to your clan
Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ
Let everyone carry only their own load and never assist another person
Charge a fee whenever you help a neighbor carry heavy luggage

questions.correctAnswer: Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:2 commands: "Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ." Helping others through sickness, grief, poverty, and challenges fulfills Christ’s law of love.
questions.socraticHint: What command to bear one another’s burdens fulfills the royal law of Christ?

questions.prompt: In Luke 10:33, what made the Samaritan’s response to the beaten traveler on the road so exceptional compared to the religious leaders?
questions.text: In Luke 10:33, what made the Samaritan’s response to the beaten traveler on the road so exceptional compared to the religious leaders?

options.text: He took the traveler’s wallet and brought it to the temple in Jerusalem
He walked past even faster because he had an urgent business appointment in Jericho
He had compassion that translated into immediate, costly, and practical action
He delivered a long theological speech about why bad things happen to good people

questions.correctAnswer: He had compassion that translated into immediate, costly, and practical action
questions.explanation: Unlike the priest and Levite who saw the man and passed by, the Samaritan felt compassion and took immediate, costly action—bandaging wounds, providing transportation, and paying an innkeeper.
questions.socraticHint: Did the Samaritan merely feel sorry, or did his compassion lead to immediate, practical, and costly aid?

questions.prompt: How does practicing hospitality toward strangers reflect Hebrews 13:2?
questions.text: How does practicing hospitality toward strangers reflect Hebrews 13:2?

options.text: Never open your door to anyone who does not possess a government identification card
Hospitality should only be practiced when strangers bring expensive gold gifts
Strangers should always be reported to the village chief before being given water
Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it

questions.correctAnswer: Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:2 reminds believers: "Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it," recalling Abraham hosting divine messengers in Genesis 18.
questions.socraticHint: What surprising heavenly beings might believers entertain unknowingly when showing hospitality to strangers?

questions.prompt: What profound theological truth explains why Christians are compelled to serve persons with disabilities, orphans, and refugees?
questions.text: What profound theological truth explains why Christians are compelled to serve persons with disabilities, orphans, and refugees?

options.text: Every human being is created in the image of God (Imago Dei) and loved by Christ; serving them is directly serving Jesus Himself
Because the United Nations requires all religious groups to perform charitable tasks
Because wealthy people have an excess of money that must be thrown away
Because good deeds guarantee that a person will become a political leader in Kenya

questions.correctAnswer: Every human being is created in the image of God (Imago Dei) and loved by Christ; serving them is directly serving Jesus Himself
questions.explanation: The Christian motivation for service is rooted in the sacred dignity of every person created in God’s image and Christ’s declaration that serving the vulnerable is serving Him (Matthew 25:40).
questions.socraticHint: How does recognizing God’s image in every person and serving Christ in them motivate Christian charity?

questions.prompt: What threefold summary of God’s moral requirement for human beings is proclaimed in Micah 6:8?
questions.text: What threefold summary of God’s moral requirement for human beings is proclaimed in Micah 6:8?

options.text: To attend religious festivals while taking bribes from merchants
To act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God
To build large stone palaces, accumulate silver coins, and conquer foreign lands
To offer thousands of burnt sacrifices and rivers of olive oil without changing one’s heart

questions.correctAnswer: To act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 states: "He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God."
questions.socraticHint: Which famous verse calls humanity to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God?

questions.prompt: In Amos 5:24, what powerful imagery does the prophet Amos use to describe the unstoppable flow of justice and righteousness?
questions.text: In Amos 5:24, what powerful imagery does the prophet Amos use to describe the unstoppable flow of justice and righteousness?

options.text: Let righteousness evaporate like dew in the morning sunshine
Let justice be sold in the market like wheat and olive oil
Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream
Let justice stand still like a stagnant muddy puddle in the road

questions.correctAnswer: Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream
questions.explanation: Amos 5:24 declares: "But let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!" True worship must result in active societal justice and defense of the oppressed.
questions.socraticHint: Which water imagery compares justice to a rolling river and righteousness to a never-failing stream?

questions.prompt: What clear command against accepting bribes is given in Exodus 23:8?
questions.text: What clear command against accepting bribes is given in Exodus 23:8?

options.text: Accept bribes as long as you use half of the money to support your local church
Bribes are acceptable if the government salaries are too low to pay school fees
Only judges are forbidden from accepting bribes while police officers may take them
Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the innocent

questions.correctAnswer: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the innocent
questions.explanation: Exodus 23:8 strictly commands: "Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the innocent." Bribery corrupts justice and oppresses the innocent.
questions.socraticHint: Why does God forbid bribes, noting that they blind clear vision and subvert justice?

questions.prompt: What warning does Proverbs 17:23 give concerning corrupt practices in judicial and leadership matters?
questions.text: What warning does Proverbs 17:23 give concerning corrupt practices in judicial and leadership matters?

options.text: The wicked accept secret bribes to pervert the course of justice
Accepting gifts from travelers brings honor to the royal palace
Bribery is a wise method to settle difficult court cases quickly
God blesses whoever collects the most bribes in public office

questions.correctAnswer: The wicked accept secret bribes to pervert the course of justice
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:23 states: "The wicked accept bribes in secret to pervert the course of justice." Secret bribes subvert fairness, denying justice to the innocent and honest.
questions.socraticHint: What does Proverbs say wicked people accept in secret to pervert justice?

questions.prompt: What does Romans 13:1-7 teach regarding a Christian’s civic duty toward lawful governing authorities and the paying of taxes?
questions.text: What does Romans 13:1-7 teach regarding a Christian’s civic duty toward lawful governing authorities and the paying of taxes?

options.text: Overthrow the government by force whenever a traffic police officer stops your car
Submit to governing authorities, obey just laws, and pay taxes and revenue honestly as responsible citizens
Refuse to obey all civil laws because Christians have their own heavenly kingdom
Evade paying taxes by hiding money in secret foreign bank accounts

questions.correctAnswer: Submit to governing authorities, obey just laws, and pay taxes and revenue honestly as responsible citizens
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1-7 instructs believers to respect governing authorities, live law-abiding lives, and pay taxes conscientiously: "Give to everyone what you owe them: If you owe taxes, pay taxes; if revenue, then revenue; if respect, then respect; if honor, then honor."
questions.socraticHint: How are Christians commanded to relate to governing authorities and fulfill civic duties like paying taxes?

questions.prompt: In Matthew 22:21, what famous principle of dual citizenship and civic duty did Jesus establish when questioned about paying taxes to Caesar?
questions.text: In Matthew 22:21, what famous principle of dual citizenship and civic duty did Jesus establish when questioned about paying taxes to Caesar?

options.text: Take Caesar’s money and use it to buy weapons for the temple guards
Christians are exempt from paying any earthly taxes to governments
Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God
Refuse to touch Roman coins because they are unclean pagan metal

questions.correctAnswer: Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God
questions.explanation: Jesus said: "Give back to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s." Christians have a dual duty: fulfilling civic obligations to legitimate earthly government while giving their ultimate devotion and worship to God.
questions.socraticHint: Which famous statement divided civic obligation to the state from ultimate devotion to God?

questions.prompt: A voter is offered 500 shillings by a politician’s agent to vote for a corrupt candidate in a general election. How should a Christian voter respond?
questions.text: A voter is offered 500 shillings by a politician’s agent to vote for a corrupt candidate in a general election. How should a Christian voter respond?

options.text: Take the money, buy meat for dinner, and vote for the candidate who gave the cash
Take money from all candidates and vote for whoever paid the highest amount
Stay at home on election day because all politicians are dishonest
Firmly reject the bribe, report the election offense, and vote conscientiously for a person of integrity and servant leadership

questions.correctAnswer: Firmly reject the bribe, report the election offense, and vote conscientiously for a person of integrity and servant leadership
questions.explanation: Voter bribery corrupts democracy and violates Exodus 23:8. Christian citizenship requires standing against corruption, refusing voter bribery, and voting with a clear conscience for candidates with moral integrity.
questions.socraticHint: Why is rejecting voter bribery essential for protecting democracy and honoring Christian integrity?

questions.prompt: How did John the Baptist instruct tax collectors who came to be baptized in Luke 3:12-13?
questions.text: How did John the Baptist instruct tax collectors who came to be baptized in Luke 3:12-13?

options.text: Don’t collect any more than you are required to
Resign from your jobs immediately and become fishermen in Galilee
Charge double tax on Roman soldiers and keep the profits for yourselves
Keep collecting secret bribes from merchants passing through the gates

questions.correctAnswer: Don’t collect any more than you are required to
questions.explanation: John the Baptist told tax collectors: "Don’t collect any more than you are required to." He demanded honesty, fair weights, and complete integrity in public revenue collection.
questions.socraticHint: What simple standard of financial honesty did John the Baptist demand of tax collectors?

questions.prompt: In Luke 19:8, how did the corrupt chief tax collector Zacchaeus demonstrate genuine repentance and restitution after encountering Jesus?
questions.text: In Luke 19:8, how did the corrupt chief tax collector Zacchaeus demonstrate genuine repentance and restitution after encountering Jesus?

options.text: He locked his treasury books in a vault so nobody could audit his past taxes
He gave half of his possessions to the poor and promised to repay fourfold anyone he had cheated
He promised to build a tall stone watchtower outside the city of Jericho
He gave Jesus a bag of Roman silver coins to secure a seat in heaven

questions.correctAnswer: He gave half of his possessions to the poor and promised to repay fourfold anyone he had cheated
questions.explanation: Zacchaeus declared: "Look, Lord! Here and now I give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have cheated anybody out of anything, I will pay back four times the amount." True repentance involves restorative justice.
questions.socraticHint: What fourfold financial repayment and donation to the poor did Zacchaeus pledge to prove his changed heart?

questions.prompt: A school prefect in Grade 5 is offered sweets by a classmate to remove their name from the list of noisemakers. What should the prefect do?
questions.text: A school prefect in Grade 5 is offered sweets by a classmate to remove their name from the list of noisemakers. What should the prefect do?

options.text: Demand five more sweets before agreeing to keep the secret
Write down innocent pupils’ names instead to protect the friend
Politely refuse the sweets, maintain an accurate list, and explain that a leader must be fair and honest
Eat the sweets quickly and erase the name from the list of noisemakers

questions.correctAnswer: Politely refuse the sweets, maintain an accurate list, and explain that a leader must be fair and honest
questions.explanation: Refusing petty bribes and upholding fair rules trains young learners in anti-corruption integrity and trustworthy servant leadership, honoring God’s standard of justice.
questions.socraticHint: How does refusing snacks in exchange for favoring a wrongdoer show anti-corruption integrity in school?

questions.prompt: Why is corruption referred to as a "cancer" to national development in Kenya from a Christian ethical perspective?
questions.text: Why is corruption referred to as a "cancer" to national development in Kenya from a Christian ethical perspective?

options.text: It makes currency notes dirty and tear easily in market stalls
It causes too many international tourists to visit game parks in the dry season
It prevents agricultural crops from receiving seasonal rains
It steals public funds intended for hospitals, schools, and roads, hurts the poor most, and destroys moral trust in society

questions.correctAnswer: It steals public funds intended for hospitals, schools, and roads, hurts the poor most, and destroys moral trust in society
questions.explanation: Corruption robs communities of vital public services, deprives children of school books, starves hospitals of medicine, and perverts justice, directly violating God’s commands to care for the poor and act justly.
questions.socraticHint: How does diverting public resources away from hospitals, schools, and roads cause widespread suffering?

questions.prompt: What role should the Church play in Kenya when public leaders engage in corruption and human rights abuses?
questions.text: What role should the Church play in Kenya when public leaders engage in corruption and human rights abuses?

options.text: Act as the prophetic conscience of the nation, fearlessly speaking truth to power, defending the vulnerable, and advocating for justice
Remain completely silent and praise leaders who give large donations regardless of how the money was acquired
Instruct believers to stay away from civic issues and never vote in national elections
Form an army of soldiers to wage civil war against government institutions

questions.correctAnswer: Act as the prophetic conscience of the nation, fearlessly speaking truth to power, defending the vulnerable, and advocating for justice
questions.explanation: Like prophets Nathan, Elijah, and Amos, the Church is called to serve as the prophetic conscience of society—speaking truth to power, exposing corruption, and demanding justice for the oppressed.
questions.socraticHint: How do biblical prophets model the Church’s calling to act as the moral and prophetic conscience of a nation?

questions.prompt: What revolutionary statement of human unity and equality in Christ does the Apostle Paul proclaim in Galatians 3:28?
questions.text: What revolutionary statement of human unity and equality in Christ does the Apostle Paul proclaim in Galatians 3:28?

options.text: Believers must never eat food with someone who speaks a different mother tongue
There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus
Only people born in Jerusalem are eligible to become true citizens of heaven
Men are spiritually superior to women and should receive twice as many blessings

questions.correctAnswer: There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:28 declares that our shared identity in Christ demolishes ethnic, social, and gender divisions: "There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus."
questions.socraticHint: Which verse states that in Christ Jesus, ethnic, social, and gender barriers are overcome through oneness?

questions.prompt: Why is negative ethnicity (tribalism) incompatible with Christian discipleship in Kenya?
questions.text: Why is negative ethnicity (tribalism) incompatible with Christian discipleship in Kenya?

options.text: Because ethnic diversity was an accidental mistake that God never intended
Because having diverse cultures prevents farmers from planting maize
It breeds prejudice, discrimination, and hatred against fellow human beings created in God’s image, violating Christ’s law of love
Because the Bible requires all Christians to speak only the English language

questions.correctAnswer: It breeds prejudice, discrimination, and hatred against fellow human beings created in God’s image, violating Christ’s law of love
questions.explanation: Tribalism exalts ethnic identity above God’s command to love our neighbors as ourselves. In Christ, every person is our brother or sister, and discrimination against any tribe is a sin against God.
questions.socraticHint: How does tribal discrimination contradict Christ’s fundamental commandment to love all neighbors equally?

questions.prompt: In Romans 12:18, what peacebuilding counsel does Scripture offer to all believers?
questions.text: In Romans 12:18, what peacebuilding counsel does Scripture offer to all believers?

options.text: Fight anyone who disagrees with your personal political opinion
Retaliate twice as hard whenever someone insults your ethnic community
Only seek peace with people who belong to your own family clan
If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone

questions.correctAnswer: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone
questions.explanation: Romans 12:18 urges: "If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone." Christians must take active responsibility to pursue peace, forgive offenses, and resolve conflicts calmly.
questions.socraticHint: What personal responsibility does Romans 12:18 place on us to live peacefully with all people?

questions.prompt: What does the opening line of the Kenya National Anthem declare about our nation’s spiritual foundation?
questions.text: What does the opening line of the Kenya National Anthem declare about our nation’s spiritual foundation?

options.text: It is a prayer addressing God: "O God of all creation, bless this our land and nation"
It praises the military forces of Kenya for defending our borders
It lists the mineral resources and cash crops found across the forty-seven counties
It celebrates the geographical height of Mount Kenya above the clouds

questions.correctAnswer: It is a prayer addressing God: "O God of all creation, bless this our land and nation"
questions.explanation: The Kenya National Anthem was composed as an authentic prayer to the Almighty God, opening with "O God of all creation, bless this our land and nation," seeking divine blessing, justice, unity, and liberty.
questions.socraticHint: Which prayerful words open the first stanza of the Kenya National Anthem?

questions.prompt: How can primary school pupils from diverse ethnic backgrounds across Kenya foster genuine national cohesion in school?
questions.text: How can primary school pupils from diverse ethnic backgrounds across Kenya foster genuine national cohesion in school?

options.text: Only voting for school prefect candidates who come from their home county
Making friends across ethnic communities, learning about each other’s cultural traditions, and working together cooperatively in class projects
Forming tribal cliques on the playing field and refusing to share balls with other groups
Mocking classmates who speak with accents from different regions of Kenya

questions.correctAnswer: Making friends across ethnic communities, learning about each other’s cultural traditions, and working together cooperatively in class projects
questions.explanation: National cohesion begins with mutual respect, inter-ethnic friendships, active collaboration in class and sports, and appreciating cultural diversity as a God-given national strength.
questions.socraticHint: Which actions foster inter-ethnic friendships, cultural appreciation, and collaborative teamwork?

questions.prompt: During national election periods in Kenya, political tensions sometimes rise. How can Christian learners act as ambassadors of peace in their neighborhoods?
questions.text: During national election periods in Kenya, political tensions sometimes rise. How can Christian learners act as ambassadors of peace in their neighborhoods?

options.text: Shout provocative slogans in the street to provoke fights between neighbors
Spread alarming, unverified rumors on social media to frighten classmates
Refuse to repeat hateful political gossip, encourage friends to stay calm and loving, and pray for peaceful, fair elections
Wear party hats and throw stones at houses belonging to rival political supporters

questions.correctAnswer: Refuse to repeat hateful political gossip, encourage friends to stay calm and loving, and pray for peaceful, fair elections
questions.explanation: Christians are called to be ambassadors of reconciliation (2 Corinthians 5:20) and peacemakers. Rejecting hate speech, promoting calm, and interceding for the nation during elections builds social peace.
questions.socraticHint: How does rejecting divisive rumors, promoting calm, and praying for the nation foster electoral peace?

questions.prompt: In Ephesians 2:14, how does Scripture describe what Jesus Christ accomplished concerning historic human divisions and hostility?
questions.text: In Ephesians 2:14, how does Scripture describe what Jesus Christ accomplished concerning historic human divisions and hostility?

options.text: He instructed each ethnic nation to build high stone barricades along their borders
He taught that only one chosen culture is superior to all others in the world
He encouraged groups to compete in warfare to see which one God favored
For He Himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility

questions.correctAnswer: For He Himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:14 proclaims: "For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility." Christ tears down walls of ethnic suspicion and creates one new, united family.
questions.socraticHint: Which verse celebrates Christ breaking down the dividing wall of hostility to bring peace?

questions.prompt: How does the Biblical story of Ruth, a Moabite foreigner who became the great-grandmother of King David, challenge ethnic prejudice?
questions.text: How does the Biblical story of Ruth, a Moabite foreigner who became the great-grandmother of King David, challenge ethnic prejudice?

options.text: It proves that God welcomes and honors people from all nations who walk in faithful love, regardless of historical ethnic enmities
It shows that foreigners should never be allowed to marry Israelites under any circumstances
It demonstrates that only Moabites possessed true religious wisdom in the ancient world
It proves that King David’s lineage was completely hidden from historical records

questions.correctAnswer: It proves that God welcomes and honors people from all nations who walk in faithful love, regardless of historical ethnic enmities
questions.explanation: Although Moab was an enemy of Israel, Ruth chose to follow the God of Israel and was embraced into God’s covenant family, becoming an ancestor of both King David and Jesus Christ. God looks at heart faith, not ethnic origin.
questions.socraticHint: How does Ruth the Moabite being honored in Christ’s genealogy demonstrate God’s welcome of all nations?

questions.prompt: In Colossians 3:12-14, what Christian virtues are believers urged to clothe themselves with to maintain communal harmony?
questions.text: In Colossians 3:12-14, what Christian virtues are believers urged to clothe themselves with to maintain communal harmony?

options.text: Expensive linen robes, gold necklaces, and silver bracelets
Compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience, and above all, love, which binds them all together in perfect unity
Suspicion, envy, pride, tribal arrogance, and bitterness
Military armor, bronze spears, iron shields, and war banners

questions.correctAnswer: Compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience, and above all, love, which binds them all together in perfect unity
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:12-14 urges: "Clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience. Bear with each other and forgive one another... And over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity."
questions.socraticHint: Which list of virtues ends with love as the perfect bond of unity among believers?
