questions.prompt: Two rival schools in Nakuru get into a heated dispute over a controversial referee decision during a football final. What is the Christian peacemaking approach?
questions.text: Two rival schools in Nakuru get into a heated dispute over a controversial referee decision during a football final. What is the Christian peacemaking approach?

options.text: Encourage players to engage in physical fistfights on the pitch to determine who is stronger
Refuse to leave the pitch until the tournament organizers award the trophy to both teams
Encourage team captains and teachers to shake hands, discuss grievances through official sporting mediation, and respect the decision with grace
Start throwing stones and vandalizing the opposing school’s transport bus

questions.correctAnswer: Encourage team captains and teachers to shake hands, discuss grievances through official sporting mediation, and respect the decision with grace
questions.explanation: Christian sportsmanship and peacemaking pursue dialogue, self-control, official mediation, and respectful acceptance over violence, preventing playground disagreements from turning into destructive conflict.
questions.socraticHint: Which approach uses respectful dialogue, sportsmanship, and mediation rather than violence?

questions.prompt: What does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 instruct Christians to pray for regarding our nation’s leaders and government?
questions.text: What does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 instruct Christians to pray for regarding our nation’s leaders and government?

options.text: Pray that leaders experience failure so that new leaders take over every month
Only pray for leaders who belong to our own church denomination
Refuse to pray for government leaders because politics has no connection to faith
Pray for kings and all those in authority, that we may live peaceful and quiet lives in all godliness and holiness

questions.correctAnswer: Pray for kings and all those in authority, that we may live peaceful and quiet lives in all godliness and holiness
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 2:1-2 urges prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving for rulers and all in authority so that society may enjoy peace, order, justice, and the freedom to live godly lives.
questions.socraticHint: Why does Paul urge believers to intercede for leaders so that the nation may enjoy peaceful, godly lives?

questions.prompt: How does living out Christian values of integrity, justice, love, and reconciliation directly contribute to nation building in Kenya?
questions.text: How does living out Christian values of integrity, justice, love, and reconciliation directly contribute to nation building in Kenya?

options.text: It creates trustworthy citizens, eliminates corruption, fosters communal peace, protects the vulnerable, and fulfills our national destiny as a united, prosperous people
It makes sure that all citizens stop working in agriculture and commerce
It ensures that Kenya becomes completely isolated from all neighboring African countries
It replaces the need for schools, hospitals, and national infrastructure

questions.correctAnswer: It creates trustworthy citizens, eliminates corruption, fosters communal peace, protects the vulnerable, and fulfills our national destiny as a united, prosperous people
questions.explanation: When citizens embody Christian values—acting justly, rejecting bribes, loving neighbors across ethnic lines, and serving with integrity—the nation flourishes with peace, trust, economic progress, and moral strength, fulfilling our National Anthem’s prayer for plenty within our borders.
questions.socraticHint: How do personal integrity, social justice, and selfless love transform our schools, communities, and entire nation?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What severe divine warning opens Surah Al-Humazah in the first Ayah?
questions.text: What severe divine warning opens Surah Al-Humazah in the first Ayah?

options.text: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the army of elephants?
Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (defamer)!
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds
By the passing time, indeed mankind is in loss

questions.correctAnswer: Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (defamer)!
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Humazah (104:1) opens with "Wailul-likulli humazatil-lumazah," meaning "Woe to every slanderer and backbiter," severely warning those who mock, insult, or defame others.
questions.socraticHint: Which grave consequence ("Woe") is pronounced upon people who mock and backbite others behind their backs?

questions.prompt: What does the term "Humazah" specifically mean in the context of Islamic ethics and Qur’anic commentary?
questions.text: What does the term "Humazah" specifically mean in the context of Islamic ethics and Qur’anic commentary?

options.text: One who leads prayers at the mosque with a beautiful voice
One who travels long distances across the desert for trade
One who slanders, backbites, or insults others behind their backs
One who gives generous charity to orphans in secret

questions.correctAnswer: One who slanders, backbites, or insults others behind their backs
questions.explanation: In classical Tafsir, "Humazah" refers to a person who criticizes, insults, ridicules, or defames people in their absence through speech or gestures.
questions.socraticHint: Does "Humazah" refer to someone who speaks maliciously about people behind their backs or someone who helps them?

questions.prompt: According to Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 2, what false belief does the hoarder of wealth possess?
questions.text: According to Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 2, what false belief does the hoarder of wealth possess?

options.text: He believes that his wealth will automatically build a school for poor children
He thinks that wealth is a temporary test that must be shared quickly
He believes that true wealth only exists in heaven
He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal (live forever)

questions.correctAnswer: He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal (live forever)
questions.explanation: Ayah 3 states: "Yahsebu anna malahu akhladah"—"He thinks that his wealth will make him last forever." The Qur’an condemns the arrogant delusion that material wealth can save someone from death or judgment.
questions.socraticHint: What unrealistic illusion does the hoarder have about wealth protecting him from death forever?

questions.prompt: What is "Al-Hutamah" as described in Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 4-7?
questions.text: What is "Al-Hutamah" as described in Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 4-7?

options.text: The Crushing Fire of Hell ignited by Allah that ascends over the hearts
A vast mountain of silver in the desert of Arabia
A deep well of fresh, sweet water outside the city of Makkah
A palace of pearls reserved for truthful merchants

questions.correctAnswer: The Crushing Fire of Hell ignited by Allah that ascends over the hearts
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Humazah (104:4-7) describes Al-Hutamah as "The Fire of Allah, fueled and blazing, which mounts right up to the hearts," crushing and consuming the arrogant wrongdoers.
questions.socraticHint: Which severe punishment of Hellfire is described as crushing and ascending over the inner hearts?

questions.prompt: Two learners in a school in Mombasa notice a classmate wearing old torn shoes and begin whispering insults and giggling behind his back. How does Surah Al-Humazah condemn this action?
questions.text: Two learners in a school in Mombasa notice a classmate wearing old torn shoes and begin whispering insults and giggling behind his back. How does Surah Al-Humazah condemn this action?

options.text: It says that making fun of poor people is completely harmless fun
It identifies them as "Humazah" (backbiters and mockers) who face severe divine punishment unless they repent and apologize
It praises them for noticing fashion mistakes in school uniforms
It advises them to take photos of the shoes and post them on social media

questions.correctAnswer: It identifies them as "Humazah" (backbiters and mockers) who face severe divine punishment unless they repent and apologize
questions.explanation: Mocking and slandering a person for poverty or appearance is strictly forbidden in Islam. Surah Al-Humazah warns against this very behavior, demanding empathy, kindness, and repentance.
questions.socraticHint: Which severe warning in the Surah applies directly to laughing at and defaming someone behind their back?

questions.prompt: According to the Prophet Muhammad (SAW), what does the Islamic term "Gheebah" (backbiting) mean?
questions.text: According to the Prophet Muhammad (SAW), what does the Islamic term "Gheebah" (backbiting) mean?

options.text: Reciting the Holy Qur’an aloud during early morning Fajr prayer
Inviting neighbors to attend Eid celebrations at home
Saying something about your brother or sister in their absence that they would dislike hearing
Sharing a packed lunch of dates and milk with a traveling stranger

questions.correctAnswer: Saying something about your brother or sister in their absence that they would dislike hearing
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) defined backbiting: "It is saying something about your brother that he dislikes." When asked, "What if it is true?" he replied, "If it is true, you have backbitten him; and if it is not true, you have slandered (defamed) him."
questions.socraticHint: How did the Prophet (SAW) define mentioning things about another person in their absence that they dislike?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) compare backbiting a fellow Muslim to in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12)?
questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) compare backbiting a fellow Muslim to in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12)?

options.text: Drinking saltwater from the Red Sea
Walking barefoot across hot desert coals
Breaking a clay water pot in the courtyard
Eating the dead flesh of one’s own brother

questions.correctAnswer: Eating the dead flesh of one’s own brother
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12) asks: "Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it!" This vivid, disgusting imagery portrays the grave spiritual ugliness of backbiting.
questions.socraticHint: Which shocking metaphor compares backbiting to consuming the flesh of one’s deceased sibling?

questions.prompt: How can a Muslim businessperson in Kenya avoid the negative behavior condemned in Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 2?
questions.text: How can a Muslim businessperson in Kenya avoid the negative behavior condemned in Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 2?

options.text: By paying honest Zakat, giving Sadaqah to the needy, and using wealth to support community development rather than hoarding it arrogantly
By hiding all profits under the floorboards of their warehouse
By refusing to hire workers and keeping all money locked in safe boxes
By purchasing gold jewelry solely to show off at wedding parties

questions.correctAnswer: By paying honest Zakat, giving Sadaqah to the needy, and using wealth to support community development rather than hoarding it arrogantly
questions.explanation: Islam does not forbid earning wealth honestly, but it condemns hoarding, greed, and arrogance. Wealth should circulate through Zakat, charity, fair wages, and ethical investments that benefit society.
questions.socraticHint: How does giving Zakat and sharing wealth purify wealth and prevent the sin of greedy hoarding?

questions.prompt: What description is given to the gates and columns of Hell in the final verses of Surah Al-Humazah (Ayah 8-9)?
questions.text: What description is given to the gates and columns of Hell in the final verses of Surah Al-Humazah (Ayah 8-9)?

options.text: It will have iron ladders allowing wrongdoers to climb out easily
It will be closed in over them (vaulted shut) in extended, towering columns
It will have open wooden windows overlooking green river valleys
It will be guarded by angels offering cool cups of pomegranate juice

questions.correctAnswer: It will be closed in over them (vaulted shut) in extended, towering columns
questions.explanation: Ayat 8-9 state: "Innaha ‘alayhim mu’sadah, fee ‘amadin mumaddadah"—"Indeed, it is vaulted shut over them, in extended columns," meaning there is no escape for unrepentant evil-doers.
questions.socraticHint: Which phrase describes Hell being vaulted shut in tall towering columns around the wrongdoers?

questions.prompt: When Amina is invited into a school WhatsApp group where pupils are sharing embarrassing pictures of their teacher, what should she do based on Surah Al-Humazah?
questions.text: When Amina is invited into a school WhatsApp group where pupils are sharing embarrassing pictures of their teacher, what should she do based on Surah Al-Humazah?

options.text: Add rude comments under the pictures to show that she is funny
Save the pictures on her phone to show to her family members at dinner
Refuse to take part, advise her classmates that cyberbullying and defamation are sinful, and leave the group
Forward the pictures to other school groups to get more likes and followers

questions.correctAnswer: Refuse to take part, advise her classmates that cyberbullying and defamation are sinful, and leave the group
questions.explanation: Participating in online slander (cyberbullying) is a modern form of "Humazah" and "Lumazah." A conscientious Muslim refuses to take part, stands against wrongdoing, and protects others’ honor.
questions.socraticHint: How does refusing to participate in digital gossip and advising others against cyberbullying protect moral integrity?

questions.prompt: Why does the fire in Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 7 specifically "mount right up to the hearts" (Allati tattali’u ‘ala al-af’idah)?
questions.text: Why does the fire in Surah Al-Humazah Ayah 7 specifically "mount right up to the hearts" (Allati tattali’u ‘ala al-af’idah)?

options.text: Because the heart is the only organ inside the human chest
Because the heart pumps blood to the hands that counted the money
Because physical fire has no effect on any other part of the body
Because the heart is the origin of arrogance, malice, greed, and ill-will toward others

questions.correctAnswer: Because the heart is the origin of arrogance, malice, greed, and ill-will toward others
questions.explanation: In Islamic theology, the heart (Qalb) is the seat of intention, faith, and spiritual health. The sins of malice, pride, and greed originate in the corrupt heart, which is why the divine punishment penetrates to the very core.
questions.socraticHint: Why is the spiritual heart—the center of pride, greed, and hateful thoughts—specifically targeted by the fire?

questions.prompt: Which historic Quraysh leader in Makkah was notorious for slandering the Prophet (SAW) and is cited by many commentators as an example of the character warned in Surah Al-Humazah?
questions.text: Which historic Quraysh leader in Makkah was notorious for slandering the Prophet (SAW) and is cited by many commentators as an example of the character warned in Surah Al-Humazah?

options.text: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah (and Umayyah ibn Khalaf)

questions.correctAnswer: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah (and Umayyah ibn Khalaf)
questions.explanation: Tafsir commentators note that while the moral warning is universal, figures like Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf were notorious for backbiting the Prophet (SAW) and boasting of their immense wealth.
questions.socraticHint: Which arrogant Makkah pagan leader who defamed the Prophet is cited in historical commentaries of this Surah?

questions.prompt: By what magnificent creation does Allah swear an oath in the opening verse of Surah Al-Asr (103:1)?
questions.text: By what magnificent creation does Allah swear an oath in the opening verse of Surah Al-Asr (103:1)?

options.text: By the mountains of the Arabian peninsula
By Time (the declining day / the passing era)
By the mighty cedar trees of Lebanon
By the stars of the desert sky

questions.correctAnswer: By Time (the declining day / the passing era)
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Asr begins: "Wal-‘Asr"—"By time!" Allah swears by time to emphasize its immense preciousness and the fleeting nature of human earthly existence.
questions.socraticHint: Which precious, non-renewable dimension of life does Allah swear by at the beginning of Surah Al-Asr?

questions.prompt: What profound reality about humanity does Allah declare in Ayah 2 of Surah Al-Asr?
questions.text: What profound reality about humanity does Allah declare in Ayah 2 of Surah Al-Asr?

options.text: Mankind will live forever on earth without facing death
Mankind has conquered all the mysteries of the universe
Indeed, mankind is in loss (ruin / deficit)
Mankind will naturally become wealthy without any effort

questions.correctAnswer: Indeed, mankind is in loss (ruin / deficit)
questions.explanation: Ayah 2 states: "Inna al-insana lafee khusr"—"Indeed, mankind is in loss." Every passing moment that is not spent in obedience to Allah represents an eternal deficit and loss for human beings.
questions.socraticHint: What general condition of deficit and "loss" does the Qur’an state all humanity is naturally in?

questions.prompt: How many conditions for escaping loss and attaining salvation are outlined in Surah Al-Asr Ayah 3?
questions.text: How many conditions for escaping loss and attaining salvation are outlined in Surah Al-Asr Ayah 3?

options.text: Ten conditions (Fasting throughout the whole year)
One condition (Memorizing the names of all prophets)
Four conditions (Faith, Righteous Deeds, Advising Truth, Advising Patience)

questions.correctAnswer: Four conditions (Faith, Righteous Deeds, Advising Truth, Advising Patience)
questions.explanation: Ayah 3 lists four essential requirements: 1) Iman (Faith), 2) Amal Salih (Righteous deeds), 3) Tawasaw bil-Haqq (Mutual counsel to truth), and 4) Tawasaw bis-Sabr (Mutual counsel to patience).
questions.socraticHint: Which fourfold path of faith, good works, upholding truth, and patience protects humanity from loss?

questions.prompt: What did the great Islamic scholar Imam Ash-Shafi’i remark about the profound wisdom of Surah Al-Asr?
questions.text: What did the great Islamic scholar Imam Ash-Shafi’i remark about the profound wisdom of Surah Al-Asr?

options.text: If Allah had revealed only this Surah as a proof to His creation, it would have been sufficient for them
This Surah was only meant for ancient desert nomads and not for modern learners
This Surah should only be recited during the pilgrimage of Hajj in Makkah
The Surah is too short to teach any important moral lessons

questions.correctAnswer: If Allah had revealed only this Surah as a proof to His creation, it would have been sufficient for them
questions.explanation: Imam Ash-Shafi’i famously said: "If people were to reflect upon Surah Al-Asr alone, it would suffice them," because it encapsulates the entire human purpose, belief, ethics, and mutual responsibility in three concise verses.
questions.socraticHint: Which famous Imam stated that Surah Al-Asr would have been sufficient for all humanity if nothing else had been revealed?

questions.prompt: What does the third condition, "Tawasaw bil-Haqq" (advising one another to the truth), require of believers in their community?
questions.text: What does the third condition, "Tawasaw bil-Haqq" (advising one another to the truth), require of believers in their community?

options.text: Remaining completely silent when seeing someone being bullied or mistreated
Encouraging one another to stand for justice, obey Allah’s commands, speak truth, and reject falsehood
Agreeing with friends even when they tell lies or cheat in school tests
Demanding that only people from one’s own tribe should be defended in court

questions.correctAnswer: Encouraging one another to stand for justice, obey Allah’s commands, speak truth, and reject falsehood
questions.explanation: "Tawasaw bil-Haqq" means mutually recommending and enjoining truth, justice, sincerity, and divine commandments, ensuring the community remains anchored in righteousness.
questions.socraticHint: What does mutual encouragement in truth and justice require when living among peers and community members?

questions.prompt: What does "Tawasaw bis-Sabr" (advising one another to patience and perseverance) mean for a Grade 5 pupil facing school challenges?
questions.text: What does "Tawasaw bis-Sabr" (advising one another to patience and perseverance) mean for a Grade 5 pupil facing school challenges?

options.text: Complaining loudly and blaming others whenever an exam result is disappointing
Fighting physically with classmates who perform better in academic tests
Supporting friends to remain steadfast, endure hardships patiently, keep working hard, and resist sinful temptations
Telling friends to drop out of school whenever mathematics problems become difficult

questions.correctAnswer: Supporting friends to remain steadfast, endure hardships patiently, keep working hard, and resist sinful temptations
questions.explanation: Sabr encompasses patience in doing good deeds, patience in staying away from sins, and patience during trials. Encouraging friends to persevere through difficulties honors Surah Al-Asr.
questions.socraticHint: How does mutual encouragement in patience and perseverance help learners overcome academic and life hurdles?

questions.prompt: Why is time considered one of the most critical and non-renewable blessings granted by Allah to humanity?
questions.text: Why is time considered one of the most critical and non-renewable blessings granted by Allah to humanity?

options.text: Because time only moves forward during daytime and pauses during the night
Because clocks and watches are expensive items manufactured in European cities
Because humans can store extra minutes in bank accounts for future use
Once time passes, it can never be bought back, stored, or retrieved, and every second brings humans closer to the Day of Judgment

questions.correctAnswer: Once time passes, it can never be bought back, stored, or retrieved, and every second brings humans closer to the Day of Judgment
questions.explanation: Hasan al-Basri famously said: "O son of Adam, you are but a number of days; whenever a day passes, a part of you has gone." Time cannot be recovered, making its righteous use essential.
questions.socraticHint: Can passed time ever be bought back or recovered, or is every fleeting second a non-renewable divine gift?

questions.prompt: Rashid spends six hours every evening playing computer video games, missing his Maghrib and Isha prayers and leaving his homework undone. How does Surah Al-Asr correct Rashid’s lifestyle?
questions.text: Rashid spends six hours every evening playing computer video games, missing his Maghrib and Isha prayers and leaving his homework undone. How does Surah Al-Asr correct Rashid’s lifestyle?

options.text: It warns him that wasting precious time in vanity while neglecting faith, prayers, and duties leads directly to spiritual loss
It encourages him to play for eight hours instead of six so he beats his high score
It says that video games are more important than daily prayers and academic study
It suggests that homework should be thrown away because life on earth is short

questions.correctAnswer: It warns him that wasting precious time in vanity while neglecting faith, prayers, and duties leads directly to spiritual loss
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Asr teaches that wasting life without faith and righteous productivity brings eternal loss. Muslims must steward time responsibly, prioritizing worship, study, and family duties.
questions.socraticHint: How does neglecting prayers and studies for endless gaming lead directly to the spiritual loss warned in Surah Al-Asr?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say about the two blessings that many people are careless with (Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari)?
questions.text: What did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say about the two blessings that many people are careless with (Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari)?

options.text: There are two blessings: Fast camels and Sharp swords
There are two blessings in which many people are deceived (take for granted): Health and Free Time
There are two blessings: Gold jewelry and Silver coins
There are two blessings: High mountains and Flowing rivers

questions.correctAnswer: There are two blessings in which many people are deceived (take for granted): Health and Free Time
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "There are two blessings which many people lose: health and free time" (Bukhari). Both blessings must be invested in good works before illness and busy old age arrive.
questions.socraticHint: Which two precious blessings of physical wellness and available hours did the Prophet say people take for granted?

questions.prompt: How did the noble Companions (Sahabah) demonstrate their deep love for Surah Al-Asr when meeting each other?
questions.text: How did the noble Companions (Sahabah) demonstrate their deep love for Surah Al-Asr when meeting each other?

options.text: They only recited it once a year during the battle of Badr
They refused to recite any other chapter of the Qur’an in their daily prayers
They would not separate or depart until one of them recited Surah Al-Asr to the other as a mutual reminder of their sacred mission
They would write the Surah on stone tablets and bury them in the desert sand

questions.correctAnswer: They would not separate or depart until one of them recited Surah Al-Asr to the other as a mutual reminder of their sacred mission
questions.explanation: Imam At-Tabarani recorded that whenever two Companions of the Prophet (SAW) met, they would not part until one recited Surah Al-Asr to the other and they concluded with greetings of peace (Salam).
questions.socraticHint: What parting tradition of reciting Surah Al-Asr to one another did the Companions practice upon meeting?

questions.prompt: A learner named Fatuma is studying for her end-of-term examinations in Garissa. How does applying the balance of Surah Al-Asr help her organize her day?
questions.text: A learner named Fatuma is studying for her end-of-term examinations in Garissa. How does applying the balance of Surah Al-Asr help her organize her day?

options.text: She decides that because time is passing, revision is unnecessary and she should sleep all day
She stops praying Salah because studying takes all of her available time
She studies continuously without eating or sleeping until she collapses
She creates a balanced daily timetable allocating focused time for daily prayers, syllabus revision, assisting with household chores, and healthy sleep

questions.correctAnswer: She creates a balanced daily timetable allocating focused time for daily prayers, syllabus revision, assisting with household chores, and healthy sleep
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Asr inspires disciplined time management. A balanced Muslim student harmonizes spiritual obligations (prayers), academic excellence, domestic duties, and proper rest.
questions.socraticHint: How does creating a balanced daily schedule for prayer, study, chores, and rest exemplify proper time stewardship?

questions.prompt: How do Surah Al-Humazah and Surah Al-Asr complement each other in shaping the moral character of a Muslim?
questions.text: How do Surah Al-Humazah and Surah Al-Asr complement each other in shaping the moral character of a Muslim?

options.text: Surah Al-Humazah warns against the destructive vices of slander, backbiting, and greed, while Surah Al-Asr provides the positive blueprint of faith, good works, truth, and patience
Surah Al-Humazah is strictly for adults while Surah Al-Asr is strictly for young children
They contradict each other because one praises wealth while the other praises poverty
Neither Surah has any practical relevance to daily social life in modern Kenya

questions.correctAnswer: Surah Al-Humazah warns against the destructive vices of slander, backbiting, and greed, while Surah Al-Asr provides the positive blueprint of faith, good works, truth, and patience
questions.explanation: Together, the two chapters provide both prevention (cleansing oneself of destructive sins like slander and greed in Al-Humazah) and construction (building a righteous life of faith, deeds, truth, and patience in Al-Asr).
questions.socraticHint: How does one Surah warn against destructive speech and greed, while the other builds a positive formula for salvation?

questions.prompt: What does the title "At-Takathur" in the 102nd chapter of the Holy Qur’an mean?
questions.text: What does the title "At-Takathur" in the 102nd chapter of the Holy Qur’an mean?

options.text: The sacred migration from Makkah to Madinah
Mutual rivalry and competition in multiplying worldly increase (wealth and numbers)
The morning sunrise over the desert plains
The opening chapter of the Holy Mushaf

questions.correctAnswer: Mutual rivalry and competition in multiplying worldly increase (wealth and numbers)
questions.explanation: Surah At-Takathur (102:1) addresses "At-Takathur"—the mutual competition, rivalry, and boasting in accumulating material possessions, status, wealth, and children.
questions.socraticHint: Which concept refers to competing with and boasting against others in accumulating possessions and numbers?

questions.prompt: What does Ayah 1-2 of Surah At-Takathur state about what diverts humans from remembering Allah?
questions.text: What does Ayah 1-2 of Surah At-Takathur state about what diverts humans from remembering Allah?

options.text: Farming maize in the highlands diverts you until harvest time
Traveling across the ocean diverts you until you reach port
Competition in worldly increase diverts you, until you visit the graves
Reading books of science diverts you until you become teachers

questions.correctAnswer: Competition in worldly increase diverts you, until you visit the graves
questions.explanation: Ayat 1-2 declare: "Alhakumu at-takathur, hatta zurtumu al-maqabir"—"Competition in worldly increase diverts you, until you visit the graveyards." Obsession with worldly gain distracts people until death.
questions.socraticHint: What competition diverts people until they reach the final destination of the graveyards?

questions.prompt: What profound question of divine accountability concludes Surah At-Takathur in Ayah 8?
questions.text: What profound question of divine accountability concludes Surah At-Takathur in Ayah 8?

options.text: Then you will be asked how many gold coins you accumulated in your house
Then you will be asked why you traveled across foreign countries
Then you will be asked how many war camels were grazing in your paddock
Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the pleasures (blessings of Allah)

questions.correctAnswer: Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the pleasures (blessings of Allah)
questions.explanation: Ayah 8 concludes: "Thumma latus’alunna yawma’idhin ‘ani an-na’eem"—"Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure/delights (blessings)." We must account for how we used every gift from Allah.
questions.socraticHint: What will humans surely be questioned about on the Day of Judgment according to the final Ayah?

questions.prompt: What are examples of "An-Na’eem" (blessings of Allah) that Kenyan learners enjoy and must thank Allah for?
questions.text: What are examples of "An-Na’eem" (blessings of Allah) that Kenyan learners enjoy and must thank Allah for?

options.text: Good health, eyesight, intellect, clean drinking water, food, loving parents, and national peace
Possessing weapons, armored vehicles, and large iron shields
Having the ability to shout louder than teachers during class
Boasting about how many expensive smartphones one’s family owns

questions.correctAnswer: Good health, eyesight, intellect, clean drinking water, food, loving parents, and national peace
questions.explanation: "An-Na’eem" encompasses all divine gifts—life, health, sanity, sight, hearing, safety, cold water on a hot day, and daily nourishment. True gratitude means using these blessings in obedience to Allah.
questions.socraticHint: Which fundamental gifts of physical health, water, food, sight, and family are divine blessings?

questions.prompt: What does "Ilm al-Yaqeen" mean as mentioned in Surah At-Takathur Ayah 5?
questions.text: What does "Ilm al-Yaqeen" mean as mentioned in Surah At-Takathur Ayah 5?

options.text: The temporary rules of games played in the schoolyard
The knowledge of certainty based on divine truth and firm belief
The guesswork of fortune tellers in the marketplace
The human opinion of foreign philosophy teachers

questions.correctAnswer: The knowledge of certainty based on divine truth and firm belief
questions.explanation: "Ilm al-Yaqeen" is the knowledge of absolute certainty that comes from divine revelation, giving a believer unshakeable conviction about the reality of the Hereafter before seeing it physically.
questions.socraticHint: Which level of deep certainty refers to knowledge based on revealed divine truth?

questions.prompt: What does "Ayn al-Yaqeen" refer to in Surah At-Takathur Ayah 7?
questions.text: What does "Ayn al-Yaqeen" refer to in Surah At-Takathur Ayah 7?

options.text: Using a magnifying glass to read Arabic calligraphy in books
Looking at the reflection of the moon in a desert oasis
The vision or sight of certainty (seeing the reality with one’s own physical eyes on the Day of Judgment)
Closing one’s eyes while taking an examination at school

questions.correctAnswer: The vision or sight of certainty (seeing the reality with one’s own physical eyes on the Day of Judgment)
questions.explanation: "Ayn al-Yaqeen" is the certainty that comes from direct physical observation and visual witness, when every soul will see Hellfire and the Day of Judgment clearly before their eyes.
questions.socraticHint: Which certainty refers to witnessing the reality directly with your own physical eyes?

questions.prompt: Two wealthy families in a village in Isiolo constantly compete to see who builds the tallest mansion and buys the most luxury cars, ignoring poor neighbors. How does Surah At-Takathur evaluate their competition?
questions.text: Two wealthy families in a village in Isiolo constantly compete to see who builds the tallest mansion and buys the most luxury cars, ignoring poor neighbors. How does Surah At-Takathur evaluate their competition?

options.text: It praises them as the most beloved servants of Allah in Kenya
It encourages other families to borrow bank loans to join the building competition
It guarantees that tall buildings will be turned into palaces in Paradise
It rebukes their rivalry as a foolish distraction that diverts them from preparing for the grave and eternal accountability

questions.correctAnswer: It rebukes their rivalry as a foolish distraction that diverts them from preparing for the grave and eternal accountability
questions.explanation: Surah At-Takathur directly addresses this foolish vanity: competing in material displays diverts hearts from remembering death, judgment, and using wealth to uplift the needy.
questions.socraticHint: How does the Surah condemn competing in material displays and wasting resources instead of preparing for the grave?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say true richness consists of in Sahih al-Bukhari?
questions.text: What did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say true richness consists of in Sahih al-Bukhari?

options.text: Richness does not lie in an abundance of worldly goods; true richness is the richness of the soul (contentment of the heart)
Richness is having more camels than any tribe in Arabia
Richness is possessing ten palaces made of carved soapstone
Richness is wearing silk clothing embroidered with pure gold threads

questions.correctAnswer: Richness does not lie in an abundance of worldly goods; true richness is the richness of the soul (contentment of the heart)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "Richness is not having many possessions, but richness is the contentment of the soul (Ghina an-Nafs)." A contented heart is peaceful and free from greedy competition.
questions.socraticHint: Did the Prophet say true wealth comes from an abundance of possessions or from inner contentment of the soul?

questions.prompt: How does the Islamic virtue of "Shukr" (gratitude) protect a believer from the traps of At-Takathur?
questions.text: How does the Islamic virtue of "Shukr" (gratitude) protect a believer from the traps of At-Takathur?

options.text: It requires people to give away their clothes and walk without shoes
It makes a person appreciate whatever Allah has provided, fostering inner peace, generosity, and contentment instead of greedy comparison
It makes a person boast to their classmates that Allah favors them more than others
It encourages believers to stop working because gratitude produces magic food

questions.correctAnswer: It makes a person appreciate whatever Allah has provided, fostering inner peace, generosity, and contentment instead of greedy comparison
questions.explanation: Shukr recognizes that all blessings come from Allah. A grateful believer is content with their provision, thanks Allah with worship, and shares with others rather than obsessing over having more than their neighbor.
questions.socraticHint: How does thanking Allah for what you have cultivate contentment and eliminate envious competition?

questions.prompt: When pupils at school compare the brands of their school bags and mock those with plain bags, what advice from Surah At-Takathur should be shared?
questions.text: When pupils at school compare the brands of their school bags and mock those with plain bags, what advice from Surah At-Takathur should be shared?

options.text: Encourage them to hide the bags of poor pupils in the latrines
Tell them that school bags determine a person’s eternal rank in Jannah
Remind them that material brands are fleeting and unimpressive to Allah; what matters is knowledge, good character, and thanking Allah for having a bag
Advise them to ask their parents to buy even more expensive bags on credit

questions.correctAnswer: Remind them that material brands are fleeting and unimpressive to Allah; what matters is knowledge, good character, and thanking Allah for having a bag
questions.explanation: Surah At-Takathur teaches that competing in material brands is vanity. In Islam, nobility is determined by Taqwa (God-consciousness) and moral conduct, not designer logos or wealth.
questions.socraticHint: Why are good character, knowledge, and gratitude far more valuable than competing over material brands?

questions.prompt: Why does Surah At-Takathur use the phrase "until you visit the graves" (Hatta zurtumu al-maqabir) to describe death?
questions.text: Why does Surah At-Takathur use the phrase "until you visit the graves" (Hatta zurtumu al-maqabir) to describe death?

options.text: Because dead bodies stay in the grave for only twenty-four hours before disappearing
Because humans can leave the cemetery whenever they wish to visit relatives
To indicate that visiting cemeteries on weekends is the only duty of Muslims
To signify that the grave is merely a temporary resting place (Barzakh) and visit, because the final eternal home is in the Hereafter

questions.correctAnswer: To signify that the grave is merely a temporary resting place (Barzakh) and visit, because the final eternal home is in the Hereafter
questions.explanation: The word "zurtum" (you visited) subtly implies that a stay in the grave is not the permanent end; it is a temporary stage (Barzakh) before the resurrection to eternal accountability in the Hereafter.
questions.socraticHint: Why is the grave called a "visit" rather than a permanent destination in the journey of the soul?

questions.prompt: What core lesson does Surah At-Takathur convey about human purpose on earth?
questions.text: What core lesson does Surah At-Takathur convey about human purpose on earth?

options.text: Human life is not an endless contest to amass worldly possessions, but a sacred trust to worship Allah, practice gratitude, and prepare for eternal reckoning
Humans should focus on hoarding as much gold as possible before becoming old
Humans should never own any clothes, food, or shelter in this worldly life
The only purpose of human existence is to boast of numbers and clan ancestry

questions.correctAnswer: Human life is not an endless contest to amass worldly possessions, but a sacred trust to worship Allah, practice gratitude, and prepare for eternal reckoning
questions.explanation: The overarching message of Surah At-Takathur is that life is a purposeful preparation for eternity. Earthly blessings are tests of stewardship, not trophies for self-glorification or boastful rivalry.
questions.socraticHint: What higher spiritual purpose of worship, gratitude, and moral accountability defines human life on earth?

questions.prompt: What is the literal meaning of the title "Al-Qari’ah" in Surah 101 of the Holy Qur’an?
questions.text: What is the literal meaning of the title "Al-Qari’ah" in Surah 101 of the Holy Qur’an?

options.text: The Holy City where the Prophet was born
The Striking Calamity (The Day of Resurrection that strikes hearts with awe)
The Morning Star that shines in the dawn sky
The Gentle Breeze that blows over the ocean waters

questions.correctAnswer: The Striking Calamity (The Day of Resurrection that strikes hearts with awe)
questions.explanation: "Al-Qari’ah" comes from the Arabic root meaning "to strike with sudden, loud impact." It refers to the Day of Resurrection, whose immense thunderous reality strikes fear and awe into all hearts.
questions.socraticHint: Which title translates as "The Striking Calamity," referring to the awe-inspiring Day of Judgment?

questions.prompt: How will human beings appear on the Day of Al-Qari’ah according to Ayah 4?
questions.text: How will human beings appear on the Day of Al-Qari’ah according to Ayah 4?

options.text: Like birds singing joyfully in tall green trees
Like fish swimming peacefully in deep ocean waters
Like moths scattered about in confusion (Ka-al-farashi al-mabthuth)
Like stone statues standing frozen in rows

questions.correctAnswer: Like moths scattered about in confusion (Ka-al-farashi al-mabthuth)
questions.explanation: Ayah 4 states: "Yawma yakoonu an-nasu ka-al-farashi al-mabthuth"—"The Day mankind will be like moths scattered about," wandering in overwhelming shock, confusion, and awe.
questions.socraticHint: Which small, fragile winged creatures scattered in confusion describe the state of humanity on that Day?

questions.prompt: What will happen to the solid, massive mountains on that Day according to Ayah 5?
questions.text: What will happen to the solid, massive mountains on that Day according to Ayah 5?

options.text: They will grow twice as high and touch the clouds
They will turn into solid bars of pure gold and silver
They will remain completely undisturbed without any change
They will be like fluffed, carded wool floating in the air (Ka-al-’ihni al-manfush)

questions.correctAnswer: They will be like fluffed, carded wool floating in the air (Ka-al-’ihni al-manfush)
questions.explanation: Ayah 5 says: "Wa takoonu al-jibalu ka-al-’ihni al-manfush"—"And the mountains will be like carded wool." Even the mightiest mountains will crumble into lightweight, floating fibers of dust.
questions.socraticHint: Which soft, fluffy textile material floating in the air describes the crumbled state of mountains?

questions.prompt: What divine instrument of justice is used to evaluate human deeds in Surah Al-Qari’ah Ayah 6-8?
questions.text: What divine instrument of justice is used to evaluate human deeds in Surah Al-Qari’ah Ayah 6-8?

options.text: A golden measuring tape used by angels
An hourglass filled with colored sand
A written examination paper with multiple-choice questions

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qari’ah refers to "Mawazin" (the Scales of justice). On the Day of Judgment, every person’s righteous deeds and evil actions will be placed upon the Mizan to be weighed with absolute divine precision.
questions.socraticHint: Which instrument of weighing (the Scales/Mizan) measures the heavy and light balance of deeds?

questions.prompt: What joyful reward awaits the person whose scale of good deeds is heavy in Ayah 6-7?
questions.text: What joyful reward awaits the person whose scale of good deeds is heavy in Ayah 6-7?

options.text: He will be sent back to earth to live for another hundred years
He will be in a life of pleasant, well-pleased contentment in Jannah (Paradise)
He will be granted a crown of diamonds to reign as king of an earthly island
He will never have to answer any questions about his past actions

questions.correctAnswer: He will be in a life of pleasant, well-pleased contentment in Jannah (Paradise)
questions.explanation: Ayat 6-7 state: "Fa-amma man thaqulat mawazeenuhu, fahuwa fee ‘eeshatin radiyah"—"Then as for him whose scales are heavy [with good deeds], he will be in a pleasant, well-pleased life in Paradise."
questions.socraticHint: What blissful and well-pleased life in Paradise awaits the one whose righteous deeds tip the scales?

questions.prompt: What will be the dwelling of the person whose scale of good deeds is light in Ayah 8-9?
questions.text: What will be the dwelling of the person whose scale of good deeds is light in Ayah 8-9?

options.text: A comfortable room in the palace of the angels
An ordinary village house on the outskirts of Makkah
His refuge and dwelling will be the Abyss (Hawiyah)
A quiet garden by the side of a cold mountain stream

questions.correctAnswer: His refuge and dwelling will be the Abyss (Hawiyah)
questions.explanation: Ayat 8-9 declare: "Wa-amma man khaffat mawazeenuhu, fa-ummuhu hawiyah"—"But as for him whose balance is light, his mother [dwelling/refuge] will be an abyss (Hawiyah)."
questions.socraticHint: Which terrible abyss (Hawiyah) is named as the dwelling for those whose good deeds are light?

questions.prompt: How does Allah describe "Hawiyah" in the concluding Ayat 10-11 of Surah Al-Qari’ah?
questions.text: How does Allah describe "Hawiyah" in the concluding Ayat 10-11 of Surah Al-Qari’ah?

options.text: It is a cold, icy cave beneath the ocean floor
It is an endless desert with howling winds and dust
It is a dark cloud that blocks out the sunlight
It is "Narun hamiyah"—an intensely blazing, scorching fire!

questions.correctAnswer: It is "Narun hamiyah"—an intensely blazing, scorching fire!
questions.explanation: Ayat 10-11 explain: "Wa ma adraka ma hiyah? Narun hamiyah!"—"And what can make you know what it is? It is a Fire, intensely blazing and hot!"
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic phrase meaning an intensely scorching and blazing fire describes Hawiyah?

questions.prompt: What everyday good actions can a Grade 5 pupil in Kenya perform to make their scales heavy on the Day of Judgment?
questions.text: What everyday good actions can a Grade 5 pupil in Kenya perform to make their scales heavy on the Day of Judgment?

options.text: Praying on time, speaking the truth, being respectful to parents and teachers, helping classmates, and giving charity
Boasting about how many expensive clothes they own compared to others
Cheating on exams and hiding other students’ books in the rubbish bin
Refusing to help with home chores and arguing with elderly neighbors

questions.correctAnswer: Praying on time, speaking the truth, being respectful to parents and teachers, helping classmates, and giving charity
questions.explanation: Every righteous deed—performing Salah, truthfulness, kindness to parents, assisting peers, cleaning the environment, and saying Dhikr—carries real weight on the divine Scales (Mizan).
questions.socraticHint: Which set of actions includes punctuality in prayer, honesty, filial respect, and kindness?

questions.prompt: What easy phrase did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) describe as "light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful"?
questions.text: What easy phrase did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) describe as "light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful"?

options.text: Astaghfirullahal-Adheem al-ladhi la ilaha illa Huwa
La hawla wala quwwata illa billahil-Kabir

questions.explanation: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet (SAW) said: "Two words are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: ‘SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil-Adheem’" (Glory and praise be to Allah, Glory be to Allah the Almighty).
questions.socraticHint: Which pair of tasbeeh phrases praising Allah’s majesty and perfection is famously heavy on the Scales?

questions.prompt: Why does Surah Al-Qari’ah describe the refuge of the wicked as their "mother" (Fa-ummuhu hawiyah)?
questions.text: Why does Surah Al-Qari’ah describe the refuge of the wicked as their "mother" (Fa-ummuhu hawiyah)?

options.text: Because the word for mother in Arabic has no other linguistic meaning
Because the wrongdoer will be given a comfortable bed inside the abyss
Just as a mother clings to and holds her child closely, the pit of Hellfire will cling to and envelop the wrongdoer without letting them go
Because mothers in Makkah were responsible for taking care of desert fires

questions.correctAnswer: Just as a mother clings to and holds her child closely, the pit of Hellfire will cling to and envelop the wrongdoer without letting them go
questions.explanation: Linguists and Tafsir scholars explain that "his mother will be Hawiyah" means the Abyss will embrace, cling to, and envelop the condemned like a mother tightly clasping her child, with no possibility of release.
questions.socraticHint: How does the metaphor of a mother embracing her child convey how inescapably the abyss will envelop the wrongdoer?

questions.prompt: How does knowing that our deeds will be weighed on the Mizan encourage a learner to do small acts of kindness?
questions.text: How does knowing that our deeds will be weighed on the Mizan encourage a learner to do small acts of kindness?

options.text: It shows that small deeds are completely ignored and only millionaires can enter Paradise
It proves that deeds on earth have no connection to what happens after death
It suggests that people should only do good deeds when other people are watching and applauding
It teaches that no good deed is too small; even removing a thorn from a path or offering a friendly smile can tip the balance toward Paradise

questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that no good deed is too small; even removing a thorn from a path or offering a friendly smile can tip the balance toward Paradise
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "Do not regard any good deed as insignificant, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face." On the Scales, every atom’s weight of good (Zarratin khayran) counts (Surah Az-Zalzalah 99:7).
questions.socraticHint: Why is no good deed insignificant when every single righteous action adds real weight to the Scales?

questions.prompt: What common theme unites both Surah At-Takathur and Surah Al-Qari’ah in the Holy Qur’an?
questions.text: What common theme unites both Surah At-Takathur and Surah Al-Qari’ah in the Holy Qur’an?

options.text: Both chapters emphasize the reality of the Hereafter, warning against being distracted by temporary worldly pursuits and urging believers to prepare righteous deeds for the Scales of Judgment
Both chapters explain the military victories of Islamic armies in ancient Persia
Both chapters describe how to build wooden trade sailing dhows on the Indian Ocean
Both chapters give rules on how to conduct business partnerships in foreign marketplaces

questions.correctAnswer: Both chapters emphasize the reality of the Hereafter, warning against being distracted by temporary worldly pursuits and urging believers to prepare righteous deeds for the Scales of Judgment
questions.explanation: Both Makkan chapters call humanity to awaken from the stupor of worldly obsession: At-Takathur warns against material distraction until the grave, while Al-Qari’ah depicts the dramatic reckoning where only heavy scales of good deeds will matter.
questions.socraticHint: How do both chapters call humans to look past temporary worldly vanity and focus on eternal accountability and good deeds?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What are the two foundational components that make up any authentic Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?
questions.text: What are the two foundational components that make up any authentic Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?

options.text: The City of Makkah and the Valley of Madinah
The Isnad (chain of trustworthy narrators) and the Matn (the actual text or statement)
The Title of the chapter and the Page number of the book
The Arabic alphabet and the Swahili translation notes

questions.correctAnswer: The Isnad (chain of trustworthy narrators) and the Matn (the actual text or statement)
questions.explanation: In Hadith science (Mustalah al-Hadith), an authentic report consists of the Isnad (the unbroken chain of reliable transmitters reaching the Prophet) and the Matn (the text and message spoken or demonstrated).
questions.socraticHint: Which pair of Arabic terms identifies the transmission chain of narrators and the actual spoken text?

questions.prompt: What comprehensive principle of charity did the Prophet (SAW) teach in the Hadith: "Kullu ma’roofin sadaqah"?
questions.text: What comprehensive principle of charity did the Prophet (SAW) teach in the Hadith: "Kullu ma’roofin sadaqah"?

options.text: Charity is strictly reserved for wealthy merchants with large herds
Good deeds are only accepted during the holy month of Ramadan
Every good deed is an act of charity (Sadaqah)
Only gold coins given to kings count as charity

questions.correctAnswer: Every good deed is an act of charity (Sadaqah)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated: "Kullu ma’roofin sadaqah"—"Every good deed is charity." This broadens the definition of charity beyond monetary wealth to include any righteous, kind, or helpful action.
questions.socraticHint: How did the Prophet summarize that every single kind, moral, and helpful action is counted as charity?

questions.prompt: In Jami’ at-Tirmidhi, what simple, cost-free facial expression did the Prophet (SAW) say is rewarded as charity?
questions.text: In Jami’ at-Tirmidhi, what simple, cost-free facial expression did the Prophet (SAW) say is rewarded as charity?

options.text: Frowning seriously to look important to others
Winking with one eye while speaking to elders
Staring coldly without greeting anyone on the road
Smiling in the face of your brother or sister

questions.correctAnswer: Smiling in the face of your brother or sister
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "Tabassumuka fee wajhi akheeka laka sadaqah"—"Smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you." A cheerful, warm smile spreads joy and brotherhood.
questions.socraticHint: Which cheerful expression costs no money yet brings joy and is rewarded as an act of Sadaqah?

questions.prompt: What environmental action did the Prophet (SAW) specifically identify as an act of charity in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim?
questions.text: What environmental action did the Prophet (SAW) specifically identify as an act of charity in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim?

options.text: Removing harmful objects (stones, thorns, litter) from the pathway
Digging deep pits in the middle of school playing fields
Throwing plastic bags into flowing river waters
Chopping down indigenous trees in town parks for fun

questions.correctAnswer: Removing harmful objects (stones, thorns, litter) from the pathway
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "And removing harmful things from the road is an act of charity." Keeping roads and paths clear of thorns, nails, stones, and litter protects people from injury.
questions.socraticHint: Which civic and environmental action prevents injury to travelers and is counted as Sadaqah?

questions.prompt: A learner in Garissa sees broken glass on the path where barefoot children walk to school. Applying the Hadith on Sadaqah, what should the learner do?
questions.text: A learner in Garissa sees broken glass on the path where barefoot children walk to school. Applying the Hadith on Sadaqah, what should the learner do?

options.text: Laugh and wait to see which classmate steps on the glass
Carefully pick up the broken glass using a stick or safe tool and dispose of it properly in a rubbish bin
Kick the broken glass deeper into the pathway so people step on it
Run past quickly without caring because someone else will clean it

questions.correctAnswer: Carefully pick up the broken glass using a stick or safe tool and dispose of it properly in a rubbish bin
questions.explanation: Removing harmful debris protects the community and directly fulfills the prophetic teaching on charity, earning reward from Allah and demonstrating responsible citizenship.
questions.socraticHint: Which protective action safely removes the hazardous obstacle to protect fellow schoolmates from injury?

questions.prompt: According to prophetic Hadith, what kind of words are rewarded as an act of charity (Sadaqah)?
questions.text: According to prophetic Hadith, what kind of words are rewarded as an act of charity (Sadaqah)?

options.text: Boastful words about how rich one’s parents are
Lies told to save a friend from being punished by a teacher
A good, kind, and peaceful word (Al-Kalimatu at-tayyibah sadaqah)
Sharp, sarcastic insults that make everyone in class laugh

questions.correctAnswer: A good, kind, and peaceful word (Al-Kalimatu at-tayyibah sadaqah)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "Al-kalimatu at-tayyibah sadaqah"—"A good word is charity." Speaking politely, comforting the sad, encouraging a struggling classmate, and giving good advice are all rewarded.
questions.socraticHint: What kind of words ("Al-Kalimah at-Tayyibah") that bring comfort and truth are rewarded as Sadaqah?

questions.prompt: How does planting trees and crops qualify as ongoing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah) in prophetic teachings?
questions.text: How does planting trees and crops qualify as ongoing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah) in prophetic teachings?

options.text: Because trees turn into solid blocks of silver in Paradise
Because only people who own orchards are allowed to enter the mosque
Because chopping down trees is mandatory during festival days
Whenever a bird, wild animal, or human eats fruit or finds shade from that tree, it is recorded as a continuous charity for the planter

questions.correctAnswer: Whenever a bird, wild animal, or human eats fruit or finds shade from that tree, it is recorded as a continuous charity for the planter
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "There is no Muslim who plants a tree or sows seeds and then a bird, or a person, or an animal eats from it, but it is regarded as a charity for him" (Bukhari and Muslim).
questions.socraticHint: How does providing nourishment and shade for birds, animals, and humans yield continuous charity?

questions.prompt: Bilal does not have pocket money to donate to the school charity box. How can he practice Sadaqah based on the Hadith of good deeds?
questions.text: Bilal does not have pocket money to donate to the school charity box. How can he practice Sadaqah based on the Hadith of good deeds?

options.text: By helping sweep the classroom, smiling warmly at peers, speaking kindly, and assisting a classmate with physical challenges
By borrowing money from a shopkeeper with interest to put in the charity box
By feeling sad and believing that poor children have no way to earn rewards from Allah
By taking money from his mother’s purse without permission to give to charity

questions.correctAnswer: By helping sweep the classroom, smiling warmly at peers, speaking kindly, and assisting a classmate with physical challenges
questions.explanation: Islam opens the door of charity to all people. Physical help, cheerful smiles, kind speech, and caring for others are authentic forms of non-monetary Sadaqah fully rewarded by Allah.
questions.socraticHint: Which practical everyday actions of helpfulness, warm smiles, and kind words provide non-financial Sadaqah?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) say about directing someone to a good action (Hadith in Sahih Muslim)?
questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) say about directing someone to a good action (Hadith in Sahih Muslim)?

options.text: Only religious scholars are permitted to direct people toward good deeds
The one who guides someone to a good deed will have a reward equal to the one who performs it
Guiding others takes away all the reward from your own good deeds
You should keep good deeds a secret so no one else learns how to do them

questions.correctAnswer: The one who guides someone to a good deed will have a reward equal to the one who performs it
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "Man dalla ‘ala khayrin falahu mithlu ajri fa’ilihi"—"Whoever guides someone to a good deed will have a reward like that of its doer." Encouraging others multiplies our own rewards.
questions.socraticHint: What equal reward is granted to someone who guides and encourages another person to do a good deed?

questions.prompt: How does greeting a fellow Muslim with "As-salamu alaykum" (Peace be upon you) fulfill the Hadith of good deeds?
questions.text: How does greeting a fellow Muslim with "As-salamu alaykum" (Peace be upon you) fulfill the Hadith of good deeds?

options.text: It is a secret password that allows people into trading markets
It replaces the need to perform the five daily prayers
It is a prayer of peace, mercy, and divine blessing that fosters love, breaks arrogance, and is rewarded as a good deed
It is a military greeting only used when greeting army commanders

questions.correctAnswer: It is a prayer of peace, mercy, and divine blessing that fosters love, breaks arrogance, and is rewarded as a good deed
questions.explanation: The Salam greeting is an act of worship and charity. The Prophet (SAW) taught: "You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I guide you to something that will spread love? Spread peace (Salam) among yourselves."
questions.socraticHint: How does spreading the greeting of peace foster communal love and earn divine rewards as a good deed?

questions.prompt: Why did the Prophet (SAW) emphasize non-monetary acts of charity alongside financial Sadaqah?
questions.text: Why did the Prophet (SAW) emphasize non-monetary acts of charity alongside financial Sadaqah?

options.text: Because physical money has no real value in the sight of Allah
To prevent wealthy people from giving their wealth to the poor
Because the early Muslim community had completely banned the use of gold coins
To ensure that every believer, rich or poor, can earn immense spiritual rewards and cultivate a compassionate, active character in society

questions.correctAnswer: To ensure that every believer, rich or poor, can earn immense spiritual rewards and cultivate a compassionate, active character in society
questions.explanation: By including smiles, good speech, guiding travelers, and removing obstacles, Islam democratizes charity, empowering every individual to actively contribute to community welfare and spiritual elevation regardless of wealth.
questions.socraticHint: How does defining good deeds as charity allow every person regardless of income to participate in Sadaqah?

questions.prompt: Which of the following actions best illustrates the spirit of "Kullu ma’roofin sadaqah" in a Kenyan primary school?
questions.text: Which of the following actions best illustrates the spirit of "Kullu ma’roofin sadaqah" in a Kenyan primary school?

options.text: Sharing a textbook with a classmate who forgot theirs, listening patiently to a troubled friend, and picking up dropped pens
Demanding rent before allowing a classmate to sit at the same wooden desk
Hiding revision questions from other students so only you get the top grade
Mocking pupils who make pronunciation mistakes during English reading

questions.correctAnswer: Sharing a textbook with a classmate who forgot theirs, listening patiently to a troubled friend, and picking up dropped pens
questions.explanation: Every act of selfless kindness, sharing learning materials, offering comfort, and helping peers embodies the prophetic standard of "Every good deed is charity."
questions.socraticHint: Which collection of everyday helpful actions demonstrates true non-monetary charity at school?

questions.prompt: How did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) define true strength in the famous Hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah (RA)?
questions.text: How did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) define true strength in the famous Hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah (RA)?

options.text: The strong person is the one who shouts insults louder than anyone else
The strong person is not the one who overpowers others in wrestling; the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry
The strong person is the one who can lift fifty heavy sacks of grain at the market
The strong person is the one who carries the heaviest iron shield in battle

questions.correctAnswer: The strong person is not the one who overpowers others in wrestling; the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "Laysa ash-shadeedu bis-sura’ah, innama ash-shadeedu alladhee yamliku nafsahu ‘inda al-ghadab"—"The strong person is not the one who can wrestle others down; rather, the strong person is the one who controls himself in anger."
questions.socraticHint: Does the Prophet define true strength as physical muscle power or as self-control over anger?

questions.prompt: What spiritual phrase did the Prophet (SAW) instruct a person to recite when they feel the heat of anger rising within them?
questions.text: What spiritual phrase did the Prophet (SAW) instruct a person to recite when they feel the heat of anger rising within them?

options.text: A’udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajeem (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan)

questions.correctAnswer: A’udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajeem (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan)
questions.explanation: When two men argued in front of the Prophet (SAW) and one became red with anger, the Prophet said: "I know a word which, if he were to say it, what he feels would leave him: ‘A’udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajeem’" (Bukhari).
questions.socraticHint: Which phrase of seeking refuge in Allah from Satan cools down the fire of rage?

questions.prompt: What physical action did the Prophet (SAW) advise a person to take if they become angry while standing up (Sunan Abi Dawud)?
questions.text: What physical action did the Prophet (SAW) advise a person to take if they become angry while standing up (Sunan Abi Dawud)?

options.text: He should run around the house three times shouting loudly
He should punch the nearest wooden door to release energy
He should climb onto the roof of the house and stay there
He should sit down; if the anger leaves him, well and good, otherwise he should lie down

questions.correctAnswer: He should sit down; if the anger leaves him, well and good, otherwise he should lie down
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "When one of you becomes angry while standing, he should sit down. If the anger leaves him, fine; otherwise, he should lie down." Lowering posture reduces physical arousal and prevents aggressive actions.
questions.socraticHint: What change of physical posture from standing to sitting down calms rising anger?

questions.prompt: Why does performing Wudhu (ablution) with cool water help extinguish anger according to prophetic wisdom?
questions.text: Why does performing Wudhu (ablution) with cool water help extinguish anger according to prophetic wisdom?

options.text: Anger is from Satan, who was created from fire, and fire is extinguished by water
Wudhu is only meant to wash off physical dirt from the hands
Cold water makes a person sleepy so they forget why they were angry
Water washes away all memory of who offended you

questions.correctAnswer: Anger is from Satan, who was created from fire, and fire is extinguished by water
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) explained: "Anger comes from the devil, and the devil was created from fire; fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you gets angry, let him perform ablution (Wudhu)" (Abu Dawud).
questions.socraticHint: How does washing with cool water physically and spiritually extinguish the fiery temper sparked by Satan?

questions.prompt: What threefold social guideline did the Prophet (SAW) link directly to faith in Allah and the Last Day (Sahih al-Bukhari)?
questions.text: What threefold social guideline did the Prophet (SAW) link directly to faith in Allah and the Last Day (Sahih al-Bukhari)?

options.text: Whoever believes in Allah should travel across the sea every three months
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor, honor his guest, and speak good or remain silent
Whoever believes in Allah should conquer foreign cities, collect gold, and build fortresses
Whoever believes in Allah should never speak to strangers, never share food, and live in isolation

questions.correctAnswer: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor, honor his guest, and speak good or remain silent
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) declared: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent."
questions.socraticHint: Which three duties—honoring neighbors, welcoming guests, and guarding speech—are signs of true faith in the Last Day?

questions.prompt: How did the Prophet (SAW) emphasize the rights of the neighbor regarding Archangel Jibril’s repeated reminders?
questions.text: How did the Prophet (SAW) emphasize the rights of the neighbor regarding Archangel Jibril’s repeated reminders?

options.text: Jibril advised that neighbors should never share food during festivals
Jibril warned that neighbors should only be greeted once a year
Jibril kept enjoining good treatment of the neighbor so persistently that the Prophet thought he would make the neighbor an heir to his estate
Jibril instructed that neighbors should build stone walls between their compounds

questions.correctAnswer: Jibril kept enjoining good treatment of the neighbor so persistently that the Prophet thought he would make the neighbor an heir to his estate
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "Jibril continued to advise me to treat neighbors well until I thought he would make them heirs" (Bukhari & Muslim). This shows the sacred, profound importance of neighborly kindness in Islam.
questions.socraticHint: What extreme level of neighborly care did Jibril advise, to the point of almost making the neighbor an heir?

questions.prompt: In a housing estate in Nakuru, a neighbor plays loud music late at night, disturbing babies and elderly residents. How does this behavior violate prophetic teachings?
questions.text: In a housing estate in Nakuru, a neighbor plays loud music late at night, disturbing babies and elderly residents. How does this behavior violate prophetic teachings?

options.text: Playing loud music is recommended because it keeps neighborhood watchmen awake
It is permissible as long as the music has lyrics praising ancient kingdoms
The Prophet encouraged disturbing neighbors to test their level of patience
The Prophet (SAW) stated: "By Allah, he does not believe... the one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm and annoyance"

questions.correctAnswer: The Prophet (SAW) stated: "By Allah, he does not believe... the one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm and annoyance"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) solemnly swore: "By Allah, he does not believe! ... He whose neighbor is not safe from his mischief/harm (Bawa’iqahu)" (Bukhari). Causing noise pollution and disturbance harms neighbors and violates Islamic ethics.
questions.socraticHint: Which severe Hadith warns that one whose neighbor is not safe from their harm lacks true faith?

questions.prompt: During a football match at school, an opponent accidentally trips Hamza. Hamza feels an urge to punch the opponent. What is the prophetic response?
questions.text: During a football match at school, an opponent accidentally trips Hamza. Hamza feels an urge to punch the opponent. What is the prophetic response?

options.text: Control his anger, say "A’udhu billah," accept the opponent’s apology, and shake hands with sportsmanship
Punch the opponent immediately to prove that he is a strong fighter
Throw mud at the referee and storm off the football pitch shouting insults
Call older siblings to beat up the opponent after school dismisses

questions.correctAnswer: Control his anger, say "A’udhu billah," accept the opponent’s apology, and shake hands with sportsmanship
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) praised the one who controls their temper in provocation. Controlling his reaction proves Hamza’s true moral strength, diffusing violence and showing Islamic sportsmanship.
questions.socraticHint: Which reaction demonstrates true strength through self-restraint and peaceful forgiveness over retaliation?

questions.prompt: How should a Muslim family treat a non-Muslim neighbor who lives next door in a Kenyan estate?
questions.text: How should a Muslim family treat a non-Muslim neighbor who lives next door in a Kenyan estate?

options.text: By demanding that they convert to Islam before receiving any neighborly assistance
With full neighborly respect, kindness, sharing food, checking on them in illness, and living in peaceful coexistence
By ignoring them completely and refusing to greet them because of different religious beliefs
By throwing garbage over their fence into their compound

questions.correctAnswer: With full neighborly respect, kindness, sharing food, checking on them in illness, and living in peaceful coexistence
questions.explanation: Scholars of Islam explain that neighbors have rights: a non-Muslim neighbor who is not a relative has the sacred right of neighborliness (Haqq al-Jiwar). Kindness, fairness, and generosity are owed to all neighbors regardless of religion.
questions.socraticHint: Does Islamic neighborly duty require kindness, respect, and peaceful coexistence toward all neighbors regardless of their faith?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) advise his companion Abu Dharr (RA) regarding cooking broth at home (Sahih Muslim)?
questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) advise his companion Abu Dharr (RA) regarding cooking broth at home (Sahih Muslim)?

options.text: Sell leftover soup to your neighbors for a few copper coins
Never cook hot meals when guests are visiting your house
When you cook broth (soup/stew), add more water to it and send some of it to your neighbors with kindness
Cook only inside closed rooms so your neighbors do not smell your food

questions.correctAnswer: When you cook broth (soup/stew), add more water to it and send some of it to your neighbors with kindness
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) advised Abu Dharr: "When you cook broth, increase its water and take care of your neighbors." This beautiful tradition encourages sharing food and looking after neighbors’ well-being.
questions.socraticHint: What advice about adding more water to cooked broth to share with neighbors did the Prophet give Abu Dharr?

questions.prompt: Why does the Prophet (SAW) command: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent"?
questions.text: Why does the Prophet (SAW) command: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent"?

options.text: Because humans have a limited quota of words they can speak before losing their voices
Because speaking in public was forbidden by ancient Arabian customary laws
Because silence is the only method to prevent human beings from catching illnesses
Because words carry moral weight; speaking good builds love and earns rewards, while speaking careless evil causes harm and divine accountability

questions.correctAnswer: Because words carry moral weight; speaking good builds love and earns rewards, while speaking careless evil causes harm and divine accountability
questions.explanation: Speech is a reflection of the soul. Controlling one’s speech prevents slander, lies, insults, and gossip. If one cannot say something truthful, kind, or beneficial, silence is the safest and most righteous path.
questions.socraticHint: Why is keeping silent better than uttering words that cause hurt, falsehood, or sin?

questions.prompt: What profound connection exists between emotional self-control, neighborly kindness, and genuine faith (Iman)?
questions.text: What profound connection exists between emotional self-control, neighborly kindness, and genuine faith (Iman)?

options.text: Faith is not just theoretical ritual; it must be manifested through gentle emotional restraint, gracious neighborly relations, and protective social harmony
Faith requires physical isolation from all neighbors and community members
Faith allows believers to be angry and aggressive whenever they want
Emotional restraint and neighborly rights were invented by modern civil laws without spiritual basis

questions.correctAnswer: Faith is not just theoretical ritual; it must be manifested through gentle emotional restraint, gracious neighborly relations, and protective social harmony
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) repeatedly linked belief in Allah and the Last Day with social ethics: controlling anger, treating neighbors with honor, and guarding speech prove that faith has transformed one’s character.
questions.socraticHint: How do self-control, peaceful speech, and honoring neighbors prove that true faith resides in a believer’s heart?

questions.prompt: In which mountain and cave outside Makkah did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) retreat for worship and contemplation before receiving revelation?
questions.text: In which mountain and cave outside Makkah did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) retreat for worship and contemplation before receiving revelation?

options.text: Cave Hira atop Jabal an-Nur (Mount of Light)
Mount Sinai in the Sinai desert

questions.correctAnswer: Cave Hira atop Jabal an-Nur (Mount of Light)
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) retreated to Cave Hira located on Jabal an-Nur (Mount of Light) near Makkah to pray and reflect away from the polytheism and corruption of Makkah society.
questions.socraticHint: Which mountain called the "Mount of Light" houses the famous Cave of Hira?

questions.prompt: In which holy month and at what age did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) receive the first divine revelation (Bi’thah)?
questions.text: In which holy month and at what age did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) receive the first divine revelation (Bi’thah)?

options.text: During the month of Shawwal at the age of sixty-three (63) years
