During the month of Rajab at the age of twelve (12) years
During the month of Ramadan at the age of forty (40) years
During the month of Muharram at the age of twenty-five (25) years

questions.correctAnswer: During the month of Ramadan at the age of forty (40) years
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) received the first revelation in the month of Ramadan (Laylat al-Qadr) in 610 CE when he was forty years old, marking the beginning of his prophetic mission.
questions.socraticHint: In which fasting month of the Islamic calendar and at what mature age of 40 was the first revelation sent?

questions.prompt: Which archangel appeared to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Cave Hira with the first command of revelation?
questions.text: Which archangel appeared to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Cave Hira with the first command of revelation?
questions.explanation: Archangel Jibril (AS), the angel entrusted with delivering divine revelation to all prophets, appeared to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Cave Hira with the words of Allah.
questions.socraticHint: Which archangel is specifically tasked by Allah to deliver revelation to the Prophets?

questions.prompt: What was the very first word spoken by Angel Jibril to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Cave Hira?
questions.text: What was the very first word spoken by Angel Jibril to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Cave Hira?
questions.explanation: The very first word revealed was "Iqra!" (Read or Recite!), emphasizing the fundamental importance of literacy, divine knowledge, and recitation in Islam.
questions.socraticHint: Which one-word divine command meaning "Read" or "Recite" opened the revelation of the Qur’an?

questions.prompt: What was the humble reply of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when Angel Jibril commanded him to read?
questions.text: What was the humble reply of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when Angel Jibril commanded him to read?

options.text: I do not wish to read anything until tomorrow morning
Ma ana bi-qari (I am not a reader / I do not know how to read)
I can read all the books in the libraries of Persia
I will only read if you give me a written scroll of papyrus

questions.correctAnswer: Ma ana bi-qari (I am not a reader / I do not know how to read)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) was unlettered (Ummi), having never been taught to read or write by human teachers. He replied honestly: "Ma ana bi-qari" ("I do not know how to read").
questions.socraticHint: What honest answer acknowledging that he was unlettered did the Prophet give to Jibril?

questions.prompt: Which five verses of the Holy Qur’an were the very first to be revealed in Cave Hira (Surah Al-Alaq 96:1-5)?
questions.text: Which five verses of the Holy Qur’an were the very first to be revealed in Cave Hira (Surah Al-Alaq 96:1-5)?

options.text: Say, "He is Allah, who is One; Allah, the Eternal Refuge; He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent"
When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes
Read in the name of your Lord who created; created man from a clinging clot. Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man that which he knew not
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Sovereign of the Day of Recompense

questions.correctAnswer: Read in the name of your Lord who created; created man from a clinging clot. Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man that which he knew not
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Alaq (96:1-5) was the first revelation, teaching that Allah is the Creator who fashioned humanity from a clinging embryo, the Most Generous who bestowed knowledge through the pen.
questions.socraticHint: Which verses proclaim that Allah created humanity from a clinging clot and taught man by the pen?

questions.prompt: When the Prophet (SAW) returned home trembling with awe, what did he say to his wife Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA)?
questions.text: When the Prophet (SAW) returned home trembling with awe, what did he say to his wife Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA)?

options.text: Prepare a celebratory feast with fifty roast sheep immediately!
Pack our luggage so we can move to the city of Yathrib right now!
Call the tribal elders of Quraysh to come to our home!
Zammilooni! Zammilooni! (Cover me! Cover me / Wrap me up!)

questions.correctAnswer: Zammilooni! Zammilooni! (Cover me! Cover me / Wrap me up!)
questions.explanation: Overwhelmed by the magnitude of the encounter with Jibril and the divine words, the Prophet (SAW) returned with his heart trembling, saying to Khadijah: "Zammilooni, zammilooni" (Cover me, wrap me up).
questions.socraticHint: Which emotional words pleading to be wrapped in a cloak did the trembling Prophet speak to Khadijah?

questions.prompt: What profound qualities of the Prophet’s character did Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA) highlight to comfort him that Allah would never disgrace him?
questions.text: What profound qualities of the Prophet’s character did Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA) highlight to comfort him that Allah would never disgrace him?

options.text: You uphold ties of kinship, speak the truth, help the poor and needy, serve guests generously, and assist victims of disaster
You have accumulated more gold and silver than any merchant in the Arabian peninsula
You have defeated fifty warriors in wrestling contests outside Makkah
You possess the fastest war camels and finest silk robes in Hijaz

questions.correctAnswer: You uphold ties of kinship, speak the truth, help the poor and needy, serve guests generously, and assist victims of disaster
questions.explanation: Khadijah comforted him with unwavering faith: "Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep good relations with kith and kin, tell the truth, help the poor and destitute, serve your guests generously, and assist the deserving calamity-afflicted ones."
questions.socraticHint: Which moral virtues of helping the destitute, honoring guests, and upholding kinship did Khadijah recount?

questions.prompt: To whom did Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA) take Prophet Muhammad (SAW) to seek understanding about the supernatural encounter in Cave Hira?
questions.text: To whom did Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA) take Prophet Muhammad (SAW) to seek understanding about the supernatural encounter in Cave Hira?

options.text: A Roman fortune teller traveling with a trade caravan
Waraqah ibn Nawfal, her elderly cousin who was a scholar of the ancient scriptures
Abu Jahl, the chief elder of the Banu Makhzum clan
Herod Antipas, the governor residing in Jerusalem

questions.correctAnswer: Waraqah ibn Nawfal, her elderly cousin who was a scholar of the ancient scriptures
questions.explanation: Khadijah took him to her paternal cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, an elderly, blind scholar who had studied the Hebrew scriptures (the Torah and Gospel) and followed monotheism.
questions.socraticHint: Which learned monotheistic scholar of ancient scriptures was Khadijah’s elderly cousin?

questions.prompt: What did Waraqah ibn Nawfal confirm after listening attentively to what the Prophet (SAW) experienced in Cave Hira?
questions.text: What did Waraqah ibn Nawfal confirm after listening attentively to what the Prophet (SAW) experienced in Cave Hira?

options.text: You should immediately pay thirty silver coins to the keepers of the Ka’bah idols
You should stop meditating and become a caravan guard in Syria
This is the Namus (Archangel Jibril) whom Allah sent to Prophet Musa (Moses), and you are the promised Prophet of this nation
This was a bad desert dream caused by fasting too long in the heat

questions.correctAnswer: This is the Namus (Archangel Jibril) whom Allah sent to Prophet Musa (Moses), and you are the promised Prophet of this nation
questions.explanation: Waraqah exclaimed: "This is the Namus (the heavenly angel of divine secrets, Jibril) whom Allah sent down to Musa (Moses). I wish I were young and alive when your people will expel you!" He confirmed Muhammad’s prophethood.
questions.socraticHint: Which heavenly angel of revelation ("Namus") sent previously to Prophet Musa did Waraqah identify?

questions.prompt: What lesson on marriage and family support can modern Kenyan Muslim families learn from Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA)?
questions.text: What lesson on marriage and family support can modern Kenyan Muslim families learn from Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA)?

options.text: Spouses should compete against each other to see who earns more money in business
When a family member faces a challenge, others should laugh and tell them to handle it alone
Family members should keep their religious beliefs completely secret from each other
A spouse should be a source of comfort, emotional security, unwavering faith, and practical encouragement in moments of anxiety and crisis

questions.correctAnswer: A spouse should be a source of comfort, emotional security, unwavering faith, and practical encouragement in moments of anxiety and crisis
questions.explanation: Khadijah’s profound wisdom, emotional support, and absolute belief in her husband model ideal marital partnership. Her reassuring response provided vital stability during the momentous birth of Islam.
questions.socraticHint: How does Khadijah’s loving comfort and emotional strength model the ideal supportive spouse?

questions.prompt: Why was the revelation of "Iqra" (Read) and the mention of "The Pen" in Surah Al-Alaq revolutionary in 7th-century Arabia?
questions.text: Why was the revelation of "Iqra" (Read) and the mention of "The Pen" in Surah Al-Alaq revolutionary in 7th-century Arabia?

options.text: In a largely illiterate society driven by tribal warfare and superstition, it elevated reading, literacy, education, and moral truth as the supreme path of human honor
It made pens the most expensive trade commodity in the markets of Yemen
It required everyone in Arabia to abandon agriculture and become professional scribes
It proved that books were only intended for foreign kings and rulers

questions.correctAnswer: In a largely illiterate society driven by tribal warfare and superstition, it elevated reading, literacy, education, and moral truth as the supreme path of human honor
questions.explanation: Pre-Islamic Arabia was an oral, largely unlettered society (Jahiliyyah). Divine revelation began by honoring reading and the pen, establishing literacy and pursuit of knowledge as sacred duties for all believers.
questions.socraticHint: How did beginning revelation with reading and the pen transform an illiterate tribal society into a civilization of learning?

questions.prompt: Who was the very first person in the world to accept Islam and believe in Prophet Muhammad’s message?
questions.text: Who was the very first person in the world to accept Islam and believe in Prophet Muhammad’s message?
questions.explanation: Sayyidatna Khadijah (RA) was the first human being to embrace Islam. She believed in him without hesitation, supported him with her wealth, and comforted him through every early trial.
questions.socraticHint: Which noble wife of the Prophet was the first human being to believe and embrace Islam?

questions.prompt: Who was the first free adult male to accept Islam when invited by the Prophet (SAW)?
questions.text: Who was the first free adult male to accept Islam when invited by the Prophet (SAW)?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) was the first adult male outside the household to accept Islam. The Prophet said: "Whenever I invited anyone to Islam, they had some hesitation, except Abu Bakr; he accepted immediately without hesitation."
questions.socraticHint: Which loyal friend, known as "As-Siddiq" (The Truthful), was the first adult male to accept Islam?

questions.prompt: Who was the first youth/child to accept Islam, being approximately ten years old at the time?
questions.text: Who was the first youth/child to accept Islam, being approximately ten years old at the time?
questions.explanation: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), the Prophet’s young cousin living in his household, was the first child/youth to accept Islam at approximately ten years of age, demonstrating great spiritual maturity.
questions.socraticHint: Which young cousin of the Prophet living in his home was the very first child to accept Islam?

questions.prompt: Who was the first freed slave to accept Islam and join the early believers in Makkah?
questions.text: Who was the first freed slave to accept Islam and join the early believers in Makkah?
questions.explanation: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA), who had been freed and adopted by the Prophet (SAW), was the first freed slave to accept Islam, proving that Islam honors individuals across all social backgrounds.
questions.socraticHint: Which beloved companion, freed and raised by the Prophet, was the first freed slave to become Muslim?

questions.prompt: How long did the initial period of secret preaching (Da’wah Sirriyyah) last in Makkah before public proclamation began?
questions.text: How long did the initial period of secret preaching (Da’wah Sirriyyah) last in Makkah before public proclamation began?
questions.explanation: The secret phase of Da’wah lasted for three years, during which the Prophet (SAW) privately invited trustworthy individuals, building a firm spiritual and moral core without prematurely provoking violent opposition.
questions.socraticHint: How many years—three years—did the Prophet spend quietly sharing the message with close trusted individuals?

questions.prompt: Whose home near Mount Safa was chosen by Prophet Muhammad (SAW) as the secret meeting place and sanctuary for the early Muslims?
questions.text: Whose home near Mount Safa was chosen by Prophet Muhammad (SAW) as the secret meeting place and sanctuary for the early Muslims?

options.text: The palace of the Roman ambassador in Makkah
The house of Abu Jahl at the town square
The house of Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam (Dar al-Arqam)
The house of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb

questions.correctAnswer: The house of Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam (Dar al-Arqam)
questions.explanation: The house of Al-Arqam (Dar al-Arqam), located near Mount Safa, served as the first educational center and sanctuary where early Muslims gathered to pray, learn the Qur’an, and receive prophetic guidance.
questions.socraticHint: Which young companion’s home ("Dar al-Arqam") became the secret center of early Islamic teaching?

questions.prompt: Why did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) strategically choose the house of Al-Arqam as the secret center for the early Muslim community?
questions.text: Why did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) strategically choose the house of Al-Arqam as the secret center for the early Muslim community?

options.text: The house had high stone towers equipped with archer weapons
It was the largest commercial warehouse in Makkah
It was located outside the Arabian desert near the Red Sea
Al-Arqam was a young, quiet teenager whose home would not arouse suspicion from the hostile Quraysh leaders

questions.correctAnswer: Al-Arqam was a young, quiet teenager whose home would not arouse suspicion from the hostile Quraysh leaders
questions.explanation: Al-Arqam was only around 16 years old and not from the Prophet’s clan (Banu Hashim), so Quraysh never suspected that the new movement would hold meetings in a youth’s home, ensuring privacy and safety.
questions.socraticHint: Why would the home of a young, unobtrusive teenager near Safa avoid raising suspicion from Quraysh chiefs?

questions.prompt: How did Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) contribute decisively to the growth of Islam during the secret Da’wah period?
questions.text: How did Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) contribute decisively to the growth of Islam during the secret Da’wah period?

options.text: He actively reached out to influential, upright friends like Uthman ibn Affan, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, and Talhah, who all accepted Islam
He purchased swords from Syria to organize an armed uprising in Makkah
He advised the Prophet to keep Islam secret for fifty years
He moved his business permanently to Persia to avoid meeting Quraysh leaders

questions.correctAnswer: He actively reached out to influential, upright friends like Uthman ibn Affan, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, and Talhah, who all accepted Islam
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr used his high social standing, honesty, and broad network to invite noble friends. Through his personal Da’wah, major leaders like Uthman, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, and Az-Zubayr joined Islam.
questions.socraticHint: Which key early leaders did Abu Bakr personally invite into Islam using his trusted reputation?

questions.prompt: What did young Ali ibn Abi Talib’s decision to accept Islam at age ten teach Kenyan primary school learners today?
questions.text: What did young Ali ibn Abi Talib’s decision to accept Islam at age ten teach Kenyan primary school learners today?

options.text: Children have no responsibility to pray or practice good morals
Young people possess moral discernment and spiritual capacity, and can choose truth and righteousness regardless of their young age
Children should wait until they are forty years old before learning about religion
Young people should follow whatever bad habits their peers practice without thinking

questions.correctAnswer: Young people possess moral discernment and spiritual capacity, and can choose truth and righteousness regardless of their young age
questions.explanation: Ali (RA) embraced Islam while still a boy, standing bravely for truth in a polytheistic culture. This proves that children and youth can have strong moral discernment, sincere faith, and leadership in good deeds.
questions.socraticHint: Can young learners embrace faith, truth, and moral character like ten-year-old Ali did?

questions.prompt: What activities took place inside Dar al-Arqam during the secret phase of Islam?
questions.text: What activities took place inside Dar al-Arqam during the secret phase of Islam?

options.text: The believers engaged in commercial grain trading with Persian merchants
They drafted treaties to divide political control of Makkah with the Quraysh
The Prophet (SAW) taught the newly revealed Qur’anic verses, led communal prayers, instilled Islamic Akhlaq, and fostered deep brotherhood
The Muslims manufactured weapons of war to attack Makkah caravans

questions.correctAnswer: The Prophet (SAW) taught the newly revealed Qur’anic verses, led communal prayers, instilled Islamic Akhlaq, and fostered deep brotherhood
questions.explanation: Dar al-Arqam served as a spiritual sanctuary and academy where the early Muslims learned the Qur’an, performed Salah, cultivated spiritual purity (Tazkiyah), and built strong bonds of mutual solidarity.
questions.socraticHint: Which spiritual, educational, and communal activities formed the core of life inside Dar al-Arqam?

questions.prompt: How did the diversity among the first four converts (a mature woman, an adult merchant, a young boy, and a freed slave) reflect Islam’s universal appeal?
questions.text: How did the diversity among the first four converts (a mature woman, an adult merchant, a young boy, and a freed slave) reflect Islam’s universal appeal?

options.text: It showed that only four types of people were ever permitted to accept the Islamic faith
It was a coincidence that had no deeper significance for the early community
It proved that religious belief depends on a person’s tribal wealth and status
It showed that Islam breaks all social, gender, economic, and age barriers, offering dignity and equality before Allah to all humanity

questions.correctAnswer: It showed that Islam breaks all social, gender, economic, and age barriers, offering dignity and equality before Allah to all humanity
questions.explanation: The pioneer converts encompassed women (Khadijah), men (Abu Bakr), children (Ali), and former slaves (Zayd), proving from the very beginning that Islam is a universal message of human dignity, justice, and spiritual equality.
questions.socraticHint: How does the inclusion of a woman, an adult man, a child, and a freed slave demonstrate universal equality in Islam?

questions.prompt: What strategic lesson on wisdom and planning (Hikmah) does the three-year secret phase of Da’wah teach believers?
questions.text: What strategic lesson on wisdom and planning (Hikmah) does the three-year secret phase of Da’wah teach believers?

options.text: Noble goals require prudent preparation, establishing a firm foundation, and choosing the right timing before facing public challenges
Believers should be afraid and permanently hide their good deeds from the world
Planning and strategy are forbidden in religious matters because miracles happen automatically
It is wise to abandon one’s principles whenever people disagree with them

questions.correctAnswer: Noble goals require prudent preparation, establishing a firm foundation, and choosing the right timing before facing public challenges
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) balanced divine trust (Tawakkul) with practical wisdom (Hikmah). Building a solid, spiritually grounded core in secret prevented the movement from being crushed prematurely by Quraysh.
questions.socraticHint: How does wise planning, preparation, and careful timing demonstrate practical wisdom alongside divine trust?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: How many years did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) preach Islam privately (Da’wah Sirriyyah) before Allah commanded him to proclaim it openly?
questions.text: How many years did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) preach Islam privately (Da’wah Sirriyyah) before Allah commanded him to proclaim it openly?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) engaged in secret da'wah (calling to Islam) for the first three years in Makkah, meeting covertly at Dar al-Arqam before receiving the divine command for open proclamation.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the number of years spent gathering the pioneer believers secretly at Dar al-Arqam before going public on Mount Safa.

questions.prompt: Which Quranic verse in Surah Ash-Shu'ara (26:214) commanded Prophet Muhammad (SAW) to begin preaching openly to his relatives?
questions.text: Which Quranic verse in Surah Ash-Shu'ara (26:214) commanded Prophet Muhammad (SAW) to begin preaching openly to his relatives?

options.text: "Recite in the name of your Lord"
"Read what has been revealed to you"

questions.explanation: Surah Ash-Shu'ara verse 214 instructed: "Wa andhir 'ashiretaka al-aqrabin" ("And warn your closest kinsfolk"), commanding the Prophet to call his Banu Hashim family and close relatives first.
questions.socraticHint: Which instruction specifically tells the messenger to direct warnings to his nearest family members and tribe?

questions.prompt: From which prominent hill near the Ka'bah in Makkah did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) address all the gathered Quraysh clans to announce his prophethood openly?
questions.text: From which prominent hill near the Ka'bah in Makkah did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) address all the gathered Quraysh clans to announce his prophethood openly?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) ascended Mount Safa, an elevated hill near the Ka'bah, where he raised his voice to summon the leaders and people of the Quraysh clans.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the hill that forms the starting point of Sa'i between two small hills near the Ka'bah.

questions.prompt: What traditional Makkan warning cry of imminent danger did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) use from Mount Safa to assemble the people?
questions.text: What traditional Makkan warning cry of imminent danger did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) use from Mount Safa to assemble the people?
questions.explanation: "Ya Sabahah!" was the customary ancient Arab alert shouted when an enemy army was spotted advancing to attack at dawn, prompting immediate assembly of the entire community.
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic phrase was specifically shouted at dawn to alert people of sudden danger or enemy invasion?

questions.prompt: Before delivering his message from Mount Safa, what question did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) ask the Quraysh to establish their trust in him?
questions.text: Before delivering his message from Mount Safa, what question did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) ask the Quraysh to establish their trust in him?

options.text: Whether they had ever seen the Cave of Hira at night
Whether they would believe him if he warned that enemy horsemen were behind the valley ready to attack
Whether they would agree to give him gold and silver treasures
Whether they would elect him as the king of Makkah

questions.correctAnswer: Whether they would believe him if he warned that enemy horsemen were behind the valley ready to attack
questions.explanation: The Prophet asked if they would believe him if he told them an enemy cavalry was behind the valley; they replied they had only ever known him to speak the absolute truth.
questions.socraticHint: How did the Prophet use a hypothetical military threat to verify that they considered him completely honest and truthful?

questions.prompt: What unanimous reply did the Quraysh clans give when the Prophet (SAW) asked about his truthfulness on Mount Safa?
questions.text: What unanimous reply did the Quraysh clans give when the Prophet (SAW) asked about his truthfulness on Mount Safa?

options.text: "We do not know your character or honesty"
"You must provide written testimony from foreign traders first"
"Yes, we have never known you to speak anything but truth (As-Sadiq Al-Amin)"

questions.correctAnswer: "Yes, we have never known you to speak anything but truth (As-Sadiq Al-Amin)"
questions.explanation: The Quraysh testified to his lifelong integrity, acknowledging that for 40 years he had never told a lie, known universally as As-Sadiq (the Truthful) and Al-Amin (the Trustworthy).
questions.socraticHint: What title had the people of Makkah given Muhammad (SAW) throughout his youth because of his unmatched honesty?

questions.prompt: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) disrespectfully cursed him on Mount Safa by saying, "May you perish for the rest of this day! Is this why you gathered us?"
questions.text: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) disrespectfully cursed him on Mount Safa by saying, "May you perish for the rest of this day! Is this why you gathered us?"
questions.explanation: Abu Lahab (Abd al-Uzza) openly insulted the Prophet (SAW) with the derogatory remark "Tabban laka sa'ir al-yawm" (May you perish for the rest of the day!), rejecting the divine call.
questions.socraticHint: Which uncle became a fierce opponent whose condemnation is explicitly recorded in Surah Al-Masad?

questions.prompt: Which Surah of the Holy Qur'an was revealed by Allah to condemn Abu Lahab and his wife for their hostility towards the Prophet (SAW)?
questions.text: Which Surah of the Holy Qur'an was revealed by Allah to condemn Abu Lahab and his wife for their hostility towards the Prophet (SAW)?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Masad (also known as Surah Tabbat) was revealed condemning Abu Lahab and his malicious wife Umm Jamil, declaring that his wealth and gains would never save him from punishment.
questions.socraticHint: Which short Surah begins with "Tabbat yada abi lahabin wa tabb"?

questions.prompt: How did Abu Lahab's wife, Umm Jamil, participate in harassing Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Makkah?
questions.text: How did Abu Lahab's wife, Umm Jamil, participate in harassing Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Makkah?

options.text: She refused to trade food in the market of Ukadh
She scattered thorny branches along the pathway where the Prophet walked
She burned down houses of believers in Makkah
She wrote hostile poems on the walls of the Ka'bah

questions.correctAnswer: She scattered thorny branches along the pathway where the Prophet walked
questions.explanation: Umm Jamil would bundle sharp desert thorns and spread them along the path the Prophet (SAW) used to injure his feet, earning her the description "carrier of firewood" in Surah Al-Masad.
questions.socraticHint: What painful physical obstacles did she scatter on the road to injure the Prophet while he walked?

questions.prompt: Which verse in Surah Al-Hijr (15:94) ordered the Prophet (SAW) to proclaim the message openly without fearing the idolaters?
questions.text: Which verse in Surah Al-Hijr (15:94) ordered the Prophet (SAW) to proclaim the message openly without fearing the idolaters?

options.text: "O you who wrap yourself up in garments, stand through the night"
"Proclaim openly what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists"
"Hold fast to the rope of Allah altogether"

questions.correctAnswer: "Proclaim openly what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists"
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hijr verse 94 states: "Fasda' bima tu'mar wa a'rid 'anil-mushrikin" ("Proclaim openly that which you are commanded, and withdraw from the polytheists").
questions.socraticHint: Which verse directly commands the Prophet to publicly disclose what he was ordered and disregard the polytheists?

questions.prompt: Why were the aristocratic leaders of Quraysh so strongly opposed to the open message of Islam preached by Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?
questions.text: Why were the aristocratic leaders of Quraysh so strongly opposed to the open message of Islam preached by Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?

options.text: They wanted the Prophet to worship idols only on Fridays
They preferred reading foreign scriptures in Persian
They wanted all trade in Makkah to cease completely
Islam demanded the abolition of idol worship, social equality for slaves, and an end to corrupt exploitation

questions.correctAnswer: Islam demanded the abolition of idol worship, social equality for slaves, and an end to corrupt exploitation
questions.explanation: The Quraysh elite feared losing their religious prestige, lucrative idol-pilgrimage income, and hierarchical dominance over slaves, poor people, and women under Islam's egalitarian teachings.
questions.socraticHint: Consider how Islam threatened their financial profits from idol worship and dismantled their unjust tribal caste system.

questions.prompt: What vital moral lesson do Kenyan primary learners learn from the Prophet's 40-year reputation as "Al-Amin" before preaching publicly?
questions.text: What vital moral lesson do Kenyan primary learners learn from the Prophet's 40-year reputation as "Al-Amin" before preaching publicly?

options.text: Personal trustworthiness and honest character must be proven in daily life before expecting others to trust our leadership
Only wealthy people can be trusted in society
One should only be honest when speaking to powerful leaders
Honesty is only necessary after one reaches forty years of age

questions.correctAnswer: Personal trustworthiness and honest character must be proven in daily life before expecting others to trust our leadership
questions.explanation: The Prophet's lifelong honesty shows that authentic leadership and moral authority are built on consistent integrity, truthfulness, and reliability in daily personal conduct.
questions.socraticHint: How does personal integrity in school and community lay the foundation for being believed and respected by others?

questions.prompt: Who was the Ethiopian enslaved believer who was tortured under heavy stones by Umayyah ibn Khalaf yet continuously proclaimed "Ahad, Ahad"?
questions.text: Who was the Ethiopian enslaved believer who was tortured under heavy stones by Umayyah ibn Khalaf yet continuously proclaimed "Ahad, Ahad"?
questions.explanation: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) endured brutal torture under the blazing sun with a heavy rock on his chest, refusing to renounce Islam and crying "Ahad, Ahad" (Allah is One, Allah is One).
questions.socraticHint: Which noble companion later became the first Mu'adhin (caller to prayer) of Islam?

questions.prompt: Who purchased and emancipated Bilal ibn Rabah from slavery, ending his brutal torture in Makkah?
questions.text: Who purchased and emancipated Bilal ibn Rabah from slavery, ending his brutal torture in Makkah?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) paid Umayyah ibn Khalaf a high price to purchase Bilal and set him free immediately for the sake of Allah.
questions.socraticHint: Which close companion and first adult male convert used his personal wealth to free many enslaved Muslims?

questions.prompt: Who was the first martyr (Shahidah) in the history of Islam, killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to abandon her faith?
questions.text: Who was the first martyr (Shahidah) in the history of Islam, killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to abandon her faith?
questions.explanation: Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA), the mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, was ruthlessly murdered by Abu Jahl, earning her the eternal distinction of being the first martyr in Islam.
questions.socraticHint: Which brave woman from the family of Yasir sacrificed her life rather than renounce monotheism?

questions.prompt: What comforting promise did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) give to the family of Yasir while they were being tortured in Makkah?
questions.text: What comforting promise did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) give to the family of Yasir while they were being tortured in Makkah?

options.text: "Be patient, O family of Yasir, for indeed your destination is Paradise (Jannah)!"
"Fight back against the Quraysh with swords!"
"Pretend to worship their idols openly and renounce Islam forever!"
"Leave Makkah and go live alone in the desert caves!"

questions.correctAnswer: "Be patient, O family of Yasir, for indeed your destination is Paradise (Jannah)!"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) passed by them as they were tortured and comforted them: "Sabran ya aala Yasir, fa'inna maw'idakumul-Jannah" ("Be patient, family of Yasir, your promised meeting place is Paradise").
questions.socraticHint: What ultimate eternal reward did the Prophet guarantee to Yasir and Sumayyah for their patience under torture?

questions.prompt: Why did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) advise the vulnerable Muslims to migrate across the sea to Abyssinia (Al-Habashah)?
questions.text: Why did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) advise the vulnerable Muslims to migrate across the sea to Abyssinia (Al-Habashah)?

options.text: Because the Quraysh commanded them to go there as traders
Because its Christian King (Negus) was a just ruler under whom no one was wronged
Because Abyssinia had great gold mines they could trade
Because the people of Abyssinia spoke Arabic fluently

questions.correctAnswer: Because its Christian King (Negus) was a just ruler under whom no one was wronged
questions.explanation: The Prophet praised King Negus (an-Najashi) as a just Christian king who sheltered the oppressed and would not permit any injustice within his realm.
questions.socraticHint: What moral virtue of justice did the King of Abyssinia possess that made his country a safe sanctuary for refugees?

questions.prompt: Who was the eloquent cousin of the Prophet (SAW) who led and spoke on behalf of the Muslim migrants before King Negus of Abyssinia?
questions.text: Who was the eloquent cousin of the Prophet (SAW) who led and spoke on behalf of the Muslim migrants before King Negus of Abyssinia?
questions.explanation: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA), the older brother of Ali, was the chosen spokesperson whose articulate speech and recitation moved King Negus and his court to tears.
questions.socraticHint: Which son of Abu Talib and elder brother of Ali addressed the royal court in Abyssinia?

questions.prompt: Which Surah from the Holy Qur'an did Ja’far ibn Abi Talib recite to King Negus to explain Islam's reverence for Prophet Isa (Jesus AS) and Maryam (Mary)?
questions.text: Which Surah from the Holy Qur'an did Ja’far ibn Abi Talib recite to King Negus to explain Islam's reverence for Prophet Isa (Jesus AS) and Maryam (Mary)?
questions.explanation: Ja'far recited verses from Surah Maryam describing the miraculous conception and birth of Prophet Isa (AS) and the righteousness of his mother Maryam.
questions.socraticHint: Which Surah is named directly after the blessed mother of Prophet Isa (Jesus AS)?

questions.prompt: What was the reaction of King Negus of Abyssinia when he heard the verses of Surah Maryam recited by Ja’far?
questions.text: What was the reaction of King Negus of Abyssinia when he heard the verses of Surah Maryam recited by Ja’far?

options.text: He wept until his beard was wet and declared that the message comes from the same source of light as the Gospel
He ordered the Muslims to be arrested immediately and handed to the Quraysh
He demanded a heavy ransom in gold before giving them shelter
He rejected the recitation and expelled both parties from his palace

questions.correctAnswer: He wept until his beard was wet and declared that the message comes from the same source of light as the Gospel
questions.explanation: King Negus was deeply moved to tears and recognized the divine truth, stating: "Verily, this and what Jesus brought come from the very same lamp of light," granting Muslims safety.
questions.socraticHint: How did the righteous Christian king demonstrate deep emotional and spiritual connection to the message of Surah Maryam?

questions.prompt: Who was the primary delegate sent by the Quraysh chieftains to Abyssinia with expensive gifts to convince King Negus to extradite the Muslims?
questions.text: Who was the primary delegate sent by the Quraysh chieftains to Abyssinia with expensive gifts to convince King Negus to extradite the Muslims?

options.text: Amr ibn al-Aas (before his conversion to Islam)

questions.correctAnswer: Amr ibn al-Aas (before his conversion to Islam)
questions.explanation: Amr ibn al-Aas was a clever diplomat sent by Quraysh bearing luxurious leather gifts to persuade King Negus, though Negus firmly refused to betray the Muslims.
questions.socraticHint: Which brilliant Makkan statesman (who later embraced Islam and liberated Egypt) led the Quraysh delegation?

questions.prompt: What special prayer did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) lead in Madinah when news reached him that King Negus (an-Najashi) had passed away?
questions.text: What special prayer did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) lead in Madinah when news reached him that King Negus (an-Najashi) had passed away?
questions.explanation: Because King Negus died far away in Abyssinia as a believer, the Prophet (SAW) performed Salat al-Gha'ib (absentee funeral prayer) with the companions in Madinah.
questions.socraticHint: What specific Islamic funeral prayer is offered when the deceased person has passed away in another distant country?

questions.prompt: How does King Negus’s reception of the Muslim refugees in Abyssinia model interfaith relations for Kenya today?
questions.text: How does King Negus’s reception of the Muslim refugees in Abyssinia model interfaith relations for Kenya today?

options.text: It shows that people of different faiths should never speak to one another
It implies that refugees should be forced to abandon their native culture
It proves that religious leaders should only help members of their own tribe
It demonstrates mutual respect, protection of persecuted minorities, and peaceful coexistence between Christians and Muslims

questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates mutual respect, protection of persecuted minorities, and peaceful coexistence between Christians and Muslims
questions.explanation: The historical sanctuary granted by a Christian king to Muslim refugees highlights universal compassion, interfaith solidarity, and the duty to protect the oppressed regardless of religion.
questions.socraticHint: How does a Christian king protecting Muslim refugees showcase harmony and shared moral values between faiths?

questions.prompt: In what way does Kenya's hosting of refugees at Kakuma and Daadab camps reflect the prophetic legacy of seeking and providing sanctuary?
questions.text: In what way does Kenya's hosting of refugees at Kakuma and Daadab camps reflect the prophetic legacy of seeking and providing sanctuary?

options.text: By offering shelter, legal safety, and humanitarian protection to families fleeing violence, just as Abyssinia protected early Muslims
By charging high taxes on vulnerable displaced persons
By forcing refugees to engage in unpaid community labor
By closing national borders to anyone experiencing injustice

questions.correctAnswer: By offering shelter, legal safety, and humanitarian protection to families fleeing violence, just as Abyssinia protected early Muslims
questions.explanation: Kenya’s long-standing humanitarian role sheltering hundreds of thousands of refugees reflects the timeless moral duty of providing refuge and defending vulnerable lives against oppression.
questions.socraticHint: Think about how safe asylum protects vulnerable people fleeing war and persecution in East Africa.

questions.prompt: Which number is Belief in the Divine Scriptures (Kutubullah) among the Six Pillars of Iman in Islam?
questions.text: Which number is Belief in the Divine Scriptures (Kutubullah) among the Six Pillars of Iman in Islam?
questions.explanation: The Six Pillars of Iman in order are: 1) Belief in Allah, 2) Belief in the Angels, 3) Belief in the Divine Books, 4) Belief in the Messengers, 5) Belief in the Day of Judgment, and 6) Belief in Qadar (Divine Decree).
questions.socraticHint: Recall the classic order: Allah, Angels, Books, Messengers, Day of Judgment, and Divine Decree.

questions.prompt: To which prophet of Allah was the divine book known as the Tawrat (Torah) revealed?
questions.text: To which prophet of Allah was the divine book known as the Tawrat (Torah) revealed?
questions.explanation: The Tawrat was revealed to Prophet Musa (AS) to guide the Children of Israel (Bani Isra'il) with divine commandments and moral laws.
questions.socraticHint: Which prophet led the Children of Israel out of Egypt and received the revelation at Mount Sinai?

questions.prompt: To which prophet was the holy scripture known as the Zabur (Psalms) revealed by Allah?
questions.text: To which prophet was the holy scripture known as the Zabur (Psalms) revealed by Allah?
questions.explanation: The Zabur was revealed to Prophet Dawud (AS), filled with praises, prayers, hymns of devotion, and wisdom.
questions.socraticHint: Which prophet was a righteous king known for his beautiful voice of praise and defeating Jalut (Goliath)?

questions.prompt: Which divine scripture was revealed to Prophet Isa (Jesus AS) to confirm the Tawrat and preach spiritual purity?
questions.text: Which divine scripture was revealed to Prophet Isa (Jesus AS) to confirm the Tawrat and preach spiritual purity?
questions.explanation: Allah revealed the Injil (Gospel) to Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) to guide people with mercy, love, and righteousness, confirming what was in the Torah.
questions.socraticHint: What Arabic term refers to the Gospel revealed to Prophet Isa (AS)?

questions.prompt: To whom was the Holy Qur'an revealed as the final and universal divine scripture for all humankind?
questions.text: To whom was the Holy Qur'an revealed as the final and universal divine scripture for all humankind?
questions.explanation: The Holy Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) through Archangel Jibril over a duration of 23 years as the final revelation for all humanity.
questions.socraticHint: Who is the Seal of the Prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin) to whom the Qur'an was revealed?

questions.prompt: Which prophets were given the divine scrolls known as Suhuf according to the Holy Qur'an (Surah Al-A'la 87:18-19)?
questions.text: Which prophets were given the divine scrolls known as Suhuf according to the Holy Qur'an (Surah Al-A'la 87:18-19)?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-A'la concludes with: "Suhufi Ibrahima wa Musa" ("The Scriptures/Scrolls of Abraham and Moses"), acknowledging the divine scrolls granted to them.
questions.socraticHint: Look at the concluding verse of Surah Al-A'la mentioning the Suhuf of two great messengers.

questions.prompt: What divine promise regarding the preservation of the Holy Qur'an is stated in Surah Al-Hijr (15:9)?
questions.text: What divine promise regarding the preservation of the Holy Qur'an is stated in Surah Al-Hijr (15:9)?

options.text: The Qur'an will only exist in written form in Arabia
The Qur'an will be replaced by a new book after five hundred years
Humans alone are responsible for keeping copies safe without divine protection
Allah Himself guarantees that He sent it down and will guard it against any change or corruption

questions.correctAnswer: Allah Himself guarantees that He sent it down and will guard it against any change or corruption
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hijr 15:9 declares: "Inna nahnu nazzalna adh-dhikra wa inna lahu lahafizun" ("Indeed, it is We who sent down the message and indeed, We will be its guardian").
questions.socraticHint: Who takes absolute personal responsibility for preserving the Holy Qur'an from alteration or distortion?

questions.prompt: How is the scope and audience of the Holy Qur'an different from the earlier revealed scriptures like the Tawrat and Injil?
questions.text: How is the scope and audience of the Holy Qur'an different from the earlier revealed scriptures like the Tawrat and Injil?

options.text: Earlier scriptures were sent to specific communities for a specific era, whereas the Qur'an is universal for all humankind for all time
The Qur'an was only intended for the Arabs of Makkah
Earlier scriptures were meant for everyone while the Qur'an is for one continent
There is no difference in their scope or intended audience

questions.correctAnswer: Earlier scriptures were sent to specific communities for a specific era, whereas the Qur'an is universal for all humankind for all time
questions.explanation: Earlier prophets and books were sent specifically to their own nations (e.g., Bani Isra'il), whereas Prophet Muhammad (SAW) and the Qur'an were sent to all creation until the Day of Judgment.
questions.socraticHint: Was the Qur'an sent to a single ethnic group or to all of humanity until the end of time?

questions.prompt: Over approximately how many years was the Holy Qur'an revealed piecemeal (gradually) to Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?
questions.text: Over approximately how many years was the Holy Qur'an revealed piecemeal (gradually) to Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?

options.text: 23 years (13 years in Makkah and 10 years in Madinah)

questions.correctAnswer: 23 years (13 years in Makkah and 10 years in Madinah)
questions.explanation: The revelation of the Qur'an was gradual over 23 years—13 years during the Makkan period addressing faith and patience, and 10 years in Madinah detailing community laws and governance.
questions.socraticHint: Add the 13 years of the Makkan period to the 10 years spent in Madinah after the Hijrah.

questions.prompt: What title is given to a person who memorizes the entire Holy Qur'an by heart from beginning to end?
questions.text: What title is given to a person who memorizes the entire Holy Qur'an by heart from beginning to end?
questions.explanation: A person who preserves the entire text of the Qur'an in their memory is honored with the title Hafidh (preserver/memorizer), a major vehicle for the Qur'an's miraculous oral preservation.
questions.socraticHint: What Arabic term derived from the root "to preserve or protect" describes someone who has committed the whole Qur'an to memory?

questions.prompt: What should be the attitude of a Muslim towards previous revealed books like the original Tawrat, Zabur, and Injil?
questions.text: What should be the attitude of a Muslim towards previous revealed books like the original Tawrat, Zabur, and Injil?

options.text: Reject and insult them entirely as false
Claim that Allah never sent any guidance before Prophet Muhammad (SAW)
Follow the laws of earlier scriptures instead of the Qur'an
Believe that in their original revealed forms they were authentic words of Allah, while following the Qur'an as the final, complete guide

questions.correctAnswer: Believe that in their original revealed forms they were authentic words of Allah, while following the Qur'an as the final, complete guide
questions.explanation: A Muslim must believe in all original divine books as true revelations from Allah, while adhering to the Holy Qur'an which confirms, completes, and supersedes previous laws.
questions.socraticHint: Does Iman require Muslims to respect and believe in the divine origin of earlier holy books sent by Allah?

questions.prompt: How does daily recitation and application of the Holy Qur'an positively impact a Grade 5 learner in Kenyan society?
questions.text: How does daily recitation and application of the Holy Qur'an positively impact a Grade 5 learner in Kenyan society?

options.text: It nurtures moral conscience, encourages academic honesty, promotes peace, and inspires respectful service to family and nation
It isolates the learner from having friendships with classmates
It discourages learning mathematics and natural sciences
It focuses exclusively on material wealth and prestige

questions.correctAnswer: It nurtures moral conscience, encourages academic honesty, promotes peace, and inspires respectful service to family and nation
questions.explanation: Living by the teachings of the Holy Qur'an builds strong character (Ihsan), moral resilience, kindness towards neighbors, respect for parents, and diligent citizenship in Kenya.
questions.socraticHint: How do Quranic values of justice, truthfulness, and kindness help children grow into responsible Kenyan citizens?

questions.prompt: From what substance were the Angels (Mala’ikah) created by Allah according to authentic Hadith in Sahih Muslim?
questions.text: From what substance were the Angels (Mala’ikah) created by Allah according to authentic Hadith in Sahih Muslim?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "The angels were created from light (Nur), the jinn were created from smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from that which has been described to you (clay)."
questions.socraticHint: Humans were made of clay and jinn from fire; what luminous creation was used to form the angels?

questions.prompt: Unlike human beings, what characteristic is unique to the Angels regarding obedience to Allah?
questions.text: Unlike human beings, what characteristic is unique to the Angels regarding obedience to Allah?

options.text: They can choose whether to obey or disobey depending on the situation
They need food, drink, and rest after performing worship
They do not disobey Allah in whatever He commands them, and they execute exactly what they are told without sin or fatigue
They make mistakes and repent every evening

questions.correctAnswer: They do not disobey Allah in whatever He commands them, and they execute exactly what they are told without sin or fatigue
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tahrim (66:6) states that angels "do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded." They possess no desires or rebellious free will.
questions.socraticHint: Do angels possess physical desires to rebel against Allah or do they obey commands flawlessly?

questions.prompt: Which Archangel was entrusted with conveying divine revelation (Wahy) from Allah to all the prophets and messengers?
questions.text: Which Archangel was entrusted with conveying divine revelation (Wahy) from Allah to all the prophets and messengers?
questions.explanation: Archangel Jibril (Gabriel) is the leader of the angels and the messenger of revelation (Ar-Ruh al-Amin), bringing Allah’s divine messages to the prophets.
questions.socraticHint: Which angel brought the first revelation "Iqra" to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Cave Hira?

questions.prompt: What primary responsibility is assigned to Archangel Mika’il (Michael)?
questions.text: What primary responsibility is assigned to Archangel Mika’il (Michael)?

options.text: Directing rainfall, winds, and the growth of crops and provision by Allah’s command
Blowing the trumpet on the Day of Judgment
Taking the souls of living creatures

questions.correctAnswer: Directing rainfall, winds, and the growth of crops and provision by Allah’s command
questions.explanation: Archangel Mika’il is tasked with overseeing precipitation, clouds, vegetation, and the distribution of Allah’s physical sustenance across creation.
questions.socraticHint: Which archangel is associated with rain, vegetation, and natural nourishment on Earth?

questions.prompt: Which Archangel will blow the Trumpet (As-Soor) to signal the end of the world and summon humanity for Resurrection?
questions.text: Which Archangel will blow the Trumpet (As-Soor) to signal the end of the world and summon humanity for Resurrection?
questions.explanation: Archangel Israfil is designated to sound the Trumpet: the first blast terminates worldly life, and the second blast initiates the Resurrection and Gathering.
questions.socraticHint: Which angel stands waiting with the Trumpet ready to blow at Allah's command on the Day of Judgment?

questions.prompt: What is the divine role of Malak al-Mawt (The Angel of Death)?
questions.text: What is the divine role of Malak al-Mawt (The Angel of Death)?

options.text: Taking the souls of human beings and all living beings at their appointed time of death
Recording good deeds on the right shoulder

questions.correctAnswer: Taking the souls of human beings and all living beings at their appointed time of death
questions.explanation: Surah As-Sajdah 32:11 states: "Say, 'The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you, then to your Lord you will be returned.'"
questions.socraticHint: Which angel retrieves the soul (Ruh) when a person's lifespan (Ajal) comes to an end?

questions.prompt: What are the names and responsibilities of the two recording angels known collectively as Kiraman Katibin?
questions.text: What are the names and responsibilities of the two recording angels known collectively as Kiraman Katibin?

options.text: Munkar on the right asks questions, and Nakir on the left answers them
Malik guards the right gate, and Ridwan guards the left gate
Jibril records the Qur'an, and Mika'il records the rain
Raqib on the right records good deeds, and Atid on the left records sins and bad deeds

questions.correctAnswer: Raqib on the right records good deeds, and Atid on the left records sins and bad deeds
questions.explanation: Surah Qaf 50:17-18 describes the two recording angels (Raqib and Atid) positioned on the right and left shoulders recording every single spoken word and deed.
questions.socraticHint: Which honorable scribes on our right and left shoulders record every good and bad deed we perform?

questions.prompt: Which two angels question every deceased person in their grave (Al-Qabr) regarding their Lord, their religion, and their Prophet?
questions.text: Which two angels question every deceased person in their grave (Al-Qabr) regarding their Lord, their religion, and their Prophet?
questions.explanation: Munkar and Nakir are the two terrifying angels who visit every soul in the grave to ask the three foundational questions of faith: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?"
questions.socraticHint: Which pair of angels pose the three questions in the realm of Barzakh (the grave)?

questions.prompt: Who is the guardian angel assigned to the gates of Jahannam (Hellfire)?
questions.text: Who is the guardian angel assigned to the gates of Jahannam (Hellfire)?
questions.explanation: Malik is the stern, unsmiling guardian of Hellfire named in Surah Az-Zukhruf (43:77): "And they will call: O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!"
questions.socraticHint: Which angel is specifically named in Surah Az-Zukhruf as the keeper of the Fire?

questions.prompt: Who is the joyful guardian angel assigned to welcome the righteous believers into Jannah (Paradise)?
questions.text: Who is the joyful guardian angel assigned to welcome the righteous believers into Jannah (Paradise)?
questions.explanation: Ridwan is the noble angel who serves as the keeper and gatekeeper of Paradise, welcoming the pious believers into eternal bliss.
questions.socraticHint: Whose name means "pleasure or satisfaction" and guards the eternal gardens of Paradise?

questions.prompt: How does believing in the recording angels (Kiraman Katibin) cultivate personal integrity in a Kenyan pupil during examinations?
questions.text: How does believing in the recording angels (Kiraman Katibin) cultivate personal integrity in a Kenyan pupil during examinations?

options.text: The pupil writes very quickly to confuse the recording angels
The pupil believes that angels will write the exam answers for them
The pupil only studies when someone gives them a reward
The pupil refrains from cheating because they know Allah and His angels record every secret deed even when the teacher is not looking

questions.correctAnswer: The pupil refrains from cheating because they know Allah and His angels record every secret deed even when the teacher is not looking
questions.explanation: Belief in Kiraman Katibin nurtures Ihsan (God-consciousness), instilling the awareness that all private and public actions are recorded, inspiring steadfast honesty regardless of external supervision.
questions.socraticHint: How does knowing that an angel records our private deeds prevent us from cheating in an exam?

questions.prompt: What honor did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) teach that angels give to students and seekers of Islamic knowledge in schools?
questions.text: What honor did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) teach that angels give to students and seekers of Islamic knowledge in schools?

options.text: The angels lower their wings out of pleasure for the seeker of knowledge and pray for their forgiveness
The angels grant students physical money during lessons
The angels exempt learners from doing household chores
The angels prevent students from feeling hungry during tests

questions.correctAnswer: The angels lower their wings out of pleasure for the seeker of knowledge and pray for their forgiveness
questions.explanation: In Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi, the Prophet (SAW) stated: "Verily, the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge out of pleasure with what he is seeking," showing immense respect for educational effort.
questions.socraticHint: How do angels express deep satisfaction and reverence towards children and adults striving to learn?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What are the three main classifications of physical impurities (Najasaat) in Islamic jurisprudence?
questions.text: What are the three main classifications of physical impurities (Najasaat) in Islamic jurisprudence?
questions.explanation: Islamic law classifies impurities into Mukhaffafah (light, e.g. unweaned boy's urine), Mutawassitah (medium, e.g. blood, feces, urine), and Mughalladhah (heavy, e.g. dog saliva, swine).
questions.socraticHint: Which terms translate to Light, Medium, and Heavy physical impurities in Arabic jurisprudence?

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of Najasah Mukhaffafah (Light Impurity)?
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Najasah Mukhaffafah (Light Impurity)?

options.text: Flowing blood from a deep wound
Stagnant muddy rainwater on a footpath
The urine of a male infant under two years old who consumes only breast milk
The saliva of a dog that licks a cooking bowl

questions.correctAnswer: The urine of a male infant under two years old who consumes only breast milk
questions.explanation: The urine of a nursing baby boy who has not yet begun eating solid food is classified as Mukhaffafah (light impurity), which can be cleansed by sprinkling water over it.
questions.socraticHint: Think of an unweaned infant boy who feeds solely on his mother's milk.

questions.prompt: How is a fabric contaminated with Najasah Mukhaffafah (light impurity) properly purified?
questions.text: How is a fabric contaminated with Najasah Mukhaffafah (light impurity) properly purified?

options.text: By washing seven times with soil and detergent
By cutting away and burning the affected piece of fabric
By leaving it in direct sunlight for three days without water
By sprinkling clean water thoroughly over the contaminated spot until it is soaked

questions.correctAnswer: By sprinkling clean water thoroughly over the contaminated spot until it is soaked
questions.explanation: The Sunnah instructs that for the urine of a male nursing baby, it is sufficient to sprinkle (rashsh) pure water thoroughly over the area until completely wet.
questions.socraticHint: Does light impurity require extensive scrubbing or merely thorough sprinkling of water?

questions.prompt: Which group of substances belongs to Najasah Mutawassitah (Medium Impurity)?
questions.text: Which group of substances belongs to Najasah Mutawassitah (Medium Impurity)?

options.text: Human urine, feces, pus, flowing blood, vomit, and unslaughtered dead animals (Maytah)
Dog saliva and pig meat only
River mud, sea salt, and plant sap
Clean dust and sand from the garden

questions.correctAnswer: Human urine, feces, pus, flowing blood, vomit, and unslaughtered dead animals (Maytah)
questions.explanation: Standard bodily wastes and dead carcasses belong to Najasah Mutawassitah, which must be washed with clean water until color, smell, and residue are eradicated.
questions.socraticHint: Which common bodily wastes and fluids require washing with water until trace and smell vanish?

questions.prompt: How must an eating utensil licked by a dog (Najasah Mughalladhah) be cleansed according to the Prophet (SAW)?
questions.text: How must an eating utensil licked by a dog (Najasah Mughalladhah) be cleansed according to the Prophet (SAW)?

options.text: Wiped dry with a clean paper towel
Washed seven times, one of which must be with clean soil/earth
Washed once with warm river water

questions.correctAnswer: Washed seven times, one of which must be with clean soil/earth
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "When a dog drinks from the vessel of any of you, let him wash it seven times, the first [or one] of them with earth (soil)."
questions.socraticHint: How many times must it be washed, and what natural substance must be included in one of the washings?

questions.prompt: Under what circumstances is a Muslim permitted to perform Tayammum (dry ablution) instead of Wudhu with water?
questions.text: Under what circumstances is a Muslim permitted to perform Tayammum (dry ablution) instead of Wudhu with water?

options.text: When the weather is slightly cloudy or breezy
Whenever one is wearing clean leather shoes
When pure water is unavailable or when using water would cause or worsen severe illness or injury
Whenever one feels lazy or in a hurry to catch a bus

questions.correctAnswer: When pure water is unavailable or when using water would cause or worsen severe illness or injury
questions.explanation: Tayammum is a divine concession valid only when water cannot be found despite searching, or when medical necessity (wounds/sickness) forbids water contact.
questions.socraticHint: Is Tayammum permitted for mere convenience or only when water is legitimately absent or medically harmful?

questions.prompt: What natural substance must be used to perform Tayammum according to the Holy Qur'an (Surah An-Nisa 4:43)?
questions.text: What natural substance must be used to perform Tayammum according to the Holy Qur'an (Surah An-Nisa 4:43)?

options.text: Flour or maize meal from the kitchen
Wood ash or coal from the fire
Clean earth, dust, or soil (Sa'eedan Tayyiba)

questions.correctAnswer: Clean earth, dust, or soil (Sa'eedan Tayyiba)
questions.explanation: Surah An-Nisa 4:43 commands: "Fatayammamu sa'eedan tayyiba" ("take clean earth/soil and wipe your faces and hands"). It must be pure and free from contamination.
questions.socraticHint: What pure earth substance provided by nature on the ground is used for dry ablution?

questions.prompt: Which two parts of the body are wiped during the performance of Tayammum?
questions.text: Which two parts of the body are wiped during the performance of Tayammum?
questions.explanation: The Quran specifies wiping the face and the hands in Tayammum: "Wipe with it your faces and your hands" (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6).
questions.socraticHint: Unlike regular Wudhu which includes feet and hair, which two parts are wiped in Tayammum?

questions.prompt: What happens to a person's Tayammum if clean water becomes available before they begin their prayer?
questions.text: What happens to a person's Tayammum if clean water becomes available before they begin their prayer?

options.text: The Tayammum remains valid until sunset
The Tayammum becomes invalid immediately and they must perform regular Wudhu with water
They can continue praying with Tayammum for the next three days
They must pay a financial fine before using the water

questions.correctAnswer: The Tayammum becomes invalid immediately and they must perform regular Wudhu with water
questions.explanation: The fundamental legal rule states: "Idha wujida al-ma'u batala at-tayammum" ("When water is found, Tayammum is invalidated"). The person must make Wudhu with water.
questions.socraticHint: Can dry ablution remain valid if the original reason for its use (lack of water) no longer exists?

questions.prompt: Why should a person blow gently on their hands after striking the clean dust before wiping their face in Tayammum?
questions.text: Why should a person blow gently on their hands after striking the clean dust before wiping their face in Tayammum?

options.text: To test which direction the wind is blowing
To make a whistling sound that alerts others
To remove excess heavy dust and prevent dirt from soiling the eyes or face, following the Sunnah of the Prophet
To warm up the hands before touching the skin

questions.correctAnswer: To remove excess heavy dust and prevent dirt from soiling the eyes or face, following the Sunnah of the Prophet
questions.explanation: Blowing off excess dust ensures that Tayammum remains a clean, symbolic spiritual purification rather than smearing thick dirt on one's face.
questions.socraticHint: How does blowing away heavy dust keep the face clean while fulfilling the spiritual ritual?

questions.prompt: In arid counties of Northern Kenya like Marsabit or Wajir during drought, why is the practice of Tayammum an important act of resource conservation?
questions.text: In arid counties of Northern Kenya like Marsabit or Wajir during drought, why is the practice of Tayammum an important act of resource conservation?

options.text: It makes people stop praying until the rainy season begins
It replaces all drinking water with herbal teas
It encourages wasting water on watering wild shrubs
It preserves scarce potable water strictly for drinking and sustaining human and livestock life without neglecting prayer

questions.correctAnswer: It preserves scarce potable water strictly for drinking and sustaining human and livestock life without neglecting prayer
questions.explanation: Islamic law prioritizes saving lives (Hifdh an-Nafs); during severe water scarcity, water must be preserved for hydration of humans and animals while using Tayammum for Salah.
questions.socraticHint: How does Tayammum allow worship to continue while saving every drop of drinking water for survival?

questions.prompt: How does maintaining daily Taharah (cleanliness of clothes, body, and surroundings) benefit a learner's health in a Kenyan school?
questions.text: How does maintaining daily Taharah (cleanliness of clothes, body, and surroundings) benefit a learner's health in a Kenyan school?

options.text: It prevents waterborne and infectious bacterial diseases, promoting physical hygiene, dignity, and focused learning
It guarantees that the learner will never need to study for exams
It allows pupils to avoid eating school lunch
It exempts learners from physical education classes

questions.correctAnswer: It prevents waterborne and infectious bacterial diseases, promoting physical hygiene, dignity, and focused learning
questions.explanation: Taharah combines spiritual devotion with proven preventive health practices, shielding pupils from infectious pathogens, parasites, and illness while fostering self-respect.
questions.socraticHint: How does washing away impurities protect children from germs and illnesses in school?

questions.prompt: What is the voluntary two-rak’ah prayer performed upon entering a mosque before sitting down called?
questions.text: What is the voluntary two-rak’ah prayer performed upon entering a mosque before sitting down called?
questions.explanation: Tahiyyat al-Masjid (Greeting the Mosque) is a highly recommended 2-rak'ah Sunnah prayer performed immediately upon entering a mosque before taking a seat.
questions.socraticHint: Which prayer literally means "Greeting of the Mosque"?

questions.prompt: At what time of the day is Salat ad-Dhuha (the forenoon prayer) performed?
questions.text: At what time of the day is Salat ad-Dhuha (the forenoon prayer) performed?

options.text: Between Asr and Maghrib as the sun sets
Between after sunrise (when the sun has risen a spear’s length) and just before the zenith of Dhuhr
Immediately at midnight before Fajr begins

questions.correctAnswer: Between after sunrise (when the sun has risen a spear’s length) and just before the zenith of Dhuhr
questions.explanation: Salat ad-Dhuha is prayed in the mid-morning/forenoon after sunrise has fully passed until approximately 15 minutes before the Dhuhr prayer begins.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the mid-morning hours when the sun has risen well above the horizon before midday.

questions.prompt: According to authentic Hadith, praying two rak’ahs of Salat ad-Dhuha fulfills daily charity (Sadaqah) on behalf of how many joints in the human body?
questions.text: According to authentic Hadith, praying two rak’ahs of Salat ad-Dhuha fulfills daily charity (Sadaqah) on behalf of how many joints in the human body?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) taught in Sahih Muslim that there are 360 joints in the human frame requiring daily charitable thanksgiving, and two rak'ahs of Dhuha suffices for all of them.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the number 360 mentioned in prophetic biology regarding human joints.

questions.prompt: How many total regular Sunnah rak’ahs (Sunan ar-Rawatib) attached to daily obligatory prayers did the Prophet (SAW) describe for building a palace in Paradise?
questions.text: How many total regular Sunnah rak’ahs (Sunan ar-Rawatib) attached to daily obligatory prayers did the Prophet (SAW) describe for building a palace in Paradise?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said in Sahih Muslim: "Whoever prays twelve rak'ahs during the day and night, a house will be built for him in Paradise" (2 before Fajr, 4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after Isha).

questions.prompt: How many Sunnah Mu’akkadah rak’ahs are prayed immediately before the obligatory Fajr prayer?
questions.text: How many Sunnah Mu’akkadah rak’ahs are prayed immediately before the obligatory Fajr prayer?
questions.explanation: The two Sunnah rak'ahs before Salat al-Fajr are the most emphasized of all Sunnah prayers, described by the Prophet as better than the world and all it contains.
questions.socraticHint: How many light rak'ahs are offered after the Fajr Adhan and before the Iqamah?

questions.prompt: What special characteristic distinguishes Salat al-Witr from other night prayers?
questions.text: What special characteristic distinguishes Salat al-Witr from other night prayers?

options.text: It must be prayed in total silence without reciting Surah Al-Fatihah
It is performed while seated facing away from the Qiblah
It is concluded with an odd number of rak’ahs (such as 1, 3, or 5) and includes Du’a al-Qunut
It can only be prayed outdoors in the rain

questions.correctAnswer: It is concluded with an odd number of rak’ahs (such as 1, 3, or 5) and includes Du’a al-Qunut
questions.explanation: The word "Witr" means odd number; it is prayed after Isha and night prayers with an odd number of rak'ahs, concluding with the special supplication called Du'a al-Qunut.
questions.socraticHint: What does the word "Witr" mean in Arabic arithmetic?

questions.prompt: What is the special supplication recited standing in the final rak’ah of Salat al-Witr called?
questions.text: What is the special supplication recited standing in the final rak’ah of Salat al-Witr called?
questions.explanation: Du'a al-Qunut is the supplication of obedience and seeking divine guidance recited while standing in the last rak'ah of Salat al-Witr.
questions.socraticHint: Which special prayer begins with "Allahumma ihdini fiman hadayt"?

questions.prompt: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say about Allah’s love for odd numbers in relation to Salat al-Witr?
questions.text: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say about Allah’s love for odd numbers in relation to Salat al-Witr?

options.text: "Indeed, Allah is One (Witr) and He loves that which is odd-numbered"
"Allah prefers even numbers above all things"
"Prayers should only be performed in multiples of four"

questions.correctAnswer: "Indeed, Allah is One (Witr) and He loves that which is odd-numbered"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated: "Inna Allaha witrun yuhibbul-witr, fa awtiru ya ahlal-Qur'an" ("Indeed, Allah is One/Odd and loves that which is odd, so observe Witr, O people of the Qur'an!").
questions.socraticHint: How does the uniqueness and oneness of Allah relate to odd numbers in Witr prayer?

questions.prompt: Why is it recommended for a Muslim to perform Sunan ar-Rawatib prayers in their home rather than always in the mosque?
questions.text: Why is it recommended for a Muslim to perform Sunan ar-Rawatib prayers in their home rather than always in the mosque?

options.text: Because homes have softer carpets than mosques
To bring divine blessings, light, and peace into the home and model prayer for children and family members
Because praying in the mosque is forbidden for voluntary prayers
To avoid walking to the mosque during daylight

questions.correctAnswer: To bring divine blessings, light, and peace into the home and model prayer for children and family members
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) encouraged praying voluntary prayers at home, stating: "Make some of your prayers in your homes and do not turn your homes into graves," filling houses with Barakah and pious examples.
questions.socraticHint: How does praying voluntary prayers at home fill the household with divine light and teach younger siblings?

questions.prompt: What primary role do voluntary Sunnah prayers play on the Day of Judgment when a servant's deeds are audited?
questions.text: What primary role do voluntary Sunnah prayers play on the Day of Judgment when a servant's deeds are audited?

options.text: They allow a person to skip questioning in the grave
They replace the need to fast during Ramadan
They compensate for and complete any flaws or omissions in the obligatory (Fard) prayers
They cancel out all other pillars of Islam

questions.correctAnswer: They compensate for and complete any flaws or omissions in the obligatory (Fard) prayers
questions.explanation: In Hadith Qudsi, Allah tells the angels: "Look and see if My servant has any voluntary prayers," using them to patch up and complete deficiencies in obligatory prayers.
questions.socraticHint: How do extra voluntary good deeds help fill in gaps where obligatory prayers lacked focus or perfection?

questions.prompt: How does the regular performance of Salat ad-Dhuha help a Grade 5 Kenyan learner during morning school hours?
questions.text: How does the regular performance of Salat ad-Dhuha help a Grade 5 Kenyan learner during morning school hours?

options.text: It excuses the pupil from taking notes in class
It allows the pupil to skip break-time games
It gives the pupil permission to arrive late to school
It cultivates spiritual focus, mindfulness, emotional calm, and a grateful attitude towards teachers and classmates

questions.correctAnswer: It cultivates spiritual focus, mindfulness, emotional calm, and a grateful attitude towards teachers and classmates
questions.explanation: Taking a few mindful minutes in the forenoon for prayer instills tranquility, mental clarity, and gratitude, helping learners approach academic tasks with focus and patience.
questions.socraticHint: How does a quiet morning prayer of gratitude recharge a student's emotional calm and focus?

questions.prompt: What attitude should a Muslim child maintain if they miss a voluntary Sunnah prayer?
questions.text: What attitude should a Muslim child maintain if they miss a voluntary Sunnah prayer?

options.text: Feel encouraged to do better next time without despair, while ensuring that all obligatory (Fard) prayers remain strictly fulfilled
Believe they are permanently condemned to punishment

questions.correctAnswer: Feel encouraged to do better next time without despair, while ensuring that all obligatory (Fard) prayers remain strictly fulfilled
questions.explanation: Voluntary prayers are opportunities for extra reward and closeness to Allah without incurring sin if missed; learners maintain enthusiasm and steadfastness in Fard duties.
questions.socraticHint: Is missing a voluntary prayer a punishable sin or an encouraging opportunity to strive better?

questions.prompt: In which Surah and verse of the Holy Qur’an did Allah prescribe fasting during Ramadan for all believers to attain Taqwa?
questions.text: In which Surah and verse of the Holy Qur’an did Allah prescribe fasting during Ramadan for all believers to attain Taqwa?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183 states: "O you who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may attain Taqwa (piety)."
questions.socraticHint: Which foundational verse in the longest Surah of the Qur'an begins with "Kutiba 'alaykumu as-siyam"?

questions.prompt: What are the two essential pillars (Arkan) of Sawm (fasting) in Islam?
questions.text: What are the two essential pillars (Arkan) of Sawm (fasting) in Islam?

options.text: Wearing white clothes and sleeping through the afternoon
Reciting the entire Qur’an in a single day
Niyyah (intention in the heart) and Imsak (abstaining from food, drink, and fast-breakers from dawn to sunset)
Eating dates and drinking cold water at noon

questions.correctAnswer: Niyyah (intention in the heart) and Imsak (abstaining from food, drink, and fast-breakers from dawn to sunset)
questions.explanation: The validity of fasting rests on two pillars: making the intention (Niyyah) before true dawn, and abstaining (Imsak) from all invalidators from Fajr until Maghrib.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the internal intention in the heart and the outward refraining from dawn to sunset.

questions.prompt: When does the fasting period begin and end each day during Ramadan?
questions.text: When does the fasting period begin and end each day during Ramadan?

options.text: Begins at sunrise and ends at midnight
Begins at 8:00 AM and ends at 5:00 PM
Begins at sunset and ends at dawn
Begins at true dawn (Adhan al-Fajr) and ends at sunset (Adhan al-Maghrib)

questions.correctAnswer: Begins at true dawn (Adhan al-Fajr) and ends at sunset (Adhan al-Maghrib)
