questions.explanation: Quran 2:187 instructs Muslims to eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread, then complete the fast until nightfall (sunset).
questions.socraticHint: Which prayer calls mark the exact start at dawn and the breaking of fast at sunset?

questions.prompt: What happens to the fast of a person who accidentally eats or drinks out of genuine forgetfulness while fasting?
questions.text: What happens to the fast of a person who accidentally eats or drinks out of genuine forgetfulness while fasting?

options.text: Their fast remains completely valid; they should stop immediately upon remembering and continue fasting
Their fast is broken and they must fast sixty consecutive days as penalty
They must restart the entire month of Ramadan
They must give away all their clothes to charity

questions.correctAnswer: Their fast remains completely valid; they should stop immediately upon remembering and continue fasting
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Whoever forgets while he is fasting and eats or drinks, let him complete his fast, for it was Allah who fed him and gave him drink."
questions.socraticHint: Does an unintentional, accidental action done out of forgetfulness break an act of worship in Islam?

questions.prompt: Which of the following actions deliberately breaks and invalidates the fast (Mubtilat as-Siyam)?
questions.text: Which of the following actions deliberately breaks and invalidates the fast (Mubtilat as-Siyam)?

options.text: Smelling pleasant food aromas while walking through a market
Intentionally swallowing food or drink during daylight hours
Brushing teeth with a Miswak stick without swallowing
Taking a shower or pouring cool water over one’s head to relieve heat

questions.correctAnswer: Intentionally swallowing food or drink during daylight hours
questions.explanation: Deliberately ingesting any food, beverage, or medicine into the stomach invalidates the fast. Merely showering, using Miswak, or smelling food does not break it.
questions.socraticHint: Which deliberate action involves putting nutritional sustenance into the stomach?

questions.prompt: Who among the following is legitimately exempted by Allah from fasting during Ramadan?
questions.text: Who among the following is legitimately exempted by Allah from fasting during Ramadan?

options.text: A shopkeeper working on a sunny day
Anyone who feels thirsty at 10:00 AM
A person traveling on a strenuous journey or someone who is acutely sick
A student taking a regular mathematics quiz

questions.correctAnswer: A person traveling on a strenuous journey or someone who is acutely sick
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185 explicitly permits the sick and travelers to break the fast and make up the missed days later (Qadha).
questions.socraticHint: Which two categories of people experiencing hardship are mentioned directly in Surah Al-Baqarah 185?

questions.prompt: What is the Islamic term for making up missed fasting days later in the year on a day-for-day basis?
questions.text: What is the Islamic term for making up missed fasting days later in the year on a day-for-day basis?
questions.explanation: Qadha refers to making up missed obligatory acts of worship (like missed fasting days) after the designated time has passed.
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic term means to "make up" or compensate for an obligatory duty missed on its time?

questions.prompt: What compensation is required from a chronically ill or permanently frail elderly person who cannot fast at all and cannot make up days later?
questions.text: What compensation is required from a chronically ill or permanently frail elderly person who cannot fast at all and cannot make up days later?

options.text: Paying Fidyah: feeding a needy person a wholesome meal for each missed day
Fasting twice as many days in the cold season

questions.correctAnswer: Paying Fidyah: feeding a needy person a wholesome meal for each missed day
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:184 establishes Fidyah: those who are permanently unable to fast due to chronic age or incurable illness feed an impoverished person for every day missed.
questions.socraticHint: What charitable payment involves feeding one poor person for each day missed?

questions.prompt: What pre-dawn meal is highly recommended (Sunnah) to eat before the fast begins?
questions.text: What pre-dawn meal is highly recommended (Sunnah) to eat before the fast begins?
questions.explanation: Suhur is the blessed meal eaten before true dawn. The Prophet (SAW) advised: "Take Suhur, for indeed in Suhur there is blessing (Barakah)."
questions.socraticHint: Which meal is eaten in the early hours before dawn to provide strength for the day ahead?

questions.prompt: With what food item did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) preferably break his fast (Iftar) at sunset?
questions.text: With what food item did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) preferably break his fast (Iftar) at sunset?

options.text: Fresh or dry ripe dates (Rutab / Tamr) and water

questions.correctAnswer: Fresh or dry ripe dates (Rutab / Tamr) and water
questions.explanation: The Sunnah of breaking the fast is to begin with ripe or dry dates, or sips of water if dates are unavailable, providing gentle, rapid glucose to the body.
questions.socraticHint: What sweet desert fruit is traditionally eaten first when hearing the sunset Adhan?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) teach about a person who fasts from food but does not abstain from lying, insulting, and cheating?
questions.text: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) teach about a person who fasts from food but does not abstain from lying, insulting, and cheating?

options.text: "His fast is double rewarded because it was difficult"
"He should continue lying as long as he does not drink water"
"Allah has no need for him to leave his food and drink"

questions.correctAnswer: "Allah has no need for him to leave his food and drink"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) emphasized in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Whoever does not leave false speech and evil action, Allah has no need that he should leave his food and drink," proving fasting requires moral discipline.
questions.socraticHint: Does fasting merely mean starving the stomach or guarding the tongue and actions from sin?

questions.prompt: How does fasting in Ramadan nurture empathy and social brotherhood among pupils in a Kenyan school?
questions.text: How does fasting in Ramadan nurture empathy and social brotherhood among pupils in a Kenyan school?

options.text: Experiencing temporary hunger helps pupils deeply appreciate Allah’s provisions and feel sincere compassion for impoverished people who lack food daily
It causes pupils to compete over who eats the most food at Iftar
It isolates Muslim pupils from interacting with classmates
It teaches pupils that poor people do not need food assistance

questions.correctAnswer: Experiencing temporary hunger helps pupils deeply appreciate Allah’s provisions and feel sincere compassion for impoverished people who lack food daily
questions.explanation: Fasting breaks pride and physical comfort, letting every person feel real hunger so their hearts soften with active charity, compassion, and solidarity for the hungry and vulnerable in society.
questions.socraticHint: How does feeling hunger firsthand make a person more compassionate toward hungry people in our country?

questions.prompt: What is the obligatory charity of staple food distributed before the Eid al-Fitr prayer called?
questions.text: What is the obligatory charity of staple food distributed before the Eid al-Fitr prayer called?
questions.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is the food charity mandated upon every Muslim (young, old, male, female) at the conclusion of Ramadan before the Eid prayer.
questions.socraticHint: Which Zakat is specifically tied to the breaking of the fast of Ramadan (Fitr)?

questions.prompt: What measure of staple food (such as maize, wheat, or rice) is required per person for Zakat al-Fitr?
questions.text: What measure of staple food (such as maize, wheat, or rice) is required per person for Zakat al-Fitr?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) mandated one Sa' (equal to four double-handfuls or mudd, roughly 2.5–3 kg) of the local staple food per person.
questions.socraticHint: Which ancient Islamic volume measure equals roughly 2.5 to 3 kilograms of grain?

questions.prompt: What is the primary objective of paying Zakat al-Fitr before the Eid prayer commences?
questions.text: What is the primary objective of paying Zakat al-Fitr before the Eid prayer commences?

options.text: To build new roads between cities
To pay the salaries of government officials
To decorate the prayer ground with colorful banners
To ensure that poor and needy families have ample food to celebrate Eid with dignity and joy alongside everyone else

questions.correctAnswer: To ensure that poor and needy families have ample food to celebrate Eid with dignity and joy alongside everyone else
questions.explanation: The Prophet stated that Zakat al-Fitr purifies the faster from idle speech and provides food for the needy so that no one goes hungry on the day of celebration.
questions.socraticHint: Why is it essential that every poor family has food on the morning of Eid?

questions.prompt: What is the standard percentage rate calculated on eligible savings and commercial wealth for Zakat al-Maal?
questions.text: What is the standard percentage rate calculated on eligible savings and commercial wealth for Zakat al-Maal?
questions.explanation: Zakat al-Maal on monetary wealth, gold, silver, and business merchandise is set at 2.5% (or 1/40th) of qualifying surplus wealth held for one lunar year.
questions.socraticHint: What percentage corresponds to 1 out of every 40 shillings saved?

questions.prompt: What is the minimum threshold of wealth that must be possessed before Zakat al-Maal becomes obligatory called?
questions.text: What is the minimum threshold of wealth that must be possessed before Zakat al-Maal becomes obligatory called?
questions.explanation: Nisab is the minimum qualifying amount of wealth (traditionally equivalent to 85 grams of gold or 595 grams of silver) that obligates the payment of Zakat.
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic term describes the qualifying financial threshold for Zakat?

questions.prompt: What is the condition that savings must be held for a full lunar year before paying Zakat called in Arabic?
questions.text: What is the condition that savings must be held for a full lunar year before paying Zakat called in Arabic?
questions.explanation: Hawl refers to the completion of one full Islamic lunar year (approx. 354 days) of wealth remaining at or above the Nisab threshold.
questions.socraticHint: Which term signifies the passage of one complete lunar year of possessing surplus wealth?

questions.prompt: How many rightful categories of recipients (Asnaf) of Zakat are specified by Allah in Surah At-Tawbah (9:60)?
questions.text: How many rightful categories of recipients (Asnaf) of Zakat are specified by Allah in Surah At-Tawbah (9:60)?
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tawbah verse 60 explicitly defines the eight groups entitled to receive Zakat: the poor, the needy, administrators, reconciled hearts, freeing slaves, debtors, in God’s path, and wayfarers.
questions.socraticHint: Count the groups listed in Surah At-Tawbah verse 60.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between "Al-Fuqara" (the destitute poor) and "Al-Masakin" (the needy) among the Zakat recipients?
questions.text: What is the difference between "Al-Fuqara" (the destitute poor) and "Al-Masakin" (the needy) among the Zakat recipients?

options.text: Al-Fuqara have virtually no income or property at all, while Al-Masakin have some income but it is insufficient to cover basic life necessities
Al-Fuqara are elderly people, while Al-Masakin are young children
Al-Fuqara live in cities, while Al-Masakin live in forests
There is no difference; they mean exactly the same thing in every way

questions.correctAnswer: Al-Fuqara have virtually no income or property at all, while Al-Masakin have some income but it is insufficient to cover basic life necessities
questions.explanation: Scholars define Al-Faqir as someone possessing less than half of their basic survival needs, whereas Al-Miskin possesses half or more but still cannot meet full household living costs.
questions.socraticHint: Who is more severely impoverished: someone with zero assets or someone with some earnings that fall short?

questions.prompt: Who are "Al-Gharimin" listed as eligible recipients of Zakat in Surah At-Tawbah (9:60)?
questions.text: Who are "Al-Gharimin" listed as eligible recipients of Zakat in Surah At-Tawbah (9:60)?

options.text: Professional athletes who lost a game
People burdened by heavy, legitimate debts incurred through necessity that they cannot repay
Wealthy business owners buying luxury cars

questions.correctAnswer: People burdened by heavy, legitimate debts incurred through necessity that they cannot repay
questions.explanation: Al-Gharimin are individuals overwhelmed by crushing debts taken for legitimate needs (e.g. emergency medical bills, basic survival, or community reconciliation) unable to settle them.
questions.socraticHint: Which category refers to people trapped under overwhelming debts?

questions.prompt: Who is "Ibn as-Sabil" among the eight rightful recipients of Zakat?
questions.text: Who is "Ibn as-Sabil" among the eight rightful recipients of Zakat?

options.text: An owner of large herds of camels
A traveler stranded away from home without money or means to return, even if they have assets in their home country
A child who refuses to attend school

questions.correctAnswer: A traveler stranded away from home without money or means to return, even if they have assets in their home country
questions.explanation: Ibn as-Sabil (the wayfarer / son of the road) is a traveler stranded without financial means, who is helped from Zakat funds to reach safety and home.
questions.socraticHint: Which phrase literally means "son of the road" and describes a stranded traveler in need of help?

questions.prompt: If a Kenyan Muslim trader has 100,000 Kenyan Shillings in qualifying savings that have completed a full year above Nisab, how much Zakat al-Maal is due?
questions.text: If a Kenyan Muslim trader has 100,000 Kenyan Shillings in qualifying savings that have completed a full year above Nisab, how much Zakat al-Maal is due?
questions.explanation: To calculate 2.5% of 100,000 KES: 100,000 * 0.025 = 2,500 KES (or 100,000 divided by 40 = 2,500 KES).
questions.socraticHint: Calculate 2.5% of 100,000 by dividing 100,000 by 40.

questions.prompt: How does systematic collection and distribution of Zakat foster social peace and cohesion across Kenyan counties?
questions.text: How does systematic collection and distribution of Zakat foster social peace and cohesion across Kenyan counties?

options.text: It narrows the gap between rich and poor, reduces desperate poverty and theft, and builds compassionate community solidarity
It causes inflation and discourages hard work in agriculture
It creates disputes over money and divides families
It forces wealthy people to leave the country

questions.correctAnswer: It narrows the gap between rich and poor, reduces desperate poverty and theft, and builds compassionate community solidarity
questions.explanation: Zakat prevents the dangerous concentration of wealth among the elite (Surah Al-Hashr 59:7), elevating the destitute, restoring dignity, and creating a harmonious and peaceful society in Kenya.
questions.socraticHint: How does sharing wealth with the needy reduce crime, remove bitterness, and strengthen national brotherhood?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What is the full comprehensive wording of the Islamic greeting of peace and blessings?
questions.text: What is the full comprehensive wording of the Islamic greeting of peace and blessings?

options.text: "La Hawla wa La Quwwata illa Billah"

questions.explanation: The full greeting means: "May the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you," which carries the highest reward of thirty good deeds.
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic phrase conveys Peace, Mercy (Rahmah), and Blessings (Barakah) to the person greeted?

questions.prompt: According to prophetic etiquette, who should initiate the greeting when two people meet?
questions.text: According to prophetic etiquette, who should initiate the greeting when two people meet?

options.text: The seated person must stand and shout first
Only the wealthier person should initiate the greeting
The younger person greets the elder, the walking person greets the seated person, and the smaller group greets the larger group
The elder always speaks first and the younger remains silent

questions.correctAnswer: The younger person greets the elder, the walking person greets the seated person, and the smaller group greets the larger group
questions.explanation: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet (SAW) taught: "The younger should greet the elder, the passerby should greet the seated, and the smaller group should greet the larger."
questions.socraticHint: Think about how youth show respect to elders and moving pedestrians acknowledge seated people.

questions.prompt: What three pieces of advice did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) give to the boy Umar ibn Abi Salamah when he sat down to eat?
questions.text: What three pieces of advice did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) give to the boy Umar ibn Abi Salamah when he sat down to eat?

options.text: "Eat as fast as you can, use both hands, and reach for the center of the dish"
"Do not eat until adults finish, stand up while chewing, and leave leftovers"
"Wash hands after eating only, chew with mouth open, and drink all the water first"
"Say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is directly in front of you"

questions.correctAnswer: "Say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is directly in front of you"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) instructed: "Ya ghulam, sammillah, wa kul bi yameenik, wa kul mimma yaleek" ("O boy, mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you").
questions.socraticHint: Remember the famous three rules: mention Allah's name, use the right hand, and take from the portion closest to you.

questions.prompt: Why did the Prophet (SAW) prohibit eating and drinking with the left hand?
questions.text: Why did the Prophet (SAW) prohibit eating and drinking with the left hand?

options.text: Because Satan (Shaytan) eats and drinks with his left hand
Because the left hand cannot hold spoons
Because left-handed people are forbidden from eating warm meals
Because the left hand should always be kept inside pockets

questions.correctAnswer: Because Satan (Shaytan) eats and drinks with his left hand
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said in Sahih Muslim: "Let not any of you eat with his left hand or drink with it, for indeed Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with his left hand."
questions.socraticHint: Whose negative behavior are we instructed to avoid when eating with the right hand?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) teach regarding the ideal division of the stomach during a meal to avoid overeating?
questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) teach regarding the ideal division of the stomach during a meal to avoid overeating?

options.text: Three quarters for water and one quarter for fruit
One third for food, one third for drink, and one third for breath/air
Completely full of food with no room for water
Half for food and half for sweets

questions.correctAnswer: One third for food, one third for drink, and one third for breath/air
questions.explanation: In Sunan at-Tirmidhi, the Prophet taught moderation: if a person must fill their stomach, let it be "one third for food, one third for his drink, and one third for his breath."
questions.socraticHint: Which three-way division ensures healthy digestion and easy breathing after meals?

questions.prompt: How did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) advise Muslims to drink water properly?
questions.text: How did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) advise Muslims to drink water properly?

options.text: Blowing warm breath into the water before drinking
Drinking while running across the field
While seated, taking two or three paused sips, and without breathing into the cup
Standing up and gulping the entire glass down in one single breath

questions.correctAnswer: While seated, taking two or three paused sips, and without breathing into the cup
questions.explanation: The Sunnah of drinking is to sit down, say Bismillah, drink in two or three calm breaths, remove the cup away from the mouth when breathing, and say Alhamdulillah.
questions.socraticHint: Should water be gulped quickly while standing or sipped calmly while seated without exhaling into the cup?

questions.prompt: What was the lifelong habit of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) regarding food that was offered to him if he did not find it appealing?
questions.text: What was the lifelong habit of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) regarding food that was offered to him if he did not find it appealing?

options.text: He would criticize the cook loudly and demand a replacement meal
He would throw the dish onto the floor
He would force someone else to eat it immediately
He never found fault with any food; if he liked it he ate it, and if he disliked it he left it quietly without complaining

questions.correctAnswer: He never found fault with any food; if he liked it he ate it, and if he disliked it he left it quietly without complaining
questions.explanation: Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari: "The Prophet (SAW) never criticized any food at all. If he liked it he ate it, and if he disliked it he left it," protecting the feelings of the host.
questions.socraticHint: Did the Prophet complain about meals or leave food quietly without hurting the host?

questions.prompt: What Islamic virtue is described by Prophet Muhammad (SAW) as "bringing nothing except good" and being an essential branch of Iman?
questions.text: What Islamic virtue is described by Prophet Muhammad (SAW) as "bringing nothing except good" and being an essential branch of Iman?

options.text: Haya' (Modesty / Sense of shame before Allah and people)

questions.correctAnswer: Haya' (Modesty / Sense of shame before Allah and people)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "Al-Haya'u la ya'tee illa bi khayr" ("Modesty brings nothing but good") and "Modesty is a branch of faith," guarding morality and chastity.
questions.socraticHint: Which virtue represents modest dignity, self-respect, and moral decency in speech and appearance?

questions.prompt: How does practicing Haya' (modesty) manifest in the daily speech and conduct of a Grade 5 pupil at school?
questions.text: How does practicing Haya' (modesty) manifest in the daily speech and conduct of a Grade 5 pupil at school?

options.text: The pupil writes rude graffiti on classroom desks
The pupil speaks with respect, avoids vulgar words or insults, dresses decently, and refrains from vulgar jokes
The pupil speaks loudly and interrupts the teacher repeatedly
The pupil refuses to participate in classroom discussions

questions.correctAnswer: The pupil speaks with respect, avoids vulgar words or insults, dresses decently, and refrains from vulgar jokes
questions.explanation: Haya' protects moral purity: a modest pupil uses courteous language, dresses appropriately, respects personal boundaries, and avoids foul or shameless talk.
questions.socraticHint: How does a sense of moral modesty protect a student from using foul language or rude behavior?

questions.prompt: What words of praise and thanks to Allah should a Muslim recite upon finishing eating a meal?
questions.text: What words of praise and thanks to Allah should a Muslim recite upon finishing eating a meal?
questions.explanation: Saying "Alhamdulillah" expresses heartfelt gratitude to Allah who provided the nourishment and quenched hunger and thirst.
questions.socraticHint: Which phrase meaning "All praise belongs to Allah" is recited after eating?

questions.prompt: Why is wasting food (Israf) strictly condemned in Islam according to Surah Al-A'raf (7:31)?
questions.text: Why is wasting food (Israf) strictly condemned in Islam according to Surah Al-A'raf (7:31)?

options.text: Because food left on a plate turns into plastic
Because leftover food is legally forbidden to animals
Because wasting food makes plates heavy
Because Allah states: "Eat and drink, but waste not by excess; indeed He loves not the wasteful"

questions.correctAnswer: Because Allah states: "Eat and drink, but waste not by excess; indeed He loves not the wasteful"
questions.explanation: Surah Al-A'raf 7:31 prohibits extravagance (Israf). Throwing away good edible food is ungratefulness to Allah while millions around the world suffer malnutrition.
questions.socraticHint: What does the Qur'an say about those who indulge in wasteful excess (Al-Musrifin)?

questions.prompt: How does spreading the greeting of Salam contribute to peace and safety within a Kenyan school environment?
questions.text: How does spreading the greeting of Salam contribute to peace and safety within a Kenyan school environment?

options.text: It breaks down social barriers, removes hatred and suspicion, and creates an atmosphere of warmth, brotherhood, and safety
It causes students to waste study time talking in hallways
It ensures only pupils of the same clan speak to each other
It eliminates the need for school rules and discipline

questions.correctAnswer: It breaks down social barriers, removes hatred and suspicion, and creates an atmosphere of warmth, brotherhood, and safety
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I guide you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the Salam among you!"
questions.socraticHint: How does offering a sincere wish of peace melt animosity and bring hearts closer together?

questions.prompt: In Surah Al-Isra (17:23), what minor expression of irritation or disrespect towards parents is strictly forbidden by Allah?
questions.text: In Surah Al-Isra (17:23), what minor expression of irritation or disrespect towards parents is strictly forbidden by Allah?

options.text: Walking behind them along the pathway
Saying even the mildest word of contempt like "Uff" (sighing in annoyance)
Asking them what they would like for breakfast

questions.correctAnswer: Saying even the mildest word of contempt like "Uff" (sighing in annoyance)
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Isra 17:23 states: "Fala taqul lahuma uff" ("Say not to them so much as 'Uff' and do not repel them, but speak to them a noble word"). Even a tiny sigh of exasperation is prohibited.
questions.socraticHint: What short sound of grumbling or sighing in irritation is explicitly outlawed in Surah Al-Isra?

questions.prompt: When a man asked Prophet Muhammad (SAW) who was most deserving of his good companionship and care, how many times did the Prophet reply "Your mother" before saying "Your father"?
questions.text: When a man asked Prophet Muhammad (SAW) who was most deserving of his good companionship and care, how many times did the Prophet reply "Your mother" before saying "Your father"?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) answered: "Your mother," then "Your mother," then "Your mother," and on the fourth time said: "Then your father," giving the mother threefold honor.
questions.socraticHint: How many times did the Prophet repeat "your mother" in the famous Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari?

questions.prompt: Why does Islamic teaching give the mother three times special honor and consideration compared to others?
questions.text: Why does Islamic teaching give the mother three times special honor and consideration compared to others?

options.text: Because mothers earn more money in business than fathers
Because mothers do not have to perform prayers
Because mothers always stay in Makkah
Because of her unique hardships of pregnancy, the labor pains of childbirth, and years of devoted breastfeeding and nurturing

questions.correctAnswer: Because of her unique hardships of pregnancy, the labor pains of childbirth, and years of devoted breastfeeding and nurturing
questions.explanation: Scholars explain that the threefold mention corresponds to three hardships borne exclusively by mothers: bearing the child during pregnancy, the suffering of delivery, and nursing.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the three unique physical and emotional sacrifices made by mothers that fathers do not experience.

questions.prompt: What beautiful supplication for parents is taught by Allah in Surah Al-Isra (17:24)?
questions.text: What beautiful supplication for parents is taught by Allah in Surah Al-Isra (17:24)?

options.text: "Rabbi irhamhuma kama rabbayani sagheera" ("My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small")
"Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanah"
"Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana"

questions.correctAnswer: "Rabbi irhamhuma kama rabbayani sagheera" ("My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small")
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Isra 17:24 instructs children to lower the wing of humility out of mercy and pray: "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was a child."
questions.socraticHint: Which prayer asks Allah to have mercy on parents just as they tenderly cared for us in our childhood?

questions.prompt: What is the Islamic term for maintaining and strengthening family ties with relatives and kin?
questions.text: What is the Islamic term for maintaining and strengthening family ties with relatives and kin?
questions.explanation: Silat ar-Rahim literally means "connecting the womb/kinship," referring to keeping loving ties, communication, and mutual assistance with blood relatives.
questions.socraticHint: Which phrase contains the word "Rahim" (womb/kinship) and signifies upholding family connections?

questions.prompt: What worldly and spiritual rewards did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) promise to a person who faithfully practices Silat ar-Rahim?
questions.text: What worldly and spiritual rewards did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) promise to a person who faithfully practices Silat ar-Rahim?

options.text: Being given a golden crown in this worldly life
Expansion and abundance in wealth/provision, and a prolonged life blessed with good deeds
Exemption from paying taxes to the government

questions.correctAnswer: Expansion and abundance in wealth/provision, and a prolonged life blessed with good deeds
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Whoever loves that his provision be expanded and his life prolonged, let him maintain the ties of kinship."
questions.socraticHint: Which two blessings—plentiful sustenance and a long blessed lifespan—are linked to maintaining kinship?

questions.prompt: What should a Muslim child do if their parents command them to do something that violates the commandments of Allah (such as lying or not praying)?
questions.text: What should a Muslim child do if their parents command them to do something that violates the commandments of Allah (such as lying or not praying)?

options.text: Shout at the parents and run away from home forever
Obey the parents even if it displeases Allah
Insult the parents in front of community elders
Politely and respectfully decline to commit the sin while continuing to treat their parents with kindness and noble companionship

questions.correctAnswer: Politely and respectfully decline to commit the sin while continuing to treat their parents with kindness and noble companionship
questions.explanation: Surah Luqman (31:15) instructs that if parents urge disobedience to Allah, do not obey them in that sin, but accompany them in worldly life with kindness and respect.
questions.socraticHint: Can obedience to humans supersede obedience to Allah, and how must one treat parents even when disagreeing?

questions.prompt: Who is the true maintainer of kinship (Al-Wasil) according to Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?
questions.text: Who is the true maintainer of kinship (Al-Wasil) according to Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?

options.text: The one who reaches out and mends ties when relatives cut them off, not merely the one who reciprocates visits
The one who only visits relatives when they give him expensive presents
The one who attends weddings but boycotts funerals
The one who talks about family ancestry on social media

questions.correctAnswer: The one who reaches out and mends ties when relatives cut them off, not merely the one who reciprocates visits
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said in Sahih al-Bukhari: "The one who maintains ties is not the one who merely reciprocates; rather, the one who maintains ties is the one who, when kinship is severed, reconnects it."
questions.socraticHint: Is true kinship just exchanging equal favors or reconnecting with relatives who have drifted away?

questions.prompt: How can a child continue to honor and benefit their parents after the parents have passed away?
questions.text: How can a child continue to honor and benefit their parents after the parents have passed away?

options.text: By building an empty monument with statues
By making constant Du’a (supplication) for their forgiveness, giving charity (Sadaqah) on their behalf, and honoring their friends and relatives
By selling all the family land and keeping the money for vacations
By forgetting about them and never mentioning their names

questions.correctAnswer: By making constant Du’a (supplication) for their forgiveness, giving charity (Sadaqah) on their behalf, and honoring their friends and relatives
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught that when a person dies, their deeds cease except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for them.
questions.socraticHint: Which three continuous acts keep sending divine reward to deceased parents in the grave?

questions.prompt: In Kenyan culture and Islamic teaching, how does helping elderly grandparents in rural areas demonstrate Birr al-Walidayn?
questions.text: In Kenyan culture and Islamic teaching, how does helping elderly grandparents in rural areas demonstrate Birr al-Walidayn?

options.text: It is done only to gain an inheritance
It replaces the need to care for one's own parents
It fulfills the religious duty of honoring family elders with physical care, respect, and emotional warmth in their vulnerable old age
It allows children to escape school homework

questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the religious duty of honoring family elders with physical care, respect, and emotional warmth in their vulnerable old age
questions.explanation: Grandparents are an extension of one's parents; serving them with humility, fetching water, herding goats, or cooking meals reflects deep moral piety and family devotion.
questions.socraticHint: How does caring for elderly grandparents honor our family roots and fulfill religious filial piety?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) say about Paradise and the mother’s service in the Hadith narrated by Mu’awiyah ibn Jahima?
questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) say about Paradise and the mother’s service in the Hadith narrated by Mu’awiyah ibn Jahima?

options.text: "Leave her and go on distant military expeditions"
"Fathers alone hold the keys to Paradise"
"Stay with her, for indeed Paradise lies at her feet"

questions.correctAnswer: "Stay with her, for indeed Paradise lies at her feet"
questions.explanation: When Jahima asked to go for voluntary struggle, the Prophet asked if his mother was alive. When he said yes, the Prophet replied: "Cling to her feet, for Paradise is there!"
questions.socraticHint: Where did the Prophet say Paradise lies when advising a young man to care for his living mother?

questions.prompt: Why is severing family ties (Qat' ar-Rahim) warned against so sternly in the Holy Qur'an (Surah Muhammad 47:22-23)?
questions.text: Why is severing family ties (Qat' ar-Rahim) warned against so sternly in the Holy Qur'an (Surah Muhammad 47:22-23)?

options.text: Because destroying family bonds causes social breakdown, emotional trauma, community disintegration, and forfeits Allah's mercy
Because relatives are legally required to sign business contracts daily
Because it causes physical illness in livestock
Because family members must always attend the same school

questions.correctAnswer: Because destroying family bonds causes social breakdown, emotional trauma, community disintegration, and forfeits Allah's mercy
questions.explanation: The Prophet warned: "The one who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise." Discarding family connections breeds isolation, bitter feuds, and communal decay.
questions.socraticHint: How does breaking family ties destroy community harmony and bring severe spiritual consequences?

questions.prompt: What did Allah command believers regarding non-Muslims who do not fight them or expel them from their homes in Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:8)?
questions.text: What did Allah command believers regarding non-Muslims who do not fight them or expel them from their homes in Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:8)?

options.text: To compel them to convert to Islam against their will
To be righteous, kind, and just towards them, for indeed Allah loves those who act justly
To refuse to speak to them or trade with them
To drive them out of their neighborhoods

questions.correctAnswer: To be righteous, kind, and just towards them, for indeed Allah loves those who act justly
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:8 explicitly enjoins Birr (benevolent kindness) and Qist (fair justice) towards non-Muslims who live peacefully alongside Muslims.
questions.socraticHint: Does Allah command fairness and kindness or hostility towards peaceful non-Muslim neighbors?

questions.prompt: What historic multi-faith constitutional treaty did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) draft upon arriving in Madinah to establish peaceful civic coexistence?
questions.text: What historic multi-faith constitutional treaty did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) draft upon arriving in Madinah to establish peaceful civic coexistence?
questions.explanation: The Sahifat al-Madinah was the pioneering written constitution that bound Muslims, Jewish tribes, and Arab clans into one civic commonwealth with equal rights and mutual security.
questions.socraticHint: Which document established the civic rights and religious freedom of all groups living together in Madinah?

questions.prompt: What guarantee did the Constitution of Madinah give to Jewish and other non-Muslim citizens living in the city?
questions.text: What guarantee did the Constitution of Madinah give to Jewish and other non-Muslim citizens living in the city?

options.text: They were forced to leave the Arabian peninsula immediately
They were forbidden from participating in public markets
They were required to change their ancestral names
Freedom of religious practice, security of their property, and equal protection under civic law

questions.correctAnswer: Freedom of religious practice, security of their property, and equal protection under civic law
questions.explanation: The charter established: "To the Jews is their religion, and to the Muslims is their religion," guaranteeing life, property, dignity, and religious practice.
questions.socraticHint: What essential democratic and civil rights of religion and property were protected in the charter?

questions.prompt: What does the Holy Qur’an state in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:256) regarding religious belief and freedom of conscience?
questions.text: What does the Holy Qur’an state in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:256) regarding religious belief and freedom of conscience?

options.text: "There is no compulsion in religion; truth stands out clearly from falsehood"
"Everyone in the world must be forced to accept faith"
"Faith can only be taught through physical punishment"
"Religious beliefs should be decided by lottery"

questions.correctAnswer: "There is no compulsion in religion; truth stands out clearly from falsehood"
questions.explanation: "La ikraha fid-deen" (There is no compulsion in religion) guarantees that faith must come from voluntary personal conviction of the heart, never through coercion.
questions.socraticHint: Which famous verse clearly states "La ikraha fid-deen"?

questions.prompt: Why does Surah Al-An'am (6:108) forbid Muslims from insulting or reviling the idols or deities worshiped by polytheists?
questions.text: Why does Surah Al-An'am (6:108) forbid Muslims from insulting or reviling the idols or deities worshiped by polytheists?

options.text: Because insulting idols makes the weather cloudy
Lest they in their ignorance insult Allah out of retaliation and enmity, escalating conflict and hatred
Because idols have magical powers to harm people
Because Muslims are required to worship those idols alongside Allah

questions.correctAnswer: Lest they in their ignorance insult Allah out of retaliation and enmity, escalating conflict and hatred
questions.explanation: The Quran warns: "And do not insult those they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge," safeguarding civic harmony and mutual respect.
questions.socraticHint: How does insulting someone else's beliefs provoke them to retaliate and insult Allah?

questions.prompt: What stern warning did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) issue to anyone who harms a non-Muslim peaceful citizen (Mu'ahid) living in the Muslim society?
questions.text: What stern warning did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) issue to anyone who harms a non-Muslim peaceful citizen (Mu'ahid) living in the Muslim society?

options.text: "He should merely pay a small market fee"
"His deeds will be praised by the community"
"I will be his opponent and accuser on the Day of Judgment!"
"He will receive a bonus reward of ten camels"

questions.correctAnswer: "I will be his opponent and accuser on the Day of Judgment!"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated: "Beware! Whoever oppresses a non-Muslim citizen with a covenant, curtails his rights, or burdens him beyond his capacity, I will be his adversary on the Day of Judgment!"
questions.socraticHint: Who will directly stand as the prosecutor on the Day of Judgment against anyone oppressing non-Muslim minorities?

questions.prompt: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) do when the funeral procession of a Jewish person passed before him in Madinah?
questions.text: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) do when the funeral procession of a Jewish person passed before him in Madinah?

options.text: He turned his back and walked away quickly
He told the companions to stop the procession
He closed his eyes and remained seated
He stood up out of respect; when his companions asked why he stood for a Jewish funeral, he replied: "Is it not a human soul?"

questions.correctAnswer: He stood up out of respect; when his companions asked why he stood for a Jewish funeral, he replied: "Is it not a human soul?"
questions.explanation: In Sahih al-Bukhari, when a funeral bier passed by, the Prophet stood. When told it was a Jew, he declared: "A laysat nafsan?" ("Was it not a human soul?"), showing universal reverence for human dignity.
questions.socraticHint: What rhetorical question did the Prophet ask to affirm the inherent sanctity and dignity of every human being?

questions.prompt: How do Muslim pupils in Kenya practice peaceful coexistence with classmates of different religious backgrounds during school break times?
questions.text: How do Muslim pupils in Kenya practice peaceful coexistence with classmates of different religious backgrounds during school break times?

options.text: By sharing play equipment, respecting each other's dignity, collaborating in class assignments, and maintaining kind friendship
By sitting in separate corners and refusing to play games together
By mocking the religious traditions of other communities
By demanding that non-Muslims leave the playground

questions.correctAnswer: By sharing play equipment, respecting each other's dignity, collaborating in class assignments, and maintaining kind friendship
questions.explanation: Kenyan national values and Islamic ethics foster inclusive friendship, cooperative games, and mutual support among children of all backgrounds in our diverse nation.
questions.socraticHint: How does playing together and sharing equipment build inclusive friendship among classmates of all faiths?

questions.prompt: In Kenyan towns like Mombasa, Malindi, or Nairobi, how do Muslim and Christian leaders collaborate to prevent ethnic or religious conflict?
questions.text: In Kenyan towns like Mombasa, Malindi, or Nairobi, how do Muslim and Christian leaders collaborate to prevent ethnic or religious conflict?

options.text: By banning people of other faiths from entering public transport
Through interfaith peace councils, joint community barazas, and shared humanitarian initiatives during national challenges
By holding public arguments in the market square
By building high walls between residential neighborhoods

questions.correctAnswer: Through interfaith peace councils, joint community barazas, and shared humanitarian initiatives during national challenges
questions.explanation: Interfaith dialogue committees bring religious leaders together to resolve local misunderstandings, mediate disputes, and preach tolerance and unity across communities.
questions.socraticHint: How do joint community barazas and peace committees bring diverse leaders together for national unity?

questions.prompt: What does the Qur’anic principle in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13) teach about the divine wisdom behind human ethnic and tribal diversity?
questions.text: What does the Qur’anic principle in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13) teach about the divine wisdom behind human ethnic and tribal diversity?

options.text: Tribal differences exist to cause perpetual competition and war
People should only marry within their own clan
Mankind was created into nations and tribes so that they may know and appreciate one another (Li ta'arafoo), not despise one another
Certain tribes were created superior to rule over all others

questions.correctAnswer: Mankind was created into nations and tribes so that they may know and appreciate one another (Li ta'arafoo), not despise one another
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13 declares: "We made you into nations and tribes that you may know each other. Truly the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous."
questions.socraticHint: Did Allah create human diversity for mutual hatred and division or for mutual learning and knowing one another?

questions.prompt: How does participation in national Harambee (community self-help) projects reflect the Islamic duty of civic cooperation?
questions.text: How does participation in national Harambee (community self-help) projects reflect the Islamic duty of civic cooperation?

options.text: It proves that communities should rely only on foreign donations
It is done solely for political recognition
It violates the principle of individual worship
It puts into practice the Quranic command to "Cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression" (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:2)

questions.correctAnswer: It puts into practice the Quranic command to "Cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression" (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:2)
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:2 orders mutual cooperation in Birr (righteousness) and Taqwa (good deeds). Harambee embodies collective community service for the common good.
questions.socraticHint: Which verse in Surah Al-Ma'idah urges believers to collaborate for good and shun aggression?

questions.prompt: Why is tribalism (Asabiyyah / negative ethnic chauvinism) considered destructive and strictly prohibited in Islam?
questions.text: Why is tribalism (Asabiyyah / negative ethnic chauvinism) considered destructive and strictly prohibited in Islam?

options.text: It blinds people to justice, promotes prejudice and nepotism, and divides society into warring factions instead of a unified nation of righteous citizens
It helps build larger schools in rural areas
It is permitted as long as people wear traditional clothes
It guarantees economic success in business

questions.correctAnswer: It blinds people to justice, promotes prejudice and nepotism, and divides society into warring factions instead of a unified nation of righteous citizens
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) condemned tribalism firmly: "He is not one of us who calls to tribal partisanship, nor who fights for tribalism, nor who dies for tribalism."
questions.socraticHint: How does tribalism undermine justice and national unity by favoring clans over moral righteousness?

questions.prompt: What title and responsibility did Allah bestow upon human beings on Earth according to Surah Al-Baqarah (2:30)?
questions.text: What title and responsibility did Allah bestow upon human beings on Earth according to Surah Al-Baqarah (2:30)?

options.text: Khalifah (Stewards / Trustees responsible for caring for and preserving creation)
Tyrants allowed to exploit and pollute nature without restriction
Spectators who have no responsibility toward the environment

questions.correctAnswer: Khalifah (Stewards / Trustees responsible for caring for and preserving creation)
questions.explanation: Allah declared to the angels: "Inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifah" ("Indeed, I will make upon the earth a viceregent/steward"), charging humans with sacred stewardship of creation.
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic term describes our role as trustees and custodians of Allah's creation?

questions.prompt: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) tell his companion Sa'd when he saw him using excessive water for Wudhu?
questions.text: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) tell his companion Sa'd when he saw him using excessive water for Wudhu?

options.text: "Water from rivers cannot be used for prayer"
"Washing quickly is better than washing thoroughly"
"Do not waste water, even if you are on the banks of a flowing river!"
"Use as much water as you like because it cleanses sins faster"

questions.correctAnswer: "Do not waste water, even if you are on the banks of a flowing river!"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) prohibited wastefulness (Israf) in water use even if standing beside a boundless flowing river, establishing conservation as an inviolable spiritual discipline.
questions.socraticHint: Did the Prophet permit water wastage even when an abundant flowing river is right in front of you?

questions.prompt: According to authentic Hadith, what reward does a Muslim receive when birds, people, or animals eat fruit from a tree they planted?
questions.text: According to authentic Hadith, what reward does a Muslim receive when birds, people, or animals eat fruit from a tree they planted?

options.text: They receive financial compensation from the government
They are granted ownership of wild birds
The fruit becomes tasteless for animals
It counts as ongoing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah) for the planter throughout its lifetime

questions.correctAnswer: It counts as ongoing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah) for the planter throughout its lifetime
questions.explanation: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet (SAW) taught: "No Muslim plants a tree or sows seeds, and then a bird, person, or animal eats from it, but that it is regarded as a charity (Sadaqah) for him."
questions.socraticHint: How does planting a fruit-bearing tree continue generating spiritual rewards for the planter even when wild animals eat from it?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) say should be done if the Day of Resurrection begins while a person holds a date-palm sapling in their hand?
questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) say should be done if the Day of Resurrection begins while a person holds a date-palm sapling in their hand?

options.text: "If he is able to plant it before he stands up, let him plant it!"
"Throw it away immediately and run away"
"Give the sapling to someone else to hold"

questions.correctAnswer: "If he is able to plant it before he stands up, let him plant it!"
questions.explanation: In Musnad Ahmad, the Prophet said: "If the Final Hour comes while one of you has a palm shoot in his hand, if he can plant it before standing, let him do so!" underscoring hope and stewardship.
questions.socraticHint: Does the Prophet urge us to plant the sapling even at the very last second of worldly existence?

questions.prompt: What story did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) narrate regarding a sinful person who was forgiven all sins for showing mercy to an animal?
questions.text: What story did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) narrate regarding a sinful person who was forgiven all sins for showing mercy to an animal?

options.text: A farmer who trained pigeons to carry trade letters
A person drew water in their leather shoe from a deep well to save a panting, dying thirsty dog in the desert heat
A person who bought thousands of horses for a parade
A hunter who captured a wild lion and locked it in a cage

questions.correctAnswer: A person drew water in their leather shoe from a deep well to save a panting, dying thirsty dog in the desert heat
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) narrated that a traveler climbed down into a well, filled his leather sock with water, and quenched the thirst of a dying dog; Allah appreciated this deed and forgave him.
questions.socraticHint: Which animal was dying of thirst licking damp sand until a traveler quenched its thirst with water in a leather sock?

questions.prompt: Conversely, what warning did the Prophet (SAW) give about the woman who was punished in Hellfire regarding a cat?
questions.text: Conversely, what warning did the Prophet (SAW) give about the woman who was punished in Hellfire regarding a cat?

options.text: She gave the cat sweet milk instead of clean water
She bought the cat from a market trader outside Makkah
She imprisoned a cat without feeding it or letting it go free to eat insects and mice from the ground until it starved to death
She allowed the cat to sleep on her clean prayer rug

questions.correctAnswer: She imprisoned a cat without feeding it or letting it go free to eat insects and mice from the ground until it starved to death
questions.explanation: In Sahih al-Bukhari, a woman entered Hellfire because she tied up a cat, refusing to feed it or let it forage for food until it died of starvation, showing cruelty to animals is a grave sin.
questions.socraticHint: Why was the woman punished: for locking up the cat without food or freedom until it died?

questions.prompt: What is the Islamic ruling regarding bribery (Rashwah) in public offices and judicial decisions?
questions.text: What is the Islamic ruling regarding bribery (Rashwah) in public offices and judicial decisions?

options.text: It is permissible as long as the amount is small
It is encouraged to speed up government services
It is considered a legitimate form of voluntary charity
It is strictly Haram (forbidden); Prophet Muhammad (SAW) cursed both the one who gives a bribe and the one who accepts a bribe

questions.correctAnswer: It is strictly Haram (forbidden); Prophet Muhammad (SAW) cursed both the one who gives a bribe and the one who accepts a bribe
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) declared: "La'ana Allahu ar-rashi wal-murtashi" ("May the curse of Allah be upon the briber and the bribe-taker"). Bribery perverts justice and ruins society.
questions.socraticHint: Did the Prophet pronounce a curse upon both the giver and the taker of bribes in judgment?

questions.prompt: How does Kenya’s national initiative to grow 15 billion trees by 2032 align with the prophetic concept of Sadaqah Jariyah?
questions.text: How does Kenya’s national initiative to grow 15 billion trees by 2032 align with the prophetic concept of Sadaqah Jariyah?

options.text: Trees fight deforestation and climate change, providing oxygen, shade, and food for future generations, serving as continuous ongoing charity
Trees prevent people from traveling between counties
Trees eliminate the need for agricultural farming
Trees are planted only for timber exports

questions.correctAnswer: Trees fight deforestation and climate change, providing oxygen, shade, and food for future generations, serving as continuous ongoing charity
questions.explanation: Planting trees restores watersheds, combats desertification in arid counties, and brings ongoing blessings (Sadaqah Jariyah) for the planter long after they pass away.
questions.socraticHint: How do planted trees provide environmental benefits and continuous spiritual rewards for generations to come?

questions.prompt: Why is public property and infrastructure (such as schools, taps, roads, and hospitals) considered a sacred trust (Amanah) in Islam?
questions.text: Why is public property and infrastructure (such as schools, taps, roads, and hospitals) considered a sacred trust (Amanah) in Islam?

options.text: Because repairing buildings is not allowed in Islamic architecture
Because public assets belong to the entire community and defacing or vandalizing them harms everyone and violates trust before Allah
Because public property is owned by foreign organizations
Because only police officers are permitted to use public facilities

questions.correctAnswer: Because public assets belong to the entire community and defacing or vandalizing them harms everyone and violates trust before Allah
questions.explanation: Public resources serve the common welfare. Misusing, damaging, or embezzling public goods is a severe breach of trust (Ghuluwl) that impacts the rights of all citizens.
questions.socraticHint: Why is vandalizing community property a grave sin that hurts all citizens and violates sacred trust?

questions.prompt: How can a Grade 5 pupil actively practice water conservation when making Wudhu at school in Kenya?
questions.text: How can a Grade 5 pupil actively practice water conservation when making Wudhu at school in Kenya?

options.text: By splashing water across the floor for fun
By leaving the tap fully open while conversing with friends
By turning off the tap between washings or using a cup/small bowl rather than leaving the water tap running continuously
By washing each limb twenty times

questions.correctAnswer: By turning off the tap between washings or using a cup/small bowl rather than leaving the water tap running continuously
questions.explanation: Using a small container or gently turning the tap off between washing limbs emulates the Prophet's practice of making Wudhu with just one mudd (approx. 650 ml) of water.
questions.socraticHint: How does using a cup or turning off the tap between limb washings prevent wasting clean tap water?

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) teach about the removal of harmful objects (such as sharp glass or stones) from public roads and paths?
questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) teach about the removal of harmful objects (such as sharp glass or stones) from public roads and paths?

options.text: It should only be done by paid municipal workers
It is a waste of personal time
It is only rewarded if done during the month of Ramadan
It is an authentic act of charity (Sadaqah) and a branch of true faith (Iman)

questions.correctAnswer: It is an authentic act of charity (Sadaqah) and a branch of true faith (Iman)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) declared: "Imatatul-adha 'anit-tareeqi sadaqah" ("Removing harmful things from the road is charity") and noted that a person was admitted to Jannah for removing a thorny branch from a pathway.
questions.socraticHint: Which branch of faith directly involves clearing thorns and sharp debris from where people walk?

questions.prompt: How does combining Islamic moral character (Akhlaq) with diligent academic study help Kenyan pupils build a prosperous and corrupt-free nation?
questions.text: How does combining Islamic moral character (Akhlaq) with diligent academic study help Kenyan pupils build a prosperous and corrupt-free nation?

options.text: It equips learners with both technical competence and deep ethical integrity (Amanah), creating honest leaders who serve society with fairness and devotion
It encourages learners to avoid public leadership roles
It focuses solely on accumulating personal wealth at the expense of others
It prevents students from learning modern digital skills

questions.correctAnswer: It equips learners with both technical competence and deep ethical integrity (Amanah), creating honest leaders who serve society with fairness and devotion
questions.explanation: Integrating competence with God-consciousness (Taqwa) and integrity (Amanah) produces incorruptible doctors, engineers, teachers, and leaders who steer Kenya toward justice and prosperity.
questions.socraticHint: How does uniting academic skills with ethical integrity ensure that future leaders reject corruption and serve the Kenyan people faithfully?

questions.prompt: How many 50-shilling notes make 200 shillings?
questions.explanation: 4 × 50 = 200 shillings.
questions.socraticHint: Count by fifties: 50, 100, 150...
questions.kenyanCulturalContext: Fifty shilling notes feature Kenyan wildlife.

questions.prompt: What does the attribute "Sarvavyapi" mean regarding the Supreme Divine (Paramatma)?
questions.text: What does the attribute "Sarvavyapi" mean regarding the Supreme Divine (Paramatma)?

options.text: Living only on high mountain peaks away from humans
Omnipresent—existing everywhere in the universe and in every living creature
Able to speak only one language
Existing only inside temple sanctums during festivals

questions.correctAnswer: Omnipresent—existing everywhere in the universe and in every living creature
questions.explanation: "Sarvavyapi" combines "Sarva" (all) and "Vyapi" (permeating/pervading), expressing that Paramatma is omnipresent, dwelling in all creation and within every soul as Atman.
questions.socraticHint: Which English word starting with "omni-" means present in all places at all times?

questions.prompt: What does the divine attribute "Sarvashaktiman" signify in Hindu philosophy?
questions.text: What does the divine attribute "Sarvashaktiman" signify in Hindu philosophy?

options.text: Needing physical weapons to create the world
Relying on humans to provide strength
Omnipotent—possessing all power and the ultimate source of all cosmic energy
Possessing strength only equal to five elephants

questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotent—possessing all power and the ultimate source of all cosmic energy
questions.explanation: "Sarvashaktiman" means all-powerful (omnipotent). Paramatma possesses boundless spiritual, cosmic, and creative power that sustains all planetary systems.
questions.socraticHint: What term means having infinite, unlimited power over all of creation?

questions.prompt: What is the meaning of the attribute "Sarvajna" when describing Paramatma?
questions.text: What is the meaning of the attribute "Sarvajna" when describing Paramatma?

options.text: Knowing only what is written in printed books
Knowing only events that happened in ancient times
Unable to understand the silent thoughts of humans
Omniscient—all-knowing, aware of all actions, thoughts, and intentions across time

questions.correctAnswer: Omniscient—all-knowing, aware of all actions, thoughts, and intentions across time
questions.explanation: "Sarvajna" means all-knowing (omniscient), understanding the innermost thoughts, motivations, and deeds of all creatures in past, present, and future.
questions.socraticHint: Which word describing God refers to complete, infinite knowledge of everything?

questions.prompt: What term refers to the eternal individual soul residing within each living being that is a spark of Paramatma?
questions.text: What term refers to the eternal individual soul residing within each living being that is a spark of Paramatma?
questions.explanation: The Atman is the immortal, divine soul present within all living beings, reflecting the omnipresent light of Paramatma.
questions.socraticHint: Which Sanskrit word refers to the immortal spiritual soul within every person and animal?

questions.prompt: What classic analogy in the Upanishads illustrates how Paramatma is invisible yet present everywhere in the universe?
questions.text: What classic analogy in the Upanishads illustrates how Paramatma is invisible yet present everywhere in the universe?

options.text: A piece of wood burning into smoke
Salt dissolved in water, which cannot be seen with the eye yet makes every drop taste salty
A stone sinking to the bottom of a river
A bird flying out of a metal cage

questions.correctAnswer: Salt dissolved in water, which cannot be seen with the eye yet makes every drop taste salty
questions.explanation: In the Chandogya Upanishad, the sage Uddalaka asks his son Svetaketu to dissolve salt in water: though invisible, salt pervades every drop, just as Paramatma pervades creation.
questions.socraticHint: Think of salt or sugar stirred into a glass of water—can you see it, or do you taste its presence everywhere?

questions.prompt: What profound Sanskrit phrase from the Maha Upanishad teaches that the entire world is one interconnected family?
questions.text: What profound Sanskrit phrase from the Maha Upanishad teaches that the entire world is one interconnected family?

options.text: "Ahimsa Paramo Dharmah" (Non-violence is the supreme virtue)
"Matru Devo Bhava" (Revere your mother as divine)

questions.explanation: "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" means "the entire Earth is a single family," reminding us that because all beings share the same divine essence, we should love all people equally.
questions.socraticHint: Which universal phrase translates to "The whole Earth is indeed one family"?

questions.prompt: How does understanding that Paramatma is Sarvajna (all-knowing) influence a pupil's moral choices when they are alone?
questions.text: How does understanding that Paramatma is Sarvajna (all-knowing) influence a pupil's moral choices when they are alone?

options.text: The pupil only behaves well when an adult is holding a reward
The pupil believes that secret actions have no consequences
The pupil speaks lies whenever they are outside the classroom
The pupil acts honestly and kindly even when no teacher or parent is watching, knowing God is aware of every thought and deed

questions.correctAnswer: The pupil acts honestly and kindly even when no teacher or parent is watching, knowing God is aware of every thought and deed
questions.explanation: Recognizing that Paramatma knows our innermost thoughts inspires genuine integrity (Satya) and moral discipline, eliminating deceit whether observed or unobserved.
questions.socraticHint: How does knowing that God sees all private thoughts and actions encourage personal honesty?

questions.prompt: What form of greeting do Hindus practice by joining both palms together in front of the chest, acknowledging the divine spark (Atman) in the other person?
questions.text: What form of greeting do Hindus practice by joining both palms together in front of the chest, acknowledging the divine spark (Atman) in the other person?
questions.explanation: "Namaste" literally means "I bow to the divine presence within you," expressing profound humility, equality, and reverence for the sacred soul in every human being.
questions.socraticHint: Which customary greeting involves placing both hands together near the heart and bowing slightly?

questions.prompt: How does believing that Paramatma is Sarvavyapi (present everywhere) encourage environmental respect among pupils?
questions.text: How does believing that Paramatma is Sarvavyapi (present everywhere) encourage environmental respect among pupils?

options.text: It encourages building concrete walls around all green spaces
It teaches that trees, rivers, and animals share divine life and must not be polluted, deforested, or harmed recklessly
It suggests that people should avoid walking on grass altogether
It means nature does not need to be cared for by humans

questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that trees, rivers, and animals share divine life and must not be polluted, deforested, or harmed recklessly
questions.explanation: Because divine consciousness pervades all nature, Hindu tradition reveres rivers (as sacred mothers), trees, and wildlife, instilling deep conservation ethics.
questions.socraticHint: If God resides within all living nature, how should we treat forests, rivers, and animals?

questions.prompt: In Nairobi, how do Grade 5 learners at SSDN Temple and local schools put the teaching of "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" into practice?
questions.text: In Nairobi, how do Grade 5 learners at SSDN Temple and local schools put the teaching of "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" into practice?

options.text: By refusing to participate in national holiday events
By competing selfishly for school prizes
By showing respect, sharing learning materials, and welcoming classmates of all ethnic and religious communities as brothers and sisters
By only associating with students from their own neighborhood

questions.correctAnswer: By showing respect, sharing learning materials, and welcoming classmates of all ethnic and religious communities as brothers and sisters
questions.explanation: Treating the world as one family means embracing all fellow Kenyan citizens with kindness, overcoming tribal or religious prejudices, and building national solidarity.
questions.socraticHint: How does viewing all Kenyans as family members promote harmony and friendship in school?

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between Paramatma (Supreme Soul) and Jivatma (individual embodied soul)?
questions.text: What is the relationship between Paramatma (Supreme Soul) and Jivatma (individual embodied soul)?

options.text: They are hostile enemies constantly at war
Paramatma was created by human thoughts while Jivatma is made of rock
There is no connection between them whatsoever
Paramatma is the infinite cosmic ocean of consciousness, while the Jivatma is like an individual drop of water originating from that same ocean

questions.correctAnswer: Paramatma is the infinite cosmic ocean of consciousness, while the Jivatma is like an individual drop of water originating from that same ocean
questions.explanation: The individual soul (Jivatma) shares the same divine essence with the Supreme Soul (Paramatma), just as a drop of sea spray has the same nature as the boundless ocean.
questions.socraticHint: Think of an individual water droplet and the vast ocean from which it comes.

questions.prompt: Why is practicing prayer and silent meditation (Dhyana) beneficial for a Grade 5 pupil's mental well-being in Kenya?
questions.text: Why is practicing prayer and silent meditation (Dhyana) beneficial for a Grade 5 pupil's mental well-being in Kenya?

options.text: It calms turbulent thoughts, connects the mind with inner peace, improves concentration for studies, and reduces anxiety
It makes the pupil fall asleep during examinations
It replaces the need to do physical exercise and sports
It guarantees that one will never experience rainy weather

questions.correctAnswer: It calms turbulent thoughts, connects the mind with inner peace, improves concentration for studies, and reduces anxiety
questions.explanation: Meditation (Dhyana) still the mind, centers the awareness on the divine presence within, enhances academic focus, and nurtures emotional resilience.
questions.socraticHint: How does taking quiet time to calm the breath and mind improve focus and reduce stress for pupils?

questions.prompt: What ancient Vedic concept represents the cosmic order, truth, and natural harmony governing the entire universe?
questions.text: What ancient Vedic concept represents the cosmic order, truth, and natural harmony governing the entire universe?
questions.explanation: Rta is the foundational Vedic concept of the universal cosmic rhythm and moral order that regulates nature, celestial bodies, and ethical conduct.
questions.socraticHint: Which short three-letter Vedic term signifies the eternal cosmic harmony and natural balance?

questions.prompt: Which divine deity in the Rigveda is especially revered as the guardian and protector of Rta (Cosmic Order)?
questions.text: Which divine deity in the Rigveda is especially revered as the guardian and protector of Rta (Cosmic Order)?
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, Lord Varuna is known as Rtasya Gopa (the guardian of Rta), overseeing the moral and physical laws that keep the universe in equilibrium.
questions.socraticHint: Which deity is described as Rtasya Gopa—the keeper of cosmic order and ocean depths?

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of Rta manifesting in the physical natural world around us?
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Rta manifesting in the physical natural world around us?

options.text: Traffic jams during rush hour in Nairobi
A broken bicycle wheel left by the roadside
An unexpected loud sound from a television
The predictable rhythm of day and night, the cycling of rainy and dry seasons, and rivers flowing to the ocean

questions.correctAnswer: The predictable rhythm of day and night, the cycling of rainy and dry seasons, and rivers flowing to the ocean
questions.explanation: Rta is evident in the ordered, dependable cycles of the natural cosmos: sunrise, moon phases, rain patterns, plant growth, and planetary orbits.
questions.socraticHint: Look for recurring, dependable natural phenomena like day and night or weather seasons.

questions.prompt: How does the cosmic concept of Rta connect to the moral virtue of Dharma in human life?
questions.text: How does the cosmic concept of Rta connect to the moral virtue of Dharma in human life?

options.text: Dharma is the practice of living in personal harmony with Rta through truthfulness, justice, duty, and kindness
Dharma means breaking natural laws whenever convenient
Rta applies only to animals while Dharma applies only to stones
There is no connection between cosmic order and human moral conduct

questions.correctAnswer: Dharma is the practice of living in personal harmony with Rta through truthfulness, justice, duty, and kindness
questions.explanation: While Rta is cosmic order in nature, Dharma is the human expression of that order—living ethically, doing one's duty, and preserving social and ecological harmony.
questions.socraticHint: How does practicing righteousness (Dharma) bring our personal actions into alignment with natural cosmic order (Rta)?

questions.prompt: What happens to the natural environment when human beings disrupt Rta through reckless exploitation and pollution?
questions.text: What happens to the natural environment when human beings disrupt Rta through reckless exploitation and pollution?

options.text: Wild animals relocate peacefully to cities
Ecological imbalance results, leading to severe droughts, water scarcity, loss of wildlife, and climate disasters
Nature automatically becomes twice as productive
Rainfall increases and cleans the rivers without effort

questions.correctAnswer: Ecological imbalance results, leading to severe droughts, water scarcity, loss of wildlife, and climate disasters
questions.explanation: Disrupting Rta (natural balance) causes ecological degradation—deforestation, erratic climate patterns, poisoned water sources, and suffering for all living species.
questions.socraticHint: What environmental crises occur when humans cut forests recklessly and pollute fresh water?

questions.prompt: How can Kenyan pupils help preserve Rta (natural harmony) within their school compound?
questions.text: How can Kenyan pupils help preserve Rta (natural harmony) within their school compound?

options.text: By wasting tap water while washing their hands
By uprooting flowering shrubs in the courtyard
By planting indigenous trees, harvesting rainwater, managing waste, and caring for school gardens
By throwing plastic wrappers under classroom desks

questions.correctAnswer: By planting indigenous trees, harvesting rainwater, managing waste, and caring for school gardens
questions.explanation: Active ecological stewardship—tree planting, waste reduction, water conservation—restores and protects the natural harmony of Rta right at school.
questions.socraticHint: Which positive ecological activities support clean soil, healthy trees, and conserved water in school?

questions.prompt: Why are major rivers like the Ganga in India and rivers in Kenya revered as sacred mothers in spiritual traditions?
questions.text: Why are major rivers like the Ganga in India and rivers in Kenya revered as sacred mothers in spiritual traditions?

options.text: Because rivers are made of pure silver
Because rivers flow only backwards up mountains
Because fish are not allowed to swim in rivers
Because water sustains all life, irrigates crops, quenches thirst, and purifies, acting as a nurturing mother to all living beings

questions.correctAnswer: Because water sustains all life, irrigates crops, quenches thirst, and purifies, acting as a nurturing mother to all living beings
questions.explanation: Rivers provide life-giving water for farming, drinking, and purification, embodying maternal sustenance and deserving the highest care and protection from pollution.
questions.socraticHint: How do rivers nurture and sustain all crops, animals, and human communities just like a mother?

questions.prompt: In Nakuru, how does the Hindu youth community's lake cleanup project protect wildlife in alignment with Rta?
questions.text: In Nakuru, how does the Hindu youth community's lake cleanup project protect wildlife in alignment with Rta?

options.text: By clearing dangerous plastic and waste from the lakeshore, preserving clean habitats for flamingos and endangered animals
By catching flamingos to keep as domestic pets
By pouring soap into the lake to wash the water
By restricting wild animals from drinking lake water

questions.correctAnswer: By clearing dangerous plastic and waste from the lakeshore, preserving clean habitats for flamingos and endangered animals
questions.explanation: Removing non-biodegradable plastics from the ecosystem protects birds and marine life from choking and toxicity, upholding the sacred balance of Rta.
questions.socraticHint: How does removing plastic waste from lake shores keep bird and animal habitats clean and safe?

questions.prompt: What principle of living in harmony with Rta encourages simplicity and prevents greed from destroying nature?
questions.text: What principle of living in harmony with Rta encourages simplicity and prevents greed from destroying nature?

options.text: Aparigraha (Non-possessiveness / contentment with taking only what is needed)

questions.correctAnswer: Aparigraha (Non-possessiveness / contentment with taking only what is needed)
questions.explanation: Aparigraha teaches taking only what is necessary for sustainable life without hoarding or overconsumption, preserving natural resources for future generations.
questions.socraticHint: Which virtue involves non-greed, simplicity, and not hoarding excess material possessions?
