questions.text: A regular tetrahedron is a triangular-based pyramid whose faces are all equilateral triangles. How many faces does it have?
questions.explanation: A tetrahedron has 4 faces (all equilateral triangles), 4 vertices, and 6 edges.
questions.socraticHint: The prefix 'tetra-' means four in Greek (e.g., 4 triangular faces).

questions.prompt: The net of a complete closed cone consists of which two geometric figures?
questions.text: The net of a complete closed cone consists of which two geometric figures?

options.text: A sector of a circle and a circular base

questions.correctAnswer: A sector of a circle and a circular base
questions.explanation: The curved sloped surface of a cone unrolls into a sector of a circle, while the flat bottom is a circle.
questions.socraticHint: Think of an ice cream cone unrolled flat: it forms a fan-like sector of a circle, with a circular lid at the base.

questions.prompt: A mineral crystal polyhedron has 12 vertices and 30 edges. Using Euler's formula F + V - E = 2, how many faces does it have?
questions.text: A mineral crystal polyhedron has 12 vertices and 30 edges. Using Euler's formula F + V - E = 2, how many faces does it have?
questions.explanation: Euler's formula: F + V - E = 2 => F + 12 - 30 = 2 => F - 18 = 2 => F = 2 + 18 = 20 faces (an icosahedron).
questions.socraticHint: Use F = 2 + E - V. What is 2 + 30 - 12?

questions.prompt: Why does a flat pattern of 5 connected squares in a single straight row NOT form a closed cube when folded?
questions.text: Why does a flat pattern of 5 connected squares in a single straight row NOT form a closed cube when folded?

options.text: It has a strip of 5 consecutive squares, causing two faces to overlap when folded

questions.correctAnswer: It has a strip of 5 consecutive squares, causing two faces to overlap when folded
questions.explanation: A cube can have at most 4 connected squares in a straight row. A row of 5 squares causes the 1st and 5th squares to overlap onto the same face, leaving one side open.
questions.socraticHint: A cube can only have at most 4 connected squares in a straight row to fold into 4 walls without overlapping.

questions.prompt: A cube's net is drawn on cardboard. If each square face has an edge length of 8 cm, what is the total surface area of the cube?
questions.text: A cube's net is drawn on cardboard. If each square face has an edge length of 8 cm, what is the total surface area of the cube?
questions.explanation: Area of 1 face = 8 x 8 = 64 cm². Total surface area of 6 faces = 6 x 64 = 384 cm².
questions.socraticHint: Find the area of one square face (8 x 8 = 64) and multiply by all 6 faces.

questions.prompt: A closed cylindrical tin has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Using pi = 22/7, what is its total surface area?
questions.text: A closed cylindrical tin has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Using pi = 22/7, what is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Curved surface area = 2 x pi x r x h = 2 x (22/7) x 7 x 10 = 440 cm². Area of 2 circular bases = 2 x (pi x r²) = 2 x ((22/7) x 7 x 7) = 308 cm². Total surface area = 440 + 308 = 748 cm².
questions.socraticHint: Add the curved surface area (2 pi r h) to the two circular bases (2 pi r²).

questions.prompt: What are the coordinates of the origin (the point where the horizontal x-axis and vertical y-axis meet) in the Cartesian plane?
questions.text: What are the coordinates of the origin (the point where the horizontal x-axis and vertical y-axis meet) in the Cartesian plane?
questions.explanation: The origin is the reference intersection point of the coordinate axes, designated as (0, 0).
questions.socraticHint: The starting intersection where both horizontal and vertical values are zero.

questions.prompt: In the ordered pair (4, 7), which coordinate represents the horizontal distance from the y-axis along the x-axis?
questions.text: In the ordered pair (4, 7), which coordinate represents the horizontal distance from the y-axis along the x-axis?
questions.explanation: In (x, y), the first coordinate is the x-coordinate (4), representing horizontal displacement.
questions.socraticHint: Coordinates are always written in alphabetical order: (x, y). The first number is x.

questions.prompt: A point P is located 5 units to the right of the origin along the horizontal axis and 3 units upwards along the vertical axis. What are the coordinates of P?
questions.text: A point P is located 5 units to the right of the origin along the horizontal axis and 3 units upwards along the vertical axis. What are the coordinates of P?
questions.explanation: Horizontal movement along x is 5, vertical movement along y is 3, yielding (5, 3).
questions.socraticHint: Write the horizontal movement first, then the vertical movement: (x, y).

questions.prompt: What is the distance between point A(2, 6) and point B(9, 6) on a Cartesian grid?
questions.text: What is the distance between point A(2, 6) and point B(9, 6) on a Cartesian grid?
questions.explanation: Both points lie on the horizontal line y = 6. Distance = 9 - 2 = 7 units.
questions.socraticHint: Since both points have the same y-coordinate (6), subtract the smaller x-coordinate from the larger: 9 - 2.

questions.prompt: What is the distance between point C(4, 1) and point D(4, 9) on a Cartesian grid?
questions.text: What is the distance between point C(4, 1) and point D(4, 9) on a Cartesian grid?
questions.explanation: Both points lie on the vertical line x = 4. Distance = 9 - 1 = 8 units.
questions.socraticHint: Since both points have the same x-coordinate (4), subtract the y-coordinates: 9 - 1.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5), and (1, 5). What is its perimeter?
questions.text: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5), and (1, 5). What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Length = 7 - 1 = 6 units. Width = 5 - 1 = 4 units. Perimeter = 2 x (6 + 4) = 2 x 10 = 20 units.
questions.socraticHint: Find the length (7 - 1 = 6) and the width (5 - 1 = 4), then calculate 2 x (length + width).

questions.prompt: What is the area of the rectangle with vertices (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5), and (1, 5)?
questions.text: What is the area of the rectangle with vertices (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5), and (1, 5)?
questions.explanation: Length = 6 units, Width = 4 units. Area = Length x Width = 6 x 4 = 24 square units.
questions.socraticHint: Multiply the length by the width: 6 x 4.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has vertices at (2, 2), (8, 2), and (2, 7). What is its area?
questions.text: A right-angled triangle has vertices at (2, 2), (8, 2), and (2, 7). What is its area?
questions.explanation: Base = 8 - 2 = 6 units. Height = 7 - 2 = 5 units. Area = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x 6 x 5 = 15 square units.
questions.socraticHint: The horizontal base is 8 - 2 = 6, and the vertical height is 7 - 2 = 5. Use A = 1/2 b h.

questions.prompt: Three vertices of a rectangle are A(3, 2), B(9, 2), and C(9, 6). What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex D?
questions.text: Three vertices of a rectangle are A(3, 2), B(9, 2), and C(9, 6). What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex D?
questions.explanation: Vertex D must align vertically with A (x = 3) and horizontally with C (y = 6), giving D(3, 6).
questions.socraticHint: In a rectangle, opposite vertical sides share the same horizontal coordinate (x = 3) and opposite horizontal sides share the same vertical coordinate (y = 6).

questions.prompt: Point P(2, 4) is translated 3 units to the right and 2 units upwards. What are its new coordinates?
questions.text: Point P(2, 4) is translated 3 units to the right and 2 units upwards. What are its new coordinates?
questions.explanation: New x = 2 + 3 = 5. New y = 4 + 2 = 6. Translated point = (5, 6).
questions.socraticHint: Add 3 to the x-coordinate and add 2 to the y-coordinate.

questions.prompt: Point M(4, 5) is reflected in the horizontal line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the reflected image M'?
questions.text: Point M(4, 5) is reflected in the horizontal line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the reflected image M'?
questions.explanation: Point M is 2 units above y = 3 (5 - 3 = 2). Its reflected image is 2 units below y = 3 (3 - 2 = 1). The x-coordinate remains 4, yielding (4, 1).
questions.socraticHint: Point M is 2 units above the line y = 3. The reflected image must be 2 units directly below the line y = 3.

questions.prompt: What are the coordinates of the midpoint between point J(2, 5) and point K(8, 5)?
questions.text: What are the coordinates of the midpoint between point J(2, 5) and point K(8, 5)?
questions.explanation: Midpoint x = (2 + 8) / 2 = 10 / 2 = 5. Midpoint y = 5. Midpoint coordinates = (5, 5).
questions.socraticHint: Find the average of the x-coordinates: (2 + 8) / 2.

questions.prompt: Five Grade 6 pupils scored 72, 85, 68, 90, and 75 in a mathematics assessment test. What was their mean score?
questions.text: Five Grade 6 pupils scored 72, 85, 68, 90, and 75 in a mathematics assessment test. What was their mean score?
questions.socraticHint: Add all five scores together and divide by 5.

questions.prompt: What is the median of the following set of daily egg counts from a poultry farm: 14, 22, 18, 25, 12, 19, 16?
questions.text: What is the median of the following set of daily egg counts from a poultry farm: 14, 22, 18, 25, 12, 19, 16?
questions.explanation: Arranged in ascending order: 12, 14, 16, 18, 19, 22, 25. The middle value (4th of 7 items) is 18.
questions.socraticHint: First arrange the 7 numbers in ascending order from smallest to largest, then pick the middle number.

questions.prompt: What is the median of this data set: 8, 12, 15, 19, 23, 27?
questions.text: What is the median of this data set: 8, 12, 15, 19, 23, 27?
questions.explanation: There are 6 items (even number). The two middle values are 15 and 19. Median = (15 + 19) / 2 = 34 / 2 = 17.
questions.socraticHint: When there is an even number of values, add the two middle numbers (15 and 19) and divide by 2.

questions.prompt: A shoe store in Eldoret recorded shoe sizes sold in one afternoon: 38, 40, 39, 41, 40, 42, 40, 39. What is the modal shoe size?
questions.text: A shoe store in Eldoret recorded shoe sizes sold in one afternoon: 38, 40, 39, 41, 40, 42, 40, 39. What is the modal shoe size?
questions.explanation: The number 40 occurs 3 times, which is more frequent than any other shoe size. Mode = 40.
questions.socraticHint: The mode is the value that appears most frequently in the data.

questions.prompt: The daily maximum temperatures recorded in Lodwar over one week were: 34°C, 38°C, 36°C, 41°C, 35°C, 39°C, 37°C. What is the range of the temperatures?
questions.text: The daily maximum temperatures recorded in Lodwar over one week were: 34°C, 38°C, 36°C, 41°C, 35°C, 39°C, 37°C. What is the range of the temperatures?
questions.explanation: Range = Highest value - Lowest value = 41°C - 34°C = 7°C.
questions.socraticHint: Range is the difference between the highest value (41) and the lowest value (34).

questions.prompt: The mean of four numbers 15, 22, 18, and x is 20. What is the value of x?
questions.text: The mean of four numbers 15, 22, 18, and x is 20. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Sum of the four numbers = 4 x 20 = 80. Sum of three known numbers = 15 + 22 + 18 = 55. x = 80 - 55 = 25.
questions.socraticHint: The four numbers must add up to 4 x 20 = 80. Subtract the sum of the three known numbers from 80.

questions.prompt: In a primary school of 720 pupils, 180 participate in athletics. What angle represents athletics on a circular pie chart?
questions.text: In a primary school of 720 pupils, 180 participate in athletics. What angle represents athletics on a circular pie chart?
questions.socraticHint: Find what fraction 180 is out of 720, then multiply by 360°.

questions.prompt: On a pie chart displaying agricultural land use, tea farming is represented by a sector of 144 degrees. If the total farm size is 50 hectares, how many hectares are under tea?
questions.text: On a pie chart displaying agricultural land use, tea farming is represented by a sector of 144 degrees. If the total farm size is 50 hectares, how many hectares are under tea?
questions.explanation: Hectares under tea = (144 / 360) x 50 = (2 / 5) x 50 = 20 hectares.
questions.socraticHint: Divide 144° by 360° (which simplifies to 2/5), then multiply by 50.

questions.prompt: A frequency table shows football goals scored: 0 goals (2 matches), 1 goal (4 matches), 2 goals (3 matches), 3 goals (1 match). What is the total number of goals scored across all matches?
questions.text: A frequency table shows football goals scored: 0 goals (2 matches), 1 goal (4 matches), 2 goals (3 matches), 3 goals (1 match). What is the total number of goals scored across all matches?
questions.socraticHint: Multiply each goal number by its frequency and add the products: (0 x 2) + (1 x 4) + (2 x 3) + (3 x 1).

questions.prompt: Using the football data from question 9 (13 total goals across 10 matches), what was the mean number of goals scored per match?
questions.text: Using the football data from question 9 (13 total goals across 10 matches), what was the mean number of goals scored per match?
questions.explanation: Total matches = 2 + 4 + 3 + 1 = 10 matches. Mean goals per match = 13 / 10 = 1.3 goals.
questions.socraticHint: Divide the total goals (13) by the total number of matches (10).

questions.prompt: In a statistical tally chart, four vertical tally marks crossed by a fifth diagonal stroke represent what count?
questions.text: In a statistical tally chart, four vertical tally marks crossed by a fifth diagonal stroke represent what count?
questions.explanation: In tallying, a bundle consists of four vertical strokes crossed by one diagonal stroke to represent 5.
questions.socraticHint: In standard tallying, a diagonal slash across four bars completes a bundle of 5.

questions.prompt: A bar graph records rainfall in Kitale: February had 60 mm, while April had 180 mm. By how many millimetres did rainfall increase between February and April?
questions.text: A bar graph records rainfall in Kitale: February had 60 mm, while April had 180 mm. By how many millimetres did rainfall increase between February and April?
questions.explanation: Rainfall increase = April (180 mm) - February (60 mm) = 120 mm.
questions.socraticHint: Subtract the February rainfall (60 mm) from the April rainfall (180 mm).

questions.prompt: What is the theoretical probability of tossing a fair coin and obtaining a 'Head'?
questions.text: What is the theoretical probability of tossing a fair coin and obtaining a 'Head'?
questions.explanation: There is 1 favorable outcome (Head) out of 2 possible equally likely outcomes (Head, Tail). Probability = 1/2.
questions.socraticHint: There is 1 favorable outcome (Heads) out of 2 possible outcomes (Heads or Tails).

questions.prompt: A standard six-sided die has faces numbered 1 to 6. What is the probability of rolling an even number (2, 4, or 6)?
questions.text: A standard six-sided die has faces numbered 1 to 6. What is the probability of rolling an even number (2, 4, or 6)?
questions.explanation: There are 3 even numbers (2, 4, 6) out of 6 possible faces. Probability = 3 / 6 = 1/2.
questions.socraticHint: Three out of the six faces are even numbers: 3/6 simplifies to what?

questions.prompt: A bag contains 4 red beads, 5 green beads, and 6 yellow beads. If one bead is picked at random without looking, what is the probability that it is green?
questions.text: A bag contains 4 red beads, 5 green beads, and 6 yellow beads. If one bead is picked at random without looking, what is the probability that it is green?
questions.explanation: Total beads = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 beads. Probability of picking green = 5 / 15 = 1/3.
questions.socraticHint: Find the total number of beads (4 + 5 + 6 = 15), then divide the number of green beads by 15.

questions.prompt: What is the probability of an impossible event that cannot occur under any circumstances?
questions.text: What is the probability of an impossible event that cannot occur under any circumstances?
questions.explanation: An impossible event has a probability of 0, while an event that is absolutely certain has a probability of 1.
questions.socraticHint: A certain event has probability 1, while an event that cannot happen has probability zero.

questions.prompt: Solve for y in the linear equation: y + 17 = 42.
questions.text: Solve for y in the linear equation: y + 17 = 42.
questions.explanation: Subtract 17 from both sides: y = 42 - 17 = 25.
questions.socraticHint: Subtract 17 from both sides of the equation: 42 - 17.

questions.prompt: Solve for x in the equation: 3x + 8 = 29.
questions.text: Solve for x in the equation: 3x + 8 = 29.
questions.socraticHint: First subtract 8 from 29 to get 3x = 21, then divide by 3.

questions.prompt: Solve for m in the equation: (m / 4) - 3 = 5.
questions.text: Solve for m in the equation: (m / 4) - 3 = 5.
questions.socraticHint: First add 3 to both sides to get m / 4 = 8, then multiply by 4.

questions.prompt: Juma had k shillings. His father gave him KES 150, and he now has KES 400. Which algebraic equation correctly represents this statement?
questions.text: Juma had k shillings. His father gave him KES 150, and he now has KES 400. Which algebraic equation correctly represents this statement?
questions.explanation: Adding 150 to Juma's initial money k results in a total of 400: k + 150 = 400 (so k = 250).
questions.socraticHint: Adding 150 to Juma's original money k gives a total of 400.

questions.prompt: Three identical exercise books and a pen costing KES 25 cost a total of KES 145. What is the cost of one exercise book?
questions.text: Three identical exercise books and a pen costing KES 25 cost a total of KES 145. What is the cost of one exercise book?
questions.socraticHint: Subtract the pen's price (25) from the total (145) to get 120, then divide by 3 books.

questions.prompt: Simplify the algebraic expression: 4a + 7b + 2a - 3b.
questions.text: Simplify the algebraic expression: 4a + 7b + 2a - 3b.
questions.explanation: Collecting like terms: (4a + 2a) + (7b - 3b) = 6a + 4b.
questions.socraticHint: Group like terms together: (4a + 2a) and (7b - 3b).

questions.prompt: A rectangle has length (2x + 3) cm and width (x + 1) cm. What is the simplified algebraic expression for its perimeter?

Classify the five Kenyan vertebrates correctly by their protective outer body covering:
(1) Leopard, (2) Ostrich, (3) Cobra, (4) Tree frog, (5) Tilapia

questions.text: How many body segments and how many walking legs does an adult insect (such as a grasshopper or honeybee) have?
questions.explanation: Insects have bodies divided into three segments: head, thorax, and abdomen, with 3 pairs of jointed walking legs (6 legs total) attached to the thorax.
questions.socraticHint: Count the legs on an ant or bee: How many pairs of legs do insects possess?
questions.prompt: How many body segments and how many walking legs does an adult insect (such as a grasshopper or honeybee) have?

questions.text: Which group of invertebrates includes spiders, scorpions, and ticks, characterized by having 8 walking legs and no antennae?
questions.explanation: Arachnids have two body parts (cephalothorax and abdomen), 4 pairs of legs (8 legs), no antennae, and no wings.
questions.socraticHint: How many legs does a spider have? What is the scientific name for the spider and scorpion group?
questions.prompt: Which group of invertebrates includes spiders, scorpions, and ticks, characterized by having 8 walking legs and no antennae?

questions.text: To which invertebrate group do crabs, prawns, and lobsters belong, characterized by a hard calcified carapace and 2 pairs of antennae?
questions.explanation: Crustaceans are predominantly aquatic arthropods possessing a hard, chitinous and calcified exoskeleton, 2 pairs of antennae, and branched appendages.
questions.socraticHint: What class of marine and freshwater arthropods includes crabs and prawns?
questions.prompt: To which invertebrate group do crabs, prawns, and lobsters belong, characterized by a hard calcified carapace and 2 pairs of antennae?

questions.text: Which soft-bodied invertebrate is commonly found in gardens, moves with a muscular foot, and carries a protective spiral shell on its back?
questions.explanation: The garden snail is a gastropod mollusc with a soft unsegmented body, a muscular creeping foot, and a calcareous coiled protective shell.
questions.socraticHint: Which slow garden creature retreats into its hard shell when touched?
questions.prompt: Which soft-bodied invertebrate is commonly found in gardens, moves with a muscular foot, and carries a protective spiral shell on its back?

questions.text: How do earthworms benefit agricultural soil in Kenyan farming communities like Meru and Kisii?

options.text: They compact the soil to make it as hard as rock
They burrow tunnels that aerate the soil and their castings enrich soil fertility
They eat and destroy the root tubers of growing crops
They produce chemical poisons that kill all earth microorganisms

questions.correctAnswer: They burrow tunnels that aerate the soil and their castings enrich soil fertility
questions.explanation: Earthworms are decomposers; as they burrow, they aerate the soil, improve water infiltration, and digest organic matter, releasing nutrient-rich worm castings.
questions.socraticHint: How does an earthworm's burrowing and feeding help crop roots get air and organic nutrients?
questions.prompt: How do earthworms benefit agricultural soil in Kenyan farming communities like Meru and Kisii?

questions.text: Through which anatomical structures do insects breathe atmospheric air?
questions.explanation: Insects breathe through tiny lateral openings along their thorax and abdomen called spiracles, which lead into a branching network of tracheal tubes.
questions.socraticHint: What are the tiny breathing pores along the sides of an insect's body called?
questions.prompt: Through which anatomical structures do insects breathe atmospheric air?

questions.text: A student observes a small creature with 2 main body segments, 8 walking legs, no wings, and no antennae. How should this organism be classified?
questions.explanation: Having 2 body parts (cephalothorax and abdomen), 8 legs, and no antennae is the diagnostic combination of arachnids (e.g., spider, scorpion).
questions.socraticHint: Which class of arthropods has 8 legs and lacks antennae?
questions.prompt: A student observes a small creature with 2 main body segments, 8 walking legs, no wings, and no antennae. How should this organism be classified?

questions.text: Which of the following invertebrates is a dangerous parasite that transmits East Coast Fever in Kenyan livestock?
questions.explanation: Ticks are parasitic arachnids that suck blood from cattle and transmit protozoan pathogens causing East Coast Fever (Theileriosis).
questions.socraticHint: Which blood-sucking livestock pest is removed when cattle are plunged into a cattle dip?
questions.prompt: Which of the following invertebrates is a dangerous parasite that transmits East Coast Fever in Kenyan livestock?

questions.text: What is the key difference in leg count between insects, arachnids, and decapod crustaceans (like crabs)?

options.text: All three groups have exactly the same number of legs
Insects have 6 legs, arachnids have 8 legs, and crabs have 10 legs
Insects have 8 legs, arachnids have 6 legs, and crabs have 4 legs
Insects have 4 legs, arachnids have 8 legs, and crabs have 12 legs

questions.correctAnswer: Insects have 6 legs, arachnids have 8 legs, and crabs have 10 legs
questions.explanation: Insects (hexapods) have 3 pairs (6 legs); arachnids have 4 pairs (8 legs); decapod crustaceans (like crabs and prawns) have 5 pairs (10 legs).
questions.socraticHint: Count by pairs: 3 pairs (insects), 4 pairs (arachnids), 5 pairs (crabs).
questions.prompt: What is the key difference in leg count between insects, arachnids, and decapod crustaceans (like crabs)?

questions.text: Why do arthropods (insects, crabs, spiders) periodically undergo moulting (ecdysis) during their growth stages?

options.text: To lay eggs on the discarded shell
Because they want to transform into vertebrates
Their rigid chitinous exoskeleton cannot expand, so they must shed it to grow larger
They shed skin solely to change color for camouflage

questions.correctAnswer: Their rigid chitinous exoskeleton cannot expand, so they must shed it to grow larger
questions.explanation: The exoskeleton is a rigid external casing that does not grow. In order to increase in size, arthropods must periodically moult (shed the old exoskeleton) and expand while the new cuticle is soft.
questions.socraticHint: Can a hard, rigid external suit of armour stretch as an animal grows inside it?
questions.prompt: Why do arthropods (insects, crabs, spiders) periodically undergo moulting (ecdysis) during their growth stages?

questions.text: Which group of organisms consists entirely of invertebrates belonging to the phylum Mollusca?
questions.explanation: Snails, slugs, octopuses, and squids are all molluscs, characterized by unsegmented soft bodies, often with a shell or internal vestige, and a mantle cavity.
questions.socraticHint: Which list contains only soft-bodied creatures with a mantle, muscular foot, or tentacles?
questions.prompt: Which group of organisms consists entirely of invertebrates belonging to the phylum Mollusca?

questions.text:
Use the simple dichotomous key below to identify the animal described:
1a. Has backbone ................. Go to 2
1b. Has no backbone ............. Go to 3
3a. Has jointed legs ............ Go to 4
3b. Has no jointed legs ......... Earthworm
4a. Has 6 legs .................. Animal X
4b. Has 8 legs .................. Spider
What is Animal X?
questions.explanation: Following the key: 1b (no backbone) -> 3a (jointed legs) -> 4a (has 6 legs) points definitively to an insect such as the honeybee.
questions.socraticHint: Follow the steps in the key: No backbone -> Jointed legs -> 6 legs. Which organism has 6 legs?
questions.prompt:
Use the simple dichotomous key below to identify the animal described:
1a. Has backbone ................. Go to 2
1b. Has no backbone ............. Go to 3
3a. Has jointed legs ............ Go to 4
3b. Has no jointed legs ......... Earthworm
4a. Has 6 legs .................. Animal X
4b. Has 8 legs .................. Spider
What is Animal X?

questions.text: What are the green, leaf-like outer structures of a flower that enclose and protect the delicate petals in the bud stage?
questions.explanation: Sepals are the outermost green floral parts forming the calyx, which protect the reproductive organs and petals while the flower is still an unopened bud.
questions.socraticHint: What green structures cover a rose bud before it opens?
questions.prompt: What are the green, leaf-like outer structures of a flower that enclose and protect the delicate petals in the bud stage?

questions.text: Which part of the male stamen produces and releases pollen grains?
questions.explanation: The anther is the pollen-bearing sac at the tip of the stamen where male microspores (pollen grains) are produced and matured.
questions.socraticHint: Which part of the stamen sits atop the filament and holds yellow powdery pollen?
questions.prompt: Which part of the male stamen produces and releases pollen grains?

questions.text: What is the sticky surface at the top of the female pistil that catches and traps pollen grains during pollination?
questions.explanation: The stigma is the receptive surface of the pistil (carpel), typically sticky or feathery, specialized for capturing pollen grains.
questions.socraticHint: Which sticky female flower part receives pollen during pollination?
questions.prompt: What is the sticky surface at the top of the female pistil that catches and traps pollen grains during pollination?

questions.text: What biological process takes place when pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma of a flower?
questions.explanation: Pollination is the mechanical transfer of pollen grains from the male anther to the receptive female stigma.
questions.socraticHint: What is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma called?
questions.prompt: What biological process takes place when pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma of a flower?

questions.text: Which set of characteristics is typical of wind-pollinated flowers, such as maize and savannah grasses?

options.text: Bright yellow petals with large sticky thorns
Dull greenish petals, no scent or nectar, long feathery stigmas, light powdery pollen
Bright red petals, sweet nectar, strong scent, heavy sticky pollen
Large scented petals opening only at night with lots of honey

questions.correctAnswer: Dull greenish petals, no scent or nectar, long feathery stigmas, light powdery pollen
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers do not need to attract animals; they produce copious lightweight pollen and exposed feathery stigmas to catch airborne grains.
questions.socraticHint: Do maize tassels and grasses need bright petals and sweet nectar if the wind carries their pollen?
questions.prompt: Which set of characteristics is typical of wind-pollinated flowers, such as maize and savannah grasses?

questions.text: What is the primary difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination?

options.text: Self-pollination occurs only in conifers, while cross-pollination occurs only in algae
There is no difference; both produce identical clones
Self-pollination occurs within the same flower/plant, while cross-pollination transfers pollen between different plants of the same species
Self-pollination requires animals, while cross-pollination requires water only

questions.correctAnswer: Self-pollination occurs within the same flower/plant, while cross-pollination transfers pollen between different plants of the same species
questions.explanation: Self-pollination transfers pollen to a stigma of the same flower or plant. Cross-pollination transfers pollen between genetically distinct individuals of the same species, enhancing genetic diversity.
questions.socraticHint: Does "cross" pollination involve crossing over to a different plant of the same kind?
questions.prompt: What is the primary difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination?

questions.text: What happens immediately after a compatible pollen grain lands on a receptive stigma of a flower?

options.text: The flower immediately drops all of its roots
The petals turn into green leaves instantly
The stigma explodes into small seeds
A pollen tube germinates and grows down through the style into the ovary

questions.correctAnswer: A pollen tube germinates and grows down through the style into the ovary
questions.explanation: Upon landing, the pollen grain absorbs moisture and germinates a pollen tube that grows down through the style to deliver the male gametes to the ovules inside the ovary.
questions.socraticHint: How does the male genetic material travel from the sticky stigma down into the ovary?
questions.prompt: What happens immediately after a compatible pollen grain lands on a receptive stigma of a flower?

questions.text: Following successful fertilization in a flowering plant, what do the ovary and the ovules develop into?

options.text: The ovary becomes the fruit, and the ovules become the seeds
The ovary becomes the stem, and the ovules become the leaves
The ovary becomes the petals, and the ovules become sepals
The ovary becomes roots, and the ovules become flowers

questions.correctAnswer: The ovary becomes the fruit, and the ovules become the seeds
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the ovary wall ripens and swells into the fruit (pericarp), while the fertilized ovules develop into seeds containing the embryo.
questions.socraticHint: In a ripe avocado or mango, which part was the ovary and which part was the ovule?
questions.prompt: Following successful fertilization in a flowering plant, what do the ovary and the ovules develop into?

questions.text: Which floral adaptation directly encourages nocturnal animal pollinators, such as bats and moths, to visit certain night-blooming plants in Kenya?

options.text: Small odorless petals that produce no nectar
Pale white petals that reflect moonlight and strong nocturnal fragrance
Bright red petals that blend into the darkness
Feathery green stigmas that close at sunset

questions.correctAnswer: Pale white petals that reflect moonlight and strong nocturnal fragrance
questions.explanation: Flowers pollinated by nocturnal moths and bats are typically white or pale to stand out in the dark and emit strong sweet perfumes at night to guide pollinators by scent.
questions.socraticHint: What color is most visible under moonlight, and how can night pollinators find flowers in the dark?
questions.prompt: Which floral adaptation directly encourages nocturnal animal pollinators, such as bats and moths, to visit certain night-blooming plants in Kenya?

questions.text: What are the two components of the female pistil (carpel) that a pollen tube must penetrate before reaching the ovule?
questions.explanation: The pollen tube germinates on the stigma and burrows downwards through the tissue of the style to enter the ovary chamber where ovules reside.
questions.socraticHint: The tube starts at the top of the pistil and travels through its neck. Name those two parts.
questions.prompt: What are the two components of the female pistil (carpel) that a pollen tube must penetrate before reaching the ovule?

questions.text: A farmer in Makueni notices that bean yields increase significantly when European honeybee (Apis mellifera) hives are placed next to the crop field. Why does this happen?

options.text: Honeybees scare away birds and insects by buzzing
Honeybees spray honey directly onto the bean roots
Honeybees provide shade that cools the bean flowers
Honeybees transfer pollen efficiently from flower to flower, increasing fertilization rates

questions.correctAnswer: Honeybees transfer pollen efficiently from flower to flower, increasing fertilization rates
questions.explanation: Honeybees are highly active insect pollinators; their foraging transfers pollen between blooms, substantially boosting fertilization and pod set.
questions.socraticHint: What vital service do bees provide to flowers as they forage for nectar?
questions.prompt: A farmer in Makueni notices that bean yields increase significantly when European honeybee (Apis mellifera) hives are placed next to the crop field. Why does this happen?

questions.text: Examine the floral formula: Flower X has long versatile anthers hanging loosely on slender filaments outside the petals, and large feathery stigmas. What is Flower X's mode of pollination?
questions.explanation: Hanging versatile anthers and feathery exposed stigmas are classic adaptations for wind pollination, allowing gentle breezes to shake pollen free and feathery nets to catch floating grains.
questions.socraticHint: Why would anthers hang outside the flower and stigmas look like feathers if not to catch wind?
questions.prompt: Examine the floral formula: Flower X has long versatile anthers hanging loosely on slender filaments outside the petals, and large feathery stigmas. What is Flower X's mode of pollination?

questions.text: What is the main biological advantage of fruit and seed dispersal for flowering plants?

options.text: It kills all competing insects in the soil
It prevents overcrowding and reduces competition for light, water, and soil minerals
It ensures all seeds fall directly under the parent tree trunk
It stops seeds from ever germinating

questions.correctAnswer: It prevents overcrowding and reduces competition for light, water, and soil minerals
questions.explanation: Dispersal scatters offspring away from parent plants, reducing intraspecific competition for vital resources like water, light, and nutrients.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to young seedlings if hundreds of them sprout directly beneath a parent tree?
questions.prompt: What is the main biological advantage of fruit and seed dispersal for flowering plants?

questions.text: Black jack (Bidens pilosa) seeds stick tenaciously to animal fur and socks. What is their primary agent of dispersal?
questions.explanation: Black jack seeds possess sharp barbed hooks (awns) designed specifically to latch onto animal fur and human clothing, carrying them far away.
questions.socraticHint: How does black jack travel when its barbed seeds latch onto your socks or a dog's fur?
questions.prompt: Black jack (Bidens pilosa) seeds stick tenaciously to animal fur and socks. What is their primary agent of dispersal?

questions.text: Which adaptive feature enables coconut fruits to be dispersed across coastal waters and ocean currents?

options.text: Tiny parachute hairs that catch breeze
Sharp hooks that cling to fish fins
Exploding loudly when submerged in water
A fibrous, buoyant, water-resistant husk that traps air

questions.correctAnswer: A fibrous, buoyant, water-resistant husk that traps air
questions.explanation: Coconuts possess a thick, fibrous, waterproof mesocarp that contains trapped air pockets, allowing the fruit to float high in seawater for months.
questions.socraticHint: Why can a coconut float on ocean water without sinking or rotting?
questions.prompt: Which adaptive feature enables coconut fruits to be dispersed across coastal waters and ocean currents?

questions.text: Bean pods and pea pods split suddenly when dry, flinging seeds away from the plant. What dispersal mechanism is this?
questions.explanation: In explosive dispersal, drying bean or pea carpels contract unevenly until mechanical tension suddenly causes the pod to twist and burst, hurling seeds.
questions.socraticHint: When dry bean pods burst open in hot sunshine, what mechanism is that called?
questions.prompt: Bean pods and pea pods split suddenly when dry, flinging seeds away from the plant. What dispersal mechanism is this?

questions.text: Which adaptation is characteristic of wind-dispersed seeds such as dandelion, sonchus, and cotton?

options.text: Sharp hooked barbs that stick to fur
Silky tufts of hairs (parachutes) that increase air resistance
Heavy calcium shells that sink in mud

questions.correctAnswer: Silky tufts of hairs (parachutes) that increase air resistance
questions.explanation: Seeds dispersed by wind often possess fine, silky parachute hairs (pappus) or papery wings that reduce falling speed and allow air currents to carry them far.
questions.socraticHint: What structure acts like a parachute to keep dandelion seeds floating in the breeze?
questions.prompt: Which adaptation is characteristic of wind-dispersed seeds such as dandelion, sonchus, and cotton?

questions.text: A vervet monkey in the Aberdares eats ripe wild figs and drops seeds in its feces kilometres away. What dispersal mechanism is this?
questions.explanation: Animals consume sweet fleshy fruits; the hard indigestible seeds pass intact through the alimentary tract and are deposited far away in nutrient-rich dung.
questions.socraticHint: When an animal eats sweet fruit and passes the seeds unharmed in droppings, how were they dispersed?
questions.prompt: A vervet monkey in the Aberdares eats ripe wild figs and drops seeds in its feces kilometres away. What dispersal mechanism is this?

questions.text: Jacaranda and Nandi flame trees produce seeds with thin papery wing-like extensions. How are these seeds dispersed?
questions.explanation: Winged seeds spin and glide like helicopters in wind currents, drifting considerable distances away from the canopy of the parent tree.
questions.socraticHint: What natural agent catches flat, papery winged seeds as they fall from high branches?
questions.prompt: Jacaranda and Nandi flame trees produce seeds with thin papery wing-like extensions. How are these seeds dispersed?

questions.text: Which of the following plants uses explosive mechanism to disperse its seeds?
questions.explanation: Castor oil (mbono) capsules dry out under the sun until the three-lobed fruit explosively bursts, popping seeds out forcefully.
questions.socraticHint: Which plant produces spiky capsules that pop open explosively when dry?
questions.prompt: Which of the following plants uses explosive mechanism to disperse its seeds?

questions.text: Why do seeds dispersed by animals internally (like guava, tomato, and passion fruit) have tough, impermeable seed coats?

options.text: To prevent the seed from ever absorbing water
To prevent digestive stomach acids and enzymes from destroying the plant embryo
To make them float easily in air currents
To allow them to explode inside the animal's stomach

questions.correctAnswer: To prevent digestive stomach acids and enzymes from destroying the plant embryo
questions.explanation: Tough testas (seed coats) resist mechanical chewing and gastric acid digestion, allowing the viable embryo to pass unharmed into the soil.
questions.socraticHint: How does a seed survive the harsh acidic digestive juices of an animal's gut?
questions.prompt: Why do seeds dispersed by animals internally (like guava, tomato, and passion fruit) have tough, impermeable seed coats?

questions.text:
A student collected 4 different seeds around a school shamba in Kitale:
Seed 1: Has hooks
Seed 2: Has parachute hairs
Seed 3: Sits inside a pod that twisted open
Seed 4: Has a fibrous air-filled husk
Identify the agents of dispersal in order (1, 2, 3, 4):
questions.explanation: Hooks = Animal; Parachute hairs = Wind; Twisted open pod = Explosive mechanism; Fibrous air-filled husk = Water.
questions.socraticHint: Match each feature: hooks -> animals; parachute -> wind; twisted pod -> explosive; fibrous husk -> water.
questions.prompt:
A student collected 4 different seeds around a school shamba in Kitale:
