questions.prompt: What did David do when Prophet Nathan exposed his grave sin regarding Bathsheba and Uriah (2 Samuel 12:13)?

questions.text: In 1 Kings 3:5, God appeared to young King Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and said: "Ask for whatever you want me to give you." What was Solomon’s request?

options.text: A discerning heart (wisdom) to govern God’s great people and distinguish between right and wrong
Long life and great personal wealth
The death and destruction of all his political enemies
A palace covered in diamonds and rubies

questions.correctAnswer: A discerning heart (wisdom) to govern God’s great people and distinguish between right and wrong
questions.explanation: Solomon recognized his youth and inexperience ("I am only a little child and do not know how to carry out my duties") and asked for wisdom to serve God’s people justly.
questions.socraticHint: Did Solomon ask for money and power, or for wisdom to govern God’s people fairly?
questions.prompt: In 1 Kings 3:5, God appeared to young King Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and said: "Ask for whatever you want me to give you." What was Solomon’s request?

questions.text: Why was God pleased with Solomon’s prayer for wisdom at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:11-13)?

options.text: Because Solomon offered to build God a palace in Egypt
Because he asked for discernment to administer justice rather than selfish riches, long life, or vengeance
Because Solomon asked for the shortest prayer possible
Because Solomon promised to sacrifice 10,000 sheep every day

questions.correctAnswer: Because he asked for discernment to administer justice rather than selfish riches, long life, or vengeance
questions.explanation: God was delighted by Solomon’s selfless priority for justice and the welfare of the people; God granted him wisdom, plus wealth and honor.
questions.socraticHint: Why does God reward leaders who put the needs and justice of the people ahead of personal greed?
questions.prompt: Why was God pleased with Solomon’s prayer for wisdom at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:11-13)?

questions.text: How did King Solomon settle the dispute between two mothers claiming the same surviving baby (1 Kings 3:16-28)?

options.text: He flipped a coin to decide who kept the child
He banished both women from Jerusalem
He ordered the baby to be cut in two with a sword, knowing the true mother would rather give her child away than see him killed
He gave the baby to the oldest woman

questions.correctAnswer: He ordered the baby to be cut in two with a sword, knowing the true mother would rather give her child away than see him killed
questions.explanation: Solomon’s wise test exposed genuine maternal love: the real mother pleaded for the child’s life to be spared, proving her true identity.
questions.socraticHint: How did Solomon reveal the real mother by threatening to divide the infant in two?
questions.prompt: How did King Solomon settle the dispute between two mothers claiming the same surviving baby (1 Kings 3:16-28)?

questions.text: What tragic moral failure led to Solomon’s spiritual decline later in his reign (1 Kings 11:1-4)?

options.text: He gave away the Ark of the Covenant to foreign traders
He forgot how to read the Hebrew language
He married many foreign wives who turned his heart away after other idols and pagan gods

questions.correctAnswer: He married many foreign wives who turned his heart away after other idols and pagan gods
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11 records that in his old age, Solomon compromised his devotion, building pagan altars for foreign deities and failing to remain wholehearted toward God.
questions.socraticHint: What compromise caused King Solomon’s heart to turn away from God in his later years?
questions.prompt: What tragic moral failure led to Solomon’s spiritual decline later in his reign (1 Kings 11:1-4)?

questions.text: What does Jesus Christ teach about leadership in the Kingdom of God in Mark 10:43-45?

options.text: "Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first must be slave of all"
"Leaders should boss around other people and make them work"
"Leaders should take all the best food and clothes for themselves"
"Leadership is only for the strongest fighters"

questions.correctAnswer: "Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first must be slave of all"
questions.explanation: Jesus completely overturned worldly concepts of autocratic power, defining true greatness as humble, sacrificial servanthood.
questions.socraticHint: How does Jesus define greatness in leadership in the Gospel of Mark?
questions.prompt: What does Jesus Christ teach about leadership in the Kingdom of God in Mark 10:43-45?

questions.text: How should a Grade 6 class prefect behave toward a student who has made a minor disciplinary mistake?

options.text: Mock them publicly during school assembly
Gently and firmly correct them with kindness, explaining the rule and helping them improve
Scream at them and beat them in front of the whole school
Demand bribes or lunch snacks so as not to report them

questions.correctAnswer: Gently and firmly correct them with kindness, explaining the rule and helping them improve
questions.explanation: Christian servant leaders correct others with restorative kindness, patience, and fairness, emulating the shepherd heart of Christ.
questions.socraticHint: Should a good student leader humiliate a classmate or guide them kindly and firmly?
questions.prompt: How should a Grade 6 class prefect behave toward a student who has made a minor disciplinary mistake?

questions.text: Why is David described in Acts 13:22 as "a man after God’s own heart"?

options.text: Because he was the tallest warrior in Israel
Because he was the wealthiest king in human history
Because he possessed a willing, humble heart that sought to do all of God’s will and repented when he fell
Because he never made a single mistake in his life

questions.correctAnswer: Because he possessed a willing, humble heart that sought to do all of God’s will and repented when he fell
questions.explanation: David was not sinless, but his heart was genuinely devoted to God, passionate for worship, quick to repent, and committed to obeying God’s purposes.
questions.socraticHint: Why did God cherish David’s heart despite David’s human flaws?
questions.prompt: Why is David described in Acts 13:22 as "a man after God’s own heart"?

questions.text: How did King David demonstrate covenant loyalty and kindness to Jonathan’s crippled son Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9)?

options.text: He banished Mephibosheth to a distant foreign land
He forced Mephibosheth to become a servant in the stables
He invited Mephibosheth to eat at the king’s royal table continually and restored all his family’s lands

questions.correctAnswer: He invited Mephibosheth to eat at the king’s royal table continually and restored all his family’s lands
questions.explanation: David honored his covenant with his beloved friend Jonathan by welcoming Mephibosheth into the royal palace with dignity, honoring persons with disabilities.
questions.socraticHint: How did David honor Jonathan’s memory by caring for Mephibosheth at his table?
questions.prompt: How did King David demonstrate covenant loyalty and kindness to Jonathan’s crippled son Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9)?

questions.text: What is the core difference between worldly leadership and biblical servant leadership?

options.text: Worldly leadership seeks power, personal privilege, and dominance; servant leadership seeks humble service, justice, and uplifting others
Worldly leadership is always honest, while servant leadership is secretive
There is no difference between the two styles
Servant leaders never make any decisions for their followers

questions.correctAnswer: Worldly leadership seeks power, personal privilege, and dominance; servant leadership seeks humble service, justice, and uplifting others
questions.explanation: Worldly power focuses on self-exaltation and controlling others; biblical servant leadership focuses on sacrificially serving the community and honoring God.
questions.socraticHint: Does biblical servant leadership focus on serving others or lording power over them?
questions.prompt: What is the core difference between worldly leadership and biblical servant leadership?

questions.text: What does Jesus promise to the "poor in spirit" in the first Beatitude (Matthew 5:3)?

options.text: "For theirs is the kingdom of heaven"
"They will inherit great bags of silver"
"They will be elected as kings on earth"

questions.correctAnswer: "For theirs is the kingdom of heaven"
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:3 declares: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven," promising divine inheritance to those who recognize their total dependence on God.
questions.socraticHint: Which heavenly reward is promised to those who acknowledge their spiritual need before God?
questions.prompt: What does Jesus promise to the "poor in spirit" in the first Beatitude (Matthew 5:3)?

questions.text: What divine comfort is promised to those who mourn in Matthew 5:4?

options.text: "For they will live without sadness forever on earth"

questions.explanation: Jesus promises: "Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted," assuring believers that God brings deep solace to those brokenhearted over sin or loss.
questions.socraticHint: What assurance does God give to those who experience sorrow and grief?
questions.prompt: What divine comfort is promised to those who mourn in Matthew 5:4?

questions.text: What does biblical "meekness" mean according to the Beatitude "Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth" (Matthew 5:5)?

options.text: Cowardice and being too weak to stand up
Refusing to speak to anyone in school
Allowing others to steal your belongings without caring
Gentle strength and power placed under God’s humble control, without aggressive arrogance

questions.correctAnswer: Gentle strength and power placed under God’s humble control, without aggressive arrogance
questions.explanation: Biblical meekness is not weakness; it is disciplined strength, humility, and self-restraint channeled for God’s righteous purposes.
questions.socraticHint: Is meekness weakness, or is it power and strength harnessed under divine self-control?
questions.prompt: What does biblical "meekness" mean according to the Beatitude "Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth" (Matthew 5:5)?

questions.text: What divine promise is given to those who "hunger and thirst for righteousness" (Matthew 5:6)?

options.text: "For they will never need to drink water again"
"For they will own vast banqueting halls"

questions.explanation: Matthew 5:6 promises that those who long deeply for God’s righteousness and justice will be completely filled with spiritual satisfaction.
questions.socraticHint: What does God promise will happen to those who earnestly desire His righteousness?
questions.prompt: What divine promise is given to those who "hunger and thirst for righteousness" (Matthew 5:6)?

questions.text: Why does Jesus state: "Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy" (Matthew 5:7)?

options.text: Because mercy is only necessary during wartime
Because those who forgive and show compassion reflect God’s character and will receive divine mercy themselves
Because only weak people show mercy to others
Because mercy makes wrongdoers pay double fines

questions.correctAnswer: Because those who forgive and show compassion reflect God’s character and will receive divine mercy themselves
questions.explanation: Showing mercy to others opens our hearts to experience the limitless mercy and grace of God; an unmerciful heart cannot receive mercy.
questions.socraticHint: How does extending mercy to others connect with receiving God’s mercy?
questions.prompt: Why does Jesus state: "Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy" (Matthew 5:7)?

questions.text: What remarkable blessing is promised to the "pure in heart" in Matthew 5:8?

options.text: "For they will understand all human languages"

questions.explanation: Matthew 5:8 promises: "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God." A heart cleansed of deceit, hypocrisy, and malice enters intimate communion with God.
questions.socraticHint: Which supreme spiritual privilege is promised to those with pure, unhypocritical hearts?
questions.prompt: What remarkable blessing is promised to the "pure in heart" in Matthew 5:8?

questions.text: What honorable family title is given to peacemakers in Matthew 5:9?

options.text: "For they will be called judges of the earth"
"For they will be named generals of the army"
"For they will be called masters of philosophy"
"For they will be called children of God"

questions.correctAnswer: "For they will be called children of God"
questions.explanation: Peacemakers reflect the nature of the God of peace (Romans 15:33); therefore, they are honored with the title of "children of God."
questions.socraticHint: Whose children are peacemakers called because they reflect the Father’s reconciling love?
questions.prompt: What honorable family title is given to peacemakers in Matthew 5:9?

questions.text: How should Christian pupils respond when mocked or persecuted because of standing up for what is right (Matthew 5:11-12)?

options.text: Rejoice and be glad, because great is their reward in heaven, just as the prophets before them were persecuted
Seek immediate physical revenge after school hours
Deny their faith and join the persecutors in doing evil
Complain bitterly that God has abandoned them

questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice and be glad, because great is their reward in heaven, just as the prophets before them were persecuted
questions.explanation: Jesus encourages persecuted believers to hold fast with joyful confidence, knowing that suffering for righteousness shares in the noble heritage of God’s prophets.
questions.socraticHint: Why does Jesus tell us to rejoice and be glad even when mocked for doing what is right?
questions.prompt: How should Christian pupils respond when mocked or persecuted because of standing up for what is right (Matthew 5:11-12)?

questions.text: What is the crucial difference between a "peacekeeper" who avoids difficult conflicts and a biblical "peacemaker"?

options.text: A peacemaker only cares about personal safety
A peacemaker actively confronts injustice and works to restore genuine reconciliation and truth, whereas a mere peacekeeper sweeps problems under the carpet
A peacemaker uses military force to stop fights
There is no difference between the two terms

questions.correctAnswer: A peacemaker actively confronts injustice and works to restore genuine reconciliation and truth, whereas a mere peacekeeper sweeps problems under the carpet
questions.explanation: True peacemaking requires actively resolving roots of conflict through truth, justice, and forgiveness, not just maintaining superficial calm.
questions.socraticHint: Does real peacemaking involve actively restoring broken relationships through truth and justice?
questions.prompt: What is the crucial difference between a "peacekeeper" who avoids difficult conflicts and a biblical "peacemaker"?

questions.text: How does a Grade 6 learner practically practice being "merciful" in school when a classmate accidentally breaks their ruler?

options.text: Refusing to speak to the classmate for the rest of the term
Forgiving the classmate readily, refusing to harbor grudges or demand harsh punishment
Breaking the classmate’s ruler in return to be even

questions.correctAnswer: Forgiving the classmate readily, refusing to harbor grudges or demand harsh punishment
questions.explanation: Practicing mercy means choosing gracious forgiveness over retaliation and petty anger when mistakes occur.
questions.socraticHint: How does choosing forgiveness over revenge show mercy in the classroom?
questions.prompt: How does a Grade 6 learner practically practice being "merciful" in school when a classmate accidentally breaks their ruler?

questions.text: Why does Jesus describe the Beatitudes at the beginning of the Sermon on the Mount before giving specific moral instructions?

options.text: Because the crowd was too tired to listen to long rules
Because the Beatitudes are only meant for the twelve apostles
Because rules do not matter in the Kingdom of God
Because outward righteous actions must flow from a transformed inner heart and character

questions.correctAnswer: Because outward righteous actions must flow from a transformed inner heart and character
questions.explanation: The Beatitudes describe the inner heart dispositions of Kingdom citizens; genuine Christian behavior naturally flows from who we are on the inside.
questions.socraticHint: Why must our inner heart and motives be changed first before our outward actions can be truly good?
questions.prompt: Why does Jesus describe the Beatitudes at the beginning of the Sermon on the Mount before giving specific moral instructions?

questions.text: What does "purity of heart" mean for young Christians in an era of constant social media bombardment?

options.text: Keeping our inner desires, thoughts, and intentions focused on God and untainted by lust, dishonesty, or malice
Washing our hands with soap ten times every hour
Only reading books that have white covers
Never having any conversation with anyone outside school

questions.correctAnswer: Keeping our inner desires, thoughts, and intentions focused on God and untainted by lust, dishonesty, or malice
questions.explanation: Purity of heart is single-minded devotion to God, guarding our secret thoughts and desires against corrupt, vulgar, or malicious influences.
questions.socraticHint: How does guarding our inner thoughts and intentions keep our hearts pure before God?
questions.prompt: What does "purity of heart" mean for young Christians in an era of constant social media bombardment?

questions.text: In Matthew 5:13, what warning does Jesus give if salt loses its saltiness (savor)?

options.text: "It should be sold to merchants at double price"
"It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot"
"It can be boiled to regain its flavor"

questions.correctAnswer: "It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot"
questions.explanation: Jesus warned that tasteless salt has lost its distinct preservative purpose; similarly, a Christian who compromises and conforms to worldly corruption loses moral influence.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to salt that has lost its flavor and preservative power?
questions.prompt: In Matthew 5:13, what warning does Jesus give if salt loses its saltiness (savor)?

questions.text: In Matthew 5:14-16, where did Jesus say a person places a lighted lamp in a house?

options.text: Locked inside a deep cellar cupboard
On a stand, where it gives light to everyone in the house, not under a bowl (basket)
Under a heavy wooden bowl where nobody can see it

questions.correctAnswer: On a stand, where it gives light to everyone in the house, not under a bowl (basket)
questions.explanation: Jesus taught: "Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house."
questions.socraticHint: Where do people place a lamp so that its light illuminates the whole room?
questions.prompt: In Matthew 5:14-16, where did Jesus say a person places a lighted lamp in a house?

questions.text: What is the ultimate purpose of letting our light shine before others through good deeds (Matthew 5:16)?

options.text: So that everyone will praise and elect us as politicians
So that we can boast about how righteous we are
To earn money and gold prizes from spectators
So that people may see our good deeds and glorify our Father in heaven

questions.correctAnswer: So that people may see our good deeds and glorify our Father in heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:16 says: "Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven." Good deeds point people to God, not our own egos.
questions.socraticHint: Who should receive glory and praise when people see our Christian good deeds?
questions.prompt: What is the ultimate purpose of letting our light shine before others through good deeds (Matthew 5:16)?

questions.text: What revolutionary standard of love did Jesus command regarding enemies in Matthew 5:44?

options.text: "Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you"
"Hate your enemies and plot revenge in secret"
"Pretend to like your enemies while smiling falsely"
"Attack your enemies before they have a chance to strike"

questions.correctAnswer: "Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you"
questions.explanation: Jesus replaced the ancient code of retaliation ("an eye for an eye") with divine radical love: actively loving, blessing, and praying for our enemies.
questions.socraticHint: What surprising command did Jesus give regarding how we should treat our enemies and persecutors?
questions.prompt: What revolutionary standard of love did Jesus command regarding enemies in Matthew 5:44?

questions.text: Why does Jesus point to the sun and rain to explain why we should love our enemies (Matthew 5:45)?

options.text: Because crops cannot grow without heavy storms
Because God causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous
Because the sun only shines when people are obedient
Because rain is a punishment for wicked people

questions.correctAnswer: Because God causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous
questions.explanation: God extends common grace and providential blessings to all human beings without partiality; Christians emulate this universal divine benevolence.
questions.socraticHint: How does God’s gift of sunshine and rain to both good and bad people model universal love?
questions.prompt: Why does Jesus point to the sun and rain to explain why we should love our enemies (Matthew 5:45)?

questions.text: In Matthew 6:1-4, what warning does Jesus give about giving to the needy (charity)?

options.text: Only give money to people who promise to vote for you
Never give anything to anyone under any circumstances
Do not give to be seen by others and do not blow a trumpet, but give in secret so your Father who sees in secret will reward you
Always invite photographers when helping poor people so everyone knows

questions.correctAnswer: Do not give to be seen by others and do not blow a trumpet, but give in secret so your Father who sees in secret will reward you
questions.explanation: Jesus condemns hypocritical giving designed for human admiration: "Do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that your giving may be in secret."
questions.socraticHint: Should acts of charitable giving be done secretly for God or loudly for public attention?
questions.prompt: In Matthew 6:1-4, what warning does Jesus give about giving to the needy (charity)?

questions.text: What instructions did Jesus give regarding prayer in Matthew 6:5-6?

options.text: Shout loudly with megaphones so everyone knows you are praying
Repeat the same empty words for hours without thinking
Only pray when standing on high hilltops
Go into your inner room, close the door and pray to your Father in secret, rather than standing on street corners to be seen by people

questions.correctAnswer: Go into your inner room, close the door and pray to your Father in secret, rather than standing on street corners to be seen by people
questions.explanation: Authentic prayer is personal, intimate communion with our heavenly Father, avoiding theatrical performances designed to impress onlookers.
questions.socraticHint: Where did Jesus teach us to go for private, intimate prayer with our heavenly Father?
questions.prompt: What instructions did Jesus give regarding prayer in Matthew 6:5-6?

questions.text: Why does Jesus caution against hoarding treasures on earth in Matthew 6:19-20?

options.text: Because on earth moths and rust destroy and thieves break in and steal, while heavenly treasures are secure forever
Because money weighs down school bags
Because banks did not exist in biblical times
Because gold is dangerous to touch

questions.correctAnswer: Because on earth moths and rust destroy and thieves break in and steal, while heavenly treasures are secure forever
questions.explanation: Earthly wealth is perishable, insecure, and temporary. Heavenly treasures (faith, love, generosity, service) have eternal, incorruptible value.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to material worldly wealth compared to eternal treasures stored in heaven?
questions.prompt: Why does Jesus caution against hoarding treasures on earth in Matthew 6:19-20?

questions.text: What profound truth does Matthew 6:21 declare about where a person’s heart is focused?

options.text: "A wise heart thinks only about silver and gold"
"For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also"
"Your heart is located on the left side of your chest"

questions.correctAnswer: "For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also"
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:21 reveals that our desires, passions, and loyalties inevitably follow whatever we value most in life.
questions.socraticHint: Where does your heart inevitably stay according to Matthew 6:21?
questions.prompt: What profound truth does Matthew 6:21 declare about where a person’s heart is focused?

questions.text: In Matthew 6:24, why did Jesus declare that "no one can serve two masters"?

options.text: Because human brains cannot remember two names
Because masters are always enemies with each other
Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money
Because employees are only allowed to have one job contract

questions.correctAnswer: Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money
questions.explanation: Spiritual loyalty cannot be divided: worshiping wealth and possessions crowds out wholehearted devotion and obedience to God.
questions.socraticHint: Which two competing masters did Jesus say cannot be served at the same time?
questions.prompt: In Matthew 6:24, why did Jesus declare that "no one can serve two masters"?

questions.text: What prescription against anxiety over food and clothing did Jesus give in Matthew 6:33?

options.text: "Never eat breakfast or wear warm clothes"
"But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well"

questions.correctAnswer: "But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well"
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:33 establishes the golden priority of Christian living: making God’s Kingdom and righteousness our first pursuit, trusting God for daily provision.
questions.socraticHint: What should we seek first above all worries according to Matthew 6:33?
questions.prompt: What prescription against anxiety over food and clothing did Jesus give in Matthew 6:33?

questions.text: How does Jesus illustrate judging others versus examining oneself in Matthew 7:3-5?

options.text: Why look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?
Why carry a stick when you have a spear?
Why walk on a road when you can ride a chariot?
Why look at a tree when you can see a forest?

questions.correctAnswer: Why look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?
questions.explanation: Jesus humorously yet piercingly warns against hypocritical judgment, commanding believers to remove the giant log of sin from their own eyes before correcting others.
questions.socraticHint: What vivid picture of a speck of sawdust versus a wooden plank did Jesus use to teach about hypocritical judgment?
questions.prompt: How does Jesus illustrate judging others versus examining oneself in Matthew 7:3-5?

questions.text: When Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive a brother who sins against him (Matthew 18:21), what was Jesus’s answer?

options.text: Ten times, then report him to the elders
Not seven times, but seventy-seven times (limitless forgiveness)
Only once, then cut all ties
Three times, then retaliate with force

questions.correctAnswer: Not seven times, but seventy-seven times (limitless forgiveness)
questions.explanation: Jesus answered: "I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times," signifying that forgiveness in God’s Kingdom must be boundless and continuous without keeping score.
questions.socraticHint: Did Jesus limit forgiveness to 7 times, or did He say seventy-seven times to show it must be limitless?
questions.prompt: When Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive a brother who sins against him (Matthew 18:21), what was Jesus’s answer?

questions.text: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant (Matthew 18:23-35), how large was the debt that the king graciously canceled for his servant?

options.text: Ten thousand talents (an astronomical, unpayable debt)

questions.correctAnswer: Ten thousand talents (an astronomical, unpayable debt)
questions.explanation: Ten thousand talents represented millions of dollars—billions in modern terms—symbolizing the overwhelming, unpayable debt of human sin that God wipes away.
questions.socraticHint: How huge was the debt canceled by the merciful king in the parable?
questions.prompt: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant (Matthew 18:23-35), how large was the debt that the king graciously canceled for his servant?

questions.text: What shocking action did the forgiven servant take when he encountered a fellow servant who owed him a mere 100 denarii?

options.text: He canceled the debt with joy
He gave him an extra 100 denarii to help him
He invited him to a feast at his house
He choked him, demanded immediate payment, and had him thrown into prison

questions.correctAnswer: He choked him, demanded immediate payment, and had him thrown into prison
questions.explanation: Despite having been forgiven an impossible debt, the wicked servant showed zero mercy for a tiny debt of 100 denarii, having his fellow servant jailed.
questions.socraticHint: Did the forgiven servant show mercy to his debtor, or did he violently demand payment and jail him?
questions.prompt: What shocking action did the forgiven servant take when he encountered a fellow servant who owed him a mere 100 denarii?

questions.text: What consequence befell the unforgiving servant when the king heard about his cruelty (Matthew 18:32-34)?

options.text: The king called him a wicked servant, revoked the pardon, and handed him over to the jailers to be tortured until all was paid
The king promoted him to prime minister
The king gave him a reward for strict financial discipline
The king ignored the matter entirely

questions.correctAnswer: The king called him a wicked servant, revoked the pardon, and handed him over to the jailers to be tortured until all was paid
questions.explanation: The king rebuked him: "Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?" and handed him over to punishment.
questions.socraticHint: What did the master do when he discovered that his servant had refused to show mercy to a fellow worker?
questions.prompt: What consequence befell the unforgiving servant when the king heard about his cruelty (Matthew 18:32-34)?

questions.text: What primary moral lesson does Jesus convey through the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant?

options.text: People should only forgive those who give them gifts
Since God has graciously forgiven us our immense debt of sin, we must genuinely forgive others from our hearts
Never borrow money from anyone under any circumstances
Kings should never forgive debts of their servants

questions.correctAnswer: Since God has graciously forgiven us our immense debt of sin, we must genuinely forgive others from our hearts
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:35 concludes: "This is how my heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart."
questions.socraticHint: Why must we forgive others from our hearts in light of how much God has forgiven us?
questions.prompt: What primary moral lesson does Jesus convey through the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant?

questions.text: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11-32), what did the younger son do with his share of the estate?

options.text: He built schools and hospitals for poor children
He gave it all to his older brother
He traveled to a distant country and squandered his wealth in wild, wasteful living
He invested it in fertile farmland and doubled his inheritance

questions.correctAnswer: He traveled to a distant country and squandered his wealth in wild, wasteful living
questions.explanation: The younger son demanded his inheritance prematurely, left his family, and squandered all his resources in reckless self-indulgence.
questions.socraticHint: How did the younger son waste his inheritance in a faraway country?
questions.prompt: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11-32), what did the younger son do with his share of the estate?

questions.text: To what humiliating task was the prodigal son reduced when a severe famine struck the distant country (Luke 15:15)?

options.text: Serving as a priest in a temple
Feeding pigs and longing to fill his stomach with the carob pods the pigs were eating

questions.correctAnswer: Feeding pigs and longing to fill his stomach with the carob pods the pigs were eating
questions.explanation: For a Jewish boy, feeding unclean swine and starving alongside them was the ultimate symbol of utter moral and physical rock bottom.
questions.socraticHint: Which unclean animals was the starving prodigal son hired to feed?
questions.prompt: To what humiliating task was the prodigal son reduced when a severe famine struck the distant country (Luke 15:15)?

questions.text: What happened when the prodigal son "came to his senses" (Luke 15:17-19)?

options.text: He acknowledged his sin against heaven and his father, and decided to return home to ask to be a hired servant
He decided to become a bandit to steal food
He blamed his father for giving him money too early
He gave up and chose to starve in the pigpen

questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledged his sin against heaven and his father, and decided to return home to ask to be a hired servant
questions.explanation: Repentance begins when a sinner recognizes their brokenness, admits their sin, and humbly turns back to the Father seeking mercy.
questions.socraticHint: What humble confession did the prodigal son prepare to say to his father upon his return?
questions.prompt: What happened when the prodigal son "came to his senses" (Luke 15:17-19)?

questions.text: How did the father react when he saw his prodigal son returning from a long distance away (Luke 15:20)?

options.text: He made his son sleep outside in the dirt for a month
He was filled with compassion, ran to his son, threw his arms around him, and kissed him
He locked the gate and ordered the servants to chase him away

questions.text: In Ephesians 6:1-3, what special promise is attached to the commandment to honor your parents?

options.text: "That you will never take any examinations in school"
"That it may go well with you and that you may enjoy long life on the earth"
"That you will become a millionaire before age twenty"
"That you will never have to wash dishes at home"

questions.correctAnswer: "That it may go well with you and that you may enjoy long life on the earth"
questions.explanation: Paul notes that the Fifth Commandment is "the first commandment with a promise: that it may go well with you and that you may enjoy long life on the earth."
questions.socraticHint: What double blessing of life and well-being did God promise to children who honor their parents?
questions.prompt: In Ephesians 6:1-3, what special promise is attached to the commandment to honor your parents?

questions.text: What does Ephesians 6:4 instruct Christian parents regarding how they should raise their children?

options.text: "Never speak to your children about spiritual matters"
"Give children everything they demand without discipline"
"Fathers, do not exasperate (provoke) your children; instead, bring them up in the training and instruction of the Lord"
"Fathers, leave your children to raise themselves on the streets"

questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:4 instructs parents to avoid harshness and unreasonable provocation, nurturing children patiently in godly instruction and discipline.

questions.text: How can a Grade 6 child show genuine honor and respect to their parents on a daily basis?

options.text: By arguing loudly whenever asked to do chores
By ignoring parents’ advice and running away with rebellious friends
By only talking to parents when demanding pocket money
By obeying instructions cheerfully, helping with home chores, speaking respectfully, and praying for them

questions.correctAnswer: By obeying instructions cheerfully, helping with home chores, speaking respectfully, and praying for them
questions.explanation: Honoring parents involves practical helpfulness, courteous words, loving obedience, and gratitude for their tireless sacrifices.

questions.prompt: How can a Grade 6 child show genuine honor and respect to their parents on a daily basis?

questions.text: What Christian principle from Colossians 3:13 should be applied when siblings argue over television channels or household chores?

options.text: "Bear with each other and forgive one another... Forgive as the Lord forgave you"
"Use physical force to settle who gets the item"
"Stop talking to your sibling for the rest of the year"

questions.correctAnswer: "Bear with each other and forgive one another... Forgive as the Lord forgave you"
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:13 commands mutual forbearance and quick forgiveness, resolving home disputes through love and Christ-like grace.
questions.socraticHint: How should brothers and sisters resolve minor fights based on Colossians 3:13?
questions.prompt: What Christian principle from Colossians 3:13 should be applied when siblings argue over television channels or household chores?

questions.text: Why are daily family devotions (reading scripture and praying together) essential for a Christian home?

options.text: They are an ancient legal punishment
They build spiritual unity, instill moral values in children, invite God’s blessing, and strengthen family bonds
They take the place of attending school during weekdays
They make family members too tired to have conversations

questions.correctAnswer: They build spiritual unity, instill moral values in children, invite God’s blessing, and strengthen family bonds
questions.explanation: Family prayer and Bible reading foster spiritual resilience, open channels of honest communication, and root children in God’s peace.
questions.socraticHint: How does praying together as a family each evening draw family members closer to God and each other?
questions.prompt: Why are daily family devotions (reading scripture and praying together) essential for a Christian home?

questions.text: In 1 Timothy 5:8, what strong warning is given to someone who fails to provide for and care for their own family members?

options.text: "They have fulfilled all requirements of the church"
"Anyone who does not provide for their relatives, and especially for their own household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever"
"They should be rewarded with a medal of independence"

questions.correctAnswer: "Anyone who does not provide for their relatives, and especially for their own household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever"
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 5:8 underscores that neglecting the care and support of one’s family is a grave moral failure that denies Christian faith.
questions.socraticHint: What does scripture say about a person who refuses to care for the needs of their own family?
questions.prompt: In 1 Timothy 5:8, what strong warning is given to someone who fails to provide for and care for their own family members?

questions.text: What should children do when their parents or guardians face difficult financial hardships and cannot afford luxury items?

options.text: Throw temper tantrums and refuse to eat food
Express empathy, show contentment with what is available, assist at home, and pray for God’s provision

questions.correctAnswer: Express empathy, show contentment with what is available, assist at home, and pray for God’s provision
questions.explanation: Christian maturity is demonstrated when children appreciate their parents’ sacrifices, exercise contentment, and stand with their family in hard times.
questions.socraticHint: How does showing contentment and gratitude support parents when money is tight?
questions.prompt: What should children do when their parents or guardians face difficult financial hardships and cannot afford luxury items?

questions.text: How did Jesus care for His earthly mother Mary even as He hung dying on the cross (John 19:26-27)?

options.text: He entrusted Mary to the care of His beloved disciple John, saying: "Dear woman, here is your son," and to John: "Here is your mother"
He asked the Roman soldiers to arrest her
He told her to return alone to Nazareth

questions.correctAnswer: He entrusted Mary to the care of His beloved disciple John, saying: "Dear woman, here is your son," and to John: "Here is your mother"
questions.explanation: Even in His deepest physical agony, Jesus fulfilled the duty of filial love, ensuring His mother was provided for and protected by John.

questions.prompt: How did Jesus care for His earthly mother Mary even as He hung dying on the cross (John 19:26-27)?

questions.text: How does Proverbs 22:6 describe the enduring impact of godly parenting on a child’s lifelong moral journey?

options.text: "Children should be left to learn from social media alone"
"Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it"
"Children will always do the exact opposite of what parents teach"
"Only teachers in school can teach children what is right"

questions.correctAnswer: "Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it"
questions.explanation: Proverbs 22:6 highlights the foundational power of early parental training in shaping lasting character, integrity, and faith.
questions.socraticHint: What proverb promises that children trained in the right way will remember it even in old age?
questions.prompt: How does Proverbs 22:6 describe the enduring impact of godly parenting on a child’s lifelong moral journey?

questions.text: What destructive habit breaks trust and creates deep hostility between siblings in a home?

options.text: Praying for each other before bed
Tattletale lying, backbiting, stealing each other’s belongings, and jealousy
Helping each other with mathematics revision

questions.correctAnswer: Tattletale lying, backbiting, stealing each other’s belongings, and jealousy
questions.explanation: Dishonesty, theft, and jealousy breed bitterness and division among siblings, eroding the sacred bond of family trust.
questions.socraticHint: Which dishonest behaviors poison sibling relationships and destroy household harmony?
questions.prompt: What destructive habit breaks trust and creates deep hostility between siblings in a home?

questions.text: How did Ruth demonstrate extraordinary family loyalty and love toward her widowed mother-in-law Naomi (Ruth 1:16-17)?

options.text: She abandoned Naomi to marry a rich foreign merchant
She demanded Naomi’s remaining inheritance money
She complained that Naomi was a burden to her
She refused to leave her, declaring: "Where you go I will go... Your people will be my people and your God my God"

questions.correctAnswer: She refused to leave her, declaring: "Where you go I will go... Your people will be my people and your God my God"
questions.explanation: Ruth showed selfless covenant loyalty (hesed), clinging to Naomi in her grief and adopting Naomi’s people and God as her own.

questions.prompt: How did Ruth demonstrate extraordinary family loyalty and love toward her widowed mother-in-law Naomi (Ruth 1:16-17)?

questions.text: What should a student do if they feel overwhelmed by family stress or emotional anxiety at home?

options.text: Confide in a trusted school guidance counselor, chaplain, or mature Christian teacher who can offer prayer and counsel
Keep it bottled up inside and start taking illicit drugs
Run away from home and live on the streets
Post angry threats against their family on social media

questions.correctAnswer: Confide in a trusted school guidance counselor, chaplain, or mature Christian teacher who can offer prayer and counsel
questions.explanation: Seeking godly, professional guidance from trusted counselors or chaplains provides emotional support, pastoral wisdom, and healthy solutions.
questions.socraticHint: Who at school can you turn to safely for spiritual advice and counseling during hard family times?
questions.prompt: What should a student do if they feel overwhelmed by family stress or emotional anxiety at home?

questions.text: What wisdom about friendship is expressed in Proverbs 27:17?

options.text: "Having many friends is better than having wise friends"
"As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another"
"A friend should always lend you money without asking for it back"

questions.correctAnswer: "As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another"
questions.explanation: Proverbs 27:17 shows that true friends positively challenge, sharpen, and refine each other’s intellect, character, and spiritual walk.

questions.prompt: What wisdom about friendship is expressed in Proverbs 27:17?

options.text: He demanded that David bow down before him as prince
He told King Saul where David was hiding so Saul could kill him
He made a covenant with David and gave him his own royal robe, tunic, sword, bow, and belt
He tried to poison David out of jealousy for the crown

questions.correctAnswer: He made a covenant with David and gave him his own royal robe, tunic, sword, bow, and belt
questions.explanation: Jonathan gave David his royal robe and weapons, symbolically surrendering his royal rights to David in profound selfless love.

questions.text: What stern warning does 1 Corinthians 15:33 deliver about associating closely with corrupt companions?

options.text: "Bad friends will help you become stronger in your faith"
"You can do whatever your friends do without any consequences"
"Company does not affect how you think or behave"
"Do not be misled: Bad company corrupts good character"

questions.correctAnswer: "Do not be misled: Bad company corrupts good character"
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:33 emphasizes that spending continuous time with immoral, dishonest peers gradually erodes personal integrity and values.

questions.prompt: What stern warning does 1 Corinthians 15:33 deliver about associating closely with corrupt companions?

questions.text: What is negative peer pressure in a primary school setting?

options.text: Being pressured by friends or classmates to engage in harmful, illegal, or sinful behaviors against your conscience
Friends encouraging you to study hard for your examinations
Classmates inviting you to join the school choir or athletics team
Teachers giving homework assignments to the whole class

questions.correctAnswer: Being pressured by friends or classmates to engage in harmful, illegal, or sinful behaviors against your conscience
questions.explanation: Negative peer pressure coerces individuals into compromising their values (e.g. cheating, drug experimentation, vandalism) to gain social acceptance.

questions.prompt: What is negative peer pressure in a primary school setting?

questions.text: What should a Christian pupil do when friends pressure them to taste alcohol, smoke, or chew miraa (khat)?

options.text: Hide in the corner and watch them without saying anything
Firmly and boldly say: "No, I choose not to do that," and walk away to join positive companions
Try it just once to avoid being laughed at or called cowardly
Buy the drugs for the friends even if they don’t use them

questions.correctAnswer: Firmly and boldly say: "No, I choose not to do that," and walk away to join positive companions
questions.explanation: Moral courage requires clear, unambiguous refusal ("Just say No"), protecting one’s body as the temple of the Holy Spirit.
questions.socraticHint: What clear and firm response protects your health and morals when peers urge you to take drugs?
questions.prompt: What should a Christian pupil do when friends pressure them to taste alcohol, smoke, or chew miraa (khat)?

questions.text: Why does 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 state that our physical bodies must be kept pure from substance abuse and sexual immorality?

options.text: Because hospitals in Kenya are too expensive
Because sports competitions require good fitness
Because our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, bought with a price, and must be used to honor God
Because bodies do not belong to human beings at all

questions.correctAnswer: Because our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, bought with a price, and must be used to honor God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 reveals that our bodies house the Holy Spirit; abusing them through drugs, drunkenness, or immorality defiles God’s dwelling place.

questions.prompt: Why does 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 state that our physical bodies must be kept pure from substance abuse and sexual immorality?

"Like a mighty warrior in heavy armor"
"Like a diamond shining in a gold ring"
"Like a city whose walls are broken through is a person who lacks self-control"

questions.correctAnswer: "Like a city whose walls are broken through is a person who lacks self-control"

Staying awake all night drinking energy drinks without sleep
Skipping meals and refusing to speak to friends
Cheating on exams so they don’t have to study

questions.correctAnswer: Balancing study with rest, exercising regularly, praying and meditating on scripture, and talking with supportive mentors
questions.explanation: Healthy mental well-being blends spiritual peace, physical wellness (sleep, nutrition), disciplined study, and open communication with mentors.

questions.text: What biblical promise in Philippians 4:6-7 brings peace to troubled minds and hearts?

options.text: "Only rich people can have peace of mind"
"Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God... will guard your hearts"
"Worry as much as you can about tomorrow"
"Never ask God for help when you are anxious"

questions.correctAnswer: "Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God... will guard your hearts"

questions.text: What quality makes someone a "true friend in times of adversity" according to Proverbs 17:17?

options.text: Running away as soon as you get into difficulty
Telling everyone in school about your private embarrassments
Standing by you and supporting you when you face sickness, grief, or trouble, rather than abandoning you
Only visiting you when you have sweets and snacks to share

questions.correctAnswer: Standing by you and supporting you when you face sickness, grief, or trouble, rather than abandoning you
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:17 affirms: "A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity." Loyalty in trials distinguishes true friendship from fair-weather friends.

questions.prompt: What quality makes someone a "true friend in times of adversity" according to Proverbs 17:17?

questions.text: How can a Christian learner be a positive influence (positive peer pressure) on their classmates?

options.text: By forcing everyone to give them their lunch money
By boasting about how holy and righteous they are
By gossiping about teachers in secret
By inviting peers to study groups, encouraging those feeling down, demonstrating honesty, and standing up against bullying

questions.explanation: Positive peer influence leverages social relationships to inspire kindness, academic focus, moral bravery, and mutual support.

questions.text: In 2 Timothy 1:7, what three gifts does God give believers instead of a spirit of fear?

options.text: A spirit of power, of love, and of self-discipline (a sound mind)
A spirit of pride, wealth, and anger
A spirit of doubt, worry, and sadness
A spirit of silence, weakness, and retreat

questions.correctAnswer: A spirit of power, of love, and of self-discipline (a sound mind)
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:7 assures us: "For the Spirit God gave us does not make us timid, but gives us power, love and self-discipline," providing courage and emotional stability.

questions.prompt: In 2 Timothy 1:7, what three gifts does God give believers instead of a spirit of fear?

questions.text: What powerful imagery did Prophet Amos use in Amos 5:24 to describe God’s standard of social justice?

options.text: "Let justice be bought and sold in the marketplace"
"Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!"
"Let justice be locked inside the king’s treasure chest"
"Let righteousness blow away like dry dust in the wind"

questions.correctAnswer: "Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!"
questions.explanation: Amos 5:24 is one of the most famous biblical calls for social justice, comparing justice to an unstoppable, life-giving river and righteousness to a perennial flowing stream.

questions.prompt: What powerful imagery did Prophet Amos use in Amos 5:24 to describe God’s standard of social justice?

questions.text: Why did God reject the religious festivals, sacrifices, and musical worship of the Israelites in Amos 5:21-23?

options.text: Because they sang without playing harps
Because they held worship services on the wrong day of the week
Because they practiced external religious ceremonies while practicing injustice and oppressing the poor in daily life
Because their sheep were too small to be sacrificed

questions.correctAnswer: Because they practiced external religious ceremonies while practicing injustice and oppressing the poor in daily life
questions.explanation: God hates empty religious hypocrisy: religious songs and sacrifices are meaningless when worshipers exploit the poor, take bribes, and ignore justice.

questions.prompt: Why did God reject the religious festivals, sacrifices, and musical worship of the Israelites in Amos 5:21-23?

options.text: To build large stone temples, fast three days a week, and memorize genealogies
To defeat enemy nations, accumulate silver, and rule over tribes
To offer thousands of rams and ten thousand rivers of olive oil
To act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God

questions.correctAnswer: To act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 sums up the heart of biblical morality: practicing practical justice, displaying loving-kindness (mercy), and living in humble relationship with God.

questions.prompt: What three supreme moral requirements does God demand of humanity according to Micah 6:8?

questions.text: What specific fraudulent economic practice did Prophet Amos condemn merchants for in Amos 8:5?

Selling fresh milk at low prices
Giving free grain to hungry travelers
Allowing farmers to trade without licenses

questions.correctAnswer: Using dishonest scales and skimped measures to cheat buyers and selling sweepings mixed with wheat
questions.explanation: Amos exposed merchants who manipulated scales, made the bushel small and the shekel large, and exploited vulnerable customers for profit.

questions.prompt: What specific fraudulent economic practice did Prophet Amos condemn merchants for in Amos 8:5?

"Don’t collect any more than you are required to"
"Charge double the tax and keep half for yourself"
"Refuse to pay any taxes to the government"

questions.correctAnswer: "Don’t collect any more than you are required to"
questions.explanation: Tax collectors routinely inflated tax bills to extort money for personal gain; John demanded immediate financial honesty and ethical restraint.

questions.prompt: What practical instruction on economic fairness did John the Baptist give to tax collectors in Luke 3:13?

"Don’t extort money and don’t accuse people falsely—be content with your pay"

questions.prompt: What ethical command did John the Baptist give to soldiers who asked how they should live righteously (Luke 3:14)?

questions.text: What did Prophet Isaiah proclaim in Isaiah 1:17 as the true expression of pure religion?

"Build high walls around your private estate"
"Ignore the poor so they learn to work harder"

He was a wealthy nobleman in King Jeroboam’s palace

questions.correctAnswer: They framed innocent Naboth with false witnesses, had him stoned to death, and seized his ancestral vineyard
questions.explanation: Jezebel orchestrated judicial murder and land-grabbing through perjury; Prophet Elijah confronted Ahab, pronouncing God’s stern judgment upon the corrupt royal house.

questions.text: What warning does Proverbs 14:31 give concerning the mistreatment and oppression of the poor?

"Oppressing the poor makes a nation economically powerful"
"Whoever oppresses the poor shows contempt for their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors God"

questions.prompt: What warning does Proverbs 14:31 give concerning the mistreatment and oppression of the poor?

questions.text: How did tax collector Zacchaeus demonstrate true biblical repentance when Jesus entered his home in Jericho (Luke 19:8)?

He promised to never collect taxes again

questions.text: What is the role of the Church when leaders in society practice injustice and corruption?

options.text: To be the prophetic conscience of the nation, speaking truth to power, defending the vulnerable, and advocating for fairness
To remain completely silent and support corruption in exchange for money
To organize violent armed uprisings to overthrow the state
To tell citizens that justice on earth does not matter

questions.correctAnswer: To be the prophetic conscience of the nation, speaking truth to power, defending the vulnerable, and advocating for fairness
questions.explanation: The Church must emulate biblical prophets, courageously holding leaders accountable to God’s standards of justice, integrity, and servant leadership.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the Church when leaders in society practice injustice and corruption?

questions.text: What does Exodus 23:8 say about accepting bribes?

options.text: "Only large bribes are forbidden; small bribes are fine"
"Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the innocent"
"Accepting bribes is a smart way to get rich quickly"
"Bribes are acceptable as long as nobody finds out"

questions.correctAnswer: "Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the innocent"
questions.explanation: Exodus 23:8 explains that bribery corrupts moral discernment, blinds judges and leaders, and subverts the cause of innocent people.

questions.prompt: What does Exodus 23:8 say about accepting bribes?

questions.text: How does corruption directly harm poor and vulnerable citizens in Kenya?

options.text: It has no effect on ordinary people
It only affects foreign tourists visiting Kenya
Public funds meant for medicine in clinics, clean water, and free schooling are stolen, leaving the poor to suffer and die needlessly
It makes poor people become wealthy quickly

questions.correctAnswer: Public funds meant for medicine in clinics, clean water, and free schooling are stolen, leaving the poor to suffer and die needlessly
questions.explanation: Corruption deprives citizens of vital life-saving services: stolen health funds cause shortages of essential drugs, while stolen road funds cause lethal accidents.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to public health and schools when national resources are stolen by corrupt officials?
questions.prompt: How does corruption directly harm poor and vulnerable citizens in Kenya?

questions.text: What constitutes academic dishonesty (corruption) in a primary school?

options.text: Borrowing a pencil from a friend and returning it
Studying past examination papers with a revision group
Asking the teacher to explain a difficult mathematics question
Cheating during exams, copying homework from a classmate, or paying someone to do your school projects
