questions.correctAnswer: "Bala wa ana ‘ala thalika minash-shahideen" (Yes, indeed! And I am among the witnesses to that)
questions.explanation: Sunnah teaches that upon hearing "A-laysallahu bi-ahkamil hakimeen", one responds: "Bala, wa ana ‘ala thalika minash-shahideen" in testimony to Allah’s supreme justice.
questions.socraticHint: Which Sunnah phrase confirms "Yes, indeed, and I bear witness that Allah is the Most Just of Judges"?
questions.prompt: What response did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) teach believers to utter when reciting or hearing the final verse of Surah Al-Tin?

questions.text: How does the concept of "Ahsani Taqwim" (best of forms) inspire self-worth and discourage youth from drug abuse?

options.text: It encourages youth to spend money on cosmetic surgery
It teaches that physical appearance is all that matters
It reminds us that our bodies, minds, and souls are masterfully fashioned by Allah, so poisoning them with drugs or alcohol defiles our sacred dignity
It means human bodies cannot be harmed by poisonous substances

questions.correctAnswer: It reminds us that our bodies, minds, and souls are masterfully fashioned by Allah, so poisoning them with drugs or alcohol defiles our sacred dignity
questions.explanation: Recognizing that Allah fashioned us in the finest mold instills self-respect, motivating youth to guard their brains, bodies, and health against toxic substances.
questions.socraticHint: How does knowing Allah made you in the best mold motivate you to protect your mind and body from drugs?
questions.prompt: How does the concept of "Ahsani Taqwim" (best of forms) inspire self-worth and discourage youth from drug abuse?

questions.text: What nutritional and environmental value is highlighted by the swearing by "The Fig and the Olive" in the Qur’an?

options.text: They are the only two plants that Muslims are permitted to cultivate
They are fruits that never rot or decay
They can only grow inside the borders of Kenya
They are wholesome, health-giving fruits of deep ecological, medicinal, and nutritional benefit celebrated in prophetic tradition

questions.correctAnswer: They are wholesome, health-giving fruits of deep ecological, medicinal, and nutritional benefit celebrated in prophetic tradition
questions.explanation: Qur’anic oaths draw attention to the extraordinary medicinal properties, nutritional richness, and ecological value of figs and olives in human wellness.
questions.socraticHint: Why does the Qur’an draw attention to the medicinal and nutritional qualities of figs and olives?
questions.prompt: What nutritional and environmental value is highlighted by the swearing by "The Fig and the Olive" in the Qur’an?

questions.text: What enduring message about human responsibility connects Surah Al-Qadr and Surah Al-Tin?

options.text: Allah has honored humanity with the greatest revelation (the Qur’an) and the finest creation (Ahsani Taqwim), calling us to live with faith, righteousness, and justice
Human beings should focus only on building worldly trade wealth
Only people in ancient times received guidance from Allah
Righteous deeds are not required if you belong to a particular tribe

questions.correctAnswer: Allah has honored humanity with the greatest revelation (the Qur’an) and the finest creation (Ahsani Taqwim), calling us to live with faith, righteousness, and justice
questions.explanation: Both chapters celebrate the divine dignity bestowed on humanity—honored with the Qur’an on Laylatul Qadr and created in the best mold—demanding sincere faith and righteous living.
questions.socraticHint: How do both surahs emphasize the supreme honor Allah gave humanity through the Qur’an and noble creation?
questions.prompt: What enduring message about human responsibility connects Surah Al-Qadr and Surah Al-Tin?

questions.text: According to the Hadith on truthfulness, what does Sidq (truthfulness) lead to, and where does that ultimate path lead?

options.text: Truthfulness leads only to worldly fame
Truthfulness leads to righteousness (Birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise (Jannah)
Truthfulness leads to poverty and defeat
Truthfulness leads to pride and arrogance

questions.correctAnswer: Truthfulness leads to righteousness (Birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise (Jannah)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated: "Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise."
questions.socraticHint: Which golden progression connects truthfulness to righteousness, and righteousness to Paradise?
questions.prompt: According to the Hadith on truthfulness, what does Sidq (truthfulness) lead to, and where does that ultimate path lead?

questions.text: What warning did the Prophet (SAW) give regarding Kithb (falsehood/lying)?

options.text: Lying leads to righteousness if done for money
Lying does not affect a Muslim’s spiritual record
Lying leads to wickedness (Fujur), and wickedness leads to the Fire (Jahannam)
Lying is acceptable if you are talking to friends

questions.correctAnswer: Lying leads to wickedness (Fujur), and wickedness leads to the Fire (Jahannam)
questions.explanation: The Hadith sternly warns: "Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire."
questions.socraticHint: What destructive spiritual destination does chronic lying lead to according to the Hadith?
questions.prompt: What warning did the Prophet (SAW) give regarding Kithb (falsehood/lying)?

questions.text: What noble title is recorded with Allah for a person who continually speaks the truth and strives to be truthful?

options.text: Siddiq (A champion of truth / deeply truthful)

questions.correctAnswer: Siddiq (A champion of truth / deeply truthful)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) explained that a person continues to tell the truth until he is recorded in the heavens as a "Siddiq."
questions.socraticHint: What title of honor—also carried by Abu Bakr—is recorded for a consistently truthful person?
questions.prompt: What noble title is recorded with Allah for a person who continually speaks the truth and strives to be truthful?

questions.text: What rule of speech did the Prophet (SAW) establish in the Hadith: "Man kana yu’minu billahi wal-yawmil-akhiri..."?

options.text: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent"
"Whoever believes in Allah should shout loudly in arguments"
"Whoever believes in Allah should speak continuously without stopping"
"Whoever believes in Allah should speak only in poetry"

questions.correctAnswer: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) linked faith in Allah and the Judgment Day to speech: if a word is not wholesome, beneficial, or kind, silence is superior.
questions.socraticHint: What two choices did the Prophet give: either speak what is good or do what?
questions.prompt: What rule of speech did the Prophet (SAW) establish in the Hadith: "Man kana yu’minu billahi wal-yawmil-akhiri..."?

questions.text: When Mu’adh ibn Jabal asked the Prophet (SAW) what would most ensure his entry into Paradise, what did the Prophet point to (holding his own tongue)?
questions.explanation: The Prophet held his tongue and told Mu’adh: "Restrain this." Mu’adh asked if we are held accountable for what we say, and the Prophet replied that people are cast into Hell primarily due to the harvest of their tongues.
questions.socraticHint: Which organ of the body did the Prophet hold while telling Mu’adh to restrain it?
questions.prompt: When Mu’adh ibn Jabal asked the Prophet (SAW) what would most ensure his entry into Paradise, what did the Prophet point to (holding his own tongue)?

questions.text: How does truthfulness in school examinations reflect the prophetic teaching of Sidq?

options.text: It means copying only from the smartest student
It means bribing the teacher to get higher marks
It means writing only what you have honestly learned, refusing to smuggle notes or peek at another student’s paper
It means helping friends cheat so they pass

questions.correctAnswer: It means writing only what you have honestly learned, refusing to smuggle notes or peek at another student’s paper
questions.explanation: Academic honesty is a direct application of Sidq; cheating is deceit (Khiyanah), which the Prophet strictly condemned: "Whoever deceives us is not of us."
questions.socraticHint: How does refusing to cheat or copy during an examination demonstrate prophetic truthfulness?
questions.prompt: How does truthfulness in school examinations reflect the prophetic teaching of Sidq?

questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) guarantee in the Hadith: "I guarantee a house in the middle of Paradise for one who..."?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) guaranteed a home in the middle of Paradise for the person who abandons falsehood even in jest, teaching that truthfulness must be maintained in humor.
questions.socraticHint: What reward did the Prophet promise for giving up lying even when telling jokes?
questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) guarantee in the Hadith: "I guarantee a house in the middle of Paradise for one who..."?

questions.text: Why does lying in trade or business transactions destroy Allah’s blessing (Barakah)?

options.text: Because concealing product defects and swearing false oaths to sell goods invites divine displeasure and removes true profit
Because merchants should only sell goods for free
Because customers prefer being told lies
Because barter trade was forbidden in Arabia

questions.correctAnswer: Because concealing product defects and swearing false oaths to sell goods invites divine displeasure and removes true profit
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated that if buyers and sellers are truthful, their trade is blessed; but if they lie and conceal defects, the blessing of their transaction is obliterated.
questions.socraticHint: What happens to the blessing (Barakah) of trade when sellers conceal defects and tell lies?
questions.prompt: Why does lying in trade or business transactions destroy Allah’s blessing (Barakah)?

questions.text: How should a Muslim pupil apply the Hadith "speak good or remain silent" when interacting on social media WhatsApp groups?

options.text: Post private pictures of other pupils to mock them
Post uplifting, helpful messages and study notes, and refuse to participate in online insults, trolling, or spreading gossip
Forward every rumor received without checking if it is true
Use abusive nicknames for classmates in group chats

questions.correctAnswer: Post uplifting, helpful messages and study notes, and refuse to participate in online insults, trolling, or spreading gossip
questions.explanation: Guarding the tongue applies equally to the keyboard: digital words carry the exact same moral weight and accountability before Allah.
questions.socraticHint: How does typing only kind words and refusing to forward gossip apply guarding the tongue online?
questions.prompt: How should a Muslim pupil apply the Hadith "speak good or remain silent" when interacting on social media WhatsApp groups?

questions.text: What sign of a hypocrite (Munafiq) relates directly to speech according to the famous Hadith?

options.text: "When he sleeps, he wakes up for Fajr"
"When he eats, he uses his right hand"

questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) identified three signs of a hypocrite: "When he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when he is trusted, he betrays it."
questions.socraticHint: What does a hypocrite do whenever he speaks according to the Prophet’s warning?
questions.prompt: What sign of a hypocrite (Munafiq) relates directly to speech according to the famous Hadith?

questions.text: What internal peace does truthfulness bring according to the Hadith: "Truthfulness brings tranquility (Tum’anina), while falsehood brings doubt (Rayb)"?

options.text: The ability to sleep without dreaming
Immediate physical strength to lift heavy rocks
Freedom from having to take school tests
A clear conscience free of fear of being exposed, while a liar lives in continuous stress and anxiety

questions.correctAnswer: A clear conscience free of fear of being exposed, while a liar lives in continuous stress and anxiety
questions.explanation: Truthfulness produces inner serenity and security; lying forces a person to fabricate more lies, living in perpetual paranoia and guilt.
questions.socraticHint: Why does speaking the truth give your heart calm peace while lying brings restless anxiety?
questions.prompt: What internal peace does truthfulness bring according to the Hadith: "Truthfulness brings tranquility (Tum’anina), while falsehood brings doubt (Rayb)"?

questions.text: What happens to a person who is labeled with Allah as a "Kath-thab" (chronic liar)?

options.text: They lose divine trust, their word is despised by people, and they are recorded for divine punishment
They receive special leadership positions in the mosque
Their memory becomes twice as sharp
They are granted immunity from sins

questions.correctAnswer: They lose divine trust, their word is despised by people, and they are recorded for divine punishment
questions.explanation: Persistent lying hardens the heart until a person is registered in the heavens as a chronic liar, losing moral credibility on earth and in the hereafter.
questions.socraticHint: What spiritual ruin and loss of human trust falls on someone branded as a habitual liar?
questions.prompt: What happens to a person who is labeled with Allah as a "Kath-thab" (chronic liar)?

questions.text: In the Hadith "Al-Deen Al-Naseehah", what does the Arabic word "Naseehah" mean?

options.text: Sincere advice, goodwill, and genuine loyalty with pure intentions
Taking long journeys to commercial cities

questions.correctAnswer: Sincere advice, goodwill, and genuine loyalty with pure intentions
questions.explanation: Naseehah comes from the root meaning purity and sincerity (like filtering honey from impurities); it denotes sincere counsel and genuine goodwill toward others.
questions.socraticHint: Does Naseehah mean sincere, pure-hearted advice and goodwill?
questions.prompt: In the Hadith "Al-Deen Al-Naseehah", what does the Arabic word "Naseehah" mean?

questions.text: What does showing sincere advice (Naseehah) to the Book of Allah (His Book) involve?

options.text: Translating it only into European languages
Using it as a decorative paper ornament
Believing in it, reciting it with Tajweed, contemplating its meanings, and putting its moral teachings into practice
Keeping it locked on a high shelf without ever opening it

questions.correctAnswer: Believing in it, reciting it with Tajweed, contemplating its meanings, and putting its moral teachings into practice
questions.explanation: Sincerity toward the Qur’an means honoring it as the Word of Allah, learning its recitation, understanding its guidance, and living by its principles.
questions.socraticHint: How do reciting, studying, and obeying the Holy Qur’an show sincerity toward God’s Book?
questions.prompt: What does showing sincere advice (Naseehah) to the Book of Allah (His Book) involve?

questions.text: What does Naseehah toward the common folk of the Muslims ("wa li-’ammatihim") require from believers?

options.text: Cheating them in market trade to make quick profit
Ignoring them when they face disease or poverty
Boasting about our superior family lineages
Loving for them what we love for ourselves, guiding them kindly, assisting the needy, and protecting their dignity

questions.correctAnswer: Loving for them what we love for ourselves, guiding them kindly, assisting the needy, and protecting their dignity
questions.explanation: Sincerity to everyday citizens entails wishing them well, defending their rights, aiding them in distress, and counseling them with love.
questions.socraticHint: How does wishing for your fellow citizens the same good you wish for yourself fulfill Naseehah?
questions.prompt: What does Naseehah toward the common folk of the Muslims ("wa li-’ammatihim") require from believers?

questions.text: What proper etiquette should a Muslim observe when giving advice to a friend who is making a mistake?

options.text: Advise them privately, gently, with loving words, avoiding public shaming or self-righteous anger
Shout their mistake across the whole school playground
Post about their mistake on a public WhatsApp group
Tell all their enemies so they can mock them

questions.correctAnswer: Advise them privately, gently, with loving words, avoiding public shaming or self-righteous anger
questions.explanation: Islamic manners demand that advice be delivered in private with gentle compassion; public correction is humiliation (Fadihah) that hardens hearts.
questions.socraticHint: Should you correct a friend privately with kindness or embarrass them publicly?
questions.prompt: What proper etiquette should a Muslim observe when giving advice to a friend who is making a mistake?

questions.text: How did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) define Gheebah (backbiting)?

options.text: "Praising a person’s good qualities behind their back"
"Mentioning about your brother that which he dislikes in his absence"
"Saying hello to someone who is far away"
"Advising a student in the presence of a teacher"

questions.correctAnswer: "Mentioning about your brother that which he dislikes in his absence"
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: "Gheebah is mentioning about your brother that which he dislikes." A companion asked: "What if it is true?" The Prophet said: "If it is true, you have backbitten him; if it is false, you have slandered him (Buhtan)."
questions.socraticHint: What did the Prophet say backbiting is even if what you say is actually true?
questions.prompt: How did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) define Gheebah (backbiting)?

questions.text: To what abhorrent act does the Holy Qur’an compare backbiting in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12)?

options.text: Throwing stones into an empty well
Eating the flesh of one’s dead brother
Drinking sea water in a desert

questions.correctAnswer: Eating the flesh of one’s dead brother
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:12 asks: "Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would abhor it!" to illustrate how repulsive backbiting is.
questions.socraticHint: What horrifying image in Surah Al-Hujurat illustrates how detestable backbiting is?
questions.prompt: To what abhorrent act does the Holy Qur’an compare backbiting in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12)?

questions.text: What is Nameemah (tale-bearing), and why did the Prophet (SAW) warn that a tale-bearer will not enter Paradise?

options.text: Carrying heavy bags for elderly neighbors
Teaching young children how to read the alphabet
Telling true historical stories to students
Carrying gossip and hearsay between people with the evil motive of causing conflict and ruining relationships

questions.correctAnswer: Carrying gossip and hearsay between people with the evil motive of causing conflict and ruining relationships
questions.explanation: Nameemah is maliciously transferring words ("so-and-so said this about you") to sow discord, break friendships, and spark hatred among people.
questions.socraticHint: What destructive habit carries private words between friends specifically to create fights?
questions.prompt: What is Nameemah (tale-bearing), and why did the Prophet (SAW) warn that a tale-bearer will not enter Paradise?

questions.text: What should a Muslim student do if they sit with a group of friends who start backbiting and mocking an absent classmate?

options.text: Defend the absent classmate’s honor, remind the group to fear Allah, and leave the gathering if they persist
Join in the laughter and add more insulting rumors
Secretly record the conversation and sell it online

questions.correctAnswer: Defend the absent classmate’s honor, remind the group to fear Allah, and leave the gathering if they persist
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother in his absence, Allah will protect his face from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection."
questions.socraticHint: How does defending an absent brother or sister protect your own face from the Fire?
questions.prompt: What should a Muslim student do if they sit with a group of friends who start backbiting and mocking an absent classmate?

questions.text: What is Buhtan (slander), and how does it differ from Gheebah (backbiting)?

options.text: There is no difference between the two terms
Buhtan is fabricating completely false lies and spreading them about someone, which is even more severe than Gheebah
Buhtan is giving advice to a teacher
Buhtan is another name for performing wudhu

questions.correctAnswer: Buhtan is fabricating completely false lies and spreading them about someone, which is even more severe than Gheebah
questions.explanation: While Gheebah mentions a true fault behind someone’s back, Buhtan is inventing blatant, malicious lies that the person never did or said.
questions.socraticHint: Is Buhtan inventing completely false lies about someone behind their back?
questions.prompt: What is Buhtan (slander), and how does it differ from Gheebah (backbiting)?

questions.text: How does practicing Naseehah (sincere advice) strengthen unity in Kenya’s multi-ethnic schools?

options.text: It eliminates all homework and tests
It forces everyone to agree on everything without discussion
It creates an atmosphere of mutual trust, constructive correction, and care, preventing misunderstandings from turning into hatred
It makes all pupils speak only one language

questions.correctAnswer: It creates an atmosphere of mutual trust, constructive correction, and care, preventing misunderstandings from turning into hatred
questions.explanation: When students advise each other with love and respect, conflicts are defused early, fostering a supportive, cohesive, and harmonious school community.
questions.socraticHint: How does loving mutual correction build trust and unity among diverse learners?
questions.prompt: How does practicing Naseehah (sincere advice) strengthen unity in Kenya’s multi-ethnic schools?

questions.text: What did the Prophet (SAW) say about two people having a private whispered conversation in the presence of a third person?

options.text: They should whisper in foreign languages so he cannot understand
Whispering is recommended in all gatherings
The third person should be ordered to leave the room
Two people should not whisper privately excluding the third, as it causes him grief and makes him feel suspicious

questions.correctAnswer: Two people should not whisper privately excluding the third, as it causes him grief and makes him feel suspicious
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught exquisite social sensitivity: whispering that excludes a third companion hurts their feelings and breeds suspicion, violating Islamic manners.
questions.socraticHint: Why is whispering in front of a third person forbidden in Islamic etiquette?
questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (SAW) say about two people having a private whispered conversation in the presence of a third person?

questions.text: What should someone do if they realize they have previously backbitten a brother or sister in school?

options.text: Make sincere Tawbah to Allah, seek the person’s forgiveness if it will not cause greater harm, and speak well of them in the same gatherings where they were defamed
Pretend nothing happened and do it again
Blame the people who listened to the gossip

questions.correctAnswer: Make sincere Tawbah to Allah, seek the person’s forgiveness if it will not cause greater harm, and speak well of them in the same gatherings where they were defamed
questions.explanation: Expiation for backbiting requires repenting to Allah, praying for the victim, seeking their pardon, and praising their good qualities to restore their reputation.
questions.socraticHint: How do sincere repentance and praising the victim help repair the sin of backbiting?
questions.prompt: What should someone do if they realize they have previously backbitten a brother or sister in school?

questions.text: Which two close pillars of support passed away in the 10th year of Prophethood, leading it to be called the "Year of Sorrow" (‘Am al-Huzn)?

options.text: His companion Abu Bakr and his cousin Ali
His uncle Abu Talib and his beloved wife Sayyidah Khadijah (RA)
His father Abdullah and his mother Aminah
His grandfather Abdul Muttalib and his uncle Hamza

questions.correctAnswer: His uncle Abu Talib and his beloved wife Sayyidah Khadijah (RA)
questions.explanation: The Prophet suffered double bereavement in the 10th year of Bi’thah: his protective uncle Abu Talib and his comforting, loyal wife Khadijah (RA) passed away.
questions.socraticHint: Which protective uncle and devoted first wife died during the Year of Sorrow?
questions.prompt: Which two close pillars of support passed away in the 10th year of Prophethood, leading it to be called the "Year of Sorrow" (‘Am al-Huzn)?

questions.text: Why was the death of Abu Talib particularly dangerous for the Prophet’s physical safety in Makkah?

options.text: Abu Talib commanded the Roman army
Abu Talib owned all the water wells in Makkah
Abu Talib had provided tribal clan protection (Jiwar) from Banu Hashim that prevented the Quraysh from physically assassinating the Prophet
Abu Talib was the governor of Makkah

questions.correctAnswer: Abu Talib had provided tribal clan protection (Jiwar) from Banu Hashim that prevented the Quraysh from physically assassinating the Prophet
questions.explanation: Under Arab customary tribal law, Abu Talib’s clan protection shielded the Prophet from lethal assault. His death left the Prophet vulnerable to open violence.

questions.prompt: Why was the death of Abu Talib particularly dangerous for the Prophet’s physical safety in Makkah?

questions.prompt: Which adopted companion accompanied Prophet Muhammad (SAW) on the difficult 80-kilometer journey to the city of Ta’if?

questions.prompt: Which tribe inhabited the city of Ta’if and rejected the Prophet’s invitation to Islam?

questions.text: How did the hostile leaders of Ta’if treat Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when he left their city?

options.text: They built a house for him inside the city walls
They incited street mobs and youths who lined the path, hurling stones and insults until his feet bled
They escorted him safely with a cavalry honor guard
They gave him bags of silver and invited him to return

questions.correctAnswer: They incited street mobs and youths who lined the path, hurling stones and insults until his feet bled
questions.explanation: The chieftains unleashed ruffians who formed two rows, pelting the Prophet with stones, wounding his shins and feet until his sandals were stained with blood.

questions.prompt: How did the hostile leaders of Ta’if treat Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when he left their city?

questions.text: In whose grape orchard did the bleeding Prophet (SAW) take refuge to rest and pray to Allah outside Ta’if?

options.text: The orchard belonging to Abu Lahab
The orchard belonging to King Negus
The orchard belonging to ‘Utbah and Shaybah ibn Rabi’ah
The orchard belonging to Abu Jahl

questions.correctAnswer: The orchard belonging to ‘Utbah and Shaybah ibn Rabi’ah
questions.explanation: The Prophet found refuge in the private vineyard of the sons of Rabi’ah (‘Utbah and Shaybah), where he poured out his heart in humble prayer to Allah.

questions.prompt: In whose grape orchard did the bleeding Prophet (SAW) take refuge to rest and pray to Allah outside Ta’if?

questions.text: Who was ‘Addas, and how did he interact with the Prophet (SAW) in the vineyard at Ta’if?

options.text: A Roman soldier who tried to arrest the Prophet
A merchant who sold bread to Zayd
A desert guide who showed them the way back
A Christian slave boy from Nineveh who brought grapes to the Prophet, recognized him as a true prophet, and embraced Islam

questions.correctAnswer: A Christian slave boy from Nineveh who brought grapes to the Prophet, recognized him as a true prophet, and embraced Islam
questions.explanation: When the Prophet said "Bismillah" before eating the grapes, ‘Addas was astonished. Hearing that the Prophet knew of Prophet Yunus (Jonah) of Nineveh, ‘Addas kissed the Prophet’s hands and head.

questions.prompt: Who was ‘Addas, and how did he interact with the Prophet (SAW) in the vineyard at Ta’if?

questions.text: What did the Angel of the Mountains offer to do to the people of Ta’if when he appeared alongside Jibril?

options.text: To crush them between the two steep mountains surrounding Makkah (Al-Akhshabayn)
To send a flood of boiling water across their city
To turn their grape orchards into dry salt deserts

questions.correctAnswer: To crush them between the two steep mountains surrounding Makkah (Al-Akhshabayn)
questions.explanation: The Angel of the Mountains greeted the Prophet and offered: "If you wish, I will bring together the two mountains upon them." Divine power was at the Prophet’s command.
questions.socraticHint: What destructive punishment using the two mountains did the Angel offer to execute on Ta’if?
questions.prompt: What did the Angel of the Mountains offer to do to the people of Ta’if when he appeared alongside Jibril?

questions.text: What was Prophet Muhammad’s (SAW) astonishingly merciful reply to the Angel of the Mountains?

options.text: "Take all their cattle and bring them to Makkah"
"No, rather I hope that Allah will raise from their descendants people who will worship Allah alone without associating partners with Him!"
"Yes, destroy them all immediately because they injured my feet"
"Wait until tomorrow, then crush half of their houses"

questions.correctAnswer: "No, rather I hope that Allah will raise from their descendants people who will worship Allah alone without associating partners with Him!"
questions.explanation: The Prophet’s response is the ultimate proof of his title "Rahmatan lil-’Alameen" (A Mercy to the Worlds): refusing revenge and praying for the salvation of their future generations.
questions.socraticHint: How did the Prophet choose mercy and hope for their future children rather than seeking revenge?
questions.prompt: What was Prophet Muhammad’s (SAW) astonishingly merciful reply to the Angel of the Mountains?

questions.text: What timeless lesson does the Prophet’s supplication in the vineyard of Ta’if teach believers facing severe rejection or hardship?

options.text: To blame friends for not fighting on your behalf
To turn entirely to Allah with humble surrender, seeking His pleasure above all human acceptance or earthly power
To give up on life and stop praying

questions.correctAnswer: To turn entirely to Allah with humble surrender, seeking His pleasure above all human acceptance or earthly power
questions.explanation: The Prophet prayed: "So long as You are not angry with me, I do not care [about human rejection]." True faith finds peace solely in Allah’s divine pleasure.
questions.socraticHint: What did the Prophet care about most in his du’a: human praise or Allah’s divine pleasure?
questions.prompt: What timeless lesson does the Prophet’s supplication in the vineyard of Ta’if teach believers facing severe rejection or hardship?

questions.socraticHint: Which noble Makkan chieftain escorted the Prophet safely back into Makkah with his armed sons?
questions.prompt: Under whose clan protection (Jiwar) was Prophet Muhammad (SAW) able to safely re-enter Makkah after the journey to Ta’if?

questions.text: How can primary school pupils emulate the Prophet’s reaction to the Ta’if trial when mistreated or bullied by peers?

By bringing stones to school to throw at the bullies after class

questions.text: According to prophetic Hadith, which of the following will be the first matter a servant is held accountable for on the Day of Judgment regarding deeds?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated: "The first matter that the slave will be brought to account for on the Day of Judgment is the prayer (Salah). If it is sound, then the rest of his deeds will be sound..."
questions.socraticHint: Which foundational pillar of daily worship is assessed first before all other deeds?
questions.prompt: According to prophetic Hadith, which of the following will be the first matter a servant is held accountable for on the Day of Judgment regarding deeds?

questions.text: What is the special lake or cistern granted to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) on the Day of Resurrection, from which whoever drinks will never thirst again?
questions.explanation: Al-Hawd is the prophetic cistern whose water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; drinking from it ensures one never experiences thirst again.
questions.socraticHint: Recall the special pool connected to Surah Al-Kawthar.
questions.prompt: What is the special lake or cistern granted to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) on the Day of Resurrection, from which whoever drinks will never thirst again?

questions.text: Who is the guardian angel of Hellfire (Jahannam) mentioned in Surah Az-Zukhruf (43:77)?
questions.explanation: Malik is the angel who oversees Hellfire; the transgressors will call out to him: "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!" but he will reply: "Indeed, you will remain."
questions.socraticHint: Distinguish between Ridwan (gatekeeper of Paradise) and Malik (keeper of Hellfire).
questions.prompt: Who is the guardian angel of Hellfire (Jahannam) mentioned in Surah Az-Zukhruf (43:77)?

questions.text: What does Islam teach about a person who has oppressed others in this world when standing before the Mizan?

options.text: Their good deeds will be taken and given to their victims to settle the score of injustice
Their wealth in world bank accounts will buy their forgiveness
Their powerful relatives will bribe the angels
The oppression is completely forgotten and ignored

questions.correctAnswer: Their good deeds will be taken and given to their victims to settle the score of injustice
questions.explanation: In the Hadith of the bankrupt person (Al-Muflis), the Prophet explained that good deeds are transferred to victims of backbiting, theft, or slander until justice is satisfied.
questions.socraticHint: How does divine balance compensate victims of human injustice on the Day of Judgment?
questions.prompt: What does Islam teach about a person who has oppressed others in this world when standing before the Mizan?

questions.text: Which pillar of Iman is belief in Al-Qadar (Divine Destiny)?
questions.explanation: In Hadith Jibril, when asked about Iman, the Prophet listed: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and belief in Al-Qadar (the sixth pillar).
questions.socraticHint: Count the six articles of faith from Hadith Jibril.
questions.prompt: Which pillar of Iman is belief in Al-Qadar (Divine Destiny)?

questions.text: What is the first fundamental level (Martabah) of Al-Qadar?

options.text: Al-’Ilm (Allah’s comprehensive, eternal knowledge of all things)

questions.correctAnswer: Al-’Ilm (Allah’s comprehensive, eternal knowledge of all things)
questions.explanation: Al-’Ilm is the first stage: Allah knows all things before they exist, what has happened, what will happen, and what did not happen how it would have happened.
questions.socraticHint: Which stage refers to Allah’s infinite omniscience?
questions.prompt: What is the first fundamental level (Martabah) of Al-Qadar?

questions.text: Where were all decrees and destinies written fifty thousand years before the creation of the heavens and the earth?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated that Allah commanded the Pen to write everything that will happen until the Day of Resurrection in Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz.
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic phrase means "The Well-Preserved Tablet"?
questions.prompt: Where were all decrees and destinies written fifty thousand years before the creation of the heavens and the earth?

questions.text: What are the four recognized levels (Maratib) of Al-Qadar in Islamic theology?

options.text: Birth, Youth, Adulthood, and Old age

questions.explanation: Scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah outline the four pillars of Qadar as: 1) Al-’Ilm, 2) Al-Kitabah, 3) Al-Mashi’ah, and 4) Al-Khalq.
questions.socraticHint: Look for the theological sequence starting from divine knowledge to divine creation.
questions.prompt: What are the four recognized levels (Maratib) of Al-Qadar in Islamic theology?

questions.text: When a Bedouin asked whether he should tie his camel or leave it loose and trust in Allah, what did the Prophet (SAW) reply?

options.text: "Do not worry about the camel at all"
"Tie her, and then rely on Allah" (I’qilha wa tawakkal)
"Leave her untied, for tying shows a lack of faith"
"Sell the camel and walk on foot"

questions.correctAnswer: "Tie her, and then rely on Allah" (I’qilha wa tawakkal)
questions.explanation: The Prophet clarified that true reliance on Allah (Tawakkul) requires taking practical responsibility and precautions first, not reckless passivity (Tawaakul).
questions.socraticHint: Does true faith mean being reckless or taking proper precautions before trusting Allah?
questions.prompt: When a Bedouin asked whether he should tie his camel or leave it loose and trust in Allah, what did the Prophet (SAW) reply?

questions.text: What is the vital difference between Tawakkul (true reliance on Allah) and Tawaakul (false resignation)?

options.text: Tawakkul means ignoring medical treatment during illness
There is no difference; they mean the exact same thing
Tawakkul combines active effort with trust in Allah, while Tawaakul is laziness without effort
Tawakkul is only for scholars, while Tawaakul is for general Muslims

questions.correctAnswer: Tawakkul combines active effort with trust in Allah, while Tawaakul is laziness without effort
questions.explanation: Tawakkul requires using legitimate means, studying, working, and praying, while Tawaakul is neglecting responsibility and making excuses.
questions.socraticHint: How does making an effort distinguish genuine faith from mere laziness?
questions.prompt: What is the vital difference between Tawakkul (true reliance on Allah) and Tawaakul (false resignation)?

questions.text: Can a person who commits a crime or refuses to revise for exams blame Al-Qadar (Divine Decree) for their failure?

options.text: Yes, because everything is pre-recorded, humans have no moral responsibility
Yes, Qadar excuses all criminal acts and negligence
Only if they committed the act during daytime hours
No, because humans possess free choice and intellect, making them accountable for their decisions

questions.correctAnswer: No, because humans possess free choice and intellect, making them accountable for their decisions
questions.explanation: Islam rejects fatalism; Allah gave humans guidance, reasoning, and choice. When someone chooses to sin or be lazy, they are responsible for that decision.
questions.socraticHint: Why does God reward good deeds and punish evil if humans had no choice?
questions.prompt: Can a person who commits a crime or refuses to revise for exams blame Al-Qadar (Divine Decree) for their failure?

questions.text: What noble attitude should a believer display when struck by an unforeseen calamity or loss?

options.text: Patience (Sabr), saying "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un", and trust in Allah’s wisdom
Anger, screaming curses at destiny, and despair
Giving up daily prayers and abandoning work
Blaming innocent neighbors and plotting retaliation

questions.correctAnswer: Patience (Sabr), saying "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un", and trust in Allah’s wisdom
questions.explanation: Belief in Qadar grants emotional tranquility. In hardship, the believer exercises Sabr and says "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we shall return," knowing trials contain hidden mercy.
questions.socraticHint: What virtue enables a Muslim to endure hardship with dignity and calm faith?
questions.prompt: What noble attitude should a believer display when struck by an unforeseen calamity or loss?

questions.text: When experiencing grand success or wealth, how does belief in Al-Qadar protect a Muslim from arrogance?

options.text: It allows them to boast endlessly about their personal brilliance
It reminds them that success is a blessing and test from Allah, inspiring Shukr (Gratitude) and humility
It makes them believe they are superior to all other humans
It proves they are inherently holier than poorer people

questions.correctAnswer: It reminds them that success is a blessing and test from Allah, inspiring Shukr (Gratitude) and humility
questions.explanation: Belief in Qadar keeps a person humble, realizing their talents and opportunities are gifts from Allah, inspiring gratitude (Shukr) rather than pride (Kibr).
questions.socraticHint: Who is the true grantor of victory, intellect, and wealth?
questions.prompt: When experiencing grand success or wealth, how does belief in Al-Qadar protect a Muslim from arrogance?

questions.text: What famous phrase did Caliph Umar say when deciding to turn back from entering Syria during the devastating plague of Amwas?

options.text: "Destiny cannot harm those with pure intentions"
"Plague only affects those who do not pray"
"We flee from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah"
"A warrior never retreats even from disease"

questions.correctAnswer: "We flee from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah"
questions.explanation: Umar wisely noted that taking medical precaution by avoiding an infected town is itself acting in accordance with Allah’s decree.
questions.socraticHint: Recognize Umar’s balance between taking precautions and honoring God’s decree.
questions.prompt: What famous phrase did Caliph Umar say when deciding to turn back from entering Syria during the devastating plague of Amwas?

questions.text: Why does the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) prohibit obsessing over "What if..." (Law) when an accident or loss occurs?

options.text: Because grammar rules forbid using conditionals in Arabic
Because the past can be changed through magic
Because feelings of grief are unlawful in all circumstances
Because saying "If only..." opens the door to Satan’s despair and regret

questions.correctAnswer: Because saying "If only..." opens the door to Satan’s despair and regret
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught: "If something befalls you, do not say: If only I had done such-and-such... Rather say: Qaddar Allahu wa ma sha’a fa’ala (Allah has decreed, and what He willed has occurred), for ‘if only’ opens the work of Satan."
questions.socraticHint: How does excessive regret and "if only" trap a person in sorrow and distrust of God?
questions.prompt: Why does the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) prohibit obsessing over "What if..." (Law) when an accident or loss occurs?

questions.text: How should a Grade 6 learner apply belief in Al-Qadar when sitting for national school examinations?

options.text: Study hard, make du’a, follow exam rules, and peacefully accept the final outcome as Allah’s decree
Do not read books or revise, expecting Allah to fill in the exam answers magically
Cheat if questions are difficult, claiming it was destined to happen
Become hopeless and skip the examination completely

questions.correctAnswer: Study hard, make du’a, follow exam rules, and peacefully accept the final outcome as Allah’s decree
questions.explanation: Pairing thorough academic revision with prayer (Tawakkul) and having peace of mind regarding the outcome reflects true belief in Al-Qadar.
questions.socraticHint: What is the balanced prophetic recipe for academic success and peace of mind?
questions.prompt: How should a Grade 6 learner apply belief in Al-Qadar when sitting for national school examinations?

questions.text: What does the term "Qasr" mean in the context of Swalatul Musafir?

options.text: Shortening four-rak’ah obligatory prayers to two rak’ahs
Skipping the prayer completely without making it up
Combining all five prayers into one single session

questions.correctAnswer: Shortening four-rak’ah obligatory prayers to two rak’ahs
questions.explanation: Qasr literally means reduction or shortening, referring to reducing the 4-rak’ah prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha) down to 2 rak’ahs for a traveler.
questions.socraticHint: Which Islamic term refers to cutting 4-rak’ah prayers in half during travel?
questions.prompt: What does the term "Qasr" mean in the context of Swalatul Musafir?

questions.text: Which obligatory prayers can be shortened (Qasr) by a traveler?
questions.explanation: Only the 4-rak’ah prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha) can be shortened to 2 rak’ahs. Fajr (2 rak’ahs) and Maghrib (3 rak’ahs) cannot be shortened.
questions.socraticHint: Which daily prayers normally consist of four units (rak’ahs)?
questions.prompt: Which obligatory prayers can be shortened (Qasr) by a traveler?

questions.text: Why can Maghrib prayer NEVER be shortened under Qasr?

options.text: Because it is performed after sunset
Because it has no recitation of Surah Al-Fatihah
Because travelers are not permitted to pray Maghrib
Because it consists of an odd number of rak’ahs (3 rak’ahs), known as Witr of the daytime

questions.correctAnswer: Because it consists of an odd number of rak’ahs (3 rak’ahs), known as Witr of the daytime
questions.explanation: Maghrib consists of three rak’ahs and is regarded as the Witr of daytime prayers; according to authentic Sunnah, it must always be prayed as three rak’ahs.
questions.socraticHint: How many rak’ahs does Maghrib have, and can three rak’ahs be halved into an even prayer?
questions.prompt: Why can Maghrib prayer NEVER be shortened under Qasr?

questions.text: Which two pairs of prayers are permissible to combine under Jam’a during travel?

options.text: Dhuhr with Asr, and Maghrib with Isha
Fajr with Dhuhr, and Asr with Maghrib
Fajr with Isha, and Dhuhr with Maghrib
Isha with Fajr, and Asr with Dhuhr

questions.correctAnswer: Dhuhr with Asr, and Maghrib with Isha
questions.explanation: In Islamic law, combining prayers is strictly limited to Dhuhr joined with Asr, and Maghrib joined with Isha. Fajr cannot be combined with any other prayer.
questions.socraticHint: Which prayers occur consecutively during daytime and evening?
questions.prompt: Which two pairs of prayers are permissible to combine under Jam’a during travel?

questions.text: What is it called when a traveler performs Asr early during the time of Dhuhr?
questions.explanation: Jam’a Taqdim means advancing the second prayer to be performed in the time window of the first prayer (e.g., praying Asr during Dhuhr time).
questions.socraticHint: The Arabic word "Taqdim" comes from bringing something forward or early.
questions.prompt: What is it called when a traveler performs Asr early during the time of Dhuhr?

questions.text: What is it called when a traveler delays Maghrib prayer to perform it later alongside Isha during Isha time?
questions.explanation: Jam’a Ta’khir means delaying the first prayer to be prayed alongside the second prayer in the second prayer’s designated time period.
questions.socraticHint: The Arabic word "Ta’khir" signifies delaying or postponing.
questions.prompt: What is it called when a traveler delays Maghrib prayer to perform it later alongside Isha during Isha time?

questions.text: If a traveling Muslim joins a local resident congregation led by a resident Imam for Dhuhr prayer, how many rak’ahs must the traveler pray?

options.text: Two rak’ahs, making Salam while the Imam continues
Four rak’ahs, following the Imam fully

questions.correctAnswer: Four rak’ahs, following the Imam fully
questions.explanation: According to prophetic Sunnah, when a traveler prays behind a resident Imam who is praying 4 rak’ahs, the traveler is required to follow the Imam and complete all 4 rak’ahs.
questions.socraticHint: What happens when a traveler joins a resident imam leading a complete prayer?
questions.prompt: If a traveling Muslim joins a local resident congregation led by a resident Imam for Dhuhr prayer, how many rak’ahs must the traveler pray?

questions.text: What is the Islamic legal term for divine concessions and allowances granted by Allah to ease hardship, such as Qasr during travel?
questions.explanation: Rukhsah is an Islamic legal allowance granted in response to difficult circumstances, such as shortening prayers, breaking fast during travel, or Tayammum.
questions.socraticHint: Which term contrasts with Azeemah (the standard strict obligation)?
questions.prompt: What is the Islamic legal term for divine concessions and allowances granted by Allah to ease hardship, such as Qasr during travel?

questions.text: What minimum travel distance is generally recognized by the majority of jurists for applying the concessions of Swalatul Musafir?

options.text: Any distance outside the compound gate
Approximately 80 kilometers (48 miles) away from one’s hometown boundaries

questions.correctAnswer: Approximately 80 kilometers (48 miles) away from one’s hometown boundaries
questions.explanation: Classical scholars estimated the travel distance (Masafat al-Qasr) as four Burud (approximately 80 to 88 kilometers) leaving the boundary of one’s home city.
questions.socraticHint: Think of the traditional distance equal to approximately two days of marching camel travel (~80 km).
questions.prompt: What minimum travel distance is generally recognized by the majority of jurists for applying the concessions of Swalatul Musafir?

questions.text: Can a person combine Fajr prayer with Dhuhr prayer if they woke up late while traveling?

options.text: Yes, travelers can combine all five prayers whenever they like
No, Fajr cannot be combined with any other prayer under any circumstance
Yes, as long as it is done before afternoon

questions.correctAnswer: No, Fajr cannot be combined with any other prayer under any circumstance
questions.explanation: Fajr prayer stands completely independent and must be performed in its own designated dawn time period; it cannot be combined with any other prayer.
questions.socraticHint: Remember the strict rule regarding the dawn prayer.
questions.prompt: Can a person combine Fajr prayer with Dhuhr prayer if they woke up late while traveling?

questions.text: What spiritual wisdom does the permission of Qasr and Jam’a reflect about the nature of Islamic Shari’ah?

options.text: It shows that prayers are unimportant during journeys
It indicates that Allah changes His laws randomly
It allows travelers to abandon faith practices
It reflects divine mercy and the principle that religion brings ease, not hardship (Yusr wa laysa ‘Usr)

questions.correctAnswer: It reflects divine mercy and the principle that religion brings ease, not hardship (Yusr wa laysa ‘Usr)
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: "Indeed, the religion is easy." Allah grants concessions during exhausting travels to ensure worship remains sweet and accessible.
questions.socraticHint: How does divine facilitation highlight Islam’s compassion for human weakness?
questions.prompt: What spiritual wisdom does the permission of Qasr and Jam’a reflect about the nature of Islamic Shari’ah?

questions.text: Amina is traveling on a bus from Kisumu to Nairobi (over 340 km). When the bus stops for lunch at 1:30 PM, how should she pray Dhuhr and Asr?

options.text: Pray 2 rak’ahs for Dhuhr, make Salam, then pray 2 rak’ahs for Asr (Jam’a Taqdim with Qasr)
Pray 8 rak’ahs continuously without any break
Wait until reaching Nairobi late at night and skip Asr
Pray 1 rak’ah for Dhuhr and skip Asr

questions.correctAnswer: Pray 2 rak’ahs for Dhuhr, make Salam, then pray 2 rak’ahs for Asr (Jam’a Taqdim with Qasr)
questions.explanation: As a traveler, Amina can perform Jam’a Taqdim: praying 2 shortened rak’ahs for Dhuhr, concluding with Salam, then immediately standing to pray 2 shortened rak’ahs for Asr.
questions.socraticHint: Apply the rules of shortening and early combination for Dhuhr and Asr.
questions.prompt: Amina is traveling on a bus from Kisumu to Nairobi (over 340 km). When the bus stops for lunch at 1:30 PM, how should she pray Dhuhr and Asr?

questions.text: What category of Islamic obligation does Swalatul Janazah (Funeral Prayer) fall under?
questions.explanation: Swalatul Janazah is Fardh Kifayah: if some members of the community perform it, the obligation is lifted from the rest, but if nobody does, all share the sin.
questions.socraticHint: Which legal category means communal responsibility rather than mandatory on every individual?
questions.prompt: What category of Islamic obligation does Swalatul Janazah (Funeral Prayer) fall under?

questions.text: How many Takbirat (saying "Allahu Akbar") are performed in Swalatul Janazah?
questions.explanation: The standard established Sunnah for Swalatul Janazah consists of four Takbirat, with specific recitations recited after each one.
questions.socraticHint: Count the number of Takbirs from the first opening Takbir to the final fourth Takbir.
questions.prompt: How many Takbirat (saying "Allahu Akbar") are performed in Swalatul Janazah?

questions.text: What unique physical characteristic distinguishes Swalatul Janazah from the regular five daily prayers?

options.text: It must be performed while sitting down on the floor
It requires reciting the entire Qur’an aloud
It includes three prostrations per unit
It has NO Ruku (bowing) and NO Sujud (prostration); it is performed standing entirely

questions.correctAnswer: It has NO Ruku (bowing) and NO Sujud (prostration); it is performed standing entirely
questions.explanation: Swalatul Janazah consists strictly of standing (Qiyam), Takbirat, and supplications; there is no bowing (Ruku) or prostrating (Sujud) at any point.
questions.socraticHint: Think about whether anyone bows or prostrates on the ground during a funeral prayer.
questions.prompt: What unique physical characteristic distinguishes Swalatul Janazah from the regular five daily prayers?

questions.text: What is recited immediately after the FIRST Takbir in Swalatul Janazah?
questions.explanation: After the first Takbir (Takbirat al-Ihram), the worshiper seeks refuge with Allah and recites Surah Al-Fatihah silently.
questions.socraticHint: Which foundational Surah begins every Islamic prayer?
questions.prompt: What is recited immediately after the FIRST Takbir in Swalatul Janazah?

questions.text: What is recited after the SECOND Takbir in Swalatul Janazah?

options.text: As-Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah (Sending blessings and prayers upon Prophet Muhammad)

questions.correctAnswer: As-Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah (Sending blessings and prayers upon Prophet Muhammad)
questions.explanation: After the second Takbir, the worshiper recites As-Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah (Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammad wa ‘ala aali Muhammad...).
questions.socraticHint: Which prayer invokes blessings on the Prophet Muhammad and the family of Ibrahim?
questions.prompt: What is recited after the SECOND Takbir in Swalatul Janazah?

questions.text: What is the primary action performed after the THIRD Takbir in Swalatul Janazah?

options.text: Singing poetic eulogies about the person’s ancestors
Sincere du’a (supplication) asking Allah to forgive and have mercy upon the deceased

questions.correctAnswer: Sincere du’a (supplication) asking Allah to forgive and have mercy upon the deceased
questions.explanation: The third Takbir is dedicated specifically to pleading for Allah’s mercy, forgiveness, and pardon for the deceased ("Allahumma ighfir lahu warhamhu...").
questions.socraticHint: What is the main purpose of gathering to pray for someone who has passed away?
questions.prompt: What is the primary action performed after the THIRD Takbir in Swalatul Janazah?

questions.text: How does Swalatul Janazah conclude after the fourth Takbir and short du’a for all Muslims?

options.text: Making two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sujud al-Sahw)
Shaking hands while walking around the body seven times
Making Tasleem (turning the head to the right saying "Assalamu alaykum wa Rahmatullah")

questions.correctAnswer: Making Tasleem (turning the head to the right saying "Assalamu alaykum wa Rahmatullah")
questions.explanation: The prayer finishes like other prayers with Tasleem to exit the sacred state of prayer, typically to the right side.
questions.socraticHint: How does any Islamic prayer officially end?
questions.prompt: How does Swalatul Janazah conclude after the fourth Takbir and short du’a for all Muslims?

questions.text: What are the three essential stages of preparing a deceased Muslim’s body before the Janazah prayer and burial?

options.text: Embalming, display in public halls, and cremation
Singing dirges, wearing black mourning robes, and fasting for forty days
Taking photographs, reading wills, and scattering ashes

questions.explanation: Islamic funeral rites require ritual washing (Ghusl), wrapping in clean unstitched white cloth (Kafan), and dignified burial facing Qiblah (Dafan).
questions.socraticHint: Which three Arabic terms describe the washing, wrapping, and burying of the deceased?
questions.prompt: What are the three essential stages of preparing a deceased Muslim’s body before the Janazah prayer and burial?

questions.text: How many sheets of clean white cloth are customarily used to shroud (Kafan) a deceased male Muslim?
questions.explanation: According to authentic Sunnah reported by Sayyidah Aisha, the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) was shrouded in three clean white Sahuli cotton garments.
questions.socraticHint: Recall how many simple white cloths wrapped the Prophet’s body.
questions.prompt: How many sheets of clean white cloth are customarily used to shroud (Kafan) a deceased male Muslim?

questions.text: What is Ta’ziyah in Islamic community ethics?

options.text: Wailing loudly and tearing clothes at the grave
Imposing heavy fees on the mourning family
Visiting and consoling the bereaved family with comforting words and assistance

questions.correctAnswer: Visiting and consoling the bereaved family with comforting words and assistance
questions.explanation: Ta’ziyah means offering condolences, cheering the hearts of those grieving, encouraging patience, and helping them through their bereavement.
questions.socraticHint: Which term refers to comforting and sympathizing with grieving family members?
questions.prompt: What is Ta’ziyah in Islamic community ethics?

questions.text: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) instruct his companions to do when news of Ja’far ibn Abi Talib’s martyrdom arrived?

options.text: "Expect Ja’far’s family to host a lavish feast for all visitors"
"Ask the grieving family for monetary donations"
"Stay away from their house for forty days"
"Prepare food for the family of Ja’far, for there has come upon them that which engages them"

questions.correctAnswer: "Prepare food for the family of Ja’far, for there has come upon them that which engages them"
questions.explanation: The Prophet instituted the empathetic Sunnah of neighbors and relatives cooking meals for the mourning family, relieving them of daily chores in their sorrow.
questions.socraticHint: Should grieving families cook for guests, or should friends and neighbors cook for them?
questions.prompt: What did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) instruct his companions to do when news of Ja’far ibn Abi Talib’s martyrdom arrived?

questions.text: Which practice is strictly FORBIDDEN in Islam during times of mourning and bereavement?

options.text: Wailing hysterically (Niyaha), tearing clothes, and slapping cheeks
Shedding natural, quiet tears of grief
Paying off the debts left behind by the deceased

questions.correctAnswer: Wailing hysterically (Niyaha), tearing clothes, and slapping cheeks
questions.explanation: The Prophet condemned pre-Islamic customs of violent mourning (tearing clothes, beating cheeks, and screaming objections to God’s decree), while permitting quiet tears of compassion.
questions.socraticHint: Which pagan pre-Islamic reaction expresses rejection of divine decree through violent behavior?
questions.prompt: Which practice is strictly FORBIDDEN in Islam during times of mourning and bereavement?

questions.text: What is the foundational prerequisite of capability required for Hajj to become an obligation called?
questions.explanation: Istita’ah encompasses physical health, safe routes, and financial means to afford the journey and support one’s family while away (Surah Ali Imran 3:97).
questions.socraticHint: Which Arabic term describes having the capacity or ability to perform pilgrimage?
questions.prompt: What is the foundational prerequisite of capability required for Hajj to become an obligation called?

questions.text: What are the four non-negotiable Pillars (Arkan) of Hajj without which Hajj is completely invalid?

options.text: Wearing shoes, climbing Mount Uhud, visiting Madinah, and drinking Zamzam
Giving charity in Makkah, reading the Quran, fasting on Friday, and buying souvenirs
Ihram, Wuquf at Arafat, Tawaf al-Ifadah, and Sa’i
Slaughtering a sheep, fasting three days, shaving hair, and sleeping in Mina

questions.correctAnswer: Ihram, Wuquf at Arafat, Tawaf al-Ifadah, and Sa’i
questions.explanation: The four essential pillars of Hajj are: 1) Ihram (intention & state), 2) Standing at Arafat, 3) Tawaf al-Ifadah, and 4) Sa’i between Safa and Marwah.
questions.socraticHint: Which four central rites cannot be substituted even by animal sacrifice (Dam)?
questions.prompt: What are the four non-negotiable Pillars (Arkan) of Hajj without which Hajj is completely invalid?

questions.text: On which Islamic date does the pinnacle rite of Hajj—Wuquf (Standing at Arafat)—take place?
questions.explanation: The Day of Arafat is on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah; standing at Arafat from after noon until sunset on this day is the cornerstone of Hajj.
questions.socraticHint: Identify the day immediately preceding Eid ul-Adha (10th Dhul-Hijjah).
questions.prompt: On which Islamic date does the pinnacle rite of Hajj—Wuquf (Standing at Arafat)—take place?

questions.text: What did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say regarding the supreme importance of the Day of Arafat?
questions.explanation: The Prophet emphasized the central pillar of pilgrimage by declaring: "Al-Hajju Arafah" (Hajj is Arafat). Missing Arafat invalidates the entire Hajj.
questions.socraticHint: Recall the concise three-word prophetic Hadith summarizing the climax of pilgrimage.
questions.prompt: What did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) say regarding the supreme importance of the Day of Arafat?

questions.text: What is the designated geographical boundary point beyond which a pilgrim may not pass without entering the state of Ihram called?
questions.explanation: Al-Miqat refers to the specific stations appointed by the Prophet (such as Dhul-Hulayfah or Yalamlam) where pilgrims enter the sacred state of Ihram.
questions.socraticHint: Which term means the designated border station for putting on Ihram garments?
questions.prompt: What is the designated geographical boundary point beyond which a pilgrim may not pass without entering the state of Ihram called?

questions.text: How many circuits (Ashwat) are made around the Ka’bah during Tawaf?
questions.explanation: Every Tawaf consists of seven anti-clockwise circuits starting and ending at the corner of the Black Stone (Al-Hajar al-Aswad).

questions.text: Why is the sacred word "Shanti" (Peace) chanted exactly THREE times at the conclusion of Hindu prayers?

"May everyone travel across the seven seas"

questions.text: What are the Niyamas in Sage Patanjali’s classical Ashtanga Yoga system?

options.text: Dietary rules only for forest hermits
Personal observances, inner disciplines, and positive habits for self-purification
Social restraints and rules for dealing with enemies
Physical martial arts techniques for warfare

questions.correctAnswer: Personal observances, inner disciplines, and positive habits for self-purification
questions.explanation: While the Yamas govern interpersonal social ethics, the Five Niyamas are internal personal disciplines that purify character and cultivate inner strength.
questions.socraticHint: Distinguish between social ethics (Yamas) and personal inner disciplines (Niyamas).
questions.prompt: What are the Niyamas in Sage Patanjali’s classical Ashtanga Yoga system?

questions.text: How many Niyamas are formulated in the Yoga Sutras of Sage Patanjali?

questions.prompt: How many Niyamas are formulated in the Yoga Sutras of Sage Patanjali?

questions.text: What is the first Niyama, which signifies both physical cleanliness and mental purity?
questions.explanation: Shaucha is purity: external cleanliness of the body, environment, and food (Bahya Shaucha), and internal purity of thoughts and emotions (Abhyantara Shaucha).
questions.socraticHint: Which Sanskrit term signifies cleanliness, purity, and sanitation?
questions.prompt: What is the first Niyama, which signifies both physical cleanliness and mental purity?

questions.text: What is "Abhyantara Shaucha" (Internal Purity) in daily character development?

options.text: Cleansing the mind of jealousy, anger, hatred, and deceit through noble thoughts and compassion
Drinking ten liters of water every hour
Sweeping the classroom floor three times daily

questions.correctAnswer: Cleansing the mind of jealousy, anger, hatred, and deceit through noble thoughts and compassion
questions.explanation: Internal purity pertains to the mental and emotional sphere: harboring pure intentions, forgiving others, and cultivating goodwill instead of spite.
questions.socraticHint: How does one cleanse the mind and heart internally?
questions.prompt: What is "Abhyantara Shaucha" (Internal Purity) in daily character development?

questions.text: What is the second Niyama, which signifies gratitude, contentment, and joy with what one has?
questions.explanation: Santosha means contentment—being cheerful, thankful for life’s blessings, and free from the restless craving to constantly acquire more material toys.
questions.socraticHint: Which term means contentment and peaceful satisfaction?
questions.prompt: What is the second Niyama, which signifies gratitude, contentment, and joy with what one has?

questions.text: Does practicing Santosha (contentment) mean a student should become lazy and stop trying to improve their grades?

options.text: Yes, students should refuse to take tests
Only if they are already in Grade 6

Yes, it means sleeping all day without opening books

questions.correctAnswer: No, Santosha means working hard cheerfully without being poisoned by bitter jealousy or anxiety over what others possess
questions.explanation: Contentment is an inner state of peaceful gratitude; it empowers a student to strive for academic excellence with joyful enthusiasm rather than toxic envy.
questions.socraticHint: Does genuine gratitude encourage laziness or joyful, diligent effort?
questions.prompt: Does practicing Santosha (contentment) mean a student should become lazy and stop trying to improve their grades?

questions.text: What is the third Niyama, which represents perseverance, disciplined effort, and spiritual fortitude?
questions.explanation: Tapas comes from the root "Tap" (to heat or burn), signifying the burning zeal of self-discipline and perseverance required to purify character and achieve great goals.
questions.socraticHint: Which term means austerity, perseverance, and disciplined focus?
questions.prompt: What is the third Niyama, which represents perseverance, disciplined effort, and spiritual fortitude?

options.text: Just as intense heat in a furnace burns away dross to reveal pure gold, disciplined effort purges weaknesses to reveal noble character
Gold becomes softer when left in cold water
Gold is produced by planting seeds in wet soil
Gold cannot be changed by heat

questions.correctAnswer: Just as intense heat in a furnace burns away dross to reveal pure gold, disciplined effort purges weaknesses to reveal noble character
questions.explanation: In Vedic metaphors, Tapas is the spiritual fire of discipline that dissolves laziness, impatience, and selfishness, refining the individual into pure gold.
questions.socraticHint: How does fire refine precious gold from impurities?
questions.prompt: How is Tapas compared to the process of purifying raw gold from rock ore?

questions.text: Dev is tempted to play video games all evening instead of revising for his term science test. If he chooses to turn off the console and study diligently for two hours, which Niyama is he practicing?

questions.text: How does practicing Shaucha (purity) protect a school community from infectious illnesses like cholera and flu?

It turns dirty water into medicine

It creates pleasant aromas that chase away germs magically

questions.explanation: Bahya Shaucha translates directly to practical hygiene and public health measures, preventing the spread of communicable diseases in schools.

questions.text: What does Sage Patanjali declare is attained from mastering Santosha (Yoga Sutra 2.42)?

options.text: Immense political power over foreign kingdoms
Ability to fly through the clouds
Anuttamah Sukhalabhah (Unsurpassed, supreme happiness is attained)

questions.correctAnswer: Anuttamah Sukhalabhah (Unsurpassed, supreme happiness is attained)
questions.explanation: Patanjali explains: "Santoshad anuttamah sukhalabhah"—from true contentment arises unmatched happiness, because an insatiable mind can never experience peace.

questions.prompt: What does Sage Patanjali declare is attained from mastering Santosha (Yoga Sutra 2.42)?

questions.text: How does social media peer pressure challenge Santosha (contentment) among modern Kenyan youth?

options.text: It tempts youth to compare themselves to curated online lifestyles, generating fake inadequacy and discontent
It encourages youth to read more classical books
It teaches students how to cultivate vegetable gardens

questions.correctAnswer: It tempts youth to compare themselves to curated online lifestyles, generating fake inadequacy and discontent
questions.explanation: Comparing oneself to artificial online perfection breeds jealousy and unhappiness; practicing Santosha anchors young minds in gratitude for real-world blessings.

questions.prompt: How does social media peer pressure challenge Santosha (contentment) among modern Kenyan youth?

questions.text: What is the fourth Niyama, which means self-study, reading sacred texts, and honest self-reflection?
questions.explanation: Svadhyaya ("Sva" = self, "Adhyaya" = study) involves the study of wisdom literature as well as the introspective examination of one’s own thoughts and conduct.

questions.prompt: What is the fourth Niyama, which means self-study, reading sacred texts, and honest self-reflection?

questions.text: What are the two complementary dimensions of practicing Svadhyaya?

options.text: Painting wall murals and playing flutes
Arguing with teachers and skipping homework
Reading sacred/uplifting scriptures and engaging in daily personal introspection (self-audit)
Memorizing phone numbers and watching entertainment videos

questions.correctAnswer: Reading sacred/uplifting scriptures and engaging in daily personal introspection (self-audit)
questions.explanation: Svadhyaya requires both studying spiritual knowledge (such as the Gita and Upanishads) and holding a mirror to one’s own conscience to self-correct.
questions.socraticHint: Notice how Svadhyaya pairs study of external wisdom texts with internal self-examination.
questions.prompt: What are the two complementary dimensions of practicing Svadhyaya?

questions.text: What is the fifth Niyama, representing surrender to the Divine and dedicating all actions to God?
questions.explanation: Ishvara Pranidhana means surrender (Pranidhana) to the Supreme Lord (Ishvara)—releasing egoistic pride and offering one’s work as a sacred dedication to God.

questions.prompt: What is the fifth Niyama, representing surrender to the Divine and dedicating all actions to God?

questions.text: How does practicing Ishvara Pranidhana protect an achiever from destructive arrogance (Ahankara)?

options.text: It reminds them that talents, breath, and opportunities are gifts from God, inspiring humility and gratitude
It makes them boast that God favors them above everyone else
It encourages them to stop sharing credit with others
It convinces them that they no longer need to work

questions.correctAnswer: It reminds them that talents, breath, and opportunities are gifts from God, inspiring humility and gratitude
questions.explanation: Dedication to the Divine dissolves ego; when success comes, the practitioner acknowledges: "This is God’s grace working through me, not my personal pride."
questions.socraticHint: Who is the ultimate source of all talent, intelligence, and breath?
questions.prompt: How does practicing Ishvara Pranidhana protect an achiever from destructive arrogance (Ahankara)?

questions.text: What healthy mental attitude does "Prasada Buddhi" cultivate when facing life’s outcomes under Ishvara Pranidhana?

options.text: Demanding that other people take the blame
Accepting results peacefully with gratitude as divine gifts/lessons, without bitter despair or arrogance
Blaming God furiously whenever things go wrong
Giving up on all ambitions forever

questions.correctAnswer: Accepting results peacefully with gratitude as divine gifts/lessons, without bitter despair or arrogance
questions.explanation: Prasada Buddhi views outcomes like sacred temple offerings (Prasada)—received with grace, calm dignity, and contentment, knowing life is a learning journey.

questions.prompt: What question should a learner ask themselves every evening when conducting Svadhyaya (self-audit)?

questions.prompt: Which sacred text studied during Svadhyaya provides dialogue between Lord Krishna and Arjuna on righteous living?

questions.text: What does the Sanskrit word "Ashtanga" literally mean in Ashtanga Yoga?

questions.text: Which limb of Ashtanga Yoga constitutes the third step, focusing on physical postures?

A posture must cause extreme pain and suffering
A posture should only be done while standing on one foot

questions.prompt: What is Padmasana, commonly used for meditation and quiet breathing practice?

Balancing on the head with legs in the air
Sitting with legs stretched forward touching the toes
Lying flat on the back completely motionless

questions.explanation: Bhujangasana ("Bhujanga" = cobra serpent) strengthens spinal extensor muscles, expands lung capacity, and relieves stiffness from long hours of sitting in school desks.

questions.prompt: What ancient sun salutation sequence combines twelve coordinated Asanas with mindful breathing to invigorate the whole body?

questions.text: What is Pranayama in the Ashtanga Yoga system?

options.text: The conscious control and regulation of vital life-force breath
The practice of loud public chanting
A diet consisting only of raw grains

questions.correctAnswer: The conscious control and regulation of vital life-force breath

questions.text: What is Nadi Shodhana (also known as Anuloma Viloma) Pranayama?

Alternate Nostril Breathing that balances the nervous system and brain hemispheres

questions.prompt: What is Nadi Shodhana (also known as Anuloma Viloma) Pranayama?

questions.text: What is Bhramari Pranayama, and why is it especially useful for students suffering from tension or headaches?

options.text: Running around the school field shouting like an animal
Blowing air through a musical flute
The "Humming Bee" breath where exhaling with a humming sound soothes the brain and releases anxiety

questions.prompt: What is Bhramari Pranayama, and why is it especially useful for students suffering from tension or headaches?

questions.text: What is the fifth limb of Ashtanga Yoga, known as Pratyahara?

Physical fasting on full moon days
Painting sacred mandalas with colored sand

questions.correctAnswer: Withdrawal of the senses from external attractions and distractions
questions.explanation: Pratyahara is sensory withdrawal—turning attention inward away from outside sights, sounds, and screens so the mind is not tossed by sensory cravings.
questions.socraticHint: Which limb bridges external physical practices with internal mental meditation?
questions.prompt: What is the fifth limb of Ashtanga Yoga, known as Pratyahara?

questions.text: What is the sixth limb of Ashtanga Yoga, known as Dharana?

options.text: One-pointed concentration of the mind on a single chosen object or thought
Walking in a circle around a temple

questions.text: How does practicing Pratyahara (sensory withdrawal) help modern learners cope with digital overload from smartphones?

It makes phones run out of battery faster
It empowers them to consciously step away from screen pings and social media noise to give their nervous system peaceful rest
It forces them to smash electronic devices with rocks

questions.prompt: What is the eighth and ultimate limb of Ashtanga Yoga, representing supreme spiritual realization and oneness with Paramatma?

Service to humanity is worship of God
Only kings are worthy of receiving service
